[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Let $(\Psi(n))_{n\geq 0}$ be a positive sequence that we assume monotone decreasing to zero.
Assume that there exists $\kappa > 0$, $C,c > 0$, and a polynomial $P$ such that for any $1 \leq m \leq n$, 
\begin{equation}
\Psi(2n) \leq P(m)\Psi((1-\kappa)n)^2 + C\e^{-cm}. 
\end{equation}
Then, $\Psi(n)$ tends superpolynomially fast to 0, that is, for any $A>0$, 
\[n^A \Psi(n) \underset{n\rightarrow \infty}{\longrightarrow} 0. \]

[Theorem theorem_size_bias_bound of arXiv:2606.03442, 'Stein's method in network analysis'] Let~$X$ be a non-negative random variable with finite variance~$\sigma^2$, and let~$X^{(s)}$ be constructed on the
 same probability space as~$X$, having the size bias distribution of~$X$;
 write $\nu^2 := \mathbb{E}[(X^{(s)}-X)^2]$. Let~$\mathscr{F}$ be any sub-sigma field with respect to the probability
 space on which $X$ and $X^{(s)}$ are defined.
 Then,
    \begin{align*}
        d_{{\mathrm{BW}}}\bigl(&\mathcal{L}(\sigma^{-1}  (X- \mathbb{E}[X])),N(0,1)\bigr) \\
        &\ \le\  \sigma^{-2} \mathbb{E}[X] \bigg( 4 (\mathbb{V}[\mathbb{E}[X^{(s)}-X \, \vert \, \mathscr{F} ] ]  )^{1/2} +
        \frac{7\nu}{\sigma} \bigg( \frac{\nu}{2} + (\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{V}[X \, \vert \, \mathscr{F}]]^{1/2} \bigg) \bigg).
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For every 0<a<=2 and R>=1, stationary isotropic unit-modulus fields on R^2 realize A(r)=(1+r^2)^(-a/2) and B_R(r)=A(r)exp(-(r/R)^2). A uniform phase and a Gaussian wavevector conditionally of covariance 2G I_2, with G~Gamma(a/2,1), give A; adding an independent Gaussian wavevector of covariance 2R^-2 I_2 gives B_R. Their uniform difference is <=R^-a, while r^a A(r)->1 and r^b B_R(r)->0 for every b>0. Arbitrarily small fixed additive error therefore permits destruction of the whole algebraic tail. These fields are not asserted to be Riesz Gibbs states or geometric bond fields.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Integrator-authored exact restricted calculation or proof-obstruction analysis after primary-source comparison Result: For a quadratic potential equal to kappa times the DGFF quadratic potential, the full field is exactly kappa^(-1/2) times the reference DGFF. Thus its logarithmic variance constant is g/kappa and the intermediate level 2*sqrt(g/kappa)*lambda*log(N) reduces exactly to the known DGFF level after multiplication by sqrt(kappa). This checks the necessary stiffness normalization. For general uniformly convex potentials, Gaussian exponential-moment comparison can give upper tails on the logarithmic scale, but does not automatically recover the Mills prefactor or the mixed high-point moments that determine the chaos limit. A field-level central limit statement cannot be inserted into an N-dependent indicator of a rare logarithmic-height event. Check: Changing variables h=kappa^(-1/2)*h0 in the finite-volume Gibbs density converts its quadratic Hamiltonian exactly to the reference one; the Jacobian is absorbed by normalization. This checks both covariance and threshold scaling independently. Obstruction: No extension from quadratic to general uniformly convex potentials. No moment convergence at moving rare-event thresholds is assumed.

body: Bond FPP on Z^2 with iid weights in [a,b], 0 < a <= b < infinity. For ANY geodesic gamma (any endpoints, any configuration) and any axis-aligned n x W lattice box B, the number of edges of gamma inside B is at most (b/a)(n+W). Proof: the first and last vertices x, y of gamma in the closed box satisfy d_L1(x,y) <= n+W; a monotone lattice path from x to y costs at most b(n+W), so subpath optimality gives a|gamma[x->y]| <= X_xy <= b(n+W), and every edge of gamma in B lies on gamma[x->y]. Sharp: at a=b a corner-to-corner staircase in an n x n box attains exactly 2n = n+W. Refereed 2026-08-09 (independent adversarial search: lexicographic Dijkstra maximizing box occupation, hill-climbing and annealing over {a,b} weights, serpentine gadgets, extreme aspect ratios - zero violations). Provenance: probability_open_problem_campaign_2026_08_09/problem/CRUX_iteration_arithmetic.md section 5.
title: Deterministic block-occupation lemma (FPP on Z^2, sharp constant)

          \qquad \text{for any closed } F\subset H .
      \end{align*}
      If the attractor of the limit system \eqref{e.080301} is a random point, then the large deviation lower bound also holds:
      \begin{align*}
          \liminf_{\eps\to0}\eps\ln\mu_{\sigma}^{\eps}(G)
          \geq -\inf_{u\in G}E_{\Ac(\sigma)}(u),
          \qquad \text{for any open } G\subset H .
      \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2605.12475, 'Central limit theorem for the homozygosity of the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process'] For $m \geq 2$ and $L \geq 1$, the following multivariate CLTs hold
\bal
\bm{W}_{X,L} &= (X_{1,k}(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), X_{m,L}(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta)) \xrightarrow{D} N(\bm{0}, \bm{\Sigma}_{X,L}), \qquad \text{for all $1 \leq k \leq L$} \\
\bm{W}_{T,L} &= (T_1(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta), T_{m,L}(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta)) \xrightarrow{D} N(\bm{0}, \bm{\Sigma}_{T,L}) 
\eal
as $\theta_0, \theta \to \infty$ such that $\frac{\theta_0}{\theta} \to c$, where the covariance matrices are given by
\bal
\bm{\Sigma}_{X,L} &= \begin{pmatrix}
1 - \beta & B_k(\alpha, \beta, c, m, L) \\ 
B_k(\alpha, \beta, c, m, L) & \sigma_{X,m,L}^2 
\end{pmatrix} \\
\bm{\Sigma}_{T,L} &= \begin{pmatrix}
\beta & \beta \frac{\sum_{j=1}^m j A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}}}{\sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}}}  \\ 
\beta \frac{\sum_{j=1}^m j A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}}}{\sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}}}  & \sigma_{T,m,L}^2 
\end{pmatrix},
\eal
with $\sigma_{X,m,L}^2$ the variance from Lemma \ref{homozygosityLgroupsLevel2.2CLT}, $\sigma_{T,m,L}^2$ the variance from Lemma \ref{homozygosityLgroupsLevel2.1CLT}, and 
\bal
B_k(\alpha, \beta, c, m, L) = \frac{ \sum_{j=1}^m \left(\sum_{\bm{m} \in M_{m,L}} \sum_{\bm{j} \in M_{j, L}} (m_k - \beta j_k) \prod_{\ell = 1}^L \Cs(m_\ell, j_\ell, \beta) \right) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}} }{\sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}}}.
\eal

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact identities, finite controls and structural obstruction Result: Changing one of the2n input letters changes L_n by at most1. Efron-Stein therefore gives Var L_n <=(1/2)*sum_(j=1)^(2n) E[(L_n-L_n^(j))^2]<=n/2 in the binary model: a resampled fair bit differs with probability1/2. Bounded differences also gives P(|L_n-E L_n|>=t)<=2 exp(-t^2/n). These exact upper bounds rule out fluctuations substantially larger than sqrt(n), while allowing smaller scales. Check: The Lipschitz bound follows by deleting at most one matched position from an optimal subsequence and applying the same argument in reverse. The factor n/2 uses the resampling mismatch probability; the cruder distribution-free bound is n. The known Houdré-Islak2023 CLT explicitly assumes a variance lower bound, rather than deriving it for every uniform alphabet. The archived2023 primary paper, equation1.4 onPDF3, attributes the exact general bound n*(1-sum p_k^2) to Steele; this campaign calculation is a rederivation of that known bound. Obstruction: Neither concentration nor pairwise independence of matching indicators proves a positive linear variance lower bound. Independent Bernoulli matching models can have different limiting laws. No uniform-model lower bound or direct normal approximation avoiding it is proved here.

Method: Exact recurrence, conditional-law calculation, or source-specific limiting obstruction Result: Starting a law at a convex mixture of the two known fixed points does not make the evolution stationary. The two-child update has a cross-input term of weight2p(1-p), so along the mixture line the derivative is2p(1-p)*(C-(nu_diag+nu_min)/2). Thus an apparent line of equilibria in a linear interpolation plot can be spurious. The source suggests sharing lightning until a fixed time and separating it afterward as a possible source of other equilibria, which would require a consistent infinite-process construction. Check: The derivative formula follows by expanding the independent child labels and subtracting the original mixture. It is an exact signed-measure identity, not a numerical simulation. Obstruction: No invariant family containing the proposed time-split couplings has been constructed, and no global Lyapunov function or complete basin decomposition is obtained.

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2608.29075, 'The 2-Monoidal Structure of Symmetric Sequences'] An \textit{operad} is a monoid in the monoidal category $(\catname{sSeq}, \circ, \mathcal{J})$. Explicitly, it consists of a symmetric sequence $\PP$ together with morphisms of symmetric sequences $\mu:\PP \circ \PP \rightarrow \PP$, called the \textit{multiplication}, and $\eta: \mathcal{J} \rightarrow \PP$, called the \textit{unit}, such that the following diagrams commute. 
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{(\PP \circ \PP) \circ \PP} && {\PP \circ (\PP \circ \PP)} \\
	{\PP \circ \PP} && {\PP \circ \PP} \\
	& \PP
	\arrow["{{{a_{\PP,\PP,\PP}}}}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{{\mu \circ \id_{\PP}}}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{{\id_{\PP} \circ \mu}}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\mu"', from=2-1, to=3-2]
	\arrow["\mu", from=2-3, to=3-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{\mathcal{J} \circ \PP} && {\PP \circ \PP} && {\PP \circ \mathcal{J}} && {\PP \circ \PP} \\
	& \PP &&&& \PP
	\arrow["{{\eta \circ \id_{\PP}}}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{{l_{\PP}}}"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\mu", from=1-3, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{{\id_{\PP} \circ \eta}}", from=1-5, to=1-7]
	\arrow["{{r_{\PP}}}"', from=1-5, to=2-6]
	\arrow["\mu", from=1-7, to=2-6]
\end{tikzcd}\]
The arrows labeled $a, l$, and $r$ in the diagrams above denote the associator and the unitors in ($\catname{sSeq}, \circ, \mathcal{J}$).

(Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:expr-Z-arithmetic-case of arXiv:2411.03065, 'Growing conditioned BGW trees with\\ log-concave offspring distributions'] For $n\geq 0$ we have the expressions
	\begin{align}
	\PFComp{\shift{qd+s}{\mathbf{w}},{\mathbf{b}}}{nd+(d-s)}
	&=\sum_{i\geq0}W_{i+q+1}F^{d-s}_{n,i},
	&&q\in\{0,\dots,r-1\},
	&&s\in\{1,\dots,d-1\},\\
	\PFComp{\shift{qd+0}{\mathbf{w}},{\mathbf{b}}}{nd+(d-0)}
	&=\sum_{i\geq0}W_{i+q}F^{0}_{n+1,i},
	&&q\in\{0,\dots,r-1\},
	&&s=0.
	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:expr-Z-arithmetic-case of arXiv:2411.03065

body: [Lemma thm_general_heateq of arXiv:2411.17653, 'Exclusion processes with non-reversible boundary: hydrodynamics and large deviations'] The problem (equation nonlinear_robin of the paper) has a weak solution in $L^2([0,T], H^1([0,1]))$. Moreover, if it has a solution in $C^{1,2}( {\Omega_T})$, it is unique. The uniqueness of solution extends to weak solutions in $L^2([0,T], H^1([0,1]))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma thm_general_heateq of arXiv:2411.17653

body:
[Thm divergenceoftrace of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] If $\theta_T-\theta_0\in(4k\pi+\pi,4k\pi+3\pi)$ for some integer $k$, then for any real number $a$, it holds that
    $$
    \int_a^{a+\pi}\rho_T^\lambda\cos(\varphi_T^\lambda-\zeta)d\zeta\longrightarrow -\infty,
    $$
    as $\lambda\to+\infty$, where $\rho^\lambda,\varphi^\lambda$ are defined by (equation rhovarphi of the paper).

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited); independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2 and 1<=r<K be integers. There are N contexts with K candidates each, d disjoint pairs with exactly one arbitrary A context and one systematic S context per pair, and N-2d known S contexts. All K candidates are true in S; each A has an independent uniform random r-subset of truths. A world fixes pair orientations and subsets. Its factual law p chooses contexts uniformly then a true candidate uniformly. The orientation class has VC dimension d. Training supplies n iid uniform context indices and exact A/S tags, with no candidate identities. For a partition Pi, p_Pi is uniform within each cell with that cell total p mass, and Mis_Pi(g,p)=TV(p_Pi,g) with TV half the l1 distance. Output bins depend on g alone. Competing generators g are arbitrary laws on the NK candidates. Feasibility means Mis<=c for every world compatible with the observed information; the objective is worst-world false-output mass. After training a perfect verifier discloses the orientation and all r true candidates in the A member of each of k predetermined pairs, 0<=k<=d, selected independently of tags and worlds. It covers fraction k/d of arbitrary truths by both count and factual mass. U counts the other d-k pairs untouched by training. Set kappa=1-r/K, beta=r/K, a1=(d-k)/N and m=U/N. For the source one-bin calibration Mis_1(g,p)=TV(lambda,g), lambda uniform on NK candidates, set f=kappa*k/N and w=(d-k-U)/N. The exact conditional frontier for c in [0,1] is W=beta*(f-c)_+ +(kappa/2)*(f+w-c)_+ +(kappa/2)*(f+w+2m-c)_+. The corresponding known-partition oracle sets U=0, and the exact excess is (kappa/2)*(m-|f+a1-c|)_+. The expected minimax value is E W with E[z^U]=sum_{j=0}^{d-k} binom(d-k,j)*(z-1)^j*(1-2j/N)^n. At c=0 the value is kappa*d/N for every k; at k=d it is (kappa*d/N-c)_+, whereas the exact-level-calibration frontier is zero. Removing mass from verified false atoms first, then known A, then unknown pairs and transferring it to known S attains the value in every compatible world. This is also the conditional posterior-average value. No intermediate finite-bin frontier is asserted.
Integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2,1<=r<K,0<=k<=d
d context pairs each have exactly one A and one S; all other contexts known S
S has K true candidates; A has independent uniform r-subset; target context law uniform, then uniform over truths
n iid uniform contexts with true partition tags, no candidate identities during training
Perfect verifier reveals all r A truths and orientation in each of k independently predetermined pairs
Mis_1 equals TV(uniform law on all NK candidates,g); no restriction on g
Worst-world or stated posterior-average hallucination, conditional on tags and verifier output

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:8dd0d74843430005023aea7a8912af3fa204a6d2840e1425ee942fef7983dba0","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/8d/8dd0d74843430005023aea7a8912af3fa204a6d2840e1425ee942fef7983dba0.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:6dedddd063f7908d67a9540249534c89c6c67113af4f9266de657d19e6f12543","bundle_entry_key":"one-bin-verifier-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-unrestricted-vc-verifier-frontiers-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; minimax decision theory","draft":"w709/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:paired-vc-one-bin-verifier-frontier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# One-bin versus exact-level calibration under a perfect verifier

Candidate T379-C007 v1. OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited).
Target 2, proposed kind narrowed. The hardest unproved extension here is
the matching frontier for general intermediate source finite-bin counts;
neither this theorem nor C006 supplies that extension.

Use exactly C006's annotated paired VC-d experiment and perfect verifier:
d>=1, N>=2d+1, n>=0, K>=2, integer 1<=r<K, beta=r/K,
kappa=1-beta, and 0<=k<=d independently predetermined verified pairs.
Each arbitrary context has r true candidates; the verifier reveals its
orientation and all truths in the selected pairs. Let U be the number
of unverified pairs untouched by the n tagged training samples. Write

 f=kappa*k/N, w=(d-k-U)/N, m=U/N, a'=(d-k)/N=w+m.

For Kalai--Vempala Mis_1, which is exactly TV(lambda,g) with lambda
uniform on NK candidates independently of the factual world, the exact
worst-world hallucination frontier over ALL generators is

 W_k(c,U) = beta*(f-c)_+
          +(kappa/2)*(f+w-c)_+
          +(kappa/2)*(f+w+2m-c)_+,  0<=c<=1.           (1)

The calibration constraint is world-independent here. The corresponding
posterior-average hallucination game has the same value. The expected
minimax value under conditional robust feasibility is E[W_k(c,U)], with
the same joint occupancy law of U as in C006. The known-unverified-
partition oracle for Mis_1 has U=0 and value

 W_oracle(c)=beta*(f-c)_+ +kappa*(f+a'-c)_+.           (2)

Its exact excess is

 W_k(c,U)-W_oracle(c)
    =(kappa/2)*(m-|f+a'-c|)_+.                        (3)

## Lower bound for every generator

Condition on tags and verifier output, with C006's uniform compatible
world prior. False probabilities are 1 on verified false atoms F,
kappa on unverified known-A contexts A, kappa/2 on untouched pair
contexts M, and zero on all remaining atoms. Their lambda masses are
f, w, 2m respectively. For every g with TV(lambda,g)<=c, the event
inequality and nonnegativity give

 g(F)>=(f-c)_+,
 g(F union A)>=(f+w-c)_+,
 g(F union A union M)>=(f+w+2m-c)_+.

The posterior expected false mass is exactly

 beta*g(F)+(kappa/2)*g(F union A)+(kappa/2)*g(F union A union M).

This proves (1)'s lower bound. It does not impose context-uniformity or
bin restrictions on competing generators. Worst-world H dominates this
posterior average. Averaging over any decision random seed preserves the
same affine inequalities before positive parts are taken.

## Attainment and global minimax

Begin from lambda. Remove tF=min(c,f) uniformly from F. Remove
tA=min((c-f)_+,w) uniformly from A. Remove
tM=min((c-f-w)_+,2m) uniformly from M. Empty groups contribute zero.
Add all removed mass uniformly to the fixed systematic reservoir. Never
put added mass on any of F,A,M. The sets are disjoint, so
TV(lambda,g)=tF+tA+tM<=c and all probabilities are nonnegative.

In every compatible world, F is entirely false, a kappa fraction of
candidate mass in A is false, and half the contexts in M are A with a
kappa fraction false within each. Consequently

 H=f-tF+kappa*(w-tA)+(kappa/2)*(2m-tM).

The thresholds f, f+w, f+w+2m give (1). This worldwise equality proves
attainment without assuming the posterior lower bound holds separately
for every world. For the expected minimax game, the uniform world prior
gives a lower bound E[W_k]; the same construction attains W_k in every
world and U's law is world-independent, giving equality.

Setting U=0 gives (2). To obtain (3), put x=f+a'-c and use
[(x-m)_+ +(x+m)_+]/2 - x_+ = (m-|x|)_+/2.
The beta*(f-c)_+ term cancels. This identity follows by splitting at
x=-m,0,m, and is also checked with exact rational arithmetic.

## What changes when facts are verified

At c=0, g must equal lambda, and (1) is kappa*d/N for EVERY k and U.
Thus this calibration definition prevents any hallucination reduction
at zero budget, despite the verifier's truth information. This is a
consequence of the explicit Mis_1 definition, not a universal statement
about post-training or calibration in natural language.

At k=d, every truth is known and U=w=m=0, so the one-bin frontier is
(kappa*d/N-c)_+. In contrast, C006's exact-level Mis_infinity frontier
is zero for all c, achieved by the known factual law. Therefore one
cannot transfer its zero-calibration frontier to Mis_1.

At k=0, f=0 and (1) reduces to C004's frontier. The budget giving the
largest gap between learned and known partitions in (3) is
c=f+a'=(d-beta*k)/N. At that budget, the exact expected excess is
kappa*(d-k)/(2N)*(1-2/N)^n, while the known-partition oracle is zero.
Implementation uses group sizes, ERM version-space flags,
and the k revealed supports, with the same efficient representation as
C006. C006's probability bound for U also applies unchanged.

Source of Mis_1=TV(lambda,g): Kalai--Vempala arXiv:2311.14648v3,
Definition 2 and immediately following paragraph, printed p.9.
Standard TV event bounds and piecewise-linear mass removal are not
claimed as new. This claim proposes an exact explicit target-2 family,
not the general finite-bin, unannotated-data, or noisy-verifier problem.
Finite Fraction checks supplement this general argument; no independent

Let X_1,...,X_n be independent random variables on arbitrary measurable coordinate spaces, let f be measurable and real valued, and let Z=f(X_1,...,X_n) belong to L^2. For each i let X_i_prime be an independent copy of X_i, independent of all original coordinates, and let Z^{(i)} replace X_i by X_i_prime in f. Write X_{-i} for the other coordinates and m_i=E[Z|X_{-i}]. Then Var(Z)<=v:=sum_i E[(Z-m_i)^2]=(1/2)sum_i E[(Z-Z^{(i)})^2]=sum_i E[((Z-Z^{(i)})_+)^2]. For arbitrary real X_{-i}-measurable Z_i, Var(Z)<=sum_i E[(Z-Z_i)^2], interpreted in the extended nonnegative sense; if the right side is finite, each Z_i is square integrable. In particular v is the minimum over such square-integrable Z_i, attained at Z_i=m_i. A coordinate infimum inf_x f(X_1,...,X_{i-1},x,X_{i+1},...,X_n) may be used as Z_i only when it defines a real X_{-i}-measurable random variable; those properties are additional conditions, not automatic consequences of measurability of f on arbitrary spaces. Equality Var(Z)=v holds exactly when Z=c+sum_i g_i(X_i) almost surely for some square-integrable one-coordinate functions g_i and constant c. Equality in the arbitrary-Z_i bound holds exactly when this almost-sure additive condition holds and Z_i=m_i almost surely for every i. The Efron-Stein bound is Boucheron-Lugosi-Massart, Concentration Inequalities (2013), Theorem3.1, printedpages54-55; the iff equality characterization here is independently derived using the finite orthogonal Hoeffding decomposition, rather than attributed to the theorem text.
Independent coordinates, arbitrary measurable state spaces; measurable real f and E Z^2 finite
Each resampling copy independent of original coordinates
Coordinate-infimum application requires a real X_{-i}-measurable infimum; additive equality means equality almost surely

body:
Let X be a real random variable with E[X] > 0. Then P(X = 0) <= Var(X) / (E[X]^2). In particular, if Var(X) = o(E[X]^2), then P(X > 0) -> 1 as the underlying parameter grows.
X has finite variance and positive expectation

body:
Let b>=2 and L>=1 be integers. If the rooted b-ary tree has an injective vertex map into a locally finite graph G with each parent-child image pair at distance at most L, then liminf_{r->infinity}|B_G(f(root),r)|^(1/r)>=b^(1/L)>1. Hence such a map cannot exist in a graph of subexponential volume growth.
b and L are integers with b>=2 and L>=1
G is locally finite
The vertex map is injective
Every parent-child distance is at most the same L
title: Bounded injective branching forces exponential volume

In a bounded simply connected Jordan domain with distinct accessible boundary marks a,b, approximate the domain by mesh-delta honeycomb graphs and assign each self-avoiding a-to-b path probability proportional to x_c to the power of its length, where x_c=1/sqrt(2+sqrt(2)). The conjectured mesh-zero limit is chordal SLE(8/3) from a to b. This restricted-domain formulation is related to, but is not a proved equivalent restatement of, the uniform n-step free-endpoint question P0003.
Bounded Jordan working specialization of Duminil-Copin and Smirnov, Conjecture 1
Consistent accessible boundary approximations

[Corollary dimension:BESQ_difference of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $(a,r) \in (0,\infty)\times {\mathbb R}$ and  $\mathcal S^1$, $\mathcal S^2$ be resp. a ${\rm BESQ}^{\delta_1}$ flow and a ${\rm BESQ}^{\delta_2}$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$. Set $d:=\delta_2-\delta_1$. We suppose that $d\in (0,2)$. Define $T:=\inf\{x\ge r\,:\, \mathcal S^1_{r,x}(a)=0\}$ and 
$$ \mathcal B := \{(b,x):\, \mathcal S^1_{r,x}(a) = \mathcal S^2_{r,x}(a) = b,\, x\le T \}.$$
Then $\mathcal B$ has Hausdorff dimension $\min(2-d,\frac{3-d}{2})$.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2511.09280, 'Random Walk conditioned to stay above a non-flat floor: curvature effects'] Assume the same setting as in Theorem~\ref{thm:unif_curv_free_energy}.
    Let \(\beta\in (0,1/6)\).
    With the same setup as in Theorem~\ref{thm:unif_curv_free_energy}, there are \(n_0,\lambda_0,r_0,C,c_-,c_+>0\) such that, for any \(n\geq n_0\), any \(\lambda\in[\lambda_0,n^\beta]\) and any \(k\in \{n-r_0\sqrt{\lambda}n^{2/3}, \dots, n+r_0\sqrt{\lambda}n^{2/3}\}\),
    \[
        C^{-1}e^{-c_- \lambda^{3/2}}
		\leq P_{0}^{h_n}\bigl(\rS_k \geq \lambda \bigr) \leq Ce^{-c_+ \lambda^{3/2}}.
    \]
    Moreover, there exists \(c>0\) such that
    \[
        \forall \lambda>n^{\beta},\qquad
        P_{0}^{h_n}\bigl(\rS_k \geq \lambda \bigr) \leq e^{-c \lambda}.
    \]
    In particular, for any \(r\geq 0\), there exist \(K_+(r) \geq K_-(r)>0\) such that, for all \(n\geq n_0\),
    \[
        K_-(r) \leq E_0^{h_n}(\rS_k^r) \leq K_+(r)
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        K_-(2) \leq \Var_{P_0^{h_n}}(\rS_k) \leq K_+(2).
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2511.09280

body:
Quantitative functional central limit theorem for the spatial integral of the parabolic Anderson model (Vidotto and Zheng, Theorem 3.6). Let $u$ be the mild solution, with the stochastic integral in the Skorohod sense, of $\partial_t u = \frac{1}{2}\Delta u + u\dot W$ on $\mathbb{R}_+ \times \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \ge 1$), $u(0, x) = 1$, where $\dot W$ is a centered Gaussian noise with $\mathbb{E}[\dot W(t, x)\dot W(s, y)] = \gamma_0(t - s)\gamma_1(x - y)$; here $\gamma_0 : \mathbb{R} \to [0, \infty]$ is nonnegative definite, locally integrable and nontrivial ($\int_0^a \gamma_0(t)\,dt > 0$ for every $a > 0$), and $\gamma_1$ is the Fourier transform of a nonnegative tempered measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying Dalang's condition $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \mu(d\xi)/(1 + |\xi|^2) < \infty$, with $0 < \|\gamma_1\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)} < \infty$. Fix $T \in (0, \infty)$ and let $F_R(t) = \int_{|x| \le R} (u(t, x) - 1)\,dx$, a random element of $K = L^2([0, T])$. Then $d_2(R^{-d/2}F_R, G_R) \le C R^{-d/2}$, where $G_R$ is a centered Gaussian process with the same covariance operator as $R^{-d/2}F_R$, $C$ does not depend on $R$, and $d_2(F, G) = \sup_\phi |\mathbb{E}\phi(F) - \mathbb{E}\phi(G)|$ over twice Frechet differentiable $\phi : K \to \mathbb{R}$ whose first and second derivatives are bounded by $1$. Moreover $R^{-d/2}F_R$ converges in $d_2$, as $R \to \infty$, to the continuous centered Gaussian process $G$ with covariance $\mathbb{E}[G(t)G(s)] = \omega_d \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \operatorname{Cov}(u(t, z), u(s, 0))\,dz$, $\omega_d$ the volume of the unit ball; no rate is given for this convergence.
parabolic Anderson model $\partial_t u=\frac{1}{2}\Delta u+u\dot W$ on $\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathbb{R}^d$, $u(0,x)=1$, mild solution with a Skorohod integral
noise covariance $\gamma_0(t-s)\gamma_1(x-y)$
$\gamma_0$ nonnegative definite, locally integrable, $\int_0^a\gamma_0>0$ for every $a>0$
$\gamma_1$ the Fourier transform of a nonnegative tempered measure $\mu$ with $\int\mu(d\xi)/(1+|\xi|^2)<\infty$
$0<\|\gamma_1\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}<\infty$
$T\in(0,\infty)$, $K=L^2([0,T])$

Let W, X, Y, Z be normed spaces. (a) K(X,Y) is a linear subspace of B(X,Y). (b) If Y is a Banach space, K(X,Y) is closed in B(X,Y) for the operator norm; in particular every operator-norm limit of bounded finite-rank operators X -> Y is compact. (c) If T is in K(X,Y), A in B(W,X) and B in B(Y,Z), then BTA is in K(W,Z). Consequently, for a Banach space X, K(X) is a closed two-sided ideal of the Banach algebra B(X), and the quotient B(X)/K(X) (the Calkin algebra) is a Banach algebra, nonzero exactly when X is infinite-dimensional.
W, X, Y, Z are normed spaces
for the closedness statement (b), Y is a Banach space
A and B are bounded linear operators

Bradley (2005), Question 9, Section 7, PDF p.29 (journal p.135), asks for a necessary and sufficient condition on the spectral density of a real stationary Gaussian sequence for rho*(n) to tend to zero. Here rho* takes the supremum of maximal correlation over any two nonempty coordinate sets S,T with dist(S,T)>=n, allowing interlacing. The survey explicitly calls this open. Current resolution status after limited 2026-10-14 discovery searches is UNKNOWN; no full solution is claimed. A continuous strictly positive spectral density is sufficient, but zeros cannot simply be excluded: a Gaussian MA(1) difference has a spectral zero and rho*(n)=0 for n>=2. Ordinary past-future rho-mixing has a separate classical characterization.
Real stationary Gaussian sequence
Spectral density understood up to almost-everywhere equality

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2608.30059, 'Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations'] If  \(\nu\in M_{\chi_\alpha,\sigma}(E)\)  
admits an admissible product gauge \(\tau\), then   every stochastic
representer of \(\nu\) is concentrated on \(E_\tau\). 
For every \(E\)-valued random element \(Z\) concentrated on \(E_\tau\) 
$
Y_Z\in\Sigma_\tau,   
Z=S_{R_Z}Y_Z
$ almost surely 
and
\begin{align}
\nu_Z(A)
&=
\int_{\Sigma_\tau}K_A(y)\,\mu_Z(dy),
&&A\in\mathcal E,
\\
\mu_Z(D)
&=
\int_{E_\tau}
\chi_\alpha(\tau(x))h_\tau(x)
\1_{\{\Pi_\tau x\in D\}}\,\nu_Z(dx),
&&D\in\mathcal E|_{\Sigma_\tau}.

\end{align}
Moreover  we have 
\begin{equation}

\nu_Z=\nu
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mu_Z=\varsigma_\tau
\end{equation} and hence for any \(Z,W\) concentrated on \(E_\tau\)  
$
\nu_Z=\nu_W$ is equivalent to$ 
\mu_Z=\mu_W.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:admissible solution of arXiv:2606.29622, 'Affine Structure of the Brownian Signature'] A solution $(\bm{u}_t)_{t \in [0, T]}$ to the linear equation (equation eq:heat_eq_coef_sig of the paper) is called It\^o-admissible if $\|\bm u_t\|_{\sigW[s]}$ is a.s. finite for all $(t,s) \in [0\,,T]^2\,$, and for any word ${\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}} \neq {\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{\varnothing}}}\,$, there exists a locally bounded function $f_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}}\colon \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}_+$ such that 
    $$
    \sup_{t \in [0, T]} \left(\|\bm u_t|_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}} \|_{\sigW[s]}\right) \leq f_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}}\left(\sup_{0 \leq r \leq s} |W_r|\right)\,, \quad s \in [0\,,T]\,.
    $$

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:c3489a6711cf336c86cf080dcd2b628ba1e27e0948f5c03e38f1a822eb443ed8","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/c3/c3489a6711cf336c86cf080dcd2b628ba1e27e0948f5c03e38f1a822eb443ed8.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:dfbb846ad820e6514d1a0f68de240c0fd99b58206902c8b47d2c16adc0f9314e","bundle_entry_key":"claim-015","bundle_id":"population.adam-corrected-backward-witness-fullrank-mixed-spectrum-006","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"discrete dynamical systems and adaptive optimization","draft":"w706/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.adam:adam-bias-corrected-p-greater-than-one-rank-one-uniform-tracking-obstruction","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"T421-W706-015 v3; target1; kind special; proof (unaudited).

STATEMENT
For beta1=b=9/10,beta2=d=999/1000, fix any rho_max with
 0<rho_max<rho_star=358811/13673160.
There exists delta(rho_max)>0 such that for
every scalar positive quadratic lambda*x^2/2, eta,epsilon>0 with
 0<rho=epsilon/(eta lambda)<=rho_max,
ordinary time0 separately bias-corrected Adam, epsilon outside sqrt and
standard m0=v0=0, has
 limsup_t |eta C_t-38|>=delta                               (1)
for all but countably many initial x0. Here
C_t=lambda/(sqrt(v_(t+1)/(1-d^(t+1)))+epsilon).
The same is true without bias correction. The constant delta is uniform
in rho in this interval, but existential and potentially very small.

Consequently, for every p>1, fixed lambda>0, any countable eta_n->0,
epsilon_n=eta_n^p, and an absolutely continuous initial x0, almost surely
(1) holds simultaneously for all sufficiently large n. Thus finite
burn-in cannot give eventual o(1/eta) curvature tracking in this regime.
For a rank-one quadratic H=diag(lambda,0), any absolutely continuous law
on R^2 gives the same assertion for ACTIVE curvature: the second gradient
is always zero. For two positive eigenvalues the result applies on the
exact invariant initialization family (x1,0); it does not prove a
full-dimensional positive-definite diagonal theorem. This is a stated
scalar/rank-one obstruction to the tracking variant, not a solution of
the remaining full-rank target. No time-average claim is made.

HARDEST REMAINING TARGET PIECE
The two positive-curvature channels can fluctuate separately while their
weighted active average may partly compensate. This proof does not
classify that average under full-dimensional random initialization.

1. NORMALIZATION AND THE REFLECTED CLOCK MAP
Set X=x/eta,M=m/(eta lambda),V=v/(eta lambda)^2,
alpha=b^(t+1),sigma=d^(t+1). The exact corrected map F_rho is
 M'=bM+(1-b)X, V'=dV+(1-d)X^2,
 X'=X-M'/[(1-alpha)(sqrt(V'/(1-sigma))+rho)],
 alpha'=b alpha, sigma'=d sigma.                            (2)
It commutes with reflection R(X,M,V,alpha,sigma)=(-X,-M,V,alpha,sigma).
Therefore H_rho=R F_rho iterates the alternating frame. At zero clocks,
it fixes p_+=(a,-ca,a^2,0,0) and p_-=R p_+, where
 c=1/19, D=1/38, a=D-rho>0.

Claims003/009 give the physical 3x3 derivative K at p_+ with characteristic
 P_rho(z)=z^3-(28970+760rho)z^2/10000
                  +(27999-684rho)z/10000-8991/10000.
For rho in [0,rho_max], it has exactly one simple stable eigenvalue mu
and two unstable eigenvalues, all bounded away from the unit circle
uniformly on this compact interval. The stable eigenvalue satisfies
 4/5<mu<9/10<d.                                           (3)
Indeed P_rho(4/5)=-(5168rho+63)/50000<0, and
P_rho(9/10)=81(1-38rho)/25000>0 on this interval; the factorizations are
recorded in logs/unstable_window_exact.json. Uniqueness of the inside-disk
root identifies this real root. Spectral count at rho=0 and absence of
unit crossings are proved in claims003/009 by exact algebra.
The complete unstable interval is justified without extrapolating a
numerical stability test. For P_rho, P(1)=19(1-38rho)/5000>0 until
rho=1/38>rho_star, and P(-1)=-(19rho+18990)/2500<0. Put R=8991/10000,
A=(28970+760rho)/10000,B=(27999-684rho)/10000. A nonreal unit pair
requires B-1-R*A+R^2=0, exactly rho=rho_star, and its cosine there is
359801/359820 in(-1,1). Hence there is no unit-circle crossing on
[0,rho_max]. The one-stable/two-unstable count at rho0 is audited in
003/009; it persists throughout this compact interval. The displayed
P(.8)<0<P(.9) bounds identify its unique stable root mu, with .8<mu<.9<d.
Thus every spectral gap used below is uniform for fixed rho_max<rho_star.
These rational identities are checked by scripts/check_unstable_window.py.

The augmented derivative is [[K,C],[0,diag(b,d)]], with three stable
and two unstable eigenvalues.

2. ANALYTIC STABLE GRAPH AND CLOCK FIBERS
The local stable manifold is analytic. For completeness, in adapted
stable/unstable coordinates write H(s,u)=(A s+f(s,u),B u+g(s,u)),
where ||A||<1,||B^-1||<1 and f,g vanish to order2. The analytic graph
u=h(s) solves
 h(s)=B^-1 h(A s+f(s,h(s)))-B^-1 g(s,h(s)).                 (4)
On a small complex ball of radius r, use bounded holomorphic h with
h(0)=Dh(0)=0 and sup||h||<=C r^2. Choose C large and then r small.
The argument of h stays in k r with k<1. The right side maps this ball
to itself and has Lipschitz factor ||B^-1||+O(r)<1: Cauchy estimates
on the smaller ball control the change of its argument. Banach contraction
gives the analytic graph, real on the real slice. The induced stable map
contracts. Graph-relative unstable differences expand by a factor>1,
so any orbit staying in a sufficiently small neighborhood forever lies
on this graph and converges to the fixed point. The details are also
written in proof019; no analytic conclusion is inferred merely from
a C^k center-manifold theorem.

The stable tangent space projects onto both clock coordinates. Its
forced unstable component for any clock vector is solved by the
Sylvester equation between K's unstable restriction and diag(b,d),
whose spectra are disjoint. The kernel of that clock projection is
the physical stable eigendirection. Its X-component is nonzero, as
follows from the second and third rows of K and mu!=d,-b.
Consequently (X,alpha,sigma) are analytic local coordinates on the stable
manifold by the analytic inverse-function theorem. Write it locally as
 M=mathcal M(X,alpha,sigma), V=mathcal V(X,alpha,sigma).
For fixed small clocks its connected local fiber W_(alpha,sigma) is
an analytic arc, parameterized by X in an interval around a. It contains
all sufficiently near captured states at these clocks. At clocks0 this
is the ordinary one-dimensional stable curve of the autonomous H map.

3. AN ADAM-SPECIFIC BACKWARD WITNESS
At the positive phase let P=-M. Parameterize the autonomous stable curve
by X=a+s. Its tangent at s=0 obeys
 dP/dX=(1-b)/(mu+b)>c,
 dV/dX=2(1-d)a/(mu-d)<0,                                  (5)
using (3). Therefore choose any sufficiently small s>0 to obtain a point
w on that local stable curve with the STRICT inequalities
 X>a, P>cX, 0<V<a^2.                                      (6)
This is the witness absent from the generic two-clock counterexample.

For the autonomous reflected map the exact inverse is
 Xold=P/(sqrt(V)+rho)-X,
 Pold=((1-b)Xold-P)/b,
 Vold=(V-(1-d)Xold^2)/d.                                  (7)
As long as a backward state has X>=X_w>a, P>=cX and 0<=V<a^2,
sqrt(V)+rho<c/2. Thus
 Xold>2P/c-X>=P/c>=X,
 Pold>=c Xold,
 Vold<=V.
For the momentum inequality use 1-b-bc=c: Pold>=cXold is equivalent
to cXold>=P. If Vold remains nonnegative these conditions propagate.
With L=X_w^2 and the initial witness variance V_w<L, one also has
 V_(-j)<=L+d^(-j)(V_w-L).                                 (8)
The right side becomes strictly negative at some finite j. Thus w has
NO sufficiently long backward history with nonnegative variances.
The inverse in (7) remains continuous at V=0 because rho>0; a zero
intermediate variance does not evade the strict-negative conclusion
at the next step. Equations (5)-(8) are algebraic inequalities; exact
checks are in scripts/check_backward_cone.py, not floating-point bounds.

Fix this rho and let k be one finite length excluded by (8). This k
may depend on rho; uniform k as rho->0 is unnecessary. Near w and clocks0,
let A_k be the set of augmented states with a physical k-step backward
history, meaning every recovered variance is nonnegative. Restrict clocks
so dividing them by b^k,d^k still leaves them strictly below1. For the
corrected inverse, first recover alpha_old=alpha/b,sigma_old=sigma/d,
undo R on X,M, then use
 Xold=-X-M/[(1-alpha_old)(sqrt(V/(1-sigma_old))+rho)],
 Mold=(-M-(1-b)Xold)/b,
 Vold=(V-(1-d)Xold^2)/d.                                  (9)
These inverses are unique and continuous on the closed nonnegative-
variance domain, including V=0. The set A_k is closed locally: if a
sequence of such histories has convergent output states, recursively
applying (9) makes all k preceding states converge with nonnegative
variances. Denominators stay nonzero by rho>0 and the clock restriction.
Since w is not in A_k, it has an open neighborhood disjoint from A_k.

The selected point on W_(alpha,sigma) with X=X_w varies analytically
with the clocks and tends to w as they vanish. Hence for all sufficiently
small positive clocks this fiber contains a point outside A_k. At time
n the actual clocks are alpha_n=b^(n+1),sigma_n=d^(n+1). For every
sufficiently large n>=k, this selected point cannot lie on Gamma_n,
the finite image of the standard initial line: every state in Gamma_n
has its actual n-step physical history, in particular a k-step one.
The same witness construction at the negative phase follows by reflection.

4. COUNTABLE STANDARD BASIN FOR THE CORRECTED CYCLE
For each finite n, Gamma_n is proper and closed. The raw moment sums
satisfy |M_t|<=K0 sqrt(V_t),
 K0^2=(1-b)^2/[(1-d)(1-b^2/d)].
Corrected normalized step increments have magnitude<=K0/(1-b). Hence
the physical position after n steps differs from X0 by at most
nK0/(1-b); reflection changes only its sign. This gives properness.
The finite fixed-time physical maps are injective by (9), with determinant
bd where V'>0. For X0!=0, V1>0 and all later variances stay positive;
Gamma_n is therefore an embedded real analytic curve away from its
origin. Each local cycle fiber has X near +/-a, so it avoids that origin.

Two analytic embedded curves have locally isolated intersections unless

Let S_n(s)=H_(n-1)...H_0(s,0,0), n>=1.

CLAIM. S_n is continuous, proper and injective on R. On R minus {0}
it is a real-analytic immersion and embedding. Its image is closed in
R^3, and its image away from the origin is an embedded real-analytic
one-dimensional submanifold without boundary of R^3 minus {0}.

1. First step and regularity.
The exact bias corrections give
 S_1(s)=(-s+s/(|s|+rho), -(1-b)s, (1-d)s^2).
It is continuous everywhere, analytic on each open half-line, and its
M derivative is -(1-b), so the derivative is nonzero. For s!=0 the

d>0. All later finite maps are analytic near this trajectory. There is
no assertion of analyticity at zero.

where W>0. Such a derivative cannot annihilate a nonzero tangent, which
proves immersion of S_n at each nonzero s by induction.
For an output (Y,N,Z), the only possible predecessor is
 X=-Y-N/D(Z),
 M=(-N-(1-b)X)/b,
 V=(Z-(1-d)X^2)/d.
These identities show injectivity on the physical domain V>=0, including
zero. They are continuous whenever Z>=0 since rho>0 and alpha,sigma<1.
Since S_0(s)=(s,0,0) is injective, every S_n is injective, and S_n(s)=0
if and only if s=0. The predecessor need not be physical for arbitrary
output; only uniqueness is used here.

3. A uniform bound on each corrected position increment.
Use the unreflected normalized variables x_j,m_j,v_j with m_0=v_0=0.
The moment sums at step k>=1 are
 m_k=(1-b) sum_(j=0)^(k-1) b^(k-1-j) x_j,
 v_k=(1-d) sum_(j=0)^(k-1) d^(k-1-j) x_j^2.

# Uniform local capture from bounded forward orbits
Supplement to T421-W706-015 v3 Section5 and proof062.
Kind: special; target1. Status: proof (unaudited).
Classical finite-dimensional hyperbolic argument, not a claimed new theorem.

LEMMA. Let I be compact and F_r a family of C1 maps on common-radius
neighborhoods of fixed points p_r in R^N. Suppose p_r, J_r=DF_r(p_r)
are continuous, J_r is invertible and hyperbolic for every r in I,
and the derivatives of F_r are jointly continuous near the fixed points.
Then some epsilon>0, independent of r, has this property: every forward
orbit staying in the Euclidean epsilon-ball about p_r for all n>=0
converges to p_r. Staying in a ball is a hypothesis, not a conclusion
that all points of the ball are trapped.

1. Uniform hyperbolic norms.
Translate p_r to zero. Hyperbolicity and compactness put all stable
spectra in |z|<q0 and all inverse unstable spectra in |z|<q0 for some
q0<1. Choose q with q0<q<1. The Riesz projectors P_s(r),P_u(r)
are continuous, commute with J_r and have constant ranks on each connected
component. Uniform resolvent bounds on a circle of radius between q0
and q give uniformly geometric bounds on J_r^k P_s(r) and
J_r^(-k) P_u(r). This follows directly from the matrix Cauchy integral
formula; one can use J_r P_s(r) and J_r^(-1) P_u(r) on the full space,
whose other eigenvalues are zero. The contour is uniformly separated
from their spectra on the compact parameter set, so its resolvent norm
has a finite maximum. No diagonalization or simple-eigenvalue assumption
is needed.
Define for z=s+u, s=P_s z, u=P_u z,
 |s|_s=sum_(k>=0) q^(-k) ||J_r^k s||_2,
 |u|_u=sum_(k>=0) q^(-k) ||J_r^(-k) u||_2,
 |z|_r=max(|s|_s,|u|_u).
The series converge uniformly on bounded vectors and parameters. There
exist constants m,M>0 independent of r with
 m||z||_2<=|z|_r<=M||z||_2.
For the lower bound, ||z||_2<=||s||_2+||u||_2<=2|z|_r,
so m=1/2 works. The geometric bounds give M. Moreover
 |J_r s|_s<=q|s|_s, |J_r^(-1)u|_u<=q|u|_u.

2. Extend the small nonlinear remainder.
Write F_r(z)=J_r z+f_r(z), f_r(0)=Df_r(0)=0. The jointly continuous
derivative and uniform norm equivalence give a common R>0 such that
on the |.|_r ball of radius R, f_r is L-Lipschitz in this norm,
where 0<L<(1-q)/2 can be prescribed. Indeed choose a common Euclidean
ball with sup ||Df_r||_2 <= L*m/M; choose R/m below its radius, and
integrate the derivative on segments. The norm-ball is convex.
Let P_R(z)=z*min(1,R/|z|_r), with P_R(0)=0. Radial clipping has
Lipschitz constant at most2 in any norm. To see this, order |x|>=|y|:
if both are outside, split (R/|x|)(x-y) plus
R*(1/|x|-1/|y|)*y; each term is bounded by |x-y|.
If only x is outside, split (R/|x|)(x-y) plus
(R/|x|-1)y; the second norm is at most |x|-R<=|x|-|y|
<=|x-y|. Both-inside is immediate.
Thus g_r=f_r composed with P_R is globally 2L-Lipschitz, vanishes at
zero and equals f_r on this ball. Its projected components have the
same Lipschitz bound in their respective block norms.

3. Bounded-sequence fixed point.
Fix a stable initial coordinate s0. On bounded sequences z=(z_n)_(n>=0),
with sup block norm, define
 (Tz)_n^s=J_s^n s0+sum_(j=0)^(n-1) J_s^(n-1-j) P_s g_r(z_j),
 (Tz)_n^u=-sum_(j=n)^infty J_u^(n-1-j) P_u g_r(z_j).
Here negative powers of J_u are well-defined. The unstable sum uses
powers J_u^(-1),J_u^(-2),..., so its norm sum is q/(1-q);
the stable sum has norm sum at most1/(1-q). Hence
 Lip(T)<=2L/(1-q)<1.
The operator maps the complete bounded-sequence space to itself and
therefore has exactly one fixed point.
The subspace c0 of sequences tending to zero is closed and T-invariant:
J_s^n s0 tends to zero; the stable convolution tends to zero by splitting
a finite initial segment from a uniformly small tail; the unstable
convolution is bounded by q/(1-q) times sup_(j>=n)|g_r(z_j)|, tending
to zero. Banach contraction on c0 gives a fixed point in c0. Uniqueness
in the larger bounded-sequence space identifies both fixed points.

Every bounded orbit z_(n+1)=J_r z_n+g_r(z_n) satisfies these equations.
The stable formula is finite variation of constants. For the unstable
formula, solve backward from time N:
 u_n=J_u^(-(N-n))u_N-sum_(j=n)^(N-1)J_u^(n-1-j)P_u g_r(z_j).
The first term tends to zero as N tends to infinity because u_N is
bounded and ||J_u^(-k)||<=q^k in the block norm. Thus the orbit is the
unique fixed point for its s0, and converges to zero.
Take epsilon<R/M. An original orbit staying in the Euclidean epsilon-ball
stays in the norm-ball where g_r=f_r, so this conclusion applies.
This proves the lemma with no need for analytic graph regularity.

4. Application and audit boundaries.
For015 use the augmented reflected Adam map of060 and I=[0,rho_max],
rho_max<rho_star. Its phases satisfy a=1/38-rho>=a_min>0.
There is a common neighborhood where raw updated variance stays positive,
1-alpha and 1-sigma stay away from zero, and the square-root denominator
stays positive even at rho=0. Thus maps and derivatives are jointly
analytic there. The audited spectral computations003/009, extended as
specified in015, give one stable physical root, two unstable physical
multipliers, and the additional stable clocks b,d. The determinant is
b^2 d^2>0 by060. Subject to independent audit of these spectral inputs,
the lemma supplies a common local capture radius epsilon. Reflection
gives the same conclusion at the other phase.

Taking r=epsilon in062 closes its conditional local-capture implication:
a sufficiently narrow eventual scalar curvature band forces convergence
to the reflected cycle. It does not give a basin of positive measure;
only orbits that stay in the ball are covered. The countable standard
basin and full-rank021 argument remain separately subject to audit.
No uniform global backward inverse, burn-in time or witness length at
rho=0 is inferred. No new scored frontier move is claimed.

1. Precise continuation lemma and its load-bearing hypotheses.
Let W be a connected embedded real analytic arc in a finite-dimensional
real analytic ambient space. Let Gamma be closed in that space and an
embedded real analytic curve in a neighborhood of each point of W
that belongs to Gamma. If some w_star in W is not in Gamma, then
Gamma intersect W is discrete in W and hence countable.

To prove this, let E be the set of points of W that have a relative
W-neighborhood contained in Gamma. E is open by definition. It is also
closed in W. Indeed, if w_j in E tends to w in W, closedness of Gamma
first gives w in Gamma. Near w, analytic embeddedness of Gamma supplies
analytic local defining functions of full codimension. Parameterize W
analytically near w. Each composed defining function vanishes on the
small arcs near w_j; the one-variable real analytic identity theorem
forces it to vanish near w. Thus w is in E. Connectedness now implies
that either E is empty or E=W. The witness w_star excludes E=W.
If Gamma intersect W had an accumulation point in W, closedness would
put that point in Gamma and the same local argument would make E
nonempty, contradiction. Thus the intersection is discrete. Since W
is second countable, choose for each isolated intersection point a
basic open set containing no other intersection point; distinct points
can be assigned distinct such basic sets, proving countability.
No analytic defining equation across the entire parameter line is used.

Closedness cannot be dropped: in R^2 take Gamma={(x,0):0<x<1} and
W={(x,0):0<x<2}. Both are embedded analytic arcs, and (3/2,0) is a
point of W outside Gamma, but their intersection contains an interval.
This is a control for the lemma's hypothesis, not a counterexample to015:
015 explicitly supplies closedness by properness of its finite image.

2. Applying exactly this lemma to015 Section4.
At fixed sufficiently late time n, Gamma_n is the image of the full
standard initialization line under the fixed-clock finite Adam map.
Under015's bounded-increment estimate its position differs from the
initial position by at most n*K0/(1-b), up to reflection. Hence the
parametrization is proper: an unbounded initial sequence cannot have
bounded image. Continuity gives closedness of the image. The finite
inverse is injective on the physical nonnegative-variance history,
and on nonzero initializations the updated variance is strictly positive.
Thus its image is an embedded analytic curve away from the full origin.

The fixed-clock local stable fiber W is an analytic arc in X near the
nonzero cycle amplitude. It avoids the full origin.015 Section3 provides
an interior witness w_star of that same connected fiber that has no
physical k-step prehistory, whereas every Gamma_n point has such a
prehistory when n>=k. Thus w_star is outside Gamma_n. The preceding
lemma applies with precisely those hypotheses and makes the
intersection discrete. Injectivity of the finite map gives at most
one standard initial value per intersection point. A countable union
over sufficiently late integers n and the two phases stays countable.
This is the properness-and-local-continuation argument; nonidentity
at a point outside an unspecified analytic-chart domain would not suffice.

3. Exact finite sign check used by015 Section5.
With b=9/10, after the magnitude estimate |X_t|=a+O(delta)+o(1)
where a is uniformly bounded below by a positive constant,015 obtains
 s_(t+1)+(1+b)*s_t+b*s_(t-1)=O(delta)+o(1).
There are exactly eight triples of signs in {-1,1}^3. The two alternating
triples have residual0. The remaining six have residual absolute values
9/5,2 or19/5. Therefore an eventual error strictly smaller than9/10
excludes every nonalternating triple. The strict inequality is harmless
and stronger than the needed error<9/5. Normalization by a requires
the explicit positive lower bound on a; it is not uniform as a->0.
The compact parameter range rho<=rho_max<rho_star supplies that bound.

CLEAN for the continuation lemma and the finite sign enumeration.
The implications in015 Sections3-5 are consistent with these checks,
conditional on its analytic stable fibers, physical inverse/witness,
bounded-increment estimate and uniform spectral/graph bounds. This note
does not independently audit those inputs or turn015/021 into checked
proofs. It isolates why the closed finite image is needed and certifies
the finite sign gap rather than treating analytic intersections as
countable without excluding an entire common arc.

Owner-own-work complete proof draft (unaudited), no novelty priority claimed. In the explicit-query Boolean oracle model there exists one oracle O with NP^O not contained in P^O/poly, while every fixed uniform polynomial-time O-relative nonnegative polynomial-bit rational weight family with positive normalizers has polynomial-size O-relative AR approximations Q_L with polynomial-bit dyadic next-symbol probabilities and KL(P_L||Q_L)<=L^(-c), for every fixed positive integer c, at all sufficiently large lengths. Finite exceptions can be hardwired nonuniformly. The construction uses independent unique hidden row witnesses, nested random masks with per-step fraction 2^(-floor(n^(1/3))^2) and depth floor(floor(n^(1/3))/4), and helper queries padded to at least the fourth power of the simulated clock. Helpers discard any computation that queries a newly masked row. Shorter helpers depend only on ancestor masks, giving a conditional normalized-mass bound for arbitrary weights. Small blocks exhaust their masks; every fixed polynomial query length leaves exponentially many random NP bits hidden. An adaptive membership-query transcript bound preserves circuit hardness. This is a direct construction, does not invoke IR2, and does not claim the stronger heuristic-NP hypothesis H. Independent review of fresh-mask conditioning is pending.
Uniform rational efficient-weight families, positive normalizers, usual explicit-query polynomial-time oracle model.
Oracle circuit size bounds query count and query length; next-bit probabilities have polynomially many bits.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e7efd8b61a5711af4d596bc1d1c7e829fa34028b3da8963bdc574ef24e27fd99","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e7/e7efd8b61a5711af4d596bc1d1c7e829fa34028b3da8963bdc574ef24e27fd99.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ab3e0d456eec312f400026ee069accd756c086ac9b4030e67a8dd377b5d207ba","bundle_entry_key":"autoregressive-forward-kl-padded-mask-oracle-separation","bundle_id":"population.t410-padded-nested-mask-oracle-separation-v1","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"oracle complexity; average-case complexity; autoregressive models; forward KL; random masks","draft":"w739/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:autoregressive-forward-kl-padded-mask-oracle-separation","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# A padded, nested-mask oracle for the forward-KL separation

T410-w739-C015 v1. Target: 2. Kind: moved.
Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty priority is claimed. This is a direct
oracle construction, rather than an invocation of the reported IR2 oracle.
It does not assert the additional, unnecessary hypothesis H of C013.

## Statement and model

There exists one Boolean oracle O such that NP^O is not contained in
P^O/poly, but for every fixed uniform polynomial-time O-relative family of
nonnegative rational weights w_L(x), |x|=L, with polynomial output bit length
and positive normalizer, and every fixed positive integer c, there are
polynomial-size O-relative AR models Q_L with polynomial-bit dyadic next-bit
probabilities satisfying KL(P_L||Q_L)<=L^{-c} for all sufficiently large L.
Finite exceptions can be hardwired into nonuniform models. Polynomial time
uses the usual explicit-query oracle model: writing a query of length q
costs at least q steps; oracle circuit size bounds query length and count.
The quantifier over weight families is uniform. No polynomial-time compiler
with instance-uniform approximation guarantees is asserted.

The hardest step is compatibility: a weight computation can read smaller
helper queries, but those queries must reveal no information about the
fresh mask used to truncate that weight. Sections 3 and 4 prove this step.

## 1. Base table and random masks

For every y of length n>=2, independently choose a uniform bit b_y and a
uniform n^2-bit string z_y. The unique accepted witness in row y is b_y z_y.
The base interface B(y,w) is 1 exactly for this witness, and 0 otherwise.
Encode a base query with an initial tag and self-delimited y,w, so its length
is at least n^2. Invalid encodings answer 0. The finitely many shorter rows
can be fixed arbitrarily. In particular

    A={y: there exists z in {0,1}^{n^2}, B(y,1z)=1}

is in NP^O, and its length-n truth bits are the independent bits b_y.

Independently of the entire base table, choose masks as follows. Put
a_n=floor(n^{1/3}), g_n=max(1,floor(a_n/4)), H_{n,0}={0,1}^n. For
1<=j<g_n, choose H_{n,j} uniformly among the subsets of H_{n,j-1} of size
2^{n-j*a_n^2}. These integer sizes are valid: j*a_n^2<=n/4. Choices for
different n are independent; successive choices use their conditional
uniform laws. Put H_{n,j}=empty for j>=g_n. A nonempty-mask step has
conditional per-row probability delta_n=2^{-a_n^2}. For fixed D, eventually
g_n>D and |H_{n,D}|=2^{n-D*a_n^2}>=2^{floor(n/2)}.

All random variables form a countable product of finite probability spaces.

## 2. Helper queries, defined by induction on their actual length

The other interface is a padded helper query of actual length N. Its fields
are a deterministic machine description M, input length L, unary clock T,
integers a,p, a prefix h with |h|<L, and a bit index j<=p. Require p>=2,
a>=1, all fields fit in a header of length at most T^2, L,p,a,|M|<=T,
and T^4<=N. Remaining padding is zero. Invalid requests answer 0.
The actual length N is a parameter of the helper, not just padding ignored
by its meaning. One AR model will use the SAME N at every prefix and digit.

For this helper define k(N,n)=max(1,floor(log_n N)), n>=2, using exact
integer comparisons, and let K_n=H_{n,k(N,n)}. Simulate M for at most T
steps on each L-bit x, using the actual answers to all helper queries it
makes. Such queries have length at most T<=N^{1/4}<N; they have already
been defined by the induction. Base queries are answered from B, except
that the entire simulation is discarded as soon as it queries ANY base
row y in K_{|y|}. On a nondiscarded terminating run, decode its output as a
nonnegative rational weight; invalid or negative outputs have weight zero.
Call the resulting finite weight v_N(x). Let R_N be its normalized law if
its sum is positive, and uniform otherwise.

Let alpha=2^{-a}, S_N=(1-alpha)R_N+alpha U_L. For the requested prefix h,
form the exact next-one probability s=S_N(h1)/S_N(h). Round down to the
grid of mesh 2^{-p} and clip the numerator to [1,2^p-1]. Return digit j
of the resulting p-bit numerator. This defines one Boolean oracle, by
induction on N, for every realization of the base table and masks. All sums
are finite; the oracle has no computational-time restriction. Arbitrary
rational denominators therefore cause no definitional problem. For each
fixed query the recursion is finite and the answer is measurable.

Two facts are useful. First, truncation can be described on the untruncated
reference run: v_N(x) equals its reference weight if none of that run's base
rows lies in K, and equals zero otherwise. To see this, compare the runs up
to their first visit to K. Second, truncation is a subweight for EVERY M;
no monotonicity of M's original weight in oracle answers is assumed.

## 3. Dependency and fresh-mask lemma

If a helper of length N can access base block n, even indirectly, then
n^2<=T<=N^{1/4}. Thus log_n N>=8. Put k=floor(log_n N). Any smaller helper
called by its simulated machine has length N'<=T, and, if it can access n,

    k(N',n)<=floor((log_n N)/4)<=floor((k+1)/4)<=k-1.

If N'<n^8, it cannot access block n at all: its clock is smaller than n^2,
and its recursive helper queries are shorter still. These assertions follow
by the same induction on actual query length used in the definition.

Consequently, for an active current mask H_{n,k} (k<g_n), every helper
query of length at most T depends on masks of that block only through
H_{n,0},...,H_{n,k-1}. It depends on the base table in that block only outside
H_{n,k-1}. More generally a helper of length N depends on block n only
through masks up to k(N,n) and base entries outside H_{n,k(N,n)}; if it
cannot access that block it has no dependency on it at all. This follows
inductively because a current simulation aborts before reading any masked
row, and every called helper has an ancestor mask containing the current
mask. Uniform fallbacks, sums, smoothing and rounding preserve this property.

For fixed N,M,L,T, condition on the entire base table and, in each active
block n, the ancestor masks through k(N,n)-1. Condition also on the complete
mask chains of inactive blocks, whose current masks are empty. All helper
answers at lengths at most T are then fixed. The current active child masks
retain their conditional uniform laws, independently across blocks. In
particular their per-row conditional inclusion probabilities are at most
delta_n. This remains true even though the reference weight law depends
arbitrarily on the base table and the already constructed helpers.

Let u(x) be the NONTRUNCATED weight of M with this base table and these
actual shorter helpers, and suppose Z=sum u>0. For each fixed x its reference
trace has at most T base-query rows. The conditional union bound gives

 E[ (Z-sum v_N)/Z | reference data ]
       <= T * max{delta_n: k(N,n)<g_n and n^2<=T}.                 (1)

An empty maximum is zero. The reference law u/Z is already fixed under this
conditioning, so there is NO assumption that a tiny old prefix mass remains
tiny after a new witness is planted. No witness planting takes place.

## 4. The maximum in (1) decreases faster than every inverse power of N

For an active n, writing a=a_n, we have

 log_2 N < (k(N,n)+1) log_2 n <= g_n log_2 n
          <= (3a/4) log_2(a+1).

As N increases, the minimum a of an active block tends to infinity: bounded
a allows only finitely many n, each with a finite threshold n^{g_n} beyond
which its mask is empty. Thus uniformly over active blocks

 a^2/log_2 N >= 4a/[3 log_2(a+1)] -> infinity.

It follows that for every fixed K, the maximum delta_n in (1) is eventually
at most N^{-K}. The extra factor T<=N^{1/4} can be absorbed by increasing K.
This is the purpose of the cubic-root mask depth and square cubic-root
erasure exponent: the masks eventually exhaust at small blocks, while every
fixed polynomial query length still leaves exponentially many hidden rows
at the corresponding large block.

## 5. Forward-KL models for every uniform efficient-weight family

Fix one uniform weight machine M and a clock T_L polynomial in L which
bounds its runtime and output bit length on the actual oracle. Increase the
clock to bound L,p,a and the header. Taking a polynomial clock with fixed
coefficient and exponent is allowed; there are countably many such choices.
Invalid or negative output clipping does not change the target weights.

For a fixed desired exponent c>=1, put ell=ceil(log_2 L), L>=2,
a=(c+4)ell, p=L+a+(c+5)ell+2. Choose N_L=T_L^4, increasing T_L if necessary
so its padded header fits. All queries for this model use this same N_L.
Its reference weight is exactly w_L, because its shorter helper queries are
the actual final-oracle queries, already fixed by the induction.

Write r_L=(Z_L-sum v_{N_L})/Z_L. From (1) and section 4, for every K the
unconditional E r_L is eventually at most N_L^{-K}<=L^{-K}. Markov's
inequality with epsilon_L=L^{-(c+4)} makes Pr[r_L>epsilon_L] summable.
The first Borel-Cantelli lemma implies r_L<=epsilon_L eventually, almost
surely. No independence between lengths is used. Intersect these
probability-one events over the countably many machines, polynomial clocks
and integers c. If a candidate machine has zero reference normalizer, define
r_L=0 for the probability estimate; the claimed conclusion is used only at
lengths with positive normalizer. Conditional on the reference data the
normalizer is fixed, so this convention preserves the estimate.

On the good event, R_{N_L} is the target conditioned on its nondiscarded
reference computations. For r=r_L, write

    P_L=(1-r)R_{N_L}+r W

with some law W (choose it arbitrarily if r=0). Finite log-sum, with the
component label retained and then discarded, gives

 KL(P_L || S_{N_L}) <= d(r||alpha)+r KL(W||U_L)
   <= log(1/(1-alpha)) + r [L log 2 + log(1/alpha)].              (2)

Here alpha=2^{-a}<=L^{-(c+4)}, and a<= (c+4)(log_2 L+1). On the good
event (2) is O_c(L^{-(c+3)}).

At every prefix, both next-bit probabilities of S_{N_L} are at least
alpha*2^{-L}, since the corresponding joint prefix probabilities have that
lower bound and the conditioning prefix probability is at most 1. Rounding
and clipping change each next-bit probability by at most 2^{-p}. Therefore
the relative decrease is at most

    beta=2^{L+a-p}<=L^{-(c+5)}/4.

For beta<=1/2, each log likelihood ratio from S to its rounded AR model is
at most -log(1-beta)<=2 beta. Summing over L symbols adds at most 2L beta
to (2), for ANY target law. The resulting KL is eventually at most L^{-c}.

The model retrieves p digits for each requested next probability from the
same padded helper. N_L,T_L,p are polynomial in L; writing all the queries
and unrolling the computation gives polynomial-size oracle circuits and
polynomial-bit dyadic probabilities. This even gives a fixed uniform model
construction per M, clock and c, with an eventual guarantee. No distribution
sampler, target CDF, partition-function algorithm or instance-uniform compiler
is needed. A finite set of exceptional lengths can be represented by
nonuniform hardwiring with one larger constant size bound.

## 6. Circuit hardness survives every helper

Fix d>=1 and a sufficiently large n. Set D=d+2. The mask H_{n,D} has at
least h=2^{floor(n/2)} rows. Select its lexicographically first h rows.
Fix all masks and the base table outside these rows. By section 3 every
helper query of length at most n^d is now fixed independently of the h
remaining pairs (b_y,z_y): any helper that can read this block has mask
index at most floor(log_n n^d)<=d, and hence its mask contains H_{n,D}.

Here is the needed elementary direct-product bound. An arbitrary
deterministic procedure may make at most Q membership queries to h rows,
each with an independent uniform pair (b_i,z_i) in {0,1} times [M], and
then predict all h bits. Other oracle answers are fixed independently of
these pairs. Its probability of predicting the entire bit vector correctly
is at most

    2^{-h}(1+1/M)^Q <= 2^{-h} exp(Q/M).                         (3)

Proof: memoize repeated queries. After the first positive answer in a row,
its complete row is known and future queries to it can be simulated locally.
Thus at most one actual positive answer is needed per row. A response
transcript is specified by a subset of at most Q positions for its positive
answers. If it has k positives, these are in distinct rows and prescribe
their (b_i,z_i), probability (2M)^{-k}. The final guessed bits prescribe
the remaining h-k independent b_i, with probability 2^{-(h-k)}. Ignore
negative-answer constraints, which can only increase this probability.
For this transcript and successful prediction the bound is 2^{-h}M^{-k}.
Summing over the at most binomial(Q,k) possible position sets and then over
k proves (3). This argument is valid for adaptive queries: fixing the
response positions fixes each queried cell and the final predictions.

For any size-n^d circuit, evaluate it on all 2^n inputs in a fixed order.
This is one procedure with Q<=2^n n^d relevant membership queries; all other
answers, including ALL its helper answers, are fixed as above. Use
M=2^{n^2}. Hence Q/M tends to zero. A correct circuit must predict all h
selected bits, and has conditional success probability bounded by (3).

There are at most 2^{poly_d(n)} circuits of size n^d, even allowing arbitrary
oracle gates with query lengths bounded by that size: encode at most n^d
gates and at most n^d input wires at each gate. A generous encoding uses
O(n^{2d} log(n+2)) bits. Union bounding (3) over all these circuits gives a
summable sequence of failure probabilities, since h=2^{floor(n/2)}.
The bound is independent of the fixed masks and exterior table, so it also
holds unconditionally. Borel-Cantelli, followed by a countable intersection
over d, shows that almost surely A is not in P^O/poly.

## 7. One common oracle, status and review boundary

Sections 5 and 6 each describe probability-one events in the SAME product
space of base tables and mask chains, with the helper oracle determined
from those variables by the SAME length induction. Their intersection has
probability one and is nonempty. Select an oracle in that intersection.
It has both required properties, proving the stated Target 2 separation
for the uniform rational-weight interpretation of the dossier.

The independent reviewer should check especially section 3's joint
conditioning argument: a shorter helper must depend only on ancestors of
every current active mask, including when it internally ranges over every
possible input and prefix. No earlier verdict or unpublished IR2 proof is
being used. All probability bounds above are analytic; finite diagnostics
can check the clock inequalities and small direct-product cases but cannot
certify the infinite construction. body: Let T be an index set, and suppose that for every finite subset (t_1,...,t_n) of T we are given a probability measure mu_{t_1,...,t_n} on (R^n, Borel sets), such that this family is consistent: it is invariant under permuting the t_i together with the corresponding coordinates, and marginalizing mu_{t_1,...,t_n,t_{n+1}} over the last coordinate returns mu_{t_1,...,t_n}. Then there is a probability space carrying a stochastic process (X_t)_{t in T} whose finite-dimensional distributions are exactly this family, and this process is unique in law. Due to Andrey Kolmogorov.

h: Z^d -> [0, infinity) subadditive: h(x+y) <= h(x) + h(y)
h(x) <= r|x| for all x and some r > 0
g(x) := lim_n h(nx)/n (the limit exists by subadditivity, and g(x) <= h(x) always)
CHAP with exponent a > 0 and correction phi in Phi (positive nondecreasing on (1,infinity))
no probabilistic hypothesis whatsoever

THE TWO PROPERTIES, VERBATIM FROM THE SURVEY.
  Good increments: Q_x(a,phi) := { y in Z^d : h(y) <= g_x(y) + |x|^a phi(|x|) and g_x(y) <= g(x) }, the second condition being there to prevent overshooting the increment.
  CHAP (convex hull approximation property): h satisfies CHAP with exponent a and correction phi if there is L > 1 such that x/alpha lies in Co(Q_x(a,phi)) for some alpha in [1,L], for all rational x with |x| large enough.
  GAP (general approximation property): there are M > 1 and C > 0 with g(x) <= h(x) <= g(x) + C|x|^a phi(|x|) for all x with |x| >= M.
READ THE DIRECTION CORRECTLY: g(x) <= h(x) is free from subadditivity; Alexander's content is the REVERSE inequality, an upper bound on how far h can sit above its own limit. A quotation that reports 'Alexander's bound' as though it were two-sided has claimed the trivial half as part of the theorem.
WHAT IT IS FOR: applied to h(y) = E T(0,y), whose limit g is the time constant, it converts a 'good skeleton path' condition into a rate of convergence to the limit shape. The FPP payoff is a separate application with its own probabilistic hypotheses - see the non-random-fluctuation state-of-the-art node.
SOURCE: Alexander, K. (1997), 'Approximation of subadditive functions and convergence rates in limiting-shape results', Ann. Probab., 30-55. (The survey bibliography prints the volume as '1', which looks like a typo; lane P4 did not verify the volume number.) Statement and both definitions read in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), subsection "Alexander's method", tex lines 2014-2033.
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim. Lane P4 did not read Alexander (1997).
title: Alexander (1997), Theorem 1.8: if h is a non-negative SUBADDITIVE function on Z^d with h(x) <= r|x| for some r > 0, and h satisfies the convex hull approximation property CHAP with exponent a > 0 and correction phi, then h satisfies the general approximation property GAP with the same exponent and correction, that is g(x) <= h(x) <= g(x) + C |x|^a phi(|x|) where g(x) = lim_n h(nx)/n. The theorem is purely deterministic - no probability enters it.

Write $\sigma(A(z)) = \{\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k\}$, let $V_1,\dots,V_k$ be the corresponding generalized eigenspaces, and suppose $w \in \mathbb{R}^n$ satisfies $w = \sum_{i=1}^k v_i$ for $v_i \in V_i$.     $$P_\eta(z)w \coloneqq \sum_{\{i \mid \Re \lambda_i \geq \lambda(A(z)) - \eta\}} v_i \,.$$

\nu is the future-directed timelike unit normal
title: Spacelike Mean Curvature Flow in Lorentzian Manifolds

body: In mathematics, a sheaf is a tool for systematically tracking data attached to the open sets of a topological space and defined locally with regard to them. For example, for each open set, the data could be the ring of continuous functions defined on that open set. Such data are well-behaved in that they can be restricted to smaller open sets, and also the data assigned to an open set are equivalent to all collections of compatible data assigned to collections of smaller open sets covering the original open set.
title: Sheaf (mathematics)

AUTHOR-DERIVED, UNREVIEWED exact finite witness. In the independent standard-Gaussian quadrant polymer with two vertices per path, the two paths share the origin and choose either (1,0) or (0,1). M_2=g_0+max(g_1,g_2). With OU time t>=0 and g_t=e^(-t)g+sqrt(1-e^(-2t))g' for independent g', the expected number of shared maximizing-path vertices is R_2(t)=3/2+arcsin(e^(-t))/pi, and Var(M_2)=2-1/pi. Thus R_2(t)>=3/2 and its independent-environment limit is 3/2. A bound R_2(t)<=C exp(-c t) for all t with finite C and c>0 is false. Centered-overlap estimates must also account for the first-chaos variance floor. This is a proof-step counterexample, not a disproof of polynomial variance improvement.

[Proposition prop: existence for discrete systems of arXiv:2411.05924, 'Non-negative Martingale Solutions to the Stochastic Porous Medium Equation with Sticky Beh'] For each $n\in\mathbb N$ there exists a stochastic basis $(\Omega, \mathcal F, \mathbb F, \mathbb P)$ supporting a $U$--valued $Q$--Wiener process $W$ and an $\mathbb R^n$-valued process $\mathbf u_n$ which satisfies the SDE (equation eq: discrete dynamics Rn of the paper) on $[0,\tau_n]$ and which is constant on $[\tau_n, T]$, where 
    \[
        \tau_n := T \wedge \inf \{ t \geq 0: \mathscr E_n(\mathbf u_n(t)) \geq h_n^{-\kappa} \}.
    \]
    We call the triple $((\Omega, \mathcal F, \mathbb F, \mathbb P), \mathbf u_n, W)$ a \emph{martingale solution} to (equation eq: discrete dynamics Rn of the paper).

body: Let (F_t)_{t >= 0} be a filtration satisfying the usual conditions. An adapted, right-continuous with left limits (cadlag) process (M_t)_{t >= 0} with M_0 finite is a local martingale if there exists a sequence of stopping times tau_n increasing to infinity almost surely such that, for each n, the stopped process M^{tau_n}_t = M_{t and tau_n} is a true martingale. Every true martingale is a local martingale, but a local martingale need not be a true martingale unless an additional integrability condition, such as uniform integrability of the family {M_{t and tau_n}}, holds. [standard, e.g. Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion]
title: Local Martingale

For integer n>=1, let L_n=n, K_n=2^(n^2) singleton paths of unit weight, all X_i equal one shared N(0,1) variable Z, and beta_n=n. The covariance is PSD with maximum diagonal 1. Then log D_xi=xi Z but F_beta_n(xi X)=xi Z-n*log 2, so the normalized hard-min mean is 0 and normalized soft-min mean is -log 2, for every fixed xi>=0. Thus beta_n->infinity alone does not transfer individual soft-min levels uniformly in network size. This xi-independent bias cancels in endpoint differences; the example is not an endpoint-difference counterexample or a planar LFPP model.

[Proposition prop:goodset of arXiv:2507.10531, 'Quantitative central limit theorems for exponential random graphs'] For all small enough $\varepsilon > 0$, there are some $\eta, \gamma > 0$ such that for all large enough $n$ there is a set
$\Lambda^* \subseteq \mathcal{B}_p^\eta$ satisfying the following properties, where $X \sim \mu_\mathsf{H}^\eta(n,p)$ and $(X_t^x)$ is the
Glauber dynamics conditioned on $\mathcal{B}_p^\eta$ and started at $x$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Roman*)]
    \item
    
    The set $\Lambda^*$ is large, i.e.\ we have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{P}[X \in \Lambda^*] \geq 1 - e^{-\gamma n}.
    \end{equation}
    \item
    
    The chain started near $\Lambda^*$ stays in the good region.
    Namely, whenever $\mathbf{d}_\mathrm{Ham}(x,\Lambda^*) \leq 1$,
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{P}\mleft[X_t^x \in \Gamma_p^\varepsilon \cap \mathcal{B}_p^{\eta/2} \text{ for all } t < e^{\gamma n}\mright] \geq 1 - e^{-\gamma n}.
    \end{equation}
    \item
    
    The set $\Lambda^*$ is connected under the nearest-neighbor relation.
    Moreover, for any $x,x' \in \Lambda^*$, we have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf{d}_{\Lambda^*}(x,x') \leq 2 n^2,
    \end{equation}
    where $\mathbf{d}_{\Lambda^*}(x,x')$ denotes the distance within $\Lambda^*$, i.e.\ the length of the shortest nearest-neighbor
    path between $x,x'$ which stays inside $\Lambda^*$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 5.9 of \cite{winstein2025concentration}

body: For first-order logic, Godel's completeness theorem states that a formula is provable from a set of axioms by a standard formal proof system if and only if it is semantically entailed by those axioms, that is, true in every model satisfying them. Equivalently, every syntactically consistent set of first-order sentences has a model. Thus first-order provability and first-order semantic truth coincide, so the usual first-order proof systems are sound and complete; this does not extend to second-order logic under its standard semantics. Proved by Kurt Godel in his 1929 doctoral dissertation.
title: Godel's completeness theorem

body: Let A be an n by n complex matrix with entries a_ij. For each row i, the Gershgorin disc D_i is the closed disc in the complex plane centered at the diagonal entry a_ii with radius R_i equal to the sum of the absolute values of the other, off-diagonal entries in row i. Every eigenvalue of A lies in at least one disc D_i. Moreover, if a union of k of these discs is disjoint from the remaining n-k discs, that union contains exactly k eigenvalues of A counted with multiplicity, and the complementary union contains the rest. Proved by Semyon Gershgorin in 1931.
title: Gershgorin circle theorem
