The following worker proof addresses the free global mode and retains no claim of priority or full-problem acceptance.

Label: proof (worker checked), independent audit pending w346. No novelty or full-problem solution certificate. The mode here means the global maximizer of the canonical continuous density.

Let X have mean m and finite variance sigma^2, and let mu_t be its law freely convolved with a semicircle law of variance t. If sigma=0, mu_t is a semicircle centered at m and the assertions below hold directly. Assume sigma>0. Put

    B=(sqrt(2)+2)sigma,
    A=B^2+sigma^2=(7+4sqrt(2))sigma^2,
    T=1024 A.

For every t>=T, mu_t has a unique global mode. That mode tends to m as t tends to infinity. If E|X-m|^3<infinity, putting M3=E|X-m|^3 and K=A(B+sigma)+4(B^3+M3), its location M(t) satisfies the explicit estimate |M(t)-m|<=36 K/t for t>=T. If E|X-m|^7<infinity, then

    M(t)=m-3mu_3/t+(5mu_5-22mu_2mu_3)/t^2+O_mu(t^-3),

where mu_k=E[(X-m)^k]. The threshold is a proved sufficient bound, with no optimal transition location claimed. An exponential quadratic moment, as in the original classical question, implies the required seventh moment.

Use the general Biane parametrization from Hasebe-Ueda, ALEA 15 (2018), equations (2.10), (2.13), (2.14). With w_t(u)=v_t(u)^2>0, it reads E[1/((u-X)^2+w_t(u))]=1/t, the density at psi_t(u) is sqrt(w_t(u))/(pi t), and psi_t is a homeomorphism. Hence global density maxima correspond exactly to global maxima of w_t. The function v_t is continuous and tends to zero at both infinities: for any a>0, E[1/((u-X)^2+a)] tends to zero as |u| tends to infinity by dominated convergence, forcing w_t(u)<a eventually. Thus a positive global maximum is attained.

Jensen's inequality gives w_t(m)>=t-sigma^2 when t>sigma^2. Indeed, at w=t-sigma^2 the reciprocal expectation is at least 1/t, and the expectation is strictly decreasing in positive w. Every positive solution also has w_t(u)<=t. Let u_* be any global maximizer and w_*=w_t(u_*). Then w_*>=t-sigma^2 and

    E[(u_*-X)^2/(w_*+(u_*-X)^2)]=1-w_*/t<=sigma^2/t.

Chebyshev gives P(|X-m|<=sqrt(2)sigma)>=1/2. If r=|u_*-m|-sqrt(2)sigma>0, the last expectation is at least (1/2)r^2/(t+r^2). For t>=4sigma^2 this implies r^2<=2sigma^2 t/(t-2sigma^2)<=4sigma^2. Consequently every global maximizer lies in I=[m-B,m+B].

For every u in I and t>=T, Jensen similarly yields t-A<=w_t(u)<=t. Set epsilon=1/t, r_t(u)=w_t(u)/t, d=r_t(u)+epsilon(u-X)^2, and

    C2=E[d^-2], J=E[(u-X)d^-2].

The positive implicit solution is smooth in u and r_t'(u)=-2epsilon J/C2. Its stationary points have J=0. Differentiating J along this solution gives

    J'=C2-4epsilon E[(u-X)^2 d^-3]-2r_t'(u)E[(u-X)d^-3].

Uniformly on I, E[(u-X)^2]<=A, r_t>=1-epsilon A>=1/2, C2>=(1+epsilon A)^-2>=1-2epsilon A, and |J|<=4E|u-X|. For epsilon A<=1/2, |r_t'|<=18epsilon E|u-X|, so the magnitude of the final term is at most 288epsilon A; the middle term is at most 32epsilon A. Thus J'>=1-322epsilon A>0 for t>=1024A. At least one global maximizer exists inside I, is a positive interior stationary point of w_t, and therefore has J=0. Strict increase of J permits only one such point. This proves eventual uniqueness of the global density maximizer without a compact-support or unimodality assumption.

As t tends to infinity, r_t->1 uniformly on I. The functions J(u) tend uniformly to u-m: split the integral at a bounded |X-m|, use uniform convergence on the bounded part, and dominate the tail by a constant times |X-m|+B. Its unique zero u_t therefore tends to m. The same truncation argument gives E[(u_t-X)/d]->u_t-m, so psi_t(u_t)=u_t+E[(u_t-X)/d]->m.

If M3 is finite, |d^-2-1|<=16|d-1| and |d^-1-1|<=4|d-1| because d>=1/2. With E|u-X|<=B+sigma and E|u-X|^3<=4(B^3+M3), the equation J=0 yields |u_t-m|<=16epsilon K. The spatial map then yields |psi_t(u_t)-m|<=2(16epsilon K)+4epsilon K=36K/t. All constants and hypotheses are explicit.

For the second-order expansion, translate m to zero and work with F(epsilon,u,r)=E[1/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)]-1 and J(epsilon,u,r)=E[(u-X)/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)^2]. Finite seventh absolute moment makes these functions C^3 up to epsilon=0 from epsilon>=0, for u near zero and r near one. Every derivative of total order at most three is dominated by a constant times 1+|X|^7 when r>=1/2. To use the ordinary C^3 implicit-function theorem, extend to epsilon<0 using the degree-three Taylor polynomial in epsilon at zero, with its smooth u,r-dependent coefficients; this matches all partial derivatives through order three at zero. No reciprocal expectation at negative epsilon is used. The Jacobian with respect to (u,r) at (epsilon,u,r)=(0,0,1) is [[0,-1],[1,0]], hence invertible. The resulting C^3 branch has a Taylor expansion with O(epsilon^3) remainder and is the unique global-maximizer branch already identified above.

Writing r=1+c1 epsilon+c2 epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3) and u=a1 epsilon+a2 epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3), direct expansion gives c1=-mu2, c2=mu4-mu2^2, a1=-2mu3, a2=3mu5-14mu2mu3. Inserting into psi=u+E[(u-X)/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)] gives -3mu3 epsilon+(5mu5-22mu2mu3)epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3). Translation back yields the displayed formula.

[Lemma lem:conditions of arXiv:2503.21737, 'High-intensity Voronoi percolation on manifolds'] Let \(\xi \subset \mathbb R^d\) and \(\eta \subset M\) be locally finite deterministic point sets.
    Let \(\rho \in (0,1)\) and let \(r > 0\) so that \(8r\) satisfies (equation eq:radius_condition of the paper).
    Let \(x_0 \in M\) and \(\varphi \in \pazocal{E}(x_0,8r)\).
    Then the following conditions imply that \(\varphi_*\pazocal{G}_{M}(\eta)|_{B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,r)} = \pazocal{G}_{\mathbb R^d}(\xi)|_{B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,r)}\).
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{Equality (EQL):} \(\varphi(\eta) = \xi \cap B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,8r)\).
        \item \emph{Robustness (ROB):} \(\xi\) is \((r,2\rho)\)-robust.
        \item \emph{Small cells (SMA):} \(\diam_{\mathbb R^d}(C(x,\xi)) \leq r\) for all \(x \in \xi \cap B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,r)\) and
                \(\diam_{M}(C(x,\eta)) \leq r\) for all \(x \in \eta \cap B_{M}(x_0,r)\).
        \item \emph{Similarity of metrics (SIM):}   \(\mathrm{d}_{\mathbb{R}^d} - \rho \cdot r \leq \varphi_*\mathrm{d}_M \leq \mathrm{d}_{\mathbb{R}^d} + \rho \cdot r\) on \(B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,8r)\).
    \end{itemize}

body: In probability theory, the theory of large deviations concerns the asymptotic behaviour of remote tails of sequences of probability distributions. While some basic ideas of the theory can be traced to Laplace, the formalization started with insurance mathematics, namely ruin theory with Cramér and Lundberg. A unified formalization of large deviation theory was developed in 1966, in a paper by Varadhan. Large deviations theory formalizes the heuristic ideas of concentration of measures and widely generalizes the notion of convergence of probability measures.

For f(v,p)=v[a+b tanh(kp)] with fixed b,k>0, logistic Euclidean gradient flow has an exact complete basin classification. If |a|<b, the unique finite critical point (0,atanh(-a/b)/k) is a hyperbolic saddle with stable graph v=-sign(p-p*)sqrt(G(p)-G(p*)), where G'=2h/h'. Above and below the graph the two matching-sign escaping limits have open basins. If a>=b every finite initialization escapes positively; if a<=-b every one escapes negatively, including a=+-b. Here h(p)=a+b tanh(kp), G(p)=a p/(bk)+a sinh(2kp)/(2bk^2)+sinh^2(kp)/k^2. The stable graph is defined only in the straddling case |a|<b. For a>=b all trajectories escape positively, and for a<=-b all escape negatively. Normalized joint limits are (+1,0) and (-1,0), with hard selection and zero loss on escaping orbits. Joint margin means lim f/sqrt(v^2+p^2), not a homogeneous angular objective.
One positive example, two fixed scalar token values a+-b, attention gap 2kp, trained shared head v and scalar p, continuous time.

# Target 1: affine two-token joint model (unaudited draft)

## Definition and conclusion

Fix a real a, b>0 and k>0. The two fixed scalar token values are x_+=a+b and x_-=a-b. Their attention weights are sigma(2kp) and 1-sigma(2kp). The trained parameters are a single shared prediction multiplier v and an unfactored scalar attention parameter p. Thus f(v,p)=v h(p), h(p)=a+b tanh(kp). One positive example is trained with logistic loss and Euclidean gradient flow. Tokens, b, k, and a are fixed, not independent trainable heads. This is an explicitly defined two-token extension of f=v tanh p. It does not cover every meaning of joint two-token training.

If |a|<b, there is exactly one finite critical point (0,p_*), p_*=atanh(-a/b)/k. It is a hyperbolic saddle. Define

  G(p) = a p/(bk) + a sinh(2kp)/(2bk^2) + sinh^2(kp)/k^2,
  F(p) = G(p)-G(p_*).

Then F>=0, with its only zero at p_*. The exact stable manifold is the graph

  v=B(p)=-sign(p-p_*) sqrt(F(p)), with B(p_*)=0.

Every point v>B(p) satisfies (v,p)->(+infinity,+infinity). Every point v<B(p) satisfies (v,p)->(-infinity,-infinity). Loss tends to zero in both basins. They are both nonempty and open. The stable graph has planar Lebesgue measure zero. Normalized joint parameter directions tend to (+1,0) and (-1,0); selected token values tend respectively to a+b and a-b.

If a>=b, there is no finite critical point and every trajectory satisfies (v,p)->(+infinity,+infinity). If a<=-b, there is no finite critical point and every trajectory satisfies (v,p)->(-infinity,-infinity). The boundary cases a=+b and a=-b are included: a zero-valued endpoint token does not create a finite stationary point or a finite-initialization basin escaping to that endpoint. All these conclusions concern forward time.

## Proof

As in proof 001, set ds/dt=g(f)>0, giving v'=h(p), p'=v h'(p) with h'=bk sech^2(kp)>0. Since |h|<=|a|+b and |h'|<=bk, there is no finite-time blow-up and s->infinity. Direct differentiation yields G'=2h/h', hence C=v^2-G(p) is constant.

When |a|<b, h vanishes only at p_*, and G decreases strictly to its minimum there and increases strictly afterwards. Also G tends to +infinity at either end, by its exponential terms (coefficients proportional to b-a on the left and b+a on the right). The shifted integral v^2-F is therefore conserved. Linearizing the s-time vector field at (0,p_*) gives [[0,h'(p_*)],[h'(p_*),0]], with real eigenvalues of opposite sign. In t-time multiply by g(0)=1/2. Near p_*, F(p)=(p-p_*)^2+O((p-p_*)^3), so the displayed graph is smooth with slope -1 at p_*.

The graph v=B(p) is the negative branch of v^2=F and has p' pointing toward p_*; monotonicity and the absence of any other zero imply convergence to (0,p_*). The positive branch escapes to the two matching-sign ends. For v^2-F=D>0, v keeps its sign and |v|>=sqrt(D); p'=vh' has constant sign. If p were bounded in that direction, h' would have a positive lower bound along its compact range and p' could not be integrable. Thus p diverges to that end, and the invariant forces |v|->infinity. For D<0, p stays on one side of p_* and a positive distance away from it. Hence h(p) has constant sign and magnitude bounded below. It follows that v diverges in that sign; the invariant then forces p to the corresponding end. These cases yield exactly the partition above/below B, even when p_* is nonzero.

When a>=b, h is strictly positive at every finite p; G is strictly increasing. Moreover G maps the real line onto the real line. For a>b its left exponential coefficient is negative. At a=b its exponential terms cancel at the left end and G(p)=p/k+O(1) there, still tending to -infinity. At the right end G->+infinity. For a fixed orbit C=v^2-G, there is a unique p_min with G(p_min)=-C. Hence p>=p_min always, h(p)>=h(p_min)>0, and v'=h(p) forces v through zero and then to +infinity. For all sufficiently large s, p increases; if it were bounded above, p'=v h' would preclude boundedness. Thus p->+infinity. The case a<=-b follows by (a,v,p)->(-a,-v,-p), which preserves the gradient-flow equations and the prediction. This also checks the zero-endpoint cases without an asymptotic assumption.

Finally, on any escaping orbit the leading positive exponential term of G at the selected end gives |p|=(log |v|)/k+O(1). Therefore |p|/|v|->0. The finite limiting h at that end has the sign of v and nonzero magnitude, implying f->+infinity and the stated directions and loss limit.

## Consequence for the proposed strict-saddle route

Define the natural joint directional margin on an escaping orbit as lim f(v,p)/sqrt(v^2+p^2). The two basins have margins a+b and b-a when |a|<b. The supremum possible asymptotic normalized margin is M=max(|a+b|,|a-b|)=b+|a|: the upper bound follows from |h|<=M and |v|<=sqrt(v^2+p^2), and each endpoint magnitude is achieved along its matching escaping branch. If 0<|a|<b, one entire open basin has strictly smaller margin b-|a|. Its planar measure is positive, so any initialization law assigning positive density throughout the plane has positive probability of this suboptimal selection. Each finite point in that basin has a neighborhood with the same limiting selection. Thus a universal strict-saddle or measure-zero-basin assertion for suboptimal joint selections fails for this whole parameter family and this definition of joint margin.

This does not contradict a fixed-prediction-head attention-SVM theorem. It does not identify a canonical homogeneous angular flow: f is not homogeneous in (v,p). It classifies actual limits and basins of the specified joint flow. Literature novelty is pending source verification; proof is unaudited.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a677ef65139292f0773807a5f7a72edcd9e96c2449a53814b65aaa2103d29691","revision_digest":"sha256:0172baa96c192a8d59a8dcb79a9454165c089679aff51f0f832c36a58590e535","source_id":"owner:T328:w698:claim-002:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20, exact claim version 1, reviewer claude-738954b6 PASS in AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: In probability theory, a Chernoff bound is an exponentially decreasing upper bound on the tail of a random variable based on its moment generating function. The minimum of all such exponential bounds forms the Chernoff or Chernoff-Cramér bound, which may decay faster than exponential. It is especially useful for sums of independent random variables, such as sums of Bernoulli random variables.

Every set can be well-ordered: for every set X there is a total order on X in which every non-empty subset has a least element. Over the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms ZF this statement is equivalent to the axiom of choice and to Zorn's lemma, so it is a theorem of ZFC and is not provable in ZF alone.

\quad \textrm{ and }\quad
P_t(C_b(H))\subset C_b(H),
\]

$\delta_x$ denotes the Dirac delta measure at $x$

[Proposition prop:CE-law-with-floor of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Fix $n\geq 1$. Let $V\subset \mathbb Z^2$ be a connected domain, and consider the \ensuremath{\mathbb Z\textsc{gff}}\xspace model $\pi_{V;F}^{\xi}$ with a floor at~0 imposed only on a subset $F\subset V$, and boundary conditions $\xi$ that are $H+1-n$ on a $*$-connected path in $\partial_{\mathtt v} V$ and $H-n$ elsewhere so that they induce a unique disagreement polymer $(\gamma,\{D_i\},\{h_i\})$ in $V\cup \partial_{\mathtt v} V$ that contains boundary disagreements\footnote{We say the disagreement polymer contains boundary disagreements if it contains a bond dual to ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}\mathsf v$ for ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}},\mathsf v\notin V$.}.  Then for $\beta\geq \beta_0$, the law of this unique disagreement polymer $\gamma$ is given by 
		\begin{align}
			\pi^{\xi}_{V;F}(\gamma) =\frac1{Z} \exp\bigg(-{\ensuremath{\mathscr E}}_\beta(\gamma) + \sum_{\substack{{\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}\subset V \\ {\ensuremath{\mathsf W}} \cap \Delta_\gamma \neq \emptyset}} \Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})
			\bigg)\prod_{i\geq 0}{\widehat\pi}_{D_i^\circ}^{h_i}\big(\phi_x \geq 0,\, \forall x \in D_i^{\circ}\cap F\big)\,,
		\end{align}
		for a normalizer $Z= Z(V,F,\xi,\beta,n)$ and a decoration function $\Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})$ as per (def:disagree-polymer-len-energy-decor of the paper).
		
		Moreover, if we further have $|F| \leq L e^{\kappa\sqrt{\log L}}$ and $|\partial F|\leq L^{1-\delta}$ for fixed $\kappa>0$ and $0<\delta<\frac13$, denote by $D_0$ and $D_1$ the regions of $\gamma$ containing the boundary vertices of $V$ at heights $H+1-n$ and $H-n$, respectively, and let
		\begin{align*} E:=\left\{|\gamma|\leq L^{1-\delta}\,,\;
			\;|F| - |D_0 \cap F| - |D_1 \cap F| \leq L^{1-\delta}\right\}\,,\end{align*}
		then the following holds
		for all $\beta\geq \beta_0$ (not depending on $\kappa,\delta$). The probability distribution given~by 
		\[ p_{V;F}^{\xi}(\gamma) := 
		\frac1{\overline Z} \exp\bigg(-{\ensuremath{\mathscr E}}_\beta(\gamma) + \frac{|D_0\cap F|}{N_n}+ \sum_{\substack{{\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}\subset V \\ {\ensuremath{\mathsf W}} \cap \Delta_\gamma \neq \emptyset}} \Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})  \bigg)\prod_{i \geq 2}{\widehat\pi}_{D_i^\circ}^{h_i}(\phi_x \geq 0,\, \forall x \in D_i^{\circ}\cap F)
		\]
        for $\gamma\in E$, where $\overline Z = \overline{Z}(V,F,\xi,\beta,n)$ is a normalizer, satisfies		\begin{align}
			\pi^\xi_{V;F}(\gamma \mid E) =(1+o(1))p_{V;F}^{\xi}(\gamma)\,.
		\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:kernel-sum of arXiv:2609.02544, 'A finiteness theorem for geodesic Leech wheels'] Let $M\ge3$, $R=\floor{(M-1)/2}$, and $\rho=\rho_R$, so that $R\ge1$ and the kernel $K_R$ of Lemma~(lem:kernel of the paper) is defined. Suppose $S\subseteq\{0,1,\ldots,M-1\}$ has $\abs S$ elements, of which $h$ exceed $R$. With $\zeta=\mathrm{e}^{2\pi i/M}$ and $F(z)=\sum_{a\in S}z^a$, if some $U>0$ satisfies $\abs{F(\zeta^t)}\le U$ for all $t\in\{1\}\cup\{2,4,6,\ldots,2R\}$, then
\begin{equation}
  \left(\frac\pi2+\rho\right)U
  \ge
  \sum_{a\in S}K_R\!\left(\frac{2\pi a}{M}\right)
  \ge\rho\abs S-\pi h.
\end{equation}

of $g_{\mathrm{sc}}$ has two conical singularities, and its tangent cone at
either end is the asymptotic cone of $g_{\RF,*}$.

[Lemma lem:ExpIneqM of arXiv:2608.30848, '\huge \bf Limit Laws of the Iterated Logarithm Under Sub-linear Expectations'] Let $\{X_n; n\ge 1\}$ be a martingale difference sequence on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\textsf{P})$ with respect to the $\sigma$-field filtration $\{\mathcal F_n\}$, and assume $|X_n|\le c$ a.s. Then
$$ \textsf{P}\bigg( \sum_{i=1}^n X_i\ge x \text{ and } \sum_{i=1}^n \textsf{E}[X_i^2|\mathcal{F}_{i-1}]\le y\; \text{ for some } n \text{ hold} \bigg)
\le \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{x^2}{2(xc+y)}\bigg\}.   $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:Xt-from-V-to-U of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] The following holds for every {\upshape\texttt{good}\xspace} collection $\{V_i\}_{i=1}^m$. Let $\tau_i$ be the minimum $s\geq 0$ where the backward dynamics, started at time $t_1$ from every $v\in V_i$, has its surviving history reach size at most $3$ at time $t_1-s$, or $\tau_i=t_1$ if the backward dynamics reaches time $0$ before this happens. Further let $U_i$ be the surviving history at time $\tau_i$. Then there exists some $C=C(q,\theta)>0$ such that
\begin{align*}\Big\|\prod_{i=1}^m\mathbb{P}_{\mathsf{x}_0}\big(X_{t_1}^{(i)}(V_i) \in \cdot\big) - \prod_{i=1}^m \mu_G\mathord{\upharpoonright}_{V_i} \Big\|_{\textsc{tv}}^2
\leq C\, &\mathbb{E}\bigg[
\sum_{i=1}^m
\Big\| \mathbb{P}_{\mathsf{x}_0}\big( X_{t_1-\tau_i}^{(i)}(U_i)\in\cdot\big) - 
\mu_G\mathord{\upharpoonright}_{U_i} \Big\|_{\textsc{tv}}^2 \mathbbm{1}_{\{\tau_i<t_1\}}
\bigg] \\
&+ O\big(e^{-8(\log n)^{1-\frac\upalpha2}}\big)\,.
\end{align*}

body:
[Theorem theo.SRW of arXiv:2411.19145, 'On the intersection of critical percolation clusters and other tree-like random graphs'] Let $R_\infty^k$, $k\ge 1$, be independent SRW ranges on $\mathbb Z^d$. 
\begin{enumerate}  
\item[(i)] If $d\ge 5$, then for any $k\ge 2$, there exist positive constants $c_1,c_2$, such that for any $t>1$, 
$$\exp(-c_1\, t^{1-\frac 2d}) \le \mathbb P(|R_\infty^1\cap \dots \cap R_\infty^k|>t) \le  \exp(-c_2\, t^{1-\frac 2d}). $$ 
\item[(ii)] If $d=4$, then for any $k\ge 3$, there exist positive constants $c_1,c_2$, such that for any $t>e$, 
$$\exp(-c_1\, \sqrt{t} ) \le \mathbb P(|R_\infty^1\cap \dots \cap R_\infty^k|>t) \le  \exp\big(-c_2\, (\frac{t}{\log t})^{1/2}\big).$$
\item[(iii)] If $d=3$, then for any $k\ge 4$, there exist positive constants $c_1,c_2$, such that for any $t>e$, 
$$\exp(-c_1\, t^{1/3}) \le \mathbb P(|R_\infty^1\cap \dots \cap R_\infty^k|>t) \le  \exp(-c_2\, (\frac t{\log t})^{1/3}). $$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem theo.SRW of arXiv:2411.19145

Let P be a product measure on {0,1}^E and let A_1, ..., A_k be INCREASING events with the same probability. Then max_i P(A_i) = P(A_1) >= 1 - ( 1 - P( union_i A_i ) )^{1/k}. More generally, without assuming equal probabilities, max_i P(A_i) >= 1 - (1 - P(union_i A_i))^{1/k}. The name comes from the case k = 2, where the bound reads P(A_1) >= 1 - sqrt(1 - P(A_1 or A_2)): if the union is very likely then at least one of two increasing events is likely, quantitatively. This is the standard device for turning a statement like 'some crossing of a box occurs' into 'a crossing in a specific direction occurs with probability bounded below', and it is the engine of Zhang's argument that theta(1/2) = 0 for bond percolation on Z^2. The events must be INCREASING, since the proof is Harris-FKG applied to their complements; for arbitrary events the inequality is false. [standard; e.g. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., proof of Theorem 11.11, and Bollobas-Riordan, Percolation]
product measure
all the events increasing (the proof uses FKG on the decreasing complements)

For any connected simple graph G with maximum degree Delta, the chromatic number satisfies chi(G) <= Delta, unless G is a complete graph or an odd cycle, in which cases chi(G) = Delta + 1.

The bound includes maximum degrees Delta=0,1,2: a connected graph with Delta=0 is K_1, with chi=1; a connected graph with Delta=1 is K_2, with chi=2; for Delta=2, every non-odd-cycle connected graph is 2-colorable, while an odd cycle has chi=3. Thus for every connected simple graph of finite maximum degree Delta, chi(G)<=Delta unless G is complete or an odd cycle, in which cases chi(G)=Delta+1.
G is a connected simple graph with finite maximum degree Delta >= 0

If G is Delta-regular, 2-connected, and not complete or an odd cycle, one can find a vertex v with two non-adjacent neighbors u, w such that G - {u, w} is connected. Coloring u and w with color 1 leaves v with at most Delta-2 uncolored neighbors, allowing greedy completion with Delta colors. For Delta=0,1 connectedness gives K_1,K_2. For Delta=2, a connected graph is a finite path, a cycle, a one-way infinite path or a two-way infinite path; alternating two colors works on paths and even cycles, whereas an odd cycle requires exactly three. [Definition 4 (Aggregated seating sequence) of arXiv:2606.01881, '2606.01881'] Let $\mathcal B=\{B_r:r\ge1\}$ be a partition of $\mathbb N$ whose blocks are ordered by their least elements:
\[
        \min B_1<\min B_2<\cdots.
\]
Given a seating sequence $C=(C_i:i\ge1)$, define the aggregated seating sequence $C^{\mathcal B}$ by
\[
        C_i^{\mathcal B}=r\quad\text{if and only if}\quad C_i\in B_r.
\]
This is the external, block-level dynamics: it records which block is visited, but not which original table inside that block is chosen.
title: Aggregated seating sequence

 $U$ is unbounded and $d\ge 2$, assume that  the $F$-Bregman divergence $\phi= \phi_{_F}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\forall \xi \!\in U

, \quad \liminf_{x\to \infty,\, x\in U}\phi_{_F}(\xi, x)= \sup _{x\in U} \phi_{_F}(\xi,x).
\end{equation} 

\medskip
\noindent $(a)$ Then for every $n\ge1$ there exists an $n$-tuple $x^{(n)}= \big(x^{(n)}_1, \ldots, x^{(n)}_n\big) \!\in U^n$ which minimizes $G_{n}$ over $U^n$. Moreover, if  the support (in $U$) of the distribution $P$ has at least $n$ points then $x^{(n)}$ has pairwise distinct components and $P\big(\mathring C_i(x^{(n)})\big)>0$ for every $i\!\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$.

\smallskip
\noindent $(b)$ The distribution  $P$ assigns no mass to the boundary of Bregman--Voronoi partitions of $x^{(n)}$, i.e.
\[
P\left (\bigcup_{i=1}^n\partial C_i\big( x^{(n)})\right) = 0,
\]
and $x^{(n)}$ satisfies the $\phi_{_F}$-stationary (or master) equation
\begin{equation}
P\big( C_i(x^{(n)})\big)\,x^{(n)}_i  -  \int_{ C_i(x^{(n)})} \xi P(\mathrm{d}\xi) =0, \quad  i =1,\ldots,n.
\end{equation}
 
\noindent $(c)$ The sequence $\displaystyle G_{n}\big( x^{(n)}\big) = \min_{U^n} G_{n}$ decreases as long as it is not $0$ and converges to $0$ as $n$ goes to $+\infty$.

\noindent $(d)$ When $d=1$, the above claims $(a)$-$(b)$-$(c)$ remain true without assuming~(equation eq:boundary-lsc of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemme 57 of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\mu \in \mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R})$ be atomless and such that there exists $\theta>1$

$$

\Int{\mathbb{R}}{} |x|^{\theta} \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \, < \,  +\infty \qquad  \mbox{and }  \qquad  \Int{\mathbb{R}}{} x \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \, = \,  0 \, .

$$

Then, there exists a constant $\eta_0(\mu)> 0$ such that for any $0 < \eta < \eta_0(\mu)$, there exist $K_1, K_2 > 0$ such that

\begin{align*}

\Int{-K_1}{K_2} x \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) = 0 \;, \qquad \mu\big[ [-K_1; K_2]^c \big] \,  \leq \, \eta \;, \qquad

\Int{}{} \mathbbm{1}_{[-K_1;K_2]^c}(x)  |x| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \,  \leq  \, \eta \, .

\end{align*}

Furthermore $\mathbbm{1}_{[-K_1;K_2]} \to 1$ as $\eta \searrow 0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere, in an increasing fashion. Finally, there exists $C>0$ such that

\beq

K_1+K_2 \, \leq \, \f{ C }{ \eta^{   \f{1}{\theta-1} }  } \;.

\enq (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemme 57 of arXiv:2604.00635

body:
[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \(P\) be a rank-\(m\) orthogonal projection on \(\R^d\), let $\rho=\max_{j\in[d]} P_{jj}$, and let \(q\) be a probability measure on \([d]\). Set
	\[ \sigma^2 = \frac{\rho \|q\|_2^2}{d}, \qquad M=\rho\|q\|_\infty.\]
	If \(\pi\) is uniform on \(S_d\), then
	\[
	\probb{\pi}{\norm{PD_{q_\pi}P - \frac{1}{d}P}\geq t}
	\le
	2m\exp\left(
	-\frac{t^2}
	{12\sigma^2+4\sqrt2\,Mt}
	\right)
	\qquad \text{for }t\geq0.
	\]

[Theorem Propolemiko of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $l > 1$ be a real number. Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$ and
  assume that for every $r \in \mathbb{N}$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{N^l} \log \mathbb{E} [H \text{} C
    (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A), \ldots, \lambda_N (A))] =
    \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi$ is a smooth function in a complex neighborhood of $0$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$. Then the random measure $N^{- 1} \sum_{i = 1}^N \delta \left( N^{- l}
  \lambda_i (A) \right)$ converges, as $N \rightarrow \infty$, in probability, in the
  sense of moments to the Dirac measure $\delta \left( \Psi' (0) \right)$. In more detail, this means that any moment of the former measure converges to the corresponding moment of the latter measure in probability.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:048f65dac46216c4e256fc7be3369792347ff4627bf6fc4d8e77c0bc2564a8fe","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/04/048f65dac46216c4e256fc7be3369792347ff4627bf6fc4d8e77c0bc2564a8fe.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:0f5a7de4ce67fffcf1173bf993c31713fb08f0f899b640c0c3d1c53764d47571","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c2","bundle_id":"population.i0005-four-dimensional-parking-partials-002","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"interacting particle systems and random-walk potential theory","draft":"w661/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:i0005-c2-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C2 v1: a dimension-free isolated-hole criterion

Novelty: KNOWN (generalization/repackaging of Bou-Rabee–Panagiotis, proof of Theorem 1.6, Steps 1–3, PDF p.28). The explicit criterion is supplied as a reusable reduction, not an asserted solution of I0005. Audit status: unaudited.

Fix d≥1. Consider a jointly translation-invariant random configuration on Z^d of hole indicators H(x) in {0,1} and active-site indicators B(x) in {0,1}, with H(x)B(x)=0. Let h=EH(0)>0, a=EB(0), and let distance be ℓ1. For an integer R≥1 put

S_R=sum_{0<|x|_1≤4R} E[H(0)H(x)].

Let F be the event that the origin is strictly closer to a hole than to every active site (the distance to an empty active set is infinity). Then

P(F)≥binom(R+d,d)·(h−S_R−a/2)_+.

In particular, if a≤h and S_R≤δh with δ<1/2, then

P(F)≥(1/2−δ)h R^d/d!.

For a time-indexed critical particle–hole process with a_t≤h_t and h_t→0, it is sufficient to find fixed b>0, δ<1/2 and R_t=floor(bh_t^−1/d) such that S_{R_t}≤δh_t eventually: this yields a positive lower limit at least (1/2−δ)b^d/d!. No assumption of independence among surviving holes is made.

## Proof

A hole at y is isolated if no other hole lies within distance 4R of y. The union bound shows that the density i of isolated holes is at least h−S_R. Centers of distinct isolated holes are more than 4R apart, so their closed ℓ1 balls of radius 2R are disjoint.

Each active site contained in one such ball sends one unit of mass to its center. It sends at most one unit, because the balls are disjoint. Translation invariance equates expected outgoing and incoming mass: to see this directly for the nonnegative translation-covariant transport T(x,y), Tonelli gives sum_y ET(0,y)=sum_y ET(−y,0)=sum_x ET(x,0). The outgoing expectation is at most a. Thus the density of isolated-hole centers whose radius-2R ball contains at least two active sites is at most a/2. Call an isolated hole good if its ball contains at most one active site. Good-hole density g is at least h−S_R−a/2.

For a good hole y with one active site z in the ball, select the closed coordinate orthant based at y opposite z: each coordinate sign points away from z, and choose the positive sign if z_j=y_j. If there is no active site in the ball, select the all-positive orthant. These choices commute with lattice translations. The intersection of this orthant with the ball of radius R contains exactly binom(R+d,d) lattice sites, by counting nonnegative integer coordinate vectors with sum at most R.

For w in the selected intersection and the unique active site z (when present), coordinatewise opposition gives |w−z|_1=|w−y|_1+|z−y|_1>|w−y|_1; z≠y follows from H(y)B(y)=0. Any other active site v is outside the closed radius-2R ball, so

|w−v|_1≥|v−y|_1−|w−y|_1>2R−R≥|w−y|_1.

Therefore w is strictly closer to the hole y than to every active site. Selected intersections belonging to distinct good holes are disjoint, since even their radius-R balls are disjoint. Send unit mass from each good hole to each site in its selected intersection. The expected outgoing mass at zero is binom(R+d,d)g. Incoming mass at any site is at most one and is zero outside F, so P(F)≥binom(R+d,d)g. If the lower bound for g is negative, use g≥0 instead. This proves the first inequality.

Since binom(R+d,d)≥R^d/d!, the second follows. For the time-indexed assertion, h_tR_t^d→b^d as h_t→0, and taking a lower limit proves the stated constant.

## What remains at dimension four

For the sparse source law, a_t=P(A_t(0)>0)≤EA_t(0)=EH_t(0)=h_t by conservation of signed expected density. Thus the precise unproved input is

sum_{0<|x|_1≤4floor(bh_t^−1/4)} P(H_t(0)=H_t(x)=1)≤δh_t

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.27828, 'Scaling limit of the 3D abelian Yang--Mills Langevin dynamics'] Let $d=3$ and $\bar\beta=1$. Let $\xi=(\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3)$ have independent space-time white-noise components on $\R\times\mathbf{T}^3$, defined on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, and let $\xi^\eps$ be the lattice approximation (equation eq:Disc_white_noise of the paper).

Let $I$ and $\{h_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in I}$ satisfy Assumption~(assmp:YMAction of the paper).
For every sufficiently small $\eps$, let $\lambda_\eps\in I$ and write $h_\eps = h_{\lambda_\eps}$. Let $\theta^\eps$ solve the DeTurck-gauge-fixed lattice Langevin equation (equation eq:NParaDisc of the paper), with $h=h_\eps$ and (possibly random) initial condition $\theta^\eps(0)$, up to the stopping time $\tau_\eps$.

Let $\theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2,\theta_3)$ solve the continuum stochastic heat
equation
\[  \partial_t\theta_i
    =
    \Delta\theta_i+\xi_i
\]
 with (possibly random) initial condition 
 $ \theta_i(0)$ 
 for  $i=1,2,3$.
Fix $\kappa>0$ sufficiently small and let
\[
-\frac23+\frac53\kappa<\eta<0,
\qquad
\gamma=\bigl(\eta+\tfrac12\bigr)\wedge 0.
\]

Suppose that there is a deterministic constant $M<\infty$ such that, almost surely,
\[
\sup_{0<\varepsilon\le1}\|\theta^\varepsilon(0)\|_{\mathcal C_\varepsilon^\eta}
+\|\theta(0)\|_{\mathcal C^\eta}
\le M.
\]
If
$\|\theta^\varepsilon(0);\theta(0)\|_{\mathcal C_\varepsilon^\eta}\to0$
in probability, then for every $T>0$ and $\delta>0$,
\begin{equ}
\lim_{\eps\to0}
\mathbb P\left(
\tau_\eps>T,
\ \|\theta^\eps;\theta\|_{\CC_{\gamma,\eps}^{-1/2-\kappa,T}}
\leq \delta
\right)=1.
\end{equ} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.27828

[Corollary Cor:ftc of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] Let $p$ be a semi-directed path from the origin to $(n,{\lceil v n \rceil})$ and let $\varepsilon>0$. For each proper divisor $K$ of $n$, divide the cylinder $[0,n]\times \mathbb Z$ into $n/K$ strips and count the ratio $\eta$ of strips in which the slope of $p$ is bounded from above:
\[
\eta:=\frac K n \left|\left\{ i\in \{0,...,n/K-1\}: \, f_p^*(K(i+1))-f_p^*(K i)\le K(v_n+\varepsilon) \right\}\right|
\]
where $v_n={\lceil v n \rceil}/n$ and $f_p^*(x)=f_p(x)$ as defined in Section~(Sec:equiv_model of the paper) with the exception of $f_p^*(n)=(n,{\lceil v n \rceil})$. Then $p$ moves downwards along at least $\varepsilon n/(2K)$ vertical edges or $\eta > \varepsilon/ (2(v_n+\varepsilon))$.

body: [Proposition 43 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(X\) be a qcqs smooth \(k\)-scheme and let \(D=D_1+\cdots+D_n\) be a simple normal crossings divisor. Let \(\varnothing\neq I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and assume that \(D_I\defeq\bigcap_{i\in I}D_i\) is nonempty. Let \(\pi\colon Y\defeq\Bl_{D_I}X\to X\) be the blow-up and put \(D_Y\defeq(\pi^{-1}D)_{\red}\). If the pair \((X,D)\) is log HT-split, then the pair \((Y,D_Y)\) is log HT-split. In particular, the underlying scheme \(Y\) is HT-split.
title: Proposition 43 of arXiv:2609.00567

body: A directed set is a preorder in which every pair of elements has an upper bound. A net in X is a function from a directed set D into X, written (x_d); it converges to p if for every neighborhood U of p it is eventually in U (there is d0 with x_d in U for all d >= d0). Nets generalize sequences (take D = the natural numbers) and repair the tools that sequences fail to capture outside first-countable spaces: (i) p is in cl(A) iff some net in A converges to p; (ii) f is continuous at p iff x_d -> p implies f(x_d) -> f(p) for every net; (iii) X is compact iff every net has a convergent subnet; (iv) X is Hausdorff iff every net has at most one limit.

body:
[Lemma OU flow property of arXiv:2603.14163, '\LARGE \bf Tail Bounds for Queues with Abandonment: Constant, Moderate, Large Deviations, '] Let $p>1$ and let $X\in \mathbb{R}^d$ a random vector with law $\mathcal{L}(X)\in\mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Let $T:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be a Borel measurable map such that $Y:=T(X)$ is a real random variable with $\mathbb{E}|Y|^p<\infty$. Let $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ be independent of $X$. For $t>0$ define
\[
F_t := e^{-t}Y + \sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}\,Z,
\]
and let $f_t$ denote the density of $F_t$ (w.r.t.\ Lebesgue measure). Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item (OU representation) \textnormal{[fang2022wasserstein]} The family $(F_t)_{t>0}$ is the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup acting on $Y$; equivalently, $(F_t)$ is a version of the solution to the SDE
        \[
            dF_t = -F_t\,dt + \sqrt{2}\,dB_t,\qquad F_0=Y,
        \]
        where $(B_t)$ is a standard Brownian motion independent of $Y$.

    \item (Smooth positive density) \textnormal{[johnson2001entropy]} For every $t>0$ the law of $F_t$ admits a strictly positive, smooth density $f_t$.
    \item (Commutation of OU semigroup and differentiation) \textnormal{[bakry2013analysis] [bonis2020steins]} For every $t>0 , k\in\mathbb{N}$, and $g \in C^{\infty}_c(\mathbb{R})$,
        \[
            \frac{d^k}{dx^k} P_t g(x) = e^{-kt} P_t\!\Bigl(\frac{d^k}{dx^k} g\Bigr)(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R},
        \]
        where $P_t g(x):=\mathbb{E}[g(F_t)\mid F_0=x]$ is the OU semigroup acting on $g$. Moreover,
        \[
         P_t \frac{d^k}{dx^k}g(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1- e^{-2t}}^k} \mathbb{E}[h_k(Z) g(e^{-t}x + \sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}Z)], \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},
        \]
        where $h_k(x) = (-1)^k e^{x^2/2} \frac{d^k}{dx^k}e^{-x^2/2}$ is the $k$-th Hermite Polynomial.

    \item (Continuity equation) For every $t>0$ the density $f_t$ satisfies the continuity equation
        \[
            \partial_t f_t(x) + \frac{d}{dx}\bigl(f_t(x)\,\rho_t(x)\bigr)=0,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R},
        \]
        where $\rho_t(x):=-\partial_x\log f_t(x)-x$ is the score function of $f_t$.

    \item (Score representation) \textnormal{[bonis2020steins]} For each $t>0$ the score admits the conditional expectation representation
        \[
            \rho_t(F_t)\;\overset{d.}{=}\; \mathbb{E}\!\Bigl[e^{-t}Y-\frac{e^{-2t}}{\sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}}\,Z\;\Big|\;F_t\Bigr],
        \]
        and, consequently,
        \[
            t\mapsto \|\rho_t(F_t)\|_{L^p(\mathcal{L}(F_t))}\in L^1((0,\infty)).
        \]

    \item (Moment bound and weak continuity) The curve $t\mapsto\mathcal{L}(F_t)$ is weakly continuous on $(0,\infty)$, and
        \[
            \sup_{t>0}\|F_t\|_{L^p}<\infty,
        \]
        (equivalently $\sup_{t>0}\|x\|_{L^p(\mathcal{L}(F_t))}<\infty$).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma OU flow property of arXiv:2603.14163

body: For a linear NAE triangle system with k triples on r coordinates and fibre A (the set of sign vectors in {-1,+1}^r with no triple monochromatic), the correlation excess is c = k*beta - ell, where beta = log2(4/3) and ell = r - log2|A| is the unrooted defect. c > 0 means the fibre is larger than the independence prediction 2^r (3/4)^k (positive correlation among the constraints); c is exactly additive over coordinate-disjoint unions and over blocks glued at a single shared coordinate (spin-flip symmetry makes every block fibre split evenly on any coordinate).

Let f: {-1,1}^n -> {0,1} with x uniform on {-1,1}^n, Walsh coefficients fhat(S) = E[f(x) prod_{i in S} x_i], derivative D_i f(x) = (f(x with x_i = 1) - f(x with x_i = -1))/2, and q_i = P(f(x) != f(x with x_i flipped)) the probability that coordinate i is pivotal. f is unate if for each i, D_i f >= 0 everywhere or D_i f <= 0 everywhere. If f is unate, then (1/4) sum_i q_i^2 <= Var(f) <= (1/4) sum_i q_i. The upper bound holds for every f. Either bound is an equality exactly when f is constant or f(x) = (1 + x_i)/2 or (1 - x_i)/2 for some i.

[Cor Cor_MakNikPal1 of arXiv:2606.22183, 'Expected loss of quasi-arithmetic means of exchangeable random variables'] Let $I\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a nonempty open interval, $\alpha:(I-I)\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be an even error function,
 and $L:I\to \mathbb{R}$ be a strongly $\alpha$-convex function.
Then 
 \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] $\alpha(0)=0$ and
     \[
        \lim_{t\to 0} \frac{\alpha(t)}{t} =0,
    \]
    \item[(ii)] $L$ is a strongly $\widehat\alpha$-convex function as well, 
       where $\widehat\alpha:(I-I)\to\mathbb{R}_+$ is defined by
       \begin{align}
        \widehat\alpha(u):=\sup\left\{  \frac{\alpha(tu)}{t} : t\in(0,1] \right\}, \qquad u\in (I-I).
      \end{align}
  \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: The Barabási–Albert (BA) model is an algorithm for generating random scale-free networks using a preferential attachment mechanism. Several natural and human-made systems, including the Internet, the World Wide Web, citation networks, and some social networks are thought to be approximately scale-free and certainly contain few nodes with unusually high degree as compared to the other nodes of the network. The BA model tries to explain the existence of such nodes in real networks. The algorithm is named for its inventors Albert-László Barabási and Réka Albert.

$\mathcal{E}(f,f)=-\langle\mathcal{L}_S f,f\rangle_\mu=\langle\nabla f,D\nabla f\rangle_\mu$

\begin{align}

  &= -\mathcal{E}(f,f) + k\langle V, f^2\rangle_\mu,

  \langle \mathcal{L}_k^J f, f\rangle_\mu
  &= -\mathcal{E}(f,f) + k\langle v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U, f^2\rangle_\mu
     + k^2\langle U\cdot DU, f^2\rangle_\mu,
  
\end{align}
where $\langle g, f^2\rangle_\mu = \int gf^2\mathrm{d}\mu$.

body: In mathematical statistics, the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence (also called relative entropy and I-divergence), denoted $D_{\text{KL}}(P\parallel Q)$, is a type of statistical distance: a measure of how much an approximating probability distribution Q is different from a true probability distribution P. Mathematically, it is defined as $$D_{\text{KL}}(P\parallel Q)=\sum _{x\in {\mathcal {X}}}P(x)\,\log {\frac {P(x)}{Q(x)}}{\text{.}}$$

with i.i.d.\ marks \(U(x)\) taking values in a Polish space \(\mathbb{K}\).  
Let the shot-noise field \(M\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\) with values in \( \mathbb{R}\) be defined by
\[
M(x) := \sum_{y \in \Xi} \zeta(x, \tilde{y}), \quad x \in \mathbb{R}^d,
\]
for some measurable function \(\zeta : \mathbb{R}^d \times (\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}) \longrightarrow  \mathbb{R}\)

then the random field \(M\) exhibits fast \textnormal{BL}-mixing correlations 
as in Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.BL-mixing-field of the paper) and~(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper).

body:
PROOF (UNAUDITED), T250-w712-C002 v2. For a width n>=1 zero-bias tanh MLP with independent iid N(0,1/n) weight matrices across layers and one deterministic input with initial normalized squared norm q0 in [0,1], let h_j be its preactivations and let hbar_j be the corresponding independent centered Gaussian vectors with deterministic kernel variances qbar_0=q0 and qbar_(j+1)=E tanh(sqrt(qbar_j)Z)^2. For every integer depth L>=1, W2(h_L/sqrt(n),hbar_L/sqrt(n))^2<=1152/n, and W2((h_j/sqrt(n))_(j=1)^L,(hbar_j/sqrt(n))_(j=1)^L)^2<=1152 L/n in the product Euclidean metric. Including each layer postactivation increases the joint squared bound to at most 2304 L/n. This is only the one-input tanh chain family, not arbitrary Tensor Programs. Independent review and literature novelty assessment remain outstanding. Lean runtime was unverified.
One deterministic input; q0 in [0,1]
Constant integer width n>=1, finite integer depth L>=1
Fresh independent Gaussian weight matrices, variance 1/n
Zero biases and componentwise tanh
Product Euclidean metric on normalized layer trajectories
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:f6b365a8110df7488036122974bf083176e3928d6a071bb5045b9fe5ab493e31","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/f6/f6b365a8110df7488036122974bf083176e3928d6a071bb5045b9fe5ab493e31.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:15ef18329cadf8df24c8d4aadc2edc07978a9a7d37fb1c896aace01c7f1f99fc","bundle_entry_key":"tanh-depth-uniform","bundle_id":"population.t250-critical-tanh-depth-uniform-001","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w712/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:critical-tanh-mlp-one-input-depth-uniform-gp-rate-w712","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Critical tanh chain: depth-uniform one-input Gaussian approximation

Claim T250-w712-C002, version 2. Status: proof (unaudited).
Target 1. Scope: one input, tanh MLP, critical variance 1/n, no biases. This does not cover general Tensor Programs or a multi-input tanh chain.

Let n >= 1 and q_0 in [0,1]. Independently at every layer sample n standard Gaussians Z_li and put
q_(l+1) = n^(-1) sum_i tanh(sqrt(q_l) Z_li)^2.
Let F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q) Z)^2, and qbar_(l+1)=F(qbar_l), qbar_0=q_0.
For a final independent Gaussian vector g in R^n, the layer-L preactivation has law sqrt(q_(L-1))g and its GP comparison has law sqrt(qbar_(L-1))g.

THEOREM. For every depth L>=1 and every n>=1,
W_2( sqrt(q_(L-1))g/sqrt(n), sqrt(qbar_(L-1))g/sqrt(n) )^2 <= 1152/n.
In particular this gives the target sqrt(L/n) rate and, more strongly, a depth-uniform n^(-1/2) rate for this critical non-ReLU chain. Constants are deliberately loose.

The hard step is bounding relative kernel error without multiplying absolute Lipschitz constants. The proof below uses conditional second moments, not products of marginal probability estimates.

1. Elementary tanh inequalities.
For t>=0, tanh t <= t, sinh t >= t, and therefore
 tanh(t)^2 = sinh(t)^2/(1+sinh(t)^2) >= t^2/(1+t^2).
Consequently
 t-tanh t = integral_0^t tanh(s)^2 ds >= t^3/[3(1+t^2)],
and multiplying by t+tanh t >= t gives
 t^2-tanh(t)^2 >= t^4/[3(1+t^2)].
These inequalities include t=0. Denominators are strictly positive.

2. Kernel shape.
For each fixed z, q -> tanh(sqrt(q)|z|)^2 is increasing and concave on [0,infinity). Indeed at q>0 its derivative is
 z^2 [tanh(t)/t] sech(t)^2, t=sqrt(q)|z|.
Both nonnegative factors are decreasing in t: sech(t)^2 is decreasing, and tanh(t)/t is decreasing since tanh is concave, vanishes at zero, and has derivative sech(t)^2. The z=0 case is constant. Continuous extension at zero proves concavity there too. Integrating preserves concavity and monotonicity. F(0)=0 and F(q)>0 for q>0.
The derivative argument is pointwise; no derivative is exchanged with an integral.

For 0<=q<=1, step 1 and Cauchy-Schwarz give
 q-F(q) >= (q^2/3) E[Z^4/(1+q Z^2)] >= q^2/[3(1+q)] >= q^2/6.
Cauchy-Schwarz uses E Z^2=1 and E(1+q Z^2)=1+q, with integrable nonnegative variables.
Also, using the probability measure with density Z^2 relative to Gaussian measure and Jensen for x -> 1/(1+q x),
 F(q) >= q E[Z^2/(1+q Z^2)] >= q/(1+3q) >= q/4.
The density integrates to one and its Z^2 mean is E Z^4=3.

3. Conditional sampling noise.
Set Y=tanh(sqrt(q) Z)^2. For 0<q<=1,
 E Y^2 <= q^2 E Z^4 =3q^2 <=48 F(q)^2.
Given the entire past, q_(l+1) is an average of n independent copies of Y with q=q_l. Hence
 E[q_(l+1)|past]=F(q_l),
 Var(q_(l+1)|past)<=48 F(q_l)^2/n.
No independence of q_l across layers is asserted. Since tanh^2<=1, all random and deterministic q_l lie in [0,1].

4. Relative error, before depth n/96.
Assume q_0>0. Every qbar_l>0. Set R_l=q_l/qbar_l, S_l=F(q_l)/F(qbar_l), v_l=E(R_l-1)^2.
Concavity, monotonicity and F(0)=0 imply that S_l lies between R_l and 1. This is valid also at q_l=0 by continuity. Thus
 (S_l-1)^2 <= (R_l-1)^2, S_l^2 <= 2(S_l-1)^2+2.
The conditional variance identity, with a deterministic denominator qbar_(l+1)>0, yields
 v_(l+1) = E(S_l-1)^2 + E Var(R_(l+1)|past)
 <= (1+96/n) v_l+96/n.
Starting at v_0=0, induction gives v_l <= (1+96/n)^l-1.
For 96l/n<=1, log(1+x)<=x and exp(x)-1<=2x on [0,1] imply
 v_l <=192l/n.
All moments used here are finite: for each fixed l, R_l<=1/qbar_l, a finite deterministic bound.

5. Signal decay.
Write mu_l=E q_l. Step 2 and E q_l^2>=mu_l^2 imply
 mu_(l+1)<=mu_l-mu_l^2/6.
The same inequality holds for qbar_l. For 0<a<=1, a-a^2/6>0 and
 1/[a(1-a/6)] >= 1/a+1/6.
Therefore, if a subsequent mean is positive, reciprocals increase by at least 1/6. A zero mean makes all subsequent signals zero. Thus
 mu_l, qbar_l <= 1/(q_0^(-1)+l/6) <= 6/l for l>=1.
The sharper first bound gives values <=1 at l=0 and avoids division by zero.

6. Coupling and splitting depths.
Use the same independent g for the two output vectors. Its mean squared normalized norm is one, so
 W_2^2 <= E(sqrt(q_l)-sqrt(qbar_l))^2,
where l=L-1.
For 1<=l<=n/96, using |sqrt(r)-1|<=|r-1| for all r>=0,
 E(sqrt(q_l)-sqrt(qbar_l))^2 <= qbar_l v_l <= (6/l)(192l/n)=1152/n.
For l>n/96, nonnegative square roots give (sqrt(a)-sqrt(b))^2<=a+b, hence
 E(sqrt(q_l)-sqrt(qbar_l))^2 <=mu_l+qbar_l <=12/l<1152/n.
At l=0 the error is zero. These cases exhaust every integer l, even when n<96 (the short positive-depth range is then empty). If q_0=0, both chains vanish identically. This proves the displayed uniform bound.

NETWORK INTERPRETATION.
Start with any deterministic activation vector a_0 of norm squared n q_0; let W_l have independent N(0,1/n) entries and set h_l=W_l a_(l-1), a_l=tanh(h_l). Fresh W_l implies the conditional law h_l=sqrt(q_(l-1))Z_l and q_l=||a_l||^2/n. Thus the scalar chain is exact, rather than an SDE or asymptotic surrogate. A scalar output readout has the identical bound without the vector normalization.

WHAT REMAINS.
This closes the dossier's one-input tanh absolute-rate obstruction if independently accepted. It does not prove the entire target for all critical chain programs. The next unpaid step is a multi-input tanh Gram estimate or a theorem covering a larger class of stable chains. Novelty relative to all literature is not yet established; source checks must accompany this result.


7. Joint Tensor Program trajectory (target 1).
Construct independent Gaussian vectors g_1,...,g_L on a single space. Recursively set h_j=sqrt(q_(j-1))g_j and q_j=||tanh(h_j)||^2/n. Simultaneously set hbar_j=sqrt(qbar_(j-1))g_j. The finite trajectory has the correct law by conditional Gaussianity of fresh weight matrices. The infinite-width trajectory has the correct joint law: its deterministic variances multiply independent Gaussian vectors. This independence is only across fresh layers; input correlations are not being modeled because there is just one input.

By the sum-of-squares Euclidean norm on the product of L normalized layer spaces,
 E sum_(j=1)^L ||h_j-hbar_j||^2/n <=1152 L/n.
Therefore W_2 of the joint normalized preactivation trajectories is at most sqrt(1152 L/n), uniformly for all L and n, including L<=n^(1-epsilon). If the program records postactivations as well, tanh is 1-Lipschitz, so the joint squared cost for pre- and postactivations is at most 2304 L/n. The initial deterministic input contributes zero cost.

This is a length-explicit quantitative forward Tensor Program statement on the one-input tanh chain family. It is a narrowed result, not a theorem for all critical chains or for transposed weights.

VERIFICATION RECORD.
Analytic side conditions have been checked in steps 1-6: q=0 separately, strict positivity of deterministic denominators, finiteness of relative moments at each finite depth, integrability in Cauchy-Schwarz/Jensen, and the integer depth split for n<96. scripts/verify_tanh.py independently checks Gaussian-integral inequalities numerically at q down to 1e-12 and verifies 54 finite/cutoff cases with exact rational arithmetic. These numerical integrals are diagnostics, not part of the proof. A convex counterexample F(q)=q^2 confirms that monotonicity without concavity would invalidate step 4. Full proof has not received independent review.

\big( \bs{x}_N,  \op{M} \, \bs{x}_N  \big) \, \leq \,  C \frac{\ln N}{N} \norm{ \bs{x}_N }^2 \quad   for   \,  all  \quad  \bs{x}_N \in \mc{V}^{(0)}_N \, .

\enq

Method: Integrator-authored exact restricted calculation or proof-obstruction analysis after primary-source comparison Result: For conductances c_xy=exp(beta*(h_x+h_y)), adding a constant a to the field multiplies every conductance by exp(2*beta*a) and every effective resistance by exp(-2*beta*a). This gives an exact normalization check. If m<=h_x<=M on the finite network, Rayleigh monotonicity gives exp(-2*beta*M)*R_unit<=R_h<=exp(-2*beta*m)*R_unit. Since the DGFF extrema are of logarithmic order, these elementary bounds leave a window of order log(N) in log resistance, far larger than the proposed sqrt(log(N)) scale. They cannot justify a Brownian maximum/minimum sandwich or a CGFF limit. The missing work is control of multiscale flows and cutsets that exploits cancellation and typical field structure. Check: Thomson's variational formula scales linearly with resistances, proving the constant-shift identity. Applying conductance monotonicity to the two constant networks gives the same bounds with the correct reversed signs. Obstruction: No tightness or limiting resistance field is identified; the incoming asserted Brownian-functional bounds are not retained.

Let a_1,...,a_m be independent N(0,I_n) vectors, n>=1, x in R^n fixed, and Omega a fixed nonempty compact subset of the Euclidean unit ball. Let g:R^2->R and K:R^n->[0,infinity) be fixed measurable functions. Define ||Y||_psi_p=inf{s>0:E exp(|Y|^p/s^p)<=2}, p=1,2. Assume tau,eta>0, sup_{z in Omega}||g(a^T z,a^T x)||_psi_1<=tau for a~N(0,I_n), and ||K(a)||_psi_2<=eta. Assume also that almost surely, for every z,z0 in Omega, m^(-1)sum_i |g(a_i^T z,a_i^T x)-g(a_i^T z0,a_i^T x)|<=m^(-1)sum_i K(a_i)|a_i^T(z-z0)|. This is Corollary2.2 p7 in an explicit unit-ball domain restriction, with its proof pp23-24; bounded sets of another fixed radius can first be rescaled. K(a_i) may depend on a_i.

Let independent iid walk increments on Z have P(X=0)=epsilon, P(X=+1)=(1-epsilon)p and P(X=-1)=(1-epsilon)(1-p), with 0<=epsilon<1 and 1/2<=p<=1; let S_0=0 and S_n=sum_{i=1}^n X_i. Independently let C_z be iid fair black/white scenery and Y_i=C_{S_i}. For n>=1 let CT_n be the set of k in {0,...,n-1} for which {S_0,...,S_k} and {S_{k+1},...,S_n} are disjoint AND S_k>=0. Define f(m)=sup_{n>=m}max_{y in {B,W}^n}max_{A subset {0,...,m-1}, |A|>=m/2} P(CT_n intersect A is empty | Y_1^n=y). There exists a neighborhood U of (1,0) in the allowed (p,epsilon) parameter rectangle such that for every (p,epsilon) in U, limsup_{m->infinity}(1/m)log f(m)<0, with log 0=-infinity. Thus even after conditioning on ANY future color word, the probability of avoiding every time in ANY deterministic set of at least m/2 candidate times decays exponentially, uniformly in the outer length n>=m. The neighborhood has not been identified with the entire p>4/5 region. This is a ONE-SIDED future-conditioned estimate. Source: A crossover for the bad configurations of random walk in random scenery, Definition 2.1 and equation (2.2), Lemma 2.4, PDF pages 6-7; proof Section 2.4, PDF pages 11-15.

[Lemma 4 (Bounded weak maximum principle) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] Let $D$ be a uniformly smooth domain, let $V\in L^\infty(D)$ be real, and
suppose
\[
 \lambda(-\Delta+V,D,\varrho)>0.
\]
If $w\in H^1_{\rm loc}(\overline D)\cap L^\infty(D)$ is a weak
supersolution of $(-\Delta+V)w\geq0$ with homogeneous $\cN_\varrho$
boundary condition, then $w\geq0$.  Here ``weak'' means the variational
inequality associated with the Robin form when $\varrho>0$; at
$\varrho=0$ we require the negative part of the trace to vanish and use
zero-trace test functions.

body: A probability law F on R is n-completely mixable with center mu if there exist n random variables X_1,...,X_n, all with law F, such that sum_i X_i=n*mu almost surely. No independence is required. If F is integrable, taking expectations forces mu=E[X]. Source: Wang, arXiv:1411.6190v3, Definition 3, p.4.

body:
[Lem 110 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $f:\R\to[0,\infty)$ be a smooth function which integrates to one and has compact support. Then the derivative of $f^{1/2}$ is uniformly bounded, that is,
	\[ \|(f^{1/2})'\|_\infty
	= \frac12 \bigg\|\frac{f'}{f^{1/2}}\bigg\|_\infty
	\le O(1)\,,\]
where $O(1)$ indicates a constant depending on $f$.

\begin{proof}
Since $f$ is smooth, we have $\|f''\|_\infty \le C$ where $C$ is a constant depending only on $f$. Assume without loss that $C$ is large. Now suppose $f(y)>0$ is small while $|f'|$ is large, say
$f'(y) \ge 2 C f(y)^{1/2}$. The bound on $f''$ implies $f'(x) \ge C f(y)^{1/2}$ for all $|x-y| \le f(y)^{1/2}$. It follows that
	\[
	f\Big(y-f(y)^{1/2}\Big)
	\le f(y) - Cf(y)^{1/2} \cdot f(y)^{1/2}
	< 0\,,
	\]
contradicting the assumption that $f\ge0$. The case $f'(y) \le - 2 C f(y)^{1/2}$ leads to a similar contradiction, so we conclude 
	\[\bigg\|\frac{f'}{f^{1/2}}\bigg\|_\infty
	\le 2C\,,
	\]
which proves the claim.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 110 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Definition Homological certificate of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Let
\(q \in \{ 0,\ldots,d\}\) and \(r > 0\). A finite family
\(\mathcal{A = \{}A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\}\) of measurable subsets of \(M\)
is a \emph{degree-}\(q\)\emph{, radius-}\(r\) \emph{homological
certificate} for \(M\) if every continuous path
\(\gamma:\lbrack 0,T\rbrack \rightarrow M\) hitting all targets in
\(\mathcal{A}\) satisfies
\(H_{q}\left( \operatorname{Tr}(\gamma)^{r} \right) \cong H_{q}(M)\). If the
implication holds simultaneously for every \(q = 0,\ldots,d\), then
\(\mathcal{A}\) is a \emph{full} homological certificate at radius
\(r\).
title: Homological certificate

[Theorem thm:expLPPgeoconv of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Fix $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$. Either let $\mathcal{M}_n$ equal $\mathcal{L}_n$ in Theorem (thm:expconv of the paper), or else let $\mathcal{M}_n$ equal $H_{\epsilon_n}$ in Theorem (thm:colorTASEPconv of the paper) for a sequence $\epsilon_n \to 0$. Consider a coupling where $\mathcal{M}_n \to \mathcal{L}^\rho$ almost surely, uniformly on compact sets. Then there exists a set $\Omega$ of probability $1$ such that on $\Omega$, the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
	\item Consider a sequence $(x_n, s; y_n, t) \to (x, s; y, t) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$ and a sequence of geodesics $\pi_n$ in $\mathcal{M}_n$ from $(x_n, s)$ to $(y_n, t)$. Then $\pi_n$ is precompact in the uniform topology and any subsequential limit of $\pi_n$ is a geodesic in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ from $(x, s)$ to $(y, t)$.
	\item If $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ contains a unique geodesic $\pi$ from $(x, s)$ to $(y, t)$, then $\pi_n \to\pi$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:expLPPgeoconv of arXiv:2604.10020

[Thm ABC of arXiv:2411.14090, '{\bf Exponential Ergodicity in $\W_1$ for SDEs with Distribution Dependent Noise and Parti'] Assume that for any $\mu\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$, there exists a unique invariant probability measure $\Gamma(\mu)\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$ to (equation GPS12 of the paper) such that $$\mathbb W_1((P_t^{\mu})^\ast\eta,\Gamma(\mu))\leq c_0\text{\rm{e}}^{-\lambda_0 t}\mathbb W_1(\eta,\Gamma(\mu)),\quad t\geq 0,\,\eta,\mu\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$$
for some constants $c_0\geq 1$ and $\lambda_0>0$ not depending on $\mu$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]
Suppose 
that there exists a continuous function $G:[0,\infty)\rightarrow[0,\infty)$ satisfying
$$\inf_{t>\frac{\log c_0}{\lambda_0}}\frac{G(t)}{1-c_0\text{\rm{e}}^{-\lambda_0 t}}\in[0,1)$$
such that
$$\mathbb W_1((P_t^{\mu_1})^\ast\Gamma(\mu_2),\Gamma(\mu_2))\leq  G(t)\mathbb W_1(\mu_1,\mu_2),\quad t\geq 0,\,\mu_1,\mu_2\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d).$$

 Then
there exists a unique invariant probability
measure $\mu^\ast\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$ 
for
(equation GPS of the paper).
\item[(ii)] 
Let $\nu\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$ be an invariant probability measure for (equation GPS of the paper).   Assume that there exist a constant $t_1>0$ and a continuous function $H:[0,t_1]\rightarrow[0,\infty)$ with
$$H(t_1)+c_0\text{\rm{e}}^{-\lambda_0 t_1}<1$$
such that $$\mathbb W_1(P_{t}^\ast\eta,(P_{t}^{\nu})^\ast\eta)\leq H(t)\mathbb W_1(\eta,\nu),\quad \eta\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d),\ \ t\in[0,t_1].$$
Then there exist constants $c,\lambda>0$ such that
$$\mathbb W_1(P_t^\ast\eta,\nu)\leq c\text{\rm{e}}^{-\lambda t}\mathbb W(\eta,\nu), \quad t\geq0,\, \eta\in\mathbb P_1(\mathbb R^d).$$
\end{enumerate}

DRAFT independently checked special-case derivation (w359 KEEP). For centered isotropic X=Exp(1)-1 observed through independent Gaussian noise of variance t>0, let Y=X+sqrt(t)G with independent G~N(0,1), nu_t=Law(Y), T_t f(y)=E[f(X)|Y=y], and D_rho(g)=integral |gprime|^2 d rho. Test f_a(x)=exp(a x), 0<a<1/2. A positive-tail calculation gives liminf as a increases to 1/2 of D_nu_t(T_t f_a)/D_mu(f_a)>=exp(-t/4). Hence any all-function coefficient q(t) must be at least exp(-t/4). At t=1 the explicit a=49/100 test has ratio greater than 7/10, using only the tail y>=5 in the untranslated observation coordinates. The exact Gaussian affine coefficient 1/4 at t=1 cannot hold for this law. This does not refute existence of some q<1.

0<a<1/2 ensures L2 and finite energy

body: Every elliptic curve over Q is modular: its L-function coincides with that of a weight-2 newform of level equal to the curve's conductor. Proved by Wiles and Taylor-Wiles for semistable curves (1995) - enough, with Ribet's level-lowering and Frey's construction, to yield Fermat's Last Theorem - and completed for all curves by Breuil-Conrad-Diamond-Taylor (2001). It is the GL_2 case of the Langlands program's bridge between arithmetic and automorphic forms.

body:
[Lemma eq:shuff0 of arXiv:2411.06827, 'The Exponential Lie Series and a Chen--Strichartz Formula for L{\'e}vy Processes'] With the notation of the previous section, we obtain
$$
	\mathrm{Id}=\sum\limits_{w\in{\mathbb A}^\ast}w\otimes\overline w=\sum\limits_{w^0\in({\mathbb A}^0)^\ast}w^0\otimes\overline w^0.
$$
Further, the expression of the coproduct in the basis $(\overline{\mathbb A}^0)^\ast$ of ${\mathbb R} {\langle}\overline{\mathbb A}{\rangle}$ dualises to the expression of the product $\star$  as a shuffle product in the basis $({\mathbb A}^0)^\ast$ of ${\mathbb R} {\langle}{\mathbb A}{\rangle}$:
\begin{align}
	(a_1^0\cdots a_n^0) \star (a_{n+1}^0\cdots a_{n+m}^0)
	&=\sum\limits_{\sigma\in Sh(n,m)}a^0_{\sigma(1)}\cdots a^0_{\sigma(n+m)} \\
	&=:(a_1^0\cdots a_n^0){\,\llcorner\!\llcorner\!\!\!\lrcorner\,} (a_{n+1}^0 \cdots a_{n+m}^0),
\end{align}
for  $a_i^0\in{\mathbb A}^0$, and where $Sh(n,m)$ stands for the set of permutations of $\{1,\ldots,n+m\}=:[n+m]$ such that $\sigma^{-1}(1) < \cdots < \sigma^{-1}(n)$ and $\sigma^{-1}(n+1)< \cdots < \sigma^{-1}(n+m)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma eq:shuff0 of arXiv:2411.06827

body: Let A and B be n by n normal matrices (A A* = A* A, B B* = B* B) with eigenvalues alpha_1, ..., alpha_n and beta_1, ..., beta_n respectively. Then there exists a permutation pi of {1, ..., n} such that sum_{i=1}^n |alpha_i - beta_{pi(i)}|^2 <= ||A - B||_F^2. When A and B are Hermitian, the eigenvalues are real and the minimizing permutation can be taken to pair them in matching sorted order. [Hoffman and Wielandt (1953); see Bhatia, Matrix Analysis]
title: Hoffman-Wielandt Inequality

body:
In a finite graph with inherited positive edge weights, give each simple n-edge path starting at a probability proportional to its product weight, with terminal vertex free, and assume positive total weight C_n(G;a). Define C_m(H;v) as the total weight of simple m-edge paths from v in H, with C_0=1 for a retained vertex. At a realized k-edge prefix eta, delete all its visited vertices except its tip to get G_eta. For a forbidden vertex or edge set A excluding a, the conditional avoidance probability is zero if the prefix hit A, and otherwise C_(n-k)(G_eta minus A;tip)/C_(n-k)(G_eta;tip). The denominator is positive on every realized prefix; at k=n use the avoidance indicator. Replacing C_(n-k) by an all-length partition sum changes the model.
Finite graph, fixed length n, positive inherited weights, C_n(G;a)>0
Free endpoint; no prescribed chordal terminal point
Only realized prefixes are divided by; forbidden vertices exclude the start

body: For an invertible matrix A and a choice of induced operator norm ||.||, the condition number of A is kappa(A) = ||A|| * ||A^{-1}||. For the linear system A*x = b, kappa(A) governs the worst-case amplification of relative perturbations: if (A+dA)(x+dx) = b+db for small perturbations dA, db, then to first order the relative error of the computed solution satisfies ||dx||/||x|| is bounded, up to a constant, by kappa(A) * ( ||dA||/||A|| + ||db||/||b|| ). In the matrix 2-norm, kappa_2(A) = sigma_max(A) / sigma_min(A), the ratio of the largest to smallest singular values of A. Always kappa(A) >= 1; a matrix with large kappa(A) is called ill-conditioned, and one with kappa(A) close to 1 is well-conditioned.
title: Condition Number of a Linear System

For sparse critical synchronous particle-hole parking on Z^d, d>=1, with iid signs +1 and -1 each of probability p, otherwise zero, 0<p<1/2, let A_t be active counts, H_t unfilled-hole indicators, h_t=E A_t(0)=E H_t(0), r=p/(1-2p). For every nonnegative measurable function F of the final fields, E[A_t(x)F(A_t-delta_x,H_t)]<=r E F(A_t,H_t), with the left argument evaluated only when A_t(x)>0. For falling factorials this implies E(A_t(x))_k<=r^(k-1)h_t, E A_t(x)^2<=(1+r)h_t and P(A_t(x)>0)>=(1-r/2)h_t. The deletion proof removes a never-settled label using independent per-label walks and fresh tie priorities. Novelty: KNOWN label-deletion method; UNCHECKED exact active-field bound. Status: independently checked proof.
0<p<1/2; iid sparse signs each p; d>=1
Law-equivalent independent per-label walks and fresh continuous tie priorities
F depends only on final active-count and hole fields

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:f0f1f4f868a9ade473d88f44a64378969a4cb4ef82c71af450008053b8cd89e8","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/f0/f0f1f4f868a9ade473d88f44a64378969a4cb4ef82c71af450008053b8cd89e8.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:55088415a049af5e8a9143cfc14291cb5e0f4cfd2f31ee7339c148e76a5f0314","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c18","bundle_id":"population.i0005-correlation-energy-and-active-moments-006","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"parking and comparison fields","draft":"w661/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:particle-hole-active-label-campbell-factorial-bound-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C18 v1: erasing an active label gives a Campbell bound

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN label-deletion method;
UNCHECKED this exact active-field bound. The claim concerns the actual
source process at every finite time, including long times at fixed p.

Use the sparse critical synchronous particle-hole law on Z^d, d>=1,
P(eta=1)=P(eta=-1)=p, P(eta=0)=1-2p, 0<p<1/2. Let A_t count active
particles, H_t indicate unfilled holes, h_t=E A_t(0)=E H_t(0), and
r=p/(1-2p). For every site x and every nonnegative measurable function
F of the final active-count and hole fields,

    E[A_t(x) F(A_t-delta_x,H_t)] <= r E[F(A_t,H_t)].

The left function is evaluated only when A_t(x)>0. Consequently, with
falling factorials and every integer k>=1,

    E(A_t(x))_k <= r^(k-1) h_t,
    E A_t(x)^2 <= (1+r)h_t,
    P(A_t(x)>0) >= (1-r/2)h_t.

The last inequality remains valid when its right side is negative, and
is informative for sparse p. In particular surviving active particles
have uniformly controlled multiplicities relative to their density.

## 1. A law-equivalent marked-label construction

Give each possible initial +1 excess particle a label equal to its origin
y, an independent infinite nearest-neighbor walk, and independent continuous
tie priorities at each round. At a hole, settle the smallest-priority
arriving label. This chooses uniformly among arrivals; fresh priorities
make it a construction of exactly the source law. All random variables
are assigned even to origins that do not initially have a particle.

If label y is active at x after round t, it has never settled during
those rounds. Delete it by changing eta(y)=1 to 0, keeping all assigned
walks and priorities. All other trajectories and hole fillings through t
are unchanged. Prove this round by round: at any unfilled hole visited
by y, some other label was the priority winner, since y remains active;
deleting a loser leaves the winner unchanged. Visits to filled holes
have no effect. Away from its presence nothing changes. Thus the final
fields after deletion are exactly A_t-delta_x,H_t.

This argument must use an active, never-settled label. Deleting a settled
particle can change which holes fill and does not have this property.
It uses per-label walks, a law-equivalent construction, rather than
pretending deletion leaves fixed site-stack indices unchanged.

## 2. Change of initial-sign weight and summation

For a fixed origin y, the deletion map is injective on the full assigned
randomness; the original sign is recovered as +1. Its measure changes by
the factor (1-2p)/p, so the contribution from that active label is at most

    r E[1{eta(y)=0} 1{X_t^y=x} F(A_t,H_t)].

The image also obeys constraints making the restored label stay active,
but dropping these constraints only increases the expectation. When
eta(y)=0 its assigned walk is unused by the base process and independent
of both final fields. Hence this bound equals

    r p_t(x-y) E[1{eta(y)=0}F(A_t,H_t)].

Sum over origins y. Every active particle at x has exactly one origin,
and Tonelli applies to nonnegative contributions. Since sum_y p_t(x-y)=1,

    E[A_t(x)F(A_t-delta_x,H_t)]
      <=r E[F(A_t,H_t) sum_y p_t(x-y)1{eta(y)=0}]
      <=r E F(A_t,H_t).

No independence of the survival events is used. At fixed t only finitely
many origins can reach x, so the sum also has a finite-propagation version.

## 3. Factorial moments and occupancy

Take F(A,H)=(A(x))_(k-1). For k>=2 the inequality gives
E(A_t(x))_k<=r E(A_t(x))_(k-1), proving the first assertion by induction
from E A_t(x)=h_t. The k=2 case yields
E A_t(x)^2=E(A_t(x))_2+h_t<=(1+r)h_t.

For each nonnegative integer n,
n-1{n>0}<=(n)_2/2. Taking expectations gives
h_t-P(A_t(x)>0)<=r h_t/2 and the occupancy bound.

## Source and scope

Primary model: Bou-Rabee--Panagiotis, arXiv:2609.02820v1, Section 2,
Theorem 1.6's sparse law, and the one-particle per-label walk construction
used in Proposition 8.3. Source (47) supplies equal mean active and hole
density. No stochastic domination of the whole field is claimed here;
the displayed Campbell inequality and its moment consequences are what
the proof establishes.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a1e8e0a4e9d3ea844deb3d838cd3e61ce199607ccdf1c6da584de03b25d96ae0","revision_digest":"sha256:0338898fa98bb9e72021d7b7d4eac6ac222ecfda345a3dd3b0133122e998134a","source_id":"owner-own-work:w661:I0005-C18:v1","source_revision":"v1; 2026-10-14T06:38:57.0934370+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Thm 8 of arXiv:2605.15501, 'Well-posedness of the obstacle problem for generalized Dean--Kawasaki equation\thanks{ The'] Let Assumption \ref{assu:assum for F} and Assumption \ref{assu:assu for unique} hold for $\xi^F, \psi, \Phi, \sigma$ and two initial functions $u_{1,\mathrm{init}}$ and $u_{2,\mathrm{init}}$.
Let $(u_{1},\nu_{1})$ and $(u_{2},\nu_{2})$ be stochastic kinetic solutions of the obstacle problem for \eqref{eq:main} in the sense of Definition \ref{def:def of stochastic kinetic solution} with initial data $u_{1,\mathrm{init}}$ and $u_{2,\mathrm{init}}$, respectively.
Let $\chi_{1}$ and $\chi_{2}$ be the kinetic functions of $u_{1}$ and $u_{2}$.

Then, almost surely, for almost every $s,t\in(0,T)$ with $s<t$,

\[
\int_{x,\xi} \big|\chi_{1}(x,\xi,t)-\chi_{2}(x,\xi,t)\big|^2\leq\int_{x,\xi} \big|\chi_{1}(x,\xi,s)-\chi_{2}(x,\xi,s)\big|^2.
\]
title: Thm 8 of arXiv:2605.15501

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Renewal-type argument on the cluster process viewed from the local maximum: depth-h count as a branching-like functional of the concentric decomposition. Result: Writing the cluster as the field pinned at a local maximum, e^{-alpha h} E nu(f_h) is the expected number of points at depth h weighted by e^{-alpha h}; the concentric decomposition expresses the cluster as a random walk with a Bessel-like entropic repulsion plus independent fine fields, so f_h is a sum over scales k <= log(h) of contributions, each of order e^{alpha h} times the probability that the walk is at height h at scale k. A renewal theorem for the walk under entropic repulsion would give the limit; the walk is not a true random walk (steps depend on scale through the binding fields), which is where the existing tools stop. Existence of the limit is therefore reduced to a scale-inhomogeneous renewal theorem. Obstruction: Scale inhomogeneity of the concentric-decomposition walk defeats the standard renewal theorem.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0006-existence-of-the-limit-of-e-alpha-h-e-nu-f-h-for-the-dgff-cluster-law
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved
title: Attempt on Existence of the limit of e^{-alpha h} E nu(f_h) for the DGFF cluster law

[Corollary 174 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Let $(f_h(z))_{h = 1}^{H}$ be an  tuple of functions independent of $\N$ and such that $f_h(z)$ is holomorphic in a complex neighborhood of $[\hat{a}_h,\hat{b}_h]$ for any $h \in [H]$. Under the conditions of Lemma~\ref{Lemma_glued_tilings_assumptions} and assuming that filling fractions are deterministically fixed, the random vector
\[
\left(\sum_{i = 1}^{N_h} f\bigg(\frac{\ell_i^{h}}{\N}\bigg) - \N \int_{\alpha_h}^{\beta_h} \tilde{\mu}_h(x)\dd x\right)_{h=1}^{H}
\]
is approximated in the sense of moments (Definition~\ref{Definition_convergence_moments}) by a centered Gaussian random vector with covariance
\[
\textnormal{\textsf{Cov}}[f_{h_1},f_{h_2}] = \oint_{\gamma_{h_1}}\oint_{\gamma_{h_2}} \frac{\dd z_1\dd z_2}{(2\ii\pi)^2}\,\mathcal{F}_{h_1,h_2}(z_1,z_2) f_{h_1}(z_1) f_{h_2}(z_2),
\]
where $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{F}}(z_1,z_2)$ is given by \eqref{eq_covariancepre} in terms of the bands of the simplified equilibrium measure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 174 of arXiv:2601.16377

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2604.05910, '\textbf{Well-posedness and Hurst parameter estimation for fluid equations driven by fracti'] Let $\xi \in \mathcal{B}_\infty$. We say that a process
$\omega \in C([0,T];\mathcal{B}_\alpha)
$
is a \emph{weak solution} to~\eqref{eq2} if for every test function
$\varphi \in \mathcal{B}_\infty = C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^2)$ and every $t \in [0,T]$, it holds almost surely that
\begin{align*}
\langle \omega_t,\varphi\rangle
&= \langle \omega_0,\varphi\rangle + \int_0^t\langle \omega_s, \Delta \varphi\rangle -\int_0^t \langle \omega_s, (u_s \cdot \nabla)\varphi\rangle ds - \int_0^t \langle \omega_s, (\xi \cdot \nabla)\varphi\rangle dW^H_s
\end{align*}
where $\langle \cdot,\cdot\rangle$ denotes the duality between distributions and smooth test functions on $\mathbb{T}^2$.

with \emph{floor constraint} $H_-$ and \emph{ceiling constraint}

Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have INDEPENDENT coordinates taking values in arbitrary measurable spaces, and let P be the product law on the product space. For a subset A and a point x define the convex distance d_T(x, A) = sup { inf_{y in A} sum_{i=1}^n alpha_i 1{x_i != y_i} : alpha in R^n, alpha_i >= 0, |alpha|_2 <= 1 }. Then for every measurable A, E[ exp( d_T(X, A)^2 / 4 ) ] <= 1 / P(A), and consequently P(A) P( d_T(X, A) >= t ) <= exp( - t^2 / 4 ) for every t > 0. COROLLARY for convex Lipschitz functions: if f : [0,1]^n -> R is CONVEX and 1-Lipschitz with respect to the Euclidean norm and the coordinates of X are independent with values in [0,1], then for every t > 0, P( |f(X) - M| >= t ) <= 4 exp( - t^2 / 4 ) where M is a median of f(X). The hypotheses are exactly: independence, a product structure, and for the corollary convexity together with a bounded range. Convexity cannot be dropped - the conclusion is false for general Lipschitz functions of bounded independent variables at this strength, which is why the bounded-differences (McDiarmid) inequality with its sum-of-squared-ranges denominator is the general-purpose tool and Talagrand's is the sharp one for convex functionals. The centring is at a MEDIAN; converting to the mean costs an absolute constant. [Talagrand (1995), Publ. IHES 81; see Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 7.11 and Section 7.4]
X has independent coordinates and P is a product measure
for the corollary: f convex and 1-Lipschitz for the Euclidean norm, coordinates valued in [0,1]

body: In theoretical computer science, the busy beaver game aims to find a terminating program of a given size that either produces the most output possible, or runs for the longest number of steps. Since an endlessly looping program producing infinite output or running for infinite time is easily conceived, such programs are excluded from the game. Rather than traditional programming languages, the programs used in the game are n-state Turing machines, one of the first mathematical models of computation.
title: Busy beaver

body: A family F of functions on a metric space (X,d) is equicontinuous at x if for every eps > 0 there is delta > 0 such that d(x,y) < delta implies |f(x) - f(y)| < eps for EVERY f in F simultaneously; uniformly equicontinuous if delta can be chosen independently of x. On a compact metric space, pointwise equicontinuity of the family implies uniform equicontinuity.
title: Equicontinuity

[Prop Main Proposition of arXiv:2411.07671, 'Long Time Behavior of General Markov Additive Processes'] Consider a MAP $((\xi,\Theta),\mathbb{P})$, such that Assumptions 1,2, and 3 are satisfied. Then, we have\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
 \item $\xi_t$ drifts to $-\infty$ $\:\mathbb{P}_{0,\pi}$-a.s., if and only if
 $\Bar{g}_\infty < \infty$  and $\underline{g}_\infty = \infty$   $\:\mathbb{P}_{0,\pi}$-a.s.
 \item $\xi_t$ drifts to $+\infty$ $\mathbb{P}_{0,\pi}$-a.s., if and only if $\Bar{g}_\infty = \infty$  and $\underline{g}_\infty < \infty$  $\:\mathbb{P}_{0,\pi}$-a.s.
\item $\xi_t$ oscillates $\mathbb{P}_{0,\pi}$-a.s., if and only if $\Bar{g}_\infty = \infty$  and $\underline{g}_\infty = \infty$  $\:\mathbb{P}_{0,\pi}$-a.s.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics, the axiom of choice, abbreviated AC or AoC, is an axiom of set theory. Informally put, the axiom of choice says that given any collection of non-empty sets, one can identify another set containing one element chosen from each set, even if the collection is infinite. Formally, the axiom establishes existence rather than a construction; it states that for every set I and every I-indexed family (S_i)_{i in I} of nonempty sets, there exists an I-indexed set (x_i)_{i in I} of elements of the union of the S_i such that x_i in S_i for every i in I. The axiom of choice was formulated in 1904 by Ernst Zermelo in order to formalize his proof of the well-ordering theorem.
title: In mathematics, the axiom of choice, abbreviated AC or AoC, is an axiom of set theory
