[Theorem 1 (Samuels' conjecture) of arXiv:2608.18392, 'On Samuels' Conjecture'] For every integer $n\geq1$, ordered mean vector $0\leq\mu_1\leq\cdots\leq\mu_n$, and $\lambda>\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i$,
\begin{equation}
c(\bm{\mu},\lambda)
=
\min_{1\leq i\leq n} q_i(\bm{\mu},\lambda)
=
\min_{1\leq i\leq n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left( 1- \frac{\mu_j}{ \lambda-\sum_{k=1}^{i-1}\mu_k } \right).

\end{equation}
The bound is sharp and is attained. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Samuels' conjecture

body:
[Dfn 223 (relaxed domains) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\dist(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote the Euclidean distance in $\R^N$, and define
\beq
\begin{aligned}
    S_N(\iota)
    &\equiv\bigg\{\bx\in\R^N :
    \frac{\dist(\bx,S_N)}{N^{1/2}} \le \iota
    \bigg\}\,, &
    \Sigma_N(\iota)
    &\equiv\bigg\{\bx\in\R^N :
    \frac{\dist(\bx,\Sigma_N)}{N^{1/2}} \le \iota
    \bigg\}\,.
\end{aligned}\eeq
We call $S_N(\iota)$ the \textbf{$\iota$-relaxed spherical domain},
and $\Sigma_N(\iota)$  the \textbf{$\iota$-relaxed Ising domain}.\footnote{While these relaxed domains are needed in the Ising setting for the notion of a Lipschitz algorithm to make sense, any point in $S_N(\iota)$ or $\Sigma_N(\iota)$ can be rounded to a point in $S_N$ or $\Sigma_N$ with nearly the same performance; see Remark~\ref{r:relaxed-wlog}.}
title: relaxed domains

body:
Let (M_k) be a martingale (or supermartingale for the upper tail) with respect to a filtration, with bounded increments |M_k - M_{k-1}| <= c_k almost surely. Then for all t > 0, P(M_n - M_0 >= t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2 sum of c_k^2)), and symmetrically for the lower tail: martingales with bounded steps concentrate like sums of independent bounded variables.

More explicitly, let (M_k)_{k=0}^n be an integrable real martingale with respect to a filtration (F_k), with |M_k-M_{k-1}| <= c_k almost surely for deterministic constants c_k >= 0. Write V = sum_{k=1}^n c_k^2. If V > 0 and t > 0, each of P(M_n-M_0 >= t) and P(M_n-M_0 <= -t) is at most exp(-t^2/(2V)), and P(|M_n-M_0| >= t) <= 2 exp(-t^2/(2V)). With the same increment bounds, the upper-tail inequality holds for supermartingales and the lower-tail inequality for submartingales. If V = 0 all increments vanish almost surely and all these tail probabilities are zero.
(M_k) a martingale for the given filtration
increments bounded: |M_k - M_{k-1}| <= c_k a.s.

[Proposition 4 (Equivariance of the flow-matching minimizer) of arXiv:2608.26961, 'Gromov--Monge Flow Matching for Equivariant Graph Generation'] Let $\pi\in\mathrm{c}_{\R^D}(\mu,\nu)$ be diagonally $G$-invariant and let
$v^\pi$ denote the minimizer of $J_\pi$ in \eqref{minvr}. Then $v^\pi$
admits a $G$-equivariant representative. More precisely, there exists a
jointly Borel field $\bar v:I\times\R^D\to\R^D$ such that
\[
\bar v_t=v_t^\pi
\qquad
\mu_t\text{-a.e. for a.e. }t\in I,
\]
and
\[
\bar v_t(gz)=g\bar v_t(z)
\qquad
\text{for every }g\in G,\ z\in\R^D,\ t\in I .
\]

\[
    \rho(q)=\mathbb{E}[X_0^q+X_1^q]<1,
\]
then
\[
    \sup_{n\ge0}\mathbb{E}[M_n^q]<\infty,
    \qquad
    \mathbb{E}[M^q]<\infty .
\]

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2605.13727, 'Stochastic evolution equations\\ driven by arbitrary cylindrical Lévy processes'] Let $T>0$. On the space of \(H\)-valued, adapted, c\`adl\`ag processes on \([0,T]\), define a quasi-metric \(\rho_T^{\mathrm{em}}\) by setting, for each pair of processes \(X,Y\) in this space,
\[
\rho_T^{em}(X,Y)=  \sup_{\Gamma \in \mathcal{S}_{{\rm prd}}^{1, {\rm op}}}E\Bigg[
\norm{\Gamma(0)(X-Y)(0)+ \int_{(0,T]} \Gamma(s)\, \d(X-Y)( s)}\wedge 1 \Bigg].
\]
Then $\rho_T^{\rm em}$ and $d_T^{\rm em}$ generate the same topology on the space of $H$-valued, adapted, c\`adl\`ag processes on $[0, T]$.
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2605.13727

Let f(z) = sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n z^n be an entire function with positive coefficients that is Hayman-admissible. Let r_n be the unique positive solution to r f'(r) / f(r) = n, and let b(r) = r (r f'(r)/f(r))'. Then as n -> \infty, the coefficients satisfy a_n ~ \frac{f(r_n)}{r_n^n \sqrt{2 \pi b(r_n)}}.
f is a Hayman-admissible entire function

\[
\frac{\tau_{N,\theta}^{(s)}}{N}\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{\mathbb{P}}\frac{\alpha_{s,\theta}}{\lambda},
\]
where $\alpha_{s,\theta}$ is the unique solution of
\[
(1-s)\int_0^1 x^{-s}\Bigl(1-e^{-(1-s)\alpha x^{-s}}\Bigr)\,dx=\theta.
\]

[Definition 15 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Fix a set $\Sigma = \llbracket 1 , N \rrbracket$ with $N \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ and an interval $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$.  A $\Sigma$-indexed line ensemble $\mathcal{L}$ on $\Lambda$ is said to satisfy the {\em partial Brownian Gibbs property} if and only if it is non-intersecting and for any finite set $K = \{k_1, k_1 + 1, \dots, k_2 \} \subset \Sigma$ with $k_2 \leq N - 1$, $[a,b] \subset \Lambda$ and any bounded Borel-measurable function $F: C(K \times [a,b]) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ we have $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E} \left[ F(\mathcal{L}|_{K \times [a,b]}) {\big \vert} \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}} (K \times (a,b))  \right] =\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{avoid}}^{a,b, \vec{x}, \vec{y}, f, g} \bigl[ F(\tilde{\mathcal{Q}}) \bigr].
\end{equation}
On the left side of (\ref{Eq.PBGP}), we have that
$$\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}} (K \times (a,b)) = \sigma \left \{ \mathcal{L}_i(s): (i,s) \in \Sigma \times \Lambda \setminus K \times (a,b) \right\},$$
and $ \mathcal{L}|_{K \times [a,b]}$ is the restriction of $\mathcal{L}$ to the set $K \times [a,b]$. [campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked] This is a proved finite special case and lower bound for Afonso S. Bandeira's Open Problem 11, How many deviations are needed afterall?, in Did just a couple of deviations suffice all along? (problems 10-14), Randomstrasse 101 (19 December 2024; https://randomstrasse101.math.ethz.ch/posts/HowManyDeviations/). For an n-by-n matrix A with entries in {+1,-1}, define disc(A)=min_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity, where ||y||_infinity=max_i |y_i|, and let D_n=max_{A in {+1,-1}^{n-by-n}} disc(A). One has D_9=5. An attaining matrix is specified by its nine rows ---++++++; -+---++++; +---++-++; +++++--++; +-+----++; ++--+++-+; +--+-++-+; -+-+-+--+; --+-+---+, with + meaning +1 and - meaning -1. Every sign colouring has some row dot product of absolute value at least five; the next possible discrepancy level is excluded by the counting bound. Therefore sup_{n>=1} D_n/sqrt(n)>=5/3, attained as a finite-size lower bound by this matrix. This result does not determine the supremum over all n. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
All entries are signs; discrepancy uses all sign colourings.

Let G = (V, E) be a finite connected graph with vertex degrees d(v), volume vol(S) = sum_{v in S} d(v), and for a vertex set S with 0 < vol(S) <= vol(V)/2 let phi(S) = e(S, V - S) / vol(S) be its conductance, where e(S, V - S) counts the edges leaving S. The conductance (Cheeger constant) of G is phi(G) = min over such S of phi(S). Let 0 = lambda_1 < lambda_2 <= ... <= lambda_n <= 2 be the eigenvalues of the normalised Laplacian L = I - D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}. CHEEGER'S INEQUALITY (Alon-Milman, Sinclair-Jerrum, Dodziuk; the graph form of Cheeger's 1970 Riemannian inequality): lambda_2 / 2 <= phi(G) <= sqrt(2 lambda_2). For a d-regular graph with adjacency eigenvalues d = mu_1 >= mu_2 >= ..., lambda_2 = (d - mu_2)/d and the edge expansion h(G) = min e(S, V-S)/|S| (over |S| <= n/2) satisfies (d - mu_2)/2 <= h(G) <= sqrt(2 d (d - mu_2)). Both sides are sharp up to constants: the cycle C_n has phi of order 1/n and lambda_2 of order 1/n^2 (so the square root is needed), while the hypercube and expanders have phi and lambda_2 of the same order. Consequences: a graph is an expander (phi bounded below) if and only if it has a spectral gap bounded below; the mixing time of the random walk is O(log(n) / lambda_2) and at least of order 1/phi; the sweep cut of the second eigenvector (the proof of the upper bound) is the spectral partitioning algorithm, with the guarantee phi(S) <= sqrt(2 lambda_2) for the set it returns; higher-order Cheeger inequalities (Lee-Oveis Gharan-Trevisan) relate lambda_k to k-way partitions, and the improved Cheeger inequality bounds phi by lambda_2 / sqrt(lambda_3).
G finite, connected, undirected, without isolated vertices (weighted graphs work verbatim with weighted degrees and volumes)
the spectral gap is that of the NORMALISED Laplacian; for regular graphs it is (d - mu_2)/d, and the unnormalised version scales by d
conductance is measured against volume; the vertex-count edge expansion h(G) is the same quantity only for regular graphs

[Lemma Ito formula of arXiv:2605.16963, 'Stochastic Euler Equations with Pseudo-differential Noise: Continuous and Discontinuous Pe'] Let \(\mathbb H\) be a Hilbert space and \(X\) a process given by
		\[
		X(t) = X_0 + \int_0^t a(t') \, \mathrm{d}t' + \int_0^t \int_{|l| \le 1} f(l,t') \, \widetilde{\eta}(\mathrm{d}l,\mathrm{d}t'), \quad t \geq 0,
		\]
		where \(a \in \mathscr{M}([0,\infty); \mathbb H) \cap L^1([0,\infty); \mathbb H)\) and \(f\) is a predictable \(\mathbb H\)-valued process satisfying
		$$
		\int_0^t \int_{|l| \le 1} \|f(l, t')\|_{\mathbb H}^2 \, \nu(\mathrm{d}l) \mathrm{d}t' < \infty\quad \text{for each } t > 0.
		$$
		Let \(\mathbb{S}\) be a separable Hilbert space and \(\phi: \mathbb H \rightarrow \mathbb{S}\) be a function of class \(C^1\) such that its Fr\'{e}chet derivative \(\phi': \mathbb H \rightarrow \mathcal{L}(\mathbb H; \mathbb{S})\) is locally Lipschitz continuous. Then, for every \(t > 0\), we have ${\mathbb P}\text{-}{\rm a.s.}$,
		\begin{align*}
			\phi(X(t)) - \phi(X_0) =\ & \int_0^t \Big[\phi'(X(t'-))\Big](a(t')) \, \mathrm{d}t'  + \int_0^t \int_{|l| \le 1} \bigg\{ \phi\Big(X(t'-) + f(l,t')\Big) - \phi(X(t'-))  \bigg\}\, \widetilde{\eta}(\mathrm{d}l,\mathrm{d}t')\\
			& + \int_0^t \int_{|l| \le 1} \bigg\{ \phi\Big(X(t'-) + f(l,t')\Big) - \phi(X(t'-)) - \Big[\phi'(X(t'-))\Big](f(l,t')) \bigg\}\, \nu(\mathrm{d}l)\mathrm{d}t'.
		\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2606.30349, 'Attenuated Poisson Dirichlet approximations for divisibility configurations'] Let \(X,Y,Z\) be \(\mathbf N(\mathbbm X)\)-valued random variables defined on a common probability space, and let \(B\subset \mathbf N(\mathbbm X)\) be measurable. Suppose that

\begin{align*}
p
:=
\Pb[Z\in B]\wedge \Pb[Y\in B]
>
0.
\end{align*}

Assume moreover that \(X\in B\) on the event \(\{Z\in B\}\), and that \(B\) has finite diameter with respect to \(\mathfrak d\), namely

\begin{align*}
D_B
:=
\sup_{\eta,\zeta\in B}\mathfrak d(\eta,\zeta)
<
\infty.
\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align*}
d_W\left(
\mathcal L(X\mid Z\in B),
\mathcal L(Y\mid Y\in B)
\right)
\le
\frac{\E[\mathfrak d(X,Y)]}{p}
+
\frac{2D_B}{p}\,
\Pb\big[\{Z\in B\}\Delta\{Y\in B\}\big].
\end{align*}
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2606.30349

body:
[Proposition prop:opmatch of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] Let $(H_{t})$ be a Hermitian Brownian motion as in \S(sec:dyson of the paper) and let
$X^{N}$ solve the Hermitian SDE
\begin{equation}
  \mathrm{d} X^{N}_{t}=b\big(X^{N}_{t}\big)\mathrm{d} t
  +\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\,f\big(X^{N}_{t}\big)\,\mathrm{d} H_{t}\,f\big(X^{N}_{t}\big).
\end{equation}
Then the eigenvalues satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \mathrm{d}\lambda_{i}=b(\lambda_{i})\,\mathrm{d} t
  +\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{f(\lambda_{i})^{2}f(\lambda_{j})^{2}}
  {\lambda_{i}-\lambda_{j}}\,\mathrm{d} t
  +\frac{f(\lambda_{i})^{2}}{\sqrt N}\,\mathrm{d} B_{i},
\end{equation}
with $(B_{i})$ independent standard Brownian motions. Consequently, whenever
$L_{N}(0)\to\mu_{0}$, the empirical spectral distribution converges to the solution of
the continuity equation with velocity (equation eq:opvelocity of the paper); that is, the free
equation (equation eq:opsde of the paper) and the matrix equation (equation eq:opmatrix of the paper) have the same
spectral limit.

body:
[Lemma lem:Mstat of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] For $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$, take any half-space pre-landscape $\mathcal{M}^\rho$, continuously extended to $\mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$, and  the half-space stationary horizon $\mathcal{H}^\mathsf{DL} \in \mathcal D([2\rho \vee 0, \infty), \mathbb{R}, 2\rho \vee 0)$ from Theorem (T:half-stationary-horizon of the paper) (denoting that $\mathcal{H}^\mathsf{DL}_\lambda(x) = \mathcal{H}^\mathsf{DL}(\lambda,x)$).
Then for any $\lambda\ge 2\rho \vee 0$, we have
$$
\mathcal{H}^\mathsf{DL}_{\lambda}\diamond \mathcal{M}^\rho_{0, t} - (\mathcal{H}^\mathsf{DL}_{\lambda}\diamond \mathcal{M}^\rho_{0, t})(0)\stackrel{d}{=} \mathcal{H}^\mathsf{DL}_{\lambda} \stackrel{d}{=} \mathcal{M}^\rho_{0, t}\diamond\mathcal{H}^\mathsf{DL}_{\lambda} - (\mathcal{M}^\rho_{0, t}\diamond\mathcal{H}^\mathsf{DL}_{\lambda})(0) .
$$
Moreover, when $\lambda=2|\rho|$, $\mathcal{H}^\mathsf{DL}_{\lambda}$ is a Brownian motion with slope $-2\rho$.

[Corollary 5 (The value at the mode) of arXiv:2608.13631, 'The classical discrete laws near the mode:\\ complete local expansions for the negative bi'] Let $k^{*}=\lfloor(r-1)q/p\rfloor$ and $f=\{(r-1)q/p\}$, so that
	$t^{*}=k^{*}-\mu=-\tfrac qp-f$.  Then
	\begin{equation}
		\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}\;P(k^{*})
		=1+\frac{5}{12\,r}-\frac{B_2(f)}{2\sigma^{2}}+O(r^{-2}) :
	\end{equation}
	the fractional part of the mode threshold enters exactly through $B_2(f)$, and the constant
	$\tfrac5{12}$ is independent of $p$.

[Thm cty of arXiv:2507.02518, '{\bf Exponential Ergodicity in Relative Entropy and $L^2$-Wasserstein Distance for non-equ'] Assume {\bf (C)}. There exist  $K_*,c,\tilde c,\lambda>0$, depending on $d$ and on the constants in {\bf (C)} except on $K_I$, such that, provided $K_I\leqslant K_*$, then  (equation Degth of the paper) has a unique stationary solution $\bar{\mu}\in\mathscr P_2(\mathbb R^{2d})$,
\begin{align}\mathbb W_2(P_t^\ast\mu_0,\bar{\mu})\leq c\text{\rm{e}}^{-\lambda t}\mathbb W_2(\mu_0,\bar{\mu}),\ \ t\geq 0, \mu_0\in\mathscr P_2(\mathbb R^{2d}),
\end{align}
and

\begin{align} \mathrm{Ent}(P_t^\ast\mu_0|\bar{\mu})\leq \tilde{c}\text{\rm{e}}^{-2\lambda t}\mathrm{Ent}(\mu_0|\bar{\mu}),~ t\geq 1, \mu_0\in\mathscr P_2(\mathbb R^{2d}).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Under the five hypotheses in assumptions, set b=E sigma'(Z), a=E[sigma'(Z)^2], q_l=(b^2)^(L-l), r_l=a^(L-l) for l=0,...,L-1, and r_plus=sum_(l=0)^(L-1)(r_l-q_l). Define M_n=r_plus*I_n+X_L^T X_L+sum_(l=0)^(L-1) q_l X_l^T X_l. Almost surely, n^(-1)*||K_NTK-M_n||_F^2->0, and ||K_NTK||_op is bounded eventually by a constant. Consequently K_NTK and M_n have the same weak limiting empirical spectral distribution whenever either limit exists. The source subsequently proves existence. If b=0, all q_l vanish, so the limiting NTK spectrum is that of r_plus*I_n+X_L^T X_L. This is an assertion about empirical spectral distributions at initialization, not convergence of individual extreme eigenvalues. The smoothness assumption excludes ReLU from this stated theorem.
Fixed integer depth L>=1; n,d_0,...,d_L tend to infinity; n/d_l->gamma_l in (0,infinity) for l=1,...,L.
All weights W_l in R^(d_l by d_(l-1)) and w in R^d_L have independent N(0,1) entries, independent of the input matrices.
sigma:R->R is twice differentiable with globally bounded first and second derivatives. For Z~N(0,1), E sigma(Z)=0 and E sigma(Z)^2=1.
X_0 is (epsilon_n,B)-orthonormal as in the companion definition for constant B, epsilon_n*n^(1/4)->0; the ESD of X_0^T X_0 converges to a deterministic probability measure mu_0.
X_l=d_l^(-1/2)*sigma(W_l X_(l-1)); scalar output f_theta(X_0)=w^T X_L; theta contains all hidden and readout weights; K_NTK=(grad_theta f)^T grad_theta f at random initialization.

[Definition D:substrateSpace of arXiv:2606.03079, 'Mean Field Limits for Stochastic, Underdamped Reactive Langevin Dynamics Models'] We define the substrate particle position and velocity product space analogously to $\mathbb{I}^{(\ell)}$ as
$$\mathbb{X}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V}^{(\ell)} \in (\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d)^{|\alpha^{(\ell)}|},
$$
with $\mathbb{X}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V}^{(\ell)} \supseteq (\bm{x},\bm{v}) =\bigl((x_{1}^{(1)},{v}_{1}^{(1)}), \cdots, (x_{\alpha_{\ell 1}}^{(1)},{v}_{\alpha_{\ell 1}}^{(1)}), \cdots, (x_{1}^{(J)},{v}_{1}^{(J)}), \cdots, (x_{\alpha_{\ell J}}^{(J)},{v}_{\alpha_{\ell J}}^{(J)})\bigr)$. For $(\bm{x},\bm{v}) \in \mathbb{X}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V}^{(\ell)}$, a sampled substrate position and velocity configuration for one individual $\mathcal{R}_{\ell}$ reaction, $x_{r}^{(j)}$ then labels the sampled position for the $r$th substrate particle of species $j$ involved in the reaction, and ${v}_{r}^{(j)}$ labels the sampled velocity for the same substrate particle. Let $d \bm{x}d \bm{v}=\bigl(\bigwedge_{j=1}^{J}(\bigwedge_{r=1}^{\alpha_{\ell j}} d x_{r}^{(j)}d v_{r}^{(j)})\bigr)$ be the corresponding volume form on $\mathbb{X}^{(\ell)}\otimes \mathbb{V}^{(\ell)}$ which also naturally defines an associated Lebesgue measure.
title: Definition D:substrateSpace of arXiv:2606.03079

On the Euclidean space R^d, a family of probability measures M subset M_1(Pi(R^d)) is regular if and only if for every x in R^d and R > 0, lim_{N -> infinity} sup_{mu in M} mu(N_{r, R}^x(Gamma) >= N) = o(r^{d-1}) as r -> 0.
Ambient space is R^d

Let mu be a product probability measure on {0,1}^n (Harris 1960), or more generally a measure on a finite distributive lattice satisfying the FKG lattice condition mu(x v y) mu(x ^ y) >= mu(x) mu(y) (Fortuin, Kasteleyn, Ginibre 1971). If A and B are both increasing events, then mu(A and B) >= mu(A) mu(B); equivalently, for increasing functions f and g, E[f g] >= E[f] E[g]. The same holds when both are decreasing. If one event is increasing and the other decreasing, the inequality reverses: mu(A and B) <= mu(A) mu(B). The inequality says nothing about a pair of events that are neither increasing nor decreasing, and it fails for a general (non-FKG) measure.
mu is a product measure on {0,1}^n, or satisfies the FKG lattice condition (log-supermodular)
A and B are both increasing (or both decreasing) events; f and g both monotone in the same direction
the reversed inequality needs one increasing and one decreasing event
no conclusion for events that are not monotone, and none for a non-FKG measure

[Lemma lem:fold of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $\mathcal F$ be an enterable distance-hereditary one-front fold with
ordered formal ports $x_1,\ldots,x_p$ on its carrier arcs.  For an incoming
two-front state $\Xi$, its open tensor has an identity
\[
 \mathcal F(x_1,\ldots,x_p)[\Xi]
 =\sum_\nu a_\nu
 u_\nu(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\,\Xi\,
 v_\nu(x_1,\ldots,x_p),
\tag{2.4.3}
\]
where every port variable occurs exactly once, every fixed letter in
$u_\nu,v_\nu$ is a safe gate or signed isometry, and
$\sum_\nu|a_\nu|\le A^s$ for a fold with $s$ coefficient occurrences.
After substituting safe words $X_i$ for the ports,
\[
 \|\mathcal F(X_1,\ldots,X_p)[\Xi]\|_1
 \le A^sK^s\left(\prod_i\|X_i\|\right)\|\Xi\|_1.
\tag{2.4.4}
\]

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be geodesic vector spaces, and let $c: X \times Y \to \R$ be a continuous cost function that is $1$-homogeneous in each variable. Let $1 < p, q < \infty$ such that $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} = 1$. Let $K \subset X$ and $L \subset Y$ be compact, geodesically convex sets containing the origin in their respective interiors. Then,
\[
\Ld c\left(\frac{\|\cdot\|_K^p}{p}\right)(y)=\frac{\|y\|_{K^{\circ, c}}^q}{q} \quad \text{and} \quad \Lu c\left(\frac{\|\cdot\|_L^q}{q}\right)(x)=\frac{\|x\|_{L^{\star, c}}^p}{p}.
\]
title: Proposition 17 of arXiv:2609.01460

body:
Let $X_1, \dots, X_n$ be i.i.d. with mean $\theta \ge 0$ and variance $\sigma^2$, and let the estimator respect the constraint: $\hat\theta_n = \max(0, \bar X_n)$. When the true parameter is interior ($\theta > 0$) the nonparametric bootstrap is consistent: the conditional law of $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n^* - \hat\theta_n)$ converges to $N(0, \sigma^2)$, the law of $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n - \theta)$. When the true parameter is on the boundary ($\theta = 0$) it is not: $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n - \theta) \Rightarrow \max(0, Z)$ with $Z \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$, a law with an atom of mass $1/2$ at zero, whereas the bootstrap law of $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n^* - \hat\theta_n)$ converges, conditionally on the data, to the law of $\max(0, Z + \zeta) - \max(0, \zeta)$ with $\zeta \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ a random shift that does not vanish - so the bootstrap distribution is random in the limit and does not equal the sampling distribution (Andrews 2000, Theorem 1). The same failure holds for maximum-likelihood and least-squares estimators under inequality constraints whenever the true parameter has an active constraint, in particular for nonnegatively constrained regression and portfolio weights with coordinates at zero: the bootstrap replicates flip the constrained coordinates between zero and positive values, and the spread of the replicates is not the spread of the estimator. Consistent alternatives: the $m$-out-of-$n$ bootstrap with $m \to \infty$, $m/n \to 0$, and subsampling, both of which recover the limit law at the boundary.

Bootstrap law: conditionally on the data, $\\sqrt n(\\bar X_n^* - \\bar X_n) \\Rightarrow Z^*$ with $Z^* \\sim N(0, \\sigma^2)$ independent of the data (the ordinary bootstrap CLT), and $\\sqrt n \\bar X_n = \\zeta_n$ is itself a random variable converging in law to $\\zeta \\sim N(0, \\sigma^2)$ that the bootstrap conditions on. Then $\\sqrt n(\\hat\\theta_n^* - \\hat\\theta_n) = \\max(0, \\sqrt n \\bar X_n^*) - \\max(0, \\sqrt n \\bar X_n) = \\max(0, Z^* + \\zeta_n) - \\max(0, \\zeta_n)$, whose conditional law converges to that of $\\max(0, Z^* + \\zeta) - \\max(0, \\zeta)$ given $\\zeta$. For this to equal the law of $\\max(0, Z)$ for almost every $\\zeta$ is impossible: for $\\zeta > 0$ the bootstrap statistic is $\\max(0, Z^* + \\zeta) - \\zeta = \\max(-\\zeta, Z^*)$, whose law has an atom of mass $\\Phi(-\\zeta/\\sigma)$ at $-\\zeta$, no atom at zero, and positive mass on negative values, whereas $\\max(0, Z)$ has an atom of mass $1/2$ at zero and no mass below it; so the bootstrap is inconsistent, and since $\\zeta$ is nondegenerate the bootstrap limit is random. The $m$-out-of-$n$ repair: with $m/n \\to 0$, $\\sqrt m \\bar X_n = o_p(1)$, so the shift vanishes and $\\sqrt m(\\hat\\theta_m^* - \\hat\\theta_n) \\Rightarrow \\max(0, Z)$ conditionally. =

&+\int_0^t \langle \mathsf{L}_{\mu(s)}\varphi,\mu(s)\rangle\,\de s \nonumber\\

body: Let (X,Sigma,mu) be a probability space and T: X -> X a measure-preserving transformation. T is ergodic if every T-invariant measurable set has measure 0 or 1: whenever A in Sigma satisfies T^{-1}A = A up to a mu-null set, mu(A) is 0 or 1. Equivalently, T is ergodic iff every T-invariant measurable function f (f(Tx)=f(x) a.e.) is a.e. constant; equivalently, by the Birkhoff ergodic theorem, iff for every f in L^1(X,mu) the time averages (1/N) sum_{n=0}^{N-1} f(T^n x) converge a.e. to the constant integral_X f dmu.

Let H = (L, R, E) be a finite bipartite graph and take the network with a source s, a sink t, arcs s->u of capacity 1 for u in L, arcs u->v for each edge uv, and arcs v->t of capacity 1 for v in R, the middle arcs carrying positive integer capacities. In every feasible integral s-t flow, the middle arcs with positive flow carry exactly one unit each and form a matching whose size is the flow value; conversely, every matching gives an integral flow of the same value, one unit along each path s-u-v-t. The integrality is needed: in the network on K_{2,2}, flow 1/2 on each of the four middle arcs and 1 on each terminal arc is a maximum flow of value 2 whose support is not a matching. Integer capacities guarantee that some maximum flow is integral, not that every one is.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] Let $\{ C_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be uniformly random elements of $[m]\coloneqq\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$, and let
$\{ U_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be uniformly random elements of $(0, 1)$.
Assume the family $\{ U_n, C_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is independent.
The random variable $C_n$ denotes the coupon type
obtained on day $n$.
Define the random variables
\[
  L(i, n) \coloneqq \sup\{ k \leqslant n \mid C_k = i \}, \quad i \in [m], \quad n > 0.
\]
Then $L(i, n)$ is the most recent day no later than $n$ that coupon
type $i$ was issued.
For clumsiness probability $p \in [0, 1)$, the 
clumsy coupon collection time can be defined by
\[
  T_{m, p} \coloneqq \inf \{ n > 0 \mid L(i, n) > 0 \ \text{and} \ U_{L(i, n)} \leq 1 - p \ 
    \text{for all $i \in [m]$} \},
\]
the first day that every coupon type has been updated, their most
recent updates all having been non-clumsy.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2605.14206

body: Let L/K be a finite Galois extension with Galois group G = Gal(L/K). There is an inclusion-reversing bijection between subgroups H of G and intermediate fields K <= E <= L, given by H -> Fix(H) (the fixed field of H) and E -> Gal(L/E), and these two maps are mutually inverse. Under this correspondence [L:E] = |Gal(L/E)| and [E:K] equals the index [G : Gal(L/E)]. A subgroup H is normal in G if and only if the corresponding field E = Fix(H) is itself Galois over K, in which case Gal(E/K) is isomorphic to the quotient group G/H.
title: Fundamental theorem of Galois theory

body:
[Proposition eq:residual-mixed-set of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[proposition]{prop:bulk-sparse-reduction}
Let \(V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be Borel measurable and bounded below, and let
\(0<r_N\le1\) and \(1\le k_N\le N\) be arbitrary deterministic
sequences.  Write
\[
 D_{N,r_N}
 =\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):\left\lVertx\right\rVert_\infty\le r_N\}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal A_N(k_N,\rho)
 =\left\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
 \text{some \(S\subset[N]\), \(\left\lvertS\right\rvert\le k_N\), satisfies }
 \norm{x_{S^c}}_2\le\rho\right\}.
\]
For \(\rho>0\), define the residual mixed-profile set
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_N(r_N,k_N,\rho)
 :=
 \left\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
 \left\lVertx\right\rVert_\infty>r_N,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{S\subset[N]\\|S|\le k_N}}
 \norm{x_{S^c}}_2>\rho\right\}.
\end{equation}
Then the disjoint decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb S^{N-1}(1)
 =D_{N,r_N}\,\dot\cup\,
  \bigl(\mathcal A_N(k_N,\rho)\setminus D_{N,r_N}\bigr)
  \,\dot\cup\,\mathcal R_N(r_N,k_N,\rho)
\end{equation}
holds.  Suppose only that the exact bulk slice satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
 \log\mathscr C_N^J(V;D_{N,r_N})
 =:\Phi\in\mathbb R.
\end{equation}
No independence, moment matching, tail, density, or nondegeneracy
condition is needed for the decomposition itself.
For \(\rho>0\), set
\begin{align*}
 \mathscr S_N(\rho)
 &:=
 \mathscr C_N^J\bigl(
 V;\mathcal A_N(k_N,\rho)\setminus D_{N,r_N}\bigr),\\
 \mathscr R_N(\rho)
 &:=
 \mathscr C_N^J\bigl(
 V;\mathcal R_N(r_N,k_N,\rho)\bigr),
\end{align*}
and define
\begin{align}
 \overline\Phi_{\rm sp}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 &:=
 \lim_{\rho\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \frac1N\log\mathscr S_N(\rho),
 \\
 \overline\Phi_{\rm mix}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 &:=
 \lim_{\rho\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \frac1N\log\mathscr R_N(\rho).
 
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr C_N^J(V)
 =
 \max\left\{
 \Phi,\,
 \overline\Phi_{\rm sp}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet),\,
 \overline\Phi_{\rm mix}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 \right\}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, exact universality holds if and only if both nonbulk
upper exponents are at most \(\Phi\).

If \(k_N=o(N)\), \(({\rm PT})_p\), and
(equation eq:critical-count-ceiling of the paper) also hold, then
\begin{equation}
 \overline\Phi_{\rm sp}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 \le\Xi_p^{\rm sp}(V).
\end{equation}
In particular, whenever the explicit sparse-rate compatibility condition
\begin{equation}
 \Xi_p^{\rm sp}(V)\le\Phi
\end{equation}
holds, exact universality is equivalent to the single residual condition
\begin{equation}
 \overline\Phi_{\rm mix}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 \le\Phi.
\end{equation}

Target3 source verification. Status: proof (unaudited); a correction to a named source statement requires independent reviewer verification. This is not a new mathematical theorem or a claim that the row is solved.

## Printed statement and locator

Li-Zhang-Arora, Why Are Convolutional Nets More Sample-Efficient than Fully-Connected Nets?, arXiv:2010.08515v2 (4May2021), AppendixD.6, LemmaD.8, printed p21 (PDFpage21), states

    E_(x~N(0,I_d)) [(x^T M x)^2]
       = ||(M+M^T)/2||_F^2 + (tr M)^2.

The rendered page papers/lemmaD8_page.png was visually inspected, not just OCR: neither the displayed lemma nor the last proof line includes a factor2 multiplying the squared Frobenius term. The preceding expanded sum already contains the correct diagonal coefficient3.

## Smallest counterexample

Set d=1 and M=[1]. Then x^T M x=x^2, so the left side is E x^4=3. The printed right side is1+1=2. Every stated hypothesis is met: M is a real1-by-1 matrix and x is standard Gaussian. The mismatch also occurs in any d>=1 with M=e_1 e_1^T, so it does not depend on allowing d=1.

## Correct identity and proof

For every real d-by-d M and standard Gaussian x, put S=(M+M^T)/2. Since x^T(M-M^T)x=0 and trS=trM, diagonalize S=Q diag(lambda_i)Q^T. Rotational invariance makes z=Q^T x independent standard Gaussian coordinates. Therefore

    E (x^T M x)^2
      =3 sum_i lambda_i^2 +2 sum_(i<j) lambda_i lambda_j
      =2 sum_i lambda_i^2 +(sum_i lambda_i)^2
      =2||S||_F^2 +(trM)^2.

Only finite sums occur; E z_i^4=3 and E z_i^2 z_j^2=1 for i!=j. Gaussian moments can be obtained by integration by parts: E Z^4=3E Z^2=3, the boundary terms being polynomials times exp(-z^2/2), hence0. Skew M gives S=0 and both sides0; no denominator or nonzero-matrix assumption is used.

## Source normalization affected

The same page uses LemmaD.8 to assert, for M with d^2 IID standard Gaussian entries, E_M E_x (x^T M x)^2=d(d+3)/2. Directly conditioning on x instead gives

    E_M (x^T M x)^2 = sum_(i,j) x_i^2 x_j^2 =||x||^4,
    E_x ||x||^4 =3d+d(d-1)=d(d+2).

Thus the normalization calculation is affected as well, separately from the algebra/interpolation discrepancy already recorded in SOURCE-004. This note does NOT propose a replacement for the entire Theorem5.4 or assert that its remaining lower-bound proof is repaired. Its Omega(d^2) order may survive with corrected constants.

## Model assumptions for the previous counterexample

Theorem5.4 on the same page explicitly takes targets sum_i alpha_i x_i^2; its proof explicitly identifies the O(d) orbit with sum_(i,j) beta_ij x_i x_j. Neither introduces affine terms or a constant offset. Definition3.2 permits arbitrary function-valued orthogonally equivariant learners, so the minimum-Frobenius-norm least-squares learner of SOURCE-004 is within its quantified algorithm class. This confirms that an affine-parameter dimension does not explain that candidate discrepancy.

[Proposition 20 (\textsf{Exact four-moment counterexample}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Let $\eps_1, \eps_2, \eps_3$, $\eps_a$, $\eps_b$, $\eps_c$, and
$\eps_d$   be i.i.d. symmetric
Rademacher random variables. 
Define
\[
 Q_\triangle
 :=\eps_1\eps_2
 +\eps_1\eps_3
 +\eps_2\eps_3
 \AND
  Q_\square
 :=\eps_a\eps_b
 +\eps_b\eps_c
 +\eps_c\eps_d
 +\eps_d\eps_a.
\]
Take four independent copies of $Q_\triangle$ and three independent
copies of $Q_\square$, and set their independent sums to be
\noi
\begin{align}
 F:=\sum_{j=1}^4Q_{\triangle,j}
   +\sum_{j=1}^3Q_{\square,j}.
 \notag
\end{align}
Then, $F$ belongs to the second Rademacher chaos
and satisfies 

 
\noi
\begin{align}
 \frac{F+24}{2}\in\N_0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \E[(F+24)^k]=\E[P_{24}^k],
 \qquad 1\leq k\leq4,
  \notag
\end{align}
where $P_{24}\sim\Pois(24)$.  Moreover,

\noi
\begin{align}
 \dTV\bigl(\cL(F+24),\Pois(24)\bigr)
 \geq\frac{1-e^{-48}}2.
 \notag
\end{align}

[Proposition of arXiv:2609.04101, 'Endpoint Estimates for Stein's Purely Quadratic Carleson Operator'] For large $M$ and $B\geq1$, define $\mathbf{A}(M,B,c)$ to be
	the union of Bohr sets over  $B$ many dyadic consequetive frequencies that are greater than $ M $ by the formula 
	\[ \mathbf{A}(M,B,c) \coloneqq \bigcup_{ k \in 2^{\mathbb{N}}, \; \log(k) \in [M,M+B)} \mathbf{B}\left (k,c\right ). \] Then, if $c \in (0,10^{-10})$ we have the following lower bound on $\mathbf{A}(M,B,c)$   \[\left| \mathbf{A}(M,B,c)\right|   \gtrsim \frac{(Bc)^2}{ (Bc)^2+Bc  }.\]   In particular, when  $c \gtrsim B^{-1}$ we have a uniform lower bound on $\mathbf{A}(M,B,c)$, namely $\left|\mathbf{A}(M,B,c) \right|\gtrsim 1.$

Li-Nica-Roy Proposition A.6 small-jump estimate, with conditional uniformity stated explicitly. Fix a dimension d, p,delta>0, h_n=n^(-2p), and a Markov transition increment Delta_n(y)=h_n*B_n(y)+sqrt(h_n)*sigma_n(y)*xi_n+h_n*n^(-delta)*R_n(y). The displayed random quantities refer to the one-step transition law conditional on the current state y; sigma_n(y) is deterministic. Fix q>2. For every radius R<infinity assume sup_{n,||y||<=R} (E[||B_n(y)||^q | y]+E[||xi_n||^q | y]+E[||R_n(y)||^q | y]+||sigma_n(y)||_op^q)<infinity. No independence between the within-step random terms is required for this estimate. Then, uniformly on ||y||<=R, h_n^(-1) E[||Delta_n(y)||^q | y] <= C_R,q h_n^(q/2-1). Consequently for every epsilon>0, h_n^(-1)*P(||Delta_n(y)||>epsilon | y) <= C_R,q*epsilon^(-q)*h_n^(q/2-1), and h_n^(-1)*E[||Delta_n(y)||^2*1_{||Delta_n(y)||>epsilon} | y] <= C_R,q*epsilon^(2-q)*h_n^(q/2-1). Both quantities tend to zero. This is the vanishing-large-jump/Lindeberg step of source AppendixA equationA.12, not a full path-convergence theorem.

[OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT: T407-JOINT-005 v1, proof (unaudited). Independent audit pending; priority unestablished.] Candidate joint-flow regime for q=2: a shared square-activation CNN with h=p(p+1)/2 spanning filters and patch-specific trainable readout learns every sum of k local quadratic forms from n=k h noiseless Gaussian samples, to any positive population squared error at finite data-dependent time, almost surely. Both layers are jointly trained with positive rates; the filter rate is explicitly data-dependent. Gaussian initialization of both layers is allowed, since the h rank-one filters span Sym(p) almost surely. Normalized squared-loss constant-risk/confidence lower bounds are Omega(kp^2) for arbitrary local learners and Omega((kp)^2) for equivariant learners, via the unit-sphere coefficient prior. Assumptions and scope: p,k>=1 integers, n>=k p(p+1)/2; independent standard Gaussian patches; noiseless arbitrary symmetric local quadratics; shared square-activation filters with spanning initialization; arbitrary finite readout initialization; positive data-dependent filter gradient-flow rate; no uniform runtime or discrete-SGD guarantee; lower class has unit L2 target norm and epsilon+4delta<1.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:7c7b624336aee0da6c2ac36239d4ba12095cf83c0c7ce2dd893abe4e5327d4d6","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/7c/7c7b624336aee0da6c2ac36239d4ba12095cf83c0c7ce2dd893abe4e5327d4d6.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:3bac46168a6a8c6878f91b6c5fa9c30475965b378f3d6fcfde7105561dc5174b","bundle_entry_key":"draft-joint-quadratic-flow","bundle_id":"population.t407-draft-quadratic-source-correction-and-joint-flow","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning theory","draft":"w693/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.sample_complexity:draft-joint-quadratic-flow-w693","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Target 3: joint quadratic CNN gradient flow in a stated regime

Rung: proof (unaudited); priority unestablished. This is a concrete positive-filter-rate gradient-flow regime, not a theorem about equal learning rates, discrete SGD, or uniform running time. The source Theorem 5.4 printed constant is not used (see T407-SOURCE-004).

## Model and claim

Let p,k>=1 be integers, d=kp, h=p(p+1)/2 and D=kh. Inputs X=(x_1,...,x_k) have independent x_j~N(0,I_p). Targets are f_star(X)=sum_j x_j^T M_j x_j with arbitrary symmetric p by p matrices M_j. Consider the shared-filter square-activation CNN
  f_(W,A)(X)=sum_(j=1)^k sum_(r=1)^h A_(r,j)(w_r^T x_j)^2,
where W=(w_1,...,w_h) and ALL entries of W and A are trained jointly. Let W_0 have its rank-one matrices w_r w_r^T spanning Sym(p). This holds almost surely for h independent Gaussian filters; the explicit bank e_i and e_i+e_l (i<l) is a deterministic example. A_0 can be arbitrary finite, including independent Gaussian initialization.

There is an explicit strictly positive, sample-dependent filter learning rate eta, with readout learning rate one, such that joint gradient flow on half the squared empirical residual norm converges to the true function from n>=D noiseless Gaussian observations almost surely. A computable residual threshold gives any prescribed population squared error epsilon>0 in finite sample-dependent time. Thus at every stated confidence 1-delta, D=kp(p+1)/2=O(kp^2) samples suffice in this joint-flow regime. Setting eta=0 gives the simpler second-layer-only statement.

For L2-normalized target classes, any learner of local quadratics needs at least (1-epsilon-4delta)_+ D samples at confidence 1-delta and squared error epsilon. Any orthogonally equivariant learner needs at least (1-epsilon-4delta)_+ d(d+1)/2 samples for this same local target family. For example epsilon=1/4 and delta=1/16 give lower bounds D/2 and d(d+1)/4, respectively. These are matching orders at fixed risk/confidence: kp^2 versus (kp)^2 when p is fixed. The generic full-quadratic least-squares learner achieves the latter dimension order and is equivariant. Exact risk normalization is specified below.

## 1. Finite feature space and Gaussian rank

Use an orthonormal symmetric-matrix vectorization svec, so z(x)=svec(xx^T), theta_j=svec(M_j), and x^T M_j x=<theta_j,z(x)>. The local feature vector phi(X) concatenates k such z vectors and has dimension D. Let Phi be the n by D feature design.

For n>=D, Phi has full column rank almost surely. Its determinant for D rows is a polynomial not identically zero: use k blocks of h witness inputs, with only one patch nonzero in each block; in that patch use e_i and e_i+e_l. The local evaluation matrix has diagonal-coordinate pivots 1 and off-diagonal pivots sqrt(2), after subtracting diagonal rows. Its determinant is nonzero. Gaussian absolute continuity then makes a rank failure a null event. The same polynomial witness proves that h Gaussian filters give an invertible matrix
  B(W)=[svec(w_1w_1^T),...,svec(w_hw_h^T)]
almost surely. This is a rank argument, not a concentration assertion.

Write b(W)=I_k tensor B(W), and stack A to a vector a. The network coefficient vector is theta=b(W)a. Every network output lies in the same D-dimensional local quadratic space, for every W,A. Let S=||Phi||_op and sigma=sigma_min(Phi)>0.

## 2. Explicit positive filter rate

Put M=||W_0||_F, gamma=sigma_min(B(W_0))>0, L=2M+1,
  rho=min{1,gamma/(2L)}, beta=gamma/2, C_B=(M+1)^2, lambda=beta^2 sigma^2.
For ||W-W_0||_F<=rho, the identity
  ||ww^T-vv^T||_F <= (||w||+||v||)||w-v||
gives ||B(W)-B(W_0)||_op<=L||W-W_0||_F<=gamma/2. Therefore sigma_min B(W)>=beta, ||B(W)||_op<=C_B, and max_r||w_r||<=M+1 throughout that ball.

Let e_0=Phi b(W_0)a_0-y and E=||e_0||. If E=0, Phi's full rank implies theta_0=theta_star and all gradients vanish; population error is already zero. Set eta=1 in this trivial branch. Otherwise define
  C_A=||a_0||+C_B S E/lambda >0,
  eta=min{1, rho lambda/[4 S(M+1) C_A E]} >0.
All quantities depend only on observed inputs/labels and initial weights. There is no access to unknown target coefficients and no population-distance oracle.

## 3. Joint flow and bootstrap

For loss L_emp(W,a)=||e||^2/2, e=Phi b(W)a-y, use
  dot a=-gradient_a L_emp,
  dot W=-eta gradient_W L_emp.
Let J_a=Phi b(W), and let J_W be the output Jacobian with respect to W. Then
  d(||e||^2/2)/dt=-||J_a^T e||^2-eta||J_W^T e||^2.
Since e=Phi(theta-theta_star) lies in range(Phi), whenever W remains in the ball,
  ||J_a^T e||^2 >= beta^2||Phi^T e||^2 >= lambda||e||^2.
Thus ||e(t)||<=E exp(-lambda t).

Also ||dot a||<=C_B S||e||, so ||a(t)||<=C_A before any exit. For a perturbation Delta W, each patch coefficient perturbation is sum_r A_(r,j)(w_r Delta w_r^T+Delta w_r w_r^T); Cauchy-Schwarz yields
  ||D_W theta[Delta W]|| <=2(M+1)||a|| ||Delta W||_F.
Hence ||J_W||_op<=2S(M+1)||a||, and
  ||W(t)-W_0||_F <= eta 2S(M+1)C_A integral_0^t ||e(u)||du
  <=eta 2S(M+1)C_A E/lambda <=rho/2.
A first exit at radius rho is impossible, because the bound there would be only rho/2. The bounds therefore hold for all time. The polynomial vector field is locally Lipschitz and all parameters remain bounded, so its solution exists globally; no finite-time explosion is possible. Both parameter blocks use their actual gradients with strictly positive fixed learning rates. No conditional probabilities are multiplied in this deterministic bootstrap.

## 4. Population risk and stopping time

For block-diagonal Delta M formed from coefficient error Delta theta,
  E[(X^T Delta M X)^2]=2||Delta M||_F^2+(tr Delta M)^2
  <=(d+2)||Delta theta||^2.
The Gaussian moment identity uses E X_i^4=3, E X_i^2 X_l^2=1 for i!=l, and vanishing odd moments. Phi's full rank gives ||Delta theta||<=||e||/sigma. Therefore
  R_pop(t) <= (d+2)E^2 exp(-2lambda t)/sigma^2.
Stop when the observed empirical residual satisfies ||e(t)||^2<=epsilon sigma^2/(d+2), or at the explicit time max{0,log((d+2)E^2/(sigma^2 epsilon))/(2lambda)} when E>0. This is finite for every full-rank sample and spanning initial W. The theorem makes no uniform bound on this random time: rare ill-conditioned designs or initial filters can force a tiny eta and a long run. No simulation or model training is part of the proof.

## 5. Correct dimension lower bounds without the source's bad constant

For any finite-dimensional quadratic function space V of dimension q, equipped with its L2(Gaussian) inner product, choose an orthonormal basis psi_1,...,psi_q. For the local space q=D; for all homogeneous symmetric quadratics q=Q=d(d+1)/2. The covariance of the unwhitened symmetric coefficients is positive definite, because
  E (X^T M X)^2=2||M||_F^2+(tr M)^2>0 for M!=0,
so this orthonormal basis exists and all target coefficients below are valid quadratics.

Put a uniform prior on coefficient xi in the unit sphere S^(q-1). Every target f_xi=sum xi_i psi_i has L2 norm exactly one. Conditional on the input sample, its n noiseless labels reveal only the projection of xi on the row span of the evaluation matrix. That row span has rank r<=n and is independent of xi before seeing labels. By reflection symmetry on its orthogonal complement, the posterior mean is precisely the observed projection. Among arbitrary output functions, the posterior mean target minimizes squared prediction risk. Its Bayes risk, averaged over labels and inputs, is E||xi-P_row xi||^2=1-r/q>=1-n/q (and zero is the trivial bound for n>=q). This gives minimax expected squared risk >=(1-n/q)_+; it is a known spherical-prior dimension argument, not a new statistical principle.

For confidence bounds, postprocess any learner by projecting its output into V in L2 and then clipping its coefficient norm to the unit ball. This does not increase squared error against any unit-norm target and bounds that error by four. If an output is not in L2, map it to zero: it could not have finite error against a target in V on a successful event. A uniform guarantee risk<=epsilon with probability >=1-delta would thus imply average risk <=epsilon+4delta. Therefore n>=q(1-epsilon-4delta), whenever the factor is positive. This is an inequality for real n, so the actual integer sample requirement is its ceiling.

The local class includes all diagonal quadratics. Every full homogeneous quadratic is an orthogonal rotation of a diagonal one, and its L2 norm is preserved by Gaussian rotation. For an equivariant learner, a uniform guarantee on the normalized local class therefore implies the same guarantee on the entire normalized full quadratic class. Apply the preceding q=Q Bayes lower bound. For an arbitrary local learner use q=D. Conversely D or Q Gaussian observations give exact coefficient recovery by local or full least squares, respectively; full least squares with minimum Frobenius-norm tie-breaking is orthogonally equivariant even on singular datasets.

## Scope and audit points

This covers arbitrary p,k with a finite shared filter bank, Gaussian or explicit spanning initialization, both parameter blocks trained jointly, noiseless labels, and a sample-dependent strictly positive filter learning rate. It does not cover fixed equal learning rates, ordinary discrete SGD, noisy labels, or q>2. The case p=1 is included. E=0 is handled before any division by E. The full-rank event and gamma>0 hold almost surely but no deterministic lower bound on conditioning is claimed. Source 2006.15459, Section 2 Equation (1), fixes second-layer weights; 1712.09203 treats a PSD factorization teacher. These scope checks do not prove priority for the present shared, independently weighted patch readout. Conditional on root color zero, P(K=1,2,3)=(3/5,3/10,1/10); conditional on color one it is (3/10,3/5,1/10). The full conditional-child selection lemma implies these K variables are iid along the selected ray within each color class. Hence the local dimension is h_0=(3/10)log 2+(1/10)log 3 or h_1=(3/5)log 2+(1/10)log 3 by the strong law. Both are strictly less than log(12/5), the Galton-Watson dimension. Check: For color zero the unconditioned masses are .30 for two mixed children (K=1), .15 for two zero children (K=2), and .05 for three zero children (K=3); divide by color probability .5. For color one the corresponding masses are .15,.30,.05. Cylinder mass is exactly the product of reciprocal K values; Fubini transfers the ray statement to almost every tree and almost every flow ray. body: [Definition 2 (Saturated regime) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] The parameters are saturated if the failed basin floor exceeds every child threshold by a fixed margin: there is $\delta>0$ with $\inf_{s\in B_{\mathrm{fail}}}(s-\theta_{uw})\ge\delta$ uniformly, so that $\sigma(s^{(u)}-\theta_{uw})\ge1-\varepsilon(\delta)$ for all children $w$ once $u$ is failed, with $\varepsilon(\delta)\to0$ as $\delta\to\infty$.

[Lem 84 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\acute{Y}$ be a continuous local martingale started from $\acute{Y}(0)=1$, and let $\theta$ be a stopping time with $\E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta<\infty$. If $\E [(|{{\acute{Y}}}_\theta|-1)^2] \le\epsilon$, then $\E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta \le 4\epsilon^{1/2}$.

\begin{proof}
The process
$\acute{M}(t)\equiv \acute{Y}^2(t)-\langle\acute{Y} \rangle_t$ is a continuous local martingale. It follows from e.g.\ \cite[Thm.~4.13]{MR3497465} that the stopped process $\acute{M}(t\wedge\theta)$ is a uniformly integrable true martingale, so the optional stopping theorem gives
    \[
    \E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta
    = \E\Big[ (\acute{Y}_\theta)^2-1\Big]\,.
    \]
Combining with Lemma~\ref{l:quadratic.ineq} and the hypothesis gives
    \[
    \E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta
    \le 2\epsilon^{1/2}
    + \frac{2\E[(|\acute{Y}_\theta|-1)^2]}{\epsilon^{1/2}}
    \le 4\epsilon^{1/2}\,,
    \]
as claimed.
\end{proof}

After the conditional residual-line reduction, the fixed-apex pair estimate for bounded-density subgaussian row submatrices rests on a single inequality, which is OPEN as of 2026-09-14: for overlap parameter $D \ge 3$, $\mathbb{E}_A\big[\operatorname{tr}(M_A^2)\big] \le C/D$, where $M_A = \mathbb{E}[v v^{\top} \mid A]$ is the conditional second-moment matrix of the residual null line. Perfect conditional isotropy $M_A = I_D/D$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(M_A^2) = 1/D$ exactly, so the target asserts that the conditional law of the residual null line is isotropic up to a constant factor, a statement about one matrix with no pair and no angle left in it. Note also the shape of the reduction: the singular near-parallel edge, where $|\rho| \to 1$, was closed as a SEPARATE lemma, leaving only this bulk quadratic estimate. When a bound fails only at an integrable singularity, proving the bulk and the edge as different lemmas is what reduces the obligation to one clean line.

[Dfn 3. dfn: effective resistance between sets of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Effective resistance between sets}]  
  Fix a resistance form $(\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{F})$ on $F$
  and write $R$ for the corresponding resistance metric.
  For sets $A, B \subseteq F$,
  we define
  \begin{equation}
    R(A,B)
    \coloneqq
    \left(
    \inf\{
    \mathcal{E}(f,f):
    f \in \mathcal{F},\
    f|_{A} \equiv 1,\
    f|_{B} \equiv 0
    \}
    \right)^{-1},
  \end{equation}
  which is defined to be zero if the infimum is taken over the empty set.
  Note that by (4. dfn cond: resistance forms condition 4 of the paper) 
  we clearly have $R( \{x\}, \{y\}) = R(x,y)$.
title: Dfn 3. dfn: effective resistance between sets of arXiv:2412.08236

body: [Prop of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] Let $\rho_0:\pi_1(S) \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ be a Fuchsian representation, corresponding to the hyperbolic surface $X$. [Theorem 2 (Markov chain tree theorem) of arXiv:2606.31596, 'The Invariant Measure of Multiscale Markov Chains via Fast Arborescence Factorization'] Let $X^N_t$ be a continuous-time Markov chain with transition graph $(V,E)$ and positive transition rates $r_N$.
	If $(V,E)$ is strongly connected, then $X^N_t$ admits a unique invariant measure $\pi_N$, which is strictly positive and given by
	\begin{equation}
		
		\pi_N(x)=\frac{r_N(\mathcal{T}_x)} {r_N(\mathcal{T})}\,,\quad x\in V\,.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Markov chain tree theorem

[Theorem 4 (Frydman's $R_6$ test) of arXiv:2608.08242, 'Bang--bang representation of $3\times 3$ embeddable stochastic matrices'] Let $P$ be a $3\times 3$ row-stochastic matrix with $D>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If $P$ has a zero entry, 
\[
P\in\T\Longleftrightarrow G(P)\geq 0.
\]
In that case $P\in R_5$, and $G(P)=0$ implies $P\in R_4$.

\item If $P>0$, then $P\in\V$ if and only if
$\max_{i,j}V_{ij}(P)\geq0$.  More generally,
\[
P\in\T\cup\V
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\max_{i,j}V_{ij}(P)\geq0.
\]

\item If $P\notin\T\cup\V$, then $P\in\NH$ if and only if, for some
ordered pair $(i,j)$, the quadratic $q_{ij}^P$ has a root in
$[0,\bar c_{ij}]$.

\item One has 
\[
R_6=\T\cup\V\cup\NH.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Frydman's $R_6$ test

\begin{enumerate}

\(G h_{\rm ref}\)-Hermitian endomorphism \(K\),
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Re}
 \left\langle
  \mathcal D(\log)_G(GK),K
 \right\rangle_{G h_{\rm ref}}
 \geq
 \frac{m}{M}|K|_{G h_{\rm ref}}^2.
\end{equation}

\item
Let
\[
 \mathscr S_G(\Psi):=G^{-1/2}\Psi G^{1/2},
\]
where \(\Psi\) is a fixed \(h_{\rm ref}\)-Hermitian endomorphism, and set
\[
 \mathcal Z_G(K)
 :=
 \left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}
 \mathscr S_{Ge^{sK}}(\Psi).
\]
There exists a constant
\(C_{\Psi,m,M}>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \left|

  \langle\mathcal Z_G(K),K\rangle_{G h_{\rm ref}}
 \right|
 \leq
 C_{\Psi,m,M}|K|_{G h_{\rm ref}}^2
\end{equation}
for every \(G\in\mathcal K_{m,M}\) and every
\(G h_{\rm ref}\)-Hermitian endomorphism \(K\).
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] For every compact $K\subset Z$ and every \(\gamma\in(2,4)\), there are
locally Lipschitz functions
$\eta_j:Z\to[0,1]$ whose restrictions lie in $C^\infty(\cR)$, such that
\begin{align}
 0\le\eta_j\le1,\qquad
 &\eta_j=0\text{ near }K\cap\Sing Z,\qquad
 \eta_j\longrightarrow1\text{ locally uniformly on }K\cap\cR,
 \\
 &\int_K\bigl(|1-\eta_j|^2+|\nabla\eta_j|^2\bigr)\,d\mathfrak m
   \longrightarrow0.
 
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
                  \int_K|\nabla\eta_j|^\gamma\,d\mathfrak m\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
There is also a sequence $\beta_j\in C_c^\infty(\cR)$ with
\begin{equation}
 0\le\beta_j\le1,\qquad \beta_j\to1\quad\mathfrak m\text{-a.e.},
 \qquad
 \|1-\beta_j\|_{L^2(\mathfrak m)}^2+
 \int|\nabla\beta_j|^2\,d\mathfrak m\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT, proof (unaudited), T326-w697-C10 v1; reviewer PASS pending. Bah-Rauhut-Terstiege-Westdickenberg arXiv:1910.05505v5 Theorem 4 (printed p.4) states that a bounded global negative-gradient trajectory of a real analytic function converges to a critical point. Applying it to C07's bounded polynomial augmented scalar-value/K^TQ loss proves convergence of the full parameter trajectory to a single critical point for every pool under C07's hypotheses. This resolves existence of the limit, not whether its loss is zero. The source's Theorem 39(b) (p.21), for two matrix layers and almost every ambient initialization with full-rank input covariance, does not justify a global-minimum conclusion for the exact deterministic scalar-plus-two-factor initialization here. The known analytic-gradient theorem requires a real analytic f on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and a bounded global solution x'=-grad f; it concludes one limiting critical point, not a global minimum. C07 supplies boundedness for the actual initialized polynomial loss, so the application is valid without full-rank input covariance. Theorem 39(b) has different hypotheses: two freely trained matrix layers, full-rank XX^T, almost every ambient initialization. It cannot certify the exact deterministic shared-scalar model. The related queued w696 compact-manifold convergence card was considered during dedup; this entry records the specific noncompact-Euclidean bounded-trajectory application, not a duplicate generic theorem card.

[Theorem theorem ethier kurtz path convergence of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] Let $ T_n $ be the transition operator of $ Y_n $ and $ \{ T( t ) \}_{ t \ge 0 } $ a Feller semigroup on $ C( E ) $.
    Suppose that the initial distributions of $ \{ \gamma_n( Y_n( 0 ) ) \} $ converge, say to $ \nu $, and that $ \{  \varepsilon _n \}_{ n \ge 1 } $ is a positive sequence converging to zero such that
    $$
    	T_n^{  \lfloor  t/ \varepsilon _n  \rfloor  }
    	\pi_n
    	f
    		\to
    			T( t ) f
    		,
    			\qquad
                \text{ for all }f \in C( E ),
    			\,
    			t \ge 0
    		.
    $$
    
    \noindent
    Then there exists a Markov process $ Y $ with initial distribution $ \nu $, transition semigroup $ \{ T( t ) \}_{ t \ge 0 } $, and sample paths in the Skorokhod space $ D( [ 0, \infty ), E )  $ such that the convergence
	$$
		\big(
			\gamma_n( Y_n (  \lfloor  t/ \varepsilon _n  \rfloor ) )
		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
			\Longrightarrow
        		\big(
        				Y( t )
        		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
	$$

body: [campaign status: candidate_partial_counterexample - author-checked, unrefereed] Ansatz 20, stated inside Open Problem 8 of Aldous and Janson (arXiv:2303.02529), claims for nonnegative f with f(j) = O(j^k) that (i) if sum_i a(i) f(i) converges then sum_{i <= n} a(n,i) f(i) tends to it, and (ii) if it diverges then sum_{i <= n} a(n,i) f(i) is asymptotic to sum_{i <= n} a(i) f(i); here a(n,j) is the probability that the tagged harmonic descent chain started at n visits j and a(j) = 6 H_{j-1} / (pi^2 (j-1)) is its fixed-j limit. Our result (id P0341, 2026-09-08): BOTH parts are FALSE, on the single observation that a(n,n) = 1 exactly - the chain starts at n, so it visits n surely. For (i), take f(j) = 1{j = 2^r}: f is bounded (hence of polynomial growth) and a(2^r) = O(r 2^-r), so S = sum a(i) f(i) converges; but at n = 2^K the truncated sum contains the top term a(2^K, 2^K) = 1, forcing liminf >= 1 + S against the predicted S. For (ii), take g(j) = j 1{j = 2^r} (so g(j) <= j): since a(j) j ~ (6/pi^2) log j the truncated limiting sum at n = 2^K is of order K^2 while the actual sum is at least its root term 2^K, so the ratio diverges. The refutation is scoped to the displayed Ansatz, not to Open Problem 8 as a whole - explicit bounds on |a(n,m) - a(m)| remain open. Verification as the source words it: each piece re-derived (the asymptotics of a(j) and a(j) j, the summability of a(2^r), the polynomial-growth hypothesis for both test functions, and a(n,n) = 1 from the definition); no rate of convergence and no numerical evaluation is needed anywhere. Prior art not cleared. f nonnegative with f(j) = O(j^k) a(n,j) the visit probability of the tagged harmonic descent chain, a(j) = 6 H_{j-1}/(pi^2 (j-1))

The concentration of measure phenomenon, formulated by Vitali Milman in the 1970s following insights of Paul Lévy, asserts that on high-dimensional probability spaces, any well-behaved function (such as a Lipschitz function) is almost constant almost everywhere. Specifically, the function deviates significantly from its mean or median only on a set of exponentially small measure in the dimension.

Let Q denote the law of a two-sided, nontrivial, (r_0,alpha)-semi-selfsimilar Levy process V with cadlag paths and V(0)=0, where alpha is in (0,2), Q(V(1)>0)>0 and Q(V(1)<0)>0. Strictly alpha-stable processes are included. Let nu be its Levy measure and suppose nu((0,infinity)) > 0. Let delta > 1. Put w(x) = -|x|^delta + V(x) and mu^w(dx) = exp(-w(x))dx. Let L^w be the self-adjoint operator associated with the closure on L^2(R,mu^w) of E^w(f,f) = (1/2) integral_R |f'(x)|^2 exp(-w(x))dx, f in C_c^infinity(R). For fixed x_0 > 0 set B_r(x) = (integral_x^infinity exp(w(y))dy)(integral_{x_0}^x exp(-w(y))dy). Then, Q-almost surely: limsup_{x->infinity} B_r(x) = infinity; lambda_ess(-L^w) = 0; and exp(tL^w) is noncompact. The proof is the negative-jump calculation applied to -V, with the two Hardy factors interchanged. For 0 < delta <= 1/alpha the same conclusion is the paper's Proposition 5.2. The record's claim for alpha in (1,2) and 1/alpha < delta <= 1 is not covered by the written proof. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

body:
[Theorem q>1 of arXiv:2605.10452, 'A secretary for Messrs. Luce and Mallows'] Consider the secretary problem for a Mallows distribution with $q=q_n>1$ in the case that the largest number is  of highest rank.

\noindent i. Let $q_n=1+\frac cn$, where $c>0$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
\begin{equation}
M_n^*\sim n\Big(\frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{1-e^{-c}}{e-1+e^{-c}}\big)\Big),
\end{equation}
 and the corresponding  limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q_n}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
Also, $\lim_{c\to\infty} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{1-e^{-c}}{e-1+e^{-c}}\big)=0$ and $\lim_{c\to0} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{1-e^{-c}}{e-1+e^{-c}}\big)=\frac1e$.

\noindent ii.
Let $q_n=1+\frac c{n^\alpha}$, where $c>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
$$
M_n^*\sim\frac1c\left(1-\log(e-1)\right)n^\alpha\approx0.459\frac{n^\alpha}c,
$$
 and the corresponding limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q_n}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
\noindent iii. Let $q>1$.  Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M^*)$, where
$$
M^*=\begin{cases}&\max\left\{M\ge1: \sum_{j=M}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}\ge\frac q{q-1}\right\}, \ \text{if}\ \sum_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}\ge \frac q{q-1};\\
&0,\ \text{if}\ \sum_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}<\frac q{q-1}.\end{cases}
$$
(If  $\sum_{j=M^*}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}=\frac q{q-1}$, then $M^*-1$ is also optimal.)

\noindent The corresponding limiting probability of success is given by
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q}(\mathcal{S}^\downarrow(n,M^*))=\begin{cases}&\frac{q-1}q(1-q^{-M^*})\sum_{j=M^*}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}\ge\\
&(1-q^{-M^*}),\ \text{if}\ M^*\ge1;\\
&\frac{q-1}q>,\ \text{if}\ M^*=0.\end{cases}
\end{equation}
The limiting probability in (equation SuccessProbup of the paper) is always greater or equal to $\frac1e$ and is strictly greater than $\frac1e$ for all but at most a countable number of $q$ with no accumulation points in $(0,\infty)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

AUDIT CORRECTION (w559, 2026-10-10; independent review pending) of the 2026-09-07 C0047-A001 spectral route. For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected d-regular simple Cayley graph G, let rho=||A_G||/d denote the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius. Benjamini-Schramm 1996, Theorem 4, printed p.76 (bond extension in section 2), and Juschenko-Nagnibeda 2015, Theorem 2, give the sufficient condition d*rho*p_c(G)<1 for p_c(G)<p_u(G). The original p_c<1/rho quotation omitted d and is not that criterion: it is automatic when rho<1 and p_c<=1. Nonamenability does not imply the repaired criterion for a prescribed generating set. In the simple Cayley graph C_2*C_3 with generators {a,b,b^-1}, p_c=q is the root of 2q^2+2q^3-2q^4=1 in (0.63,0.64), p_u=1, and ||A||>=2, so d*rho*p_c>1.26. This counterexample refutes only the stronger universal spectral bridge. An existence theorem for a favorable generating multiset does not establish the result for every prescribed simple generating set.     $ holds.

body: The paper proving the Aldous-Fill spectral gap conjecture leaves conditional the claim that for every sufficiently large even order n, the slowest d-regular graph (maximising relaxation time tau_2) is cubic (d=3); the finite crossover point is n=8. The 2-regular cycle has tau_2 = 1/(1-cos(2 pi/n)) ~ n^2/(2 pi^2), one third of the cubic asymptotic 3n^2/(2 pi^2), so cubic graphs must eventually overtake the cycle but do not lead at first: the slowest-known regular graph by order is 2-regular (the cycle) at n=4 (tau_2=1.0000) and n=6 (2.0000), then becomes 3-regular at n=8 (3.9271, versus the cycle's 3.4142), n=10 (13.5414, cycle 5.2361), and n=12 (17.8846, cycle 7.4641). Separately, the extremal cubic maxima (0.75, 1.50, 3.93, 13.54, 17.88 for n=4,6,8,10,12) jump by a factor of 3.5 from n=8 to n=10, out of line with the surrounding steps; this is because the extremal cubic graph acquires a BRIDGE at n=10 and CANNOT do so at any earlier order. Proof that a bridged cubic graph needs n>=10: if a cubic graph has a bridge uv, deleting it leaves a component A containing u where every vertex has degree 3 except u (degree 2), so the degree sum 3|A|-1 must be even, forcing |A| odd; |A|=1 would need a loop and |A|=3 would need four edges among three vertices (both impossible for a simple cubic graph), so both sides of any bridge are odd and at least 5, giving n>=10. This matches exact enumeration: no bridged cubic graph exists at n=4, 6, or 8; at n=10 there is exactly one bridged cubic graph and it IS the extremal one (tau_2=13.5414, versus 6.8423 for the best bridgeless cubic graph on 10 vertices); at n=12 there are four bridged cubic graphs and the extremal one among them is a 5|7 split (17.8846, versus 10.3190 for the best bridgeless cubic graph), a 6|6 split being impossible by the same parity argument. So the crossover at n=8 (cubic first overtakes the cycle, still bridgeless there, via a narrow 2-edge 4|4 cut) and the jump at n=10 (the bridge becomes possible) are two DIFFERENT events. NOT CERTIFIED: whether any regular graph of degree d>=4 ever competes with the cubic extremal graphs at these orders - only suggested: a 4-regular graph would need a second eigenvalue of 0.944 to compete, and the best 4-regular graph seen has 0.890; and a parity fact (a d-regular graph has a cut of size c across a vertex subset A only if c = d|A| mod 2, checked on 8400 random cuts with zero violations) shows a bridge is impossible outright for any EVEN degree d, which is suggestive but not a proof that odd degrees d>=5 cannot compete either.

body: There are functions on (0, 1) with Lebesgue measure that converge to 0 pointwise while their integrals do not: f_n = n 1((0, 1/n)) has int f_n = 1 for every n. No integrable function dominates all f_n, since sup_n f_n(x) = floor(1/x) >= 1/x - 1, which is not integrable near 0. So the dominated convergence theorem cannot drop its common integrable dominator.

[Proposition prop:FKG of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] Let $\mathbf{Y} \sim \mathcal{L}^{\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y},\bm{\lambda}}_{n,\ell,r,\mathbf{f},\mathbf{g}}$, recalling Definition (def:extFLE of the paper)
of this measure with $n$ curves having boundary conditions $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \in \overline{\mathbb{A}_+^n}$
on $[\ell,r]$, Lipschitz floors and ceilings given by $\mathbf{f}, \mathbf{g} : [\ell,r] \to \mathbb{A}_+^n$ with $\mathbf{f} \prec \mathbf{g}$,
and varying area tilt strengths given by $\bm{\lambda} : [\ell,r] \to \mathbb{R}_+^n$. 
We may also consider the measure without floors or ceilings, or with floors but not ceilings, et cetera.
Consider any functions $f, g$ on the space of continuous curves $[\ell,r] \to \mathbb{A}_+^n$
which are continuous in the topology of uniform convergence, increasing
with respect to the ordering $\preceq$, and such that $\operatorname{Cov}[f(\mathbf{Y}),g(\mathbf{Y})]$ is well-defined.
Then $\operatorname{Cov} \mleft[ f(\mathbf{Y}), g(\mathbf{Y}) \mright] \geqslant 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: FKG inequality

[Pro 5.1 of arXiv:2608.00420, '{Weighted $L^p$ solutions of scalar BSDEs with general unbounded stochastic coefficients}\'] Assume that the generator $g$ satisfies assumption (A:H3 of the paper) (resp. (A:H1' of the paper)). For each $n\geq1$, define the function $g_n$ as follows: for $(\omega,t,y,z)\in \Omega\times [0,\tau]\times{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}^d$,
$$
g_n(\omega,t,y,z):=\inf_{\bar{z}\in{\mathbb R}^d}\{g(\omega,t,y,\bar{z})
+\bar{\nu}_t^n(\omega)|z-\bar{z}|\}
$$
$$
({\rm resp.}\ \ g_n(\omega,t,y,z):=\inf_{(\bar y,\bar{z})\in {\mathbb R}\times {\mathbb R}^d}\{g(\omega,t,\bar y,\bar{z})+\bar\mu_t^n(\omega)|y-\bar y|
+\bar{\nu}_t^n(\omega)|z-\bar{z}|\})
$$
with
$$
\bar\mu_t^n:=\mu_t+ne^{-t}\ \ {\rm and}\ \  \bar{\nu}_t^n:=\sqrt{\nu_t^2 +ne^{-t}}.
$$
Then the sequence of function $g_n$ is well defined, and for each $n\geq1$, $g_n(\omega,t,y,z)$ is $(\mathcal{F}_t)$-progressively measurable for each $(y,z)\in{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}^d$, and it satisfies, ${\rm d}\mathbb{P}\times{\rm d} t-a.e.$,
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] For each $z\in{\mathbb R}^d$, $g_n(\omega,t,\cdot,z)$ is continuous and $g_n$ satisfies (A:H3 of the paper)(ii)-(iii) (resp. (A:H1' of the paper)(ii));
\item[(ii)] Monotonicity in $n$: for each $(y,z)\in{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}^d$, $g_n(\omega,t,y,z)$ nondecreases in $n$;
\item[(iii)] Stochastic Lipschitz condition: for each $(y,y_1,y_2,z_1,z_2)\in{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}^d\times{\mathbb R}^d,$ we have
$$
\left|g_n(\omega,t,y,z_1)-g_n(\omega,t,y,z_2)\right|\leq \bar{\nu}_t^n(\omega)|z_1-z_2|
$$
$$
({\rm resp.}\ \ \left|g_n(\omega,t,y_1,z_1)-g_n(\omega,t,y_2,z_2)\right|\leq \bar{\mu}_t^n(\omega)|y_1-y_2|+\bar{\nu}_t^n(\omega)|z_1-z_2|);
$$

\item[(iv)] Convergence: If $(y_n,z_n)\rightarrow (y,z)$, then $g_n(\omega,t,y_n,z_n)\rightarrow g(\omega,t,y,z)$, as $n\rightarrow \infty$.\vspace{0.2cm}
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem Finite-target spectral hitting estimate of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Under Assumption 2.6, let
\(\mathcal{A = \{}A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\}\) be a finite family of
measurable subsets of \(M\), each of positive capacity. Then, for

[Lemma 4 (Wave--Hodge reduction) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $X=X(t,y)$ be smooth in spacetime, let $w:=X-\mathrm{id}$ and let
$\Kmat=(dX)^{-1}$.  Then the following statements hold.
 
\emph{(i) Algebraic pressure identity.}
Without using an evolution equation or the constraint $J=1$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal Q[dw]
 =-\tr \left(
   \Kmat\mathcal A^+(dw)\Kmat\mathcal A^-(dw)\right)
 =-\Kmat^a_i\Kmat^b_j
   Q_0(\partial_aw^j,\partial_bw^i).
\end{equation}
 
\emph{(ii) Smooth MHD reduction.}
Assume in addition that $X$ is the Lagrangian flow of a smooth solution of
\eqref{eq:mhd}, with $X(0)=\mathrm{id}$ and initial magnetic field $\Binf$.
If
$\mathcal Q[dw]\in L^{r_{\mathrm{HLS}}}(\mu)$ and the pressure is normalised so
that $(\nabla p)\circ X\in L^4(\mu)$ then
\[
 (\nabla p)\circ X=F[dw]=\mathcal{P}_{\gmetric[dw]}\mathcal Q[dw],
\]
and $(w,F[dw])$ satisfies \eqref{eq:auxiliary-system}. In particular, this holds when
$v,b\in C([0,T];H^\infty)$ decay together with all their derivatives and $p$ is
the Riesz pressure \eqref{eq:return-pressure}.

body:
Let $S=\{x_1,\dots,x_N\}$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The following are equivalent: (i) there is $y$ with $\langle y,x_i\rangle>0$ for every $i$; (ii) $0 \notin \operatorname{conv}(S)$. The frequently attempted substitute is FALSE: the condition that $\operatorname{conv}(S)$ have empty interior does NOT imply (i). Counterexample in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $N=2$: take $x_1=e_1$ and $x_2=-e_1$. Their convex hull is a segment, which has empty interior, yet $0$ lies in it and no $y$ satisfies both inequalities. In particular, the observation that $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^N$ span an affine hull of dimension at most $N-1$, and so have a hull with empty interior, proves nothing about separation. What does suffice is linear independence: if $N \le d$ and $x_1,\dots,x_N$ are linearly independent then (i) holds, and an explicit witness solves $\langle y,x_i\rangle = 1$ for every $i$.
S is a finite subset of R^d
for the final claim: N <= d and x_1,...,x_N are linearly independent

For 0<s<=1,

sum_{z in 4Z^3, |z|>=16} |I_s(z)|=infinity.

Proof. Consider z=4(n,m,l), n>=4, |m|,|l|<=floor(n/4), and f(t)=K_s(z+te) for -1<=t<=1. Throughout this interval the squared cosine with e is at least 9/11 and |z+te|<=6n. Thus

f''(t)=s |z+te|^{-s-2}[(s+2)(z_1+t)^2/|z+te|^2-1]
>= (7s/11)(6n)^{-s-2}.

The exact central-difference identity gives -I_s(z)=integral_{-1}^1 (1-|t|) f''(t)dt, so |I_s(z)|>=(7s/11)(6n)^{-s-2}. There are (2floor(n/4)+1)^2>=n^2/16 such centers for each n. Distinct n give distinct centers, and the total contribution at n is therefore at least 7s/(176*6^{s+2}) n^{-s}. The p-series diverges for 0<s<=1. This proves absolute divergence on an explicit separated set, not just an upper-bound failure or an angular heuristic. Conditional angular cancellation, renormalization, and collective screening remain possible; this is not a counterexample to crystallization.

The first decays as R^-3 and the second as R^-5. The axial R^-3 series by itself converges; the cone count above is essential to establish the 3D absolute divergence. Method: Sharp constant-one comparisons of reversible mixing and stopping parameters structural calculation Result: The stopping half follows from Dynkin optional sampling. Let Lf=-lambda*f with lambda=1/tau2, mean_pi f=0, and choose x with f(x)=M=max f>0. For any integrable randomized stopping time U from x with X_U distributed as pi, E f(X_U)-f(x)=-lambda*E integral_0^U f(X_s)ds. Thus M=lambda*E integral f<=lambda*M*E U, giving E U>=tau2. The discrete-time proof replaces the integral by sum_(s<U)f(X_s). Check: Apply the identity first at U wedge n. The bounded function and integrability of U justify dominated convergence of the integral and of f(X_(U wedge n)). This avoids the false assertion that an exponential eigenfunction martingale is automatically uniformly integrable at U. Obstruction: The bound on tau1 by tau0 remains unresolved here. Worst-start total variation cannot be bounded solely by an unweighted spectral trace without controlling eigenfunction amplitudes. The source convention uses the continuized threshold and pairwise total variation, not the usual distance-to-pi threshold.

body: In mathematics, Hodge theory, named after W. V. D. Hodge, is a method for studying the cohomology groups of a smooth manifold M using partial differential equations. Such forms are called harmonic.

CANDIDATE APPLICATION, NOT INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED; PRIOR-LITERATURE STATUS UNVERIFIED. Burdzy-Scheutzow (2014), Problem 7.5 asks whether a process with law equivalent to Wiener measure can receive a random finite prefix to become Brownian motion. Apply the forward filling lemma on two-sided Wiener paths with theta w(t)=w(t+1)-w(1) and density f equal to the desired future-law density. The selected future W(N+t)-W(N) has the desired law; prefixing W[0,N] recovers the original Wiener path. A standard Borel disintegration supplies the coupling for an already-given suffix process. Auxiliary randomness and non-stopping joining times are essential permitted scope; no independence of prefix and suffix is asserted. The construction actually uses absolute continuity only. Check earlier filling, shift-coupling, and Brownian embedding literature before any claim of novelty.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Relate the intrinsic distance to the number of pivotals along the backbone plus the sizes of the intermediate sausages. Result: The intrinsic distance from 0 to x equals the sum over the backbone decomposition of the intrinsic distances through each 'sausage' between consecutive pivotal bonds; the number of pivotals is the object of Theorem 15.4, and the sausage lengths are i.i.d.-like with a fixed law in the mean-field picture (each sausage is a doubly connected piece of bounded expected size in d > 6 with exponential tails?). If the sausage intrinsic lengths were i.i.d. with finite mean m, then d(0,x) ~ m times the number of pivotals, and the intrinsic two-point function would follow from Theorem 15.4 by a renewal argument with n replaced by n/m. The obstruction is the dependence between sausage sizes and the backbone geometry, which is weak in high dimensions but not zero; the lace expansion with a memory of the intrinsic length would need a new expansion variable (a generating function in both the spatial variable and the intrinsic length), which is what the source suggests. A rigorous partial result: the intrinsic length is at least the number of pivotals plus one, so tau_n^{(in)} summed over n >= N is bounded by the pivotal-count two-point function summed over counts >= N... wait the direction: d(0,x) >= |Piv(0,x)| + 1 gives P(d >= N) >= P(|Piv| >= N - 1), a lower bound on the intrinsic tail from the pivotal tail, hence the intrinsic one-arm probability is at least the pivotal one-arm probability, consistent with both being of order 1/N. No asymptotic constant. Key identity: d_{C(0)}(0,x) >= |Piv(0,x)| + 1, so intrinsic tails dominate pivotal tails. Obstruction: Joint expansion in space and intrinsic length not available.

[Thm thm_gGE of arXiv:2411.17216, 'Large deviations of the empirical measures of a strong-Feller Markov process inside a subs'] Let $(\mathbb P_T)_{T>0}$ be a sequence of probability distribution on $\mathcal P(\mathscr S)$, such that:

\begin{enumerate}
\item For any potential $V\in b\mathcal B(\mathscr D)$,
\begin{equation}
\boldsymbol \Lambda(V)=\lim_{T\to +\infty} \frac{1}{T} \log \int_{\mathcal P(\mathscr D)} e^{T\beta(V)} \mathbb P_T (d\beta).
\end{equation}

  \item The mapping $V\mapsto \boldsymbol \Lambda(V)$ is Gateaux differentiable on $b\mathcal B(\mathscr D)$, i.e. the mapping $t\mapsto \boldsymbol \Lambda(V+t V_1)$ is differentiable  at $t=0$ for any potential $V,V_1\in b\mathcal B(\mathscr D)$.
  \item $\mathbb P_T$ is exponentially $*$-tight, namely,  $\forall L>0,\ \exists \mathbf K $ compact in $(\mathcal P(\mathscr D),\tau)$ such that for any measurable neighborhood $\mathcal{N}$ of $\mathbf K$,
  $$
  \limsup_{T\to +\infty} \frac{1}{T} \log \mathbb P_T [L_T\notin \mathcal{N}] \leqslant -L.
  $$
\end{enumerate}
Then, $\mathbb P_T$ satisfies the {\rm L.D.P.} on $(\mathcal P(\mathscr D), \tau)$ with speed $T$ and the rate function
$$
I(\beta)=\sup\left\{\beta(V)-\boldsymbol \Lambda (V),\ V\in \mathcal C_b(\mathscr D)\right\}, \ \beta\in \mathcal P(\mathscr D),
$$
which is the Legendre transform $\boldsymbol  \Lambda^*$ of the Cramer functional $\boldsymbol \Lambda$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
