Candidate tail-envelope result, T318-C9 v2: for offset-linear Gaussian random features rho(z)=sqrt(v)z+mu, let M=mu^2>0, lambda=sigma^2/s_p^2>0, r=s_*^2/s_p^2>=0, a=lambda T, and k_p(a)=a/(a+nM). For every deterministic b_p->infinity, proposed sup_{a>=b_p}|L_p(a)-E(k_p(a))|->0 in probability for teacher/training-noise-averaged conditional excess log risk, where E(k)=0.5[log((lambda+v+Mk)/lambda)+(lambda+rv+rMk^2)/(lambda+v+Mk)-1]. If b_p=o(n), all approximate tail minimizers have k_p->k_star: k_star=0 for r<=1; for r>1 put d0=M+2r(lambda+v) and k_star=2v(r-1)/(d0+sqrt(d0^2+4rMv(r-1))). Then T_hat/n->M k_star/[lambda(1-k_star)] for r>1; for r<=1 the minimizing tail is sublinear in n. This concerns only the diverging-temperature branch, not global phase selection. Assumptions: Fixed v>0 and mu nonzero; independent spherical hidden directions of radius sqrt(d), independent Gaussian training/test inputs, shared Gaussian teacher independent of features/inputs and independent Gaussian training noise. n/p->gamma and p/d->psi are positive finite constants. Prior/noise variances positive, truth variance nonnegative. Original test noise retained. Risk averages over teacher and training noise conditional on inputs/features. b_p->infinity, additionally b_p=o(n) only for the tail-minimum conclusion. The uniform argument uses exact sample-centering B=Zprime JZ+n uuprime, u=mu e+zbar, and A_a=(I+Zprime JZ/a)^(-1): a(B+aI)^(-1)=A_a-A_a uuprime A_a/[a/n+uprime A_a u]. The denominator is uniformly bounded below by M/8 with probability tending to one. This handles a->infinity with a/n->0, where the naive B/a cross-term expansion can fail. Gaussian conditional quadratic-form moments control the log and ratio uniformly because original test noise stays positive. The points of an elliptic curve E over K, including O, form an abelian group with identity O: three points sum to O exactly when they are collinear (with tangency counting multiplicity). Addition is given by the chord-and-tangent construction - draw the line through P and Q, take its third intersection with E, and reflect in the x-axis - and the coordinates of P + Q are rational functions of those of P and Q over K.
E a smooth elliptic curve with base point O

Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) be a random vector with independent centered components satisfying ||X_i||_{psi_2} <= K. Let A be an n x n real matrix. Then there exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that for all t >= 0, P(|X^T A X - E[X^T A X]| >= t) <= 2 * exp( - c * min( t^2 / (K^4 * ||A||_F^2), t / (K^2 * ||A||_{op}) ) ), where ||A||_F is the Frobenius norm and ||A||_{op} is the operator (spectral) norm.
X has independent centered sub-Gaussian components with norm K

[Cor of arXiv:2603.17858, 'Decay of correlations and zeros for the hard-core model'] Let $\Delta\in \mathbb{N}, C>0, \alpha\in (0,1)$ and $\lambda^\star>0$.
There exists $g_0=g_0(C,\alpha,\Delta,\lambda^\star)$ such that for any family $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and girth at least $g_0$, if the hard-core model on $\mathcal{G}$ satisfies strong spatial mixing at $\lambda^\star$ with parameters $C,\alpha$, then there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that for each $G=(V,E)\in \mathcal{G}$ and $\Vec\lambda\in B(\lambda^\star,\varepsilon)^V$ we have $Z_G(\Vec \lambda)\neq 0$. [Definition of arXiv:2608.30346, '\textbf{Classification complexity of homeomorphism group actions}'] Let \(X\) be a compact space and \(\mu\) be a Borel measure on \(X\) we say that a homeomorphism \(h \in \mathcal{H}(X)\) is bi-absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mu\) if for every \(E \subset X\) Borel we have \[\mu(E) = 0 \iff \mu(h(E)) = 0.\]
    We denote by \(\AC(X,\mu)\) the set of all homeomorphisms of \(X\) that are bi-absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mu\).

body: In geometric measure theory, Falconer's conjecture, named after Kenneth Falconer, is an unsolved problem concerning the sets of Euclidean distances between points in compact $d$ -dimensional spaces. Intuitively, it states that a set of points that is large in its Hausdorff dimension must determine a set of distances that is large in measure. More precisely, if $S$ is a compact set of points in $d$ -dimensional Euclidean space whose Hausdorff dimension is strictly greater than $d/2$, then the conjecture states that the set of distances between pairs of points in $S$ must have nonzero Lebesgue measure.

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2608.21551, '\bf Sparse Separable Factor Analysis in the Complex Domain with an Application to Local Fi'] For $j=1,\ldots,d$, suppose that $\Sigmab_j\in\CC^{p_j\times p_j}$ is Hermitian positive definite with factor-analytic representation
\begin{align}
  \Sigmab_j
  &=
  \Lambdab_j\Lambdab_j^\star+\Psib_j,
  \qquad
  \Lambdab_j\in\CC^{p_j\times k_j},
  
\end{align}
where $\Psib_j$ is a real-valued diagonal matrix with positive diagonal entries. Let $(c_1,\ldots,c_d)$ be the rescaling constants in \eqref{eq:iden-c}, and define
\begin{align*}
  \widetilde{\Sigmab}_j
  &=
  c_j\Sigmab_j,
  \qquad
  j=1,\ldots,d.
\end{align*}
Each $\widetilde{\Sigmab}_j$ admits the factor-analytic representation
\begin{align}
  \widetilde{\Sigmab}_j
  &=
  \Lb_j\Lb_j^\star+\Db_j,
  \qquad
  \Lb_j
  =
  c_j^{1/2}\Lambdab_j,
  \qquad
  \Db_j
  =
  c_j\Psib_j,
  \qquad
  j=1,\ldots,d,
  
\end{align}
and the rescaled diagonal matrices satisfy
\begin{align}
  \min\left\{\diag(\Db_1)\right\}
  &=
  \cdots
  =
  \min\left\{\diag(\Db_d)\right\}.
  
\end{align}
Furthermore, $\widetilde{\Sigmab}_d \otimes\cdots\otimes \widetilde{\Sigmab}_1 = \Sigmab_d \otimes\cdots\otimes \Sigmab_1$. The tuple $(\widetilde{\Sigmab}_1,\ldots,\widetilde{\Sigmab}_d)$ is the unique admissible multiplicative rescaling of $(\Sigmab_1,\ldots,\Sigmab_d)$ for which the corresponding diagonal matrices $(\Db_1,\ldots,\Db_d)$ satisfy \eqref{eq:app-cor-3}.

body:
[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2609.01770, 'Support of Dyson Brownian Motion'] Let \(z_0=u+\ri\eta\), \(w_0=u-\ri\eta\), and suppose that \(f\) is analytic in
neighborhoods of the closed discs \(B(z_0,\eta/2)\) and \(B(w_0,\eta/2)\). Define
\[
H_f(z,w):=\frac{f(z)-f(w)}{z-w}.
\]
For all integers \(a,b\geq0\),
\begin{equation}
\bigl|\partial_z^a\partial_w^bH_f(z_0,w_0)\bigr|
\leq C_{a,b}\eta^{-(a+b+1)}
\sup_{B(z_0,\eta/2)\cup B(w_0,\eta/2)}|f|,
\end{equation}
where
\[
C_{a,b}:=2^{a+b+1}a!b!\bigl(3^{-(a+1)}+3^{-(b+1)}\bigr).
\]
In particular,
\begin{equation}
\bigl|\partial_z^{k-1}\partial_w^kH_f(z_0,w_0)\bigr|
\leq\frac{2^{2k+2}}{3^{k+1}}(k-1)!k!\,\eta^{-2k}
\sup_{B(z_0,\eta/2)\cup B(w_0,\eta/2)}|f|.
\end{equation}

body:
For each n let M_n be an n by n random matrix with INDEPENDENT entries each uniform on {-1, +1}. Then P( M_n is singular ) = ( 1/2 + o_n(1) )^n. The matching lower bound is elementary: the probability that two rows are equal, or two rows are opposite, or two columns are equal, or two columns are opposite, is already of order n^2 2^{-n} = (1/2 + o(1))^n, and each such coincidence forces singularity. The content of the theorem is the UPPER bound, which settled a long-standing conjecture: Komlos (1967) proved the probability is o(1), Kahn, Komlos and Szemeredi (1995) obtained 0.999^n, and Tao-Vu and Bourgain-Vu-Wood improved the base to (1/sqrt(2) + o(1))^n before Tikhomirov reached the conjectured (1/2 + o(1))^n. Note precisely what is claimed: the ENTRIES are independent uniform signs, and the statement is asymptotic in n with an o(1) in the base, so it gives no numerical bound at any fixed n. The analogous question for a random symmetric sign matrix is a separate problem, resolved later and by different methods, and the result stated here must not be quoted for it. [Tikhomirov (2020), 'Singularity of random Bernoulli matrices', Ann. of Math. 191; arXiv:1812.09016]

[Defn def:Sm of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{2}$ be a weakly geometric
rough path. For each $m\geqslant1$, we define an analytic function
$S_{m}^{\gamma}:\mathbb{C}^{m}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ in the following
way. Given $a_{1},\cdots,a_{m}\in\mathbb{C}$, let $B:[0,1]\rightarrow\mathbb{C}^{m}$
be the path defined by 
\[
B_{t}\triangleq\sum_{j=1}^{m}\big(\int_{0}^{t}e^{a_{j}x_{s}}dy_{s}\big){\rm e}_{j}
\]
where $\{{\rm e}_{1},\cdots,{\rm e}_{m}\}$ denotes the standard basis
of $\mathbb{C}^{m}$. We define $S_{m}^{\gamma}(a_{1},\cdots,a_{m})$
to be the coefficient of the logarithmic signature of $B$ with respect
to the tensor ${\rm e}_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes{\rm e}_{m}$, i.e.
\[
S_{m}^{\gamma}(a_{1},\cdots,a_{m})\triangleq\big(\log S(B)\big)^{(1,\cdots,m)}.
\]

[Lemma lem:ExpIneq of arXiv:2608.30848, '\huge \bf Limit Laws of the Iterated Logarithm Under Sub-linear Expectations'] Let $\{X_1,\ldots, X_n\}$ be independent random variables on $(\Omega, \mathscr{H}, \widehat{\mathbb E})$. Denote
$A_n(p,y)=\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat{\mathbb E}[(X_i^+\wedge y )^p]$,
$ \breve{B}_{n,y}=\sum_{i=1}^n \breve{\mathbb E}[(X_i\wedge y)^2]$. Then for any $p\ge 2$, $x,y>0$, $0<\delta\le 1$, we have
$$
  \widehat{\mathbb V}\Big( \max_{k\le n} \sum_{i=1}^k(X_i-\breve{\mathbb E}[X_i])\ge x\Big)
\le    \widehat{\mathbb V}\big(\max_{k\le n} X_k> y \big)
+\exp\bigg\{-\frac{x^2}{2(xy+\breve{B}_{n,y})   }\bigg\},
$$
\begin{align*}
& \widehat{\mathbb V}\Big( \max_{k\le n} \sum_{i=1}^k(X_i-\breve{\mathbb E}[X_i])\ge x\Big) \\
\le & \widehat{\mathbb V}\big(\max_{k\le n} X_k> y \big)
  +2\exp\{p^p\}\bigg\{\frac{A_n(p,y)}{y^p} \bigg\}^{\frac{\delta x}{10y}}
+\exp\bigg\{-\frac{x^2}{2\breve{B}_{n,y}(1+\delta)   }\bigg\}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:ExpIneq of arXiv:2608.30848

[Corollary 2 (\textsf{Zero terminal condition}) of arXiv:2609.02064, 'Coalescence and fluctuations of O'Connell--Yor polymers\\ via the free-energy correlation '] For $n\geq1$, $\be>0$, and $x\neq\wt x$,
  \begin{align}
    \rmP_{\wt x,x}^{\rfree,\be}(\tau\leq n-1)
    &=
    \frac{2}{\be^2}\sgn(\wt x-x)
    \frac{\partial}{\partial x}
    \EE\bigl[
      \log Z_{\wt x}^{\rfree,\be}\log Z_x^{\rfree,\be}
    \bigr]
    
    \\
    &=
    \frac{2}{\be^2}\sgn(\wt x-x)
    \frac{\partial}{\partial x}
    \Cov\bigl(
      \log Z_{\wt x}^{\rfree,\be},
      \log Z_x^{\rfree,\be}
    \bigr)
    \notag\\
    &=
    -\frac{1}{\be^2}\sgn(\wt x-x)
    \frac{\partial}{\partial x}
    \EE\left[
      \bigl(
        \log Z_{\wt x}^{\rfree,\be}
        -\log Z_x^{\rfree,\be}
      \bigr)^2
    \right].
    \notag
  \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:1-companion of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Fix $\beta>0$ large enough and consider $\phi\sim \pi^0_\Lambda$, the $(2+1)$\textsc{d}  \ensuremath{\mathbb Z\textsc{gff}}\xspace model on $\Lambda=\llbracket 1,L\rrbracket^2$ 
        with a floor and zero boundary conditions. Set $H(L)$ and $N_n$ per (eq:H-def,eq:Nn-def of the paper).
For fixed $m$, let $\mathfrak{L}_n$ ($n=0,\ldots,m$) be the \texttt{large} $(H+1-n)$ level lines, where possibly $\mathfrak{L}_0$ does not exist. 
Let $I_n = \llbracket \frac{L}2- N_n^{2/3},\frac{L}2+N_n^{2/3}\rrbracket$, let $\rho_n(x) := \min\{y\geq 0 \,:\; (\frac{L}2+x,y)\in\mathfrak{L}_n\}$ be the vertical distance of~$\mathfrak{L}_n$ from $I_n$, and 
$Y_n(t) := N_n^{-1/3}\rho_n(t N_n^{2/3})$.
There exists a constant $\sigma>0$  such that:
\begin{enumerate}[1.,leftmargin=2em]
\item The law of $(Y_n(t))_{n=1}^m$ under $\pi_\Lambda^0$ converges weakly to the law of 
$m$ i.i.d.\ copies of the stationary Ferrari--Spohn diffusion $\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}$ on~$[-1,1]$.
\item For $L$ with $\pi_\Lambda^0(\mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ exists})>L^{-10}$, the law of $(Y_n(t))_{n=0}^m$ under $\pi_\Lambda^0(\cdot\mid\mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ exists})$ converges weakly to that of $m+1$ i.i.d.\ copies of 
$\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}$.
\item 
     For $L$ with $\pi_\Lambda^0(\mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ does not exist}) > L^{-10}$, the law of $(Y_n(t))_{n=1}^m$ under $\pi_\Lambda^0(\cdot\mid \mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ does not exist})$ converges weakly to that of $m$ i.i.d.\ copies of $\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}$.
\end{enumerate}
The same statements hold for $\bar{Y}_n(t)$ corresponding to $\bar{\rho}_n(x)=\max\{y\leq \frac{L}2:(\frac{L}2+x,y)\in\mathfrak{L}_n\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition 7 of arXiv:2601.22205, 'Transitive Sets of Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares'] The autotopy group of an orthogonal array (S, Xi, πi)q+2 i=1 is Aut(S, Xi) = n σ = (σi) ∈ q+2 Y i=1 ΣXi : σ(S) = S o , where ΣXi is the group of bijections from Xi to Xi and S is viewed as a subset of the product via Q πi : S →Q Xi. In fact, we will sometimes denote the array by S ⊂ q+2 Y i=1 Xi. Note that the autotopy group is just the group of isotopies from an array to itself.

On undirected nearest-neighbour Z^2 with iid Uniform[1,2] edge times and endpoints 0,n e1, integer n>=9, let gamma be the almost-sure unique geodesic and A_e the minimum passage time over paths avoiding e. The expected number of e in gamma with A_e-T(0,n e1)>=1/128 is at least n/2048. A fixed-path independence bound followed by a union over simple paths proves this marginal statement. It gives no persistence guarantee under positive coordinate resampling, and does not solve the KPZ exponent problem.

[Proposition prop:passiveshear of arXiv:2608.16915, 'Exact mean--covariance dynamics of the Weber field in the stochastic Lagrangian representa'] Fix $t_0>0$, $\nu>0$ and $0<\alpha<1$. For $K=2\pi n$, $n\in\mathbb N$, let
$a_K:=\nu K^{1-\alpha}$ and $b_K(x,y,z):=a_K\sin(Ky)\,e_1$, a smooth divergence-free field
on $\mathbb{T}^3$, and let $A^K_t$ be the inverse of the stochastic flow
$\,\mathrm{d} X_t=b_K(X_t)\,\mathrm{d} t+\sqrt{2\nu}\,\mathrm{d} W_t$. There is a constant $C_\alpha$ independent of
$K$ such that
\[
  \norm{\mathbb{E}\nabla A^K_{t_0}}_{C^\alpha}\le C_\alpha ,
\]
while, whenever $\nu K^2t_0\ge2$,
\[
  \mathbb{E}\norm{\nabla A^K_{t_0}}_{L^\infty}\ \ge\ c\,\sqrt{\nu t_0}\;K^{1-\alpha}
  \ \xrightarrow[K\to\infty]{}\ \infty .
\]

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2606.11068, '2606.11068'] Assume \eqref{eq:right-edge}. Consider the frog model on \(\mathbb Z\) in which activated particles perform
independent biased nearest-neighbour random walks with
\[
  \Pbb(X_1=1)=r,
  \qquad
  \Pbb(X_1=-1)=1-r,
\]
where \(r\in(0,1)\setminus\{1/2\}\). Set
\[
  \beta_c:=\frac1\gamma.
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If \(\E(\eta)<\infty\) and \(\beta>\beta_c\), then the frog model dies
out almost surely.
\item If \(\Pbb(\eta=0)<1\) and \(\beta<\beta_c\), then the frog model survives
with positive probability in the direction of the drift, that is, to the right
if \(r>1/2\) and to the left if \(r<1/2\).
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group, equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $X,Y$ be $G$-valued random variables with $h(X),h(Y) > -\infty$. 
    The {\em Ruzsa distance} between $X$ and $Y$ is 
    $$
    \dR(X,Y) =  h(X'-Y') - \frac{1}{2}h(X)-\frac{1}{2}h(Y),
    $$
    where $X',Y'$ are independent and have the same marginals as $X$ and $Y$,
	respectively.
    
    The {\em maximal Ruzsa distance} is
    $$
    \dstar(X,Y) = \sup h(X'-Y') - \frac{1}{2}h(X)-\frac{1}{2}h(Y)
    $$
    where the supremum is over all couplings $(X',Y')$ of $(X,Y)$, i.e.,
all jointly distributed random variables $(X',Y')$
with same marginals as $X$ and $Y$.

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em]
\item For every $h>0$ and $k\ge0$ the minimiser in (equation eq:jko of the paper) exists and is
unique.
\item As $h\downarrow0$, the piecewise-constant interpolants
$\bar\mu^{h}(t)=\mu^{h}_{\lfloor t/h\rfloor}$ converge in
$C([0,T];(\mathcal P_{2}(\mathbb{R}),W_{2}))$ to the unique gradient flow $(\mu_{t})$ of
$\mathcal{F}$ with $\mu_{0}$ as initial datum, that is, to the solution of
(equation eq:ffp of the paper) time-changed to speed $1$; the free OU flow (equation eq:forward of the paper)
corresponds to speed $\beta/2$.

    \(\alpha \in (0,\alpha_1]\),
    \[
        {\rm dim}_{\mathcal{H}}(G_{\rm loc})>1
        \qquad\text{a.s.}
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\end{enumerate}

If $X$ is a matrix with i.i.d. standard complex Gaussian entries, and if $M(t) = M+ t X$, then the eigenvalue trajectories $\{ \lambda_1(t), \dots, \lambda_N(t) \}$ are smooth on some neighborhood of $t=0$, and the derivatives at $t=0$ form a Gaussian vector with covariance $\mathscr{O}$ :

[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2607.23640, '{\sl Non-equilibrium fluctuations of a two-species exclusion process with slow boundary }'] For every \(\bm f\in\mathscr S^\dagger\),
	\[
	S_{t+\varepsilon}\bm f-S_t\bm f
	=
	\varepsilon \mathcal A^\dagger S_t\bm f
	+
	o(\varepsilon,t),
	\]
	where \(o(\varepsilon,t)\in\mathscr S^\dagger\), and
	\[
	\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow 0}
	\sup_{0\le t\le T}
	\frac{\|o(\varepsilon,t)\|_m}{\varepsilon}
	=
	0,
	\qquad
	\forall\,m\ge0.
	\]

body: For a subset K of a metric space and eps > 0, the covering number N(K, eps) is the minimum number of balls of radius eps needed to cover K; its logarithm log N(K, eps) is the metric entropy of K at scale eps. Metric entropy measures the effective size of a function class or parameter set and controls union-bound and chaining arguments in probability.
title: Covering Numbers and Metric Entropy

	The restriction of the mapping $X\mapsto\mathcal{L}_X$ to the time interval $(0\,,1]$

	\[
		\mathcal{N}_{k,\alpha,\beta,t}(\mathcal{L}_X) \lesssim \frac{\mathcal{N}_{k,\alpha,\beta,t}(X)}{\beta}
		\quad\forall t\in(0\,,1],
	\]
	and the implied constant depends on $\alpha\in(0\,,1)$ but is otherwise universal.

[Proposition prop:conv_BM_limit of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\bm{X}$ be a L\'evy process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with 
the characteristic triplet $(\bm{\gamma_X},\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{\Sigma_X}^{\scalebox{0.6}{$\top$}},\nu_{\bm{X}})$.
Let $\bm{X}^t=(\bm{X}_{st}/\sqrt{t})_{s\in[0,1]}$ for $t\in (0,1]$
and assume 
 $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d\setminus B_{\bm{0}}(1)}|\bm{w}|^q\nu_{\bm{X}}(\mathrm{d}\bm{w})<\infty$
 for some $q\in (0,2]$. 
 Let $\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{B}$ be the
Gaussian component of $\bm{X}$ in its L\'evy--It\^o decomposition~(equation eq:levy_ito_decomp of the paper) and define 
  $\bm{S}\coloneqq \bm{X}-\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{B}$. 

\noindent{\normalfont(a)} If 
$\bm{S}$ is 
of infinite variation or has finite variation with infinite activity and zero natural drift, then
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{X}^t,\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{B}\big)
=\mathcal{O}\big(t^{(q\wedge 1)
    (\min\{1/q,1/\beta_+\}-1/2)}\big), 
    \qquad \text{ as }t \downarrow 0.
\end{align*}

\noindent{\normalfont(b)} If $\bm{S}$ has finite variation and nonzero natural drift, then 
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{X}^t,\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{B}\big)
=\mathcal{O}\big(t^{(q\wedge 1)
    \min\{1/q-1/2,1/2\}}\big), 
    \qquad \text{ as }t \downarrow 0.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:conv_BM_limit of arXiv:2411.03609

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): (S12 (12)-(13).) Once the states at U are prescribed, independent-set choices factor over the gaps. For a length-two gap with endpoint states s,t in {0,1}: f_2(s,t) = 2 if s=t=0, else 1; and f_2(s,t) <= 2^{1-(s+t)/2}. For a length-three gap (its two interior vertices form an edge): f_3(s,t) = 3 if s+t=0, 2 if s+t=1, 1 if s+t=2; and f_3(s,t) <= 2^{2-(s+t)/2}. Notes: Both exponent bounds are tight only at their extreme states (f_2 at s=t=0 and at s+t=2). Multiplying over the cyclic gaps works because each selected u is an endpoint exactly TWICE, so sum of (s+t)/2 over gaps = |z|, and sum of (g-1) over gaps = n-d.

body: Let A be an n by n Hermitian matrix with eigenvalues lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ... >= lambda_n, and let 1 <= k <= n. Then max over n by k matrices V with orthonormal columns (V* V = I_k) of trace(V* A V) = lambda_1 + lambda_2 + ... + lambda_k, the sum of the k largest eigenvalues of A, with the maximum attained when the columns of V span the eigenspace of lambda_1, ..., lambda_k. Taking k=1 recovers the Rayleigh-Ritz characterization of the largest eigenvalue as a special case. [Ky Fan (1949); see Bhatia, Matrix Analysis]
title: Ky Fan's Trace Maximum Principle

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $\beta>0$, and $b\in\{0,1\}$. Then there exists a mutually independent family of smooth in space, continuous in time, centered, Gaussian fields $\{u^j\}_{j\geq 0}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $U^{\alpha,\beta,b}$ is equal to $\sum_{j= 0}^\infty u^j$ in law,
    \item for each $j\geq 1$, $u^j$ has a finite temporal range of dependence $2^{-\beta j}$,
    \item and there exists $C(d,\alpha,\beta)>0$ such that for all $j\geq 0$, $p\geq 1$, and $n\in\{0,1,2\}$,
    \[\|\nabla^n u^j\|_{L^p_\omega C^0_{t,x}}\leq  C (p^{1/2}+j^{1/2})2^{(n-\alpha)j}.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT, C012 version 1, proof (unaudited); no novelty or independent-review claim. Fix depth L>=4, H=L-1 hidden layers, input dimension d>=1 and finite total mean-field time T>=0. All hidden widths equal m>=2(4L+6). Let h^1_i=sigma(w_i dot x), h^l_j=sigma(m^(-1)sum_i B^l_ji h^{l-1}_i) for 2<=l<=H, and f=m^(-1)sum_j a_j h^H_j. Assume sigma globally C2 with absolute values of sigma and its first two derivatives at most one, ||X||<=1 and |Y|<=1, and population half-squared loss. Initialize two independent runs with every w coordinate, a entry and middle-matrix entry mutually independent standard normal. Train all parameters simultaneously by fresh-iid SGD samples or finite minibatch averages, with mean-field multipliers m on w,a and m^2 on each B^l. The common step sequence is deterministic, nonnegative and has total at most T; runs may use independent data. Write S2=sum eta_n^2. Boundary-only initial matching (w at the first layer and a at the last; internal permutations identity) has expected population loss-chord barrier bounded by C_{d,T,L}[(sqrt(log m)m^(-1/(d+2))+sqrt(S2))^(beta/2)+m^(-1/2)], with an explicit width- and dimension-independent positive beta=exp(-kappa_{T,L}T) from proof section 1. Thus eta_max<=m^(-2/(d+2)) gives O_{d,T,L}(m^(-beta/(2(d+2)))(log m)^(beta/4)). On an initialization event of failure probability <=(4L+6)/m, weighted top-matrix column averages control the top unbounded adjoint, while ordinary row and column averages bound every lower adjoint. The top truncation produces K^2 D plus an alpha-squared exponential tail; descending lower adjoints preserves the power K^2, retaining every gate difference. Accumulated Hilbert martingale noise and concave Osgood comparison give the rate. All Gaussian entries remain unbounded; trained-layer independence is not assumed. C010 v2 and C011 v1 are unaudited own-work dependencies. This does not assert a ReLU, fixed-step, low-risk-convergence, dimension-free, growing-depth or growing-time theorem; unrestricted permutation connectivity remains open.

body: Let G = (V, E) be a finite graph. A matching is a subset M of E such that no two edges in M share an endpoint. A matching M is a perfect matching if every vertex of V is an endpoint of exactly one edge of M (this requires |V| to be even). A vertex cover is a subset C of V such that every edge of E has at least one endpoint in C. [standard, e.g. Diestel, Graph Theory]
title: Matching, Perfect Matching, and Vertex Cover in a Graph

body: Let X_1, X_2, ... be independent random variables, and let T = intersection over n >= 1 of sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, ...) be the tail sigma-algebra. Then every event A in T satisfies P(A) in {0, 1}; equivalently, every T-measurable random variable is almost surely constant. [Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples]

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.03954, 'Galois representations ramified at one prime via relative deformation theory'] Let $\GG/\Z$ be a split connected reductive group with
$\dim Z(\GG)\leq1$. Fix a split maximal torus $\TT\subset\GG$ and a
set of simple roots $\Delta$. Assume that $(\GG,\TT,\Delta)$ admits an
odd cocharacter. Let $p$ be an odd prime which is Lie-good for $\GG$.
Then there exist infinitely many continuous representations $\rho:G_{\{p\}}\longrightarrow\GG(\Zp)$
whose images contain a principal congruence subgroup of
$\Gder(\Zp)$. If $\dim Z(\GG)=1$, the representations may be chosen so
that their images in $(\GG/\Gder)(\Zp)$ are open; in particular their
images are open in $\GG(\Zp)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.03954

There exists delta>0 uniform for eta>0,lambda1 in[2000,2500],lambda2 in[2600,3000], such that ordinary separately bias-corrected Adam with beta1=.9,beta2=.999,epsilon=eta outside sqrt and standard zero moments has limsup_t |eta C_active-38|>=delta for almost every full-dimensional initial position. The same holds simultaneously along any specified countable eta_n->0 for every absolutely continuous initialization law. The uniform positive constant is existential. Depends on the unaudited corrected scalar cycle-basin noncoincidence proof015v2 and source-potential strictness019v1. No p>1 or time-average conclusion is asserted.

CLAIM
There is delta>0 uniform for eta>0 and
 lambda1 in [2000,2500], lambda2 in [2600,3000]
such that ordinary separately bias-corrected Adam, b=.9,d=.999,
epsilon=eta outside sqrt, standard zero moments, on the positive
diagonal quadratic has

 limsup_t |eta*C_active,t-38| >= delta                    (1)

for Lebesgue-almost every full-dimensional initial position. No
independence assumption on the initialization law is made. For any fixed
countable eta_n->0, (1) holds simultaneously almost surely for every n
under an absolutely continuous initialization law. This is a p=1 result
with two distinct, both supercritical eigenvalues; it does not settle
p>1 or identify the nontracking attractor or an average curvature.

REVIEW PRIORITY / DEPENDENCIES
This proof depends on UNAUDITED claim015v2 (countability of the corrected
scalar unstable-cycle standard basin) and on the strict source-potential
case analysis written in019v1. Claim012 is NOT needed here: neither
coordinate is subcritical. The new hardest checks are the boundary
closure equality argument in Section2, the attractor argument in3, and
the Hausdorff/chain-transitivity reduction in4. No independent check is
claimed. The explicit delta is not computed.

1. SETUP AND COMPACTNESS
Use X_i=x_i/eta,M_i=m_i/(eta*lambda_i),V_i=v_i/(eta*lambda_i)^2,
rho_i=1/lambda_i. Let F_lambda be the uncorrected autonomous product map.
It is continuous on the physical state domain V_i>=0 and injective;
its explicit inverse is single-valued wherever there is a physical
predecessor. On a compact fully invariant set its restriction is a
homeomorphism. Corrected maps converge uniformly to F_lambda on compact
physical sets, uniformly over the stated eigenvalue rectangle, since
rho_i>=1/3000>0 and their clocks tend to zero.

The absorbing-box argument in proof023 Section1 applies independently
to each channel without a subcritical assumption: corrected increments
are bounded by80, |Mhat_next-X|<=720, every position enters[-801,801],
and raw moment limsups are bounded by801 and801^2. Thus the six-dimensional
tail is eventually in the fixed compact product box B with
|X_i|,|M_i|<=802,0<=V_i<=802^2. All omega limits lie in B.

For z=(X_i,M_i,V_i)_i define k_i(z)=1/(sqrt(dV_i+(1-d)X_i^2)+rho_i).
These are the next-step uncorrected scaled curvatures, continuous on B.
Put

 S_delta(lambda)={z in B:
 |sum_i lambda_i*X_i^2*k_i*(k_i-38)|
                  <=delta*sum_i lambda_i*X_i^2*k_i}.       (2)

If an actual corrected trajectory eventually has |eta*C_active-38|<delta,
its compact omega-limit K is fully invariant and contained in S_delta.
This follows by multiplying the quotient inequality before taking limits;
the extended inequality remains true when all X_i vanish. The quotient
itself is not divided at a zero gradient.

The set K is internally chain transitive for F_lambda. Here this means
that any ordered pair of points of K is joined by a finite epsilon-chain
in K, for every epsilon>0. To see this directly, take arbitrarily late
visits of the actual trajectory near the first and subsequently the
second point. The late segment stays arbitrarily close to K, and its
step errors relative to F_lambda tend uniformly to zero. Project all
segment states to K. Uniform continuity of F_lambda gives the required
epsilon-chain. In particular every point of K is chain recurrent.

2. EVERY FULL BOUNDED EXACT-LEVEL ORBIT HAS CRITICAL ENDS
Let K0 be any compact fully invariant subset of S_0(lambda), for fixed
positive eigenvalues with both caps>38. In source coordinates
y_i=X_i/c,mu_i=M_i/c,Vsource_i=V_i/c^2,e_i=rho_i/c, the defining identity
is exactly
 sum_i lambda_i*y_i^2*w_i,next*(w_i,next-2)=0.
Let L=sum_i lambda_i*Phi_i be the bounded Borel potential from019v1.
For every full orbit z_t in K0, the primary inequality and that identity
give

 L(z_(t+1))-L(z_t)=sum_i lambda_i*Psi_i(z_t)>=0.            (3)

The full-orbit F3 condition needed in the source proof holds at every
time by019 Section1. Since L is bounded, its values have limits at both
time ends and Psi_i(z_t)->0 as t->+infinity and as t->-infinity.

Although Phi is discontinuous, the following weaker closure fact is
enough. If scalar physical states in a fixed compact full-orbit set
converge, and their margins tend to zero, their limit is either an
origin/cycle state or on the pure-variance axis y=mu=0 with p,w<=1.
Here are the boundary checks, in addition to019's strictness cases.

Pass to a subsequence with fixed labels for p<=1 or p>1 and w<=1 or w>1.
The exact branch expressions are continuous up to their branch closures.
For both-low labels, the positive definite quadratic remains strict for
0<w<=1,u^2<=1/d; vanishing forces y=Delta=0. For upward labels, its
positive definite quadratic also remains strict at w=1, so vanishing
forces y=Delta=0. A positive-variance axis point with w>1 has a strict
Gamma decrease, and cannot be a zero limit; w=1 is the allowed axis
boundary. If p=1 and y=0, the variance recursion actually gives w>1,
so there is no additional p=w=1 zero-axis exception.

For downward labels, H(w)>0 extends to c<=w<=1. A zero limit would force
y=0; but p>=1,w<=1 and y=0 are inconsistent with V_next=dV and e<1/2.
The uniform full-orbit F3 bound stays strictly above c, so its other
endpoint is harmless. For both-high labels, the formulas extend to
p,w>=1. At y=0 they give A*Delta^2+Gamma(V)-Gamma(dV), which vanishes
only at Delta=V=0. At y!=0 the Schur and large-downward bounds of019
remain strict; equality gives exactly p=w=2,Delta=2y. The speed endpoint
u=d^(-1/2) cannot occur with e>0 on a compact physical set (the formula
for u in019 is strictly smaller). The rational gaps checked in
logs/stationary_margin_exact.json remain strictly positive on the
closed branch boundaries. This proves the stated closure fact.

Consequently both alpha- and omega-limit sets of any full orbit lie in
the product of these scalar zero-margin limit sets. Each limit set is
fully invariant. No positive-variance point on the axis can belong:
its future iterates stay on the axis and decay V geometrically, then
cross w=1 with strictly positive margin and enter a point outside that
closure-zero set. Thus both limit sets consist only of the nine product
origin/cycle states of019.

Since these states form finitely many separated fixed/period-two
orbits and F cannot jump between those groups near them, the full orbit
approaches ONE such periodic orbit at each end. Near every such state
the potential is continuous (p is either2 or1/e>2), and it has the same
value at both phases of a cycle. Denote its values on the two end
orbits by L_minus,L_plus. Equation(3) gives L_minus<=L_plus. If the
full orbit is not itself one critical periodic orbit, some scalar
margin is positive at some time: the only other zero-margin states are
the variance-axis points which exit the zero-margin set in finite time.
Therefore

 L_minus < L_plus for every noncritical connecting orbit. (4)

This is a finite, acyclic ordering of the possible critical ends. No
continuity of the potential away from the critical orbits was used.

3. AN EXACT-LEVEL INTERNALLY CHAIN-TRANSITIVE SET IS ONE CRITICAL ORBIT
Suppose K0 is also internally chain transitive. Choose one critical
periodic orbit A contained in K0 with maximal value of L among critical
orbits in K0; at least one exists by Section2. I claim A is Lyapunov
stable relative to K0. Otherwise choose a small fixed neighborhood U of
A whose closure contains no other critical orbit, points q_n->A in K0,
and their first exits from U. The exit times tend to infinity by
continuity at the periodic orbit. Extract the orbit segments centered
at their first exit in the compact set K0. Since F|K0 is a homeomorphism,
a subsequence gives a full orbit whose entire negative half is in cl(U)
and whose time0 point is an exit point away from A. Section2 implies
that its alpha-end is A and its omega-end is a critical orbit B in K0.
It is noncritical, so L(B)>L(A) by(4), contradicting maximality.

Stability plus Section2's end classification implies local attraction:
choose a smaller relative neighborhood all of whose forward orbits stay
in U; each such orbit has its omega-end in U, hence approaches A.
A compact invariant set which is Lyapunov stable and locally attractive
is an attractor. For clarity, stability and local attraction give
uniform attraction on a small compact neighborhood (finite subcover of
entry neighborhoods, then stability). Some iterate maps a sufficiently
small closed neighborhood into its interior. Saturating a suitably
nested finite family of neighborhoods under the preceding iterates
gives a trapping neighborhood for F with attractor A. This uses only
compactness and continuity.

An internally chain-transitive compact set cannot properly contain a
relative attractor: in a closed trapping neighborhood W of A, the compact
gap between F(W) and the complement of int(W) is positive. A sufficiently
small epsilon-chain starting in A cannot leave W. By choosing W to
exclude any specified point outside A (shrink the attracting neighborhood),
this contradicts internal chain transitivity unless K0=A. This is also
the attractor/chain-recurrence separation in Akin, arXiv2307.03815v1,
Theorem2.13 and equation2.32, pp.13--14. Thus K0 is one critical orbit.

4. UNIFORM NEAR-LEVEL REDUCTION
For each lambda in the stated compact rectangle choose small neighborhoods
of the five critical orbit groups (origin; two axes; two relative-phase
product cycles), continuous in their centers and with uniform radii.
They are pairwise separated; a map step near one group cannot enter a
different group, uniformly in lambda. Within a period-two group, phase
neighborhoods map only toward the opposite phase, by their positive
separation and continuity at the exact cycle. Cycle-coordinate neighborhoods
are inside claim015's uniform alternating-frame capture radius. The
origin neighborhood is small enough that both k_i>100 there and for
all sufficiently small clocks. These choices are possible uniformly:
cycle amplitudes a_i=1/38-rho_i stay bounded away from zero and claim015
supplies a uniform local cycle capture radius for rho_i in[0,.001].

There exists delta_*>0 such that any compact fully invariant, internally
chain-transitive K subset B intersect S_delta(lambda), delta<=delta_*,
lies in that union of neighborhoods. If not, take delta_n->0, parameters
lambda_n->lambda_*, and such K_n with a point outside that union.
Compactness of nonempty closed subsets of B gives a Hausdorff-convergent
subsequence K_n->K_*. Uniform convergence of F_lambda_n gives full
invariance of K_*. Continuity of(2) gives K_* subset S_0(lambda_*).

Internal chain transitivity also passes to this Hausdorff limit. Given
epsilon>0 and endpoints in K_*, approximate endpoints in K_n, take an
epsilon/3-chain inside K_n, and project all its points to K_*.
Uniform continuity and uniform map convergence bound each projected
step error by epsilon when n is large. Chain lengths need not be bounded;
the estimate is per step and does not accumulate along the chain.
Thus Section3 forces K_* to be a single critical orbit, contradicting
the selected outside-neighborhood point. This proves delta_* uniformly.

5. APPLY TO THE CORRECTED STANDARD TRAJECTORY
Choose delta=min(delta_*,1), shrinking if necessary. If the limsup in(1)
were strictly below delta, the corrected omega limit K of Section1
would satisfy the hypotheses of Section4. Its actual state tail approaches
K and hence eventually stays in the union of the chosen neighborhoods.
Uniform map convergence preserves their nonjump separation at late times,
so the tail stays in one critical orbit group's neighborhood.

If that group is the origin, both corrected scaled curvatures are>100
eventually. Their gradient-weighted average is>100 at every defined
gradient, contrary to the width<=1 band about38. Thus at least one
coordinate remains in a cycle neighborhood. By the capture conclusion
of015 its corrected scalar orbit converges to that exact two-cycle.
For each fixed eigenvalue,015 proves that only countably many standard
initial values of that coordinate can do so. The exceptional full
initializations are therefore contained in a countable union of vertical
and horizontal lines, a Lebesgue null set. No product-law assumption is
needed. Scaling from X0 to x0 preserves nullity.

Finite zero-gradient problems can be excluded by the finite-time analytic
argument in023 Section7: on each nonzero initial half-line each scalar
position X_t(X0) is analytic and not identically zero (bounded increments
give properness as |X0|->infinity). Its zero set is countable. Excluding
the corresponding countable lines leaves every active quotient defined.

The parameter choices, absorbing box, neighborhoods and compactness
contradiction were uniform over the rectangle, giving a single delta.
For a countable eta sequence, take the countable union of the null sets.
This proves the stated candidate. The full-rank p>1 gap remains: rho_i
then approach0, so the maps are not uniformly continuous at the origin
in the limiting normalization; this proof does not cover that limit.

VALIDATION
Exact rational strictness checks: scripts/check_stationary_margin.py.
Absorbing-box and scalar matrix checks: scripts/check_fullrank_algebra.py.
Source potential and equality extraction: proof026 with primary PDF
pp.54--58. Scalar corrected capture/noncoincidence: claim015v2. General
attractor separation: Akin primary Theorem2.13 and Eq2.32. The compactness
and chain arguments are mathematical proofs, not certified floating-point
computations. Every dependency and the full new claim remain UNAUDITED

[Theorem of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] [ancona]
Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group and $\mu$ be a symmetric probability measure on $G$ supported on a finite generating set of $G$. Then $\partial_M G$ is homeomorphic to the hyperbolic boundary of $G$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition 11 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM, $X$ be a sequentially closed subset of $\mf A$, and $\mu$ be an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-additive function. Let $\mathcal{K}$ be a ring such that $\mathcal{K}\subset D_\mu\subset\sigma_0(\mathcal{K})$ and $\im\mu|_{\mathcal{K}}\subset X$. Then $\im \mu\subset X$.

Let D be the open unit disk and f : D → D holomorphic. Then for all z, w in D, |f(z) - f(w)| / |1 - conj(f(w)) f(z)| ≤ |z - w| / |1 - conj(w) z|, and for all z in D, |f'(z)| ≤ (1 - |f(z)|^2) / (1 - |z|^2). If equality holds in the first inequality for some pair z ≠ w, or in the second for some z, then f is a conformal automorphism of D, f(z) = e^{iθ}(z - a)/(1 - conj(a) z) with a in D and θ real, and then equality holds everywhere. Equivalently, f does not increase the Poincaré (hyperbolic) distance on D, and strictly decreases it unless f is an automorphism.

\P(\tilde{Z}_{n+1}=j \mid \tilde{Z}_n=i) = \begin{cases}

[Proposition gammadef of arXiv:2603.20078, '\bf \Large Gated Infinite Server Queues in Light Traffic'] Suppose that $\sigma_i$ are i.i.d.\ random variables with density 
$g$ and finite moments of all orders. Let $f$ denote the invariant density of the 
stationary stage length, and suppose that $\beta_k:=\int_0^\infty x^k f(x) dx$, 
$k=1,2,\ldots$, denote its moments (which exist as shown in Proposition (prop:pi-moments of the paper)). 
Define the quantities
 \begin{equation} 
\gamma_{m,k} \;:=\; \mathbb{E}[\min(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\ldots,\sigma_k)^m].
\end{equation}
Then the moments $\{\beta_i\}$, $i=2,3,\ldots,$ satisfy the infinite linear system
\begin{eqnarray}  \nonumber
\beta_i &=& \gamma_{i,1} + \frac{\lambda^2 \beta_2}{2!} \, \left( \gamma_{i,1}-\gamma_{i,2} \right) 
- \frac{\lambda^3 \beta_3}{3!} \, \left( \gamma_{i,1}-\gamma_{i,3} \right) +\cdots
+(-1)^j \frac{\lambda^j \beta_j}{j!} \, \left( \gamma_{i,1}-\gamma_{i,j} \right) +\cdots \\ 
&& \hspace{4.1in} i=2,3,4,\ldots \;\;
\end{eqnarray}
The invariant density $f$ of the stage length can be expressed in terms of the moments 
$\{\beta_i\}$, the density $g$, and complementary distribution function $\overline{G}$ 
of the service time by the series
\begin{eqnarray}  \nonumber
f(y) &=& g(y)\,
 \left[ 1+ \frac{\lambda^2 \beta_2}{2!} \left(1- 2\overline{G}(y) \right) - \frac{\lambda^3 \beta_3}{3!} 
 \left( 1 - 3\overline{G}(y)^2 \right) \right. \\  
&& \hspace{2.3in} \left. + \frac{\lambda^4 \beta_4}{4!} \left( 1 - 4\overline{G}(y)^3 \right) - \cdots \right].
\end{eqnarray}
title: Proposition gammadef of arXiv:2603.20078

[Theorem JJKLSX_hittingprob of arXiv:2506.10448, 'Hitting probabilities and the Ekstr\"om--Persson conjecture'] Let $X$ be an Ahlfors regular metric space, $\mu$ the natural Ahlfors regular probability 
measure on $X$ and $\underline{r}$ a sequence of radii such that 
$s_2(\underline{r})\leq \dim X$. Then, for all analytic sets $F\subseteq X$, 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[i)] if $\dimp F< \dim X-s_2(\underline{r})$, then $F\cap E_{\underline{r}}(\omega)
      =\emptyset$ almost surely,

    \item[ii)] if $\dimh F>\dim X-s_2(\underline{r})$, then $F\cap E_{\underline{r}}(\omega)
      \neq\emptyset$ almost surely and

    \item[iii)] if   $\alpha>0$  and $\dimp F>\dim X-\frac 1\alpha$, then 
      $F\cap E_{\alpha}(\omega)\neq\emptyset$ almost surely.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Author-checked proof, not independently reviewed; novelty unassessed. If theta is an invertible measurable ergodic P-preserving map of a standard Borel probability space with measurable inverse, and Q=fP is a probability law, then on an extension with independent uniforms there is an almost surely finite N in {0,1,...} such that theta^N Z has law Q when Z~P. N can inspect the entire state and is not claimed to be a stopping time for a smaller natural filtration; no finite-mean bound is asserted. Deterministic integer shifts cannot generally do this.
Standard Borel probability space
Invertible ergodic P-preserving theta
Nonnegative integrable density f with integral one
Independent auxiliary uniforms permitted

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:fc9f20a51e7c9ef9dfb895c4beb4a6294fa3f0ebe26307574fdbf6e35155fb19","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/fc/fc9f20a51e7c9ef9dfb895c4beb4a6294fa3f0ebe26307574fdbf6e35155fb19.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b9824719ff4b2a3312910c728aad2c8205795c1467e95937f7821e8e485b9270","bundle_entry_key":"forward-filling","bundle_id":"population.probability-conditioned-laws-and-stationary-flows-001","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-1000-20h-20260906/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.measure:randomized-nonnegative-shift-to-absolutely-continuous-ergodic-law","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"For an integrable density h let Lh=h composed with theta^(-1). Thus pushing hP forward under theta gives (Lh)P. Set

    a_0=1,  b_0=f,
    m_n=min(a_n,b_n),
    a_(n+1)=L(a_n-m_n),
    b_(n+1)=b_n-m_n.

All these functions are measurable and nonnegative. Inductively 0<=a_n<=1. The b_n decrease and are bounded above by f, so they have an integrable pointwise limit b_infinity. Since L preserves integrals, both remaining densities have the same mass r_n:

    integral a_n dP = integral b_n dP = r_n,
    r_n decreases to r = integral b_infinity dP,
    sum_(n>=0) integral m_n dP = 1-r.

### The remaining mass must be zero

Iteration gives the exact identity

    a_n = 1 - sum_(k=0)^(n-1) L^(n-k)m_k.

For each fixed k, the ergodic theorem for the measure-preserving transformation theta^(-1) gives

    (1/M) sum_(n=k+1)^(M-1) L^(n-k)m_k
       -> integral m_k dP

in L1(P). The L1 assertion follows from the usual almost-sure ergodic theorem and equality of the integrals for nonnegative averages, or by approximation from bounded functions. Initial omitted terms do not affect the limit.

Truncate the sum in k at K. Its tail has L1 norm at most sum_(k>=K) integral m_k dP, uniformly in M. That tail tends to zero as K grows. Therefore

    (1/M) sum_(n=0)^(M-1) a_n -> r

in L1(P), where r on the right is the constant function.

Suppose r>0. There is a delta>0 such that B={b_infinity>=delta} has positive P-measure. On B,

    m_n=min(a_n,b_n) >= min(a_n,delta)
        >= min(1,delta) a_n,

where the last step uses a_n<=1. Averaging and integrating over B gives

    liminf_M (1/M) sum_(n<M) integral_B m_n dP
        >= min(1,delta) r P(B) > 0.

But the entire sum of the integrals of m_n is at most one, so its Cesaro average tends to zero. This contradiction proves r=0. In particular sum_n m_n=f in L1 and almost everywhere.

### Realizing the matching as a random shift

Sample Z with law P and independent U_0,U_1,... uniform on [0,1]. At stage n, if not previously accepted, inspect theta^n Z and accept when

    U_n <= h_n(theta^n Z),
    h_n=m_n/a_n on {a_n>0}, and h_n=0 elsewhere.

By induction, the subprobability distribution of theta^n Z before this test is a_n P. The mass accepted at stage n has distribution m_n P, and the surviving mass pushed forward has distribution a_(n+1)P. Hence P(N>=n)=r_n tends to zero, while the law of theta^N Z is sum_n m_n P=fP=Q. Every U_n is independent of Z and of preceding U's, so the induction is valid even though h_n can inspect an entire trajectory. This proves the lemma.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:b8da3914c025f776becd4c7419db38e80462225508c91d60d591f38f130c642d","revision_digest":"sha256:2b15255aa3a9ad0d5f14525fa3513e2c3fed532d5e9ecbdaa534014e943ad3e7","source_id":"owner-original-probability-research-20260906:forward-filling","source_revision":"author-checked-20260906-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Lem 248 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Assume that $L\ge1$ and that condition \eqref{e:deriv.p.bound} holds. Let $\vX\equiv \vX^N$ be the process defined by \eqref{e:X.decomp}
and \eqref{e:Delta.X.Ising}, and assume that condition~\eqref{e:w2.coupling.assumption} holds. Then the processes $\vX^\trstar$ and $\vX^\frstar$ of Definitions~\ref{d:trunc} and \ref{d:froze} can be coupled so that
	\[
	\E\Big[\|\vX^\trstar(1)
		-\vX^\frstar(1)\|^2\Big]
	\le o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
uniformly in $N$.

\begin{proof}
Consider $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$. Abbreviate 
	\[\epsilon(\trK)\equiv 
		\frac{1/\trK^6}
		{1+1/\trK^6}\,.\]
If we let $U$ denote a random variable sampled uniformly at random from the interval $[0,1]$, then 
$X^{\frstar,\sigma}(1)$ is equidistributed as
	\[
	X^{\frstar,\sigma}(1,U)
	\equiv
	\begin{cases} \displaystyle
	X^{\trstar,\sigma}\bigg(1,
		\bigg\lceil
		\frac{M\cdot U}{1-\epsilon(\trK)}
		\bigg\rceil\bigg)
	& \textup{if }U\in[0,1-\epsilon(\trK)]\,,\\
	T(U) & 
		\textup{if }U\in(1-\epsilon(\trK),1]\,,
	\end{cases}
	\]	
where $T$ is a random variable confined to $[-2\trK,2\trK]$. On the other hand, $X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1)$ is equidistributed as
	\[
	X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1,U)
	\equiv 
	\begin{cases} \displaystyle
	X^{\trstar,\sigma}\bigg(1,
		\bigg\lceil
		\frac{M\cdot U}{1-\epsilon(\trK)}
		\bigg\rceil\bigg)
	& \textup{if }U\in[0,1-\epsilon(\trK)]\,,\\ \displaystyle
	X^{\trstar,\sigma}\bigg(1,
		\bigg\lceil
		\frac{M\cdot 
			[U-(1-\epsilon(\trK))]}{\epsilon(\trK)}
		\bigg\rceil\bigg)
	&\textup{if } U\in(1-\epsilon(\trK),1]
	\end{cases}\,.
	\]
Under this coupling, we have
	\[\E\Big[(
	X^{\frstar,\sigma}(1,U)
	-X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1,U))^2
	\Big]
	\le O(1) \epsilon(\trK)
	\E\Big[
	T(U)^2 + X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1)^2\Big]\,.
	\]
Since $T(U)$ is confined to $[-2\trK,2\trK]$, we clearly have $\E[T(U)^2] \le 4\trK^2$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.II.III.Ising} that $X^\sigma(1)$ has bounded second moment for $\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$. Under condition~\eqref{e:w2.coupling.assumption}, it follows from Lemma~\ref{l:martingale.sup.bound.X.I.minus.mean} combined with \eqref{e:X.I.squared.expectation.avg.bound} that  $X^\RomI(1)$ also has bounded second moment. Combining with
Corollary~\ref{c:X.versus.trstar.X.W2.error.estimate} gives that $\vX^\trstar(1)$ has bounded second moment. Substituting into the above bound, and recalling the definition of $\epsilon(\trK)$, we conclude
	\[\E\Big[(
	X^{\frstar,\sigma}(1,U)
	-X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1,U))^2
	\Big]
	\le O(1) 
	\frac{\trK^2 + O(1)}{\trK^6}
	\le o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
which proves the claim for $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$.
A similar argument proves the analogous claim for $X^\Ising$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Bailey's 6psi6 summation (W. N. Bailey 1936). For |q| < 1 and |a^2 q/(bcde)| < 1, with (x;q)_n for negative n defined by (x;q)_(-n) = 1/(x q^(-n);q)_n, sum over n in Z of (1 - a q^(2n))/(1 - a) (b;q)_n (c;q)_n (d;q)_n (e;q)_n / ((aq/b;q)_n (aq/c;q)_n (aq/d;q)_n (aq/e;q)_n) (a^2 q/(bcde))^n = (aq, aq/(bc), aq/(bd), aq/(be), aq/(cd), aq/(ce), aq/(de), q, q/a; q)_inf / (aq/b, aq/c, aq/d, aq/e, q/b, q/c, q/d, q/e, a^2 q/(bcde); q)_inf. It is the bilateral extension of the very-well-poised 6phi5 summation: putting e = a makes aq/e = q, and since 1/(q;q)_(-m) = 0 for m >= 1 the sum stops at n >= 0 and becomes the 6phi5 sum. Letting c, d, e tend to infinity in suitable directions recovers Ramanujan's 1psi1 summation, and through it the Jacobi triple product. Proofs: Bailey's original from the 6phi5 sum and analytic continuation; Askey and Ismail by a uniqueness argument for functions of b on the points q^n; Schlosser gave elementary proofs and multidimensional extensions.
statement as in G. Gasper and M. Rahman, Basic Hypergeometric Series, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press (2004), (5.3.1) and (II.33); W. N. Bailey, Series of hypergeometric type which are infinite in both directions, Quart. J. Math. Oxford 7 (1936) 105-115; R. Askey and M. E. H. Ismail, The very well poised 6psi6, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 77 (1979) 218-222
checked numerically (check_6psi6_170.py, 60 significant digits): the bilateral sum truncated at |n| <= 400 against the products, 40 random cases with q in {0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6} and a, b, c, d, e in +-[1.1, 3.9] with |a^2 q/(bcde)| <= 0.5: worst relative error 1.7395e-56. The negative control (--neg: aq/d for aq/(de) in the numerator) failed in all 40 cases. The proof is cited, not reproduced

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited), w730-T355-C004 version 2. Not independently checked. Let d,q>=1 be finite integers, H a constant symmetric positive definite
q by q matrix, and M its largest eigenvalue. Let A:R^d->R^{q x q} be C^1,
with A(u)^T A(u)=H for all u, and assume

    sup_u sum_{i=1}^d ||partial_i A(u)||^2 <= D^2 < infinity.

Matrix norms are operator norms; vector norms are Euclidean. Let z_k in
R^q be iid, independent of the past, centrally symmetric, with
E z_k z_k^T=I_q. No moment beyond the second is assumed. Fix sigma>=0,
0<rho<2 and 0<eta<=rho/M. Initialize at deterministic u_0 and v_0=0.
Label-noise SGD for residual A(u)v and loss L(v)=v^T H v/2 is

    u_{k+1,i}=u_{k,i}-eta sigma z_k^T partial_i A(u_k)v_k,
    v_{k+1}=(I-eta H)v_k-eta sigma A(u_k)^T z_k.

The deterministic tangential gradient is zero since H is constant.
For a bounded C^2 function F:R^{d+q}->R with bounded derivatives put
f(u)=F(u,0), F_2=sup ||D^2 f|| and F_vv=sup ||D_v^2 F||. Then, for T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=k<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_k,v_k)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),

    C(T)=sigma^2 q [F_vv+T sigma^2 D^2 F_2]/[2(2-rho)].       (1)

Thus a=1, with a constant linear in T, for every finite d,q and any fixed
stability margin eta M<=rho<2. The limiting process is constant, as also
given by the known trace-Hessian flow in Li-Wang-Arora, Corollary 5.2,
arXiv:2110.06914v4, pp.8-9 and 33. The quantitative estimate is the claim
here. Priority over all later literature has not been established.
H=A(u)^T A(u) is constant positive definite with largest eigenvalue M
A in C1(R^d,R^{q x q}), sup_u sum_i operator_norm(partial_i A)^2<=D^2
iid centrally symmetric labels, independent of the past, EzzT=I_q; no fourth or sixth moment required
v0=0, deterministic u0, sigma>=0
0<rho<2, 0<eta<=rho/M

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d874efca62efe75b9f73b7a3de6f0abdc0885fb8f97f8946448f517ca7989bf8","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d8/d874efca62efe75b9f73b7a3de6f0abdc0885fb8f97f8946448f517ca7989bf8.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:247dae2f2ad9f7fa2f3b76e27faa583ce4fab2eeb096b870775440ac64ebccd3","bundle_entry_key":"t355-constant-hessian-second-moment","bundle_id":"population.t355-finite-dimensions-and-constant-hessian-second-moments-002","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability","draft":"w730/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.stochastic_approximation:t355-constant-hessian-rotating-frame-sgd-weak-order-one-second-moments","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Constant Hessian and rotating output frames: explicit second-moment rate

Claim w730-T355-C004, version 2. Kind: narrowed. Target: 1.
Status: proof (unaudited). Exact checks pass; independent review is pending.

The covariance is proportional to the Hessian **on the minimizing manifold**,
as specified in the dossier's repaired noise model. No proportionality away
from that manifold is assumed. This distinction matters in the example below.

## Statement

Let d,q>=1 be finite integers, H a constant symmetric positive definite
q by q matrix, and M its largest eigenvalue. Let A:R^d->R^{q x q} be C^1,
with A(u)^T A(u)=H for all u, and assume

    sup_u sum_{i=1}^d ||partial_i A(u)||^2 <= D^2 < infinity.

Matrix norms are operator norms; vector norms are Euclidean. Let z_k in
R^q be iid, independent of the past, centrally symmetric, with
E z_k z_k^T=I_q. No moment beyond the second is assumed. Fix sigma>=0,
0<rho<2 and 0<eta<=rho/M. Initialize at deterministic u_0 and v_0=0.
Label-noise SGD for residual A(u)v and loss L(v)=v^T H v/2 is

    u_{k+1,i}=u_{k,i}-eta sigma z_k^T partial_i A(u_k)v_k,
    v_{k+1}=(I-eta H)v_k-eta sigma A(u_k)^T z_k.

The deterministic tangential gradient is zero since H is constant.
For a bounded C^2 function F:R^{d+q}->R with bounded derivatives put
f(u)=F(u,0), F_2=sup ||D^2 f|| and F_vv=sup ||D_v^2 F||. Then, for T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=k<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_k,v_k)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),

    C(T)=sigma^2 q [F_vv+T sigma^2 D^2 F_2]/[2(2-rho)].       (1)

Thus a=1, with a constant linear in T, for every finite d,q and any fixed
stability margin eta M<=rho<2. The limiting process is constant, as also
given by the known trace-Hessian flow in Li-Wang-Arora, Corollary 5.2,
arXiv:2110.06914v4, pp.8-9 and 33. The quantitative estimate is the claim
here. Priority over all later literature has not been established.

## Proof

Set B=I-eta H and Q_k=E[v_k v_k^T]. Conditional centering gives exactly

    Q_{k+1}=B Q_k B+eta^2 sigma^2 H, Q_0=0.                 (2)

The cross terms vanish conditional on the past. The conditional covariance
of A(u_k)^T z_k is H, even though u_k and v_k are correlated. Diagonalizing
H, the geometric sum of (2) gives

    Q_k=eta sigma^2 (I-B^{2k})(2I-eta H)^{-1}.              (3)

In an eigenbasis of H, its j-th eigenvalue is

    eta sigma^2 [1-(1-eta lambda_j)^{2k}]/(2-eta lambda_j).

Here 0<eta lambda_j<2. The denominator is at least 2-rho>0 and the bracket
lies in [0,1]. Consequently

    E|v_k|^2<=eta c, c=sigma^2 q/(2-rho).                 (4)

The recurrence maps finite states to finite states almost surely. Induction
in (2) proves finiteness of the normal second moments without higher noise
moments. This also justifies the conditional covariance calculations.

Write h_k=u_{k+1}-u_k. Conditional on the past,

    E[h_k|past]=0,
    E[|h_k|^2|past]=eta^2 sigma^2 sum_i |partial_i A(u_k)v_k|^2
                  <=eta^2 sigma^2 D^2 |v_k|^2.           (5)

The bound on the Hessian of f and Taylor's theorem imply

    |E[f(u_{k+1})-f(u_k)]|
      <=F_2 E|h_k|^2/2<=F_2 eta^3 sigma^2 D^2 c/2.

The linear term has zero conditional expectation: grad f(u_k) is past
measurable and bounded, while h_k has a finite second moment by (4)-(5).
Telescoping for any integer K with K eta^2<=T yields

    |E f(u_K)-f(u_0)|<=T eta F_2 sigma^2 D^2 c/2.         (6)

The law of (u_k,v_k) is invariant under (u,v)->(u,-v). Replacing
(v,z) by (-v,-z) leaves u_{k+1} fixed and reverses v_{k+1}. Central
symmetry and v_0=0 start this induction. It follows that
E[D_v F(u_k,0)v_k]=0. Taylor's theorem in the normal variable gives

    |E[F(u_k,v_k)-f(u_k)]|<=F_vv E|v_k|^2/2<=F_vv eta c/2.

Combining with (6) proves (1), for every K and the same common horizon T.
There is no division by sigma or T. Both sigma=0 and T=0 are included.
The only independence used is that of each fresh label from the past.

## A nonconstant finite-step tangential process

For d=1,q=2, let A(u) be rotation through u, so H=I but A'(u) is nonzero.
With u_0=0, sigma=1 and independent Rademacher coordinates in z_0,z_1,

    v_1=-eta z_0, u_1=0,
    u_2-u_0=eta^2 z_1^T J z_0, J=[[0,-1],[1,0]],
    E[(u_2-u_0)^2]=2 eta^4>0.

Thus the tangential process need not be pathwise constant. This is a
different case from constant A with exclusively normal noise. It does not
contradict a statement requiring covariance proportional to Hess L at
every off-manifold point: the rotation model has tangential noise there
and does not satisfy that stronger hypothesis. On v=0, its covariance is
exactly sigma^2 diag(0,H), as required in the dossier repair and source.

## Scope

This supplies the constant-Hessian target for the explicitly stated
on-manifold covariance model, including rotating output frames and
symmetric labels with only second moments. Fixed off-manifold starts in a
uniform supremum including zero and the general curved-manifold problem
remain open. Independent review is required before checked-proof status.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:187fcaa1123ef86d82609c8874d3b3e63fce8e93ce7a1a85148d5aa8311216e5","revision_digest":"sha256:2b4377d095b1ebefa1c317c143b9e1b37320f3d7fb6515d8177c3a6f3befdb24","source_id":"owner-own-work:w730:T355:w730-T355-C004:v2","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v2-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Definition defHN of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] The \emph{logarithmic population sizes} $H^N=(H^N_0,H^N_1)$ are defined by
    $$
      H^N_i(t)
        = \log_N^+\big(X^N_i(\tfrac{t\log N}{\varphi_N})\big),
        \ i\in\{0,1\},
    $$
    where $\log_N^+(\cdot):= \max\{\log_N(\cdot), 0\}$ denotes the positive part of the logarithm to the base $N$.

    Throughout we will assume that $(X_0, X_1)$ satisfies for $t\ge 0$ the Moran dynamics~(equation Morandyn of the paper) with $a>0$ and starting condition $(X_0(0), X_1(0)) = (N-1, 1)$ where selection is moderate  or quasi-strong in the sense of Definition~(def:moderate-selection of the paper).
    With a view towards part II of Theorem~(thm:house of the paper) we extend $X^N$ to the negative time axis by putting $(X_0(t), X_1(t)) = (N,0)$ (and consequently $(H_0^N(t), H_1^N(t)) = (1,0)$) for $t<0$.
title: Definition defHN of arXiv:2605.10617

    \begin{equation}

    where $w(t) \in H$, with $H$ being the real vector space defined by
    $$H \coloneqq \{w : \mathbb{Z}^2_{\star,N}\to\mathbb{C} \mid w_k = \overline w_{-k} \} \,,$$
    
    and $W^k_t$ are $\mathbb{C}$-valued Brownian motions which are independent except for the reality condition
   $W^k = \overline{W^{-k}}$. Let $H_I \coloneqq \{w \in H \mid  w_k = 0 \text{ for all } k \notin I\}$, where $I \coloneqq \{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \mid |k| = 5\}$. Then for all $N$ large enough there are $0 < \nu_* \le \nu^* < \infty$
    (possibly depending on $N$) such that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item When $\nu < \nu_*$, (equation eq:stoch-navier-stokes of the paper) has multiple invariant measures, at least one of which gives $H_I$ measure $0$. Furthermore, for all $\delta > 0$ there is some $\eta > 0$ such that for all $w(0) \notin H_I$,
        \begin{equation}
            \limsup_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t}|\{s \leq t \mid d(w(s), H_I) < \eta \}| < \delta \quad a.s.\,,
        \end{equation}
        where $|\cdot|$ denotes Lebesgue measure on $[0,t]$ and $d(w,H_I) \coloneqq \inf_{z \in H_I} \|w - z\|$ is the distance from $w$ to $H_I$.
        \item When $\nu > \nu^*$, (equation eq:stoch-navier-stokes of the paper) has a unique invariant measure, and it is supported on $H_I$. Furthermore, almost surely
        $$\limsup_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t}\ln d(w(t),H_I) < 0 \,.$$
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Consider the initial value problem y' = f(t, y), y(t_0) = y_0, with f continuous on a rectangle around (t_0, y_0) and Lipschitz in y uniformly in t there. Then there is an interval around t_0 on which the problem has exactly one solution. Continuity of f alone (Peano) gives existence but not uniqueness: y' = 2 sqrt(|y|), y(0) = 0 has infinitely many solutions.

body:
There is an integer N(n), depending only on the dimension n, with the following property. Let A be a bounded subset of R^n and suppose that to each x in A is assigned a closed ball B(x, r(x)) with r(x) > 0 centred at x. Then one can select from that family countable subfamilies G_1, ..., G_{N(n)}, each consisting of PAIRWISE DISJOINT balls, whose union covers A. Consequence for measures: if mu is a Radon measure on R^n and the balls are a fine cover of a set A, one may extract a countable disjoint subfamily covering mu-almost all of A; this is what makes the differentiation theorem for Radon measures work without any doubling assumption.
Centres must be the points of A themselves (the theorem is FALSE for balls merely containing the points), radii positive and bounded, A bounded.
The constant N(n) depends only on dimension, not on the set or the radii;
unlike the Vitali covering lemma no enlargement of balls is needed and no doubling property of the measure is used.

On the uniform cube {-1, 1}^n let f be real, f^(S) = E[f chi_S] its Walsh coefficients and W_k = sum over |S| = k of f^(S)^2. For rho in [-1, 1], T_rho is the noise operator: T_rho f(x) = E[f(Y)] where the Y_i are independent with P(Y_i = x_i) = (1 + rho)/2, so T_rho chi_S = rho^|S| chi_S. Let S(rho) = Stab_rho[f] with f not identically 0, 0 < rho <= 1, and nu_rho(k) = W_k rho^k/S(rho). Then mu(rho) = rho S'(rho)/S(rho) = E_{nu_rho}[K] and rho mu'(rho) = Var_{nu_rho}(K) >= 0, so mu is nondecreasing on (0, 1], strictly iff the weight sits on at least two levels; mu(rho) -> k_min as rho -> 0 and mu(1) = sum_k k W_k / sum_k W_k. With k_min and k_max the least and largest levels carrying weight, a^{k_max} <= S(a rho)/S(rho) <= a^{k_min} for 0 < a <= 1, with equality for some a < 1 iff k_min = k_max; and for fixed 0 < a < 1 the ratio rho -> S(a rho)/S(rho) is nonincreasing, strictly unless one level carries all the weight.

    such that for all $0< \ep < C(\alpha,\beta)^{-1}$,  there exists $C(\ep,\alpha,\beta,d)>0$ such that for all $p \geq 1$,
    \begin{align}
        \|I^{1,j,N}\|_{\mathcal{C}^0_y L^p_\omega \mathcal{C}^{1-\frac{1-\alpha}{\beta} -\ep}_t \mathcal{C}^{1}_x } &\leq C K p^{\lambda \lor 1/2} 2^{- C^{-1} j}, \\
        \|I^{2,j,N}\|_{\mathcal{C}^0_y L^p_\omega \mathcal{C}^{1-\ep}_t \mathcal{C}^1_x} &\leq C K^{4(\frac{2-\alpha}{\beta} \lor 1)}  p^{((\frac{2-\alpha}{\beta} \lor 1) + \ep) \lambda} 2^{- C^{-1} j},
            \\
            \|I^{1,j,N}\|_{ W^{1,2p}_yL^p_\omega  \mathcal{C}^{1}_t \mathcal{C}^{1}_x } &\leq CK p^\lambda 2^{2j}  \|\nabla \Phi^N\|_{L^{2p}_\omega L^{2p}_y\mathcal{C}^0_t},
            
            \\
            \|I^{2,j,N}\|_{ W^{1,2p}_yL^p_\omega  \mathcal{C}^{1}_t \mathcal{C}^{1}_x } &\leq CK p^\lambda 2^{2j}  \|\nabla \Phi^N\|_{L^{2p}_\omega L^{2p}_y\mathcal{C}^0_t},
                           
    \end{align}
    where $\Phi^N$ is given by~\eqref{eq:truncated ODE flow}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.12475, 'Central limit theorem for the homozygosity of the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process'] Under the limiting procedure $\theta_0, \theta \to \infty$ such that $\frac{\theta_0}{\theta} \to c \in (0,\infty)$,
the homozygosity of the HPYP with $L$ groups satisfies
\bal
\tilde{H}_{m,L}(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta) &= \frac{\sqrt{\theta}}{f(\alpha, \beta, \theta; m, L, c)} \left( H_{m,L}(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta) - \frac{\sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{ \prod_{s=1}^{j-1} (\theta + s\beta) (1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)} }{ \beta^j \theta_0^{j-1}} }{L^m \theta^{m-1}} \right) \\
&\xrightarrow{D} N(0, \sigma_{c,m,L}^2)
\eal
for all $m \geq 2$, where the variance is given by
\bal
&\sigma_{c,m,L}^2 = \sigma_{X,m,L}^2 + \sigma_{T,m,L}^2 + \sigma_{1,m,L}^2 + \sum_{k=1}^L \left( \sum_{\bm{m} \in M_{m,L}} C_{\bm{m}} m_k \right)^2 \\
&- 2\sum_{k=1}^L \left( \frac{ \sum_{j=1}^m \left[\left(\sum_{\bm{m} \in M_{m,L}} \sum_{\bm{j} \in M_{j, L}} (m_k - \beta j_k) \prod_{\ell = 1}^L \Cs(m_\ell, j_\ell, \beta) \right) + \beta j A_j(\beta, m, L) \right] \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}} }{\sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}}} \right)^2
\eal
where
\bal
\sigma_{1,m,L}^2 &= \frac{\sum_{1 \leq i,j \leq m} \frac{A_i(\beta, m, L)A_j(\beta, m, L)\left[ (1 - \alpha)_{(i+j-1)} + (\alpha - ij)(1 - \alpha)_{(i-1)}(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)} \right]}{\beta^{i+j} c^{i+j-1}}}{\left( \sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}} \right)^2} \\
\sigma_{T,m,L}^2 &= \beta \frac{ \sum_{1 \leq i,j \leq m} \frac{ A_i(\beta, m, L)A_j(\beta, m, L) (1 - \alpha)_{(i-1)}(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)} }{\beta^{i+j} c^{i+j-2}} \cdot ij}{\left( \sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}} \right)^2} \\
\sigma_{X,m,L}^2 &= \frac{\sum_{j=1}^{2m} \tilde{A}_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}} -  \sum_{1 \leq i,j \leq m} A_i(\beta, m, L) A_j(\beta, m, L)  \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(i+j-1)}}{\beta^{i+j} c^{i+j-1}}  }{\left( \sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}} \right)^2}
\eal
and the coefficients $\{A_j(\beta, m, L)\}_{1 \leq j \leq m}$, $\{\tilde{A}_j(\beta, m, L)\}_{1 \leq j \leq 2m}$, and $\{C_{\bm{m}}\}_{\bm{m} \in M_{m,L}}$ are defined, respectively, as
\bal
A_j(\beta, m, L) &= \sum_{\bm{m} \in M_{m,L}} \sum_{\bm{j} \in M_{j,L}} \prod_{k=1}^L \Cs(m_k,j_k,\beta) \\
\tilde{A}_j(\beta, m, L) &= \sum_{\bm{m}_1 \in M_{m,L}} \sum_{\bm{m}_2 \in M_{m,L}} \sum_{\bm{j} \in M_{j,L}} \prod_{k=1}^L \Cs(m_{1k} + m_{2k}, j_k, \beta) \\
C_{\bm{m}} &= \frac{\sum_{j=1}^m \sum_{\bm{j} \in M_{j,L}} \prod_{\ell = 1}^L \Cs(m_\ell, j_\ell, \beta) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}}}{\sum_{j=1}^m A_j(\beta, m, L) \frac{(1 - \alpha)_{(j-1)}}{\beta^j c^{j-1}}}.
\eal (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 26 of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] Let $(A,\pi,M,\rho,\LB_A)$ be a Banach Lie algebroid which satisfies Assumption {\rm \textbf{(H)}}. For $k\geq 2$ fix a $C^k$-map $\g\colon [0,1]^2 \rightarrow M$ together with $J:=[-\eta,1+\eta]$ and an extension $\hat{\g}\colon [0,1] \times J \rightarrow M$ as in \Cref{timedepend}.
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item For $s \in [0,1]$ there is $\delta_s >0$ and an open neighborhood $\mathcal{W}_s\subseteq J \times M$ of the graph of $\hat{\g}_\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon\in I_s := [0,1] \cap [s-\delta_s,s+\delta_s]$.
 
 Then for every  $C^\ell$-map ${c}\colon [0,1]^2\to A$, $\ell \leq k$, with $\g=\pi\circ c$, there is $C^{\ell,\infty}$-map ${\mathfrak{u}^s} \colon I_s \times \mathcal{W}_s \rightarrow A$, such that $\pi \circ \mathfrak{u}^s(\varepsilon , t,y)=y$ and  $\mathfrak{u} (\varepsilon, t,\g_\varepsilon(t))=c_\varepsilon(t)$ for $(\varepsilon, t)\in I_s \times [0,1]$.
 
 Further, we can choose $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon$ constant on $\left(\left([-\eta, -\frac{\eta}{2}] \cup [1+\frac{\eta}{2},1+\eta]\right) \times M\right) \cap \mathcal{W}_s$. If $c_\varepsilon(0)=0$ (or $c_\varepsilon(1)=0$) for $\varepsilon\in I_s$, then also ${\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon}(0)=0$ (or $
  {\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon}(1)=0$).
 \item  If $M$ is smoothly paracompact, the section $\mathfrak{u}$ can be defined on $[0,1] \times J\times M$.
  \end{enumerate}

DRAFT; independent check by w395 pending. On nearest-neighbor Z^2 with finite strictly positive edge weights, let S_R={x: ||x||_infinity=R}. Let E_R mean some globally minimizing finite simple path between distinct vertices of S_R passes through 0. First-exit truncation makes E_R decreasing. An infinite branch of the finite sets of oriented simple witnesses truncated inside [-R,R]^2 shows that intersection_R E_R is exactly existence of a bigeodesic through 0. For a stationary random law, absence everywhere follows if P(E_R) tends to zero. Equation (4.25) of Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, arXiv:1511.03262, already uses this boundary-pair reduction; no novelty is asserted. This global event need not be measurable from inside edges alone at fixed R.
Nearest-neighbor undirected Z^2
Finite strictly positive weights
Global path minimization; simple paths
Stationarity only for the final everywhere-absence consequence

[Thm T_UB of arXiv:2605.15066, 'The critical activation density in graph bootstrap percolation'] Fix a graph $H$, with $\rho=\rho(H)>1$. 
If $\rho$ is rational, let $a/b$ be its expression as an irreducible fraction. 
If $\rho$ is irrational, let $b$ be arbitrarily large.  
Suppose that $np^\rho=A\log^{2+2/b} n$.
Then, for large enough $A$, with high probability, we have that 
$\langle\mathcal{G}_{n,p} \rangle_H=K_n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm T_UB of arXiv:2605.15066

[Corollary 66 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme such that every closed point of $X$ is contained in the closed fiber $X_{\F_p}$.
If $X$ is lim-perfectoid split, then \(X_{\F_p}\) is HT-split.

In particular, if $X$ is smooth and projective over $W(k)$ for a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$, then for every ample line bundle $L$ on $X$, we have
\[
H^i_{(p)}(X,\Omega^j_{X/W(k)} \otimes L^{-1})=0 \quad (i+j<\dim X).
\]

DRAFT author-proved partial result; independent referee review pending. No finite undirected graph with three distinct terminal vertices and independent edges with probabilities strictly between zero and one induces a terminal partition law supported exactly on the all-separate and all-connected partitions with positive mass on both. For m fair edges in a graph connecting the three terminals, total variation from any such all-or-none law is at least 2^(-m). This does not prove the C0017 square-lattice scaling limit.
Finite graph
Three distinct terminal vertices
Independent nondegenerate edge states
All-or-none target has all-connected mass p in (0,1)
title: DRAFT finite independent-bond obstruction

[Proposition prop:pn-tree-properties of arXiv:2607.24018, 'Jeu de taquin forests \\ and the inverse infinite RSK correspondence'] The trees of $\Phi(T)$ satisfy:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(T\arabic*)]
		\item 
		Each tree $\tau$ in $\Phi(T)$ has an asymptotic direction
		\[ z_{\tau} := \alpha_\textnormal{asym}(\tau)  \in [0,1]. \]
		
		\item 
		Distinct trees have distinct asymptotic directions.
		
		\item 
		The set of asymptotic directions of the trees coincides with
		the set of inverse-RSK values:
		\begin{equation}
			
			\{z_{\tau} : \tau \text{ a tree in } \Phi(T)\}
			= \{z_n : n \geq 1\}.
		\end{equation}

		\item 
		The set
		$\{z_{\tau} : \tau \text{ a tree in } \Phi(T)\}$ is dense in
		$[0,1]$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Asymptotic directions for all jeu de taquin forest trees

[Lemma of arXiv:2606.13264, 'Interference Queueing Networks: A Replica Mean-Field Approach in the Symmetric Setting'] Assume that \(\lambda<\mu^*\).
There exists \(r>1\) such that the function
\[
V(x)=\sum_{i=1}^N r^{x_i}, \qquad x\in\mathbb N^N,
\]
satisfies the Foster--Lyapunov drift condition
\[
\mathcal LV(x)\leq \mathcal L^{FB}V(x)\leq -cV(x)+b\mathbf 1_C(x),
\]
for some constants \(c,b>0\) and some finite set \(C\subset \mathbb N^N\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2606.13264, 'Interference Queueing Networks: A Replica Mean-Field Approac'

[Corollary ribbon tiling slope of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] Let $ X \subset \mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{Z}^d}$ be a strongly irreducible subshift for $ d \geq 2$. Let $G = G_1\times G_2\times\cdots\times G_r$, where each $G_i$ is a hyperbolic group with the CIC property and $ c: X \times \mathbb{Z}^d \rightarrow G$ is a cocycle with respect to the subgroup $W \leq \mathbb{Z}^d$ of finite index. Then there exists a homomorphism $ \theta: W \rightarrow G$ and a constant $ C$ such that for all $ x \in X\text{ and } w \in W$, there exist $h_1= h_1(x, w)$ and $h_2 = h_2(x, w)$ with $ \max(|h_1|, |h_2|) \leq C$ such that
   $$c(x, w ) = h_1 \theta(w) h_2.$$

[Proposition propexplog of arXiv:2411.06827, 'The Exponential Lie Series and a Chen--Strichartz Formula for L{\'e}vy Processes'] The degree $n$ component $y_n$ of the logarithm $\log^\ast(\exp(x))$ in $\widehat{GL(x)}$ is an element of the completion of the free pre-Lie algebra $PL(x)$ given by
$$
	y_n=\sum_{k=1}^n \sum_{j_1+\cdots + j_k=n} \frac{(-1)^{k-1}}{k}x^{j_1} * \cdots  * x^{j_k}.
$$
Therefore, we also have
$$
	\nu(y_n)=\bar\mu((\bar i^{(n)})^0)=V_{i^{(n)}}.
$$ 
In particular, we see that $V_{i^{(n)}}$ is a vector field. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Borel-Cantelli over the Hermitisation: identify which estimate is only in probability. Result: The proof of Theorem 6.2 has three inputs: (i) convergence of the singular-value distributions of n^{-1/alpha}X - z for each z, which is almost sure by the objective method (the local weak convergence to the PWIT holds a.s.); (ii) uniform integrability of log at infinity, a.s. from moment bounds; (iii) uniform integrability of log near zero, i.e. a lower bound on the small singular values, which is where only an in-probability bound s_n(n^{-1/alpha}X - z) >= n^{-c} with probability 1 - o(1) is available. To make (iii) almost sure one needs the failure probability summable in n, i.e. a bound like P(s_n <= n^{-c}) <= n^{-1-eps}. For heavy tails the row norms are not concentrated and the Rudelson-Vershynin small-ball argument gives only polynomial failure probabilities with exponent that is not obviously above 1. If the failure probability were shown to be O(n^{-1-eps}) (for instance via an Esseen-type anti-concentration in the alpha-stable domain, which gives exponent depending on alpha), Borel-Cantelli finishes the a.s. statement. So the problem reduces to a quantitative smallest-singular-value bound for heavy-tailed matrices with summable failure probability; the bound is plausible but I did not prove it. Obstruction: Need P(s_n(n^{-1/alpha}X - z) <= n^{-c}) summable in n for heavy-tailed entries.

body: In mathematics, particularly in differential topology, there are two Whitney embedding theorems, named after Hassler Whitney:The strong Whitney embedding theorem states that any smooth real m-dimensional manifold can be smoothly embedded in the real 2m-space, ⁠⁠ if m > 0. This is the best linear bound on the smallest-dimensional Euclidean space that all m-dimensional manifolds embed in, as the real projective spaces of dimension m cannot be embedded into real (2m − 1)-space if m is a power of two. The weak Whitney embedding theorem states that any continuous function from an n-dimensional manifold to an m-dimensional manifold may be approximated by a smooth embedding provided m > 2n. Whitney similarly proved that such a map could be approximated by an immersion provided m > 2n − 1. This last result is sometimes called the Whitney immersion theorem.
title: Whitney embedding theorem

body: [Theorem 1.3 of arXiv:2603.01435, 'Color symmetry in the Potts spin glass at high temperature'] For any $\kappa\geq 3$ and $\beta\in[0,\beta_{\kappa})$, we have $\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}F^{\sf bal}_{N,\beta}=\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}F_{N,\beta}=\log\kappa+\frac{\beta^{2}(\kappa-1)}{2\kappa^{2}}.$ In particular, color symmetry is preserved in this high temperature regime.
