[Theorem 13 (Pointwise macroscopic-loop criterion) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Let \(G_n\) be a random simple graph on \([n]\). Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and
\(\theta\in\mathbb N\) with \(\theta>1\). Assume that \((G_n)_n\) satisfies
Assumption~\ref{ass:sparse-random-graph}, with limiting edge density \(\alpha\), and that $\alpha>c_{\theta,u}$.
Then for every \(\delta>0\) there exist \(\eta>0\) and \(c>0\) such that for every
\[
t\ge \frac{\theta\log\theta}{(\theta-1)(\alpha-c_{\theta,u})}+\delta,
\]
one has
\[
\Pbb\!\left(
\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c
\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pointwise macroscopic-loop criterion

PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Let T_a(x1,...,xr)=sum_j a_j product_k xk_j, with every xk in the l_p unit ball. Its multilinear norm is ||a||_infinity for p<=r and ||a||_q for p>r, q=p/(p-r), with q=1 at p=infinity. For the homogeneous polynomial using one repeated vector, the same identities hold for p<=r and for odd r. For even r and p>r the polynomial norm is max(||a_+||_q,||a_-||_q), so it is within factor 2^(1/q) of the multilinear norm. Explicit Holder optimizers prove all identities; the mixed-sign example r=2,p=infinity,a=(1,-1) has norms two and one.
Diagonal real order-r tensors, r>=2
p in [2,infinity]
Independent standard coefficient Gaussians; coordinate Gaussians may be correlated
Norms are explicitly distinguished

Label: proof for diagonal tensors in both the multilinear and homogeneous polynomial conventions, awaiting w346. The cached source defines I_p using one repeated vector; the last paragraph below covers that convention. No assertion about all symmetric tensors is made.

Let r>=2 be an integer and T_a(x1,...,xr)=sum_(j=1)^d a_j product_(k=1)^r xk_j. Define ||T||_(I_p)=sup {|T(x1,...,xr)|: ||xk||_p<=1 for every k}, with p in [2,infinity]. This is a multilinear norm; it must not be confused with the same-vector polynomial norm for even degree and mixed signs.

If p<=r, ||T_a||_(I_p)=||a||_infinity: Holder with r equal exponents bounds the sum of products by product ||xk||_r<=1, and a coordinate vector attains the largest coefficient. If p>r, let q=p/(p-r) (q=1 at p=infinity). Generalized Holder gives ||T_a||_(I_p)=||a||_q. For finite p equality is attained by choosing all coordinate magnitudes proportional to |a_j|^(1/(p-r)) and putting each coefficient's sign in the first vector. For p=infinity choose every magnitude one and signs in the first vector.

For diagonal tensors T_i=T_(a_i) and independent standard Gaussians g_i, put Z_j=sum_i g_i a_(i,j) and sigma_j^2=sum_i a_(i,j)^2. The coordinate Gaussians can be correlated; independence across j is not needed.

If p<=r, the Gaussian exponential-moment union bound gives

E||sum_i g_i T_i||_(I_p) <= sqrt(2 log(2d)) [sum_i ||T_i||_(I_p)^2]^(1/2).

If p>r and q>=2, Jensen and Gaussian moments give E||Z||_q <= c_q ||sigma||_q, where c_q=(E|g|^q)^(1/q). Minkowski in l_(q/2) gives ||sigma||_q <= [sum_i ||a_i||_q^2]^(1/2).

If p>r and 1<=q<2, use ||Z||_q<=d^(1/q-1/2)||Z||_2, E||Z||_2 <= [sum_i ||a_i||_2^2]^(1/2), and ||a_i||_2<=||a_i||_q. The result is

E||sum_i g_i T_i||_(I_p) <= d^(1/2-r/p) [sum_i ||T_i||_(I_p)^2]^(1/2),

with 1/p=0 at infinity. At q=2 the dimension factor is one. The exponent max(1/2-r/p,0) is no larger than the target 1/2-1/p, so this proves the desired dimension bound throughout the diagonal multilinear family, extending the old diagonal p<=r calculation. It leaves off-diagonal tensors unresolved.

The homogeneous polynomial convention can also be covered explicitly. Define P_p(a)=sup_(||x||_p<=1) |sum_j a_j x_j^r|. For p<=r it is again ||a||_infinity. For p>r, with q as above, odd r permits each sign to be selected in x, so P_p(a)=||a||_q. For even r, P_p(a)=max(||a_+||_q,||a_-||_q), because x_j^r is nonnegative and each sign-support optimization is Holder duality. Hence ||a||_q<=2^(1/q) P_p(a), while P_p(Z)<=||Z||_q. Applying the multilinear Gaussian estimates yields the same type-2 bounds for diagonal homogeneous forms, with an additional factor at most two for even r and p>r. This avoids importing an incorrect mixed-sign polynomial norm identity. For example r=2,p=infinity,a=(1,-1) has multilinear norm two and polynomial norm one.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:531a5ddd276062b8b8612e5e597231bc49324742e8374f26aff0274068818a3d","revision_digest":"sha256:31f11c32e33972a0c67c36c26fe8e97f3ddf7be6388d2f088c5184987719fea8","source_id":"owner-own-work:w340:diagonal-tensor-multilinear-and-polynomial-norm-identities","source_revision":"2026-10-10-source-convention-confirmed-draft-awaiting-w346","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2609.01681, 'Large induced subgraphs with $k$ vertices of maximum degree'] Let \(G\) be a graph on \(n\) vertices and let \(t\) be an integer with
\(0<t<n\). Choose an \((n-t)\)-vertex subset \(S\subseteq V(G)\) that
minimizes \(e(G[S])\), and set \(D=V(G)\setminus S\). For every integer
\(k\ge2\) there exists a constant \(c_3=c_3(k)\) such that the following
holds: if for some integer \(x\) the set
\(\{v\in D : d_S(v)=x\}\)
contains an independent set $D'$ of order at least \(c_3\), then
\(s_k(G)\le |D|+2k(k-1)\).

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Supermodular ordering of speeded-up Markov chains without stochastic monotonicity (October 2026). For a stationary continuous-time Markov chain with real values, let the chain run at speed c. Leskela (Queueing Systems 100 (2022), 213-215, Problem 3) asked whether some stationary ergodic chain that is not stochastically monotone becomes smaller in the supermodular order of processes as it is speeded up. The paper shows that such chains exist on three states: a chain that leaves its smallest value for either of the other two values at any positive rates and returns from both at a common rate has this property and is not stochastically monotone. If the largest value returns faster than the middle one, the property fails already for pairs of sampling times. For reversible three-state chains with two distinct nonzero eigenvalues, the pairs are ordered exactly when the slow left eigenvector does not have the same strict sign at the two extreme states. Exact certificate identities, symbolic spectral formulas, linear programs over supermodular functions and a Lean 4 file accompany the paper. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/supermodular-speed-ordering (commit e1afd4de9728). Not refereed.
title: A three-state Markov chain that is not stochastically monotone yet becomes smaller in the supermodular order when speeded up, answering Leskela's Problem 3 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/supermodular-speed-ordering)

[Corollary of arXiv:2507.08757, 'Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner '] Call $B^{{\raisebox{1.3pt}{\hspace{0.6pt}\scaleobj{0.55}{\bullet}\hspace{0.75pt}}}} = (B^{{\raisebox{1.3pt}{\hspace{0.6pt}\scaleobj{0.55}{\bullet}\hspace{0.75pt}}}}(x,y) : x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^2)$ and let $z\in\mathbb{Z}^2\backslash\{0\}$. Then $B^{{\raisebox{1.3pt}{\hspace{0.6pt}\scaleobj{0.55}{\bullet}\hspace{0.75pt}}}}$ is strongly mixing under $T_z$. Explicitly, this means that for all events $A \in \mathcal{F}$ and Borel $C$,
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(A, B^{{\raisebox{1.3pt}{\hspace{0.6pt}\scaleobj{0.55}{\bullet}\hspace{0.75pt}}}}\circ T_z^{-n}\in C ) = \mathbb{P}(A)\hspace{0.9pt}\mathbb{P}(B^{{\raisebox{1.3pt}{\hspace{0.6pt}\scaleobj{0.55}{\bullet}\hspace{0.75pt}}}}\in C). \qedhere
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 13 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] There exists $\epsilon' > 0$ such that 
    \[S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'] 
    \subseteq S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;
    	\frac\epsilon5, \frac\epsilon3
    	\bigg)\]
for all $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$.

\begin{proof}
    We first prove the claim for a fixed $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, where $\epsilon'$ for now is permitted to depend on $(\lambda,\mu)$.
Suppose for contradiction that for all $\epsilon'>0$ we have
    \[ \emptyset\ne
    S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'] \cap 
	S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;\frac\epsilon5, \frac\epsilon3\bigg)^c 
	\subseteq
    S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'] \cap 
\overline{S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;\frac\epsilon5, \frac\epsilon{3}\bigg)^c}\,,
    \]
    where $\overline{S}$ denotes the closure of $S$ relative to the topology of $\cD_\mu$. This forms a nested family of nonempty compact sets indexed by $\epsilon' > 0$, so the intersection
    \[
        \bigcap_{\epsilon'>0} \bigg\{
        S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'] \cap \overline{S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;
        	\frac\epsilon5, \frac\epsilon{3}\bigg)^c}\bigg\}
        = S_\star(\lambda,\mu) \cap
        	\overline{S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;
			\frac\epsilon5, \frac\epsilon{3}\bigg)^c}
    \]
is also nonempty. That is, we can find $\YY\in S_\star(\lambda,\mu)$ with
	\[
	\Surplus(\YY;\lambda,\mu)
	+ \frac\epsilon5 \alpha^2\iota^3 (\|\vBBb\|_2)^2
	\ge \frac{\epsilon}{3}\,.
	\]
This contradicts Lemma~\ref{l:S.star.in.S.star.eps}, which implies 
	\[
	\Surplus(\YY;\lambda,\mu)
	+ \frac\epsilon5 \alpha^2\iota^3 (\|\vBBb\|_2)^2
	\le \frac{\epsilon}{5}\,.
	\]
This proves that for any fixed $(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda$, the claim holds for some $\epsilon'>0$ that may depend on $(\lambda,\mu)$. 
Next, for any $(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda$, let 
\[\epsilon'(\lambda,\mu)
\equiv \max\bigg\{
\epsilon':
S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'] \subseteq 
S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;\frac\epsilon5,\frac\epsilon3\bigg)\bigg\}\,,\] 
where the maximum exists because both sets are closed. We will prove below that $\epsilon'(\lambda,\mu)$ is a continuous function of $(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda$, and we have just shown that it is strictly positive on $\Lambda$. It follows that
\[
        \inf\bigg\{\epsilon'(\lambda,\mu) : (\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda\bigg\} > 0\,,
    \]
and we may take $\epsilon'$ equal to this infimum to conclude.
 
We now justify the above claim that $\epsilon'(\lambda,\mu)$ is a  continuous function of $(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda$. (Note for our purposes it suffices to show that $\epsilon'(\lambda,\mu)$ is lower semicontinuous in $(\lambda,\mu)$, but it is not much more difficult to verify that it is in fact continuous.) To this end, 
fix $(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda$ and abbreviate $\epsilon'=\epsilon'(\lambda,\mu)$, so that we have
	\[S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon']
	\subseteq
	S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;\frac\epsilon5,\frac\epsilon3\bigg)\,.
	\]
To this end, note that the function
    \beq
        f(\YY;\lambda,\mu) 
        \equiv \Surplus(\YY;\lambda,\mu) 
        	+ \frac{\epsilon}{5} \alpha^2 \iota^3 (\|\vBBb\|_2)^2\,,
    \eeq
is \emph{strictly} convex on $\cD_\mu$, as the $(\|\BBb\|_2)^2$ term ensures strict convexity in $\vBBb$. As a result, for any sufficiently small $\eta'>0$, there exists $\delta'>0$ such that
	\[S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'-\delta']
	\subseteq
	S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;\frac\epsilon5,
		\frac\epsilon3-\eta'\bigg)\,.
	\]
Let $(\lambda',\mu')\in B_\delta(\lambda,\mu)$. By Corollary~\ref{c:S.star.cts.nbd.dH}, we have
	\[
	d_H\bigg(
	S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'-\delta'],
	S_\star(\lambda',\mu')[\epsilon'-\delta']
	\bigg)
	\le o_\delta(1)\,.
	\]
Since the function $f$ is uniformly continuous on the compact domain
$[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}\times \Lambda$,
we conclude

body:
[Definition def:continuous_process_min_max_construction of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] (Continuous
  process) Let $\ell>0$,  $x_0 \in [0, \ell]$ and
  $\sigma^1_0, \sigma^2_0 \in \{-1, 1\}$ (resp.
  $\sigma^1_0, \sigma^2_0 \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$) be given. Consider two
  independent Markov jump processes $\sigma^1$ and $\sigma^2$ with the
  transition rates of figure
  (fig:single_speed_transition_rates_slowman_2016 of the paper)
  (resp. (fig:single_speed_transition_rates_slowman_2017 of the paper)) and
  respective initial states $\sigma^1_0$ and $\sigma^2_0$.

  Using the jump times $(T_i)_{i \ge 0}$ of the couple
  $(\sigma^1, \sigma^2)$, recursively define $x(t)$ by $x(0) = x_0$
  and
\begin{equation*}
x(t) = \max \left[0,  \min \left[\ell, x(T_i) + (\sigma^2(T_i) - \sigma^1(T_i)) (t - T_i) \right] \right] \text{ for } t \in [T_i, T_{i+1}[.
\end{equation*}
The process $X(t) = (x(t), (\sigma^1(t), \sigma^2(t)))$ is referred to as {continuous process}.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact minimum stationary cover time for reversible chains structural calculation Result: The assertion holds for two states. Write P(0,1)=a and P(1,0)=b,0<a,b<=1. Stationarity gives pi=(b,a)/(a+b), and E_pi C=b/[a(a+b)]+a/[b(a+b)]=(a^2+b^2)/[ab(a+b)]>=1, since a^2+b^2>=2ab and a+b<=2. Equality requires a=b=1. Check: The initial state is already visited at time0, so the two-state cover time is exactly the first hit of the other state. This fixes the common off-by-one and laziness errors. A deterministic directed cycle would violate the general bound for large n but is nonreversible and is not a counterexample. Obstruction: A many-state coupon-collector argument needs to control the distribution of the next unvisited target; its selection is biased by the history. Individual stationary hitting-time inequalities cannot simply be summed in random discovery order.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0245-exact-minimum-stationary-cover-time-for-reversible-chains

[Lemma lem:full-deposit-calculus of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Put
\[
 \mathsf C_i=\mathsf P_i-N^{-1}I_W,
 \qquad \mathsf P_i=a_ia_i^*.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathsf C_i=\mathsf C_i^*,\quad
 \sum_i\mathsf C_i=0,\quad
 \rho(R_i(\theta))^*\mathsf C_i\rho(R_i(\theta))=\mathsf C_i,
 \quad \|\mathsf C_i\|_\mathrm{op}\le1,
\tag{3.3.1w$_1$}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_i\mathsf C_i^2=(1-N^{-1})I_W.
\tag{3.3.1w$_2$}
\]
Consequently every assertion of
(lem:singleton-renewal of the paper),
(lem:singleton-order-sum of the paper), (lem:typed-pass of the paper), and
(lem:haar-passive-zero of the paper) remains valid with $W_i^\circ$ replaced by
$\mathsf C_i$ and with the better seed parameter
\[
 \eta_C=\left\|\frac1N\sum_i\mathsf C_i^2\right\|
 =\frac{N-1}{N^2}\le\frac1N.
\tag{3.3.1w$_3$}
\]

For $q\ge1$ there are scalars $\alpha_q,\beta_q$ such that
\[
 \mathsf C_i^q=\alpha_q\mathsf C_i+\beta_qI,\qquad
 |\alpha_q|\le2,\quad \beta_1=0,\quad
 |\beta_q|\le\frac3N\quad(q\ge2).
\tag{3.3.1w$_4$}
\]
More generally, for $2\le q\le L\log n$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
\[
 \left\|\frac1N\sum_i\mathsf C_i^{\otimes q}\right\|_\mathrm{op}
 \le\frac2N.
\tag{3.3.1w$_5$}
\]
After latest-pivot exposure, the same bound, with $A_L^q/N$ on the
right, survives powers on individual rails and fixed flips, dualities,
and normalized Brauer maps.  Thus a
fused nonroot full-deposit block is either one passive singleton, an
explicit scalar child of size $A_L^q/N$, or a hard intact block carrying
one $A_L^q/N$ resource.  If an intact rank-one pinch remains after
latest-pivot exposure and Ward evacuation, so that its exterior map
$T\in\operatorname{End}(W)$ is fixed with respect to the fresh plane, then
\[
 \left\|\frac1N\sum_i\mathsf P_iT\mathsf P_i\right\|_\mathrm{op}
 \le\frac1N\|T\|_\mathrm{op}.
\tag{3.3.1w$_6$}
\]

[Lemme allomqutre of arXiv:2603.21634, 'Individual-based stochastic model with unbounded growth, birth and death rates: a tightnes'] Under the allometric setting, under Assumptions~(hyp:gainenergy of the paper) and (hyp:probamortel of the paper), suppose that the weight function $\omega$ has an \hyperlink{alloform}{allometric form} with $0 \leq \kappa_{1} \leq \kappa_{2}$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[-] If $ \delta < -1$, then Assumption~(hyp:poidsomega of the paper) is equivalent to 
$$\kappa_{1}=\kappa_{2}= -\delta, \quad \alpha \in [0,1]\quad \mathrm{and} \quad \beta \leq 2+ \delta;$$
\item[-] If $-1 \leq \delta \leq 0 $, then Assumption~(hyp:poidsomega of the paper) is equivalent to 
$$ - \delta \leq \kappa_{1} \leq \kappa_{2} \leq \dfrac{1-\delta}{2} \leq 1, \quad \alpha \in [0,1], \quad \mathrm{and} \quad \beta \leq 1.$$
\item[-] If $\delta > 0 $, then Assumption~(hyp:poidsomega of the paper) cannot be verified.
\end{itemize}
These constraints on the allometic coefficients are illustrated on Figure~(fig:contraitnesallomdeux of the paper) and Figure~(fig:contraitnesallomtrois of the paper).

[Proposition eq:Gaussian-jet-law of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[proposition]{prop:Gaussian-jet}
Let the disorder be standard Gaussian.  For every deterministic frame \(O\),
\begin{equation}
 (h_G(O),g_G(O),A_G(O))\stackrel d=
 \left(
 \frac{Z_0}{\sqrt N},
 \sqrt p\,(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n),
 \gamma_{N,p}M_n-\frac{pZ_0}{\sqrt N}I_n
 \right),
 \qquad
 \gamma_{N,p}=\sqrt{\frac{2p(p-1)n}{N}}.
\end{equation}
Here \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) are independent standard Gaussians and \(M_n\) is an independent GOE matrix.

body:
[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2604.07478, 'Mixing Times and Cutoff for the Rook's Walk'] The Krawtchouk polynomial $K_{m,d,n} = K_m$ is an eigenfunction with eigenvalue $\lambda_m = 1 - \frac{nm}{d(n-1)}$ of the RWBD chain's transition matrix $P$.
   \begin{proof}
      By Lemma \ref{krav_orth}, the Krawtchouk polynomials are orthogonal wrt the inner product,
      \[\langle A,B\rangle = \sum_{i=0}^n {d \choose i}(n-1)^i A(i) B(i)=\langle A,B \rangle_\pi\]
      The transition probabilities of the RWBD chain are affine so by Theorem \ref{eig-orth}, the Krawtchouk polynomials are eigenfunctions as required. Therefore, for each $K_m$ there exists $\lambda_m$ such that,
      \[PK_m = \lambda_m K_m\]
      Specializing to the $0^\text{th}$ coordinate we have,
      \[(PK_m)(0) = \lambda_mK_m(0)\]
      Now, consider $(PK_m)(0)$
      \begin{align*}
      (PK_m)(0) &= \sum_{y\in \Omega} P(0,y)K_m(y)\\
      &= P(0,0)K_m(0)+P(0,1)K_m(1)\\& = K_m(1)
      \end{align*}
      Therefore,
      \[\lambda_m = \frac{K_m(1)}{K_m(0)}\]
      Evaluating $K_m(0)$ and $K_m(1)$,
      \begin{align*}
            K_m(0) &= \sum_{j=0}^{m}{(-1)}^j{0 \choose j}{d-0 \choose m-j}{(n-1)}^{m-j}\\
            &= {d \choose m}{(n-1)}^{m}\\
            K_m(1) &= \sum_{j=0}^{m}{(-1)}^j{1 \choose j}{d-1 \choose m-j}{(n-1)}^{m-j}\\
            &= {d-1 \choose m}(n-1)^m - {d-1 \choose m-1} {(n-1)}^{m-1}
      \end{align*}
      Recall the standard binomial coefficient identities,
      \[\frac{d}{d-m}{d \choose m}={d-1 \choose m} \quad \text{and}\quad \frac{m}{d}{d\choose m} = {d-1 \choose m-1} \]
      Therefore,
      \begin{align*}
         \lambda_m &= \frac{\frac{d}{d-m}{d \choose m}(n-1)^m - \frac{m}{d}{d \choose m} (n-1)^{m-1}}{{d \choose m}(n-1)^{m}}\\
         &= \frac{d}{d-m} - \frac{m}{d(n-1)} \\
         &= 1 - \frac{mn}{d(n-1)}
      \end{align*}
   \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 16 of arXiv:2604.07478

[Lemma 14 (Curvature in a controlled cone corridor) of arXiv:2609.02788, '\textbf{Quantized Einstein Metrics on \(S^7\) with \(SU(3)\)-Symmetry}'] Let
\[
 g=dt^2+\sum_{i=1}^3 f_i(t)^2Q|_{\mathfrak m_i}
\]
be an $SU(3)$-invariant diagonal metric satisfying $\Ric(g)=6g$ on an
interval $I\subset(0,T]$.  Suppose that, for constants $c_0,C_0>0$,
\begin{equation}
 c_0t\le f_i(t)\le C_0t,
 \qquad |tL_i(t)|\le C_0,
 \qquad i=1,2,3.
\end{equation}
Then
\[
 |\Rm(g)|(t)\le C t^{-2}\qquad(t\in I),
\]
where $C$ depends only on $c_0,C_0,T$ and the fixed homogeneous
normalization $Q$.

Independent derivation pending w440 review. For every fixed integer n>=1, the supremum of the critical probability of reaching graph distance n, over roots of infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graphs of maximum degree at most 3 with p_c<1, is 1. Indeed, for the uniformly L-subdivided 3-regular tree with L>=n, that probability is 1-(1-2^(-n/L))^3 and tends to 1 as L grows. No single f(n) tending to zero can bound the entire class. A degree-only C/n bound fails already at n=L since the probability is 7/8. This does not exclude graph-dependent bounds and does not address the smaller vertex-transitive class. The family has p_c tending to 1, growing orbit count, and volume-growth rate tending to 1.

body: exact_full_dual(points): compute $r=\operatorname{qrank}(\text{points})$, greedily keep $r$ coordinates on which the projection still has rank $r$, take $r$ independent projected points as a basis, and for each tail in $\{\pm1\}^{r-1}$ set values $=(1,\text{tail})$, solve $Bh=\text{values}$ exactly over $\mathbb Q$, and accept the form iff $|\langle x,h\rangle|=1$ for EVERY projected point $x$. Returns the accepted value-vectors as the projective full dual in evaluation coordinates. Notes: Normalization to first evaluation $=1$ is exactly the projective quotient by $\pm1$; enumerating tails is complete because a full-dual form is determined by its values on a basis of the fibre. This makes the full dual computable exactly, which is the pivot on which the whole finite programme rests.

Let Lambda be a compact hyperbolic set for a diffeomorphism f. Then f restricted to Lambda is EXPANSIVE: there is a constant c > 0 (an expansive constant) such that if x and y are in Lambda and d(f^n(x), f^n(y)) <= c for EVERY integer n, then x = y. Equivalently two distinct orbits in a hyperbolic set must separate to distance more than c at some time, forwards or backwards. Consequently the shadowing orbit of a pseudo-orbit is unique, and by Walters' theorem any partition of a generating diameter below the expansive constant is a generator for entropy purposes.
Both directions of time are used - expansiveness here is two-sided, for an invertible f on a hyperbolic set.
For non-invertible maps the corresponding notion is positive expansiveness, which is a genuinely different and more restrictive condition.

For fixed t>0, N=floor(nt), h_(n,k)=D P_((N-k)/n)f, both exact and hybrid ReLU chains satisfy sum_(k=1)^(N-1) E[theta_k h_(n,k)(U_k);alive]=(D_t/a)log(n)+O_(theta0,t)(1). Assumptions: Fixed theta0 in (0,pi], iid Gaussian zero-bias ReLU layers; U=1/(n theta) only on alive states; hybrid kernel from C039. Limiting diffusion starts at0. The full modified-operator occupation identity is stated for the hybrid chain with finite reciprocal moments. The angle transition uses n independent row pairs x=max(g,0), y=max(cos(theta)g+sin(theta)h,0), g,h iid standard Gaussians, independent across layers, and the angle between the resulting vectors. Kill at zero norm or zero angle. For the hybrid kernel use a fixed small concentration box for (mean(x^2+y^2),mean((x-y)^2)/theta^2,mean(x^2-y^2)/theta) at small theta, and ordinary Gram averages at larger theta, each centered at its expectation; self-loop on failure. Limit: Unaudited proof. Occupation of the correction is identified, but it has not yet been equated to terminal weak error by a globally controlled telescoping argument. P_s g(u)=E[g(V_s^u)] for dV=(2V+a)ds+sqrt(2)VdW,V0=u,a=1/(3pi). The semigroup sensitivity D_t=D P_t f(0)=E[exp(t+sqrt(2)W_t-V_t^0)], f(u)=1-exp(-u).

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:1fb5aaa46c694c612ced14804ff7512208355a610189cd2c4d16f2d008a8d6f7","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/1f/1fb5aaa46c694c612ced14804ff7512208355a610189cd2c4d16f2d008a8d6f7.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:af0b975c427f642f8aec1205def6bc54a1a3515149422f6182a41c5f8c3dc067","bundle_entry_key":"relu-weighted-log-occupation","bundle_id":"population.t244-logarithmic-bounded-weak-rate-015","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_015.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-relu-weighted-log-occupation","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C040-C041: sharp mesoscopic angle and weighted logarithmic occupation

Version 1, 20 October 2026. Target 1, kind moved. Proofs (unaudited).
Use C039's global hybrid normalized/ordinary Gram regularization. Its
reciprocal U=1/(n theta) is finite; no raw exact-chain reciprocal mean is
used. Fix theta0 in (0,pi] and T<infinity. Constants may depend on theta0,T.
Let a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2).

## C040: quantitative mesoscopic angular law

For either the hybrid chain or the exact chain killed at degeneracy,

    E|k theta_k-1/a|
          <= C_(theta0,T)[k^(-1/2)+sqrt(k/n)],
                         1<=k<=floor(Tn), n sufficiently large. (1)

The exact angle is defined to be zero after killing. Consequently
k_n theta_(k_n) -> 3pi in L1 whenever k_n -> infinity and k_n/n -> 0.
The constants are not uniform as theta0 decreases to zero.

### Global reciprocal estimates for the hybrid chain

For all theta in (0,pi], with u=1/(n theta), its one-step multiplier
R=U_next/u=theta/theta_next satisfies

    E[R^q] <= 1+C_q(theta+1/n), q=1,2,
    E[(R-1)^2] <= C(theta^2+1/n),                  (2)
    |E(U_next-u)-(a+2u)/n|
                   <= C[theta/n+1/n^2+u/n^(3/2)]. (3)

To check (2), the multiplier and its coordinate derivatives are uniformly
bounded on each hybrid good box, and equal one off it. Sample-average
Taylor expansion gives E R^q=(theta/F(theta))^q+O_q(1/n), while the
Lipschitz estimate gives E|R-theta/F(theta)|^2<=C/n. The deterministic
ratio theta/F(theta)=1+O(theta) uniformly on (0,pi], proving (2).

For small theta the same centered Taylor expansion through order two
has third-absolute-moment remainder O(n^(-3/2)), uniformly in theta.
The covariance-Hessian contraction for R at theta=0 is2 (C032), its
variation is O(theta), and its deterministic term is
theta/F(theta)=1+a theta+O(theta^2). Hence

    E R=1+a theta+2/n
                    +O(theta^2+theta/n+n^(-3/2)).

Multiplication by u and u*theta=1/n proves (3) on that range. On the
remaining compact angle interval, u<=C/n; bounded multipliers imply
an O(1/n) error, which is bounded by C theta/n since theta is bounded
below there. Thus (3) holds globally. None of these estimates takes
the expectation of an unregularized reciprocal.

Let m_q(j)=E U_j^q. From (2),

    m_1(j+1)<=(1+C/n)m_1(j)+C/n,
    m_2(j+1)<=(1+C/n)m_2(j)+(C/n)m_1(j).

Since U0=1/(n theta0), summing these two recurrences in that order gives

    E U_j<=C_(theta0,T)(j+1)/n,
    E U_j^2<=C_(theta0,T)(j+1)^2/n^2,
                                          0<=j<=Tn.            (4)

The second estimate includes the initial square and the sum of the first
estimate divided by n. Equation (2) also gives

    E[(U_(j+1)-U_j)^2 | U_j,theta_j]
                                      <=C(U_j^2/n+1/n^2).      (5)

### Martingale tracking and inversion

Decompose U_k-U0 into its conditional mean increments and the square-
integrable martingale M_k. Orthogonality of martingale increments and
(4)-(5) imply

    ||M_k||_2 <= C[sqrt(k^3/n^3)+sqrt(k)/n].                    (6)

Using (3), (4), and the global p=2 angle bound from C039, Minkowski gives

    ||U_k-U0-a k/n-M_k||_2
       <= (2/n)sum_(j<k)||U_j||_2
          +C/n sum_(j<k)||theta_j||_2+Ck/n^2
          +C/n^(3/2)sum_(j<k)||U_j||_2
       <= C[k(k+1)/n^2+log(k+1)/n+k/n^2
                                      +k(k+1)/n^(5/2)].        (7)

Thus with Z_k=nU_k/k,

    ||Z_k-a||_2<=C[k^(-1/2)+sqrt(k/n)], 1<=k<=Tn.              (8)

Here log(k+1)/k<=C/sqrt(k), k/n<=sqrt(T)*sqrt(k/n), and the initial
nU0/k term is O_(theta0)(1/k). These justify the simplification in (8).

Now Y_k=k theta_k=1/Z_k. C039 with p=2 gives a uniform bound E Y_k^2<=C_T.
On {Z_k>=a/2}, |Y_k-1/a|<=2|Z_k-a|/a^2. On the complementary event,
Chebyshev bounds its probability by4||Z_k-a||_2^2/a^2. Cauchy-Schwarz
and the uniform second moment of Y_k bound its contribution to the L1
error by C||Z_k-a||_2 (if this norm is large, the same inequality follows
by increasing C). This proves (1) for the hybrid chain.

Couple the exact chain with it through time k as in C039. The discrepancy
probability is Ck exp(-cn). Both angles lie in [0,pi], so the additional
L1 error in k theta_k is at most Ck^2 exp(-cn). For k<=Tn this is absorbed
by C_(T)/sqrt(k). This proves (1) for the exact chain.

## C041: the network's weighted singular occupation coefficient

Let P_s be the semigroup of dV=(2V+a)ds+sqrt(2)V dW, V0=0, and
f(u)=1-exp(-u). Fix t>0, N=floor(nt), t_n=N/n, and

    h_(n,k)(u)=D P_(t_n-k/n)f(u), 1<=k<N,
    D_t=D P_t f(0)=E[exp(t+sqrt(2)W_t-V_t)].

For both the hybrid chain and the exact chain with the alive indicator,

    sum_(k=1)^(N-1) E[theta_k h_(n,k)(U_k);alive]
                            =(D_t/a) log(n)+O_(theta0,t)(1).   (9)

For the hybrid chain, with C=B-A^2/2 from C033,

    (1/n^2)sum_(k=1)^(N-1) E[(C P_(t_n-k/n)f)(U_k)]
                    =D_t log(n)/(2pi n)+O_(theta0,t)(1/n).     (10)

This is an occupation calculation on actual chain states, not yet a
telescoped weak-error formula for the terminal observable.

Proof. The affine solution V_v^u=V_v^0+uJ_v, J_v=exp(v+sqrt(2)W_v),
gives bounded first and second initial-value derivatives of P_v f,
uniformly for 0<=v<=t and u>=0. The time derivative of D P_v f is bounded
as in C034: (Af)' is bounded and E J_v is finite. Therefore

    |h_(n,k)(u)-D_(t_n)|<=C_t(k/n+u).                         (11)

On alive states theta_k U_k=1/n. C039 gives E theta_k<=C/(k+1), so

    E[theta_k |h_(n,k)(U_k)-D_(t_n)|;alive]<=C_t/n.

Its sum is O_t(1). From (1),

    |E theta_k-1/(ak)|<=C[k^(-3/2)+1/sqrt(nk)],

whose sum from1 toN-1 is bounded by C_(theta0,t). Consequently
sum E theta_k=(1/a)log(n)+O_(theta0,t)(1). Combining these facts and
|D_(t_n)-D_t|<=C_t/n proves (9). The killed exact chain has the same
estimates and the identity theta*U=1/n only on alive states, as required.

The singular drift term in C is b/u. In (10) its contribution is b/n
times (9), giving (b/a)D_t log(n)/n. The remaining terms are

    (8u+a/5) D P_v f+(4u^2-3au/5) D^2 P_v f.

Their expected absolute values are uniformly bounded using the bounded
derivatives and (4) through time t_n. Their n^-2 sum is therefore O(1/n).
Finally b/a=1/(2pi), proving (10).

The remaining global weak-rate step is a semigroup telescoping identity
whose accumulated local errors are O(1/n) for this unbounded reciprocal
state space and whose initial-layer contribution is also O(1/n).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:48d5412d05f2566420246d906fe5e2cb5ea63da0a7aee9e2d7460ec5d88ae3f3","revision_digest":"sha256:32b753a4fdf7fd9e737ebbe90b58f470577d6a40e9cfebd36fc13ae67d0ee2b2","source_id":"owner-own-work:T244-w691-C041:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

	(equation eq:K_t_x_y_fixed_slice of the paper) of the $q$-Racah
	nonintersecting path ensemble inside the hexagon with
	sides $a,b,c,a,b,c$ (where $T=b+c$, $S=c$, $N=a$) is the
	kernel of the orthogonal spectral projection onto the
	subspace corresponding to the spectral interval
	\begin{equation}
		
		\left[ -q^{-N+1}(1-q^{N-1})(q^{-T-N}-1),0 \right]
	\end{equation}
	of the
	difference operator
	\begin{equation}
		
		\bigl(\mathfrak{D}g\bigr)(x)\coloneqq
		\sqrt{\frac{w^{qR}(\tilde x)}{w^{qR}(\tilde  x+1)}}B(\tilde  x)\hspace{1pt} g(x+1)
		-[B(\tilde x)+D(\tilde x)]\hspace{1pt} g(x)
		+
		\sqrt{\frac{w^{qR}(\tilde x)}{w^{qR}(\tilde x-1)}}D(\tilde x)\hspace{1pt} g(x-1).
	\end{equation}
	This operator on functions of $x$
	acts in the (finite-dimensional)
	$\ell^2$ space on the $t$-th vertical slice of the hexagon.
	Its coefficients are read off from

[Corollary 17 of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Consider the following classes of wavelet bases:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item A wavelet basis of \(L^2(\mathbb{R})\) associated with an MRA.
    \item A vector-valued wavelet basis of \(L^2(\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R}^m)\) (\(m \ge 2\)) associated with a VMRA.
    \item An \(m\)-multiwavelet basis of \(L^2(\mathbb{R})\) associated with an MRA.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
  \textup{(1)} \;\implies\; \textup{(2)}
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \textup{(2)} \;\iff\; \textup{(3)}.
\]
In particular, any basis in \textup{(1)} yields bases in \textup{(2)} and \textup{(3)}, and the construction preserves regularity, vanishing moments, and compact support.

[Lemma NEW-l:strong-solution-diffusion of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] {lacker2019local}}]

Consider the finite or locally finite, infinite graph $\Psi({\cal X })$ on ${\cal X }$ 
equipped with  initial conditions $\{M(x)\}_{x \in {\cal X }}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d'}$, $d'\in\mathbb{N}$,  and
uniformly  bounded over  ${\cal X }$, i.e.,
 $\sup_{x\in{\cal X }}|M(x)|\le L$. 
Consider i.i.d. standard Brownian motions $\{Z_x(\cdot)\}_{x \in {\cal X }}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d'}$ on $[0,t_0]$, for $t_0\in(0,\infty)$ and  
 the Lipschitz drift and diffusion  coefficients $b$, $\sigma$
 as per Definition~(NEW-d:lip_assum of the paper). Then the system~(equation NEW-e:sys_ID_V of the paper), with initial conditions as above, admits a {\em unique solution with the family of processes $\{M[x]\}_{x \in \mathcal{X}}$},  taking values in the space of continuous paths $\mathbb {M} \owns M[x]=(M(x,t); t \in [0, t_0])$. Moreover, the trajectories $M[x]$ are uniformly bounded in $L^2$:
 \begin{equation}
 \sup_{x\in{\cal X }}\mathbb{E}  [\| M[x]\|^2] <C',
 \end{equation}
 where  the constant $C'$ depends only on $t_0$, the Lipschitz constant $K_{t_0}$, as well as on the bound $L$ of  the initial conditions, and {\em not} on the graph structure.

body: [Lemma 3.4 (Joint Convexity of Relative Entropy for Tensors) of arXiv:2012.15428, 'Convenient tail bounds for sums of random tensors'] The relative entropy function of two positive-definite tensors is a jointly convex function. Let G be a finite undirected loopless multigraph on n vertices with positive edge weights w_e, L its weighted Laplacian, and t > 0. A spanning rooted forest is a spanning forest with one chosen root in each tree; its weight is t^|E(F)| prod_{e in F} w_e (so an unrooted forest with trees T_1, ..., T_k counts prod |T_i| times). Z(t) is the total weight of spanning rooted forests, and Q_t = (I + tL)^-1. Then det(I + tL) = Z(t) = sum over spanning rooted forests F of t^|E(F)| prod_{e in F} w_e. (P. Chebotarev and E. Shamis.)

body: In probability theory, de Finetti's theorem states that exchangeable observations are conditionally independent relative to some latent variable. An epistemic probability distribution could then be assigned to this variable. It is named in honor of Bruno de Finetti, and one of its uses is in providing a pragmatic approach to de Finetti's well-known dictum "Probability does not exist".
title: De Finetti's theorem

body: For the l^p norm on R^2 and the axis direction e_2, the dogleg excess of a midpoint-displaced point v = (d, r/2) is exactly asymptotic to (2^p/p) d^p / r^{p-1} as d/r -> 0 (second-order Taylor of (1 + x^p)^{1/p}). Consequently the enclosing-ball (quadratic lower) curvature condition excess >= c d^2/r holds at the axis if and only if p <= 2: for p < 2 the excess is of larger order than quadratic (the condition holds with room), at p = 2 it is exactly quadratic with constant 2, and for every p > 2 the contact is quartic or flatter and the enclosing-ball constant is ZERO. The curvature hypothesis consumed by localization arguments is therefore genuinely restrictive - entire familiar norm families fail it at their axis directions - and cannot be discharged by convexity or symmetry alone. Numerically verified: measured excess/predicted ratios 0.9995-1.0000 across p in {1.5, 2, 3, 4} at two offsets, and the quadratic test excess/(d^2/r) converges to a constant for p <= 2 and to zero for p > 2.

[Theorem 4 (\cite{FangShaoXu2019}) of arXiv:2512.05340, 'The rate of convergence of the critical mean-field $O(N)$ magnetization via multivariate n'] Suppose $V$ satisfies Assumption \ref{Assumption: bounds on stein solution}, and let $\mu$ have Lebesgue density proportional to $e^{-V}$.
  Let $W,W'$ be identically distributed $\RR^d$-valued random variables, defined on the same probability space, such that if $\delta:=W'-W$ then
  $W$ and $\delta\delta^\transpose$ are both integrable.
  Let $\sF\supseteq\sigma(W)$ be a $\sigma$-algebra, let $\lambda>0$, and define $R_1$ and $R_2$ via~\eqref{eq: Regression Property} and~\eqref{eq: Correlation Property}.
  Then there exists a constant $C\in(0,\infty)$ such that
    \begin{equation}
      d(\sL(W),\mu)
      \leq C\left\lbrace \frac{1}{\lambda}\mathbb{E} [|\delta|^{3}(|\log|\delta|| \vee 1)] + \mathbb{E}|R_{1}|
      + \sqrt{d}\,\mathbb{E}\,\|R_{2}\| \right\rbrace. 
    \end{equation}

body: In mathematics, the free group $F_{S}$ over a given set $S$ consists of all words that can be built from members of $S$, considering two words to be different unless their equality follows from the group axioms (e.g. $st=suu^{-1}t$ but $s\neq t^{-1}$ for $s,t,u\in S$). The members of $S$ are called generators of $F_{S}$, and the number of generators is the rank of the free group. An arbitrary group $G$ is called free if it is isomorphic to $F_{S}$ for some subset $S$ of $G$, that is, if there is a subset $S$ of $G$ such that every element of $G$ can be written in exactly one way as a product of finitely many elements of $S$ and their inverses (disregarding trivial variations such as $st=suu^{-1}t$).

body: [Defn def:alephcomp of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] The \textbf{$\aleph$-completion} of $\mathcal{Z}(\Phi)$, denoted by $\mathcal{Z}_\aleph(\Phi)$, is the subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined as follows. A multislope $\bm{s} = (s_1, \dots, s_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is in $\mathcal{Z}_\aleph(\Phi)$ if and only if there is a generalized multislope $(\widetilde s_1,\dots,\widetilde s_n)$ realized by a $\Phi$-horizontal foliation such that each index $i$ satisfies either $\widetilde{s}_i = s_i$ or $\widetilde{s}_i=\aleph$; in other words, $\aleph$ may be treated as a wildcard.
title: Defn def:alephcomp of arXiv:2608.30031

[Defn def Holder of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] A function $f: X \to \mathbb{R}$ on an infinite product space $X = \prod_{n\in \mathbb{N}} X_n$ of metric spaces $(X_n,d_n)$ is H\"older continuous with respect to the standard metric on $X$ given by
\[d(x,y) = \sum_{n\in \mathbb{N}} 2^{-n} \min\{1, d_n(x_n,y_n)\},\]
if there exists $\alpha >0$ such that
\[\abs{f(x)-f(y)}\leq d(x,y)^{\alpha} \quad \text{for all } x,y\in X. 

\]

[Definition 11 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] Let $A$ be an $\mathbf{FS}^{op}$-module. The bar construction of $A$, denoted $\mathsf{B}(A)$, is a sequence of chain complexes $\mathsf{B}(A)(n)$.  The underlying graded vector spaces are defined by:
	$$
	\mathsf{B}(A)(n) = \ds\bigoplus_{\substack{ (\mathsf{t},v)} \in n\text{-Tree}_\ast} A(\mathsf{t},v)\tensor det(\mathsf{t}).
	$$
The differential is the linear extension of the map $d_{(\mathsf{t},v)}:= \sum_{e\in E(\mathsf{t})} d_e$.

[Theorem 9 (Pressure; the Jensen gap as a chord--tangent inequality) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Under uniform ellipticity and irreducibility:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\varphi$ is convex on $[0,\infty)$ and real-analytic, with $\varphi(0)=\log m_*$ and $\varphi(1)=\log\rho(M)$.
\item $\varphi'(0)=\E_{q\otimes q}[\log p_{d,d'}]$, and for $\nu_h$-a.e.\ ray $\xi$, $n^{-1}\sum_{e\in o\to\xi,\ |e|\le n}\log p_e\to\E_{q\otimes q}[\log p]$; i.e.\ $\varphi(0)+\varphi'(0)=\ell$ is the quenched rate of Theorem~\ref{thm:gap} (with $w\equiv1$).
\item (The gap.) $\varphi(1)\ge\varphi(0)+\varphi'(0)$, i.e.
\[
\rho(M)\ge m_*\,e^{\E_{q\otimes q}[\log p]}=e^{\ell},
\]
with equality if and only if $p_{d,d'}$ is constant on $\supp q\times\supp q$. This is the sharp form of the gap in Theorem~\ref{thm:gap}(3).
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition prop:realzeroesEven of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] Assume that $n_\beta$ is even. Then $f_\beta$ has exactly one simple

body:
[Dfn 217 (stochastic control and achievable measures for symmetrized projection pursuit) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $B, W$ be one-dimensional standard Brownian motions, and let $U,U' \sim \unif([0,1])$ (with $B,W,U,U'$ mutually independent).
Define the filtrations 
\[\begin{aligned}
    \cF_X(t) &= \sigma(U, (B(s) : 0\le s\le t))\,, \\
    \cF_{\Ising}(t) &= \sigma(U', (W(s) : 0\le s\le t))\,.
\end{aligned}\]
Let $\ProgMsrbl(\cF_X)$ denote the space of stochastic processes that are progressively measurable with respect to $\cF_X$, and similarly $\ProgMsrbl(\cF_{\Ising})$ for $\cF_{\Ising}$. For $\sigma\in\ProgMsrbl(\cF_X)$ and $w\in\ProgMsrbl(\cF_{\Ising})$, let  
	\begin{align}
	
	X(t)
	&\equiv\int_0^s \sigma_t\,dB(s)\,,\\
	X^\Ising(t)
	&\equiv\int_0^t w_s\,dW(s)
	
	\end{align}
Let $\cM^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$ be the set of measures $\mu$ which can be expressed as $\mu=\Law(|X(1)|)$
(i.e., $\mu$ is the law of the real-valued random variable $|X(1)|$)
 for $X$ defined by \eqref{eq:main-process-intro-p=1}, and for controls $(\sigma,w)$ satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item the nonnegativity condition
$\sigma_t\ge0$ for all $t\in[0,1]$,
\item the time parametrization condition
$\E[(w_t)^2]=1$ for all $t\in[0,1]$,
\item the \textbf{budget constraint}
	\beq
	\E\Big[(\sigma_t-1)^2\Big]
	\le \frac{(\E w_t)^2}{\alpha}
	\eeq
for all $t\in[0,1]$, and 
\item the \textbf{endpoint condition}
$|X^{\Ising}(1)|=1$.
\end{itemize}
 Let $\cM^{\sph,\sym}(\alpha)$ be the set of measures $\mu$ which can be expressed as $\mu=\Law(|X(1)|)$ for $X$ defined by \eqref{eq:main-process-intro-p=1}, and for controls $(\sigma,w\equiv1)$ satisfying the same conditions as above, \textbf{except for the endpoint constraint}. We use $\bar{\cM}^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$,
$\bar{\cM}^{\sph,\sym}(\alpha)$ to denote the closures with respect to the $2$-Wasserstein metric $\bbW_2$ (defined by \eqref{def:W2} below).
title: stochastic control and achievable measures for symmetrized projection pursuit

body: In mathematics, specifically functional analysis, a trace-class operator is a linear operator for which a trace may be defined, such that the trace is a finite number independent of the choice of basis used to compute the trace. This trace of trace-class operators generalizes the trace of matrices studied in linear algebra. All trace-class operators are compact operators.

[Theorem S1T1 of arXiv:2410.23899, 'Tightness for interlacing geometric random walk bridges'] Suppose that $\mathfrak{L}^N$ is a sequence of random elements in $\mathbb{Y}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ that satisfies Assumptions 1 and 2 above. Define the sequence $\mathcal{L}^N = \{\mathcal{L}_i^N\}_{i = 1}^{\infty} \in C(\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{R})$ by
$$\mathcal{L}^N_i(t) = \sigma^{-1} d_N^{-1/2} \cdot \left( L_i^N(t d_N) - p td_N - C_N\right), $$
where $L_i^N(s)$ is defined for non-integer $s$ by linear interpolation. Then, $\mathcal{L}^N$ is a tight sequence of random elements in $C(\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{R})$. Moreover, any subsequential limit satisfies the Brownian Gibbs property from [CorHamA], see also [DM21]. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let integer d>=1, p>0, and mu,nu be Borel probability measures on Q=(-1,1]^d. Let P_ell be the half-open dyadic partitions of Q into2^(d ell) cubes of side2^(1-ell), and set D_p(mu,nu)=[(2^p-1)/2]sum_{ell>=1}2^(-p ell)sum_{F in P_ell}|mu(F)-nu(F)|. Define T_p(mu,nu)=inf_{pi in Couplings(mu,nu)} integral_{Q x Q}||x-y||_2^p pi(dx,dy). Then T_p(mu,nu)<=kappa_(p,d)D_p(mu,nu), where kappa_(p,d)=2^(p(1+d/2))(2^p+1)/(2^p-1). This is the compact case in Step1 ofLemma5p6,1312.2128v1. For p>1 it yields W_p(mu,nu)<=[kappa_(p,d)D_p(mu,nu)]^(1/p) under W_p=T_p^(1/p). The transport inequality is deterministic, so it applies to empirical measures with dependent samples as well; their cell-discrepancy estimates require their own probabilistic hypotheses.

Euclidean p-transport cost T_p as explicitly defined

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Ramanujan inequalities for growing families of matrix polynomials structural calculation Result: The one-generator amenable case satisfies the exact inequality at every degree: take an N-cycle permutation and remove its constant eigenvector. Its remaining eigenvalues lie on the unit circle, so the norm of any Laurent polynomial is at most its supremum on that circle, exactly the norm in the regular representation of Z. Check: A normal finite matrix is unitarily diagonalizable, and Laurent-polynomial norms are maxima over its eigenvalues. This proves the bound without an asymptotic error or probability qualifier. Obstruction: For r>=2 the free reduced group algebra is noncommutative and has no finite-dimensional faithful representation. The circle argument gives no construction for any diverging degree window in that setting.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0185-ramanujan-inequalities-for-growing-families-of-matrix-polynomials
No independent review
title: Attempt on Ramanujan inequalities for growing families of matrix polynomials

body: In mathematics, the Smith normal form is a normal form that can be defined for any matrix with entries in a principal ideal domain (PID). The Smith normal form of a matrix is diagonal, and can be obtained from the original matrix by multiplying on the left and right by invertible square matrices. In particular, the integers are a PID, so one can always calculate the Smith normal form of an integer matrix. The Smith normal form is very useful for working with finitely generated modules over a PID, and in particular for deducing the structure of a quotient of a free module. It is named after the Irish mathematician Henry John Stephen Smith.
title: Smith normal form

[Lemma 4 (Stability of increasing inverses) of arXiv:2608.26834, 'Small-time annealed large deviations principle for one-dimensional diffusions in a random '] Let $a<b$ and let $\Lambda_n,\Lambda$ be continuous strictly increasing
	functions on $[a,b]$ such that $\Lambda_n\to\Lambda$ uniformly. Suppose
	that $h_n,h\in C([0,1])$, $h_n\to h$ uniformly, and
	$h_n([0,1])\subset\Lambda_n([a,b])$. Then
	$h([0,1])\subset\Lambda([a,b])$ and
	\[
		\Lambda_n^{-1}\circ h_n
		\longrightarrow\Lambda^{-1}\circ h
		\quad\text{uniformly}.
	\]

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited), independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending. # Exact saturated single-pair frontier from integer bin counts

T379-C018 v2: proof (unaudited), exact checks PASS; independent audit pending.
Target 1, secondary target 2. Conditional robust ZERO calibration only;
arbitrary VC dimension with several saturated pairs remains open here.

## Model and exact candidate

Let N>=3,K>=2,1<=r<K,0<=s<r be integers. There is one unresolved A/S
pair L,R and N-2 fixed known S contexts. S has all K truths; A has an
independent uniform r-subset. The source p chooses contexts uniformly
and then truths uniformly. Actual untagged iid factual samples and an
optional independent partial verifier give known truth unions C_L,C_R
of sizes s and r respectively. Both orientations are still compatible.
If R is A its support is fully known; if L is A it contains C_L but
its r-s residual truths vary over the other K-s candidates.

All generators are allowed. Require source Mis_infinity=0 in EVERY
compatible world, using exact output-probability score bins.
Put F=K-r, G=gcd(r,F), lambda=1/(NK). For j=0,...,G define

 k_j=min(s,r*j/G),
 L_j=K+K*j/G-2*k_j,
 a_j=(j/G)*(F/r)*k_j/L_j.                                (1)

All counts are integers and all L_j>0. The proposed exact conditional
worst-world false-mass frontier is

 V_sat(0)=F*lambda*(1-max_{0<=j<=G}a_j).                  (2)

This is a finite optimization of G+1 explicit rational values, not a
numerical estimate or an unbounded partition search. It includes every
score partition, mixed safe atoms and arbitrary output probabilities.
No optimal positive-budget or global expected frontier is claimed.

## Lower bound for every robustly calibrated generator

Fix g and its exact score partition Pi. Robust zero calibration makes
every p(B)=g(B) invariant across all compatible worlds. Since s<r<K,
swapping two residual L candidates in an A support forces all K-s
uncertified L atoms into a single score bin B*. Let k be the number
of known L truths OUTSIDE B*, so 0<=k<=s. In B* let u be the number
of known R truths, v the number of the F candidates outside C_R,
and w the number of fixed S atoms. Flipping orientation yields

 F*(u+k)=r*v.

Consequently v=F*j/G and u=r*j/G-k for an integer 0<=j<=G, with
k<=r*j/G. The size of B* is

For completeness the divisibility step uses Bezout: r/G and F/G are
coprime; a*(r/G)+b*(F/G)=1. Multiplying by v and using (F/G)|(r/G)*v
gives (F/G)|v, then the displayed parametrization. The brain returned
this standard identity in recall/walk004.txt, full card id
claim_63c5ddfd2e7e4d178b7628c572034232. It did not supply the frontier.

 L=K+K*j/G-2k+w,

and its common calibrated score, computed in the L-A world, is

 q*=lambda*(1-k*F/(r*L)).                               (3)

In any other bin let a be its known-L-truth count, u its known-R-
truth count and v its outside-C_R count. Orientation invariance gives
F*(u-a)=r*v. Its calibrated score is

 q=lambda*(1+a*F/(r*|B|))>=lambda.

Therefore in the actual compatible world R=A (whose support is C_R),
the false mass is at least

 H_R>=v*q*+(F-v)*lambda
    >=F*lambda*[1-(j/G)*(F/r)*k/(K+K*j/G-2k)].            (4)

The second inequality uses w>=0, which can only raise q* in (3).
For fixed j the function k/(K+K*j/G-2k) increases with k on the
feasible positive-denominator range: cross multiplication cancels the
quadratic terms and leaves K*(1+j/G)*(k_2-k_1)>=0. Thus its maximum
is at k=k_j. Formula (4) proves max_world H(g)>=the value (2).
It does not assume arbitrary bins are homogeneous in truth status.

## Attainer for each j

Fix any j and k=k_j. Choose k known L truths for a safe group T;
put all other L atoms in B*. In R put r*j/G-k known truths and
F*j/G outside-C_R atoms into B*. Put k of the remaining known R
truths in T alongside its k known L truths. Put all remaining R atoms
in Z. These choices are possible: k<=s and k<=r*j/G; also j<=G
ensures enough R known truths remain for T.

The groups have these source-invariant counts and scores:

* B*: K+K*j/G-2k atoms, score (3) with w=0;
* T: 2k known true atoms, score (1/r+1/K)/(2N), omitted if k=0;
* Z: r*(G-j)/G known R truths and F*(G-j)/G outside atoms,
  total K*(G-j)/G atoms, score lambda, omitted if j=G;
* fixed S atoms: score lambda.

T has source mass k/(Nr)+k/(NK). Z has source mass (G-j)/(GN)
in either orientation. B* has the remaining pair mass, or its
invariance follows directly from F*(u+k)=r*v. Thus every group has
an invariant p mass and g is its uniform coarsening; equal lambda
scores merge harmlessly. The total is one and g is robustly calibrated
with zero budget in every compatible world.

If L=A its F false atoms all lie in B*, giving H_L=F*q*. If R=A,
H_R=(F*j/G)*q*+F*(1-j/G)*lambda. Since q*<=lambda, H_R>=H_L.
The worst risk is exactly F*lambda*(1-a_j). Maximizing a_j attains
the lower bound, proving (2).

The attaining rule uses only the observed known-truth unions and the
given model parameters: choose j by the explicit optimization, and
choose the displayed subsets of those known unions. It never reads
the hidden orientation or unobserved truth labels. Those labels enter
only the subsequent all-world verification and lower-bound argument.

## Consequences and relation to the earlier obstruction

If G=1, the only improving choice is j=1,k=s. Formula (2) becomes
the earlier smaller-count expression (K-r)*b_s. Thus the saturated
unequal case still has that expression when r and K-r are coprime.
When G>1, additional neutral truth/false bundles may improve it.

For C016's family K=3m,r=3(m-1),s=2(m-1),m>=5, G=3. The reductions
a_j for j=1,2,3 are respectively

 1/[6(m+1)], 4/[3(m+4)], 1/(m+2).

The middle value is largest: it beats the last iff m>4 and beats
the first since 24(m+1)>3(m+4). Thus C016's feasible generator is
in fact OPTIMAL in the conditional zero-budget game, with exact value

 V_sat(0)=lambda*(3m+8)/(m+4).                           (5)

This upgrades a route obstruction to an exact infinite-family frontier,
within the stated single-pair regime. It does not solve the full
arbitrary-d/global expected targets. Together with the unsaturated
C017 result and the fully-known-both-sides C013 case it gives an exact
single-pair zero-budget case map, but no larger claim is inferred.

Primary source statistic: Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3 Definitions 1--2,
pp.8--9. The new integer-count derivation is an owner-own-work draft;
independent mathematical, literature-priority and target-scope audits
are pending. Finite checks are separate from the general proof.

Exact verification: logs/saturated_single_pair_check.json records 572
parameter cases, 1144 representative-orientation calibrations, 86
exhaustive compatible-support checks, 374 coprime collapses and 20
neutral-family optimum checks. Five independently implemented exact
score-partition branch-and-bound searches start with bound 1 (not the
formula), find real optimal calibrated witnesses and agree with (2).
These finite checks validate the derivation; they do not replace it.

One unresolved A/S pair, remaining known S contexts; uniform contexts then uniform truths; arbitrary A has uniform r-subset prior
Observed truth unions of sizes s,r from actual untagged factual samples and optional independent partial verifier; no orientation labels
Robust exact-level source Mis_infinity=0 in every compatible support/orientation; arbitrary generators

given model parameters: choose j by the explicit optimization, and
choose the displayed subsets of those known unions. It never reads
the hidden orientation or unobserved truth labels. Those labels enter
only the subsequent all-world verification and lower-bound argument.

the earlier smaller-count expression (K-r)*b_s. Thus the saturated

 1/[6(m+1)], 4/[3(m+4)], 1/(m+2).

The middle value is largest: it beats the last iff m>4 and beats

Let H be bounded self-adjoint on l2(Z^3), with bounded deterministic hopping and iid real site variables of bounded support and bounded probability density rho, scaled by a fixed lambda>0. Delete x to obtain H^x and its hopping vector b_x, and put Gamma_x(E,eta)=eta+Im<b_x,(H^x-E-i eta)^(-1)b_x>. Fix 0<q<1 and an open interval I. If for each x and each compact interval J contained in I, sup_{0<eta<1} E integral_J Gamma_x(E,eta)^(-q)dE<infinity, then almost surely all site spectral measures restricted to I are absolutely continuous, with locally L^(1+q) densities, and chi_I(H)l2(Z^3) is contained in the absolutely continuous subspace. This is a conditional criterion; the moment bound is not established for the lattice Anderson model here. Nonzero spectral weight is a separate requirement.

Then  there is an $m\in \N$ depending only on  $\ell, N, (K_j)_{j=0}^\ell$, and $\alpha$, such that for 
 all $0\leq j\leq i\leq \ell$ and $n>m$, we have 
	\begin{align}
		& 
		\mathbb{E} \left[ \left( S_{j}^{X}(n) - S_{j}^{Z}(n) \right)^2 \right] \geq \left(2 - 0.01 \alpha \right) K_j \log(n),
		\\
		& 
		\mathbb{E} \left[ \left( S_{j}^{X}(n) - S_{j}^{Y}(n) \right)^2 \right] \leq \left(2 - 0.1 \alpha \right) K_j \log(n),
		\\
		&
		
		\Cov \left( \left( S_{j}^{X}(n) - S_{j}^{Z}(n) \right)^2, \left( S_{i}^{X}(n) - S_{i}^{Z}(n) \right)^2 \right) \leq 10 K_j^2 \log(n)^2 , \text{ and }
		\\
		&
		
		\Cov \left( \left( S_{j}^{X}(n) - S_{j}^{Y}(n) \right)^2, \left( S_{i}^{X}(n) - S_{i}^{Y}(n) \right)^2 \right) \leq 10 K_j^2 \log(n)^2.
	\end{align}
Furthermore,
\ban{

body:
There is NO inclusion between L^p and L^q on a general measure space, and the two familiar inclusions run in OPPOSITE directions. (a) Finite measure (mu(X) < infinity), p < q: L^q is contained in L^p, with ||f||_p <= mu(X)^{1/p - 1/q} ||f||_q; the inclusion is strict, e.g. on [0,1], f(x) = x^{-1/2} is in L^1 but not L^2. (b) Counting measure, p < q: l^p is contained in l^q, with ||a||_q <= ||a||_p - the reverse containment; strictness: a_n = 1/n is in l^2 but not l^1. (c) Lebesgue measure on R^n: NEITHER containment holds. On R, |x|^{-1/2} 1_{{|x|<1}} is in L^1 but not L^2, while (1 + |x|)^{-1} is in L^2 but not L^1 - the first fails by a local singularity, the second by slow decay at infinity. What IS always true is the interpolation statement: for p_0 < p < p_1, L^{p_0} intersect L^{p_1} is contained in L^p, with ||f||_p <= ||f||_{p_0}^{1-theta} ||f||_{p_1}^{theta}. So a step 'f in L^2 hence f in L^1' is only legitimate after the measure has been declared finite (with the factor mu(X)^{1/2} exhibited), and 'f in L^1 hence f in L^2' only on an atomic space with atoms bounded below.
all examples are for Lebesgue measure on [0,1] or R, and counting measure on N
title: Pitfall: L^p inclusions depend on the measure, and point in opposite directions for finite measures and for counting measure

[Definition def:regular-markovian-2bsde of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Fix $0\leq\alpha<1$ and $\psi\in H^2(\mu_T)$.  For the purposes of this paper,
a regular fixed-reference Markovian 2BSDE solution consists of Borel fields
$(u,p,H):Q\to\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathsf{S}^d$ and a process
$\mathfrak A\in\mathbb V^2(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\mathfrak A_0=0$.  The field
compositions must admit representatives
\begin{equation*}
 Y=u(\cdot,X),\qquad P=p(\cdot,X),\qquad \mathsf H=H(\cdot,X).
\end{equation*}
These representatives satisfy
\begin{equation*}
 Y\in\mathbb S^2(\mathbb R),\qquad
 P\in\mathbb S^2(\mathbb R^d),\qquad
 P^\top\in\mathbb H^2(\mathsf M^X;\mathbb R),\qquad
 \mathsf H\in\mathbb H^2(\mathsf M^X;\mathbb R^d),
\end{equation*}
and the fields must satisfy the regularity condition
\begin{equation*}
 F[u,p,H]\in H_{x,\alpha}^1,
\end{equation*}
as well as the following dynamics:
\begin{align}
 Y_t&=\psi(X_T)+\int_t^TF[u,p,H](s,X_s)\,\mathrm d s
          -\int_t^TP_s^\top\,\mathrm d\mathsf M_s^X,
 \\
 P_t&=P_0+\mathfrak A_t+\int_0^t\mathsf H_s\,\mathrm d\mathsf M_s^X,
 \qquad P_T=D_x\psi(X_T).
 
\end{align}
The identities $p=D_xu$ and $H=D_x^2u$, as well as absolute continuity of
$\mathfrak A$, are not imposed in this definition.

[Proposition prop:real-zero-family of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] For some $\varepsilon>0$, the following assertions hold.

For every $z\in Z$, all zeros of $F_z$ are real and simple, and
its zero set
\[
    P_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R:F_z(x)=0\}
\]
is uniformly Delone. More precisely, there is $\delta>0$ such
that
\[
    P_z=\{p_\lambda(z):\lambda\in\Lambda\},
    \qquad
    |p_\lambda(z)-\lambda|<\delta
\]
for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and $z\in Z$.

The map
\[
    z\longmapsto\delta_{P_z}
\]
is Borel, and
\[
    P_{Tz}=P_z-1
    \qquad
    (z\in Z).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

		There exist constants $\beta_0>0$ and $c>c'>0$ so that the following holds for every $\beta\geq \beta_0$ and integer $h\geq 2$. Let $V \subset \mathbb Z^2$ be a region containing $\ensuremath{\mathcal B}_r(o)$, the ball of radius $r=\lceil 2c h/\log h\rceil $ centered at the origin $o$, as well as $\ensuremath{\mathcal B}_{r+1}(z)$ for a site $z\in V$. Then
		\begin{align}
			\exp\Big(-c\beta \frac{h}{\log h}\Big) \leq &\;\frac{{\widehat\pi}_V^0(\phi_o = h)}{{\widehat\pi}_V^0(\phi_o = h-1)} \leq 
			\exp\Big(-c'\beta \frac{h}{\log h}\Big)
			\,,\\

			&\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!
			{\widehat\pi}_V^0(\phi_z = h \mid \phi_o = h) \leq \exp\Big(-c \beta \frac{h^2}{\log^2h}\Big)\,.

body: Let X_n, X be random variables or vectors with X_n -> X in distribution as n -> infinity, and let Y_n -> c in probability for a constant c. Then X_n + Y_n -> X + c in distribution, X_n Y_n -> c X in distribution, and, provided c is not 0, X_n / Y_n -> X / c in distribution. More generally, if g(x,y) is continuous at every point (x,c), then g(X_n,Y_n) -> g(X,c) in distribution. Slutsky's theorem lets one combine a distributional limit with a probability limit as though the latter were a genuine constant. Due to Eugen Slutsky.

body:
Let (M, g) be a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension n whose Ricci curvature satisfies Ric >= (n - 1) K g for a constant K, and let V_K(r) denote the volume of a geodesic ball of radius r in the simply connected complete space of constant curvature K (the sphere of radius 1/sqrt(K) for K > 0, Euclidean space for K = 0, hyperbolic space of curvature K for K < 0; for K > 0 take r <= pi / sqrt(K)). Then for every point p in M the function r |-> vol(B(p, r)) / V_K(r) is nonincreasing on (0, infinity) (on (0, pi/sqrt(K)] if K > 0) and tends to 1 as r -> 0. Consequently vol(B(p, r)) <= V_K(r) for all r (Bishop's inequality); for K = 0, vol(B(p, r)) <= omega_n r^n, volume grows at most Euclideanly and the limit vol(B(p, r)) / (omega_n r^n) as r -> infinity (the asymptotic volume ratio) exists and is at most 1; and vol(B(p, R)) / vol(B(p, r)) <= V_K(R) / V_K(r) for r <= R, which is the doubling-type estimate behind Gromov's precompactness theorem, Milnor's polynomial growth of the fundamental group under Ric >= 0, and Cheng's maximal diameter theorem (equality in the diameter bound pi/sqrt(K) forces the round sphere).
(M, g) complete, dimension n >= 2, Ric >= (n - 1) K
for K > 0 the radii are restricted to r <= pi/sqrt(K) (Myers' theorem bounds the diameter by this)
balls are metric balls; the comparison is with the constant-curvature space form of the same dimension

[Theorem thm:class5 of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] Let $B=\{b_1,\dots,b_5\}$ be a positive basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$. Up to renumbering,
independent positive rescaling of each vector, and an invertible linear map,
\[
b_1=e_1,\quad b_2=e_2,\quad b_3=-e_1-e_2,\quad
b_4=e_3-\tfrac\kappa2e_1,\quad b_5=-e_3-\tfrac\kappa2e_1,
\]
for some $\kappa\ge0$; equivalently
\begin{equation}
b_1+b_2+b_3=0,\qquad \kappa b_1+b_4+b_5=0 .
\end{equation}
For $\kappa=0$ the basis splits into a rank-$2$ triangle circuit and an
antipodal pair; all $\kappa>0$ form one orbit, in which two rank-$2$
triangle circuits share the vector $b_1$.

[Lemma 14 (Joint compactness through the endpoints) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] Let $D_n$ be a uniformly $C^{2,\gamma}$ sequence converging locally in
$C^{2,\gamma'}$, for some $\gamma'<\gamma$, to a domain $D_\infty$.  Let
$\varrho_n\to\varrho_\infty\in[0,1]$, and suppose
$u_n\in C^2(D_n)\cap C^1(\overline{D_n})$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 0\leq u_n\leq1,\qquad -\Delta u_n=f(u_n)\ \text{in }D_n,
 \qquad \cN_{\varrho_n}u_n=0\ \text{on }\partial D_n.
\end{equation}
After passage to a subsequence, $u_n$ converges locally uniformly on the
closure of each component that persists under this local smooth convergence
to a function $u_\infty$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 -\Delta u_\infty=f(u_\infty)\ \text{in }D_\infty,
 \qquad \cN_{\varrho_\infty}u_\infty=0\ \text{on }\partial D_\infty.
\end{equation}

body:
Let $G_1,\dots,G_p$ be independent $n \times n$ matrices with i.i.d. $\mathcal{N}(0,1/n)$ entries. The limiting singular value distribution of the product $G_p \cdots G_1$ is the Fuss-Catalan law of order $p$, whose upper edge is $(p+1)^{(p+1)/2}p^{-p/2}$. For $p=1$ this is $2$, recovering the square Gaussian case; for $p=2$ it is $3^{3/2}/2=\sqrt{27/4}=2.5980\ldots$; for $p=3$ it is $3.0792\ldots$. Moreover the largest singular value itself converges to that edge, not merely the bulk. This last point matters and is strictly stronger: convergence of the spectral distribution locates the edge but by itself does not exclude an outlier above it, so a bound that needs no outlier cannot be justified by the Fuss-Catalan law alone.

body:
Let $Y_n = X_n + \sigma Z_n$ where $Y_n$ is $m \times n$ with $m/n \to \beta \in (0, 1]$, $Z_n$ has i.i.d. entries of mean zero, variance one and finite fourth moment, and $X_n$ has fixed rank $r$ with singular values $\sigma\sqrt{n}\, x_1, \dots, \sigma\sqrt{n}\, x_r$ (so the $x_k$ are the signal singular values on the scale of the noise, $x_k > 0$ fixed). Write the singular values of $Y_n$ on the same scale, $y_k := s_k(Y_n) / (\sigma \sqrt{n})$. THEOREM (Gavish and Donoho, 2017). (i) For each $k \le r$: if $x_k > \beta^{1/4}$ then $y_k \to \sqrt{(x_k^2 + 1)(x_k^2 + \beta)} / x_k$, and if $x_k \le \beta^{1/4}$ then $y_k \to 1 + \sqrt\beta$ (the bulk edge); every other singular value of $Y_n$ converges to the bulk. (ii) Among all estimators of the form $\hat X = \sum_k \eta(y_k)\, \sigma\sqrt{n}\; \hat u_k \hat v_k^T$ that keep the sample singular vectors and replace each singular value by a function $\eta$ of it, the one minimizing the asymptotic Frobenius loss $\lim \|\hat X - X_n\|_F^2 / (\sigma^2 n)$ is $$\eta^*(y) = \frac{1}{y}\sqrt{(y^2 - \beta - 1)^2 - 4\beta} \quad \text{for } y \ge 1 + \sqrt\beta, \qquad \eta^*(y) = 0 \quad \text{for } y < 1 + \sqrt\beta.$$ (iii) The asymptotic loss of $\eta^*$ is strictly smaller than that of hard thresholding at any threshold and of soft thresholding at any threshold whenever some $x_k > \beta^{1/4}$; on a pure-noise matrix ($r = 0$) $\eta^*$ returns the zero matrix. The rule selects the rank (the number of $y_k$ above the edge $1 + \sqrt\beta$) and the amount of shrinkage of each retained component from the data, without cross-validation; with $\sigma$ unknown it is combined with the median estimate $\hat\sigma = y_{\mathrm{med}}/\sqrt{n \mu_\beta}$.

body:
[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.20026, 'Quasihelix properties\\ of selected Volterra Gaussian processes'] Let $\gamma\in[0,1)$. Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[1)]
\item Let $\alpha\in(-1/2+\gamma/2,1/2+\gamma/2)$. Then 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[$(i)$]
There exists a constant $C(\alpha,\gamma)>0$ such that, for any $0\le s<t$,
\[
\ex\big(U^{(2)}(t)-U^{(2)}(s)\big)^2
\le C(\alpha,\gamma)(t-s)^{2\alpha+1-\gamma}.
\]

\item[$(ii)$]
The process $U^{(2)}$ is a local
$(\alpha+\frac12,\alpha+\frac{1-\gamma}{2},0,T)$-generalized quasihelix for any $T>0$.
\end{enumerate}

\item If $\alpha\in[1/2+\gamma/2,1)$, then the process $U^{(2)}$ is a local
$(\alpha+\frac12,\alpha,0,T)$-generalized quasihelix for any $T>0$.

\item If $\alpha\ge1$, then the process $U^{(2)}$ is a local
$(\alpha+\frac12,1,0,T)$-generalized quasihelix for any $T>0$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.20026

Let Y be uniform on {-1,+1} and X|Y=y have law N(y mu,Sigma), with Sigma positive definite. For a closed l2 adversarial ball of radius epsilon>=0, define d=min_{||z||_2<=epsilon} sqrt((mu-z)^T Sigma^{-1}(mu-z)). The maximum robust classification accuracy over all measurable classifiers is Phi(d), where Phi is the standard normal CDF. If epsilon<||mu||, a minimizing z yields the optimal centered halfspace with normal Sigma^{-1}(mu-z). If epsilon>=||mu||, d=0 and a constant classifier attains accuracy 1/2. For Sigma=sigma^2 I the answer is Phi((||mu||-epsilon)_+/sigma). This optimum is known from Bhagoji, Cullina and Mittal and is restated by Dan, Wei and Ravikumar, Theorem 2.1, arXiv:2006.16384v1, printed p.5.

Closed l2 adversarial balls; measurable classifiers

There exists delta>0, depending only on these intervals, such that
for EACH fixed eigenvalue pair in these intervals and EACH eta>0,
ordinary separately bias-corrected Adam with beta1=.9,beta2=.999,
epsilon=eta outside sqrt and standard zero moments satisfies

 limsup_t |eta*C_active,t-38|>=delta                     (1)

for Lebesgue-almost every initial position in R^2. The exceptional
null set may depend on the eigenvalues and eta. For fixed eigenvalues,
the conclusion holds simultaneously along any specified countable
eta sequence under any absolutely continuous joint initialization law;
coordinate independence is not assumed.

Hence generic p=1 nontracking holds for EVERY fixed pair
lambda_h>lambda_star and0<lambda_l<38. This extends016v2's fixed
[2000,3000]x[10,20] windows to the entire strict mixed unstable/subcritical
range. It does NOT include lambda_l=38, the neutral high boundary,
or the regime38<lambda_l<lambda_star. No attracting dynamics or time
average is identified. The delta is existential, not computed.

AUDIT / HARDEST PIECE
This is UNAUDITED. It uses012v2's low-cap convergence,015v3's corrected
scalar countable cycle basin and uniform local capture,023v1's direct
zero-work full-path classification, and025v1's Green origin decay.
The difficult standard-initialization cycle countability in015v3
remains an independent audit burden. Unlike021's singular-floor proof,
this proof needs no source potential or closed-relation singular lift:
the scalar high floor rho=1/lambda_h stays strictly positive.

1. NORMALIZATION, BOUNDEDNESS AND THE LOW COORDINATE
For either coordinate let X=x/eta,M=m/(eta*lambda),
V=v/(eta*lambda)^2,rho=1/lambda. The raw scalar map is

 M'=bM+(1-b)X, V'=dV+(1-d)X^2,
 X'=X-M'/(sqrt(V')+rho).                                (2)

Corrected maps have their ordinary separate clock factors. The
elementary absorbing argument in033 Section1 gives uniform tail
bounds |X|,|M|<=802,V<=802^2, after a start-dependent burn-in.
For high rho in[1/H1,1/H0], the corrected maps converge uniformly
on this compact physical box to the continuous map F_rho in(2).
Claim012v2 gives X_l,M_l,V_l->0 since lambda_l<38, regardless of its
standard initial position.

2. A NARROW ACTIVE BAND IMPOSES A CLOSED SCALAR BAND ON THE OMEGA SET
Suppose limsup |A_t-38|<delta, A_t=eta*C_active,t. Eventually its
defined values lie within delta. Multiply this inequality by the
nonnegative active denominator sum_i g_i^2/P_i. At exact zero gradient
times both extended sides are zero. All coefficients are bounded;
the low coordinate vanishes. For any point (X,M,V) of the high
omega-limit K, taking an adjacent-state limit therefore gives

 X^2*|kappa_rho(X,V)-38|<=delta*X^2,
 kappa_rho(X,V)=1/(sqrt(dV+(1-d)X^2)+rho).                (3)

The harmless positive factor1/(sqrt(V')+rho) was canceled when X!=0;
when X=0 both sides of(3) are zero. Thus(3) remains a closed constraint
at zero positions. K is nonempty compact, F_rho(K)=K, and internally
chain transitive for F_rho. To see the latter, follow a late actual
segment between visits near prescribed x,y in K. Actual tail distance
to K and corrected-map distance to F_rho tend to zero. Project each
segment node into K. Uniform continuity of F_rho bounds each chain
error separately, independently of the segment length.

3. UNIFORM SMALL-BAND REDUCTION TO CRITICAL NEIGHBORHOODS
For delta=0, EVERY full F_rho-path in a compact invariant K satisfying
(3) is a bounded full scalar zero-work path. By023 it is an origin or
cycle path, with a=1/38-rho>0. Hence K is contained in the three
critical states; internal chain transitivity forces one critical orbit.

This exact statement gives a uniform near-critical statement on the
compact rho interval. Fix sufficiently small neighborhoods of the
origin and of the two cycle phases, centered continuously in rho.
For all sufficiently small delta, EVERY compact fully invariant
internally chain-transitive K satisfying(3) lies in their union.
Otherwise take delta_n->0, rho_n converging, and offending K_n. A
Hausdorff subsequence gives K in the common physical compact box.
Uniform convergence F_rho_n->F_rho passes full invariance and(3)
to the limit. It also passes internal chain transitivity: project
the nodes of an arbitrarily fine F_rho_n-chain into K and use uniform
continuity to control each new jump, without accumulating errors.
Thus K is one critical orbit. A selected point outside the chosen
neighborhoods persists outside at the limit, a contradiction.

Choose OUTER neighborhoods first, with these properties uniformly
over rho: they are disjoint; a corrected late step with both ends in
their union cannot change orbit groups or select a wrong cycle phase;
cycle neighborhoods are within015v3's uniform physical capture region;
the origin neighborhood is small enough for the uniform Green estimate
in Section4. Uniform continuity at the separated critical states and
compactness give the nonjump conditions. Use INNER half-radius
neighborhoods for the preceding compactness reduction. For delta small
enough, K lies in the inner union; hence the actual tail lies in the
outer union. Nonjump separation makes it eventually stay in the
origin group or the alternating cycle group.

4. THE ORIGIN ALTERNATIVE CONTRADICTS THE ACTIVE BAND
For high lambda in[H0,H1], the limiting position-pair matrix

 A_h=[[1+b-(1-b)*lambda_h,-b],[1,0]]

has real roots -b<r_s<0,r_u<-1. Their gaps from b and the unit circle
are uniform on the compact high interval. Choose
sup |r_s|<q<nu<b. Eigenbases and inverses are uniformly bounded.
The origin neighborhood and late clocks can be chosen so the actual
position-pair coefficients, throughout that neighborhood, are close
enough to A_h for BOTH Green contractions in036 Section2 (weighted
q and bounded weight1). This argument requires only boundedness and
small coefficient perturbations, NOT prior origin convergence.
Consequently a high-coordinate tail staying in this neighborhood has
|X_h,t|<=C*q^t. Stable raw moment and variance recursions then imply
M_h,V_h->0 as well. Thus both coordinates actually approach their origins.

If the standard low initial position is nonzero,025 gives a subsequence
of active sharpness tending to lambda_l<=L1<38. This is incompatible
with an eventual band delta<(38-L1)/2. We may remove the line x_l,0=0
as a null exceptional set; no assertion on that line is needed here.
Thus the origin alternative is excluded for almost every start.

For clarity, the low-coordinate lower-rate estimate can be chosen
uniformly too: the explicit matrix Q in036 Eq10 is positive definite
for fixed nu<b and every low trace T with |T|<=1+b. It obeys
A_l^T Q A_l=nu^2 Q+A_l^T A_l. On compact low parameters its strict
gain margin is uniform, and actual coefficients approach A_l once
the low coordinate decays. This confirms the rate comparison across
the whole stated low interval, including repeated-root parameters.

5. THE CYCLE ALTERNATIVE HAS A NULL STANDARD-INITIALIZATION SET
If the actual high tail stays in the alternating cycle neighborhoods,
015v3's corrected local capture gives convergence to that scalar cycle.
Here rho<=1/H0<rho_star, and015v3 applies uniformly on this compact
range. For fixed eta and lambda_h, its standard initial positions
converging to this corrected cycle form a countable set. Thus full
initial positions reaching this alternative lie on countably many
vertical lines. Together with the removed low-zero line they have
Lebesgue measure zero. No product law or coordinate independence is
needed. Outside this exceptional set, the assumed strict limsup band
is impossible, proving(1).

Active quotients at finite zero-gradient times can be treated either
by the zero extension used in Section2 or by removing their null
initial lines. For fixed finite time, a nonzero scalar standard initial
position maps analytically to its position on either sign half-line:
positive raw variance after the first update makes all subsequent
square roots analytic. The bounded-increment properness estimate
prevents that analytic function from being identically zero. Its
zeros are countable. Hence the countable union of finite-time zero
events is null, and generic trajectories have all their quotients
defined. Along any specified countable eta sequence, union the null
exceptional sets; an absolutely continuous joint law still assigns
zero mass. This gives the stated simultaneous conclusion.

[Defi 24 of arXiv:2608.02103, '$p$-Adic Diffusion and Random Walks on $[0,1]$'] For a step function $w:[0,1] \times [0,1] \rightarrow [0,1]$ define the cut norm as
\[||w||_{\Box}=\sup_{S,T\subset \mathcal{M}([0,1])}\iint_{S\times T} w(x,y)dxdy,\]
Where $\mathcal{M}([0,1])$ denotes the measurable sets of $[0,1]$. The following relations with the $L^{p},L^2$ and $L^{\infty}$norm holds true
\[||w||_{\Box}\leq||w||_{1}\leq||w||_{2}\leq||w||_{\infty} \]
The cut metric is then defined as 
\[\delta_{\Box}(w,u)=\inf_{\phi\in\mathcal{L}}||u(\phi(x),\phi(y))-w(x,y)||_{\Box}\]
where, $\mathcal{L}$ is the space of Lebesgue measurable bijections on the unit interval.

[Theorem thm: quadratic interaction random of arXiv:2503.24372, 'A criterion on the free energy for log-Sobolev inequalities in mean-field particle systems'] Let $V(x)=\frac{x^4}{4}-\lambda \frac{x^2}{2}$ ($\lambda\in\R$) or more generally suppose that $V$ satisfies Assumption~(ass_doublewell of the paper). 
Let $T_c$ denote the critical temperature (equation eq_def_beta_c of the paper) of the fully connected mean-field-model $m^{N}_T$ with $W (x,y) = - x y$. 
Let $\bbP_N$ be the uniform measure on random regular graphs $G_N$ in $\{1, \dots , N\}$ with fixed degree $d_N$ at each site or the measure of Erd\"os-R\'enyi graphs with mean degree $d_N$.

Assume either that $\lim_{N\to\infty} d_N=\infty$ in the random regular graph case, 
or that $\lim_{N\to\infty} d_N/\log N= \infty$ in the Erd\"os-R\'enyi case.
Then:

\begin{itemize}
	\item[(i)]
For $T>T_c$, there is a constant $\gamma_T>0$ such that
\begin{align}

\lim_{N \to \infty} \bbP_N \big[  \gamma^{G_N}_{\mathrm{LS}}(T) \geq  \gamma_T \big] = 1.
\end{align}

	\item[(ii)] For $T<T_c$, there is a sequence $(\delta_N)$ converging to 0 such that: 
\begin{align}

\lim_{N \to \infty} \bbP_N \big[  \gamma^{G_N}_{\mathrm{LS}}(T) \leq  \delta_N \big] = 1.
\end{align}

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2605.30560, 'Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport'] A map $F:\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)\to\mathbb{R}$ admits a
\emph{linear functional derivative} $\delta_m F$ if
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)]
    \item $\delta_m F:\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous, and for every $R>0$ there exists $C_R>0$ such that whenever $\int |x|^2 \, \rho(dx) \leq R$
    \begin{align*}
       | \delta_m F(\rho, y)| \leq C_R(1+|y|^2).
    \end{align*}
\item  It satisfies the normalization $\int\delta_m F(\rho)(y)\rho(dy)=0$, \, $\forall \, \rho \in \Pc_2(\R^d)$. 
\item For any $\rho,\rho' \in \Pc(\R^d)$, it holds that
\[
F(\rho')-F(\rho)
\;=\;
\int_0^1\!\!\int \delta_m F\big((1-t)\rho+t\rho'\big)(y)\,(\rho'-\rho)(dy)\,dt.
\]
\end{enumerate}
