[Corollary cor:lattice-transfer of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $G$ be any nontrivial torsion-free abelian group.  For all $h,k\geq1$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_G(h,k)=\mathcal R(h,k).
\end{equation}
Consequently the spectrum-only conclusions
(equation eq:endpoint-local of the paper), (equation eq:ambient-exponent of the paper), and
(equation eq:localmain of the paper), together with the four-point positive-density
conclusion, hold with $\mathcal R$ replaced by $\mathcal R_G$.  The diameter-filtered
integer-witness assertion (equation eq:quantmain of the paper) is not asserted for an
abstract group $G$.  In particular,
$|\mathcal R_G(h,k)|=h^{k-1+o_k(1)}$ for every fixed $k\geq4$, and
$|\mathcal R_G(h,4)|=\Theta(h^3)$ with positive lower density.

Let f_n, g_n, g be measurable with |f_n| <= g_n almost everywhere, f_n -> f a.e., g_n -> g a.e., every g_n and g in L^1(mu), and integral g_n dmu -> integral g dmu. Then f is in L^1, integral |f_n - f| dmu -> 0, and in particular integral f_n dmu -> integral f dmu. The classical dominated convergence theorem is the case g_n = g constant in n. The hypothesis that the integrals of the dominators CONVERGE (not merely that the dominators converge pointwise) is essential: with g_n = 1_{[n,n+1]} on R one has g_n -> 0 = g pointwise, but integral g_n = 1 does not converge to integral g = 0, and taking f_n = g_n shows the conclusion fails. [Pratt (1960), 'On interchanging limits and integrals', Ann. Math. Statist. 31, 74-77]

[Definition def:restriction-to-a-subset of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] \mbox{}\\
  Let $(X_n,T_n)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$ be a continuous-time jump process on $G$.
  Recursively, we take $\sigma_0:=0$ and for $n\in{\mathbb N}$, on the event
  $\{\sigma_{n-1}<\infty\}$, we define 
  $\sigma_n:=\inf\{l>\sigma_{n-1}:X_l\neq X_{\sigma_{n-1}}\}$ to be the index
  of the next jump to a different location. 
  The process with self-loops removed is defined by 
  $(X^{\neq},T^{\neq})=(X^{\neq}_n,T^{\neq}_n)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}:=(X_{\sigma_n},\sum_{l=\sigma_n}^{\sigma_{n+1}-1}T_l)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$
  on the event $\{\sigma_n<\infty\text{ for all }n\in{\mathbb N}\}$. 

  Let $\emptyset\neq J\subseteq\Lambda$. We set recursively $\tau_0=0$, 
  $\tau_n=\inf\{ l>\tau_{n-1}: X_l\in J\}$
  for $n\in{\mathbb N}$. In other words, on the event $\{X_0\in J\}$, 
  $\tau_n$ denotes the number of jumps up to the $n$-th return to $J$. 
  The restriction of the process to $J$ is defined
  on the event $\{\tau_n<\infty\text{ for all }n\in{\mathbb N}\}$ by
  $(X^J,T^J)=(X_n^J,T_n^J)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}:=(X_{\tau_n},T_{\tau_n})_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$.

  The notation $(X^{J\neq},T^{J\neq})$ means that both operations have
  been applied to the process $(X,T)$, first the restriction to $J$ and
  then self-loop removal.

For probability measures P and Q on one space, TV(P, Q) = sup_A |P(A) - Q(A)| and D = D(P || Q) is the Kullback-Leibler divergence in nats (+infinity unless P << Q). Then TV(P, Q) <= min(sqrt(D/2), sqrt(1 - exp(-D))). The two bounds cross at the unique positive root D* = 1.59362426004004... of D/2 = 1 - exp(-D): Pinsker's bound is the smaller for 0 < D < D* and the Bretagnolle-Huber bound for D > D*.
P and Q are probability measures on one measurable space

[Theorem 5 (Euclidean shell trichotomy) of arXiv:2609.02362, '\textbf{Farthest-cell triplet entropy: high-dimensional shell limits and hyperbolic curvat'] Under the preceding assumptions:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item if $\lambda_d\to0$, then
  \[
    H_3(P_d,d_{\mathrm{Euc}})\longrightarrow\log 3;
  \]

  \item if $\lambda_d\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, then
  \[
    H_3(P_d,d_{\mathrm{Euc}})
    \longrightarrow
    H_\infty(\lambda;F);
  \]

  \item if $\lambda_d\to\infty$ and $F$ is continuous, then
  \[
    H_3(P_d,d_{\mathrm{Euc}})\longrightarrow0.
  \]
\end{enumerate}

Every coordinate i is covered at least k times by S_1, ..., S_m

[Proposition prop:finite-time-concentration-scale of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Assume that $(\zeta(z))_{z\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ are i.i.d. For each $x$ and
		$t$, the map $\zeta\mapsto u_t(x)$ is convex and satisfies
		\[
			|u_t(x;\zeta)-u_t(x;\eta)|
			\leq
			\left(\sum_{z\in\mathbb{Z}^d}g_t(x,z)^2\right)^{1/2}
			\|\zeta-\eta\|_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)}\, .
		\]
		For every $p\geq2$ with $\mathbb{E}|\zeta(0)|^p<\infty$ there is
		$C=C(p,\mathcal L(\zeta(0)))<\infty$ such that
		\[
			\mathbb{E}\bigl|u_t(x)-\mathbb{E} u_t(x)\bigr|^p
			\leq C \Var(V_t(0))^{p/2}\, .
		\]
		In particular, if $\Var(\zeta(0))<\infty$, then
		$\Var(u_t(x))\leq C\Var(V_t(0))$.
		If $0<\Var(\zeta(0))<\infty$, then, for every $m,n\geq0$ and
		$x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^d$,
		\begin{equation}
			0\leq\Cov(u_n(x),u_m(y))
			\leq
			2\Var(\zeta(0))
			\sum_{z\in\mathbb{Z}^d}g_n(x,z)g_m(y,z)\, .
		\end{equation}

[Proposition prop:uniform-ranges of arXiv:2609.02544, 'A finiteness theorem for geodesic Leech wheels'] In a geodesic Leech wheel $W_{m+1}$ with $h$ large spokes, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If $h=0$, then $m\le39$, that is, $n\le40$.
\item If $h=1$, then $m\le40$, that is, $n\le41$.
\item If $h=2$, then $m\le41$, that is, $n\le42$.
\end{enumerate}

body: [Lemma lemma cv CLE in the rectangles of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] On the event that there is a loop of $\Gamma$ crossing $A_{s,t}(z)$ and that there are $k\ge 1$ conformal rectangles $R_1, \ldots, R_k$, for all $j \in [1, k]_\BZ$, let $\Gamma'_{R^n_j}$ be the non-nested $\CLE_{\kappa'}$ associated with the $\cwBCLE_{\kappa^\prime}(0)$/$\ccwBCLE_\kappa(-\kappa/2)$ iteration construction (see~(A025 of the paper)) in the connected component of the unexplored region $R^n_j$ containing $R_j$. For all $x\in R_j \cap \BQ^2$, consider the loop $\SCL_j^n(x)$ of $\Gamma'_{R^n_j}$ surrounding $x$. Then, for all simply connected open subset $U \subset R_j$ such that $\overline{U} \subset R_j$ there exists a sequence $(U_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of simply connected open subsets such that $\overline{U_n} \to \overline{U}$ a.s.\@ in the Hausdorff topology, $U_n \to U$ a.s.\@ in the Carathéodory sense, and such that the conditional laws given $R^n_j$ of the $\overline{U_n}\cap \SCL^n_j(x)$'s for $x\in R_j \cap \BQ^2$ converge a.s.\ weakly, in the Hausdorff topology, to the conditional law given $R_j$ of the $\overline{U} \cap \SCL_j(x)$'s for $x \in R_j \cap \BQ^2$, where the $\SCL_j(x)$'s are the loops of a $\CLE_{\kappa'}$ in $R_j$.

[Proposition 40 of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] Let $h^\rmS$ be the field as above and $\theta\in \bbR$ such that $\lambda'-\chi\pi+\theta\chi\in(-\lambda,\lambda)$. Let $x\in\bbR$. There exists a unique coupling between $(h^\rmS,\eta)$ where $\eta$ is a curve starting from $x$,  and stopped until either hitting $\bbR+i\tau$ or one of its translates $\eta+k$ where $k\in\bbZ$, such that the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item For each stopping time $\sigma$ of $\eta$ before its duration, $\eta([0,\sigma])$ is a local set of $h^\rmS$, in the sense that the conditional law of $h^\rmS$ given $\eta|_{[0,\sigma]}$ has the following description. Let $\cS_{\eta,\sigma} = \cS_\tau\backslash \cup_{k\in\bbZ}(k+\eta([0,\sigma]))$, and $\cA_{\eta,\sigma}$ be the annulus such that there is a conformal map $\varphi_{\eta,\sigma}$ with $\cA_{\eta,\sigma} = p\circ\varphi_{\eta,\sigma}\circ \cS_{\eta,\sigma}$. Let $\mathfrak{h}_{\eta,\sigma}$ be the harmonic function on $\cS_{\eta,\sigma}$ whose boundary values agrees with $h^\rmS$ on $\partial\cS_\tau$ and is given by the flow line boundary conditions on $ \cup_{k\in\bbZ}(k+\eta([0,\sigma]))$ as in Figure~\ref{fig: flow line boundary data} and~\cite[Figure 1.10]{ImagGeo1}. Then $h^\rmS|_{\cS_{\eta,\sigma}} =  {h}_{\eta,\sigma}\circ p\circ \varphi_{\eta,\sigma} + \mathfrak{h}_{\eta,\sigma}$, where ${h}_{\eta,\sigma}$ is a zero boundary GFF in $\cA_{\eta,\sigma}$ independent from $\mathfrak{h}_{\eta,\sigma}$.
        \item The curve $\eta$ is measurable with respect to $h^\rmS$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[1 14 of arXiv:2607.12303, 'Marginal Stationary Distributions and Convergence Rates of Higher Order Markov Chains'] Suppose that the transition tensor ${\cal P}$ of  an $(m-1)$th order Markov chain $\{X_t\}_{t=1}^{\infty}$ on state space
$S$ is positive, that is, ${\cal P}>0$. Let $Q$ be the transition matrix of its reduced first order chain.  Then the $(m-1)$th power of $Q$ is a positive matrix,  that is,  
$$
Q^{m-1} >0.
$$
This implies that $Q$ itself is regular. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 6 of arXiv:2607.06242, 'Exponential mixing and Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for Markov cocycles'] Let $(\Sigma,\theta,m)$ be an ergodic measure preserving dynamical system. Suppose that $A,F>0$ are measurable, $\log A\in L^1, \log^+F\in L^1$, and 
      \[\int_\Sigma \log A(\s)m(d\s)<\log q\]
      for some $q\in(0,1)$. Then
      \[N(\sigma):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q^{-(n+1)}
      F(\theta^n\sigma)\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}A(\theta^j\sigma)\]
      is finite for \(m\)-a.e. $\sigma$ and satisfies
      \[qN(\sigma)=F(\sigma)+A(\sigma)N(\theta\sigma).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 6 of arXiv:2607.06242

Method: Likelihood-ratio strategy and its exact missing input Result: For product Bernoulli measures with different parameters, the strong law gives disjoint full-measure sets of limiting digit frequencies and hence mutual singularity. A possible analogous strategy for the two Cantor measures is a likelihood-ratio martingale along a common binary coding, with cumulative conditional relative entropy forcing its limit to vanish. Check: Merely proving that two measures are unequal is insufficient: two different positive bounded densities relative to the same measure are still equivalent. The binary digits of Cantor-Lebesgue measure are not assumed iid. Obstruction: No divergent conditional-entropy estimate or martingale tail control was established for the actual harmonic measure versus base-three Cantor measure.

OWNER OWN WORK, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C006 v1. Standard-conditioning specialization for the Target 3 obstruction; neither novelty nor escape is asserted. Let d>=3, m>=1, eta>0, A have iid real N(0,1) entries, x_* a deterministic unit signal, and independently x0~N(0,I_d/d). For f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2 run unmodified GD. Put e1=x_*, q0=<e1,x0>, rho0=||x0-q0*e1||, e2=(x0-q0*e1)/rho0, E an orthonormal basis of their perpendicular space, g=A*e1, h=A*e2, B=A*E, zt=A*xt, vt=zt*(zt^2-g^2) coordinatewise, qt=<e1,xt>, pt=<e2,xt>. Excluding null events rho0*||v0||*||B^T v0||=0, define u=v0/||v0||, P=I-u*u^T, w=B^T*u, W=||w||^2, Q=I-w*w^T/W, b=B*w, r=P*b, a=P*v1, L=||a||^2, nu=Q*B^T*v1, gamma=eta*||v0||/m, kappa=-gamma-(eta/m)*(u^T*v1+r^T*v1/W). Observe in order w, then b (equivalently z1), then nu. Let F2=sigma(x0,g,h,w,b), F3=sigma(F2,nu). Conditional on F2, nu has Gaussian law with covariance L*Q. If L>0, B|F3 has mean M3=u*w^T+r*w^T/W+a*nu^T/L and residual law (P-a*a^T/L)*Z*Q for a fresh standard Gaussian matrix Z. Consequently z2|F3 is Gaussian with mean q2*g+p2*h+kappa*b-eta*||nu||^2*a/(m*L) and covariance (eta^2*||nu||^2/m^2)*(P-a*a^T/L). The conditional law of ||nu||^2/L given F2 is chi-square with d-3 degrees of freedom, including the point mass at zero for d=3. If L=0, nu=0 and z2=q2*g+p2*h+kappa*b is already F2-measurable. Thus the next response is in the adaptively chosen direction P*v1; it cannot be omitted merely by citing fresh Gaussian noise. Bounds on accumulated responses and initial-scale overlap fluctuations remain open.

independent N(0,I_d/d) start

causal observation order w then B*w then Q*B^T*v1
L=0 branch handled separately without division

[Proposition 65 (Sharp denominator growth) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For every $d\ge0$, the polynomials
$\gamma_0^{4_1},\ldots,\gamma_d^{4_1}$ form an $R$-basis of the $R$-module of
polynomials in $\Bbbk[Y]$ of degree at most $d$ that take values in $R$
at every node
$Y=Q^n$, $n\ge2$.  The leading coefficient of $\gamma_k^{4_1}(Y)$ is
\begin{equation}
 \frac{(-1)^kQ^{k(k-3)/2}}{(Q;Q)_k}.
\end{equation}
In particular, it has a pole of order $k$ along $Q=1$, so the
quantum-factorial denominator length is unbounded.

body: [Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.19065, 'Boundedly exchangeable graphs'] Let $I \coloneqq [0, \mu(S))$, with the convention $I = \rbb_+$ when $\mu(S) = \infty$. Then there is a Borel isomorphism $\phi : S \to I$ with $\phi\mu = \lambda\vert_I$, and for any such $\phi$, a random measure $\eta$ on $S^2$ is jointly $\mu$-exchangeable if and only if $(\phi \otimes \phi)\eta$ on $I^2$ is jointly $\lambda\vert_I$-exchangeable. A random variable $X: \Omega \to K$ taking values in a real separable Hilbert space $K$ is called Gaussian if for every $v \in K$, the real-valued random variable $\langle X, v \rangle_K$ is Gaussian. $X$ is centered if $\mathbb{E}[\langle X, v \rangle_K] = 0$ for all $v \in K$, and non-degenerate if $\operatorname{Var}(\langle X, v \rangle_K) > 0$ for every $v \neq 0$.
K is a real separable Hilbert space

[Proposition 12 (Consistency of the Lipschitz-case powers) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $p=\alpha-1\in(0,1)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \textup{Initial value perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=x_0+W_t+Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt x_0+W_t+Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=|x_0-\wt x_0|^p.
\]
Thus the initial error exponent $p=\alpha-1$ is exact.

\item \textup{Drift perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=bt,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt b t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=T^p|b-\wt b|^p.
\]
Since $B=T|b-\wt b|$, this is exactly $B^p$.

\item \textup{Brownian diffusion perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=aW_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt a W_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =m_p T^{p/2}|a-\wt a|^p,
\]
where $m_p=\E|N(0,1)|^p$. Since $A=T^{1/2}|a-\wt a|$, this is $m_p A^p$.

\item \textup{Stable jump coefficient perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=\sigma Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt\sigma Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =\E|Z_1|^p T^{p/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|^p.
\]
Since $S=T^{1/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|$, this is $\E|Z_1|^pS^p$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, when $\wt\eta=1$, the powers $|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}$, $B^{\alpha-1}$, $A^{\alpha-1}$ and $S^{\alpha-1}$ agree with the exact scaling of the four elementary perturbation mechanisms.

[Prop 7 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] Assume $\mathbf X$ is isotropic, exchangeable, unconditional, with the component satisfying $\sup_{n} \E X_1^4 < \infty$. Assume in addition that $\nm{\mathbf X}_2$ and $\nm{\mathbf X}_4$ are both subexponential with uniformly bounded proxy variance $2\sigma^2$, i.e., for $k = 2,4$ and $ \lambda^2 \leq 1/\sigma^2$, \[
    \E\exp\bigl(\lambda (\nm{\mathbf X}_k - \E \nm{ \mathbf X}_k)\bigr) \leq \exp(\lambda^2 \sigma^2).
\] Then given $d = o(n^{1/3})$, we have $\ESD(K_{\PrincipalT}) \wkconv \mu_{\MP(c)}$ with probability $1$. 

    
    
    Assume furthermore that $\nm{\mathbf X}_4$ is sub-Gaussian with uniformly bounded proxy variance $2\sigma^2$, i.e., for all $\lambda \in \R$, \[
        \E\exp\bigl(\lambda (\nm{\mathbf X}_4 - \E \nm{ \mathbf X}_4)\bigr) \leq \exp(\lambda^2 \sigma^2).
    \] Then given $d = o(n^{1/2})$, we have $\ESD(K_{\PrincipalT}) \wkconv \mu_{\MP(c)}$ with probability $1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 7 of arXiv:2607.21759

body:
[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2607.20714, 'High Minima of Gaussian Processes: Overshoots and Minimizer Locations'] Let $B_H$ and $\nu_H$ be as in Example~\ref{ex:fbm}.  Then $\nu_H$ is
the unique optimal measure for the covariance-energy problem on $[a,b], 0< a<b<\infty$.
For $0<H<1/2$, its density $\rho_H$ satisfies
\[
 \inf_{a<t<b}\rho_H(t)>0,\qquad \supp(\nu_H)=[a,b],
\]
and its potential is constant and positive on $[a,b]$.
For every $H\in(0,1)$, the covariance kernel $R_H$ is integrally strictly
positive definite on $[a,b]$.

body: Zorn's lemma: if P is a NONEMPTY partially ordered set in which every chain - every totally ordered subset - has an upper bound in P, then P contains at least one maximal element. Over ZF it is equivalent to the axiom of choice and to the well-ordering theorem; it is the standard tool for existence proofs (maximal ideals, bases of vector spaces, Hahn-Banach).
title: Zorn's lemma

[Lemma lem:local of arXiv:2609.03448, 'Prime-power Diophantine tuples'] Assume that the triple is not regular.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $p$ is odd, then exactly one of $e,\bar e$ is divisible by $N^2$.
\item If $p=2$ and $r\ge3$, then
\[
 \{v_2(e),v_2(\bar e)\}=\{2,2r-2\}.
\]
In particular, exactly one of $e,\bar e$ is divisible by $N^2/4$.
\end{enumerate}

For fixed n>=2, deterministic initial coordinates x0!=0 and y0, and fixed nonnegative variances s1,s2 with s1+s2>0, consider the fresh-RR common-Hessian finite sum f_i(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa_T*y^2/2+b_i*x+c_i*y with zero-sum linear terms and mean squares s1,s2 fixed across horizons T=nK. Assume kappa_T>=1 and kappa_T*log(T)/T ->0. Set B_T=n(n+1)(s1+kappa_T^2*s2)/48 and H_T=log(T^3/B_T). Every globally optimal constant step obeys T*eta_T/H_T ->1/2 and the optimal last-epoch expected function error is asymptotic to B_T*H_T^3/(8T^3). The result holds over all eta>=0 or over 0<=eta<=c/kappa_T for any fixed c>0. It includes s2=0. If s2>0 and kappa_T=T^alpha, 0<alpha<1, the step constant relative to log T is (3-2alpha)/2 and optimal error is asymptotic to n(n+1)*s2*(3-2alpha)^3*T^(2alpha-3)*log(T)^3/384. This completes a growing-parameter regime of named target 1; no full-row solution or priority claim is made.
n and initialization fixed; x0!=0; s1,s2 fixed nonnegative and not both zero; zero-sum b_i,c_i; fresh independent uniform permutations; kappa deterministic with kappa*log(T)/T->0. Arbitrary fixed mu follows by scaling f_i/mu and eta to mu*eta, as detailed in the proof.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:37fd1a0dd3bb3ce8906a1b18ff7ab4f1feea3c48b2e9b04955068457a1a40c3a","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/37/37fd1a0dd3bb3ce8906a1b18ff7ab4f1feea3c48b2e9b04955068457a1a40c3a.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:caaee6df46f3d388da80bf8d4916699ff6a94b232cc8379ab905c0f2747f33e7","bundle_entry_key":"growing-kappa-common-hessian","bundle_id":"population.t362-growing-kappa-002","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"optimization; random reshuffling; condition number; tuned last iterate","draft":"w732/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.randomreshuffling:common-hessian-random-reshuffling-growing-condition-number-optimal-step","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Target 1 extension: the globally tuned step with a growing condition number

Status: proof draft, unaudited. This extends C001's fixed-kappa limit. The exact epoch recursion is settled ground and is not re-proved. No priority claim or full-row solution is asserted.

## Statement

Fix n>=2, deterministic x0!=0 and y0, and s1,s2>=0 with s1+s2>0. For each T=nK, let kappa=kappa_T>=1 and use the target-1 common-Hessian instance

    f_i(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa*y^2/2+b_i*x+c_i*y,
    sum b_i=sum c_i=0, mean b_i^2=s1, mean c_i^2=s2.

The vectors (b_i),(c_i), n and initialization remain fixed. Each epoch has a fresh independent uniform permutation, shared by the two coordinates. No independence between coordinate noises is assumed; the objective has no mixed quadratic term. Suppose

    kappa_T*log(T)/T -> 0.

Put C=n(n+1)/48, B_T=C*(s1+kappa_T^2*s2), and H_T=log(T^3/B_T). Then H_T->infinity. For EVERY global minimizer eta_T of the expected last-epoch objective over eta>=0,

    T*eta_T/H_T -> 1/2,
    min_eta E[F_T(X_K)-F_T*] ~ B_T*H_T^3/(8*T^3).                 (1)

The same result holds if steps are restricted to 0<=eta<=c/kappa_T for any fixed c>0. No uniqueness or unimodality of the optimizer is assumed. This includes noise only on the flat coordinate (s2=0), the literal b_i-only construction in the target, as well as noise on the stiff coordinate.

For s2>0 and kappa_T=T^alpha, 0<alpha<1, (1) becomes

    min error ~ [n(n+1)*s2*(3-2alpha)^3/384]
                  *T^(2alpha-3)*log(T)^3,
    T*eta_T/log T -> (3-2alpha)/2.                              (2)

Thus replacing a fixed kappa by a growing kappa inside C001 while keeping its 3/2 step constant would be incorrect when the stiff-coordinate variance dominates.

## A uniform finite-n variance sandwich

For a coordinate of curvature h>0 and optimum variance s>=0, write a=1-h*eta. The settled recursion gives

    V_h = s/(n-1) * sum_{0<=i<j<n}(a^i-a^j)^2,
    B_h(eta) = (h/2)*eta^2*V_h/(1-a^(2n)),

where B_h is the stationary contribution to the expected objective. If 0<q=h*eta<1, then

    [s*h^2*n(n+1)/48]*eta^3*(1-q)^(2n-4)
       <= B_h(eta)
       <= [s*h^2*n(n+1)/48]*eta^3*(1-q)^(-(2n-1)).             (3)

Proof of (3). Set m=j-i. The identity

    a^i-a^j = q*a^i*sum_{r=0}^{m-1}a^r

lies between m*q*a^(j-1) and m*q. Since j-1<=n-2 and 0<a<1, it therefore lies between m*q*a^(n-2) and m*q. Square and sum; use sum_{i<j}(j-i)^2=n^2(n^2-1)/12. Also

    2n*q*a^(2n-1) <= 1-a^(2n) <= 2n*q.

All denominators are positive. Substituting the lower numerator and upper denominator gives the lower bound in (3); the opposite choices give the upper bound. The case s=0 is identically zero and requires no division by s. The exponent 2n-4 is nonnegative even at n=2.

For the two coordinates, whenever q=kappa*eta<1, summing (3) gives

    B_T*eta^3*(1-q)^(2n-4) <= B_1(eta)+B_kappa(eta)
       <= B_T*eta^3*(1-q)^(-(2n-1)).                           (4)

This uses 1-h*eta>=1-q and nonnegative coefficients; it remains valid when kappa=1, counting both coordinates. The actual finite-horizon variance is the sum of B_h(eta)*(1-(1-h*eta)^(2T)). In this range it is between (1-(1-eta)^(2T)) times the left side of (4) and the right side of (4).

## Global optimization proof

1. There are constants b0,b1>0, depending only on n,s1,s2, such that b0<=B_T<=b1*kappa^2. The assumption kappa*log T/T->0 implies eventually kappa<=T/log T. Hence

       log T + 2log log T - log b1 <= H_T <= 3log T - log b0.

   In particular H_T->infinity, H_T=O(log T), and kappa*H_T/T->0.

2. Use the candidate eta_c=H_T/(2T). Its q_c=kappa*eta_c tends to zero, so (4) applies. The deterministic contribution of the flat coordinate is at most x0^2*exp(-H_T)/2. That of the stiff coordinate is at most kappa*y0^2*exp(-kappa*H_T)/2. For H>=1 and kappa>=1,

       log kappa <= kappa-1 <= (kappa-1)*H,
       kappa*exp(-kappa*H)<=exp(-H).

   Thus the entire deterministic contribution is O(exp(-H_T)), with a constant independent of kappa. Since exp(-H_T)=B_T/T^3, and H_T->infinity, it is negligible relative to B_T*H_T^3/T^3. Equation (4) gives

       inf_eta P_T(eta) <= (1+o(1))*B_T*H_T^3/(8T^3).          (5)

   This tends to zero: B_T<=b1*kappa^2 and kappa*H_T/T->0 imply B_T*H_T^3/T^3 <= b1*(kappa*H_T/T)^2*(H_T/T)->0.

3. Existence of a minimizer holds because the exact error is a continuous coercive polynomial. In any noisy coordinate, the pair (i,j)=(0,1) alone and the final epoch alone give, for ALL eta>=0,

       P_T(eta) >= s*h^3*eta^4/[2(n-1)].                     (6)

   No step-size restriction is used in (6): the geometric variance multiplier is a sum of even powers and is at least one.

4. First suppose s2>0. With q_T=kappa*eta_T, (6) and (5) imply

       q_T^4 <= [2(n-1)/s2]*kappa*P_T(eta_T)
              <= O(kappa*B_T*H_T^3/T^3)
              <= O((kappa*H_T/T)^3) ->0.

   Thus q_T->0 and eta_T->0. If t_T=T*eta_T were bounded along a subsequence, then

       (1-eta_T)^(2T)=exp(-2t_T+O(T*eta_T^2))

   would stay bounded away from zero there. The flat deterministic contribution x0^2/2 times this quantity contradicts the vanishing optimum. Therefore t_T->infinity.

5. If s2=0 instead, s1>0 and B_T=C*s1 is constant. Using h=1 in (6) first gives eta_T->0. The same flat transient argument gives t_T->infinity. For the NOISY FLAT coordinate, (3) with q=eta_T, together with 1-(1-eta_T)^(2T)->1, yields

       P_T(eta_T)>=(1-o(1))*B_T*eta_T^3.

   Combining with (5) gives t_T=O(H_T), hence q_T=kappa*t_T/T->0 by step 1. This argument does not presuppose small q_T for the stiff coordinate.

6. Now in either case q_T->0 and t_T->infinity. The finite-horizon sandwich following (4) gives

       total variance = (1+o(1))*B_T*t_T^3/T^3.               (7)

   Its error is uniform along ANY sequence of minimizers: the factors in (4) depend only on q_T and fixed n, and the finite-horizon factor is at least 1-exp(-2t_T)->1. From (5) and (7), t_T=O(H_T). Thus T*eta_T^2=O(H_T^2/T)->0, and the flat transient equals

       A*exp(-2t_T+o(1)), A=x0^2/2>0.

   Comparing it with (5), and using B_T/T^3=exp(-H_T), gives

       2t_T >= H_T-3log H_T-O(1).

   Hence liminf t_T/H_T>=1/2. Equations (5) and (7) give limsup t_T/H_T<=1/2. Substitution into (7) and comparison with the candidate upper bound prove (1).

7. For the capped interval eta<=c/kappa, the candidate is eventually admissible since kappa*eta_c->0. Coercivity is replaced by compactness, and all lower bounds remain valid, so the same proof gives (1). Formula (2) follows from B_T~n(n+1)*s2*T^(2alpha)/48 and H_T~(3-2alpha)log T.

## Returning to an arbitrary fixed mu>0

Apply the theorem to f_i/mu with curvatures 1,kappa=L/mu, variances s1/mu^2,s2/mu^2, and normalized step mu*eta. Then

    B'_T=n(n+1)*(s1+kappa^2*s2)/(48mu^2),
    H'_T=log(T^3/B'_T),
    mu*T*eta_T/H'_T ->1/2,
    min original error ~ n(n+1)*(s1+kappa^2*s2)*(H'_T)^3/(384mu*T^3).

Here mu, n, s1, s2 and the initial point are fixed; only kappa grows. No assertion is made when kappa*log T/T fails to tend to zero, when n grows, or when x0=0. body: Let X_1..X_4 be independent with densities at most 1, S_1 = X_1 + X_2, S_2 = X_3 + X_4, and let u, v be the orthonormal pair (1,1,1,1)/2, (1,1,-1,-1)/2 rotated by the angle theta with tan theta = sqrt 2, so that every coordinate has u_i^2 + v_i^2 = 1/2. Then U = <u, X>, V = <v, X> are linear combinations of the independent S_1, S_2 with determinant -1/2, and the pair argument (condition on nothing; the two quadratic curves along the parabola have separated critical points) bounds the density of U + cV^2 by 8 for every real c and all laws. For comb laws (each X_i uniform on N teeth [j, j + 1/N]) the maximal functional M_2 = int sup_u rho_{U,V}(u, v) dv grows linearly in N, because the coefficient ratio of V is the quadratic irrational (1 + sqrt 2)^2 and the lines V = v meet a bump of height at least 1/18 for a set of v of measure of order N. Consequence for the bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture: the leverage (spread) condition does not make maximal functionals bounded, so the curved-slice statements (CS), (VD), (P2) must use the curvature of the section.

[Prop dimension-free-identity of arXiv:2608.30847, 'An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions'] Assume that $u$ is smooth and $Du\neq 0$ in an annulus containing
$\partial B_r(x_0)$. Then
$$
  D'(r)=\frac{n-p}{r}D(r)+pG(r),
$$
and
$$
   H'(r) = \frac{n-1}{r}H(r)+2D(r)+K(r).
$$
Consequently, at every such radius for which $H(r)>0$,
$$
  N_\ast'(r)+N_\ast(r)\Theta(r)  =  \frac{pr}{H(r)}
 \int_{\partial B_r(x_0)}  A \left(  \partial_\nu u-\frac{N_\ast(r)}{r}v \right)^2   \,dS .
$$
In particular,
$$
  N_\ast'(r)+N_\ast(r)\Theta(r)\ge 0.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For independent bond percolation on the infinite d-regular tree with d>=3, p_c=1/(d-1), theta(p)=0 for p<=p_c, and theta(p)=[2d(d-1)/(d-2)](p-p_c)+O((p-p_c)^2) as p decreases to p_c from above. The positive descendant-survival solution u obeys 1-u=(1-pu)^(d-1); division by u and the implicit-function theorem give the expansion, and theta=1-(1-pu)^d. This is an exact tree analogue, not a high-dimensional lattice solution.

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.22636, 'Q-Learning with Stable Infinite-Dimensional \\Linear Function Approximation'] Fix real numbers $\alpha\ge 1$ and $T>0$, and integers $n\ge0$ and $n_0>0$.  Set $\alpha_k=\alpha/(k+n_0)$,
$\tau(n,m)=\sum_{k=n}^{m-1}\alpha_{k+1}$, and
$\cW(n,T)=\setcond{m\ge n}{\tau(n,m)\le T}$.  Then, for every $m\in\cW(n,T)$,
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0+1
        \le
        e^{T/\alpha}(n+n_0+1).
        
\end{equation}

If $m_\vee=\max\cW(n,T)$ and $\alpha_{n+1}\le T/2$, then the end time satisfies
\begin{equation}
        \frac{T}{2}
        \le
        \tau(n,m_\vee)
        \le
        T.
        
\end{equation}

If either $T=1/4$ and $n+n_0\ge8$, or
$T=1/5$ and $n+n_0\ge10$, then
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0
        \le
        \frac32(n+n_0),
        \quad \forall m\in\cW(n,T).
        
\end{equation}

body:
Let f be a smooth convex transpose-invariant real matrix loss, with sufficient differentiability for the local flow theorem (C-infinity suffices), and suppose its PSD flow Phi satisfies Wprime=-W grad f(W)-grad f(W) W and is defined at all real times. Let Wbar be a critical point, a local minimum of f on PSD matrices of rank at most r, r>=1, but not a global PSD minimum. Write the eigenvalues of -grad f(Wbar) as mu1>=mu2>=... and assume mu1>mu2 (then mu1>0); let v1 be a unit top eigenvector. For PSD initial matrices Walpha suppose arrival times Talpha give Ealpha=Phi(Walpha,Talpha)->Wbar and liminf (v1^T Ealpha v1)/||Ealpha-Wbar||_F>0. Then, for each fixed real t, Phi(Walpha,Talpha+log(1/(v1^T Ealpha v1))/(2mu1)+t) converges to the canonical escape orbit WG(t)=lim_(epsilon down to 0) Phi(Wbar+epsilon v1 v1^T,log(1/epsilon)/(2mu1)+t). This limit solves the same flow and has rank at most r+1. The statement does not assert that alignment follows from a Gaussian initialization, nor that the canonical orbit ends at a rank-(r+1) local minimum. Source: arXiv:2012.09839, Theorem G.2, PDF p.33; global-flow convention in Section 3, p.3; genericity limitations in Appendix H, pp.34-35.
Smooth convex transpose-invariant loss; C-infinity suffices for differentiability
PSD flow is complete in real time, as in the source setup
Rank-r constrained local minimum that is not a global PSD minimum
Simple positive top eigenvalue of -grad f(Wbar)
Quantitative relative Gram alignment at arrival, not merely a nonzero projection

[Theorem thm:PoissonApproximation2 of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Assume that $\mu$ is critical and belongs to the domain of
attraction of an $\alpha$-stable law for some $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Let $(G_k)$
be a sequence of $\{0,1\}$-valued functions on finite plane trees,  let
$(k_n)$ be a sequence of integers and let $(M_n)$ be a cutoff sequence. Set
$$
  \pi_n=\P(G_{k_n}(\mathcal T)=1).
$$
Let $B\subset\mathbb Z_+$ be such that
$$
  c_B
  =
  \mathbb{E}\left[
    k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)
    \mathbbm{1}_{\{k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)\in B\}}
  \right]
  \in(0,\infty).
$$
Define
$$
  \widehat{G}_k(T)
  =
  \mathbbm{1}_{\{k_\varnothing(T)\in B\}}
  \mathbbm{1}_{\{\exists u\in\Gamma_\varnothing(T):G_k(T_u)=1\}}.
$$
Assume that $(G_k)$ satisfies Assumption
(hyp:S of the paper) along $(k_n)$ with respect to $(M_n)$, and that
$(\widehat G_k)$ satisfies Assumption (hyp:C of the paper) along $(k_n)$ with respect
to the same cutoff sequence $(M_n)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If $(n\pi_n)$ is bounded, then
$
  d_{\mathrm{TV}} \big(
    \#\{u\in\mathcal T^n:\widehat{G}_{k_n}(\mathcal T^n_u)=1\},
    \mathrm{Poisson}(c_B n\pi_n)
  \big)
  \to 0$.
\item[(ii)] If $n\pi_n\to\infty$, then
$
{
\#\{u\in\mathcal T^n:
\widehat G_{k_n}(\mathcal T^n_u)=1\}
}
\to \infty$ in probability.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm intro1 of arXiv:2509.08659, 'Gap metrics for stationary point processes and quantitative convexity of the free energy'] Let $\mathsf{P}_0,\mathsf{P}_1$ be the laws of two stationary point processes with unit intensity and $\mathcal F_\beta(\mathsf{P}_i)<\infty$ for $i=0,1.$ Then, there is an interpolation $(\mathsf{P}_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ between $\mathsf{P}_0$ and $\mathsf{P}_1$ and a coupling $ \mathsf{Q}^0$ between the Palm measures of $\mathsf{P}_0$ and $\mathsf{P}_1$ such that 
\begin{align}  
    \mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}_{t})\leq  (1-t)\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}_{0})+t\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}_{1})-\frac{(1-t)t\beta}{2}\int \sum_{(0,0)\neq (x,y)\in \bar\xi} (x-y)^2\inf_{z\in [x,y]}f(\left\lvertz\right\rvert) \mathsf{Q}^0(d\bar\xi),
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm intro1 of arXiv:2509.08659

body:
[Ppn 256 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In both the spherical and Ising settings, there exists $c>0$ and $C = C(\alpha) > 0$ such that the following holds.
    Let $\cA^\circ$ be a $L$-Lipschitz algorithm with $L\ge 1$.
    Let $\chi^\circ \equiv \chi_{\cA^\circ}$ and $q_0 \equiv \chi^\circ(0)$, and suppose $q_0 < 1$.
    Then, there exists an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA$ such that the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item $\chi \equiv \chi_{\cA}$ satisfies $\chi(0) = q_0$ and
    \[
        \chi'(0) \ge  \frac1{L^2}\,.
    \]
In fact, we can take
    \[
        \chi(p) = \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p)+ \frac{q_0 + (1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\item 
The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ approximates the original algorithm $\cA^\circ$ in the sense that
    \[
        \frac{1}{N} \E\Big[\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\|^2\Big]
        \le \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\end{enumerate}
We remark that the above error should be considered small, since we will prove later in Lemma~\ref{l:sM.Lip.1.trivial} that a sequence of algorithms with $q_0$ tending to one can only achieve the gaussian distribution.

\begin{proof} 
Let $\dot{\bg}$ be a standard gaussian in $\bbR^N$ independent of $\bg^{\aux}$, and
let $\bv$ be a deterministic element of $S_N$ with 
 $(\bv,\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})) = 0$. The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ is defined by
    \[\cA(\bG, (\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) 
        = \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}
            \bigg\}^{1/2}
        \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) 
        + \bigg(\frac{q_0}{1-q_0}\bigg)^{1/2} \frac{\bv}{L}
        + \frac{\dot{\bg}}{L} \,.
    \]
Then the gradient of $\cA$ can be bounded as
    \begin{align*}
        \|\nabla\cA
            (\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg})) \|^2
        &= \|\nabla_{\bG,\bg^{\aux}}
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) \|^2
        + \|\nabla_{\dot{\bg}} 
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg})) \|^2 \\
        &\le \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0) L^2}   \bigg\} L^2 
            + \frac1{L^2}
        \le L^2\,.
    \end{align*}
Since $\bv$ is deterministic and orthogonal to $\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$,
 $\dot{\bg}$ is independent of $(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$, and $\bbE[\|\dot{\bg}\|^2] = N$, we have
    \[\frac{\bbE[
             \|\cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg}))\|^2]}{N}
    =\bigg\{ 1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg\}
    	+\frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2}
	+\frac{1}{L^2}
    = 1\,,
    \]
where the last step follows from the trivial inequality $1-q_0\le1\le L^2$.  The above two displays show that $\cA$ is an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}. Moreover, recalling the abbreviations $\chi\equiv\chi_\cA$ and $\chi^\circ\equiv\chi_{\cA^\circ}$, for any $0\le p\le1$ we have
    \[\chi(p) 
    = \bigg(1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p) + \frac{q_0+(1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,,
    \]
which implies $\chi(0)=q_0$.
   As noted above, $\chi^\circ$ is nondecreasing, which implies $\chi'(0)\ge 1/L^2$. This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.CHI}. 

Next, since $|a^{1/2}-b^{1/2}| \le |a-b|^{1/2}$ for all $a,b\ge0$, we can bound
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{1}{N} \E\bigg[\Big\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\Big\|^2\bigg]
        &= \bigg(1 - \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg)^2
        + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2} \\
        &\le \frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2}
        = \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \end{align*}
This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.APPX}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:hypE of arXiv:2412.01381, 'Ergodicity and mixing for locally monotone stochastic evolution equations'] If $A=A_0+F$ where $A_0=-\partial \Phi$ is the subgradient of a lower semi-continuous convex functional $\Phi:V\to \mathbb{R}$ such that $\inf_{u\in V}\Phi(u)>-\infty$, and $F:V\to V^\ast$ is a strongly measurable (nonlinear) operator.
Suppose that
for some constants $\kappa_1\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$, $K_1\in\mathbb{R}$
that for every $u\in V$,
\begin{equation}\|F (u)\|_{V^\ast}\le \kappa_1\langle A_0 u,u\rangle+K_1.\end{equation}
Furthermore, suppose that for some constants $K_2,\kappa_2\in\mathbb{R}$, for every $u\in V$, 
\begin{equation}2\langle F(u),u\rangle\le\kappa_2\|F (u)\|_{V^\ast}+K_2,\end{equation}
or that
\begin{equation}2\langle F(u),u\rangle\le\kappa_2\langle A_0 u,u\rangle+K_2,\end{equation}
where, in the second case, we additionally assume that $\kappa_2\in (-2,\infty)$, whenever $\kappa_1<0$.
Then $A$ satisfies Hypothesis~(hyp:angle of the paper).
title: Lemma lem:hypE of arXiv:2412.01381

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): For u in U let Z_u record whether the residual L_u = A + B_u is active. For every activation pattern z in {0,1}^U, the optimal selector certificate satisfies |(A_n)_z| <= 2^{n+1-d-|z|}, d = ceil(n/3). Proof: on the a=1 half, z records the intersection of an independent set of C_n with U; a length-two gap has 2,1,1 completions and a length-three gap 3,2,1, according to the sum s+t of its endpoint states, both bounded by 2^{g-1-(s+t)/2} (g = gap edge-length). Multiplying over gaps gives 2^{n-d-|z|} completions; antipodality supplies the factor two. Summing the cells: |A_n|/2^{n+1} <= (3/4)^d, i.e. d <= ell(A_n)/log2(4/3). Notes: Solves the cycle in the stronger CELLWISE form needed for recursive entropy charging, not merely a class-count quotient. Exponents 2^{n+1-d-|z|}, 2^{g-1-(s+t)/2}, (3/4)^d reconstructed from flattened extraction; arithmetic re-verified (sum of (g-1) over gaps = n-d, sum of endpoint states = 2|z|).

body: [Lemma 100 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be a monoid and $g\colon K\to \mf A$ be a finite family. If $K = \varnothing$, then $\finsum g = 0$. If $k_0\in K$, then $\finsum g = g(k_0) + \finsum g|_{K\setminus\{k_0\}}$.

Let (X_{n, k})_{1 \le k \le r_n, n \ge 1} be a triangular array of row-wise independent random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_{n, k}] = 0 and \sigma_{n, k}^2 = \mathbb{E}[X_{n, k}^2] < \infty. Set s_n^2 = \sum_{k=1}^{r_n} \sigma_{n, k}^2. The array satisfies the Lindeberg condition if for every \epsilon > 0, \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{s_n^2} \sum_{k=1}^{r_n} \mathbb{E}\left[ X_{n, k}^2 \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_{n, k}| > \epsilon s_n\}} \right] = 0.
X_{n, k} row-wise independent, mean zero, finite variance

[Theo 10 of arXiv:2609.02261, 'Quantization and process'] Let   a function $F$ on   $\R^{2n}$ and  a bounded measure $\nu$ on  
    $\R^{2n}$  be such that   $F \star \nu$ belongs to 
  the space   $D_h (\R^{2n} )$  (see Definition \ref{Def-Dh}) and therefore has  a sesqui-holomorphic extension  $(F \star \nu)^{\rm ext}(X , Y) $.  Then, the 
  following equality is defining a bounded operator,
  
   \be  {\rm Op}_h^{\nu}(F) =  (2 \pi h)^{-2n}  \int _{\R^{4n} }  \Pi _{X h} 
   (F \star \nu)^{\rm ext}(Y, X)  \Pi _{Y h} dX  dY,\ee 
   
   where $ \Pi _{X h} $ is the orthogonal projection on the space spanned by the coherent space $ \Psi _{X h}$.  Moreover, we have for all $X\in\R^{2n}$,
    
 $$ < {\rm Op}_h ^{\nu} (F) \Psi _{X h},  \Psi _{X h} > =
  (F \star \nu) (X).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition prop:ASMs of arXiv:2609.03081, 'Non-attacking rook placements on crossword grids'] Suppose that $G$ is a sparse $n \times n$ crossword grid with no black squares on the edges.  Then there is a bijection between rook placements on $G$ and $n \times n$ alternating sign matrices with $-1$s whose positions are the same as the positions of the black squares in $G$.

body: Fix an effective enumeration phi_0, phi_1, phi_2, ... of all partial computable functions, so phi_e is the function computed by program number e. Kleene's recursion theorem states that for every total computable function f there exists an index e, a fixed point, such that phi_e equals phi_{f(e)}: program e computes exactly the function computed by the program obtained by applying f to e. This yields self-referential programs that can effectively obtain and use their own index or source code during execution, and underlies proofs of Rice's theorem and other diagonalization arguments. Proved by Stephen Kleene in 1938.
title: Kleene's recursion theorem

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let mu be a probability measure on a finite distributive lattice satisfying the FKG lattice condition mu(x v y) mu(x ^ y) >= mu(x) mu(y) for all x, y, a condition automatically satisfied by any product measure on {0,1}^E, in which case the conclusion is called the Harris inequality. Then for any two increasing (or two decreasing) functions f, g in L^2(mu), E[fg] >= E[f]E[g]; equivalently, for increasing events A, B, mu(A ^ B) >= mu(A) mu(B), so increasing events are positively correlated. This is the basic monotone-coupling tool throughout percolation and interacting particle systems, lower-bounding joint probabilities of increasing events, such as several disjoint crossings occurring together, by the product of their individual probabilities, and it justifies a wide range of comparison and sprinkling arguments. It does not give any upper bound on the correlation, which requires separate and generally harder tools such as the van den Berg-Kesten inequality for disjoint occurrence; it does not apply to a mix of an increasing and a decreasing event without flipping a sign; and the strength of the positive correlation is not quantified beyond nonnegativity. Typical failure: Applying FKG to a pair of events where one is increasing and the other decreasing without flipping the sign, which reverses the direction of the inequality; or invoking FKG for a non-product Gibbs measure, such as a random-cluster model outside the ferromagnetic regime with cluster weight q<1, without checking the lattice condition, which is known to fail there. Canonical reference: Fortuin, Kasteleyn and Ginibre, 1971, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Harris, 1960, Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society.
mu satisfies the FKG lattice condition, automatic for independent product measures but requiring verification for dependent Gibbs measures
f, g, or the events A, B, are both increasing, or both decreasing, with respect to the same partial order
the state space is finite or otherwise compactified so that all expectations involved are well defined
title: Technique: FKG (Harris) Inequality

Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and k ≥ 1 an integer. W^{k,p}(Ω) is the set of u ∈ L^p(Ω) all of whose distributional derivatives D^α u with |α| ≤ k lie in L^p(Ω): for each α there is g_α ∈ L^p(Ω) with ∫_Ω u D^α φ dx = (−1)^{|α|} ∫_Ω g_α φ dx for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω); one writes D^α u = g_α (the weak derivative, unique a.e.). The norm is ||u||_{W^{k,p}} = ( Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ||D^α u||_{L^p}^p )^{1/p} (maximum over α for p = ∞). W^{k,p}(Ω) is a Banach space, separable for p < ∞ and reflexive for 1 < p < ∞. H^k(Ω) := W^{k,2}(Ω) is a Hilbert space with ⟨u, v⟩ = Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ∫_Ω D^α u D^α v dx. W^{k,p}_0(Ω) is the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{k,p}(Ω) (functions 'vanishing on the boundary' together with derivatives of order < k); H^1_0(Ω) := W^{1,2}_0(Ω). The Sobolev conjugate of p < n is p* = np/(n − p), i.e. 1/p* = 1/p − 1/n.

Facts: C^∞(Ω) ∩ W^{k,p}(Ω) is dense in W^{k,p}(Ω) for p < ∞ and any open Ω (Meyers–Serrin); restrictions of C^∞(R^n) functions are dense when Ω is bounded with Lipschitz boundary; W^{k,p}_0(R^n) = W^{k,p}(R^n); for bounded Ω, W^{1,p}_0(Ω) is a proper closed subspace of W^{1,p}(Ω) (nonzero constants are excluded by the Poincaré inequality). On an interval, W^{1,p} functions have absolutely continuous representatives; in dimension n ≥ 2 a W^{1,p} function with p ≤ n can be unbounded and discontinuous. For a bounded Lipschitz domain, W^{1,∞}(Ω) is the space of Lipschitz functions on Ω̄.
Ω ⊂ R^n open; derivatives taken in the distributional sense
title: Sobolev spaces W^{k,p}(Ω), W^{k,p}_0(Ω), H^k(Ω)

body: In computational complexity theory, NP-complete problems are the hardest of the problems to which solutions can be verified quickly. Somewhat more precisely, a problem is NP-complete when:It is a decision problem, meaning that for any input to the problem, the output is either "yes" or "no". Each input to the problem is associated with a collection of short solutions, which might or might not validly solve the input. The output is "yes" when at least one of these solutions is valid, and "no" when none of them are. The validity of each solution can be verified quickly, and a brute-force search algorithm can find a valid solution by trying all possible solutions. The problem can be used to simulate every other problem for which we can verify quickly that a solution is valid. Hence, if we could find valid solutions of some NP-complete problem quickly, we could quickly find valid solutions for every other problem in which a given solution can be easily verified.
title: NP-completeness

For independent Exp(1) undirected bond FPP on Z^(m+1), fix integer C>=1 and positive integer sigma(n)<=2mn for n=1..C that lower-bounds the horizontal edge boundary of EVERY finite n-site subset of Z^m. On counts (a,b) in {1,..,C}^2 set r_a=1_{a<C} sigma(a), r_b=1_{b<C}(sigma(b)+max(a-b,0)), and front transition (a,b)->(b,1) at rate b. Let L be this finite generator. If a real alpha and a finite real bias h satisfy Lh(a,b)+1-alpha*b<=0 at EVERY state, then the Euclidean-normalised axis time constant satisfies mu_axis<=alpha. Front self-events at (1,1) carry one advance reward although their h increment is zero. This is a newly independently reviewed comparison, with literature priority unverified.
m>=1 integer; C>=1 finite
Boundary lower bound for arbitrary finite slab sets
Predictable uniform subset choices with independent auxiliary randomness
All-state bias inequality, self-front reward included
Usual exponential bond-FPP uniform shape theorem

[Lemma lem:orderSclosed of arXiv:2603.16824, 'Age-dependent random connection models with arc reciprocity: clustering and connectivity'] Assume \(\gamma\in[1/2,1)\) and consider \(S^c(t_o)\) as defined in~(equation eq:defSclosed of the paper). 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
	\item 
		If \(\Gamma>0\), we have
		\begin{equation*}
			\int\limits_{1/(t\log t)}^1 S^c(t_o)\,\mathrm{d} t_o
			=
			\begin{cases}
				O(1), & \gamma<2/3,
				\\
				O(\log t), & \gamma=2/3,
				\\
				O((t\log t)^{3\gamma-2}), & 2/3<\gamma<1.
			\end{cases}
		\end{equation*}
	\item
		If \(\Gamma=0\), we have instead
		\[
			\int\limits_{1/(t\log t)}^1 S^c(t_o)\,\mathrm{d} t_o
			=
			\begin{cases}
				O(1), &  \gamma<2/3,
				\\
				O(\log t), & \gamma =2/3
				\\
				O((t\log t)^{3-2/\gamma}), & \gamma>2/3.
			\end{cases}
		\]
		In particular, for all \(\gamma>2/3\), we have \(\int_{1/(t\log t)}^1 S^c(t_o)\,\mathrm{d} t_o=o((t\log t)^{2\gamma-1})\).
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:orderSclosed of arXiv:2603.16824

[Proposition $(I+P)$ is upper triangular in basis $\mathcal{B}$ of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] For any $0\leq j\leq n-1$, we have
\[
Pv^{(j)}= (-1)^{j}v^{(j)}+ \sum_{k=0}^{j-1} c_{n-1}(k, j) v^{(k)}, 
\]
In particular, the operator $(I+P)$ in the basis $\mathcal{B}$ has the matrix representation 
\[[(I+P)]_{\mathcal{B}}^{\mathcal{B}}= [\delta_{j, k}+c_{n-1}(k, j)]_{0\leq j, k\leq n-1}\;.\]

body: [Definition def:radial-flow-line of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] For $\kappa\in(0,4)$, we call a radial $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa^\beta(\underline\rho)$ curve $\eta$ coupled with the GFF $h_{\alpha\beta}:=h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ as in Theorem~(thm:radial-ig of the paper) the \emph{flow line} of $h_{\alpha\beta}$. For $\theta\in\mathbb{R}$, we call $\eta$ \emph{the flow line of} $h_{\alpha\beta}$ \emph{with angle $\theta$} if $\eta$ is the flow line of  $h_{\alpha\beta}+\chi\theta$. For $\kappa'>4$, we call a  $\mathrm{SLE}_{\kappa'}^\beta(\underline\rho)$ curve $\eta'$ coupled with $h_{\alpha\beta}$ as in Theorem~(thm:radial-ig of the paper) the \emph{counterflow line} of $h_{\alpha\beta}$.

[Bigthm thm: AlmostOptimal of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] Consider a deck of $n$ cards that is shuffled once using a single-shelf shuffler. 
Let $G$ be the strategy described above, and let $H$ be an optimal strategy without feedback, and let $S_n(G)$ and $S_{n}(H)$ denote the number of correct guesses under $G$ and $H$, respectively.
Then, 
\[
\sqrt{\frac{2n}{\pi}}-1 \leq \mathbb{E}\left[S_n(G)\right]\leq \mathbb{E}\left[S_n(H)\right]\leq \sqrt{\frac{2n}{\pi}} + 1 + O(n^{-1/2})\;.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check which ingredients of the q = 2 proof are available for other q. Result: The q = 2 proof uses (i) the parafermionic observable being discretely holomorphic (full Cauchy-Riemann), (ii) RSW-type crossing estimates for tightness, (iii) identification of the limit via the martingale observable. For q in (1,4) not 2: (ii) is available (Duminil-Copin-Sidoravicius-Tassion 2017 for q in [1,4]); (iii) would follow from (i); (i) fails: for general q the observable satisfies only the contour relations (half of the Cauchy-Riemann equations), the same obstruction as in C0017. So the conjecture is reduced, for q in [1,4], exactly to finding an additional discrete relation for the parafermionic observable; the count of unknowns versus equations (one complex relation per face versus two needed) is the precise deficit. For q < 1 even RSW is unavailable. No new relation found. Obstruction: Discrete holomorphicity is only half-satisfied for q not 2.

Let U subset R^n be open, and Lu = -sum_{i,j=1}^n partial_j(a^{ij}(x) partial_i u) a divergence-form second-order elliptic operator with a^{ij} in C^1(U), symmetric, and uniformly elliptic on U (there is theta>0 with sum_{i,j} a^{ij}(x)xi_i xi_j >= theta|xi|^2 for all x in U, xi in R^n). Suppose u in H^1(U) is a weak solution of Lu=f on U for some f in L^2(U): integral_U sum a^{ij} partial_i u partial_j v dx = integral_U f v dx for all v in C_c^infinity(U). Then u in H^2_loc(U): for every open V with compact closure in U, u in H^2(V), with ||u||_{H^2(V)} <= C(||f||_{L^2(U)} + ||u||_{L^2(U)}) for a constant C depending only on n, theta, V, U and the C^1 norms of the a^{ij}. (If a^{ij} in C^{k+1}(U) and f in H^k(U), then u in H^{k+2}_loc(U) with the analogous estimate; if the coefficients and f are C^infinity, u is C^infinity in the interior.)

[Defn 74 (Parabolic H\"older spaces) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] We define $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ to be the set of functions on $\Psi_T$ that are restrictions to $\Psi_T$ of some function in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{d+1})$, in particular we do not impose that elements of $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ vanish at the boundaries of $\Psi_T.$ 
  
    For $\alpha\in(0,1)$ we define the space $C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)$ to be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ with respect to the norm $$\|f\|_{C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)}:= \sup_{(t,x)\in \Psi_T} \frac{|f(t,x)|}{w(x)} + \sup_{|s-t|^{1/2}+|x-y|\leq 1} \frac{|f(t,x)-f(s,y)|}{w(x)(|t-s|^{1/2}+|x-y|)^{\alpha}}.$$
		For $\alpha<0$ we let $r=-\lfloor \alpha\rfloor$ and we define $C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)$ to be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ with respect to the norm $$\|f\|_{C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)}:= \sup_{(t,x)\in\Psi_T} \sup_{\lambda\in (0,1]} \sup_{\varphi \in B_r} \frac{(f,S^\lambda_{(t,x)}\varphi)_{L^2(\Psi_T)}}{w(x)\lambda^\alpha}$$ where the scaling operators are defined by 
		\begin{align}
			
			S^\lambda_{(t,x)}\varphi (s,y) = \lambda^{-d-2}\varphi(\lambda^{-2}(t-s),\lambda^{-1}(x-y)),
		\end{align}
		and where $B_r$ is the set of all smooth functions of $C^r$ norm less than 1 with support contained in the unit ball of $\mathbb R^{d+1}$.

[Corollary C:containment-quadrangle of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Consider a weighted directed acyclic graph $G = (V, E, M)$, and we let $H = (W, E|_{W\times W}, M|_{W})$ be the subgraph of $G$ induced by a vertex set $W \subset V$. Consider vertices $x_1 \prec y_1$ and $x_2 \prec y_2 \in H$ and suppose that we have the following {\bf path-crossing} property:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Let $\tau$ be any path in $H$ from $x_1$ to $y_1$ and $\pi = (\pi_0, \dots, \pi_k)$ be any path in $G$ from $x_2$ to $y_2$. Then if $\pi_i \notin W$ for some $i \in \llbracket1,k-1 \rrbracket$, there are indices $i^- < i < i^+$ such that the vertices $\pi(i^-), \pi(i^+)$ are on the path $\tau$.
\end{itemize}
Then
$$
H(x_1; y_1) + G(x_2; y_2) \le G(x_1; y_1) + H(x_2 ; y_2).
$$

[Lemma 10 (Decay of the first derivatives of the decoupled flow) of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Assume Assumption~\ref{ass:coeff-level-new}. Fix $ x \in \R^d $, $ \mu \in \Ptwo $, let
$ X_t^{x,\mu} $ be the decoupled flow, and $\omega$ be the constant
defined in \eqref{eq:def-omega-uniform-time}. Then, the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every $ h \in \R^d $, the first spatial derivative
$ \partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] $ exists and solves
\begin{equation}

d\left( \partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] \right)
=
\partial_x b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] dt
+
\partial_x \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] dB_t,
\end{equation}
with initial condition $\partial_x X_0^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] =
h$. Moreover, for every $ p \in \mathcal P $ and all $t \ge 0$,
\begin{equation}

\E\left(
\abs{\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right]}^p
\right)
\le
e^{-\frac{p\kappa_p}{2} t} \abs{h}^p
\le
e^{-p\omega t} \abs{h}^p.
\end{equation}

\item[(ii)] For every $ v \in \R^d $, the Lions derivative
$ \partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) $ exists and solves
\begin{align}

d\left( \partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) \right)
&=
\Bigg(
\partial_x b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right)
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\left( \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu} \right)
\partial_x \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu}
\right)
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\left( \widetilde{X}_t^{\widetilde{\xi},\mu} \right)
\partial_\mu \widetilde{X}_t^{\widetilde{\xi},\mu}\left( v \right)
\right)
\Bigg) dt
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\Bigg(
\partial_x \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right)
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\left( \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu} \right)
\partial_x \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu}
\right)
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\left( \widetilde{X}_t^{\widetilde{\xi},\mu} \right)
\partial_\mu \widetilde{X}_t^{\widetilde{\xi},\mu}\left( v \right)
\right)
\Bigg) dB_t,
\end{align}
with initial condition $\partial_\mu X_0^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) =
0$. Moreover, for every $ p \in \mathcal P $, there exists a constant
$ C_p > 0 $ such that, for all $t \ge 0$,
\begin{equation*}
\sup_{x,\mu,v}
\E\left(
\abs{\partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right)}^p
\right)
\le
C_p e^{-p\omega t}.
\end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}

Let P be a Markov kernel on a Polish space, reversible for probability measure mu. Let f be bounded measurable with integral f dmu=0. For every pair of starts x,y, couple two P-chains so that their time-k marginals are respectively P^k(x,.) and P^k(y,.). Assume a finite constant L uniformly bounds sum_(k>=0)|E[f(X_k)-f(Y_k)|X_0=x,Y_0=y]| for all x,y. Then F(x,y)=sum_(k>=0)E[f(X_k)-f(Y_k)|X_0=x,Y_0=y] is bounded and antisymmetric. If X has law mu and X_prime conditional on X has law P(X,.), then (X,X_prime) is exchangeable and E[F(X,X_prime)|X]=f(X). Equivalently, the summands are P^k f(x)-P^k f(y); uniform absolute summability of this series is the hypothesis of Lemma4.1. No pathwise ordering of the coupled chains is assumed.
Reversible kernel with stationary probability mu; bounded measurable centered f.
Both coupled time-k marginals are the required P^k laws for every initial pair.
Uniform finite bound on the sum of absolute conditional expected differences; measurability of the construction.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact tree identity, source-specific recurrence or explicit limiting obstruction Result: For any fixed clade shape chi of size m with positive model probability, its expected count is asymptotically n*p(chi)/m. The later fixed-clade variance bound is O(n), so Chebyshev gives probability O(1/n) that its count is zero. For any fixed finite list of distinct positive-probability shapes, all are therefore present with probability tending to1. It follows that the number of distinct shapes tends to infinity in probability, while it is always at most n-1 for internal clades. Check: For a count N with E N~c*n and Var N=O(n), P(N=0)<=Var N/(E N)^2=O(1/n). A finite union bound then proves the stated divergence without assuming independence between shapes. Obstruction: This supplies no growth rate: the constants and count estimates are not uniform over growing shapes. Largest repetitions and smallest missing shapes need joint tail information across an exponentially growing family.

Let $f_1, \dots, f_m$ be weakly stabilizing functionals on finite simplicial complexes, each satisfying the moment condition. Then for any expanding sequence of cubes $W_n \to \mathbb{R}^d$, the centered and normalized vector $|W_n|^{-1/2} (f_1(\Delta_{W_n}) - \mathbb{E}[f_1(\Delta_{W_n})], \dots, f_m(\Delta_{W_n}) - \mathbb{E}[f_m(\Delta_{W_n})])^T$ converges in distribution as $n \to \infty$ to a multivariate centered normal distribution $\mathcal{N}_m(0, \Sigma)$, where the asymptotic covariance matrix $\Sigma = (\sigma_{ij})_{i, j = 1}^m$ has entries given by the infinite-volume limit $\sigma_{ij} = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\operatorname{Cov}(f_i(\Delta_{W_n}), f_j(\Delta_{W_n}))}{|W_n|}$.

[Theorem 71 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta}, \ref{Assumptions_basic} and \ref{Assumptions_offcrit}
 hold. Choose $h \in [H]$, and a void interval $(\mathfrak{a},\mathfrak{b}) \subseteq [\hat{a}_h,\hat{b}_h]$ of the equilibrium measure. Assume that $\mathfrak{a}$ is a point separating a void from a band while $\mathfrak{b}$ is not (and is allowed to be $+\infty$). Then for any $\eps>0$, there exists $C>0$ depending only on $\eps$ and on the constants in the assumptions, such that
 \[
 \P\big[\exists i \in [N] \quad \big| \quad \ell_i \in [\N(\mathfrak{a}+\eps),\N\mathfrak{b}] \bigg] \leq C\exp\bigg(-\frac{\N}{C}\bigg).
\]
Similarly, if $\mathfrak{b}$ is a point separating a void from a band while $\mathfrak{a}$ is not (and is allowed to be $-\infty$), then
\[
\P\big[\exists i \in [N] \quad \big| \quad \ell_i \in [\N\mathfrak{a},\N(\mathfrak{b}-\eps)]\big]\leq C\exp\bigg(-\frac{\N}{C}\bigg).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma Upcrossing_lemma of arXiv:2608.08299, 'Non-linear optimal stopping with Bermudan strategies: the infinite horizon case'] Let $\rho$, depending on the first index only, satisfy properties (i),(iv),(v),(vii),(viii),(ix),(x), and the normalisation property $\rho_0[1]=1$. 
\\
   Let $X$ be a \textbf{non-negative} \emph{$(\Theta, \rho)$}-supermartingale.
    Let $0<a<b<+\infty$ ( $a,b \in \mathbb{Q}$).
    We define, by induction, the following stopping times: 
   $ T_0:=0 $
 and for all $k\in \mathbb{N}^*$, 
 \begin{align*}
S_k&:=\inf\{n \geq T_{k-1}:X_n \leq a\},  \\
T_k&:=\inf\{n \geq S_{k}:X_n \geq b\},
\end{align*}  
 with the convention that $inf \emptyset = + \infty$.
 \\ 
 Let $N_{\infty}([a,b])$ be the number of upcrossings of the interval $[a,b]$. 
  Let $N_{n}([a,b])$ be the number of upcrossings of the interval $[a,b]$ before time $n$.
  \\ Then, 
   \begin{compactenum}
   \item[(i)] $\rho_{S_k \wedge n}[\mathbb{I}_{\{T_k \leq n\}}]\leq (\frac{a}{b})\mathbb{I}_{\{S_k \leq n\}}$.
   \item[(ii)] $\rho_0[\mathbb{I}_{\{T_k<+\infty\}}]\leq (\frac{a}{b})^k$.
    \item[(iii)] 
  $P(N_{\infty}([a,b])< +\infty ) =1$.
   \end{compactenum}

body:
Pointwise identity. Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, x the position vector, and u ∈ C^2(Ω). Then, everywhere in Ω,
   div( (x·∇u) ∇u − (1/2)|∇u|^2 x ) = (x·∇u) Δu − ((n−2)/2) |∇u|^2.
The same holds almost everywhere for u ∈ H^2_loc(Ω) (all terms are then in L^1_loc). Replacing x by x − x_0 for any fixed x_0 gives the same identity (translation invariance).

Integrated form (Rellich). Let Ω be a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary, ν the outward unit normal, dS surface measure, and u ∈ C^2(Ω̄), or u ∈ H^2(Ω) with the boundary integrals read through the L^2(∂Ω) traces of ∇u. Then
   ∫_Ω (x·∇u) Δu dx = ((n−2)/2) ∫_Ω |∇u|^2 dx + ∫_∂Ω [ (x·∇u)(∂_ν u) − (1/2)|∇u|^2 (x·ν) ] dS.

Dirichlet case. If in addition u = 0 on ∂Ω (trace sense), then the tangential gradient vanishes on ∂Ω, ∇u = (∂_ν u) ν there, and the boundary term collapses to (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS. If moreover −Δu = λu in Ω, then
   λ ∫_Ω u^2 dx = (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS,
the Rellich formula expressing a Dirichlet eigenvalue by a boundary integral; equivalently 2λ||u||^2_{L^2(Ω)} = ∫_∂Ω (x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 dS. For a domain star-shaped with respect to the origin (x·ν ≥ 0 on ∂Ω) the right side is nonnegative term by term. The same computation with −Δu = f(u), u = 0 on ∂Ω, is the Pohozaev identity.

Where it fails / hypotheses that matter. The integrated form needs enough regularity to give ∇u a boundary trace: u ∈ H^2(Ω) (or C^2 up to the boundary). A Dirichlet eigenfunction on a Lipschitz domain that is not convex (a re-entrant corner) need not belong to H^2(Ω), and the identity is then not available in this form without a separate justification. Without u = 0 on ∂Ω the tangential gradient contributes and the simplified boundary term (1/2)∫(x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 is wrong: the full bracket must be kept. The sign of x·ν is not fixed for a general domain, so conclusions that use x·ν ≥ 0 (star-shapedness, Pohozaev-type nonexistence) fail otherwise. In dimension n = 2 the interior term ((n−2)/2)∫|∇u|^2 vanishes. The identity is for the Laplacian; for a variable-coefficient operator div(A∇u) extra terms involving x·∇A appear.
pointwise form: u ∈ C^2(Ω) (or H^2_loc, a.e.)
integrated form: Ω bounded with Lipschitz boundary, u ∈ C^2 up to the boundary or u ∈ H^2(Ω)
eigenvalue formula: additionally u = 0 on ∂Ω and −Δu = λu in Ω

[Thm 8 (GOE and GUE with finite-rank critical deformation) of arXiv:2605.30779, '2605.30779'] Let \(H_N\) be the GOE (resp.\ GUE) matrix of dimension \(N\) specified by \eqref{eq:defn_GOE} (resp.~\eqref{eq:defn_GUE}). Fix \(r\ge1\), and let $d_1, \dotsc, d_r$ be specified in \eqref{eq:defn_d_i}, $\w_1, \dotsc, \w_r$ be deterministic orthonormal vectors, and the spiked model $H^{(D)}_N$ be the $N \times N$ random matrix defined in \eqref{eq:defn_H^D_N}.

Let
\[
\lambda_1^{(D)}\ge \lambda_2^{(D)}\ge \cdots \ge \lambda_N^{(D)}
\]
be the eigenvalues of \(H_N^{(D)}\), and let \(\x_k^{(D)}\) be a unit eigenvector associated with \(\lambda_k^{(D)}\). Fix \(i\in\{1,\dots,r\}\) and let \(k\ge1\) be independent of \(N\). Let $\beta = 1$ for the GOE case and $\beta = 2$ for the GUE case. Put
\begin{equation}
  \Theta^{(i)}
  =
  (\theta_1,\dots,\theta_{i-1},\theta_{i+1},\dots,\theta_r),
  \qquad
  \mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{(r-1),i^c}:=\mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{\Theta^{(i)}},
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{\Theta^{(i)}}\) is the Airy-Green function from Proposition~\ref{pro:multispike_airy_green}. Let \(s_{\beta, k}^{(i)}\) be the unique solution in
\[
\bigl(
a_{\beta,k}^{(\Theta^{(i)})},
a_{\beta,k-1}^{(\Theta^{(i)})}
\bigr), \qquad a_{\beta,0}^{(\Theta^{(i)})}:= +\infty,
\]
of
\begin{equation} 
  \mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{(r-1),i^c}(x)=\theta_i.
\end{equation}
Then, as \(N\rightarrow\infty\), we have the joint convergence in distribution
\begin{align}
 N^{2/3}\bigl(\lambda_k^{(D)}-2\bigr) \Longrightarrow {}& s_{\beta,k}^{(i)},  & N^{1/3}\bigl|\langle \w_i,\x_k^{(D)}\rangle\bigr|^2
\Longrightarrow {}&
-\frac{1}{(\mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{(r-1),i^c})'\!\bigl(s_{\beta, k}^{(i)}\bigr)}.
\end{align}
Moreover, for any finite $K$, \eqref{GOE_Airy Green fun} holds jointly for $k = 1, 2, \dotsc, K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: GOE and GUE with finite-rank critical deformation

[Theorem thm:prime-filter-amplification of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix integers $d\geq1$ and $t\geq0$, and a shift-stable $d$-chart.  For all
sufficiently large integers $h$ and every admissible pair
$(\theta,\boldsymbol\ell)$, the value
$V_{\theta,\boldsymbol\ell}(h)$ in (equation eq:amplifier-value of the paper) is realized as
$|hC|$ by a primitive $(d+1+t)$-set obtained from $B_\theta$ by $t$ cyclic suspensions,
and
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal R(h,d+1+t)|
 \gg_{d,t,I_1,\ldots,I_t}
 \left(\frac h{\log h}\right)^t\frac{N_h^2}{E_h}.
\end{equation}
If, throughout the shift window,
\begin{equation}
 c_0 h^d\leq |(h-J)B_\theta|\leq C_0 h^d
\end{equation}
for fixed $0<c_0<C_0$, then every value used to prove
(equation eq:prime-suspension-quantitative of the paper) lies in a fixed interval
\begin{equation}
[c_{d,t,\mathbf I}h^{d+t},C_{d,t,\mathbf I}h^{d+t}],
\end{equation}
where these constants also depend on the fixed bounds $c_0,C_0$ in
(equation eq:amplifier-macroscopic-seed of the paper).

Every counted value admits a witness $C$ satisfying
\begin{align}
 \mathcal H_C(z)
 &=\mathcal H_{B_\theta}(z)\prod_{i=1}^t[\ell_i]_z,
 \\
 \mathcal K_C(z)
 &=\mathcal K_{B_\theta}(z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1-z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 \mathcal B_C(\xi,z)
 &=\mathcal B_{B_\theta}(\xi,z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1+\xi z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 r_q(C)&=r_q(B_\theta)+\#\{i:\ell_i\leq q\}
 \qquad(q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}),
 \\
 \operatorname{ndiam}(C)&=\left(\prod_{i=1}^t\ell_i\right)\operatorname{ndiam}(B_\theta).
 
\end{align}
If the seed projective coordinate ring is Cohen--Macaulay, then projective
Cohen--Macaulayness and Cohen--Macaulay type are preserved.  Since every
$\ell_i<h$, maximal degree-$h$ active rank propagates from the seed to $C$.

[Dfn 119 (continuous-time smoothed coefficients) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Analogously to Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth}, we define the spatially smoothed continuous-time coefficients
	\[\srrr(t,y)\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{\rrr,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}\,,\quad
	\swww(t,y)\equiv
	\frac{\varsigma_{\www,t}*\sphi(y)}
		{\varsigma_t*\sphi(y)}\,,\]
as well as
	\begin{align*}
	\sB(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{D,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv
	p'(t)^{1/2} \cdot \sbbb(t,y)\,,\\
	\sV(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{V,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv
	p(t) \cdot \svvv(t,y)\,,\\
	\sU(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{U,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv
	\Big[ p(t) \cdot t p'(t) \Big]^{1/2}
		\cdot \suuu(t,y)\,.
	\end{align*}
Analogously to Definition~\ref{d:t.smooth}, we define the 
temporally smoothed continuous-time coefficients
	\beq
	
	\tB(t,y)
	\equiv
	\int_{\R} \tphi(s) \sB(t-s,y)\,ds
	= \tE\Big[ \sB(t-\sss,y)\Big]
	\eeq
and similarly $\tV$, $\tU$, $\trrr$, $\twww$. We define also the scaled coefficients
	\begin{align*}
	\tbbb(t,y)
	&\equiv\frac{\tB(t,y)}
		{p'(t)^{1/2} }\,,\\
	\tvvv(t,y)
	&\equiv \frac{\tV(t,y)}{p(t) } 
	\,,\\
	\tuuu(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\tU(t,y)}{[ p(t)
		\cdot t p'(t)]^{1/2}} \,.
	\end{align*}
and abbreviate $\tGam\equiv(\tbbb,\tvvv,\tuuu)$. Likewise, analogously to Definition~\ref{d:t.smooth.variant}, we define $\TGam\equiv(\Tbbb,\Tvvv,\Tuuu)$ as well as $(\iB,\iV,\iU,\ir,\iw)$.

	\begin{align*}
	\sF(t,y)
	&\equiv\Big\{ \sV+2\sU+\srrr\Big\}(t,y)\,,\\
	\tF(t,y)
	&\equiv\Big\{ \tV+2\tU+\trrr\Big\}(t,y)\,,\\
	\iF(t,y)
	&\equiv\Big\{ \iV+2\iU+\ir\Big\}(t,y)\,,
	\end{align*}
analogously to \eqref{e:sp.smoothed.F.N}, \eqref{e:temp.smoothed.F.N}, and \eqref{e:ideal.smoothed.F.N}.

the model is a continuum rotationally invariant Riemannian first passage percolation on the PLANE
the model lies in the class for which Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly (2023) established their fluctuation estimates for passage times and geodesics
rotational invariance is used; the lattice Z^2 has none, so the result does not transfer as stated
the value of epsilon is not stated in the abstract

MECHANISM, in the authors' words: the argument 'uses fluctuation estimates for passage times and geodesics derived in Basu, Sidoravicius and Sly (2023) together with a multi-scale argument to establish that the geodesic exhibits disorder chaos, i.e., upon resampling a small fraction of the underlying randomness, the updated geodesic has on average a small overlap with the original one; this, established at a large number of scales, leads to a polynomial improvement of the variance bound.'
SO THE CAMPAIGN'S TARGET SHAPE IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: geodesic disorder chaos telescoped over many scales is the only route that has ever produced a polynomial gain. What it has never produced is a LATTICE gain, and the reason is that rotational invariance is consumed.
118 pages, 23 figures. Vladas Sidoravicius died in 2019; the authorship is as listed on arXiv.
SOURCE: arXiv:2604.01214v1, official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22; no journal reference as of that date.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source at the level of the authors' abstract, which states the model class, the conclusion, the dependency and the mechanism. The 118-page proof was NOT read, so nothing is asserted here about the internal hypotheses, the size of epsilon, or which steps consume rotational invariance.
title: Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly (arXiv:2604.01214, submitted 1 April 2026): for a class of ROTATIONALLY INVARIANT RIEMANNIAN first passage percolation ON THE PLANE, the variance of the passage time is O(n^{1-epsilon}) for some epsilon > 0. This is the first polynomial improvement over the n/log n barrier in any variant of first-passage percolation - and it is a continuum, rotationally invariant result, NOT a lattice result: on Z^d the best known upper bound is still n/log n.

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple...'] We consider the conformal loop ensemble (CLE) with the parameter $\kappa=4$, the critical value at or below which the loops are simple and do not intersect each other or the domain boundary. We show that the loops of a $\CLE_4$ uniquely determine a conformally invariant, local, and geodesic metric so that the metric ball growth from the domain boundary coincides with the uniform exploration of Werner and Wu. This metric was previously constructed in unpublished work of Sheffield, Watson, and Wu. Our approach differs in that we show that the metric arises as the renormalized limit of the graph metric on $\CLE_\kappa$ loops as $\kappa \downarrow 4$. In this first paper in a series of three, we prove that the subsequential limits exist and define a non-trivial conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ which is local and such that the metric ball growth from the boundary is given by the uniform exploration of Werner and Wu. In subsequent work, we will show that the subsequential limit exists as a true limit.

A finite cell exposes distinct terminals T and a state pi, a partition of T recording connectivity inside the cell. On a common deterministic skeleton a crossing event is a Boolean function f of all cell partitions. Exterior sensitivity S_i(x_-i) equals one exactly when f(x_-i,pi) is nonconstant as pi ranges over the finite allowed cell states; it depends only on the exterior.

\begin{equation}
p_{a,b,\theta}\in\HCM
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\theta=0.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, every positive \({}_0F_1\)-gamma deformation of a gamma density fails to be hyperbolically completely monotone. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $f\in L^1(\mathbb T)$, $x\in\mathbb T$ and $s\in\mathbb C$. (Dini) If $\int_0^{1/2}\frac{|f(x+t)+f(x-t)-2s|}{t}\,dt<\infty$, then the symmetric partial sums converge: $S_Nf(x)\to s$. In particular, if $f$ is Holder continuous at $x$ of some order $\alpha>0$ (i.e. $|f(x+t)-f(x)|\le C|t|^\alpha$ for all small real $t$, of either sign), or differentiable at $x$, or more generally if the two-sided Dini integral $\int_{|t|\le1/2}\frac{|f(x+t)-f(x)|}{|t|}\,dt$ is finite, then $S_Nf(x)\to f(x)$ (the two-sided condition dominates the symmetric one with $s=f(x)$, by the triangle inequality). (Riemann localization) If $f,g\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ agree on an open interval containing $x$, then $S_Nf(x)-S_Ng(x)\to0$; so convergence or divergence of a Fourier series at $x$ depends only on the behaviour of $f$ near $x$, even though the coefficients depend on $f$ globally.
f integrable on the circle
Dini: the integral of |f(x+t)+f(x-t)-2s|/t over (0,1/2) is finite; mere continuity at x is NOT enough
the Holder / two-sided Dini conditions must control t of both signs
symmetric partial sums (the statement is about S_N, not about arbitrary summation orders)

[Prop prop-vmexist of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] [bh-book] Given $\delta \geq 0$, there exists $a > 1$ such that if
	$(X,d)$ is $\delta-$hyperbolic, then for any base-point $o$,
	a visual metric $d_v $
	with parameter $a>1$ exists on $\partial X$ with respect to the base-point $o$.
	Further, for any $o' \in X$, let $d_v'$ be a visual metric on $\partial X$
 with respect to the base-point $o'$ and
	with parameter $a>1$. Then $d_v'$
	is equivalent (as a metric) to $d_v$.
	
	There exists a natural topology on $\hat{X} = X \cup \partial X$ such that
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $X$ is open and dense in $\hat X$,
		\item $\partial X$ and $\hat{X}$ are compact if $X$ is proper,
		\item the subspace topology on $\partial X$ agrees with that given by $d_v$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop prop-vmexist of arXiv:2411.14350

body: Free blocks for the single hub (bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture), with Q as in the normal form 2 X_h (L + beta) + lambda V^2 + 2 L <q, X'> + sum phi_i(X_i). (a) If a set I_1 of light coordinates carries only the hub partner (v_i = 0, d_i = 0 there, q and b proportional to w there, q_i = kappa w_i) and omega = |w_{I_1}| > 0, then ||p_Q||_inf <= 1/2 + 10.3/omega for kappa = 0 and 1/2 + (39.5 + 0.71 log(1 + 4|kappa|))/omega in general (|lambda| >= 1), for every hub law, every cross term on the other coordinates and all laws. Proof: condition on the other coordinates; t = L + beta has density <= sqrt2/omega and the hub value needed, x* = alpha/(2t) + c_0 - kappa t, is Moebius-like in t, so the hub enters through dilates of one set and int_{|t|<1} 1_S(alpha/(2t)) dt/(2|t|) <= log(1 + 1/|alpha|); the interval profile of alpha finishes. (b) If a set I_2 carries only v, then for Q = 2 X_h (L + beta) + lambda V^2 + 2 V g(X_R) + G(X_R) with any g, G: ||p_Q||_inf <= 1/2 + 8 sqrt2 |v_{I_2}|^{-1} |lambda|^{-1/2} (the free part of V gives every slice the Borel profile 4 |v_{I_2}|^{-1} (|S|/|lambda|)^{1/2}).

[Theorem result2 of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] Consider the  $d$ coupon collector's problem (d--CCP), where in each run we keep \textbf{the least} collected coupon so far. Let $T_{N,1}$ be the number of trials until all $N$ different types of coupons, which are uniformly distributed, are collected (at least once). Then, as $N\rightarrow \infty$
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}[T_{N,1}]=
\frac{N}{d}\log N
+\left(\frac{\gamma}{d}+
C_d\right)N
-
\frac{d-1}{2d}\log N
+
D_d
+
\mathcal{O}\!\left(\frac{\log N}{N}\right),

\end{equation}
where,
\begin{equation}
C_d:
=
\int_0^1
\left(
\frac{1}{1-(1-x)^d}-\frac{1}{dx}
\right)\,dx,

\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
D_d:
=
\frac{2d^2-3d+3-2\gamma \left(d-1\right)}{4d}
-\frac{d-1}{2}C_d.

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let {e_i : i in I} be an orthonormal basis of a Hilbert space H. Then for every x in H, x = sum over i of <x, e_i> e_i (with at most countably many nonzero terms, converging in norm), and ||x||^2 = sum over i of |<x, e_i>|^2. More generally <x, y> = sum over i of <x, e_i> times the conjugate of <y, e_i>. Conversely, an orthonormal family for which ||x||^2 = sum over i of |<x, e_i>|^2 holds for every x is an orthonormal basis.
H is a Hilbert space
{e_i} is an orthonormal basis of H

body: [Corollary 3.12 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] With $Y$ the partial-trace matrix of partial permutations $\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}\in\mathcal{P}^{\prime}([m])$ applied to contractions $A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\in M_{N}(\mathbb{C})^{\otimes k}$, $N^{M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})}\leq\max_{\|A_{1}\|,\ldots,\|A_{m}\|\leq 1}\|Y\|\leq N^{C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})}.$ The lower bound is attained by the same permutation tensors as in Theorem 3.11. Here, for the graph $G_{\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})=\min_{G^{\prime}}R_{G^{\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).
