[Proposition prop:sharp-lri-4d of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] ([ShiraishiWatanabe2026])

Let $S^1$ and $S^2$ be independent simple random walks on $\mathbb Z^4$ started from
$0$.  For $k\ge1$, set
\begin{align*}
        f(n,k)=
        \mathbb P\bigl(S^1[0,n]\cap S^2[kn,(k+1)n]\ne\emptyset\bigr).
\end{align*}
Then, uniformly in the range of $k$ used in this paper,
\begin{equation}

        f(n,k)=
        \frac{1}{2\log n}
        \log\left(1+\frac{1}{k^2+2k}\right)
        \left\{1+O\left(\frac{1}{k(\log n)^{3/25}}\right)\right\}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\(K,\delta_0,N,\sigma\).  The start-time threshold \(T_{\mathrm{blk}}\) may
additionally depend on the fixed Bamler tail data \(T_B(c_0)\) and
\(\eps_B^{c_0}\) for the given flow.

Let \(p(\tau)\) be a parabolically rescaled \(\delta_0\)-large block starting
at \(S\geq T_{\mathrm{blk}}\), fix a torus fibration \(\pi:M\to S^1\), and put
\[
        q(1)=p(1),\qquad r(1)=\overline{q(1)}.
\]
Suppose that \(r(1)\) is Riemannian and, with
\[
 b=\|q(1)-r(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r(1))},
 \qquad d=d_{\TT^2}(r(1)),
\]
one has
\[
        b<\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        d<\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        \BG_N(r(1);\Lambda_*).
\]
Equivalently, \((q(1),r(1))\) is an admissible stage start in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-stage-start}, with constants
\(\Lambda_*,\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\theta_{\mathrm{blk}}\).
Then the invariant Ricci flow \(r\) and the Ricci--DeTurck flow \(q\) relative
to it exist on \([1,100]\).  At the rescaled endpoint, put
\[
        q^+(1)=100^{-1}q(100),\qquad
        \rho^+=100^{-1}r(100),\qquad
        r^+(1)=\overline{q^+(1)},
\]
and set
\[
        b^+=\|q^+(1)-r^+(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r^+(1))}.
\]
Then \(r^+(1)\) is Riemannian and
\begin{equation}
        b^+\leq\tfrac12 b,\qquad
        d_{\TT^2}(r^+(1))<\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        \BG_N(r^+(1);\Lambda_*).
\end{equation}
Thus the same admissible-start conditions hold at the restart.  The ordinary
Ricci flow corresponding to \(q\) is \(p\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Block contraction theorem

[Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.03534, 'Construction and simulation of a path-valued model of dendrite development'] The \textit{graph representation} of a measure $\mu \in \mathcal{N}_\mathcal{S}^{\#}$ is a graph $G=(V,E)$ describing the spatial embedding of $\mu$, defined as follows. Let 
    \begin{align*}
        V &= \Big\{ x \in X \, \Big| \, \exists \, (\omega,a) \in [\mu] \text{ s.t. } x = \omega(0) \text{ or } x=\hat{\omega}  \Big\} \,, \\
        E &= \Big\{ (x,y) \in V \times V \, \Big| \, \exists \, (\omega,a) \in [\mu] \text{ s.t. } \omega(0)=x \text{ and } \hat{\omega}= y  \Big\} \,.
    \end{align*}
    To an edge $(x,y) \in E$ we assign the corresponding path $\omega_{xy} \in \mathcal{W}$ to be the element $(\omega_{xy},a) \in [\mu]$ with $\omega_{xy}(0)=x$ and $\hat{\omega}_{xy} = y$. 
    This network is fully determined by $\mu$ and so defines a mapping $\mu \mapsto (V,E)$ from $\mathcal{N}_\mathcal{S}^\#$ into a space of networks. Denote this mapping by $G(\mu)$.
title: Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.03534

body:
[Theorem 41 of arXiv:2609.03070, 'Variants of order semicontinuity in Banach lattices'] Let $F$ be an AM-space. Then:
\item[(i)] $F$ is semicontinuous if and only if it isometrically embeds as a regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$.
\item[(ii)] $F$ is demicontinuous if and only if it isomorphically embeds as a regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$. In this case it is topologically semicontinuous.
\item[(iii)] $F$ is pointwise demicontinuous if and only if it injectively embeds as a regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$.\medskip

    Moreover, ``regular'' can be replaced with ``order dense'', while $K$ can be assumed extremally disconnected.

[Theorem eq:wiener_hopf_factors of arXiv:2604.08889, 'Matrix Representations for Scale Functions of Spectrally Negative Lévy Processes with Rati'] Let $\{W_t\}_{t\geq 0}$ be a Brownian motion with variance $\sigma^2>0$, drift $d\in \mathbb{R}$ and starting point $W_0=0$. 
Let $U$ be a stopping time, and for fixed $\lambda+q > 0$ let $E\sim {\rm Exp}(\lambda+q)$, independent of $\{W_t\}_{t\geq 0}$. 
Then, $W_U-\min_{t\in [0,E]}W_{U+t}$ and $W_{U+E}-\min_{t\in [0,E]}W_{U+t}$ are independent and exponentially distributed random variables with respective rates
\begin{equation}
\omega_{\lambda+q} = \frac{\sqrt{d^2 + 2\sigma^2 (\lambda+q)} + d}{\sigma^2}, \qquad \eta_{\lambda+q} = \frac{\sqrt{d^2 + 2\sigma^2 (\lambda+q)} - d}{\sigma^2}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Wiener-Hopf factorisation for Brownian motion

[Definition 2 (Complex array normal distribution) of arXiv:2608.21551, '\bf Sparse Separable Factor Analysis in the Complex Domain with an Application to Local Fi'] Let $\Mcal\in\CC^{c_1\times\cdots\times c_d}$, and let $\Vb_j\in\CC^{c_j\times c_j}$ be Hermitian positive definite for $j=1,\ldots,d$. A $d$-mode array $\Ycal$ follows a proper complex array normal distribution with mean $\Mcal$ and mode-specific covariance matrices $\Vb_1,\ldots,\Vb_d$ if
\begin{align}
  
  \operatorname{vec}(\Ycal)
  \sim
  \CC\Ncal_{\prod_{j=1}^d c_j}
  \left(
    \operatorname{vec}(\Mcal),
    \Vb_d\otimes\cdots\otimes\Vb_1
  \right),
\end{align}
where $\otimes$ denotes the Kronecker product. We write $\Ycal\sim \CC\Ncal_{c_1\times\cdots\times c_d} (\Mcal,\Vb_1,\ldots,\Vb_d)$.
title: Complex array normal distribution

[Cor 17 (\cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Take $A,b,C,d$ as in Theorem~\ref{t:hoffman} with $(b,d)\in F(A,C)$.
Let $B(M_0)$ denote the ball of radius $M_0$ in $\R^n$, centered at the origin.
\begin{enumerate}[a.]
\item  Suppose $(b',d')\in F(A,C)$, and
suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S_{A,C}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then
	\[d_H\Big(S_{A,C}(b,d),S_{A,C}(b',d')\Big)
	\le c\left\| \begin{pmatrix}
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$.
\item 
Now suppose we have $(A,b,C,d)'$ of the same dimensions,
with $(b',d')\in F(A',C')$. 
Suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S\equiv S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S'\equiv S_{A',C'}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then, for any $x'\in S'$ there exists $x\in S$ with
	\[\|x-x'\|_2
	\le c \left\| \begin{pmatrix} A-A'\\ C-C'\\
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2\,,
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$, and on the right-hand side we treat $A$ and $C$ as vectors of length $mn$ and $qn$ respectively.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $x'\in S'$. Then
	\[
	Ax'-b
	=[A'+(A-A')] x'- [b' + (b-b')]
	\le (A-A')x'-(b-b')\,,
	\]
from which it follows that
	\[
	\|(Ax'-b)_+\|
	\le \| [(A-A')x'-(b-b')]_+\|
	\le \|A-A'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|b-b'\|\,.
	\]
Similarly, we can bound
	\[
	\|Cx'-d\|
	\le \|C-C'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|d-d'\|\,.
	\]
The operator norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm, so the conclusion of part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty} follows.
Part \eqref{i:hoffman.rhs} then follows from part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}

Li-Nica-Roy Proposition A.6 conditional drift and diffusion moment checks, in a precise conditional-moment specialization. Fix d,p,delta,h_n and the Markov transition increment Delta_n(y)=h_n*B_n(y)+sqrt(h_n)*sigma_n(y)*xi_n+h_n*n^(-delta)*R_n(y). Assume the companion small-jump hypotheses with q=4, uniformly on each compact set. Conditional on each current state y assume E[B_n(y)|y]=b_n(y), E[xi_n|y]=0, and E[xi_n*xi_n^T|y]=I_d. Within-step B_n,xi_n,R_n may be correlated. Suppose the deterministic b_n and sigma_n converge uniformly on compact sets to b and sigma. Let Pi_n(y,dz) be the law of y+Delta_n(y). Define the truncated characteristics beta_n(y)=h_n^(-1)*integral_{||z-y||<=1}(z-y)Pi_n(y,dz) and alpha_n(y)=h_n^(-1)*integral_{||z-y||<=1}(z-y)(z-y)^T Pi_n(y,dz). Then beta_n converges uniformly on compact sets to b, alpha_n converges uniformly on compact sets to sigma*sigma^T, and h_n^(-1)*Pi_n(y,{z:||z-y||>epsilon}) converges uniformly on compact sets to zero for every epsilon>0. These are the transition-characteristic conditions used in source equationsA.6-A.7 and checked in A.12-A.14. Path convergence additionally needs the appropriate tightness/compact-containment and well-posed diffusion/martingale-problem hypotheses; the displayed moment conclusions alone do not assert stopped or unstopped path convergence.
Fixed dimension and p,delta>0; conditional one-step moments uniformly bounded on each compact set as stated.
Additional conditional mean/covariance and coefficient convergence assumptions appear explicitly in the characteristics lemma.

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited), independent mathematical, priority and scope audits pending. Let N>=3,K>=2,1<=r<K,F=K-r,gcd(r,F)=1. One unknown A/S context pair has an arbitrary r-truth support in A and all K truths in S; N-2 other contexts are known S. The source chooses a context uniformly then a true candidate uniformly. Observe n iid untagged facts and independent uniform ell-subsets of truths in BOTH variable contexts, including S, 0<=ell<=r. Every realized generator of a randomized learning policy must satisfy source Mis_infinity<=c in all data-compatible worlds, where 0<=c<1/(2NrK), and source coarsening is uniform in exact generator-score bins. For sample counts u,v and truth-union sizes a,b in actual A,S coordinates, set h=min(a,b), kappa=F/K, A_h=F/(2(K-h))*((2-h/r-h/K)/N-c), O_a=F/(K-a)*max((r-a)/(Nr)-c,0), L(u,j)=(K/r)^u*binom(K-j,r-j)/binom(K-ell,r-ell) if j<=r and zero otherwise. For b<=r let pi=max(L(u,a),L(v,b))/(L(u,a)+L(v,b)). Set f=O_a when b>r, f=A_h when b<=r,h>=1, and f=kappa/N-kappa*c*pi when b<=r,h=0. Define P_m(j|u)=binom(m-ell,j-ell)/m^u * sum_{i=0}^{j-ell}(-1)^i binom(j-ell,i)(j-i)^u, with 0^0=1. The exact global expected robust minimax false mass is Gamma=sum_{u+v+w=n} n!/(u!v!w!)*(N-2)^w/N^n *sum_{a=ell}^r sum_{b=ell}^K P_r(a|u)P_K(b|v)f. The same-data known-partition oracle replaces f by O_a; the difference is the exact experiment-specific learning penalty. For ell>=1 the posterior whole-context correction vanishes; for ell=r, Gamma=(kappa/(2N)-c/2)*(1-kappa/N)^n. The efficient causal policy pools uncertified residuals when h>=1, reduces the posterior-more-likely-A whole context when h=0, and uses the residual oracle when resolved. Policy symmetrization, not averaging output laws, supplies global matching. This does not establish an arbitrary-VC or classical labeled-sample ERM/PAC result.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:9375fcf0a1718154957e1a719a3358fe277573b347014e444e326701c54c3478","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/93/9375fcf0a1718154957e1a719a3358fe277573b347014e444e326701c54c3478.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:edaa0080849d4a38dcaccff8130d3d83fe5184144d4924bcf369f75184d33dd5","bundle_entry_key":"global-coprime-single-pair-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-global-single-pair-coprime-all-n-verifier-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"calibrated generation; global minimax; Bayesian occupancy","draft":"w709/bundle_013.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:kalai-vempala-global-coprime-single-pair-occupancy-verifier-frontier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Global coprime single-pair frontier: working candidate

T379-C021 v2, proof (unaudited); exact checks PASS. Target 1, secondary target 2.
General multi-pair/VC frontier remains open.

Model: N>=3 contexts, K>=2 atoms per context, 1<=r<K, F=K-r,
gcd(r,F)=1. One variable A/S pair; A has arbitrary r truths, S all K.
N-2 other contexts are known S. The source chooses a context uniformly,
then a true atom uniformly. Observe n iid facts without orientation tags,
plus independent uniform ell-subsets of truths from BOTH variable contexts,
including S, with 0<=ell<=r. Every realized generator of a randomized
learning policy must have source Mis_infinity<=c in every compatible world.
Let 0<=c<1/(2NrK). Gamma(c)=inf_policy sup_fixed_world E[false mass].

In actual A/S coordinates let u,v be sample counts, a,b known union sizes,
h=min(a,b), kappa=F/K. Define

 A_h(c)=F/(2(K-h))*((2-h/r-h/K)/N-c),
 O_a(c)=F/(K-a)*max((r-a)/(Nr)-c,0),
 L(u,j)=(K/r)^u*binom(K-j,r-j)/binom(K-ell,r-ell) for j<=r,
         zero for j>r.

For unresolved data b<=r set pi_max=max(L(u,a),L(v,b))/(L(u,a)+L(v,b)).
Define f=O_a if b>r; f=A_h if b<=r and h>=1;
f=kappa/N-kappa*c*pi_max if b<=r and h=0.

For m>=ell, let

 P_m(j|u)=binom(m-ell,j-ell)/m^u
             *sum_{i=0}^{j-ell}(-1)^i binom(j-ell,i)(j-i)^u.

Use 0^0=1. The proposed exact global frontier is

 Gamma(c)=sum_{u+v+w=n} n!/(u!v!w!)*(N-2)^w/N^n
                *sum_{a=ell}^r sum_{b=ell}^K
                    P_r(a|u)*P_K(b|v)*f(u,v,a,b;c).          (1)

The same-data known-partition oracle is the same sum replacing f by O_a.
Their difference is the exact learning penalty in this VC-one family.

## Hardest step: conditional BAYES all-generator lower bound

This is the decisive analytic step; finite exact checks support it below,
and independent review remains necessary. A conditional minimax bound cannot
simply be averaged into a global expected minimax bound.

Source bin masses are integer multiples of 1/(NrK). Robustness gives
pairwise coarsened-source TV<=2c<1/(NrK); thus all score-bin source masses
are invariant across compatible worlds. This is a BIN-MASS lattice,
not a coarsened-atom-probability lattice.

Support swaps force each unsaturated outside-known set into one bin.
If one context is saturated, coprimality forces its outside-known set
into one bin too: F divides r*v, hence F divides v, and 0<=v<=F.
This is C019's already saved structural step.

Unless both contexts are saturated, outside-known bins either differ or
agree. If they differ, each contains an ENTIRE context and none of its
sibling. If common, the bin contains K-k atoms from EACH sibling, with
the same k known truths omitted from each, 0<=k<=h, plus possible fixed-S
safe atoms. Every false atom belongs to this bin. Its source score is
at least b_k=[1/K+(r-k)/(r(K-k))]/(2N), since fixed-S atoms have density
lambda=1/(NK)>=b_k. With w safe atoms, its false fraction is at most
tau_k=F/(2(K-k)). Its actual false mass in either orientation is at least
F*b_k-tau_k*c. This decreases with k, hence is at least A_h(c).
Pooling after selecting h known truths in each sibling, then transferring
c residual mass to fixed S, attains A_h in every world.

In whole-context mode, baseline posterior false mass is kappa/N. Every
bin's posterior false fraction is <=kappa*pi_max, even with safe mixing.
TV c therefore permits reduction at most kappa*pi_max*c. Removing c mass
from the more-likely-A context and adding it to fixed S attains
B_pi(c)=kappa/N-kappa*c*pi_max.

If both unions have size r, an invariant bin satisfies
F*(u_L-u_R)=r*(v_L-v_R), with u known counts, v outside counts.
Coprimality implies either balanced counts u_L=u_R,v_L=v_R, or the bin
contains an entire context and none of its sibling. One whole-context
bin forces the rest of the sibling into its own whole-context bin.
Otherwise all bins are balanced. For balanced bins, posterior false
fraction is <=1/2 and independent of orientation. Artificial fair mean
density is lambda/2 on outside atoms, while all safe densities are
>=lambda. Coarsening cannot lower mass on the outside set; TV c implies
false mass >=F*lambda/2-c/2=A_r(c). Pooling attains this.
Thus conditional Bayes optimum is min(A_h,B_pi) in every unresolved case.

For h>=1, A_h always wins on this c interval. Indeed
D_h=kappa/N-F*b_h=h*F^2/(2NrK(K-h)) and
B_pi-A_h>=D_h-c*(kappa-tau_h).
If kappa-tau_h>0, positivity at c*=1/(2NrK) reduces to
2K*h*F>K-2h, true for h>=1,F>=1. For h=0, B_pi<=A_0 since pi_max>=1/2.

Resolved data b>r identify the A context. Swaps force its outside atoms
into one bin if a<r. Safe mixing raises baseline density, and the exact
known-partition value is O_a(c). If a=r, it is zero, not an oracle slope
inferred from a zero-mass group.

## Actual posterior and global matching

Use the uniform prior on orientations and A supports. The verifier-set
marginal is identical in A and S. Conditional A supports are uniform
r-subsets containing the certificate. Relative to S, the factual sample
sequence likelihood in a context is exactly L(u,j) above. Thus pi is
the TRUE posterior, not a surrogate fair bit. With ell=0, u repeated
copies of one fact have likelihood ratio (K/r)^(u-1), not (K/r)^u.

The finite group generated by sibling swaps and within-context atom
permutations is transitive on worlds and equivariant on the experiment.
Symmetrize LEARNING POLICIES, retaining each separately realized generator.
Never average generator laws: exact-score calibration is not convex in g.
The symmetrized policy remains feasible pathwise and has constant-world
risk equal to original uniform-prior risk. Worst risk is always at least
prior-average risk. Conditional Bayes minima above are attained, so global
minimax equals their uniform-prior average. This is standard finite-group
minimax methodology, not a new minimax theorem.

Condition on sample context counts u,v. Their multinomial distribution is
the coefficient in (1). Choose j-ell new truths and use inclusion-exclusion
to require each chosen new truth to appear: this gives P_m(j|u), with
samples allowed to hit the ell original verifier truths. The two context
occupancy experiments are independent given context counts and a fixed
world. The conditional Bayes value is symmetric, hence averaging in ANY
fixed world's actual A/S coordinates yields (1).

Equivalently let V_cond=O_a on resolved data, A_h otherwise. Then

 Gamma(c)=E[V_cond]-kappa*c*
      E[(pi_max-1/2)*1_{unresolved and h=0}].                (2)

The correction vanishes for ell>=1. It must not be applied on resolved
data. At ell=r, (1) reduces to
(kappa/(2N)-c/2)*(1-kappa/N)^n. At c=0, Gamma=E[V_cond] for ONE pair.
C020's zero-budget averaging failure uses TWO pairs and is consistent.

Primary source statistic: Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3, Definitions 1--2,
pp.8--9. Structural inputs: C017/C019, unaudited. Standard minimax card:
recall/walk005.txt. Independent mathematical, priority, scope audit pending.

## Efficient policy and target scope

The policy uses sample multiplicities and observed truth unions. If the
partition is identified, use the A residual group with its native density,
remove min(c,residual source mass), and transfer this mass to fixed S.
For unresolved h>=1, choose an h-subset of known truths uniformly in each
sibling, pool their 2(K-h) remaining atoms at the common source density,
and move c mass to fixed S. Other selected-known atoms have their common
paired source score. For h=0, choose the posterior-more-likely A context
(uniform tie break), lower its entire context mass by c, and add it to
fixed S. All these operations use observed quantities only. Selected known
subsets and ties randomize policies, never averages of output laws.

The output law and the required likelihood comparison have polynomial
arithmetic complexity in n and the explicit alphabet size NK. The finite
sum (1) is also polynomial-time evaluable in n,K by precomputing the
occupancy tables. This is an expected minimax result under a pathwise
compatible-world robustness requirement, not a high-probability PAC result.
The two orientation functions form a VC-one partition class. Factual
observations do not provide labeled partition examples; this does not prove
a classical labeled-sample ERM rate or the unrestricted arbitrary-VC target.
The exact difference of sums is an experiment-specific estimation penalty,
not an assertion that it equals ordinary classification error. A MAP
orientation can be used as a data-dependent tie break among feasible
partitions, but the optimal pooled output need not be an oracle plug-in
using that single orientation. These distinctions require scope review.

## Exact independent finite checks

logs/global_single_pair_check.json records 237 conditional Bayes games and
588969 exhaustive invariant score partitions, 621 actual all-world
generator calibration checks, 237 full-world likelihood-posterior checks,
330 direct sequence/occupancy comparisons, 720 global occupancy-sum checks,
252 full-verifier closed-form checks, 24 two-sample closed-form checks, and
seven genuine repeated-fact wrong-exponent controls. Exhaustive partition
checks have NK<=9; larger parameter checks concern occupancy and algebra.

Separately logs/global_single_pair_policy_check.json sums the explicit
causal policy under all six fixed N=3,K=3,r=2 worlds, ell=0..2, n=0..4,
at zero and positive budgets: 59400 actual data/verifier histograms and
180 exact fixed-world expectations and normalizations. These equal (1)
and are constant across fixed worlds, without substituting posterior risk
for an actual-world loss. Both scripts use only integers and Fraction.
Finite checks are not an independent mathematical audit of the general proof.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:81ee50e127bfb14a5f03a78a3a06c0e51e589b42410a5a1f204312b1a99439c9","revision_digest":"sha256:39f359fca3402a1a696a1fc6c481b0860225853def9331d81be2cb29ae5ee267","source_id":"owner:w709:T379-C021:v2","source_revision":"2026-10-20T13:57:38.168701+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[campaign result 2026-09-14; values computed exactly from the intersection-array identity tau_0 = k sum_{i=1}^d (k_i+...+k_d)/(k_i c_i). That identity was checked against a direct linear-algebra solve on twelve graphs, among them the cubic graphs K_{3,3}, Q_3, Petersen, Heawood, Pappus, Desargues and the dodecahedron, with the complete graph and the cycle as independent controls.] This is the cubic case of Open Problem 7.31 in David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html). For a finite connected simple distance-regular graph G with n vertices, let tau_0 = max_{x,y} E_x[T_y] for simple random walk. By the known classification, there are exactly thirteen cubic (valency-three) distance-regular graphs. Their (n, tau_0) values are: K_4 (4, 3); K_{3,3} (6, 6); cube Q_3 (8, 10); Petersen (10, 12); Heawood (14, 19); Pappus (18, 27); Desargues (20, 65/2); dodecahedron (20, 35); Coxeter (28, 45); Tutte-Coxeter (30, 48); Foster (90, 675/4); Biggs-Smith (102, 195); Tutte 12-cage (126, 234). Hence, given the classification, the maximum of tau_0/(n-1) over all cubic distance-regular graphs is 195/101 (about 1.9307), attained uniquely by the Biggs-Smith graph. This reproduces exactly the value Aldous and Fill attribute to Biggs and settles, for valency three, Biggs's outlined claim that it is the largest. The general O(n) conjecture over non-cycle distance-regular graphs is not settled by this computation. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

[Proposition 47 (Smooth-transform criterion) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Assume \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R)\), \(\E_\nu f=0\),
\(\E_\nu f^2=1\),
\[
        \E\sup_{|u|\le\delta_0}|f(\zeta+u)|^4<\infty,
\]
and that the Taylor remainders of \(f\) and \(f^2\) satisfy
\[
        \E\sup_{|u|\le\delta_0}|f''(\zeta+u)|<\infty,
        \qquad
        \E\sup_{|u|\le\delta_0}\bigl(|f'(\zeta+u)|^2+|f(\zeta+u)f''(\zeta+u)|\bigr)<\infty.
\]
Then Condition~\ref{cond:profile-admissibility} holds with
\[
        a_1=\E f'(\zeta),
        \qquad
        b_1=2\E[f(\zeta)f'(\zeta)],
\]
\[
        b_2=\E\bigl[f'(\zeta)^2+f(\zeta)f''(\zeta)\bigr].
\]

[Theorem fredi of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $n$ be a fixed integer. Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$ and assume
  that for every finite $r$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^{n \varepsilon} \left( \frac{1}{N} \log
    \mathbb{E}[H \text{} C (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A),
    \ldots, \lambda_n (A))] - \sum_{j = 0}^{n - 1} \sum_{i = 0}^r
    \frac{1}{N^{j \varepsilon}} \Psi_j (x_i) \right) = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi_n
    (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi_0, \ldots, \Psi_n$ are smooth functions in a complex neighborhood of
  $0$, the above convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$ and $0 <
  \varepsilon < n^{- 1}$. Then the $1 / N^{n \varepsilon}$ correction of the
  average empirical distribution of $N^{- 1} A$ is given by
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^{n \varepsilon} \left( \frac{1}{N^{k + 1}}
    \mathbb{E}[\ensuremath{\operatorname{Tr}} (A^k)] - \sum_{j = 0}^{n - 1} \frac{1}{N^{j
    \varepsilon}} \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}^{(j)}_k \right) =\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k^{(n)},
    
  \end{equation}
  where for every $j \in \{0, \ldots, n\}$
  \[ \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}^{(j)}_k := \sum_{b_1 + 2 b_2 + \cdots + j \text{} b_j
     = j} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - b_1 - \cdots - b_j} \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k - m
     - b_1 - \cdots - b_j) !b_1 ! \ldots b_j !} \text{{\hspace{8em}}} \]
  \begin{equation}
    \text{{\hspace{14em}}} \times \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'_0
    (x))^{k - m - b_1 - \cdots - b_j} (\Psi'_1 (x))^{b_1} \ldots (\Psi'_j
    (x))^{b_j}) \right|_{x = 0} . 
  \end{equation}

[Lemma lem:dgt4-linearization-from-survival of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Suppose that the scenery variables are independent and identically
	distributed, atomless, centered, and have finite positive variance.
	Fix $T>0$, let $n_R\coloneqq\lfloor R^2T\rfloor$, and let
	$q_{R,j}\in[0,1]$ be deterministic for $0\leq j<n_R$. Suppose that
	as $R\to\infty$,
	\[
		R^{-2}\sum_{j=0}^{n_R-1}
		\mathbf E_0\left|
		\mathbb{P}(S_{n_R,j}(X)=1\mid X)-q_{R,j}
		\right|
		\longrightarrow0,
	\]
	and that there is $C<\infty$ such that, for every $\delta\in(0,T)$, there are
	deterministic numbers $\varepsilon_R(\delta)\geq0$ with
	$\varepsilon_R(\delta)\to0$ as $R\to\infty$ and, uniformly over
	$0\leq i,j\leq n_R-\delta R^2$ and all deterministic nearest-neighbor paths
	$X=(X_0,\ldots,X_i)$ and $Y=(Y_0,\ldots,Y_j)$,
	\[
		\left|
		\Cov(S_{n_R,i}(X),S_{n_R,j}(Y)\mid X,Y)
		\right|
		\leq
		\frac{C}{\delta R^2}
		\sum_{r=0}^i\sum_{h=0}^j\mathbf{1}_{\{X_r=Y_h\}}
		+\varepsilon_R(\delta)\, .
	\]
	Then, for every
	$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$,
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{E}\Biggl[\Biggl(R^{(d-4)/2}\Biggl(
		u_{n_R}-\mathbb{E} u_{n_R}(0)
		-\sum_{j=0}^{n_R-1}q_{R,j}P^j\zeta
		\Biggr)^{(R)}(\varphi)\Biggr)^2\Biggr]
		\longrightarrow0\, .
	\end{equation}
	Consequently, for every $s>(d-4)/2$,
	\[
		R^{(d-4)/2}
		\left(u_{n_R}-\mathbb{E} u_{n_R}(0)
		-\sum_{j=0}^{n_R-1}q_{R,j}P^j\zeta\right)^{(R)}
		\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0
		\quad\text{in }H^{-s}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)\, .
	\]

body:
[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2607.21374, 'Local structure at the maximum and sharp persistence asymptotics of rough fractional Brown'] Let \(a_n\to\infty\) be any deterministic sequence of positive real numbers.
There exist deterministic dyadic numbers \(h_n\downarrow0\), with
\(h_n\leq a_n\), such that, with
\begin{equation}
  \Delta_n:=\frac{h_n}{a_n},\qquad
  M_n:=\left\lfloor\frac{a_n}{h_n}\right\rfloor,
  \qquad
  \mathcal G_n:=\{j\Delta_n:0\leq j\leq M_n\},
  
\end{equation}
the following holds.  If \(K_n\) is the maximising index of \(B\) on
\(\mathcal G_n\), \(\tau_n=K_n\Delta_n\), and
\begin{equation}
  \Xi_n^{\mathrm{grid}}(t)
  :=a_n^H\bigl(B_{\tau_n+t/a_n}-B_{\tau_n}\bigr),
  
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
  d_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Xi_n^{\mathrm{grid}},\Xi_{a_n})\longrightarrow0
  \quad\text{almost surely}.
  
\end{equation}
Moreover, writing \(T_n=M_n\Delta_n\),
\begin{equation}
  a_n\tau_n\longrightarrow\infty,
  \qquad
  a_n(T_n-\tau_n)\longrightarrow\infty
  \quad\text{almost surely}.
  
\end{equation}

if $\dimh E\geq u$.

For $u_t+Lu\le0$ with $Lu=-a^{ij}u_{x_ix_j}+b^iu_{x_i}+cu$, the identity $\max_{\overline{U_T}}u=\max_{\Gamma_T}u$ requires $c\equiv0$; with $c\ge0$ only the weaker $\max_{\overline{U_T}}u\le\max_{\Gamma_T}u^+$ survives; with $c$ of arbitrary sign even that fails. (a) $c<0$ destroys everything: on $U=(0,\pi)$, $u(x,t)=e^t\sin x$ satisfies $u_t-u_{xx}-2u=0$ (so $c=-2$), has $u=0$ on the lateral sides and $u=\sin x\le1$ at $t=0$, hence $\max_{\Gamma_T}u=1$, yet $u(\pi/2,T)=e^T$ is arbitrarily large. (b) $c\ge0$ genuinely needs the positive part: on $U=(0,\pi)$ let $u$ solve $u_t-u_{xx}+u=0$ with $u\equiv-1$ on $\Gamma_T$ (initial and lateral data $-1$). Then $w=u+1$ solves $w_t-w_{xx}+w=1$ with $w=0$ on $\Gamma_T$, so $w\ge0$ by the $c\ge0$ principle and $w\not\equiv0$; hence $\max_{\overline{U_T}}u>-1=\max_{\Gamma_T}u$, while indeed $\max u\le0=\max_{\Gamma_T}u^+$. (c) What always survives for bounded $c$ of any sign is the comparison principle: $u_t+Lu\le0$ and $u\le0$ on $\Gamma_T$ imply $u\le0$, because $v=e^{-\gamma t}u$ solves an inequality with zeroth-order coefficient $c+\gamma\ge0$ for $\gamma\ge\|c^-\|_\infty$. Uniqueness for the initial-boundary value problem therefore holds for any bounded $c$; it is only the location of extrema that needs the sign condition. Auditor's check: whenever a proof cites 'the maximum principle' for an equation with a reaction term, ask which of (a), (b), (c) is actually being used, and note that the sign convention depends on whether the operator is written $u_t-\Delta u+cu$ or $u_t-\Delta u-cu$.
Sign convention: L u = -a^{ij} u_{x_i x_j} + b^i u_{x_i} + c u, subsolution means u_t + Lu <= 0
c identically zero for the full maximum principle
c >= 0 for the version with the positive part
bounded c of any sign for the comparison (sign) principle only
title: Pitfall: The Parabolic Maximum Principle needs a sign condition on the zeroth-order coefficient

[Lemma Lem E eps 1 eps 2 bound v of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $z_1\neq z_2\in D$
and $r_0>0$ such that the disks
$\overline{\mathbb{D}(z_1,r_0)}$ and $\overline{\mathbb{D}(z_2,r_0)}$
are disjoint and contained in $D$.
There is a constant
$c=c(D,z_1,z_2,r_0)>0$ 
(depending on $D$, $z_1$, $z_2$ and $r_0$),
such that for every $v\in\mathbb{R}$,
and for every $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\in (0,r_0]$,
$$
\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^v)
\leq
\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^0)
e^{-c v^2}.
$$

In particular, let $\mathcal{V}$ be a countable subset of $\mathbb{R}$ and 
$a:\mathcal{V}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$.
Then assuming that for every $b>0$,
$$
\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}
\vert a(v)\vert e^{-b v^2}
<+\infty,
$$
we have that as $\max(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\to 0$,
$$
\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}
a(v)\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^v)
=
\varepsilon_1^{1/8}
\varepsilon_2^{1/8}
(\mathbf{C}_{\rm{SLE}4}^{\rm loop})^2
\,
\sigma_{\rm tw}^D(z_1,z_2)
\,
\Big(
\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}a(v)
e^{-v^2 \mathcal{M}_D(z_1,z_2)}
\Big)
(1+o(1)).
$$

body: Let gamma be the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. The ORNSTEIN-UHLENBECK SEMIGROUP is defined by MEHLER'S FORMULA P_t f(x) = integral f( e^{-t} x + sqrt(1 - e^{-2t}) y ) gamma(dy) for t >= 0. It is a Markov semigroup: P_0 = identity, P_{s+t} = P_s P_t, P_t 1 = 1, P_t preserves nonnegativity, gamma is INVARIANT (integral P_t f dgamma = integral f dgamma), and P_t is SELF-ADJOINT on L^2(gamma). Its generator is L f = Laplacian f - x . grad f, which satisfies the integration-by-parts identity integral (L u) v dgamma = - integral grad u . grad v dgamma. The Hermite polynomials diagonalise it: L He_alpha = - |alpha| He_alpha and P_t He_alpha = e^{-|alpha| t} He_alpha, so the n-th Wiener chaos is the eigenspace of eigenvalue -n. The COMMUTATION RELATION grad P_t f = e^{-t} P_t grad f follows by differentiating Mehler's formula under the integral. Two facts to keep straight: this is the semigroup for the standard Gaussian, and other normalisations of the generator (for example Laplacian/2 minus x . grad/2) rescale time and change the constants in the associated Poincare and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities. As t -> infinity, P_t f -> integral f dgamma, and the exponential rate of that convergence in L^2 is exactly 1, the spectral gap, which is the Gaussian Poincare inequality. [standard; e.g. Bakry, Gentil and Ledoux, Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators, Section 2.7]

[Proposition 61 of arXiv:2608.12947, 'Branch-stationary max-stable fields on rooted trees'] The field
\begin{equation}
  U_v^\psi
  =
  \psi\left(
    \frac{\eta_v^{-\alpha}}{S_\psi}
  \right),
  \qquad v\in\mathcal T,
  
\end{equation}
has standard uniform margins and finite-dimensional copulas
\((C_K^\psi)\). In particular, these copulas extend continuously to
\([0,1]^K\) and form a projectively consistent family of Archimax
copulas.
 
The following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item \(\eta\) is branch-stationary;
\item for every non-empty finite \(K\subset\mathcal T\),
\begin{equation}
  \ell_{aK}(x^a)=\ell_K(x),
  \qquad
  a\in\mathcal T,\quad x\in[0,\infty)^K;
  
\end{equation}
\item for every non-empty finite \(K\subset\mathcal T\),
\[
  C_{aK}(u^a)=C_K(u),
  \qquad
  a\in\mathcal T,\quad u\in(0,1]^K;
\]

DRAFT proof-audit material, independent referee check pending. For every integer d>=1 and epsilon>0 there exists a stationary finite-dependent {0,1} field on Z^d with probability of good at each vertex at least 1-epsilon and all nearest-neighbour good components finite. Construct it from iid Bernoulli(q) seeds. L(v) is a nearest seed in the l-infinity ball B_R(v), with lexicographic tie-breaking, or bottom if the ball is empty. A vertex is good exactly when its non-bottom label agrees with every nearest neighbour's label. Its indicator uses seeds in B_(R+1)(v), so index sets at l-infinity distance greater than 2(R+1) are independent. Each good component has one seed label s and lies in B_R(s). For a finite dimension-dependent constant K_d, P(v bad)<=exp(-q(2R-1)^d) +K_d q^(1/d); choosing q small then R large gives the claimed density. The dependence range varies with epsilon. This is correlated site percolation and does not refute iid critical bond percolation or a fixed-range domination theorem.
d is an integer>=1
iid seeds with 0<q<1

[Corollary cor:universal-principal-skeleton of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $h\geq2$ and $k\geq3$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R^{[0]}(h,k)=\{M_{h,k}\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal R^{[1]}(h,k)
 =\{M_{h,k}-M_{h-r,k}:2\leq r\leq h\}.
\end{equation}
In particular, exactly $h$ attainable cardinalities have minimum active
rank at most one.  They are exactly the values whose realization-frequency
quasipolynomial has degree greater than $k-2$: the maximum has degree $k$,
the other $h-1$ values have degree $k-1$, and every remaining attainable
cardinality has degree at most $k-2$.

Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a stably triangulated category with coproducts and $E \in \mathcal{T}$. An object $X$ is $E$-acyclic if $E \otimes X = 0$. An object $Y$ is $E$-local if $\operatorname{Hom}(X, Y) = 0$ for all $E$-acyclic $X$. A Bousfield localization with respect to $E$ is an exact functor $L_E: \mathcal{T} \to \mathcal{T}$ equipped with a natural transformation $\eta: \operatorname{id} \to L_E$ such that for every $X$, $L_E X$ is $E$-local and the fiber of $\eta_X$ is $E$-acyclic.
\mathcal{T} is a tensor-triangulated category with coproducts

title: Bousfield Localization Functor in Triangulated Categories

body: In mathematics, the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma is a result named after William B. Johnson and Joram Lindenstrauss concerning low-distortion embeddings of points from high-dimensional into low-dimensional Euclidean space. The lemma states that a set of points in a high-dimensional space can be embedded into a space of much lower dimension in such a way that distances between the points are nearly preserved. In the classical proof of the lemma, the embedding is a random orthogonal projection.
title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma

body:
[Proposition prop:root-sweep-dictionary of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $h\geq1$ and $k\geq2$.  One has the exact difference identity
\begin{equation}
 E_{h,k}-E_{h,k}=h\mathsf R_{k-1}\cap\mathsf A_{k-1}.
\end{equation}
For an ordered real tuple $a=(a_1<\cdots<a_k)$, write
\({\bf1}=(1,\ldots,1)\in\mathbb R^k\) and let
$a^\circ=a-k^{-1}(\sum_i a_i){\bf1}$ be its centered representative.  Let
$F_h(a)$ be the face of $\mathfrak Z_{h,k}$ exposed by $a^\circ$.  The
following data determine one another:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item the total preorder on $E_{h,k}$ induced by $u\mapsto u\cdot a$
      (equivalently, its ordered weak partition into level sets);
\item the complete ordered $h$-addition table of $a$, including ties;
\item the face $F_h(a)$.
\end{enumerate}
The dimension of $F_h(a)$ is the active relation rank $r_h(a)$.  In the
ambient space ${\bf1}^{\perp}$, its normal cone has dimension
$k-1-r_h(a)$, and the relative interior of that cone consists precisely of
the centered weights inducing the same complete table.  Moreover, the same
face determines every ordered addition table in degrees $1\leq j\leq h$.

Fix any field $K$.  If $a\in\mathbb Z^k$, put
$A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and define
\[
 \varphi_a:K[x_1,\ldots,x_k]\longrightarrow K[u,t,t^{-1}],
 \qquad x_i\longmapsto u t^{a_i},
 \qquad I_a=\ker\varphi_a,
\]
where $\deg u=1$ and $\deg t=0$.  Then the number of blocks in the face
label is the Hilbert value
\begin{equation}
 |hA|=\dim_K\bigl(K[x_1,\ldots,x_k]/I_a\bigr)_h.
\end{equation}
Thus the face records the equality rank and Hilbert/block label, while its
normal cone encodes the normalized shape, realization frequency, and integer
compression developed below.

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2607.06428, 'Impact of spinning on the early-warning signs in non-Markovian stochastic systems'] A stochastic process $(\mathbf{x}_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is called strictly stationary or strongly stationary if for all $k\ge0$ and all sequences $(t_1,\dots, t_m)\in\R^m_+$ we have
    $$(\mathbf{x}_{t_1},\dots,\mathbf{x}_{t_m})\overset{d}{=}(\mathbf{x}_{t_1+k},\dots,\mathbf{x}_{t_m+k}).$$
   The process $(\mathbf{x}_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is called second order stationary or weakly stationary, if we have for all $t\in\R$ $\E[|\mathbf{x}_t|]<\infty,~\E[|\mathbf{x}_t|^2]<\infty$ and for all $s,t,\tau\ge0$
    $$V_t(\tau)=V_s(\tau).$$
    As the autocovariance only depends on $\tau$, we drop the subscript and write $V(\tau)$ whenever we consider a stationary process.
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2607.06428

Pourkamali-Macris Proposition3, independent-spectra version of the source coupling. Fix positive integers N<=M and lambda>0. Let sigma,sigma_tilde in[0,infinity)^N be independent random singular-value vectors, each with finite second moment. Let U in O(N),V in O(M) be independent normalized Haar matrices, independent of both vectors. Define S=U*diag_{N by M}(sigma)*V^T and S_tilde=U*diag_{N by M}(sigma_tilde)*V^T, so the pair shares its singular vectors. Let P_1,P_2 be the respective marginal signal priors. For j=1,2, take Y_j=sqrt(lambda)*S_j+G_j with iid N(0,1/N) Gaussian entries independent of the signal. Define Z_j(y)=E_{X~P_j} exp(N*sqrt(lambda)*Tr(X^T*y)-(N*lambda/2)*||X||_F^2), where the inner X is an independent prior draw, and F_j(lambda)=-(N*M)^(-1)*E log Z_j(Y_j) with expectation under the matching planted model. Then |F_1(lambda)-F_2(lambda)| <= (lambda/(2*N))*(sqrt(E||sigma||_2^2)+sqrt(E||sigma_tilde||_2^2))*sqrt(E||sigma-sigma_tilde||_2^2). The last expectation is over the independent spectral pair specified above, with its chosen coordinate ordering. The result is finite-dimensional; it does not by itself justify a limiting spectral-atom extension or convergence in expectation from mere weak convergence.
Finite N<=M and lambda>0.
Independent nonnegative spectral vectors with finite second moments; common independent Haar singular vectors.
Variance1/N iid Gaussian observation noise independent of each signal.

Consider testing a simple null hypothesis H0: X has density f0 against a simple alternative H1: X has density f1 (with respect to a common dominating measure), at a fixed significance level alpha in (0,1). Define a test with rejection rule: reject H0 when f1(x) > k f0(x); accept H0 when f1(x) < k f0(x); and reject with some probability gamma in [0,1] when f1(x) = k f0(x); where the constant k >= 0 and the randomization probability gamma are chosen so that the test has size exactly alpha, i.e. Pr(reject H0 | H0) = alpha. Then this likelihood-ratio test is most powerful at level alpha: for every other test phi with size at most alpha, the power of phi under H1 is no greater than the power of the likelihood-ratio test.
H0 and H1 are simple hypotheses with densities f0, f1 with respect to a common dominating measure
significance level alpha lies strictly between 0 and 1

[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2608.30875, 'A Decomposition Theorem for Topological Semi-small Maps'] Let $f:X \longrightarrow Y$ be an almost covering map, where $X$ is a closed topological manifold and $Y$ is a closed topological pseudomanifold. Suppose the fibered set $R = \bigsqcup_{\beta} T_{\beta} \subset Y$ is equipped with a suitable decomposition. Assume that $R$ is a closed topologically stratified space of codimension greater than or equal to $2$. Let $R = \bigsqcup_{\alpha} S_{\alpha}$, $T_{\beta} = \bigsqcup_{\gamma} V^{\beta}_{\gamma}\ \text{for each } \beta$, and 
	$Y = \bigsqcup_{\eta} W_{\eta}$
	be intrinsic stratifications. Furthermore, assume that the inclusion $R \xhookrightarrow[]{\phantom{.} i \phantom{.} } Y$ is locally flat. Then the decomposition
	\begin{align}
	Y = \bigl( W_{\eta_{\text{top}}} \setminus (R \cap W_{\eta_{\text{top}}}) \bigr) \;\bigsqcup_{\alpha,\eta,\beta,\gamma}\; \bigl( W_{\eta} \cap V^{\beta}_{\gamma} \cap S_{\alpha}\bigr)
	\end{align}
	is a refined stratification on $Y$, where $W_{\eta_{\text{top}}}$ denotes the top stratum of $Y$.

Let H and K be Hilbert spaces. A bounded operator T: H -> K is Hilbert-Schmidt if sum_{i in I} ||T e_i||^2 < infinity for some orthonormal basis (e_i)_{i in I} of H. The sum is then the same for every orthonormal basis of H, and ||T||_2 = (sum_i ||T e_i||^2)^{1/2} is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Equivalently, T is compact and sum_n s_n(T)^2 < infinity, with ||T||_2^2 = sum_n s_n(T)^2. Properties: ||T|| <= ||T||_2; ||T*||_2 = ||T||_2; every Hilbert-Schmidt operator is compact (it is the ||.||_2-limit, hence operator-norm limit, of finite-rank operators); the Hilbert-Schmidt operators S_2(H,K) form a Hilbert space under <A,B>_2 = sum_i <A e_i, B e_i> = tr(B*A), independent of the basis; and they form an ideal: ||A T B||_2 <= ||A|| ||T||_2 ||B|| for bounded A, B. Basis independence follows from sum_i ||T e_i||^2 = sum_i sum_j |<T e_i, f_j>|^2 = sum_j ||T* f_j||^2 for any orthonormal basis (f_j) of K.
H and K are Hilbert spaces
T: H -> K is a bounded linear operator

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, The discrepancy of Sylvester-Hadamard matrices in odd dimension (October 2026), proves that for the 2^k x 2^k Sylvester-Hadamard matrix H_k, disc(H_k) = 2^k - 2 rho(1,k), where rho(1,k) is the covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,k). With the known values and bounds for that covering radius this settles Conjecture 13 of Randomstrasse101, Open problems of 2024 (arXiv:2504.20539): disc(H_k) = 2^((k+1)/2) holds for k = 1, 3, 5, 7 and fails for every odd k >= 9, where disc(H_k) <= (7/8) 2^((k+1)/2); in particular disc(H_9) <= 28 < 32. An exhaustive check for k <= 4 accompanies the paper. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/hadamard-discrepancy-odd (commit 0ec54610b38a). Not refereed.

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For Bernoulli percolation, and more generally for FKG-satisfying, translation-invariant models with finite energy (including the random-cluster model for cluster weight q>=1), the sharpness-of-phase-transition theorem shows that below the critical point p_c, the probability of connection to distance n decays exponentially in n, proved without duality via a finite-size criterion: a box functional phi_p(S), built from crossing probabilities and a weighted sum over pivotal edges, is shown to satisfy a differential inequality in p that forces it to either stay bounded (subcritical, exponential decay) or blow up past a threshold (supercritical), with the threshold identified as p_c. This unifies and reproves the classical results of Menshikov and of Aizenman-Barsky with a single argument that is robust enough to extend to Z^d for every d, to general transitive graphs, and to the random-cluster model. The theorem does not give the exact value of p_c, does not determine critical behavior exactly at p_c (critical exponents are a separate, generally much harder, question), and the exponential-decay rate produced is not claimed to be sharp or explicit. Typical failure: Assuming the Duminil-Copin-Tassion argument extends automatically to a non-FKG regime, such as random-cluster parameters q<1 or certain long-range or antiferromagnetic models, where positive association fails; the driving differential inequality depends essentially on FKG-type monotonicity and on finite energy, and dropping either hypothesis breaks the exponential-decay conclusion outright rather than merely weakening it. Canonical reference: Duminil-Copin and Tassion, 2016, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Duminil-Copin, Raoufi and Tassion, 2019, Annals of Mathematics.

the FKG inequality for the measure, which for the random-cluster model restricts to cluster weight q>=1
finite energy, or an analogous positive-conditional-probability condition, for the percolation-type model

[Proposition prop:covbounds of arXiv:2608.16915, 'Exact mean--covariance dynamics of the Weber field in the stochastic Lagrangian representa'] Let $\sigma_J:=\sup_x(\tr Q(x))^{1/2}$ and
$L_J:=\sup_x(\mathbb{E}\left\lvert J(x)\right\rvert_{\mathrm F}^2)^{1/2}\le\sigma_J+\sqrt3\,\left\lVert M\right\rVert_{L^\infty}$, and
for $0<\beta\le1$ set
\[
  \mathsf H_{J,\beta}:=\sup_{x\ne y}
  \frac{\bigl(\mathbb{E}\left\lvert \widetilde J(x)-\widetilde J(y)\right\rvert_{\mathrm F}^2\bigr)^{1/2}}{d(x,y)^\beta},
\]
where $d$ is the geodesic distance on $\mathbb{T}^3$. Then
$\left\lVert \mathcal R\right\rVert_{L^\infty}\le\left\lVert u_0\right\rVert_{L^\infty}\sigma_J$, and there is a dimensional
constant $C$ such that
\begin{equation}
  \left\lVert \mathcal R\right\rVert_{C^\beta}\le C\Big[
  \left\lVert u_0\right\rVert_{L^\infty}(\sigma_J+\mathsf H_{J,\beta})
  +\left\lVert \nabla u_0\right\rVert_{L^\infty}\,\sigma_J\bigl(\sigma_J+\sqrt3\,\left\lVert M\right\rVert_{L^\infty}\bigr)\Big].
\end{equation}

It is named after the German mathematician Karl Weierstrass (1815–1897).

Let d>=2, K=(d+1)(d+2), X be uniform on Delta_d={x_i>=0,sum_i x_i<=1}, m=(1,...,1)/(d+1), Sigma=(I-J/(d+1))/K with J the all-ones matrix, A=Sigma^(-1/2), Y=A(X-m), a=sqrt(2K), and v=Ae_1/a. Put Z=Proj_(v-perp)Y, T=<v,Y> and S=sum_(j=2)^d X_j. For every integer k>=1 put t=1-S, f(Y)=T t^k and M_p=(p+1)! d!/(d+p)!. Then E[f|Z]=0, E Var(f|Z)=(K/6) M_(2k+2), E|partial_v f|^2=M_(2k), and E|grad f|^2=[1+k^2(d-1)/(3(d+1))] M_(2k). Thus the exact directional quotient is R_(d,k)=(K/6)(2k+2)(2k+3)/[(d+2k+1)(d+2k+2)], while the full-gradient quotient is R_(d,k)/[1+k^2(d-1)/(3(d+1))]. The extra factor is the transverse gradient cost: grad_Y S is perpendicular to v and has squared norm 2(d-1)/((d+1)K). For d=2,k=2 these give variance 1/2, directional energy 1/3 and full energy 13/27. The family generalizes the separately submitted triangle witness and explicitly preserves all gradient terms.

For a sequence of random vectors x_p in R^p and Gaussian comparison vectors g_p distributed as N(mu_p,Sigma_p), a sequence of symmetric convex sets S_p subset R^p is a domain of Gaussianity if, for every fixed bounded Lipschitz function phi:R->R, sup_{theta in S_p}|E phi(theta^T x_p)-E phi(theta^T g_p)| tends to zero as p tends to infinity. The supremum is over deterministic directions in the entire stated domain. This definition does not assert that projections at directions fitted using the same observations are Gaussian. Coordinate delocalization is an example of a domain condition for suitable independent-coordinate laws, not the definition for arbitrary dependent features.
Sequences indexed by p; symmetric convex comparison domains and a specified Gaussian law.
The limit holds for every fixed bounded Lipschitz scalar test function, uniformly over the domain.

body: The GAUSSIAN ORTHOGONAL ENSEMBLE GOE_n is the law of a real symmetric n by n matrix H whose entries are independent up to symmetry with H_{ii} distributed as N(0, 2/n) and H_{ij} distributed as N(0, 1/n) for i < j. Its density with respect to Lebesgue measure on the space of real symmetric matrices is proportional to exp( - (n/4) trace(H^2) ), and the law is invariant under H -> O H O^T for every orthogonal O. The GAUSSIAN UNITARY ENSEMBLE GUE_n is the law of a Hermitian H with H_{ii} distributed as N(0, 1/n) real and, for i < j, H_{ij} = x + i y with x and y independent N(0, 1/(2n)), so that E|H_{ij}|^2 = 1/n; its density is proportional to exp( - (n/2) trace(H^2) ) and it is invariant under H -> U H U^* for every unitary U. With THESE normalisations the empirical spectral distribution of either ensemble converges to the semicircle law on [-2, 2], the largest eigenvalue converges to 2, and the edge fluctuations are of order n^{-2/3} with Tracy-Widom limits (beta = 1 for GOE, beta = 2 for GUE). The DIAGONAL VARIANCE DIFFERS BETWEEN THE TWO ENSEMBLES - 2/n for GOE, 1/n for GUE - and that is what makes both densities come out as the invariant exponential of the trace; getting it wrong changes the density but not the limiting spectral law. Normalisation conventions vary widely across the literature: some authors use unnormalised entries of variance 1 and divide by sqrt(n) afterwards, some put the semicircle on [-1,1] or [-2 sqrt(2), 2 sqrt(2)], and some use exp(-trace(H^2)/2) with n absorbed elsewhere. Any imported constant must be checked against the convention it was derived under. [standard; e.g. Anderson, Guionnet and Zeitouni, An Introduction to Random Matrices, Sections 2.5 and 2.6]

[Lemma lem:fs_coupling of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] There are some constants $D, C, c > 0$ such that the following holds
for all $T, S > 0$ satisfying $D S^{3/2} < T$.
Let $X$ denote a Ferrari--Spohn diffusion on $[-T,T]$ with boundary conditions
$X(\pm T) \leqslant S$.
Then
for all $t \in [D S^{3/2},T]$,
$X$ may be coupled with the stationary Ferrari--Spohn diffusion $Y_{\mathrm{FS}}$
such that we have
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P} \mleft[ X(s) = Y_{\mathrm{FS}}(s) \text{ for all } |s| \leqslant T - t \mright]
    \geqslant 1 - C e^{- c t}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Coupling with a stationary process

body:
[Defn 1 of arXiv:2608.13208, 'Universality in dimension $1$ of kinetically constrained lattice gases'] A kinetically constrained lattice gas is a Markov
process on $\Omega=\{0,1\}^{\Z}$ with generator 
\begin{equation}
\cL f(\eta)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x,y\in\Z}c(x,y,\eta)(f(\eta^{xy})-f(\eta)),
\end{equation}
where $\eta^{xy}$ is the configuration after exchanging $x$ and
$y$. The rates are given by the \emph{constraint function} $c:\Z\times\Z\times\Omega\to[0,\infty]$
satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Nearest-neighbor jumps: $c(x,y,\eta)=0$ if $\left|x-y\right|\neq1$.
By convention $c(x,y,\eta)=c(y,x,\eta)$.
\item Translation invariance: $c(x,y,\eta)=c(x+z,y+z,\tau_{z}\eta)$ for
all $x,y,z$, where $\tau_{z}$ is the translation by $z$.
\item $c(x,y,\eta)$ does not depend on the occupation at $x$ and $y$,
i.e., $c(x,y,\eta)=c(x,y,\eta^{xy})$.
\item Finite range: there exists $r>0$ such that $c(x,y,\eta)$ depends
only on the configuration in $x+[-r,r]$.
\item Monotonicity: if $\eta(x)\le\omega(x)$ for all $x$, then $c(x,y,\eta)\ge c(x,y,\omega)$.
That is, adding vacancies speeds up transitions.
\end{enumerate}
We can also define the process on a finite segment $[a,b]$ of $\Z$
by fixing boundary conditions; in this article we always consider
filled boundary, i.e., for $x,y\in[a,b]$ the constraint in the segment
is given by $c_{[a,b]}(x,y,\eta)=c(x,y,\tilde{\eta})$ where $\tilde{\eta}$
agrees with $\eta$ on $[a,b]$ and equals $1$ outside.

body:
Let X be a nonempty COMPACT metrizable space and let T : X -> X be continuous. Then T admits at least one invariant Borel probability measure: there exists a Borel probability mu on X with mu(T inverse of A) = mu(A) for every Borel A. The set of such measures is nonempty, convex and weak-* compact, and its extreme points are exactly the ERGODIC invariant measures; by the Krein-Milman theorem an ergodic measure therefore exists as well.
COMPACTNESS of X and CONTINUITY of T are both essential - a continuous map of a non-compact space may have no invariant probability measure (translation on R is the standard example), and a merely measurable map of a compact space may have none either.
No hypothesis of minimality, transitivity or the existence of a reference measure is needed.

body: The expectation of a random variable X is E[X] = integral X dP (sum x P(X=x) in the discrete case, integral x f(x) dx with a density). It is linear (E[aX + bY] = aE[X] + bE[Y]) even without independence, monotone, and satisfies the law of the unconscious statistician E[g(X)] = integral g dP_X. For independent X, Y, E[XY] = E[X]E[Y]. Expectation exists when E|X| < infinity.
title: Expectation (Expected Value)

[Definition def:block of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] A whitened system $\{(\xi_i,\eta_i)\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ has \emph{orthogonal
circuit-block structure} with dimension vector $r=(r_1,\dots,r_s)$,
$\sum_jr_j=d$, if
$\mathbb{R}^d=E_1\oplus^{\perp}\dots\oplus^{\perp}E_s$ with $\dim E_j=r_j$, every
nonzero feature lies in some $E_j$, and every $E_j$ contains a positive
circuit of $r_j+1$ gradients spanning $E_j$. Here a positive circuit of
gradients means a set of indices whose gradients $g_i=\eta_i\xi_i$ carry a
strictly positive zero-sum relation, minimal with respect to support. Write
$I_j=\{i:\xi_i\in E_j\setminus\{0\}\}$ and
$R_j=\frac1N\sum_{i\in I_j}\eta_i^2$, so $\sum_jR_j\le1$; points with
$\xi_i=0$ belong to no block. The \emph{model class} $\mathcal D_r$ consists
of the datasets $D$ with full feature rank and $L_D^{\star}>0$ whose whitened system
under Lemma~(lem:whiten of the paper) has orthogonal circuit-block structure with
dimension vector $r$.
title: Definition def:block of arXiv:2608.28007

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. A nearest-neighbour proxy for the bias shift (P35, the simplex's out-of-fold residuals at the nearest calibration rows standing in for its bias at the scored rows): P35 (a) REFUTED: the full-shift blend reads -0.69 vs the R-blend on EMIT split B and -0.12 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.08 and -0.14 on split C; (c) REFUTED: cross-only vs full on EMIT -0.05 vs -0.62 (split B); falsifier (either variant worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. Scarce calibration, the ratio-metric criterion (P41, 240 calibration rows, split B, three-vertex form, registered and R_1 choices side by side): P41 (a) HELD: at n_cal = 240 the R_1 blend reads +1.17 vs the simplex on EMIT (within 1.0; the registered three-vertex blend reads -1.83); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R_1 blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells (at least 25); (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on EMIT +1.38 (at least +1.0); falsifier (R_1 worse than the simplex by more than 2.0 on EMIT) not triggered. So the P30 caveat is confined to the squared-loss criterion; the criterion in the score's own metric keeps the simplex where it should at scarce calibration. Let V be a finite honeycomb vertex set, E the edges with both endpoints in V, H the boundary mid-edges with exactly one endpoint in V, and c the number of components of (V,E). Prescribe complex g on H and b_v=sum_{h in H incident to v}(h-v)g(h). Arbitrary complex interior midpoint values F satisfying sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F(p)=0 exist iff sum_{v in C}b_v=0 on every component C. If solvable, their complex affine dimension is |E|-|V|+c. For a connected plane graph this equals the number of bounded faces. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
Finite honeycomb graph; arbitrary complex midpoint fields

body: Two hubs whose remainder crosses a split (bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture). Let X_H in R^2 and X' be independent with independent coordinates of densities <= 1, L = M X' in R^2, R(X') = X'^T A_R X' + b^T X' + c any real quadratic. Split the light coordinates into I, J; let M_J (columns in J) have singular values s_1' >= s_2' > 0, Pi the projection onto the row space of M_J, and C = (A_R)_{I,J} (Id - Pi) with rows c_i. If F = ||C||_F > 0 and |c_i|^2 <= F^2/2, then for every symmetric 2 x 2 B and beta, Q = X_H^T B X_H + 2 <X_H, L + beta> + R satisfies |phi_Q(eta)| <= pi^{3/2} 2^{5/4} (s_1' s_2' F)^{-1/2} |eta|^{-3/2} and ||p_Q||_inf <= 5.35 (s_1' s_2' F)^{-1/3}. Twists inside either half are free. The same decoupling with one hub gives |phi_Q| <= 2 pi (|w_J| F)^{-1/2} |eta|^{-1} and P(|Q - s| <= delta) <= C delta log(1/delta) for every remainder (Proposition 6.6), and |eta|^{-3/2} when the projected crossing block has rank two (Proposition 6.8).

Let $X_1,\dots,X_m$ be iid random rows in $\mathbb{R}^m$ and let $S, T$ be two distinct $(m-1)$-subsets of row indices. Put $A = S \cap T$, $B = S \setminus T$, $C = T \setminus S$ and $D = m - |A|$, so that $|B| = |C| = D - 1$. Condition on the rows indexed by $A$, let $E_A = \operatorname{span}(A)^{\perp}$, which has dimension $D$ almost surely, and let $Q_A : \mathbb{R}^D \to E_A \subset \mathbb{R}^m$ be any isometry (an $m \times D$ matrix with orthonormal columns). Then the unit null normals $u_S, u_T$ of the two $(m-1) \times m$ row submatrices satisfy $u_S = Q_A v$ and $u_T = Q_A w$, where $v, w \in S^{D-1}$ are the null directions of the residual matrices $U = B Q_A$ and $V = C Q_A$. Conditionally on $A$ the matrices $U$ and $V$ are independent, each with iid rows of law $Q_A^{\top} X$, and the pair correlation is preserved exactly: $\rho_{ST}^2 = \langle u_S, u_T \rangle^2 = \langle v, w \rangle^2$. Writing $M_A = \mathbb{E}[v v^{\top} \mid A]$ for the conditional second-moment matrix of the residual null line, $\mathbb{E}[\langle v,w\rangle^2 \mid A] = \operatorname{tr}(M_A^2)$. The content of the lemma is that a pair correlated only through a shared part becomes, after conditioning on that part, two independent objects in the lower dimension $D$ that measures exactly how much the two index sets fail to overlap.

Load-bearing hypotheses: the periodization $Pf(x)=\sum_nf(x+n)$ must be continuous at the point where the identity is evaluated, and its Fourier series must converge there (absolute summability of $(\hat f(k))_k$ is the usual sufficient condition). For a general $f\in L^1(\mathbb R)$ all that is true is $\widehat{Pf}(k)=\hat f(k)$, i.e. Poisson summation as an identity of Fourier series of an $L^1(\mathbb T)$ function - which says nothing pointwise. Concrete failure: $f=\mathbf 1_{[0,1]}$ (with $f(0)=f(1)=1$). Then $\sum_nf(n)=f(0)+f(1)=2$, while $\hat f(0)=1$ and $\hat f(k)=\int_0^1e^{-2\pi ikx}dx=0$ for $k\ne0$, so $\sum_k\hat f(k)=1\ne2$. The periodization equals $1$ off $\mathbb Z$ and $2$ on $\mathbb Z$: it is discontinuous exactly where the identity is being evaluated, and the Fourier series converges to the midpoint $1$. Redefining $f(0)=f(1)=1/2$ restores the identity. Second trap: pure decay of $f$ is not enough - one needs decay (or summability) on the transform side as well, since the right-hand series must converge; $f$ continuous and integrable with $\hat f$ merely tending to zero gives no pointwise statement. When quoting a rate, the clean hypothesis is $|f(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ and $|\hat f(\xi)|\le C(1+|\xi|)^{-1-\delta}$ with $f$ continuous, or simply $f\in\mathcal S$.

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Gaussian extensive-rank product reference has a C1 MI limit and pointwise MMSE limit for all positive finite aspect ratios, proof unaudited. For B=UV^T/sqrt(N), independent real standard Gaussian factors, P/N->alpha>0, M/N->beta>0, normalized MI converges to a C1 function on s>0 and normalized MMSE converges to twice its derivative. In canonical n<=p, p/n->kappa>1, gamma=1/kappa, rho_t is the symmetric positive-singular law of UV^T/n+sqrt(t/n)G; i(s)=E_gamma(rho_(1/s))+(log s)/2-E_gamma(noise), and m(s)=1/s-Phi_gamma(1/s)/s^2. Real Wishart output laws, gap/density regularity025, entropy chain rule026 and calibration027 separately pay the premises. Near-square sequences use022; transpose and SNR rescaling handle alpha<1. Together with006/023, every fixed centered iid finite-second-moment unit-variance factor pair has limsup per-entry MI and MMSE excess over Gaussian <=0 at every fixed s>=0. Noncentered and dimension-dependent priors are not asserted. Novelty unestablished.
Independent real Gaussian reference factors and standard Gaussian channel noise.
Positive finite limiting P/N and M/N.
For the extremality consequence, fixed centered iid unit-variance factor laws with finite second moments and independent factor arrays.
Proof dependencies006,017,022-027 remain unaudited.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ff69908262824ba48716cbe4d812386b2868967019e642923e44a45d36eb896a","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ff/ff69908262824ba48716cbe4d812386b2868967019e642923e44a45d36eb896a.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9548f3adc68903b67cd441efcd18bebcb2f7ac02a496d314a765992a9a4498a7","bundle_entry_key":"gaussian-product-all-aspects-mi-c1-mmse-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-rectangular-reference-c1-and-noncentered-comparison-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:gaussian-product-all-aspects-mi-c1-mmse-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Gaussian extensive-rank reference: all positive finite aspect ratios

Claim draft w718-T287-028, version 1. Kind: moved; target: 2. Status: proof (unaudited). Every earlier dependency is also unaudited. Novelty is unestablished. This completes the rectangular-reference route conditional on the supporting proofs, and gives a centered finite-variance partial answer to the dossier wording. Noncentered priors are not included here because centering is not explicit in that wording. Target1 remains open.

## Statement

Let independent standard real Gaussian U,V have sizes N by M and P by M, with P/N->alpha>0 and M/N->beta>0 finite. Set B=UV^T/sqrt(N), with independent standard Gaussian channel noise G. Then

i_N(s)=I(B;sqrt(s)B+G)/(NP)

has a pointwise limit i(s), continuously differentiable for every s>0. The normalized Gaussian-reference product risk m_N(s)=E||B-E[B|sqrt(s)B+G]||F^2/(NP) converges to 2i'(s) at every such s. At zero it tends to beta.

Consequently for independent iid factor arrays with fixed centered unit-variance real laws and finite second moments, at the same dimensions and noise level,

limsup_N [m_iid,N(s)-m_N(s)]<=0 for every fixed s>=0,      (1)

and likewise limsup_N[i_iid,N(s)-i_N(s)]<=0. Gaussian factors thus maximize both limiting comparisons in this centered fixed-law class; no finite-dimensional extremality is claimed. The conclusion allows a risk limsup without assuming existence of the iid-prior risk limit. The scaling is UV^T/sqrt(N); raw UV^T loss must be divided by N.

The hardest new step is the real rectangular reference C1 limit. Its most delicate dependencies are the physical boundary-branch continuation in claim025 and the logarithmic chain rule in claim026. The present proof separates those steps from MI calibration and from derivative convergence.

## 1. Canonical strictly rectangular dimensions

First take n<=p, p/n->kappa>1, M/n->b>0. Let S=UV^T/n, Z entries iid N(0,1/n). Signal B_c=sqrt(n)S is the canonical entry-scaled product. For t>0 let rho_t be the symmetrized limiting law of the n singular values of S+sqrt(t)Z. Supporting claims024-025 show compact support, a uniform gap at zero on compact positive heat intervals, bounded density, and the boundary/transport regularity needed by claim026. The source is the real conditional population-Wishart representation; no complex-to-real freeness theorem is used.

Put gamma=1/kappa and let rho_noise be the symmetric singular law of Z. Write

E_gamma(rho)=gamma Sigma(rho)+(1-gamma)integral log|x|rho(dx).

For s>0 the limiting observation law of sqrt(s)S+Z is the dilation D_sqrt(s) rho_(1/s). We claim its normalized MI limit is

i_c(s)=E_gamma(rho_(1/s))+(log s)/2-E_gamma(rho_noise).   (2)

The next two steps pay the expected-W2 and unbounded-input premises of calibration027, so (2) is not an assumed information formula.

## 2. Expected spectral W2 convergence

Conditional on U, sqrt(s)S+Z has the law T_n^(1/2)H/sqrt(n), where T_n=I+s C_n, C_n=UU^T/n, and H is independent standard Gaussian n by p. The checked Silverstein theorem gives a deterministic weak limiting squared-singular law. Gaussian sphere-net tails for U/sqrt(n), V/sqrt(n), H/sqrt(n) imply bounded moments of every fixed order of their operator norms and almost-sure eventual norm bounds, since the aspect ratios are bounded. The same holds for S and the observation.

For A_n=||T_n^(1/2)H/sqrt(n)||F^2/n, exact Gaussian conditional moments give

E[A_n|U]=(p/n) tr(T_n)/n,
Var(A_n|U)=2p tr(T_n^2)/n^4.

The expected conditional variance is O(n^-2). Also Var(tr C_n/n)=2(M/n)/n^2, so the total variance is O(n^-2), while E A_n=(p/n)(1+s M/n). Thus A_n tends almost surely to kappa(1+s b) by Chebyshev and Borel-Cantelli. Weak convergence plus convergence of these second singular moments gives singular-law W2 convergence. Its square is uniformly integrable, since it is bounded by twice the empirical second moment plus a constant and operator fourth moments are uniformly bounded. Therefore the squared W2 distance converges in expectation too.

The same argument applies at s=0 and to heat time t. Distributional conditional-Wishart representations may be coupled on a common probability space for this argument; the expected-W2 conclusion depends only on their marginals.

## 3. Norm-event conditioning and calibration

Choose a fixed C sufficiently large that E_n={||S||op<=C} has complement of exponentially small probability, by the two Gaussian-factor norm bounds. Let S^E have the conditional law of S given E_n; this law remains biorthogonally invariant. Couple S^E=S on E_n and draw an independent sample from that conditional law on its complement. This has the required marginal. With a_n=||S||F^2/p, define

d_n^2=E||S-S^E||F^2/p
 <=2E[a_n 1_(E_n^c)]+2P(E_n^c)E[a_n|E_n]->0.           (3)

Uniform operator fourth moments and the bounded aspect ratios give uniform second moments of a_n and pay the first term by Cauchy-Schwarz; E a_n=M/n and P(E_n)->1 pay the second. In particular E||S^E||F^2/p->b.

Share the noise between the two observations. Their expected squared singular-law W2 distance is at most s(p/n)d_n^2 by Hoffman-Wielandt, so the conditioned observation has exactly the same deterministic output limit in expected W2. That limit has bounded density and a positive lower edge by claims024-025. Claim027 applies to the bounded conditional prior and yields its MI limit as the difference of E_gamma at the output and pure-noise laws.

Claim006's dimension-uniform Gaussian entropy/W2 estimate transfers back:

|I(S;sqrt(s)S+Z)/(np)-I(S^E;sqrt(s)S^E+Z)/(np)|
 <=sqrt(s)d_n ->0.                                    (4)

To verify the normalization in (4), multiply both S and Z by sqrt(n). The standard-noise signal coupling error per entry is n E||S-S^E||F^2/(np)=d_n^2. MI is invariant under the common invertible rescaling. Calibration027 and the dilation identity E_gamma(D_c rho)=E_gamma(rho)+log c now prove (2).

## 4. C1 and reference MMSE

Claim026 gives E_gamma(rho_t) continuously differentiable for t>0, with derivative Phi_gamma(t)/2, where

Phi_gamma(t)=4gamma integral [H_t(x)+(kappa-1)/(2x)]^2rho_t(dx).

Consequently (2) is C1 and

2i_c'(s)=1/s-Phi_gamma(1/s)/s^2.                        (5)

For every finite n the normalized information is concave and differentiable and I-MMSE gives i_c,n'(s)=m_c,n(s)/2, with m_c,n=E||S-E[S|sqrt(s)S+Z]||F^2/p. This equals the per-entry risk for B_c=sqrt(n)S. For h>0 with s-h>0, concavity gives

[i_c,n(s+h)-i_c,n(s)]/h <=i_c,n'(s)
 <=[i_c,n(s)-i_c,n(s-h)]/h.

Take dimension limits and then h down to zero. C1 of (2) proves convergence to (5) at every fixed s>0. At s=0 both reference and centered unit-variance iid-prior risks are M/n exactly. No derivative of a merely convergent MI sequence was taken without the secant argument.

## 5. Arbitrary original aspect ratios

If alpha>1, eventually take n=N,p=P above. If alpha<1, transpose and take n=P,p=N; then B_original^T=sqrt(P/N) B_c, the canonical hidden ratio tends to beta/alpha, and

i_original,N(s)=i_c,n(s P/N).

The canonical information functions are Lipschitz in SNR with derivative at most (M/n)/2, so pointwise convergence at the limiting argument implies i_original,N(s)->i_c(alpha s). This limit is C1. Apply the same original-variable concave secants to conclude m_original,N(s)->2alpha i_c'(alpha s). This avoids assuming uniform convergence of canonical derivatives at moving arguments.

If alpha=1, claim022 already treats every sequence P/N->1, including sequences switching sides of the square. Thus all positive finite original aspect ratios are covered. At s=0 the normalized Gaussian-reference risk is M/N->beta in every case.

## 6. Fixed centered finite-variance priors

Claim023 gives expected ordered singular-profile coupling of an iid product X=UV^T/sqrt(N) to an independent Gaussian-factor reference B at all positive finite aspects, assuming fixed centered unit-variance laws and finite second moments only. Claim006 Haarizes X and proves that both its MI and its Bayes risk can only increase under the unknown orthogonal rotations. Its dimension-uniform entropy coupling estimate identifies the Haarized MI limit with the Gaussian reference. The C1 limit just proved then gives convergence of the Haarized risks by concave secants. The finite-dimensional risk inequality m_X<=m_HaarX proves (1). The corresponding MI inequality and the same value convergence give the asserted MI comparison. At s=0 both centered risks are exactly M/N. Non-unit centered variances follow by replacing SNR by their variance product and scaling the risk.

## Audit boundary

Dependencies006,017,022-027 remain proof drafts without independent PASS. In particular the weak population-Wishart law alone does not prove (2), and MI convergence alone does not prove (5); the separate calibration and C1 lemmas are essential. The conclusion is a fixed-SNR asymptotic comparison, not a finite-size inequality and not a uniform statement on dimension-dependent shrinking SNR intervals. Noncentered or dimension-dependent factor laws are not claimed here. Target1's first unsuppressed prior-dependent coefficient and uniform remainder are still open.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:965a7f6569046bdab574a5d8dade402280c470a6610623c9409c56ed763549bc","revision_digest":"sha256:3b800e4799833aee34c41412251a2c93b12d80120081dfe802ca5e2421ba863c","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:gaussian-product-all-aspects-mi-c1-mmse-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21 w718-T287-028 version1, proof unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact identities, finite controls and structural obstruction Result: A sufficient criterion is summability over all pairs of the probabilities of an inversion relative to the reference level order. Borel-Cantelli then gives only finitely many inversions, so an existing ranking permutation differs from the identity on finitely many labels. Merely making high-level inversion probabilities tend to zero is insufficient. Independently swap the two labels in block {2j-1,2j} with probability1/j for j>=2. This defines a permutation with displacement at most1 and marginal displacement probability tending to zero, yet it has infinitely many swaps almost surely. Check: The independent second Borel-Cantelli lemma applies because sum1/j diverges. Each realized transposition is confined to a disjoint two-label block, so the example is a valid permutation rather than an ordering of an unbounded collection without a first element. Obstruction: The toy permutation is not a KPZ counterexample. The missing source-specific estimate is a summable bound on deep-level inversions, together with existence of the infinite ranking. Bounded displacement alone cannot answer the finitary part, as the explicit example shows.
