[Proposition prop:largeoutdegree of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Assume that $\mu$ is critical and belongs to the domain of
    attraction of an $\alpha$-stable law for some $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Let $(d_n)$ be a sequence of positive integers such that
$d_n\to\infty$, and $\mu_{d_n}>0$ for all sufficiently large
$n$. Assume that there exists a cutoff sequence $(M_n)$ such that
$d_n=o(a_{M_n})$.
Set $
D_n
=
\#\{u\in\mathcal T^n:k_u(\mathcal T^n)=d_n\}$.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If $(n\mu_{d_n})$ is bounded, then
$$
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\left(D_n,\mathrm{Poisson}(n\mu_{d_n})\right)
\longrightarrow0.
$$
In particular, if $n\mu_{d_n}\to\lambda\in[0,\infty)$, then
$D_n$ converges in distribution to $\mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$.

\item[(ii)] If $n\mu_{d_n}\to\infty$, then
$$
\frac{D_n}{n\mu_{d_n}}
\quad\mathop{\longrightarrow}^{(\P)}_{n\to\infty}\quad
1.
$$
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 11 (Exact matrix isospectrality) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $\gamma:[0,T]\to V$ be continuous and of bounded variation, put $g=S(\gamma)$, let $l=\log g=\sum_{n\geq 1}l_n$, and put $v=l_1$.
Assume $R(l)=\infty$.
For every $q\geq1$ and every complex-linear map $\Phi:V_{\C}\to M_q(\C)$, write $I=I_q$ and define
\[
A_{\Phi}(z)=\sum_{n\geq 1}z^n\Phi^{(n)}(l_n).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\det(\zeta I-A_{\Phi}(z))
 =\det(\zeta I-z\Phi(v))
\end{equation}
for all $z,\zeta\in\C$.
Thus $A_{\Phi}(z)$ and $z\Phi(v)$ have the same eigenvalue multiset, counted with algebraic multiplicity, and
\[
\tr\bigl(A_{\Phi}(z)^p\bigr)
 =z^p\tr\bigl(\Phi(v)^p\bigr)
\qquad (p\geq1).
\]
title: Exact matrix isospectrality

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.29713, '\textbf{A Cartan geometry from a correspondence space in Riemannian geometry}'] Let $(p:\mathcal P\to N,\omega)$ be a Cartan geometry of type $(G,H)$, and let $K^\omega=d\omega+\frac12[\omega,\omega]$ be its curvature form.  The torsion of $\omega$ is the $\mathfrak m$-part of its curvature function
$\kappa^\omega$, that is, the map
\[
T^\omega:=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathfrak m}\circ\,\kappa^\omega\colon
\mathcal P\longrightarrow\Lambda^2\mathfrak m^*\otimes\mathfrak m,
\qquad
T^\omega(u)(X,Y)=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathfrak m}\left[K^\omega(u)\big(\omega^{-1}(X)(u),\omega^{-1}(Y)(u)\big)\right].
\]
We say that $\omega$ is normal if $\partial^*T^\omega=0$.
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.29713

[Theorem Foster's theorem of arXiv:2605.24671, 'Immigration Processes with Binomial Catastrophes and Random Survival Parameters'] Let $\{W_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ be an irreducible and aperiodic Markov chain on a countable state space $\mathcal{S}=\{\alpha_i,\ i\geq0\}$. Then $\{W_n\}_{n\geq 0}$ is ergodic if and only if there exist a positive function $g:\mathcal{S}\to(0,\infty)$, a constant $\varepsilon>0$, and a finite set $A\subset\mathcal{S}$ such that
\[
\mathbb{E}\big[g(W_{n+1})-g(W_n)\mid W_n=\alpha_j\big]\le -\varepsilon,
\qquad \alpha_j\notin A,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb{E}\big[g(W_{n+1})\mid W_n=\alpha_i\big]<\infty,
\qquad \alpha_i\in A.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Fix d>=2. Let P_l be the degree-l polynomials orthogonal for weight (1-t^2)^((d-3)/2) on [-1,1], normalized by P_l(1)=1. A polynomial is called positive definite in the Cohn-Kumar coefficient sense when all its P_l coefficients are nonnegative. It is strictly positive definite when every coefficient from degree0 through its degree is strictly positive. For any nonconstant real polynomial g all of whose roots lie in [-1,1), let H(a,g) be the unique polynomial of degree<deg(g) matching a and its derivatives at those roots to their multiplicities. The polynomial g is conductive if H(a,g) is positive definite for every smooth a on [-1,1) such that a and all its derivatives are nonnegative there. It is strictly conductive if it is conductive and, for every such a whose derivatives of all orders are strictly positive in (-1,1), H(a,g) is strictly positive definite of degree deg(g)-1. Endpoint derivatives at -1 are one-sided. Multiplying g by a nonzero scalar does not change H(a,g). This is Definition5.2; strict positivity refers to polynomial coefficients, not to nonsingularity of every finite kernel matrix.

For ReLU activation, there is a sequence of probability laws mu_d, supported in the unit Euclidean ball of R^(4d), and functions f_d with an absolute Lipschitz constant, such that the following hold for every shallow coefficient cap C>0 and sufficiently large d. Any depth-2 ReLU network N whose affine coefficients (including biases) all have magnitude at most C and which satisfies E_mu_d[(N-f_d)^2] <= 1/400 has width at least Omega(exp(Omega(d))/poly(C)), with asymptotic constants depending only on the activation. For every epsilon>0, there exists a depth-3 ReLU network with width O(d^2/epsilon) and affine coefficients of magnitude O(d/epsilon^2), whose error from f_d is at most epsilon uniformly on supp(mu_d). Depth means hidden-layer count plus one affine output. The constructed law is uniform on a special union of translated small boxes, not on the whole unit ball. The uniform deep-network approximation is only on this support; a Lipschitz extension to the entire ball exists, but efficient uniform approximation of that extension is not asserted. The lower bound is a width/weight tradeoff and does not apply to unrestricted coefficients. An unspecified arbitrary exponential cap is insufficient to conclude exponential width, because the polynomial-in-C denominator matters.

Let $R$ be an $m\times m$ correlation matrix with $R\neq I_m$, and let
$X\sim\mathcal N(0,R)$.  For each $i$, let
\[
  f_i(z)=e^{a_i z}\mathbf 1_{(-\infty,b_i]}(z),
  \qquad a_i>0,\quad b_i>0,
\]
and suppose that $\int zf_i(z)\,d\gamma_1(z)=0$.  Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb E\prod_{i=1}^m f_i(X_i)
  >\prod_{i=1}^m\int f_i\,d\gamma_1.
\end{equation}
The matrix $R$ may be singular.

For a finite-alphabet exterior process indexed by Z minus {0}, assume every finite exterior cylinder has positive probability and the central variable is binary. Write f_m(eta)=P(Y_0=+1|eta on O_m). Define D_n=sup_{m>=n} sup_{eta,zeta equal on O_n}|f_m(eta)-f_m(zeta)|. Every infinite exterior configuration is good in the finite-cylinder tail-tampering definition if and only if D_n tends to zero. The forward implication uses compactness: each good exterior has a central cylinder on which all deeper finite kernels have small diameter; a finite cylinder subcover gives a uniform radius. The reverse implication is immediate. Finite-depth numerical diameters are only lower bounds on D_n and cannot alone establish the limiting criterion.

For every i fix a finite-period Z^2 pattern h_i and let f_i(j) be its fraction of height j in one period. Suppose a discrete configuration s_N on B intersect N^(-1)Z^2 differs from h_i(Nx) at o(N^2) sites in each fixed P_i intersect B. Then for every integer j its height-j frequency in B converges to (1/area(B)) sum_i area(B intersect P_i) f_i(j). This is a sufficient condition; the required patchwise agreement for the actual sandpile, and the sandpile identity-element limit, are not proved here.

body: [Proposition 10 (The two regimes are opposed) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Fix the total energy $\sum_k v_k$ over the transformed per-coordinate energy vector $v=(v_k)\ge0$. (i)~The variable-rate distortion is governed by the geometric mean $\mathrm{GM}(v)=(\prod_k v_k)^{1/d}$: exactly proportional to it when every coordinate draws positive rate and the per-coordinate quantizers share one shape constant (as under the Gaussian source of \Cref{thm:klt}), and bounded below by the water-filling floor of \Cref{prop:waterfill} when the allocation is not interior; $\mathrm{GM}$ is symmetric and Schur-concave, hence minimized at the most concentrated (majorizing) $v$; equivalently the coding gain \eqref{eq:codinggain}$\,=\mathrm{AM}(v)/\mathrm{GM}(v)$ is Schur-convex. (ii)~The uniform-grid fixed-rate distortion is a sum of per-group maxima, $D_{\mathrm{fr}}=\sum_g\max_{k\in g}v_k$, which by the max-vs-mean bound satisfies $D_{\mathrm{fr}}\ge\frac1G\sum_k v_k$ with equality iff every group is internally \emph{uniform}; it is therefore minimized by within-group flattening and driven to its maximum by concentration. As functionals on the energy vector $v$, then, the two surrogate objectives are extremized at opposite ends of the \emph{within-group} majorization order, at fixed, strictly positive group sums. Because $D_{\mathrm{fr}}$ depends on the grouping it is not permutation-symmetric, hence not a functional of the global order at all, and the across-group placement of energy is a separate lever, the one the permutation family of \Cref{sec:tax-permutation} exploits; which energy vectors a given transform can actually realize, and hence whether these extrema are attainable, is the separate question taken up in \Cref{sec:inversion}.

For a unit-rate directed six-cycle Q with stationary pi uniform, choose D=diag(1/3,2/5,2/3,1,2/3,2/5). The time-stationary mean f(x)=pi(D-xQ)^(-1)1 is not convex for x>0: f double-prime at0 equals-1. Exact positive arguments1/1000,2/1000,3/1000 give f(1/1000)+f(3/1000)-2*f(2/1000)<0. Since event-stationary SCV=2*lambda*f(x)-1 with fixed lambda=pi D1, that SCV is also not convex in x. This refutes the convexity part of He2021 section4.3; it does not refute the separate monotonicity question or the reversible-chain theorem. Novelty is unverified.

[Theorem thm:CvChainPermuton of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] Let $\{ \sigma_{n,0} \}_{ n \ge 1 } $ be a sequence of (random) permutations converging to a (random) permuton $\mu_0$.
  For all $n$, let $ X _n$ be the up-down chain with transition kernel $  p^\uparrow _n  p^\downarrow _{ n + 1 } $ and initial distribution $\Law( \sigma_{n,0} )$. 
  Then there exists a Feller process $ F $ in $  \mathcal P   $ with initial distribution $\Law(\mu_0)$ and sample paths in $D([0,\infty),  \mathcal P  )$ satisfying the path convergence
	$$
		\big(
			 \iota (  X _n (  \lfloor  n^2 t  \rfloor  ) )
		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
			\Longrightarrow
        		\big(
        				 F ( t )
        		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
			.
	$$
	
	\noindent
	Here $  \iota  $ denotes the inclusion from the set of permutations to the space of permutons. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Growth of the infinite-descendant part of the FPP geodesic tree structural argument Result: In a locally finite rooted tree, an edge has infinitely many descendants exactly when it lies on an infinite ray, by the finite-branching compactness lemma. If the tree has infinitely many ends, then for every k one can choose k rays with disjoint tails outside some fixed ball; each tail crosses every sufficiently large circle. Consequently f(r)>=k eventually. Check: The forward implication is Konig's lemma applied below the edge; the reverse is immediate. A finite selection of distinct ends separates beyond finitely many branch vertices. Obstruction: This proves divergence conditional on infinitely many ends, without a rate. It supplies no unconditional ray multiplicity and no bound on where k rays separate.

Let d,N be positive integers, Lambda a positive definite d by d covariance matrix, and training tasks w~N(0,I_d) freshly sampled for each prompt. Within a prompt, x_1,...,x_N,x_q are independent N(0,Lambda), independent of w, and y_i=w^T x_i. Consider the one-layer linear-self-attention model whose invariant nonzero blocks are a matrix U and a scalar v, with predictor yhat=(v/N)sum_i y_i x_i^T U x_q, and the population loss L=(1/2)E[(yhat-w^T x_q)^2]. Initialize U_0=sigma Theta Theta^T, v_0=sigma, where sigma>0, ||Theta Theta^T||_F=1 and Theta Lambda is nonzero; the other blocks of W^PV and W^KQ are zero as in Assumption 3.3. Define Gamma=(1+1/N)Lambda+(tr Lambda/N)I_d. If sigma^2 ||Gamma||_op sqrt(d)<2, Euclidean gradient flow of the source's linear-attention parameters converges to a global minimum of the population loss. Specifically v_infinity=(tr Gamma^(-2))^(1/4) and U_infinity=(tr Gamma^(-2))^(-1/4)Gamma^(-1), so the learned effective operator v_infinity U_infinity equals Gamma^(-1). This is a fresh-Gaussian-task population theorem with finite context length, not a theorem selecting among minimizers for a fixed singular finite task pool. Source: arXiv:2306.09927v3, Section 3.3 p.7, Assumption 3.3 p.8, Theorem 4.1 pp.8-9, equation (4.1).

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] Let $f$ and $g$ be complex-valued functions that are analytic
  at zero with real coefficients. This means
  $f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n\,x^n$
  and $g(x) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty b_n\,x^n$
  holds for all $\lvert x \rvert$ small enough.
  Then
  \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $f + g$ is analytic at zero with real coefficients;
    \item $f\,g$ is analytic at zero with real coefficients; and
    \item if $g(0) \neq 0$, then $1/g$ is analytic at zero with real coefficients.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: The chromatic polynomial is a graph polynomial studied in algebraic graph theory, a branch of mathematics. It counts the number of graph colorings as a function of the number of colors and was originally defined by George David Birkhoff to study the four color problem. It was generalised to the Tutte polynomial by Hassler Whitney and W. T. Tutte, linking it to the Potts model of statistical physics.

body:
[Thmintro slippery of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Suppose $\Phi$ is LBSF and $\bm{s}$ is a strongly $\aleph$-unobstructed slippery point of $\overline{\mathcal{Z}(\Phi)}$. Then at least one of the following happens:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item Some of the $s_i$'s are rational and the corresponding Dehn filling yields a flow with a transverse sphere. In particular, the filling has an $S^1\times S^2$ summand.
            \item Two of the $s_i$'s are irrational and Dehn filling some subset of the rational ones yields a flow with a transverse $\mathbb{T}^2$-type planar lamination. In particular, the filling has a $\mathbb{T}^2 \times I$ summand and is a limit of fillings with $S^1\times S^2$ summands.
        \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Slippery points are spherical

[Definition 10 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Let $V$ be a $k[H]$-module and let $\mathcal V$ be a lift of $V$ to $R$. 

\medskip
{\bf (1)} We call $\mathcal V$ an end-hull of $V$ if the $R$-algebra-linear map 
$$\End_{R[H]}(\mathcal V)\rightarrow\End_{k[H]}(V)$$ 
defined by the reduction modulo $\upsilon$ is surjective.

\smallskip
{\bf (2)} Suppose that $R$ contains $R_s$. For $t\in\mathbb Z\setminus p\mathbb Z$ we say that $\mathcal V$ is potentially $t$-invariant if the $B[H]$-modules $\mathcal V\otimes_R B$ and $\mathcal V^{(t)}\otimes_R B$ are isomorphic and we say that $\mathcal V$ is $t$-invariant if the $R[H]$-modules $\mathcal V$ and $\mathcal V^{(t)}$ are isomorphic.

[Definition 84 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] We introduce the Stieltjes transform of the components of the equilibrium measure
\[
\forall h \in [H]\qquad \Gm_{\mu_{h}}(z) = \int_{\hat{a}'_h}^{\hat{b}'_h} \frac{\mu_h(x)\dd x}{z - x}.
\]
and $\Gm_{\mu}(z) = \sum_{h = 1}^{H} \Gm_{\mu_h}(z)$. We also introduce a $2H$-tuple auxiliary functions $(q_h^{\pm}(z))_{h = 1}^{H}$ defined for $\tau \in \{\pm 1\}$ and $z \in \amsmathbb{M}_h \setminus \amsmathbb{A}$ by
\begin{equation}

q_h^{\tau}(z) := \phi_h^{+}(z)\cdot \exp\bigg(\sum_{g = 1}^H \theta_{h,g}\,\Gm_{\mu_{g}}(z)\bigg) + \tau\,\phi_h^{-}(z) \cdot \exp\bigg(- \sum_{g = 1}^H \theta_{h,g}\,\Gm_{\mu_{g}}(z)\bigg).
\end{equation}
title: Definition 84 of arXiv:2601.16377

[Prop checking-the-inequalities-new of arXiv:2411.03065, 'Growing conditioned BGW trees with\\ log-concave offspring distributions'] Assume that ${\mathbf{w}}$ is $d$-arithmetic, that ${\mathbf{W}}=(w_0,w_d,w_{2d,\dots})$ is a log-concave sequence, and that $r=r_{d}({\mathbf{w}})$ is finite.
	Then we have
	\begin{align}
	\tfrac{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{d+1}}{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{1}}
	= R_0(0,0)\geq R_0(1,0)\geq\dots\geq R_0\bigl(r-1,0\bigr),
	\end{align}
	and for all $n\geq1$, we have the following long chain of inequalities, where each line continues the preceding one,
	\begin{align*}
	\begin{matrix}
		&	 R_n(0,0)
			&\geq& 	R_n(1,0)
				&\geq&	\dots
					&\geq& 	R_n\bigl(r-1,0\bigr)
								\\

		\geq&  R_n(0,1)
			&\geq& 	R_n(1,1)
				&\geq&	\dots
					&\geq& 	R_n\bigl(r-1,1\bigr)
								\\

		&  \vdots
			&& 	\vdots
				&&	\vdots
					&& 	\vdots
								\\

		\geq&  R_n(0,d-2)
			&\geq& 	R_n(1,d-2)
				&\geq&	\dots
					&\geq& 	R_n\bigl(r-1,d-2\bigr)
								\\

		\geq&  R_n(0,d-1)
			&\geq& 	R_n(1,d-1)
				&\geq&	\dots
					&\geq& 	R_n\bigl(r-1,d-1\bigr).
	\end{matrix}
	\end{align*}
	The first and last term of this chain of inequalities read as follows:
	\begin{align*}
	 R_n(0,0) 
	 	= \frac{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{(n+1)d+1}}{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{nd+1}}
	 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
	 R_n\bigl(r-1,d-1\bigr) 
	 	= \frac{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{nd+1}}{\PFtrees{{\mathbf{w}}}{(n-1)d+1}}.
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:lbm-tilted-product-energy of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Let $x\in\Omega_{\rm LBM}$, $f\in C_c^\infty(D)$, and
$\mu=e^{\gamma f}M_x$.  Put
\[
 K_G(\mu)
 :=\sup_{z\in D}\int_DG_D(z,y)^2\,\mu(dy).
\]
For $w\in L^2(\mu)$, write
\[
 G_\mu w(z):=\int_DG_D(z,y)w(y)\,\mu(dy).
\]
Then
\begin{align}
 K_G(\mu)
 &\le e^{\gamma\|f\|_\infty}K_G(x)<\infty,
 \\
 \iint_{D^2}G_D(z,y)^2\,\mu(dz)\mu(dy)
 &\le e^{2\gamma\|f\|_\infty}
 \iint_{D^2}G_D(z,y)^2\,
 M_x(dz)M_x(dy)<\infty.
 
\end{align}
Every real $L^2(\mu)$-normalized eigenfunction of $A_\mu$ has a bounded
continuous quasi-continuous representative.  Any two positive eigenpairs
$(\Lambda_i^\mu,\phi_i)$ and $(\Lambda_j^\mu,\phi_j)$ with real normalized
eigenfunctions satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \phi_i\phi_j\,\mu\in\mathcal M_{\rm fe}(D),
 \qquad
 I_D(|\phi_i\phi_j|\mu)
 \le
 \mu(D)^{1/2}K_G(\mu)^{3/2}
 \min\{(\Lambda_i^\mu)^2,(\Lambda_j^\mu)^2\}.
 
\end{equation}

Let A and B be linear operators in a Banach space X. B is relatively bounded with respect to A (A-bounded) if D(A) ⊂ D(B) and there are constants a, b ≥ 0 with ‖Bx‖ ≤ a‖Ax‖ + b‖x‖ for all x ∈ D(A). The infimum of all admissible a is the A-bound (relative bound) of B; the corresponding b usually grows as a approaches the infimum, and the infimum itself need not be attained. In a Hilbert space the condition ‖Bx‖² ≤ a'²‖Ax‖² + b'²‖x‖² defines the same relative bound. Relative bound 0 means: for every ε > 0 there is b_ε with ‖Bx‖ ≤ ε‖Ax‖ + b_ε‖x‖. If A is closed, B is closable, and D(A) ⊂ D(B), then B is automatically A-bounded (closed graph theorem applied to B on the Banach space (D(A), graph norm of A)). The form analogue: for A ≥ 0 self-adjoint with form q_A(x) = ‖A^{1/2}x‖² on Q(A) = D(A^{1/2}), a symmetric form β is A-form-bounded with bound a if Q(A) ⊂ D(β) and |β(x, x)| ≤ a q_A(x) + b‖x‖² for x ∈ Q(A). Operator-boundedness with bound a implies form-boundedness with bound at most a, not conversely.
A and B are linear operators in the same Banach space

[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be two Polish spaces, and let $c: X \times Y \to \R$ be a continuous cost function. For any functions $\psi: X \to \R$ and $\varphi: Y \to \R$, $$\Lu c\Ld c \psi \leq \psi \quad \text{and} \quad \Ld c\Lu c \varphi \leq \varphi.$$
    It follows that, if $f: X\to\R_+$ and $g:Y\to\R_+$, then,
    $$(f^{\circ, c})^{\star, c} \geq f \quad \text{and} \quad (g^{\star, c})^{\circ, c}\geq g.$$

[Defn def:SymProd of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $A_{1},\cdots,A_{r},{\rm e}_{1},v$ be given
symbols. We define the linear operator 
\[
A_{1}\partial_{{\rm e}_{1}}\hat{\otimes}_{{\rm s}}\cdots\hat{\otimes}_{{\rm s}}A_{r}\partial_{{\rm e}_{1}}:T((\langle{\rm e}_{1},v\rangle))\rightarrow T((\langle{\rm e}_{1},v,A_{1},\cdots,A_{r}\rangle))
\]
in the following way. Let $\mathfrak{f}_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathfrak{f}_{N}$
be a given monomial where $\mathfrak{f}_{i}={\rm e}_{1}$ or $v$.
We first define
\begin{align*}
 & A_{1}\partial_{{\rm e}_{1}}\hat{\otimes}_{{\rm }}\cdots\hat{\otimes}A_{r}\partial_{{\rm e}_{1}}(\mathfrak{f}_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathfrak{f}_{N})\\
 & \triangleq\sum\mathfrak{f}_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathfrak{f}_{i_{1}-1}\otimes A_{1}\otimes\mathfrak{f}_{i_{1}+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathfrak{f}_{i_{r}-1}\otimes A_{r}\otimes\mathfrak{f}_{i_{r}+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathfrak{f}_{N},
\end{align*}
where the summation is taken over all $r$-subsets $\{i_{1},\cdots,i_{r}\}$
with $\mathfrak{f}_{i_{j}}={\rm e}_{1}$. In other words, the action
is given by replacing $r$ ${\rm e}_{1}$'s by $(A_{1},\cdots,A_{r})$
and summing over all such possibilities. The definition is extended
to the tensor algebra $T((\langle{\rm e}_{1},v\rangle))$ by linearity.
We then set 
\[
A_{1}\partial_{{\rm e}_{1}}\hat{\otimes}_{{\rm s}}\cdots\hat{\otimes}_{{\rm s}}A_{r}\partial_{{\rm e}_{1}}\triangleq\sum_{\sigma\in{\cal S}_{r}}A_{\sigma(1)}\partial_{{\rm e}_{1}}\hat{\otimes}_{{\rm }}\cdots\hat{\otimes}A_{\sigma(r)}\partial_{{\rm e}_{1}}.
\]

[Theorem theo:Conv_SHE of arXiv:2608.27828, 'Scaling limit of the 3D abelian Yang--Mills Langevin dynamics'] Let $-\frac23<\eta<0$, fix $\kappa>0$ sufficiently small, and set
\[
\gamma=\bigl(\eta+\tfrac12\bigr)\wedge 0\;.
\]
Suppose that there is a deterministic $M<\infty$ such that, almost surely,
\[
\sup_{0<\varepsilon\le1}\|\theta^\varepsilon(0)\|_{\CC^\eta_\varepsilon}
+\|\theta(0)\|_{\CC^\eta}
\le M,
\]
and suppose that
\[
\|\theta^\varepsilon(0);\theta(0)\|_{\CC^\eta_\varepsilon}\to 0
\qquad\text{in probability}.
\]
Then, for every $T>0$ and $\delta>0$,
\[
\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}
\P\left(
\|\Psi^\varepsilon;\Psi\|_{\CC^{-1/2-\kappa,T}_{\gamma,\varepsilon}}>\delta
\right)=0.
\]

body: In mathematics, a Noetherian ring is a ring that satisfies the ascending chain condition on left and right ideals. If the chain condition is satisfied only for left ideals or for right ideals, then the ring is said left-Noetherian or right-Noetherian respectively. Formally, every increasing sequence $I_{1}\subseteq I_{2}\subseteq I_{3}\subseteq \cdots$ of left (or right) ideals has a largest element; that is, there exists an $n$ such that $I_{n}=I_{n+1}=\cdots.$

[Lem 91 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We have $\sM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0) \subseteq \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0)$.
\begin{proof} Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$.
    Then, there exists
    \[
        (q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising) \in \Adm^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
    \]
    such that $\mu^{\sym}(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta) = \mu$.
    Let $\tilde p$ denote the restriction of $p$ to $[q_*,1] \subseteq [q_0,1]$.
    Note that $(b,\sigma,w,\tilde p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ satisfies the assumptions of
    Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-chaotic} with $q_*$ in place of $q_0$.
    Indeed, conditions~\ref{it:1.1}, \ref{it:2.1}, \ref{it:3.1}, \ref{it:4.2}, \ref{it:5.1}, and \ref{it:6.1} provide assumptions~(\ref{i:IAMP-main-coefs}), (\ref{i:IAMP-main-diffusivity}), (\ref{i:IAMP-main-p}), (\ref{i:IAMP-main-budget}), (\ref{i:IAMP-main-endpt}), and (\ref{i:IAMP-main-init}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}.

    By Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-chaotic}, there exists $\iota = \iota(\epsilon)$ with $\lim_{\epsilon\rightarrow 0} \iota(\epsilon) = 0$ such that for all (sufficiently large) $N$, there exists a $C(L,\epsilon)$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$ with
    \[
        \WERR^\sym(\cA_N,\mu)=
        \max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big(\sym(\mu(\cA_N)), \mu\Big),
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N), \cP(\{\pm 1\})\Big)
        \bigg\}
        \le \iota\,,
    \]
    which furthermore satisfies $\chi_{\cA_N}(0) = 0$ and $\chi_{\cA_N}(1-\iota) \le \iota$.
    This implies
    \[
        \cM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0;C(L,\epsilon),\iota(\epsilon))\,.
    \]
    The rest of the proof is identical to that of Lemma~\ref{l:IAMP.in.Lip}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 91 of arXiv:2608.29416

Fix an integer horizon k>=2 and deterministic surrogate functions g_(t,m), t=1,...,k,m=1,...,M. Each surrogate is convex and beta-smooth, w_star minimizes every surrogate, and g_(t,m)(w_star)=f_m(w_star). Suppose there are numbers nu_t>=0 such that, for all w,t,m, g_(t,m)(w)-g_(t,m)(w_star)<=f_m(w)-f_m(w_star)<=(1+nu_t*beta)*(g_(t,m)(w)-g_(t,m)(w_star)). Choose 0<eta<=3/(13*beta), eta_t=eta*(k-t+2)/(k+1), and require nu_t<=eta_t. For any deterministic w_0, with fresh independent tau_t~Uniform{1,...,M}, update w_t=w_(t-1)-eta_t*grad g_(t,tau_t)(w_(t-1)). Put D2=||w_0-w_star||^2. Then E f(w_k)-f(w_star)<=9*D2/[2*eta*(k+1)]. In particular, eta=3/(13*beta) gives an upper bound20*beta*D2/(k+1). The task law is fixed and sampled with replacement; the deterministic surrogate objectives vary with time.

body: A random vector X in R^n is sub-Gaussian with proxy parameter sigma^2 if, for every unit vector u in R^n (||u||_2 = 1), the real-valued random variable <u, X> is sub-Gaussian with proxy sigma^2, that is, E[exp(t <u, X - E[X]>)] <= exp(sigma^2 t^2 / 2) for every real t. This one-dimensional-marginals definition reduces the vector case to the scalar sub-Gaussian definition applied to every direction simultaneously. [standard, e.g. Vershynin, High-Dimensional Probability]
title: Sub-Gaussian Random Vector in R^n

body: [Definition Knaster-Reichbach covering of arXiv:2608.30346, '\textbf{Classification complexity of homeomorphism group actions}'] Let \(X,Y\) be zero-dimensional spaces and let \(A\) be a closed nowhere dense subset of \(X\) and \(B\) be a closed nowhere dense subset of \(Y\). Suppose that \(h: A \to B\) is a homeomorphism, \(\mathcal{U} = \{U_i; i \in \mathbb{N}\}\) is a covering of \(X \setminus A\) by disjoint non-empty clopen subsets of \(X\) and \(\mathcal{V}=\{V_i; i \in \mathbb{N}\}\) is a covering of \(Y \setminus B\) by disjoint non-empty clopen subsets of \(Y\). Then \(\{(U_i,V_i); i \in \mathbb{N}\}\) is a Knaster-Reichbach covering or KR-covering for \((X\setminus A, Y \setminus B, h)\) if, whenever \(h_i: U_i \to V_i\) is a bijection for each \(i \in \mathbb{N}\), the combination mapping \(\tilde{h} = h \cup \bigcup_{i \in \mathbb{N}}h_i : X \to Y\) is continuous in points of \(A\) and \(\tilde{h}^{-1}\) is continuous in points of \(B\).
title: Knaster-Reichbach covering

[Definition D:geo of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $X:\mathbb{Z}^2 \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\cup\{\infty\}$ be a field of random variables that are independent subject to the symmetry condition $X(i,j)=X(j,i)$ for all $i,j$, and distributed as follows.

\textbf{Exponential setting.}
Take real parameters $\alpha$ and $\{\gamma_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}$. For any $i\in\mathbb{Z}$, take $X(i,i)\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\alpha+\gamma_i)$ if $\alpha+\gamma_i>0$, and $X(i,i)=\infty$ otherwise.  
For any $i\neq j\in\mathbb{Z}$, take $X(i,j)=X(j,i)\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\gamma_i+\gamma_j)$ if $\gamma_i+\gamma_j>0$, and $X(i,j)=X(j,i)=\infty$ otherwise.

\textbf{Geometric setting.}
Take positive parameters $\alpha$ and $\{\gamma_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}$. For any $i\in\mathbb{Z}$, take $X(i,i)\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\alpha\gamma_i)$ if $\alpha\gamma_i\in(0,1)$, and $X(i,i)=\infty$ otherwise.  
For any $i\neq j\in\mathbb{Z}$, take $X(i,j)=X(j,i)\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\gamma_i\gamma_j)$ if $\gamma_i\gamma_j\in(0,1)$, and $X(i,j)=X(j,i)=\infty$ otherwise.

For any $u\le v$ in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, define the \emph{passage time}
\[
X(u;v)=\max_{\pi}\sum_{(i,j)\in\pi}X(i,j),
\]
where the maximum is taken over all up-right paths $\pi$ from $u$ to $v$ satisfying (equation E:diagonal-condition of the paper).
title: Definition D:geo of arXiv:2604.10020

body:
[Definition def:prelimit_barcode_kernel of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] Let $L$ be a positive integer.
	Consider the hexagon with parameters $T=8L$, $N=S=4L$.
	Denote $T_0\coloneqq2L$, and $X_0\coloneqq3L$. The point $(T_0,X_0)$
	is in the first zone of the hexagon
	(equation eq:hexagon_zone_1 of the paper),
	and asymptotically lies
	on the
	center line $\mathsf{x}=\frac12(\mathsf{t}+\mathsf{S})$ of the waterfall region.
	Let $s,t\in \mathbb{Z}$ be such that $|s|,|t|<L$.
	We define the \emph{pre-limit barcode kernel} by
	\begin{equation}
		
		K^{\mathrm{barcode}}_{(L)}(s,t)\coloneqq
		\mathrm{Kast}^{-1}\left( T_0+s,X_0;T_0+t-1,X_0 \right),
	\end{equation}
	where $\mathrm{Kast}^{-1}$ is the inverse Kasteleyn matrix
	for the $q$-Racah measure on lozenge tilings
	of our specific hexagon.
	In other words, the pre-limit barcode kernel
	describes the joint distribution of the
	square lozenges
	$\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline = (current
	bounding box.south),scale=.25]
	\draw[thick] (0,0)--++(1,0)--++(0,1)--++(-1,0)--cycle;
	\end{tikzpicture}$
	around the point $(T_0,X_0)$
	in the waterfall region.
title: Pre-limit barcode kernel

Status: proof (unaudited). C006 v1. Novelty unestablished.

Let d,q>=1 be finite, H a constant symmetric positive definite q by q
matrix, and 0<m<=lambda(H)<=M. Fix sigma,D>=0, 0<rho<2 and
0<eta<=rho/M. Let (F_k) be a filtration and (u_k,v_k) adapted, with
deterministic u_0 and v_0=0. At each step let the jointly sampled oracle
noise (xi_k^u,xi_k^v) in R^d x R^q be F_{k+1}-measurable, with

    E[xi_k^u|F_k]=0, E[xi_k^v|F_k]=0,
    E[xi_k^v (xi_k^v)^T|F_k] <= sigma^2 H,
    E[|xi_k^u|^2|F_k] <= sigma^2 D^2 |v_k|^2.           (1)

The matrix inequality is in Loewner order and holds almost surely.
The two noise components may be dependent; their law may depend on the
entire past and on k. No iid, Markov, symmetry or higher-moment hypothesis
is imposed. Consider the unbiased stochastic-gradient oracle recursion
for the population loss L(u,v)=v^T H v/2:

    u_{k+1}=u_k-eta xi_k^u,
    v_{k+1}=B v_k-eta xi_k^v, B=I-eta H.               (2)

Here "oracle" means an unbiased estimator of grad L; this theorem does
not assert that every allowed noise field is the gradient of an individual
random sample loss. The label-gradient models of C005 are included.

For F in C_b^2(R^{d+q}), let f(u)=F(u,0), a(u)=D_v F(u,0), and define

    F_2=sup ||D^2 f||_op,
    F_vv=sup ||D_v^2 F||_op,
    F_uv=sup ||D_u a||_op,
    c=sigma^2 q/(2-rho), gamma=min{m,M(2-rho)/rho}.

Then, for every T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=K<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_K,v_K)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),
    C(T)=c[F_vv/2+T sigma^2 D^2 F_2/2+F_uv sigma D/gamma]. (3)

Thus a=1. If, in addition, the normal conditional covariance equals
sigma^2 H on the event v_k=0, then (1) forces xi_k^u=0 there almost
surely. Consequently the full noise covariance on the minimizing
manifold is sigma^2 diag(0,H), proportional to the population Hessian.
That equality is the target-compatible subclass; the estimate itself
uses only domination. No global covariance proportionality is asserted.
Finite d,q; constant SPD H with spectrum in [m,M]
Adapted states, deterministic u0, v0=0; jointly sampled oracle noise centered conditional on the past
Normal conditional covariance <=sigma^2 H; tangential conditional second moment <=sigma^2 D^2 |v|^2
0<rho<2; 0<eta<=rho/M; sigma,D>=0; F in C_b^2
Unbiased gradient oracle; individual random sample-loss gradient representation not asserted
For the proportional-covariance target subclass require normal covariance equality on v=0; proportionality is on the manifold only

Claim w730-T355-C006 v1. Kind: narrowed. Target: 1.
Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty and independent review unresolved.

## Statement

Let d,q>=1 be finite, H a constant symmetric positive definite q by q
matrix, and 0<m<=lambda(H)<=M. Fix sigma,D>=0, 0<rho<2 and
0<eta<=rho/M. Let (F_k) be a filtration and (u_k,v_k) adapted, with
deterministic u_0 and v_0=0. At each step let the jointly sampled oracle
noise (xi_k^u,xi_k^v) in R^d x R^q be F_{k+1}-measurable, with

    E[xi_k^u|F_k]=0, E[xi_k^v|F_k]=0,
    E[xi_k^v (xi_k^v)^T|F_k] <= sigma^2 H,
    E[|xi_k^u|^2|F_k] <= sigma^2 D^2 |v_k|^2.           (1)

The matrix inequality is in Loewner order and holds almost surely.
The two noise components may be dependent; their law may depend on the
entire past and on k. No iid, Markov, symmetry or higher-moment hypothesis
is imposed. Consider the unbiased stochastic-gradient oracle recursion
for the population loss L(u,v)=v^T H v/2:

    u_{k+1}=u_k-eta xi_k^u,
    v_{k+1}=B v_k-eta xi_k^v, B=I-eta H.               (2)

Here "oracle" means an unbiased estimator of grad L; this theorem does
not assert that every allowed noise field is the gradient of an individual
random sample loss. The label-gradient models of C005 are included.

For F in C_b^2(R^{d+q}), let f(u)=F(u,0), a(u)=D_v F(u,0), and define

    F_2=sup ||D^2 f||_op,
    F_vv=sup ||D_v^2 F||_op,
    F_uv=sup ||D_u a||_op,
    c=sigma^2 q/(2-rho), gamma=min{m,M(2-rho)/rho}.

Then, for every T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=K<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_K,v_K)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),
    C(T)=c[F_vv/2+T sigma^2 D^2 F_2/2+F_uv sigma D/gamma]. (3)

Thus a=1. If, in addition, the normal conditional covariance equals
sigma^2 H on the event v_k=0, then (1) forces xi_k^u=0 there almost
surely. Consequently the full noise covariance on the minimizing
manifold is sigma^2 diag(0,H), proportional to the population Hessian.
That equality is the target-compatible subclass; the estimate itself
uses only domination. No global covariance proportionality is asserted.

## Proof

### The covariance inequality is enough

Finite second moments of v_k follow inductively: the conditional second
moment of xi_k^v is at most sigma^2 tr H, a deterministic finite bound.
The tangential noise is then square integrable by (1), so all u_k also
have finite second moments at finite k. Conditional centering eliminates
the normal cross terms because v_k is F_k-measurable. With
Q_k=E[v_k v_k^T], equations (1)-(2) give

    Q_{k+1} <= B Q_k B+eta^2 sigma^2 H, Q_0=0.          (4)

Set S_0=0 and S_{k+1}=B S_k B+eta^2 sigma^2 H. Congruence preserves
Loewner order: if X<=Y then B X B<=B Y B, since B is symmetric and
w^T B(Y-X)Bw>=0 for every w. Induction in (4) gives Q_k<=S_k.
Diagonalizing H computes the comparison sequence, not Q_k, as

    S_k=eta sigma^2(I-B^{2k})(2I-eta H)^{-1}.

Its eigenvalue for lambda is
eta sigma^2[1-(1-eta lambda)^{2k}]/(2-eta lambda). Since
0<eta lambda<=rho<2, it is between zero and eta sigma^2/(2-rho).
Taking traces therefore gives

    E|v_k|^2 <= eta c.                                 (5)

This step does not assume that Q_k commutes with H or that covariances
at different times are independent. Taking expectations in a conditional
matrix inequality is justified by testing each deterministic vector.

Write h_k=-eta xi_k^u. Then (1) and (5) give

    E[h_k|F_k]=0, E|h_k|^2<=eta^3 sigma^2 D^2 c.        (6)

Taylor's theorem for f and adaptedness of its bounded gradient imply

    |E f(u_K)-f(u_0)|<=K eta^3 sigma^2 D^2 c F_2/2
                        <=T eta sigma^2 D^2 c F_2/2.   (7)

### Mixed correlation under adapted noise

For every eigenvalue lambda of H,

    1-|1-eta lambda|=min{eta lambda,2-eta lambda}
      >=min{eta m,2-rho}>=eta gamma.

Thus r=||B||_op<1 and 1-r>=eta gamma. Let a:R^d->R^q be bounded
and Lipschitz, with constant L_a. Keep the matrix N_k=E[v_k a(u_k)^T]
until the final trace. Adding and subtracting a(u_k), conditional
centering gives exactly

    N_{k+1}=B N_k+R_k, N_0=0,
    R_k=E[v_{k+1}(a(u_{k+1})-a(u_k))^T].               (8)

The noise term E[xi_k^v a(u_k)^T] vanishes by conditioning on F_k;
independence of xi_k^v from u_k is not required. Unconditional
Cauchy-Schwarz, using (5)-(6), gives

    E[|v_{k+1}| |a(u_{k+1})-a(u_k)|]
      <=L_a sqrt(E|v_{k+1}|^2 E|h_k|^2)
      <=L_a sigma D c eta^2.                          (9)

These correlated factors have not been treated as independent. Iterate
(8) as a finite matrix identity. Since

    |tr(B^j R_k)|<=r^j L_a sigma D c eta^2,

we obtain

    |E[a(u_K)^T v_K]|=|tr N_K|
      <=L_a sigma D c eta^2 sum_{j=0}^{K-1}r^j
      <=L_a sigma D c eta/gamma.                     (10)

For K=0 the sum is empty and the estimate holds. Taylor expansion in v
for the observable in (3) gives

    |F(u,v)-f(u)-a(u)^T v|<=F_vv |v|^2/2.

For this a, L_a<=F_uv. Combining (5), (7) and (10) proves (3), including
sigma=0, D=0 and T=0. There is no division by these parameters.

On the event v_k=0, the final inequality in (1) gives zero conditional
second moment of xi_k^u, hence xi_k^u=0 almost surely on that event.
The stated covariance identity on the manifold follows if normal
covariance equality there is additionally imposed.

## Review and attribution

This extends C005's iid label model by replacing its exact normal
covariance closure with domination and by using adapted centering only.
The new step most in need of independent review is (4) and its Loewner
comparison; the comparison sequence S_k commutes with H, but Q_k need
not. It is a candidate quantitative target result, not a priority claim.
The qualitative on-manifold framework is Li-Wang-Arora,

body: [Theorem 50 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a $\sigma$-ring, $\mathbb K$ be an algebraic ring, and $\mf A$ be both an HTG and a left $\mathbb K$-module. Suppose $x\mapsto k x$ is a continuous map from $\mf A$ to itself for every $k\in \mathbb{K}$.  Then $\ms M(\mathcal Q,\mf A)$ is a left $\mathbb K$-module. If $k\in \mathbb{K}$ is invertible, then $k\mu = k\cdot\mu$ for every $\mu\in \ms M(\mathcal Q,\mf A)$. If $\mf B$ is a sequentially closed submodule of $\mf A$ endowed with the induced topology, then $\ms M(\mathcal Q,\mf B)$ is a submodule of $\ms M(\mathcal Q,\mf A)$.

[Lemma 12 (Averaging in parabolic H\"older norms) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(h(t)\), \(a\leq t\leq b\), be a smooth family of invariant metrics for the fixed torus structure, and let
\(\mathcal A\) be the corresponding averaging operator.  For every integer
\(m\geq2\) and every time-dependent tensor field \(U\),
\begin{equation}
 \|\mathcal A U\|_{X_h^m[a,b]}\leq\|U\|_{X_h^m[a,b]},
 \qquad
 \|\mathcal A U\|_{Y_h^m[a,b]}\leq\|U\|_{Y_h^m[a,b]}.
\end{equation}
If \(\PBG_m(h;\Lambda;[a,b])\) holds, the analogous estimates in the
fixed-chart uniformly local norms hold with a constant depending only on
\(m,\sigma,\Lambda\), and \(b-a\); in those norms the constant need not equal
one.  Averaging commutes with constant metric scaling.

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $m\in \N$. Let $a,b\in \R\cup\{\pm \infty\}$, with $a<b$, and let $F:(a,b]\to \R_+$ be a continuous, non-decreasing function such that $\lim_{r\to a^+}F(r)=0$. Let $\lambda_i\in (0,1)$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1$ and set $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m)$. 
    
    We say Polish measure spaces $(X_1,\mu_1),\dots,(X_m,\mu_m)$ satisfy the cost-Santal\'o inequality associated with $(\lambda,c,F)$, with domain $(\mathcal{C}_{x_1},\dots, \mathcal{C}_{X_m})$, where $\mathcal{C}_{X_i}\subset 2^{X_i}$, if they satisfy the equivalent inequalities in Lemma~\ref{l:transfer} with these parameters.
    
    If a single space $(X,\mu)$ is repeated $m$-times, we mention this space just once; the amount of occurrences is dictated by the length of $\lambda$. If $m=2$, we may list $\lambda$ just once, since $\lambda_1=\lambda$ and $\lambda_2=1-\lambda$ in this case.

body:
Let X, Y be Banach spaces. A linear operator K : X → Y is compact if it maps the closed unit ball of X onto a relatively compact subset of Y; equivalently, for every bounded sequence (x_n) in X the sequence (Kx_n) has a norm-convergent subsequence. Compact operators are bounded. They form a norm-closed two-sided ideal in the bounded operators: norm limits of compact operators are compact, and BK and KB are compact whenever K is compact and B is bounded. Every bounded finite-rank operator is compact; in a Hilbert space (and in every Banach space with the approximation property) every compact operator is a norm limit of finite-rank operators. K is compact iff its adjoint K* is compact (Schauder). The identity of an infinite-dimensional space is not compact (Riesz), so on an infinite-dimensional space a compact operator never has a bounded inverse. A compact operator maps weakly convergent sequences to norm-convergent sequences; the converse (complete continuity implies compactness) holds when X is reflexive, e.g. a Hilbert space, but fails in ℓ^1 (Schur property).

Examples: diag(λ_n) on ℓ^2 is compact iff λ_n → 0; integral operators with L^2 kernels (Hilbert–Schmidt operators) are compact; the embedding H^1_0(Ω) → L^2(Ω) for bounded open Ω is compact (Rellich), so the inverse of the Dirichlet Laplacian is a compact self-adjoint operator on L^2(Ω). Non-examples: the shift operators on ℓ^2; multiplication by a function f on L^2[0,1] is compact only when f = 0 a.e.
X, Y Banach spaces

Let (a_n)_{n >= 0} be a nonincreasing sequence of nonnegative reals with a_n -> 0. Then the alternating series S = sum_{n >= 0} (-1)^n a_n converges, and for every N the remainder satisfies |S - S_N| <= a_{N+1}, where S_N = sum_{n=0}^{N} (-1)^n a_n; moreover S lies between any two consecutive partial sums, and S - S_N has the sign of the first omitted term (-1)^{N+1} a_{N+1}. The monotonicity hypothesis cannot be dropped: with a_{2k-1} = 1/k and a_{2k} = 1/k^2 one has a_n -> 0 but sum (-1)^n a_n diverges, since pairing consecutive terms gives sum_k (-1/k + 1/k^2), whose harmonic part diverges. The series need not converge absolutely (a_n = 1/(n+1) gives the conditionally convergent series log 2 = 1 - 1/2 + 1/3 - ...).
a_n >= 0 and a_{n+1} <= a_n for all n (eventually monotone suffices, discarding finitely many terms)

Let H be a Hilbert space (real or complex) and let f be a bounded linear functional on H. Then there exists a unique vector y in H such that f(x) = <x, y> for every x in H, and moreover ||f|| = ||y||. The map sending y to the functional x -> <x, y> is thus an isometric bijection from H onto its continuous dual H* (linear in the real case, conjugate-linear in the complex case).
H is a Hilbert space
f is a bounded (continuous) linear functional on H

[Proposition 46 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(k\) be a perfect field of characteristic \(p>0\), and let
\[
\pi\colon Y \to  X
\]
be a smooth projective morphism between smooth projective \(k\)-schemes.
Let \(D\) be a simple normal crossings divisor on \(X\), and let \(E\)
be a relative simple normal crossings divisor on \(Y\) over \(X\).
Set $B \defeq E+\pi^*D$ and
\[
d \defeq \dim X,\qquad
n \defeq \dim(Y/X),\qquad
N \defeq \dim Y=d+n.
\]
Suppose that the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the pair \((Y,B)\) is \(W_2(k)\)-liftable;
\item \(d\leq p\);
\item for every \(0\leq b\leq n\), one has
\[
R^q\pi_*
\left(
\Omega^b_{Y/X}(\log E)\otimes\omega_{Y/X}
\right)=0
\qquad(q<n).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then the pair \((Y,B)\) is log HT-split.

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): Let T be an arbitrary real lower statistic and s an arbitrary target, with the lower equal pair contributing the completion kernel (1,2,1). Then: T nonconstant on Omega_0 implies N_s(T; Omega_0) <= 4788, and T nonconstant on Omega_1 implies N_s(T; Omega_1) <= 4776. Uniform in both T and s. Unequal-coefficient case: conditioning on the other ten signs gives at most C(10,5)*3 + 2*C(10,6)*2 = 756 + 840 = 1596 weighted completions per upper minority state, and 3*1596 = 4788; equal coefficients: nonidentical translates of the (1,2,1) kernel give the smaller 4776 bound for Omega_1. Notes: This conditional-counting step is the repair replacing the earlier unsupported coupling shortcut; it assumes neither target zero nor reversal symmetry. Arithmetic digester-verified.

[Lem commutatortrick of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $N$ be an even positive integer. Let 
    $$\Homeo_{N\mathbb{Z}}^+(\mathbb{R}) \coloneqq \big\{f\in \Homeo_+(\mathbb{R}) \mid \forall x \in \mathbb{R}, \ f(x+N) = f(x) + N \big\}.$$
    Let $0 < \varepsilon < 1/100$, and suppose $f$, $g$, $\overline{f}$, and $\overline{g}$ are four elements of $\Homeo^+_{N\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{R})$ satisfying the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] $f$ has $N$ fixed points $x_1,\dots x_N$ (and possibly other fixed points as well) and $g$ has $N$ fixed points $y_1,\dots y_N$,
        \item[(b)] $x_i \in (i-\varepsilon, i+\varepsilon)$,
        \item[(c)] $y_i \in (i+0.5-\varepsilon,i+0.5+\varepsilon)$,
        \item[(d)] On the interval $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$, if $i$ is odd then $f$ is $\varepsilon$-strongly increasing. For $i$ even, $\overline{f}$ is $\varepsilon$-strongly increasing,
        \item[(e)] On the interval $[y_i,y_{i+1}]$, if $i$ is odd then $g$ is $\varepsilon$-strongly increasing. For $i$ even, $\overline{g}$ is $\varepsilon$-strongly increasing.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $\overline{g}\overline{f}gf$ has positive translation number (in fact, a translation number $\geq 2$).
title: Commutator trick

Consider a finite-state finite-action discounted MDP, bounded rewards with conditional mean r(s,a), discount 0<gamma<1, fixed target policy pi, and a fixed behavior policy mu whose state-action chain is ergodic with stationary vector d_mu>0. Let X have row x(s,a)^T and full column rank, D=diag(d_mu), and let P_pi be the row-stochastic target transition matrix on state-action pairs. Use Euclidean vector and operator norms, and define ||P_pi||_D=||D^(1/2)P_pi D^(-1/2)||_2. Fix ridge eta>0 and xi in (0,1). Set C0=2(1-xi)sqrt(eta)/(gamma||P_pi||_D) and C1=||r||/(2 xi sqrt(eta))+1. Assume ||X||<C0 and choose radii C1<R1 and R1-xi<R2<R1. For the concentric balls B1,B2 and projections Gamma1,Gamma2, take theta_0 in B1 and finite w_0. Let alpha_t,beta_t be deterministic positive nonincreasing sequences with sum alpha_t=sum beta_t=infinity, sum alpha_t^2+sum beta_t^2<infinity, and for some p>0, sum_t (beta_t/alpha_t)^p<infinity. Generate the behavior trajectory with A_t sampled from mu(.|S_t). Put x_t=x(S_t,A_t), xbar_(t+1)=sum_a pi(a|S_(t+1))x(S_(t+1),a), delta_t=R_(t+1)+gamma xbar_(t+1)^T theta_t-x_t^T w_t, and update w_(t+1)=w_t+alpha_t(delta_t x_t-eta w_t), theta_(t+1)=Gamma1(theta_t+beta_t[Gamma2(w_t)-theta_t]). Then w_t converges almost surely to the unique solution w_eta of (A+eta I)w=b, where A=X^T D(I-gamma P_pi)X and b=X^T D r. The target iterate also converges to this same fixed point by the general target-network theorem. This states the convergence clause of source Theorem2, with bounded rewards explicitly imposed; it concerns decreasing two-timescale steps, fixed linear features, both projections, and ridge regularization.

[Thm phase_transition_231 of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] For $\beta >0,$ we let
\[
    f^{231}_\beta(x) := 1 - \frac{1}{\beta} \log\left( 1 + \textup{e}^\beta - \textup{e}^{\beta x} \right) \,.
\]
Then, the random permutations $\tau^{\beta,231}_{n}$ converge almost surely in the sense of permutons to the deterministic permuton
\[
    \mu^{231}_\beta :=  \big(X,f^{231}_\beta(X)\big)_\# \min\left(1,(f^{231}_\beta)'(x) \right) \textup{d} x
    + \big( X,1-X \big)_\# \max\left(0, 1- (f^{231}_\beta)'(x) \right) \textup{d} x 
\]
if $\beta>0$,
and to the diagonal permuton if $\beta\le 0.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\]

body: [Theorem 2.1 (Hoeffding’s Inequality) of arXiv:2603.10190, 'Hoeffding-Type Concentration Bounds for Exchangeable Random Variables'] Let $X_{1},\ldots,X_{M}$ be independent and identically distributed random variables taking values in $[0,1]$. Set $\bar{X}_{M}\coloneqq\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}X_{m},\qquad\mu\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[X_{1}].$ Then, for every $t>0$, $\mathbb{P}\left(\bar{X}_{M}-\mu\geq t\right)\leq e^{-2Mt^{2}},\qquad\mathbb{P}\left(\mu-\bar{X}_{M}\geq t\right)\leq e^{-2Mt^{2}}.$

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $0<a\le b<\infty$, $\eta>0$, $k,d\in\mathbb N$, and $d\ge2$. There exists
a constant $C:=C(a,b,\eta,k,d)>0$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every
log-concave measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$, and every
$
f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\in\mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^k)
$
satisfying
\[
a\le \operatorname{Var}_{\mu}(f_j)\le b
\quad
\forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}
\quad
\text{and}
\quad
\det \Sigma_\mu^d(f)\ge \eta,
\]
one has
\[
\sigma(\mu\circ f^{-1},t)
\le
C t^{\frac{1}{k(d-1)+1}}
\quad
\forall t>0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 15 of arXiv:2608.08242, 'Bang--bang representation of $3\times 3$ embeddable stochastic matrices'] Let $P$ be a row-stochastic matrix. Suppose  that
	$P\in R_n\setminus\bigl(R_{n-1}\cup\V\bigr)$ and   $n\geq 6$.
	Then $P$ has a minimal representation
	\[
	P=(K_1K_2K_3K_4K_5)(K_6\cdots K_n),
	\]
	where 	$K_1,\ldots,K_n$ are e.r.s. matrices and
	\[
	P'=K_1K_2K_3K_4K_5\in\V
	\]
	satisfies exactly one vestibule equality. Moreover, in any such
	representation, if the unique vestibule equality is $V_{ji}(P')=0$ and $k$ is the remaining state, then the move types of the e.r.s. matrices 
	$K_1,\ldots,K_n$ are, successively,
	\[
	(k,i),\ (j,k),\ (i,j),\ (k,i),\ (j,k),\ (i,j),\ldots .
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 15 of arXiv:2608.08242

body: [Lemma 51 of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] For $\wh m$-a.e.\ $\tau$, we have the following domain Markov property for $M_\tau$. Let $D=\cA_\tau$ and $A$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:GFF-Markov-0}. Let $(\cA_\tau,\phi_0,-i)$ be sampled according to $M_\tau$. Then conditioned on $\phi_0|_{D\backslash A}$, $\phi_0|_A\overset{d}{=} h+\mathfrak{h}$, where $h$ is a GFF on $A$ with zero boundary condition on $\partial A\backslash\partial D$ and free boundary condition on $\partial A\cap \partial D$, and $\mathfrak{h}$ is the harmonic extension of   $ \phi_0|_{D\backslash A}$ onto $A$ with zero normal derivative on $\partial A\cap \partial D$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 5 (Kronecker theorem ++) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $P\in \mathbb{Q}(t_1,\ldots,t_r)[X]$ be an irreducible polynomial. 
    If modulo all maximal primes $q$ from an open dense subset of an integral model of $\mathbb{Q}(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ it has a root in $\mathbb{F}_p$, where $p>0$ is the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$, then $P$ is linear, and its root is a rational number.

    Consequently, if $K$ is a field of characteristic zero, $f\in K$, and $f$ modulo $q$ for all maximal ideal $q$, in an open dense subset of a suitable integral finite-type model of a subfield $f\in K'\subset K$, satisfies $X^p=X$, where $p>0$ is the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$, then $f\in \mathbb{Q}$.
title: Kronecker theorem ++

body:
Let n,m,N be positive integers with m>=2 and N>=(n+1)*m. For any family F_s:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, sample a seed S and a coordinate permutation Pi independently of a uniform N-bit pad Z. The seed and permutation may have any joint law. Fix y in{0,1}^N independently of(S,Pi,Z). Parse the first(n+1)*m bits of(Pi^(-1) applied to y) xor Z into m disjoint pairs(X_j,W_j) in{0,1}^n times{0,1}. Put A=sum_j indicator{W_j=F_S(X_j)}. Conditional on each(S,Pi), A has the Binomial(m,1/2) law. Consequently for every t>=0, P(A>m/2+t)<=exp(-2*t^2/m); in particular the Algorithm1 acceptance threshold m/2+ln(m)*sqrt(m) has false-acceptance probability at most exp(-2*ln(m)^2). If the parameter-dependent m is polynomially bounded above and m>=lambda^c for some fixed c>0 eventually, this probability is negligible in lambda. Neither pseudorandomness nor locality of F_s is needed for this soundness statement. The fixed-word independence is essential; this is not adaptive chosen-word soundness against an adversary that knows the pad.
Positive integer n,m,N,m>=2,N>=(n+1)*m; m disjoint parsed pairs.
The N-bit pad is uniform and independent of the seed, permutation, and tested fixed word.
For the negligible-security-error corollary only: m>=lambda^c eventually for a fixed c>0.

Method: Largest coefficient dimension compatible with strong convergence structural calculation Result: Expected outlier counts can fail as a method even when the extreme eigenvalue converges in probability. Let E_N have probability p_N tending to0, and take X_N=1_(E_N)*I_(D_N). Then its norm tends to0 in probability, but the expected number of eigenvalues above1/2 equals D_N*p_N. With D_N=exp(N) and p_N=exp(-N/2), that count diverges. Check: The event norm(X_N)>1/2 is exactly E_N, whereas the count on that event is exactly D_N. This isolates multiplicity rather than a failure of norm convergence. Obstruction: The example does not refute strong convergence in the requested models. It explains why a trace-statistic proof needs a different mechanism once coefficient dimension creates large multiplicities.

Setting: online SGD for a soft committee machine with K students w_1..w_K in R^N and M = K orthonormal teachers v_1..v_K, activation g(x) = erf(x/sqrt 2), output sum_i g(w_i . x), Gaussian inputs, no noise, step eta/N. As N -> infinity the overlaps Q_ij = w_i . w_j and R_in = w_i . v_n follow a deterministic ODE in time t = steps/N (the Saad-Solla equations, including the eta^2 term). For K = M, the symmetric fixed point of the eta -> 0 flow has every student equal to r(v_1 + ... + v_K) with r^2 = 1/(K(2K-1)), so Q_ii = Q_ij = 1/(2K-1) and R_in = r. The unstable rate lambda(eta) of the plateau satisfies lim_{eta -> 0} lambda(eta)/eta = 2K / (pi sqrt(2K-1) (2K+1)^(3/2)), which is 4 sqrt(15)/(75 pi) = 0.0657498 at K = 2, about 0.0461179 at K = 3 and asymptotically 1/(2 pi K).

DRAFT author-derived material; independent review pending; no novelty or parent-solved claim. Fix 0<beta<beta_c in the translation-invariant symmetric free Ising state on Z^3. Let G>=0, chi=sum G<infinity, xi the positive finite exponential correlation length, and K=-U4>=0 be summable over its last three indices. Define g_+=sum K(0,x2,x3,x4)/(chi^2 xi^3). Let ell be the smallest positive integer with sum_{|z|_infinity<=ell}G(z)>=chi/2; put R=max(1,ceil(xi),ell), Lambda={|x|_infinity<=2R}, N=(4R+1)^3, S=sum_{x in Lambda}sigma_x, V=E S^2, r=sqrt(V)*y_1, and B=-kappa4(S)/V^2. Here y_1 is the first zero of the infinite-volume Gibbs-marginal block-field MGF, not an isolated free-boundary partition function. Positivity gives -kappa4(S)<=N*g_+*chi^2*xi^3, while V>=N*chi/16 and N>=64*xi^3. Consequently g_+>=B/4>=3/r^4. Bounded r along beta_n increasing to beta_c is a sufficient condition for nonvanishing g_+. An eventual bound r<=C implies liminf g_+>=3/C^4. This does not prove such a bound or the converse implication from r escaping to g_+ vanishing.

[Lem 81 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For sufficiently small $\epsilon$, we have $|\lambda(I)| \ge |I| \ge 1 - q_0 - \epsilon^{1/10}$.

\begin{proof}
Define the ``bad'' intervals
    \begin{align*}
    I_1 &\equiv |\{t \in [q_0,\gamma(1)] : \lambda'(t) > 1 + \epsilon^{1/4}\}|\,,\\
    I_2&\equiv   |\{t \in [q_0,\gamma(1)] : \bbE[w_{\lambda(t)}] > \bbE[\tilde w_t] + \epsilon^{1/8} \}|\,.
    \end{align*}
By Markov's inequality combined with Proposition~\ref{p:gamma-1},
    \[
    |I_1|
    \le \int_{q_0}^{\gamma(1)}
    \frac{\lambda'(s)-1}{\epsilon^{1/4}}\,ds
    =\frac{1-\gamma(1)}{\epsilon^{1/4}}
    \le \frac{4\epsilon^{1/2}}{\epsilon^{1/4}}
    = 4\epsilon^{1/4}\,.
    \]
Similarly, by Markov's inequality combined with Proposition~\ref{p:budget-loss-small},
    \[
    |I_2|
    \le
     \int_{q_0}^{\gamma(1)} \frac{\big(\E[w_{\lambda(s)}] - \E[w_s]\big)_+
     }
        {\epsilon^{1/8}}\,ds
    \le \frac{2\epsilon^{1/4}}{\epsilon^{1/8}}
    \le 2\epsilon^{1/8}\,.
    \]
Combining with Proposition~\ref{p:gamma-1} shows
    \begin{align*}
        |I| &\ge \gamma(1) - q_0 - (4\epsilon^{1/4} + 2\epsilon^{1/8}) \\
        &\ge 1 - q_0 - (4\epsilon^{1/2} + 4\epsilon^{1/4} + 2\epsilon^{1/8})
        \ge 1 - q_0 - \epsilon^{1/10}\,,
    \end{align*}
    where the last inequality holds
    for sufficiently small $\epsilon$.
    Finally, since $\lambda' \ge 1$, we have $|\lambda(I)| \ge |I|$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 81 of arXiv:2608.29416

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:12a2f982345d5409a65dec9989ac472ec9b0659824a22175fae0dc84fcdac626","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/12/12a2f982345d5409a65dec9989ac472ec9b0659824a22175fae0dc84fcdac626.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:bd43de8dcb06f799c171e84b491fd3ed96f16a4aa79c15e2b93e64bffef0ad46","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c01","bundle_id":"population.t309-equilateral-ddpm-symmetry-breaking-drafts","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability, score matching, Gaussian mixture learning","draft":"w721/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:equilateral-three-gaussian-high-noise-angular-loss","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T309: the first angular signal for three equilateral components

Claim T309-w721-C01, version 3. Status: proof (unaudited), restricted population model. This is not a solution of Target 2 and makes no novelty claim.

The hardest open piece remains the transfer from a data-independent random initialization to a neighborhood in which covariance, mean, and plane errors are smaller than the angular signal. The theorem below describes the exact population loss on the covariance-matched angular circle. It does not assert that this circle is invariant under ordinary GD.

## Statement

Let d >= 2 and let u_j=(cos(2 pi j/3),sin(2 pi j/3)), j=0,1,2, embedded in a fixed two-dimensional plane in R^d. Let R_theta rotate this plane. For a>0 define

    q_{a,theta}(x) = (1/3) sum_j phi_d(x-a R_theta u_j),
    s_{a,theta} = grad_x log q_{a,theta},
    F_a(theta) = E_{X~q_{a,0}} ||s_{a,theta}(X)-s_{a,0}(X)||^2.

There exist absolute a_0>0 and C<infinity, independent of d, such that, for 0<a<=a_0,

    ||F_a(theta) - (a^6/4)(1-cos(3 theta))||_{C^2(R/2pi Z)} <= C a^8.       (1)

For all sufficiently small such a the only critical points are theta = n pi/3. The even n are strict global minima with F_a=0, and the odd n are strict local maxima. In particular, every solution of the scalar gradient flow theta'=-F_a'(theta) starting away from the maxima converges to a correct permutation of the three centers.

There are also absolute constants c,C_1 such that F_a'(theta)/sin(3theta) lies between c a^6 and C_1 a^6 away from the zeros, with continuous extension at each zero. For scalar GD with a step size at most 1/(C_1' a^6), an initialization at angular distance at least delta>0 from every maximum reaches angular distance at most eta from a minimum in O((h a^6)^(-1) [1+log(1/delta)+log(1/eta)]) steps. The implied constants are absolute; take 0<delta,eta<=1/10 and h>0. This is a one-variable constrained optimization guarantee, not a guarantee for updates of the full d-by-3 parameter matrix.

## 1. Reduction to two dimensions and relation to DDPM

All mixtures factor as their planar density times a standard Gaussian in the perpendicular coordinates. The perpendicular scores agree exactly. Integration over those coordinates is 1. Consequently F_a is precisely the same function for every d>=2; none of the estimates below use a d-dimensional Gaussian norm.

For a fixed OU noise level t>0, the population DDPM objective in Shah--Chen--Klivans, Eq. (5), differs from E||s(X_t)-grad log q_t(X_t)||^2 by a constant independent of s. Indeed, conditioning its denoising label Y=-Z/sqrt(1-exp(-2t)) on X_t gives E[Y|X_t]=grad log q_t(X_t); the conditional cross term vanishes. Thus F_a is the exact excess objective for their Eq. (9) student restricted to these means. An original radius r becomes a=r exp(-t), since each component's covariance stays I under OU smoothing (their Lemma 3). Large original separation sqrt(3)r is compatible with arbitrarily small a. The theorem remains a restricted optimization result even in that regime.

## 2. The score expansion and its justification

Write y for the two planar coordinates, v_j=R_theta u_j, and

    Z(a,theta,y)=(1/3) sum_j exp(a v_j dot y),
    b(a,theta,y)=a (sum_j v_j exp(a v_j dot y))/(sum_j exp(a v_j dot y)).

The common factor exp(-a^2/2) cancels in the score, giving s=-x+b. The triples obey E_j v_j=0 and E_j v_j v_j^T=I_2/2. Taylor expansion at a=0 yields

    b(a,theta,y)=a^2 y/2 + (a^3/2) T_theta[y,y] + O(a^4),                (2)

where T_theta=(1/3)sum_j v_j tensor v_j tensor v_j and T[y,y] has coordinates sum_{k,l} T_{i,k,l} y_k y_l. Its trace vanishes: sum_k T_{i,k,k}=E_j v_{j,i}||v_j||^2=0. Thus T_theta[y,y]=T_theta:(yy^T-I_2), the quadratic Hermite term.

The remainders in this argument are valid after expectation and after any fixed finite number of a and theta derivatives. Here is an explicit domination argument, needed to avoid treating a pointwise expansion as an integrated one. For |a|<=1 every softmax weight is between 0 and 1. Every fixed mixed derivative of b is a finite sum of products of weights, bounded components of v_j and their theta derivatives, powers of a, and monomials in y. It is therefore bounded in absolute value by a polynomial in 1+||y||, uniformly in a and theta. This follows inductively from differentiating weights: a derivative is a weight multiplied by a derivative of its logit minus the weighted average of that derivative. No inverse softmax weight is introduced.

The teacher density divided by phi_2 is exp(-a^2/2) Z(a,0,y). Its fixed finite derivatives in a are bounded by a polynomial in 1+||y|| times exp(||y||). The latter times phi_2 is integrable, with every polynomial factor. Products required for derivatives of ||b_theta-b_0||^2 have the same domination. In particular F_a is C^8 in a with all theta derivatives through order 2 continuous and uniformly bounded for |a|<=1. This justifies differentiation under the integral and Taylor's theorem uniformly in theta. Higher orders used to obtain C^8 in a and C^2 in theta are also covered by the same fixed-order argument.

The common a^2 term in (2) cancels. The teacher density tends to phi_2, so

    F_a(theta) = (a^6/4) E_{G~N(0,I_2)} ||(T_theta-T_0)[G,G]||^2 + O_C2(a^7).

For a trace-free symmetric order-three tensor D, Wick's formula gives

    E ||D[G,G]||^2 = 2 ||D||_F^2.                                    (3)

In detail, E[G_j G_k G_l G_m] is delta_jk delta_lm + delta_jl delta_km + delta_jm delta_kl. The first contraction is the squared trace vector, which is zero, and the remaining two are each ||D||_F^2. This is a Gaussian moment computation, with no independence assertion about successive GD iterates.

Finally F_{-a}(theta)=F_a(theta): change variables y to -y in its integral and use b(-a,theta,-y)=-b(a,theta,y). The odd Taylor coefficients vanish identically as functions of theta. Applying the uniform order-eight Taylor remainder improves O_C2(a^7) to O_C2(a^8).

## 3. Exact tensor coefficient

Writing c=cos(3theta), s=sin(3theta), the independent tensor entries are

    T_xxx=c/4,  T_xxy=s/4,  T_xyy=-c/4,  T_yyy=-s/4.

The multiplicities of these entries in the Frobenius norm are 1,3,3,1. Hence ||T_theta||_F^2=1/4, <T_theta,T_0>=cos(3theta)/4, and

    ||T_theta-T_0||_F^2 = (1-cos(3theta))/2.

Together with (3), this proves (1). In particular the first orientation-identifying score term is quadratic in y and order a^3. A cubic-only score truncation that drops this term misses the leading angular signal for this family.

## 4. Exact critical points, not just limiting critical points

The loss has period 2pi/3 because rotating the student by that angle permutes its components. It is even in theta, since reflection in the x-axis preserves the teacher and takes the student angle theta to -theta. These two symmetries force F_a'(n pi/3)=0 exactly for every integer n.

Let E_a(theta)=F_a(theta)-(a^6/4)(1-cos(3theta)). It has the same symmetries, so E_a'(n pi/3)=0 and ||E_a''||_infinity<=C a^8. If rho is the distance from theta to the nearest n pi/3, then 0<=rho<=pi/6. The mean value theorem gives |E_a'(theta)|<=C a^8 rho. On this interval |sin(3theta)|=sin(3rho)>=(6/pi)rho. Therefore

    |E_a'(theta)| <= (pi C/6) a^8 |sin(3theta)|.

Choose a_0 small enough that (pi C/6) a_0^2 <= 3/8. Then F_a'(theta) has exactly the sign of sin(3theta), and its quotient by that sine lies in [3a^6/8,9a^6/8]. At the zeros, (1) gives F_a''(n pi/3)=(9a^6/4)(-1)^n+O(a^8), which has the asserted strict sign after decreasing a_0 if needed. These are all critical points. At even n the student equals the teacher as a distribution, so F_a=0.

## 5. Scalar GD rate and its interpretation

Each open basin between consecutive maxima has one minimum. Let x in (0,pi/3) be angular distance to that minimum on one side. Then F_a'(x)=k_a(x) sin(3x), with c a^6<=k_a(x)<=C_1 a^6. Also |F_a''|<=L a^6 for an absolute L by (1). For h<=1/(L a^6), the update map x -> x-h F_a'(x) is nondecreasing. It fixes the endpoints 0 and pi/3, hence never overshoots either. The loss derivative has the right sign throughout the interval, so the iterates decrease to 0.

If x>=pi/6, write z=pi/3-x, the distance to the adjacent maximum. Then sin(3x)=sin(3z)>=(6/pi)z. While this phase persists, z_next>=z(1+(6c/pi)h a^6), so it lasts O((h a^6)^(-1)[1+log(1/delta)]) steps if z_0>=delta. Once x<=pi/6, the same sine lower bound gives x_next<=x(1-(6c/pi)h a^6). This phase needs O((h a^6)^(-1)[1+log(1/eta)]) steps to reach eta. Other sides of other basins follow by the exact symmetries. A uniform random initial angle lies within delta of some maximum with probability 3delta/pi for delta<=pi/3; this is the union of three intervals of length 2delta on a circle of circumference 2pi.

If the actual means are constrained to the angular circle and updated by its induced Euclidean gradient flow, the circle metric is sum_j ||d(a R_theta u_j)/dtheta||^2=3a^2. Thus theta'=-F_a'(theta)/(3a^2); its natural time scale is a^(-4), whereas the coordinate gradient theta'=-F_a'(theta) has scale a^(-6). This metric distinction matters when comparing this calculation with the original algorithm.

## What this does not establish

The covariance-matched angular circle need not be invariant under the full gradient. A student may have the correct covariance and still have nonzero derivatives in radius, centroid, or anisotropic shape. Consequently the scalar theorem does not imply the target's random-initialization GD theorem. A valid transfer needs a quantitative normal-attraction/tracking estimate and an anti-concentration argument for the resulting angular coordinate, followed by finite-sample and discrete-step control. None is claimed here.

Source: Shah, Chen, Klivans, arXiv:2307.01178v1 (4 July 2023), Eqs. (5), (8), (9), pp. 7--8, and Theorem 16 with Assumptions 14--15, p. 12. body: In mathematics, Hensel's lemma, also known as Hensel's lifting lemma, named after Kurt Hensel, is a result in modular arithmetic, stating that if a univariate polynomial has a simple root modulo a prime number p, then this root can be lifted to a unique root modulo any higher power of p. More generally, if a polynomial factors modulo p into two coprime polynomials, this factorization can be lifted to a factorization modulo any higher power of p.

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Let B=U_G V_G^T/sqrt(N) for independent standard real Gaussian factors of sizes N by M and P by M, where M>=N+P+1. Let X be any random N by P matrix with finite second moment. For any coupling of their decreasing singular-value profiles a,b, put delta^2=E sum_(j=1)^min(N,P) (a_j-b_j)^2/(NP). Define m_Q(s)=E||Q-E[Q|sqrt(s)Q+W]||_F^2/(NP), with independent standard Gaussian W, s>=0. Then m_X(s)<=(sqrt(m_B(s))+2delta)^2 and m_X(s)-m_B(s)<=4sqrt(M/N)delta+4delta^2, uniformly in s>=0. The Gaussian product log-concavity gives a globally 1/sqrt(s)-Lipschitz, biorthogonally equivariant Bayes denoiser for s>0; shared Haar singular vectors and Gaussian noise give the direct risk comparison. Consequently, for independent fixed centered iid unit-variance finite-fourth-moment real factor laws, positive finite limits alpha=P/N,beta=M/N, and M>=N+P+1 eventually, the expected spectral W2 coupling of unaudited claim 008 gives limsup_N sup_(s>=0)[m_X_N(s)-m_B_N(s)]<=0; beta>1+alpha suffices. The asymptotic part depends on that unaudited spectral-coupling proof. These are channel-scaled product losses: for raw R=UV^T, L_R=N*m_X, so the raw comparison divides the loss gap by N. Other aspect regimes, including N=P=M, remain open; novelty and independent audit are pending.
Real matrices; standard independent Gaussian observation noise, per-entry squared error.
Finite-dimensional comparison: any X with finite second moment, Gaussian reference B, and M>=N+P+1.
Asymptotic consequence: independent arrays of fixed centered iid real unit-variance entry laws with finite fourth moments, and positive finite aspect limits.
The asymptotic conclusion depends on the expected spectral W2 coupling in unaudited claim 008; no MMSE limit existence is assumed.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ac8e009ef6b13b4daaaab39f320e0cd617128a098fff917c77ed919b6a9a891a","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ac/ac8e009ef6b13b4daaaab39f320e0cd617128a098fff917c77ed919b6a9a891a.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:235e82196ece14cc4302c0cd85fe5c21acc54bb11c4aacd75c90153e26068f72","bundle_entry_key":"gaussian-product-mmse-logconcave-wedge-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-gaussian-product-logconcavity-mmse-and-normalization-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:gaussian-product-mmse-logconcave-wedge-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Gaussian-reference MMSE extremality in the log-concavity wedge

**Proof draft, unaudited.** Primary source hypotheses have been checked.
Independent review and novelty assessment remain open. The asymptotic
corollary uses the unaudited spectral-coupling result in claim 008.

All matrices are real. Squared errors use the Frobenius norm and are divided
by d=NP. Information and mutual-information derivatives are not used here.


## Product-loss convention

Here the signal is the channel-scaled product X=UV^T/sqrt(N). For the raw
product R=UV^T in the same observation, its NP-normalized Bayes loss L_R
is exactly N*m_X. Thus the uniform asymptotic comparison below is
limsup_N sup_s (L_R-L_R^G)/N<=0. It does not assert an unscaled raw-loss
gap tending to zero. The literal raw loss diverges even for Gaussian
factors at fixed positive noise; proofs/product_loss_normalization.md
gives the exact identity and a finite-dimensional lower bound.

## 1. Statement of the finite-dimensional comparison

Fix positive integers N,P,M with M>=N+P+1. Let

    B=U_G V_G^T/sqrt(N),

where U_G is N by M, V_G is P by M, and both have independent standard
Gaussian entries. Let X be any random N by P matrix with finite second
moment. Put r=min(N,P). Choose any coupling of the decreasing singular-value
vectors a of X and b of B, and set

    delta^2=E sum_(j=1)^r (a_j-b_j)^2/(NP).

For Q=X or B, define

    m_Q(s)=E||Q-E[Q|sqrt(s)Q+W]||_F^2/(NP),

with W independent standard Gaussian noise. For every s>0,

    m_X(s) <= (sqrt(m_B(s))+2 delta)^2.                 (1)

In particular, since E||B||_F^2/(NP)=M/N,

    m_X(s)-m_B(s) <= 4 sqrt(M/N) delta+4 delta^2.        (2)

The same bound applies at s=0, by the zero estimator and the L2 triangle
inequality; for the centered equal-variance products considered below their
two zero-SNR MMSEs are both M/N. The constants in (1)-(2) do not depend on s.

## 2. The Gaussian product has a log-concave density

Put h=N+P and stack the factors into the h by M Gaussian matrix
T=[U_G; V_G]. Its Wishart Gram matrix S=T T^T has density proportional to

    det(S)^k exp[-tr(S)/2], S>0,
    k=(M-h-1)/2 >= 0.                                 (3)

The density is with respect to the h(h+1)/2 independent symmetric matrix
coordinates; only a positive normalization constant is omitted. Its domain
is the convex positive definite cone. Log det is concave there, as follows
from the second directional derivative

    -tr(S^(-1)H S^(-1)H)<=0, H symmetric.

Thus (3), extended by zero outside S>0, is log-concave. Its upper-right
block is exactly U_G V_G^T. Write the block coordinates as

    S = [ A, sqrt(N) B; sqrt(N) B^T, C ].              (4)

This is an invertible linear change between symmetric S and the independent
coordinates A in Sym_N, C in Sym_P, B in R^(N by P), with a constant
positive Jacobian. Prékopa's marginalization theorem, integrating A,C,
therefore makes the B density log-concave.

The marginal is positive for every B: the fiber contains the positive
definite block matrix with A=t I_N,C=t I_P whenever
t>sqrt(N)||B||_op, together with an open neighborhood in the fiber. It is
finite for every B as well. On the positive cone, A,C are positive
definite and det(S)^k is at most ((tr(A)+tr(C))/h)^(h*k). Hence its fiber
integral is bounded by a polynomial times exp[-(tr(A)+tr(C))/2] integrated
over the two positive definite cones. This is finite, since their traces
dominate their Frobenius norms. No regularity or integrability assertion
about the marginal is being inferred from a value on a null set.

The exact marginal theorem is recorded in Saumard-Wellner, arXiv:1404.5886,
Theorem 3.3, with two proofs following it; the result is due to Prékopa.
The existing brain card is the Prékopa-Leindler inequality, full id
claim_1d4b5a350b6c1f8b10c1e28f6294d7585ab806703fc9ee66340f1431f547361d.

## 3. The reference Bayes denoiser is globally Lipschitz

Fix s>0 and let p_s(y) be the density of sqrt(s)B+W. The joint density
p_B(b) phi(y-sqrt(s)b) is log-concave in b,y, so Prékopa's theorem makes p_s
log-concave. Gaussian convolution makes it smooth and strictly positive.
Its moments and likelihood derivatives can be differentiated under the
integral: on each compact y set, a polynomial times the Gaussian likelihood
is bounded as a function of b, and p_B is a probability density.

Define the everywhere-defined posterior mean

    F_s(y)= integral b p_B(b) phi(y-sqrt(s)b) db / p_s(y).

In vectorized coordinates, direct differentiation of this ratio gives

    D F_s(y)=sqrt(s) Cov(B|sqrt(s)B+W=y),
    Hess log p_s(y)=s Cov(B|sqrt(s)B+W=y)-I_d.          (5)

Since p_s is log-concave, its log Hessian is negative semidefinite. Equation
(5) therefore gives, for every y,

    0 <= Cov(B|Y=y) <= I_d/s,
    ||D F_s(y)||_op <= 1/sqrt(s).                     (6)

Integration along line segments proves the global 1/sqrt(s)-Lipschitz bound
for F_s in Frobenius norm. No smoothness of the prior log density is needed.

The Gaussian factors make B biorthogonally invariant. Changing variables
in the posterior integral proves, for all orthogonal L,R and all y,

    F_s(L y R^T)=L F_s(y) R^T.                        (7)

## 4. Coupling, equivariance and the risk comparison

Take coupled profiles a,b as in Section 1 and independent Haar orthogonal
matrices L of size N and R of size P. Form rectangular diagonal matrices
D(a),D(b) with those profiles, and define

    X_tilde=L D(a) R^T,  B_tilde=L D(b) R^T.

Biorthogonal invariance implies B_tilde has the law of B: averaging any test
function over the left/right group depends only on singular values. X_tilde
has the law of an independent Haar rotation of X. By construction,

    E||X_tilde-B_tilde||_F^2/(NP)=delta^2.             (8)

Use the same independent Gaussian W for both channels. From (6), pointwise,

    ||F_s(sqrt(s)X_tilde+W)-X_tilde
        -F_s(sqrt(s)B_tilde+W)+B_tilde||_F
      <= ||F_s(sqrt(s)X_tilde+W)-F_s(sqrt(s)B_tilde+W)||_F
           +||X_tilde-B_tilde||_F
      <= 2||X_tilde-B_tilde||_F.                     (9)

The L2 triangle inequality, (8), and Bayes optimality of F_s for B give

    sqrt(E||F_s(sqrt(s)X_tilde+W)-X_tilde||_F^2/(NP))
      <= sqrt(m_B(s))+2 delta.                       (10)

The risk of F_s is unchanged by independent Haar rotations of X: condition
on fixed L,R, use (7), and rotate the isotropic Gaussian noise. Thus the left
side is the square root of the risk of F_s on the original X. Bayes
optimality for X bounds m_X by that risk. This proves (1). Expanding the
square and using m_B(s)<=M/N proves (2).

At s=0, m_X(0)<=E||X||_F^2/(NP), and the profile coupling gives
sqrt(E||X||_F^2/(NP))<=sqrt(M/N)+delta. This is sufficient for (2) there
as well. In the stated application both means vanish and both variances
are exactly M/N, so the gap at zero is zero.

## 5. Extensive-rank consequence and remaining gap

Let X_N=U_N V_N^T/sqrt(N), with independent centered iid real unit-variance
factor laws, fixed with N and having finite fourth moments. Assume P/N and
M/N converge to positive finite limits alpha,beta. The spectral-coupling
result in claim 008 gives couplings of the Gaussian and non-Gaussian
profiles for which delta_N->0. Equivalently, if mu_X and mu_B are the r-point
empirical singular-value laws of X_N/sqrt(N), B_N/sqrt(N), then

    delta_N^2=(r/P) E W_2(mu_X,mu_B)^2 -> 0.

If M>=N+P+1 eventually, (2) holds with the same delta_N for every s>=0,
and hence

    limsup_N sup_(s>=0) [m_X_N(s)-m_B_N(s)] <= 0.      (11)

In particular beta>1+alpha guarantees this conclusion. No existence of an
individual thermodynamic MMSE limit is assumed. Fixed positive factor
variances reduce to the unit-variance statement by rescaling the signal
and SNR.

This is a partial Target 2 result. The proof does not cover the general
remaining aspect region, including N=P=M. It also does not pay the uniform
Taylor-remainder obligation in Target 1. The central remaining MMSE issue
is risk transfer for a Gaussian reference outside this log-concavity regime.

## Checked sources and dependency

The Gaussian Wishart density is printed as f_(n,d)(A) in the proof of
Theorem 7, page 17, of Bubeck-Ding-Eldan-Rácz, *Testing for high-dimensional
geometry in random graphs*, arXiv:1411.5713. It is stated for integer d>=n.
Substitute their n=N+P, d=M and their matrix A=S. This yields exactly the
density and determinant exponent used in (3). No CLT or d/n^3 asymptotic
