body: OPEN PROBLEM (optimal quadratic Littlewood-Offord bound). For Q = sum c_ij xi_i xi_j with all coefficients nonzero and xi_i i.i.d. Bernoulli, is sup_z P(Q = z) = O(n^{-1/2})? More generally, the optimal anti-concentration exponent for polynomials of degree d. Source: Tao and Vu, From the Littlewood-Offord problem to the circular law, Section 6. Known: Costello (2013) proved n^{-1/2+o(1)} for quadratic forms. Meka, Nguyen and Vu (2016) proved, for a multilinear polynomial of degree d and rank r with Rademacher inputs and every interval I of length 1, P(P(xi) in I) <= min{B d^{4/3} (log r)^{1/2} r^{-1/(4d+1)}, exp(B d^2 (log log r)^2) r^{-1/2}}. For d = 2 the second bound is r^{-1/2} times exp(4B (log log r)^2), a factor that grows faster than every power of log r, so the loss is superpolylogarithmic, not logarithmic; the exact O(n^{-1/2}) remains open.

[Definition def:nprefix of arXiv:2604.20660, 'The Legendre structure of the TAP complexity\\ for the Ising spin glass'] Fix $n\geq 1$ and set $q_0=0$. Given a strictly increasing sequence
		$(q_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$ in $(0,1)$ and a strictly increasing sequence of
		weights $(u_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$ in $(0,1)$, we write
		$\mathrm{Prefix}_{n+1}\!\bigl((u_i)_{1\leq i\leq n},(q_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}\bigr)$
		for the collection of probability measures $\zeta$ on $[0,1]$ satisfying
		\begin{equation*}
			\mathrm{supp}(\zeta)\cap[0,q_n]=\{q_0,q_1,\ldots,q_n\}
			\qquad\text{and}\qquad
			\zeta([0,q_{i-1}])=u_i \;\text{ for all }\; i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
		\end{equation*}
		We say that such $\zeta$ has an \emph{$(n+1)$-atom prefix} $\{0,q_1,\ldots,q_n\}$.
title: Probability measures with an $(n+1)$-atom prefix

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.23742, 'Second-order fusion asymptotics for $\Sine_\beta$ correlation functions'] Let $\beta>0$, $m\ge2$, and suppose $m\beta>1$. For pairwise distinct $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R$, as $\varepsilon\to0$,
\begin{align}
\rho^{(m)}_\beta(\varepsilon a_1,\ldots,\varepsilon a_m)
&=C^{(m)}_\beta|\varepsilon|^{\beta\binom m2}\prod_{i<j}|a_i-a_j|^\beta\notag\\
&\quad\times\left[1-\frac{\beta^2}{8(m\beta-1)(2m+1)}V(a)\varepsilon^2+o(\varepsilon^2)\right].
\end{align}
The remainder is locally uniform when $a$ ranges over compact subsets of the set of pairwise distinct configurations. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Second-order fusion asymptotics

[Prop 53 (Strict convexity of the rate functional) of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] For any pair of probability measures $\mu_0, \mu_1 \in \mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R})$ (possibly equal), and any $\alpha \in \intff{0}{1}$, we have
$$I[(1-\alpha) \mu_0 + \alpha \mu_1 ] \leq (1-\alpha) I[\mu_0] + \alpha I[\mu_1] \, .$$
If $I[\mu_0], I[\mu_1] < +\infty$ and $ \mu_0 \neq \mu_1$, then for all $\alpha \in ]0;1[$ we have the strict inequality
$$I[(1-\alpha) \mu_0 + \alpha \mu_1 ] < (1-\alpha) I[\mu_0] + \alpha I[\mu_1] \, .$$
title: Strict convexity of the rate functional

[Proposition pr:reduction of arXiv:2604.21142, 'Gaussian fluctuations for Internal DLA on cylinders'] Fix $\n > 0$ and $m \geq 1$, with $T^\sharp$ as in the statement of Theorem~(th:max_fluct of the paper). For every integer $T$ with $T^\sharp \leq T \leq N^m$ and every $N$ large enough, there exist an integer $T'$ with $1 \leq T' \leq T^\sharp$ and a non-negative integer $k$ with $T' + N k = T$, together with a coupling of $A(T)$ and an IDLA process $(A_*(t))_{t \geq 0}$ on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb G}} _N$ starting from $A_*(0) = R_0$, such that
	\[ {\ensuremath{\mathbb P}} \big( A(T) = A_*(T') + R_k \big) \geq 1 - N^{-(\n+1)}\,, \]
where $A_*(T') + R_k \coloneqq \{(x, y+k) : (x, y) \in A_*(T')\}$.

body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): For the conditional block of (23), $\sum_s c_s\le L_{Q\mid W}$ and $N=\sum_s a_s\le\kappa L_{Q\mid W}$ (tag 24b); the matching endpoints give a private core of size $\le2\kappa L_{Q\mid W}$, and the free/never-free entropy step adds $\le L_{Q\mid W}$ further private directions, whence $\boxed{\dim\frac{R+\operatorname{span}W}{\operatorname{span}W}\le(2\kappa+1)L_{Q\mid W}}$. [Definition 49 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Suppose that  $(\eta_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\eta^{\prime}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ are defined on the same underlying graph $G=(V,E)$ (either the integer lattice or the torus of length $N$), but are allowed to have different initial data. 
We define the \textbf{basic coupling} $\mathbf{P}$ between the ASEPs $(\eta_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\eta^{\prime}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ as follows.
For all edges in $E$, we place independent rate $(1+q)$ Poisson clocks. Whenever the clock of an edge $e=\{ x,x+1\}$ rings, and the exclusion processes are in states $\eta$ and $\eta^{\prime}$, respectively, we sample an independent Bernoulli-$(1+q)^{-1}$-distributed random variable $B$. If
\begin{itemize}
\item $B=1$: Then, if $\eta(x)=1-\eta(x+1)=1$ holds, we move the particle at site $x$ to site $x+1$ in configuration $\eta$. Similarly, if $\eta^{\prime}(x)=1-\eta^{\prime}(x+1)=1$ holds, we move the particle at site $x$ to site $x+1$ in configuration $\eta^{\prime}$. 
\item $B=0$. Then, if $\eta(x)=1-\eta(x+1)=0$ holds, we move the particle at site $x+1$ to site $x$ in configuration $\eta$. Similarly, if $\eta^{\prime}(x)=1-\eta^{\prime}(x+1)=0$ holds, we move the particle at site $x+1$ to site $x$ in configuration $\eta^{\prime}$. 

\end{itemize}
In all other cases, the configuration does not change.

On P_2(R^d), let F=G+tau H be convex under linear mixing, where tau>0 and H(mu)=integral log(dmu/dx) dmu for absolutely continuous mu, and +infinity otherwise. For every mu, G admits a first variation G_prime[mu] in C^1(R^d) of the form G_prime[mu](x)=a|x|^2/2+V[mu](x), with a,L>0 independent of mu and |grad V[mu](x)|<=L for every mu,x. A Wasserstein gradient flow here means a P_2-continuous distributional solution partial_t mu_t=div(mu_t grad G_prime[mu_t])+tau Delta mu_t, positive for t>0, which satisfies F(mu_t2)-F(mu_t1)=-integral_t1^t2 integral |grad G_prime[mu_s]+tau grad log(mu_s)|^2 dmu_s ds. Define tau_c=inf{s>=0:G+s H is convex}. Let mu_0 satisfy integral exp(|x|^2/M_0^2) dmu_0<=2 for some M_0>0. Enlarge M_0 if necessary so that M_0>=sqrt(8 tau/a), which preserves this moment assumption. (1) If tau>=tau_c>0, set t_0=a^(-1)[5+log(M_0^2 a/tau)]. There is C>0 depending only on d,a,tau,L,M_0 such that for t>=t_0, F(mu_t)-inf F <= [(F(mu_t0)-inf F)^(-1)+C(t-t_0)]^(-1). (2) If tau>tau_c>=0, then for every kappa>1, set t_0=a^(-1)[5+log(M_0^2 a kappa/tau)]. There is C>0 depending only on d,kappa,a,tau,L,M_0 such that for t>=t_0, F(mu_t)-inf F <= [(F(mu_t0)-inf F)^(-1/kappa)+C(tau-tau_c)^(1+1/kappa)(t-t_0)]^(-kappa). A zero gap at t_0 remains zero. Constants are computable from the proofs; the theorem does not assert polynomial dependence on d or 1/tau.

[Definition def:external-K-sparse-event of arXiv:2605.06511, 'Logarithmic Mixing of Random Walks on Dynamical Random Cluster Models'] Given $v \in V$, let $E_v \coloneqq E\left(B_R (v)\right)$ and consider the discrete-time random cluster Glauber dynamics $\left(\eta_{\langle t \rangle}^{E_v}\right)_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ with parameters $(p, q)$, that is, the dynamics where all edges in $E_v$ are wired open. 
		
		For all $F \subseteq \partial B_R (v)$, we define $S^F_{\langle t \rangle} \left(B_R(v)\right)$ as the event that, in the graph $\left(V,\eta_{\langle t \rangle}^{E_v}  \setminus E_v\right)$, the vertices in $\partial B_R (v)$ which are in non-trivial components are exactly $F$. 
		
		We define $S_{\langle t \rangle} \left(B_R(v), K\right)$ as the event that $S^F_{\langle t \rangle} \left(B_R(v)\right)$ holds for some $F \subseteq \partial B_R (u)$ such that $|F| \leq K$. Furthermore, we define $S_{\langle t \rangle} (R, K) \coloneqq \cap_{v \in V} S_{\langle t \rangle} (B_R(v), K)$. For $t'' > t' > 0$, by $S_{\langle[t', t'']\rangle} (R, K)$ we denote the event that $S_{\langle t \rangle} (R, K)$ holds for all $t \in [t', t'']$.
		
		By  $S^F_t \left(B_R (v)\right)$, $S_t \left(B_R (v), K\right)$, $S_t (R, K)$ and $S_{[t', t'']} (R, K)$ we will denote the continuous-time analogues of each event, respectively.

body:
[Proposition 26 (Two-sided finite-matrix criticality certificates) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] For $k\in\mathbb N$ partition $[0,a_*]$ into cells $I_1,\dots,I_k$ of mesh $a_*/k$, giving the finite partition $\{X_j\}$ of $X$ into $mk$ cells. Define the $mk\times mk$ nonnegative matrices
\[
\big(M^{(k)}_-\big)_{ij}=\inf_{x\in X_i,\ y\in X_j}\kappa(x,y)\,\nu(X_j),\qquad \big(M^{(k)}_+\big)_{ij}=\sup_{x\in X_i,\ y\in X_j}\kappa(x,y)\,\nu(X_j).
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Sandwich.) $\rho\big(M^{(k)}_-\big)\le\rho(K)\le\rho\big(M^{(k)}_+\big)$ for every $k$.
\item (Convergence.) $\rho\big(M^{(k)}_\pm\big)\to\rho(K)$ as $k\to\infty$.
\item (Certificates.) $\rho(M^{(k)}_-)>1$ for some $k$ certifies supercriticality of the sensitive-regime cascade skeleton; $\rho(M^{(k)}_+)<1$ certifies subcriticality. Both certificates are verifiable in finite linear algebra, and one of the two obtains for every non-critical parameter point.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Proposition 34 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\), define
\[
\Sigma_a
:=
\left\{
\theta\in\mathbb{C}:
1+(e^{\theta}-1)r\in(-\infty,0]
\text{ for some } r\in[0,\rho_a]
\right\}.
\]
Then \(\Lambda_a\) extends holomorphically to \(\mathbb{C}\setminus\Sigma_a\). For every integer \(n\geq1\),
\[
\Lambda_a^{(n)}(0)
=
\frac{1}{4\pi(a-1)}
\sum_{m=1}^{n}
(-1)^{m+1}(m-1)!S(n,m)
B\left(\frac{m}{a-1},m+1\right),
\]
where \(S(n,m)\) is the Stirling number of the second kind. The Taylor radius \(R_a\) of \(\Lambda_a\) at \(0\) is
\[
R_a
=
\operatorname{dist}(0,\Sigma_a)
=
\sqrt{
\pi^2+
\left(
\max\left\{
\log\frac{1-\rho_a}{\rho_a},
0
\right\}
\right)^2
}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
R_a
=
\begin{cases}
\pi,
&
a\geq a_c,\\[2mm]
\sqrt{\pi^2+\log^2\left(\frac{1-\rho_a}{\rho_a}\right)},
&
1<a<a_c,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(a_c>1\) is the unique solution of \((a_c-1)a_c^{-a_c/(a_c-1)}=1/2\).

body:
[Lem 48 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Suppose $J_+ \neq \emptyset$, and define
    \begin{align}
        
        \Delta_+(\vartheta) 
        &\equiv \vartheta + \gamma_+(z_\star) - \gamma_+(\beta_\star(\gamma_\star + \vartheta))
        \,,\\
        
        \Delta_-(\vartheta) 
        &\equiv \vartheta + \gamma_+(\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta)) - \gamma_+(z_\star)\,.
    \end{align}
These functions are continuous and strictly increasing on the intervals $[0,+\infty)$ and $[0,\vartheta_{-,\max})$ respectively, where in the latter case we define
    \[
        \vartheta_{-,\max} \equiv \sup\lt\{
            \vartheta \ge 0 : \beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta) > z_0
        \rt\}\,.
    \]
    Furthermore, $\Delta_+(0) = \Delta_-(0) = 0$ and 
    \beq
        
        \lim_{\vartheta \uparrow +\infty} \Delta_+(\vartheta)
        = \lim_{\vartheta \uparrow \vartheta_{-,\max}} \Delta_-(\vartheta)
        = +\infty\,.
    \eeq
    In particular, for any $\delta > 0$, there exist (unique) solutions $\vartheta_+ \in (0,+\infty)$, $\vartheta_- \in (0,\vartheta_{-,\max})$ to the equations
    \beq
        
        \Delta_+(\vartheta_+) = \Delta_-(\vartheta_-) = \delta\,.
    \eeq
\begin{proof}
    Since $J_+ \neq \emptyset$, we have $\hv_1 > 0$ and $z_0 = m^{-1}(\alpha / \hv_1)$, and thus case \eqref{i:fp-case2} or \eqref{i:fp-case3} of Remark~\ref{r:fp.cases} holds. In either case, we have $z_\star > z_0$. Note that $\gamma_+$ is strictly decreasing for $z > z_0$. Since $\beta_\star(\gamma_\star) = z_\star$, we have $\Delta_+(0) = \Delta_-(0) = 0$.
Recall that $\beta_\star$ is nondecreasing by Lemma~\ref{l:fp-g2}\eqref{i:fp-beta-incr}; it follows that $\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta) > z_0$ for all $\vartheta \in [0,\vartheta_{-,\max})$. Moreover, $\beta_\star$ is continuous, so $\Delta_+$ and $\Delta_-$ are continuous and strictly increasing on their respective domains. It remains to verify \eqref{e:fp-vartheta-limit}.
Since $\Delta_+(\vartheta)\ge\vartheta$, it is clear the limit involving $\Delta_+$ is $+\infty$.
Similarly, since $\Delta_-(\vartheta)\ge\vartheta$, 
 the limit involving $\Delta_-$ is also clearly $+\infty$ in the case $\vartheta_{-,\max} = +\infty$.
    Otherwise, we must have $\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta) \downarrow z_0$ as $\vartheta \uparrow \vartheta_{-,\max}$, so $\gamma_+(\beta_\star(\gamma_\star - \vartheta)) \uparrow +\infty$.
    This proves \eqref{e:fp-vartheta-limit}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 48 of arXiv:2608.29416

body:
[Proposition proposition of arXiv:2411.05541, 'Gaskets of $O(2)$ loop-decorated random planar maps'] Let $(g_j)_{j\ge 1}$ be a sequence of non-negative real numbers such that $\sum_{j\ge 1} jg_j \le 1$. Let $\nu$ be defined by (equation eq nu 2 of the paper). Assume that $\nu(0)<1$ and that for all $k\in \mathbb{Z}$, we have $\nu(k)\ge 0$. Then $\nu$ is a probability distribution and $h^\downarrow$ is $\nu$-harmonic on $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$. Moreover, for all $k\ge 1$,
	$$
	\nu(k-1) - \nu(-k-1)= g_k\ge 0.
	$$
	In particular, the sequence ${\bf q}= (q_k)_{k\ge 1}$ defined by setting for all $k\ge 1$,
	$$
	q_k = \nu(k-1) (\nu(-1)/2)^{k-1}
	$$
	is the weight sequence of the gasket of a critical $O(2)$ loop-decorated map. The associated triple $(\widetilde{\bf q}, 1/c_{\bf q}, 2)$ is given by $c_{\bf q} = 2/\nu(-1)$ and for all $k\ge 1$,
	$$
	\tilde{q}_k = g_k (\nu(-1)/2)^{k-1}.
	$$
title: Proposition proposition of arXiv:2411.05541

[Lem DevShuf of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] For any $k=1,\cdots,m-1$, one has 
\begin{align}
 & \big[e^{x_{t_{\sigma(m-k)}}{\rm ad}_{A}}(F_{I}({\rm e}_{2})),\big[\cdots\big[e^{x_{t_{\sigma(m-1)}}{\rm ad}_{A}}(F_{I}({\rm e}_{2})),e^{x_{t_{\sigma(m)}}{\rm ad}_{A}}(F_{I}({\rm e}_{2}))\big]\big]\big]\nonumber \\
 & =\sum_{j}\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}(-1)^{j+k-i-1}\big(((e^{a_{j}},\stackrel{\nearrow}{\cdots},e^{a_{i-1}})\shuffle(e^{a_{j+k}},\stackrel{\searrow}{\cdots},e^{a_{i+2}}))\nonumber \\
 & \ \ \ \ \ \ \otimes[e^{a_{i}},e^{a_{i+1}}]\big)(t_{\sigma(m-k)},\cdots,t_{\sigma(m)})E_{j,j+k+1}.
\end{align}
Here the Lie bracket is taken in $\mathfrak{sl}_{m+1}(\mathbb{C})$
and we adopt the convention that $E_{p,q}=0$ if $p,q\leqslant0$
or $\geqslant m+2$.

Method: Ordered-phase susceptibility exponent on random trees and graphs structural reduction Result: At zero cavity field, the expected generation-k contribution to susceptibility is proportional to nu^(k-1)*(tanh beta)^k, yielding a geometric series only when nu*tanh beta<1. Above criticality that same bound diverges, so it cannot prove the desired finite susceptibility asymptotic in the plus state. [Definition def_supermartingaleBIS of arXiv:2608.08299, 'Non-linear optimal stopping with Bermudan strategies: the infinite horizon case'] Let $\phi=(\phi(\tau), \, \tau \in \Theta)$ be a \emph{non-negative admissible} family.
 We say that $\phi$
 is a \emph{$(\Theta, \rho)$}-supermartingale (resp. \emph{$(\Theta, \rho)$}-martingale) \emph{family} if 
 for all $\sigma, \tau$ in $\Theta$ such that $\sigma\leq\tau$ a.s., we have 
$$\rho_{\sigma,\tau}[\phi({\tau})]\leq \phi({\sigma}) \text{ (resp. }=\phi(\sigma)) \text{ a.s.} $$

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Identify what makes q = 1 and q = 2 expandable and whether a q-analogue of the random-current switching lemma exists. Result: q = 1 is Bernoulli percolation (independence gives the pivotal decomposition); q = 2 is expandable through the random-current representation and the switching lemma (Sakai's lace expansion for the Ising model). For integer q >= 3 the Potts model has a random-current-like representation (the 'random-current representation for Potts' via the Edwards-Sokal coupling with q colours) but the switching lemma fails because currents are Z_q-valued and the pairing structure that gives the switching identity is specific to Z_2. A lace expansion needs a 'pivotal' notion for which the model factorises across the pivotal: in FK with general q the cluster weight q^{k(omega)} couples the two sides of a pivotal edge only through the count of clusters, which changes by one when the pivotal is closed; this suggests an expansion in which each pivotal carries a factor q or 1 depending on whether closing it splits a cluster, i.e. a lace expansion for the two-point function with the cluster count as an extra variable, which is exactly the generating function in the number of clusters, i.e. the Tutte polynomial. So the expansion would be an expansion of the Tutte polynomial's two-point version, which is #P-hard to evaluate in general, suggesting no simple diagrammatic expansion exists for generic q; for the infrared bound one might instead use reflection positivity (available for integer q and for the FK model on Z^d with q >= 1 via the Potts representation), which gives the infrared bound for the Potts spin-spin covariance directly for integer q >= 1 (Frohlich-Simon-Spencer), without a lace expansion. Recorded: for integer q the infrared bound is available by reflection positivity (this is classical), so the source's 'and use it to derive an infrared bound' is partly moot for integer q; the genuinely open content is the expansion itself and the non-integer q infrared bound. Key identity: Reflection positivity gives the infrared bound for integer-q Potts covariances without any expansion; the open part is non-integer q and the expansion. Obstruction: No switching lemma for Z_q currents; the natural expansion variable is a Tutte-polynomial quantity.

[Theorem thm:explicit_current_2 of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be an ergodic diffusion with invariant measure $\mu$ whose
symmetric part $\mathcal{L}_S$ satisfies the Poincar\'e inequality~(equation eq:poincare of the paper)
with spectral gap $\lambda_\mathrm{gap}>0$ (Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper)). 
Let $\overline{J}_t(U)$ denote the empirical current according to Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper)
with ergodic mean $\E^\mu[\overline{J}_t(U)]=\E^\mu[v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U]= \E^\mu[W]$,
and let $\nu\ll\mu$ with $\mathrm{d}\nu/\mathrm{d}\mu\in L^2(\mu)$.
Then for all $t > 0$ and $a > 0$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}^\nu\left(\overline{J}_t(U) - \E^\mu[\overline{J}_t] \geq a\right)
\leq
\left\|\frac{\mathrm{d}\nu}{\mathrm{d}\mu}\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}
\exp\left[-t \frac{\tilde\sigma_{J,2}^2}{c_{J,2}^2}
  h\left(\frac{c_{J,2} a}{\tilde\sigma_{J,2}^2}\right)\right],

\end{align}
where $h(u) = 1 + u - \sqrt{1+2u}$ and the parameters 
$\tilde\sigma_{J,2}^2$ and $c_{J,2}$ as in
Lemma~(lem:bernstein_current of the paper).
title: Explicit concentration bound for the empirical current (Approach 2)

[Proposition prop:clock of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] For the symmetric chain, $\cos\theta(t)=e^{-2t}$ is the relaxation factor of the
slowest non-constant mode, whose generator eigenvalue is $-2$ by
(cor:ehr-spec of the paper). Moreover $\theta(t)/2$ is a statistical angle. If
$q_t=(p(t),1-p(t))$ is the law of one ball and $\delta_a=(1,0)$, then with the
Bhattacharyya coefficient $\mathrm{BC}(p,q)=\sum_i\sqrt{p_iq_i}$ and the statistical
angle $\arccos\mathrm{BC}$ ((sec:primer-info of the paper)),

\[
\mathrm{BC}(\delta_a,q_t)=\sqrt{p(t)},\qquad
\arccos\mathrm{BC}(\delta_a,q_t)=\arccos\sqrt{p(t)}=\frac{\theta(t)}2 .
\]

[Theorem thm:introduction-density-bound of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $\eta$ be a translation-invariant point process of intensity
$\rho$, supported on uniformly separated configurations. If
\[
    \sigma_\eta(\Omega)=0,
\]
then
\[
    \rho\geq\mathcal D(\Omega).
\]
In particular, if $C\subset\Omega$ is symmetric and convex, then
\[
    \rho\geq2^{-d}\lambda_d(C).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $(M,g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature and without boundary (for instance $M=\mathbb R^n$), and let $u>0$ be a smooth solution of $u_t=\Delta u$ on $M\times(0,\infty)$. Then the differential Harnack (Li-Yau) inequality holds pointwise: $\frac{|\nabla u|^2}{u^2}-\frac{u_t}{u}\le\frac{n}{2t}$, equivalently $-\Delta\log u\le\frac n{2t}$. Integrating along geodesics gives the classical Harnack form: for $x_1,x_2\in M$ and $0<t_1<t_2$, $u(x_1,t_1)\le u(x_2,t_2)\Big(\frac{t_2}{t_1}\Big)^{n/2}\exp\Big(\frac{d(x_1,x_2)^2}{4(t_2-t_1)}\Big).$ Both are sharp: equality in the differential form holds for the Gaussian $u=\Phi(x,t)$ on $\mathbb R^n$. Positivity of $u$ on the whole of $M\times(0,\infty)$ and $\mathrm{Ric}\ge0$ are both needed; if $\mathrm{Ric}\ge-K$ with $K>0$ the estimate degrades to $\alpha\frac{|\nabla u|^2}{u^2}-\frac{u_t}{u}\le\frac{n\alpha^2}{2t}+\frac{n\alpha^2K}{2(\alpha-1)}$ for any $\alpha>1$.
(M,g) complete, without boundary, Ric >= 0 (M = R^n is the model case)
u > 0 everywhere on M x (0,infinity) and smooth
u solves the heat equation u_t = Delta u

[Theorem 29 (EFIID implies analyticity \cite{Ott_Analyticity_Ising,Ott_Analyticity_RCM}) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Let $\mu$ be a stationary random field on $S^{\Z^d}$.
 Write $\sigma\sim\mu$ for the random element.
 Consider a finite set $A\subset\Z^d$
 and a bounded observable $F_A$ that is $\sigma|_A$-measurable.
 If $\mu$ is an EFIID, then there exists a constant $\delta=\delta(\mu,F_A)>0$ such that the function
 \[
    \tilde F_A:(-\delta,\delta)\to\R,\,\epsilon\mapsto
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1{|\Lambda_n|}\log\mu\Big[ \exp\Big(\eps\sum\nolimits_{x\in\Lambda_n}F_A(\tau_x\sigma)\Big)\Big]
 \]
 is analytic. 
 Here $\tau_x(\sigma)$ means that we translate the configuration $\sigma$ by $x$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: EFIID implies analyticity \cite{Ott_Analyticity_Ising,Ott_Analyticity_RCM}

[Lemma 21 (Doeblin minorization) of arXiv:2512.02661, 'Worst-case mixing estimates for Brownian motion with semipermeable barriers'] Suppose that one is given some $C,T>0$ such that for every $x_0\in D$ and measurable $E\subseteq D$,
	\begin{align}
		\bbP(X_T \in E \mid X_0 = x_0) \geq C  \Area(E).
	\end{align}
	Then,
	$
		\pi_{\min} \geq C
	$ and the mixing time satisfies
	$
		\tmix \leq T \lceil \ln(1/4)/\ln(1 - C\Area(D))\rceil.
	$
title: Doeblin minorization

body: In infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, Gaussian measures with different covariance operators are mutually singular by the Cameron-Martin / Feldman-Hajek theorem, making the total variation distance $d_{\mathrm{TV}}$ degenerate ($= 1$). The $d_2$ probability metric, requiring two continuous bounded Fréchet derivatives on test functions, provides the natural topology for quantitative functional CLTs in infinite-dimensional path spaces.
title: Comparison between d2 Distance and Total Variation

body: Theorem 1.12 (0/1-Polytopes with Poor Vertex Expansion). Let pi be the uniform distribution. For any k > 2 and any n > 2k sufficiently large, there is a 0/1-polytope Q = Q_{n,k} in {0, 1}^n with O(n^k) vertices and psi(Q) <~ (4k)^k / n^{k-2}. Here psi(Q) is the weighted vertex expansion (Definition 1.2) of the graph of Q: for S in V with vertex boundary dS := {v not in S | uv in E for some u in S}, psi(S) := pi(dS)/pi(S), and psi(G) := min{1, min over S in V with 0 < pi(S) <= 1/2 of psi(S)}; with pi uniform, psi(S) = |dS|/|S|.

[Lemma cap.translation of arXiv:2411.19145, 'On the intersection of critical percolation clusters and other tree-like random graphs'] For any finite sets $A,B \subset V$, one has the subadditivity property, 
$${\rm Cap}_\beta(A\cup B) \le {\rm Cap}_\beta(A) + {\rm Cap}_\beta(B). $$ 
Furthermore ${\rm Cap}_\beta$ is monotone for the inclusion of sets.

On G = {0,1}^2 put F(0,0) = 1/10, F(1,0) = F(0,1) = 3/5 and F(1,1) = 1. F is order-preserving and F(1,1) = 1, but its mixed difference at (1,1) is 1 - 3/5 - 3/5 + 1/10 = -1/10 < 0, so F is the CDF of no random vector on G: a negative full mixed difference, not a failure of monotonicity, is what rules it out.

body: In mathematics, a simple group is a nontrivial group whose only normal subgroups are the trivial group and the group itself. A group that is not simple can be broken into two smaller groups, namely a nontrivial normal subgroup and the corresponding quotient group. This process can be repeated, and for finite groups one eventually arrives at uniquely determined simple groups, by the Jordan–Hölder theorem.
title: Simple group

[Corollary Wulff corollary of arXiv:2608.27248, 'Optimal Transport and the ABP Method in Higher Codimension'] Let $n\geq2$ and $1\leq m\leq4$.  Let
$X:\Sigma\to\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ be a compact minimal immersion with smooth boundary,
and let $\mathcal E\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ be a centered ellipsoid.  Then
$\partial\Sigma\ne\varnothing$ and
\[
 \int_{\partial\Sigma}h_{\mathcal E}(\eta)\,\mathrm d\sigma
 \geq nV_*(\mathcal E)^{1/n}|\Sigma|^{\frac{n-1}{n}}.
\]
Equality holds if and only if, for an $n$-plane $P$ realizing
$V_*(\mathcal E)$, $X$ is an embedding onto
$x_0+r\,\overline{\operatorname{proj}_P\mathcal E}$ for some
$x_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ and $r>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sharp ellipsoidal Wulff inequality

body: Invariance of domain: Let n >= 1, let U be an open subset of R^n, and let f : U -> R^n be an injective continuous map. Then f(U) is open in R^n, and f is a homeomorphism from U onto f(U). The equality of dimensions is essential: the conclusion fails for injective continuous maps of an open subset of R^n into R^m with m > n (for example, the inclusion of R^1 as a line in R^2 has image with empty interior).
title: Invariance of domain

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2609.00448, 'Equivariant formality and representation theory'] \textnormal{(cf. \cite[Theorem 6.2]{CFok}).}
	We have the ring isomorphism
	\[K^*(G/K; \mathbb{Q})\cong (R(K; \mathbb{Q})/i^*I(G; \mathbb{Q})\oplus\mathfrak{a})\otimes\bigwedge\nolimits^*P.\]
	Here $R(K; \mathbb{Q})/i^*(G; \mathbb{Q})$ is the image of the map $\alpha: R(K; \mathbb{Q})\to K^0(G/K; \mathbb{Q})$ defined by the associated vector bundle $\alpha(\rho):=[G\times_K V]$, $\mathfrak{a}$ is an ideal of the first tensor factor on the RHS. We also have that $j^*$ maps $P$ isomorphically onto $Q$. Moreover, $\text{dim }P=\text{dim }Q\leq \text{rank }G-\text{rank }K$, and equality holds if and only if $G/K$ is formal, if and only if $\mathfrak{a}=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 13 of arXiv:2609.00448

Let Ω ⊂ R^n be bounded and open, let λ > 0, and let H: Ω̄ × R^n → R be continuous and satisfy the structure condition |H(x,p) - H(y,p)| ≤ ω( |x-y| (1 + |p|) ) for all x,y ∈ Ω̄ and all p ∈ R^n, where ω: [0,∞) → [0,∞) is nondecreasing with ω(0+) = 0. Let u ∈ USC(Ω̄) be a viscosity subsolution and v ∈ LSC(Ω̄) a viscosity supersolution of λ w + H(x,Dw) = 0 in Ω (the test-function definition is used verbatim for semicontinuous functions). If u ≤ v on ∂Ω, then u ≤ v on Ω̄. In particular the Dirichlet problem λ w + H(x,Dw) = 0 in Ω, w = g on ∂Ω, has at most one continuous viscosity solution.
Ω bounded and open (compactness of Ω̄ is used)
λ > 0 strictly: the zero-order term must be strictly monotone in w

u upper semicontinuous subsolution, v lower semicontinuous supersolution on Ω̄
u ≤ v on ∂Ω

[Theorem 37 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $n\in\Nsf$, let $M'$ be a manifold and let $f: M'\to R_n^2M'$ be a rough velocity field. Let also $M$ be a properly embedded submanifold of $M'$ with $\phi: M\to M'$ being the embedding. Then the following statements are equivalent:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
	\itemsep0em
	\item It holds that $(f\circ\phi) (M)\subseteq \mathrm{Im}( R_n^2\phi )$.
	\item For every interval $[S,T]\subseteq\Rsf$, every $n$-dimensional branched rough path $X$ on interval $[S,T]$ with regularity $p\in [1,3)$ and control function $\omega$, and every integral curve $Y:[S,T]\to M'$ of $f$ driven by $X$ such that $Y(S)\in \phi(M)$, we have that $Y(t)\in \phi(M) $ for every $t\in [S,T]$.
	\end{enumerate}

[Lemma L:massOutofCompact of arXiv:2606.03079, 'Mean Field Limits for Stochastic, Underdamped Reactive Langevin Dynamics Models'] There exists a sequence of $C_{b}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d)$ functions $\{f_{m}(x,v)\}_{m \geq 0}$ with $f_{0} \equiv 1$ such that
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{m}(x,v) &=0 \text { when }\|x\| + \|v\| \leq m-1 \\
f_{m}(x,v) &=1 \text { when }\|x\|+ \|v\|>m \\
0 \leq f_{m}(x,v) & \leq 1 \text { when } m-1<\|x\| + \|v\|\leq m .
\end{aligned}
$$
Additionally, $\displaystyle\sup _{m \geq 0}\|f_{m}(x,v)\|_{C_{b}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d)}:=\sup _{m \geq 0} \mkern22mu \smashoperator{\sup_{\substack{ x \in \mathbb{R}^{d},v \in \mathbb{R}^{d},\\ |\alpha| \leq 2\strut}}}|D_{\alpha} f_{m}(x,v)|<\infty$. For such a sequence of functions $\{f_{m}(x,v)\}_{m \geq 0}$, we have
$$
\lim _{m \rightarrow \infty} \limsup _{\zeta \rightarrow 0} \mathbb{E}\left[\sup _{t \in[0, T]}\langle f_{m}, \mu_{t}^{\zeta, j}\rangle \right]=0
$$
for all $j=1,2, \cdots, J$.

	\[
	
	\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
		R & Q \\
		{X\times X} & {Y\times Y.}
		\arrow["{\exists \bar f}"', dashed, from=1-1, to=1-2]
		\arrow[tail, from=1-1, to=2-1]
		\arrow[tail, from=1-2, to=2-2]
		\arrow["{f\times f}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	The map $\bar f$ is unique if it exists. The commutativity of the square above is equivalent to saying that the \emph{source} and \emph{target squares} commute:

		\arrow["f", from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\end{tikzcd}
	\qquad\text{and}\qquad
	\begin{tikzcd}[cramped]
		R & Q \\
		X & {Y.}
		\arrow["{\bar f}", from=1-1, to=1-2]

		\arrow["{t_Q}", from=1-2, to=2-2]

      \leq
      \tilde{c}_2(K,t) 2^{-\ell \varepsilon}.
    \end{equation}

DRAFT proof (unaudited), T318-C6 v2. Let s>0 and, conditionally on a random training environment, let V_p(g)>=0 and f_p(g) be test functions with E_g V_p -> c>0, Var_g V_p ->0, E_g f_p^2 ->R>0 in probability and E_g f_p^4=O_P(1). Then all measurable exact or o_P(1)-approximate global minimizers over T>=0 of L_p(T)=0.5 E_g[log((s+T V_p)/s)+(s+f_p^2)/(s+T V_p)-1] converge in probability to R/c. No independence of V_p and f_p is assumed. Compact uniform convergence follows from a uniform derivative bound; the event V_p>=c/2 has test probability tending to one and gives a logarithmic tail lower bound excluding all diverging T uniformly. Applied to the unaudited C4 shared-feature Gaussian teacher model with fixed nonconstant globally Lipschitz activation, independent spherical hidden directions, Gaussian inputs, positive finite aspect ratios, prior variance s_p^2>0, teacher variance s_*^2>=0, and correct positive test/training noise sigma^2, this proves whole-posterior finite-model temperature minimizers converge to 1+(r-1)lambda m_2(lambda)/m(lambda). Here lambda=sigma^2/s_p^2, r=s_*^2/s_p^2, m(a) is the positive centered-covariance weighted resolvent from C4 and m_2=-mprime. This includes raw ReLU. Likelihood tempering is excluded; no independent audit or priority claim.

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): In the component encoding, sequences with k = O(n/log n) and ell -> infinity are controlled whenever 4^ell = o(ell*log n); the residual error from 9*4^ell + ell is then negligible against the leading saving -(n-r)*ell. Equivalently the uniformly controlled range includes ell ≤ (1/2)*log2 log n + (1/2)*log2 log log n - omega(1). Quantifier (audit-corrected): if a sequence merely fails the little-o condition, the corresponding lower bound on ell is valid only along a subsequence where 4^ell/(ell*log n) stays bounded below - not an every-index conclusion for an oscillating sequence. Fixed-defect cases are handled separately by finite-core enumeration. Notes: 'Controlled' is relative to the moment-argument encoding; this does NOT decide the conjecture, and a substantial regime remains where 4^ell is too large to pay directly. Threshold re-checked: at the stated ell bound, 4^ell = (log n)(log log n)*2^(-omega(1)) = o(ell*log n). Superscripts flattened in extraction.

body: For every n except 2 and 6 there exists a pair of orthogonal Latin squares of order n, i.e. N(n) >= 2 for all n not in {2, 6}. [Lemma lem: distribution of X of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Let $n=ml$, such that $m,l\ge 2$. Suppose the entries of $A=(a_{ij})\in\Mat_m(\mathbb{Z})$ are nonnegative, and all the rows and columns have sum $l$. Let $\tau$ be distributed with respect to $U_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$. Then, we have
$$\mathbf{P}(X(\tau)=A)=\frac{(l!)^{2m}}{n!\cdot\prod_{1\le i,j\le m}a_{ij}!}.$$
Moreover, suppose 
$t=\frac n2\left(\log n-\frac 12\log l+c\right)$,  where $c\in \mathbb{R}$ is an absolute constant. Let $\sigma$ be distributed with respect to $\mu_n^t$. Then, for all $k\ge 0$, we have
$$\mathbf{P}(X(\sigma)=A\mid |S_t|=k)=\sum_{r_1+\cdots+r_m=k}\frac{k!(l!)^m\prod_{i=1}^m(l-r_i)!}{n!\prod_{i\ne j}a_{ij}!}\prod_{i=1}^m\binom{a_{ii}}{r_i}.$$

[Definition def:asymptotic-direction of arXiv:2607.24018, 'Jeu de taquin forests \\ and the inverse infinite RSK correspondence'] Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}_0^2$ be an infinite set of boxes in the positive
	quarter-plane.
	We say that $A$ has an \emph{asymptotic direction} if the limit
	\[
		\alpha_\textnormal{asym}(A) := \lim_{n\to\infty} \alpha(x_n, y_n)
	\]
	exists for any enumeration $((x_n,y_n))_{n=1}^\infty$ of
	the elements of $A$ for which $x_n+y_n
	\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} \infty$. The limit value
	$\alpha_\textnormal{asym}(A) \in [0,1]$ is called the \emph{asymptotic
		RSK-angle of~$A$}, or, in a slight abuse of language, the
	asymptotic direction of~$A$.

[Proposition prop:uniform flows of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph, $q\geq 2$ be an integer, $x_e\in (0,1)$ for each $e\in E,$ $\Omega=\{0,1\}^E,$ $\Sigma=\ker(\partial)$ and $f:\Omega\to 2^{\Sigma}$ be defined by $f(\omega)=\ker(\partial^\omega)$ and 
$$
\rho[\omega]\propto \mathbb{P}_x[\omega],\quad\forall \omega\in \Omega,\qquad \gamma[\eta]\propto 1,\quad\forall \eta\in \Sigma.
$$
	Then, under the coupling measure $\mathscr{P}$ defined in Theorem (thm:generalcoupling of the paper), 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$ is $\ell^q_{G,x}$.
        For each $\omega\in\Omega$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \omega]$ on $\Sigma$ is the uniform  measure on $\ker(\partial^\omega)$, i.e. a uniform divergence free $q$-coloring of $\omega$.
		\item[(b)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$ is the random-cluster model with cluster-weight $q$ and edge-weights $(p_e)_{e\in E}$  satisfying $\frac{x_e}{1-x_e}=\frac{p_e}{q(1-p_e)},$ 
        \[
        \phi^q_{G,p}[\omega]\propto \left(\prod_{e\in \omega} \frac{p_e}{1-p_e}\right)q^{\kappa(\omega)}.
        \]
        For each $\eta\in\Sigma$, the 
        conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \eta] = \mathbb{P}_{x} \cup \delta_{\eta}$ on $\Omega$ is Bernoulli percolation on $E$ with parameter $(x_e)_{e\in E}$ conditioned on all edges in $\eta$ being open.
	\end{enumerate}

PRIVATE HEURISTIC, author-recorded. In scale-free percolation with weight tail exponent tau and long-range parameter alpha (connection probability 1 - exp(-lambda W_x W_y |x-y|^{-alpha d})), the annealed two-point connection decays like |x-y|^{-alpha d (tau-1)}, i.e. like long-range percolation with P(x <-> y) ~ |x-y|^{-d-s} for s = d(alpha(tau-1) - 1). Long-range percolation is mean-field for d > 3 min(s, 2) (Heydenreich-van der Hofstad-Sakai), which predicts mean-field critical behaviour for scale-free percolation iff alpha(tau - 1) < 4/3 or d > 6, with tau > 3 (for tau in (2,3) the model percolates instantly). This is a prediction for Heydenreich-van der Hofstad Open Problem 16.8, not a theorem: the quenched weights induce correlations that the annealed long-range comparison ignores.
Scale-free percolation on Z^d with parameters alpha, tau, lambda
Long-range percolation upper critical dimension 3 min(s,2)
title: Scale-free percolation: an effective long-range exponent and the predicted mean-field region

A residual certificate for the reduced coordinate family lifts with the same dimension; the free coordinate contributes at most one new quotient class, exactly matching the increase in ambient rank, so dgeo(F') ≤ 2 implies dgeo(F) ≤ 2. By induction, arbitrarily many zero columns may be deleted and reinserted without changing density or invalidating a low-dimensional certificate; a hypothetical distance-three counterexample remains a counterexample after deletion. Notes: Repairs an implicit step in the earlier project tree; justifies reducing to nonzero Gale columns before the finite normal-form analysis.

[Defn 7 (Colored fat tree) of arXiv:2604.26499, 'Spectrum of Random Matrices with Exploding Moments'] A connected directed graph $T=(V, E)$, whose each edge is colored by red or blue, is called colored fat tree if it satisfies the following properties.
Any directed edge $u\to v$ is accompanied by at least one more edge of any color in the same direction, and there is no edge in the reverse direction. It does not contain any vertex with a loop. Additionally, the underlying simple graph $\mathcal{T}=(V, \mathcal{E}),$ obtained by ignoring orientation and multiplicity satisfies $|V|=|\mathcal{E}|+1$.

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02320, 'Analysis of Triggered Packet Streams: A Matrix-Analytic Method for Exponential Triggering...'] In many communication networks, the transmission of a packet may automatically trigger the transmission of a subsequent packet from the same source after a (possibly random) delay, without requiring acknowledgment or feedback. Such behavior arises in multi-stage status updating, proactive protocols, and other applications where users generate causally dependent packet streams. In this paper, in order to analyze these systems, we introduce the $\mathrm{M^T/G/1}$ queue. In this model, primary customers arrive according to a Poisson process, and each primary customer triggers a secondary customer to join the queue after an independent delay. This arrival mechanism falls outside the scope of classical queueing models with renewal arrival processes. When the triggering delays follow an exponential distribution, we exploit the memoryless property to set up a tractable Markov description. By truncating the number of pending secondary customers, we derive a finite system of linear algebraic equations in the Laplace--Stieltjes transform domain and solve them using matrix-analytic methods. Based on the resulting workload distribution, we compute class-specific performance metrics using PASTA for primary customers and Palm conditioning for secondary customers. Finally, we validate the accuracy of this truncation through numerical experiments.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.02320: Analysis of Triggered Packet Streams: A Matrix-Analytic Method for Exponential Triggering...

[Theorem 4 (Sharp one-arm asymptotics) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Consider critical nearest-neighbour bond percolation on $\Z^d$ with $d\geq 11$. Then
\[
\lim_{r\to\infty}\ r^2\,\bP\bigl(0\leftrightarrow\partial B_r\bigr)
\;=\;\theta_1\;\in(0,\infty),
\]
where, with $\mathfrak a,\lambda$ as in \eqref{eq:guiding-kp}
\[
\theta_1\;=\;\mathbb{N}_{0,\lambda/\mathfrak a}\bigl(\Ran\not\subset\overline B_1\bigr)\;=\;\frac{\mathfrak a}{\lambda}\,\mathbb{N}_{0,1}\bigl(\Ran\not\subset\overline B_1\bigr),
\]
and $\mathbb{N}_{0,1}$ is the standard canonical measure of super-Brownian motion (i.e.\ the $(\tfrac12\Delta,1)$-super-Brownian motion); thus $\theta_1$ equals $\mathfrak a/\lambda$ times the probability that the range of standard super-Brownian motion is not contained in the unit ball. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let n>=1 and y_i in {-1,+1}, and let f(w;x_i) be continuously differentiable in w in R^D. Assume global constants rho>0 and beta>0 satisfy ||grad f(w;x_i)||_2<=rho and ||grad f(w;x_i)-grad f(v;x_i)||_2<=beta||w-v||_2 for every w,v and every training index i. Define L(w)=(1/n)sum_i log(1+exp(-y_i f(w;x_i))) and w_{k+1}=w_k-eta grad L(w_k), where eta>0 denotes the source paper's eta_tilde. If an integer r>=0 satisfies L(w_r)<=1/[eta(2rho^2+beta)], then L(w_t) is non-increasing for t>=r. Suppose additionally a global constant kappa>0 satisfies |f(w;x_i)-<grad f(w;x_i),w>|<=kappa for every w,i, and an integer s>=0 satisfies L(w_s)<=min{1/[2n exp(kappa+2)],1/[eta(4rho^2+2beta)]}. Then as t->infinity, L(w_t)=Theta(1/t), ||w_{t+1}||>=||w_t|| for t>=s, and ||w_t||=Theta(log t). For the normalized margin gamma_bar(w)=min_i y_i f(w;x_i)/||w||, there exists a modified margin gamma_c, non-decreasing and bounded along t>=s, and a constant c>0 with gamma_c(w_t)<=gamma_bar(w_t)<=[1+c/log(1/L(w_t))]gamma_c(w_t). Constants may depend on the fixed problem and initial stable-phase state; no dimension- or width-uniform constants are claimed. This theorem is conditional on reaching the displayed risk levels. The fixed-output-sign, trainable-first-layer network example in the source is one application; this statement does not establish a burn-in theorem when both layers are trained.

Let (X, Y) be a jointly Gaussian random vector in R^a x R^b with means mu_X, mu_Y and covariance blocks A = Cov(X), B = Cov(X, Y), C = Cov(Y), so its covariance matrix is M = [[A, B], [B^T, C]], possibly singular; A^+ is the Moore-Penrose inverse, and a value x is compatible when x - mu_X lies in the range of A (the support of X). For every compatible x, the conditional law of Y given X = x is Gaussian with mean mu_Y + B^T A^+ (x - mu_X) and covariance K = C - B^T A^+ B, which is positive semidefinite and does not depend on x; and rank M = rank A + rank K.

body: A map f from a topological space X to a topological space Y is continuous if for every open set V of Y the preimage f^(-1)(V) = {x in X : f(x) in V} is open in X. Equivalently: the preimage of every closed set is closed; equivalently, for every x in X and every open neighborhood V of f(x) there is an open neighborhood U of x with f(U) contained in V (continuity at every point). For maps between metric spaces this agrees with the epsilon-delta definition. Compositions of continuous maps are continuous.
title: Continuous map between topological spaces

body: [Lem isotopy_extension of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a $\Phi$-horizontal foliation on $M$. Let $(h_t)_{t\in [0,1]}$ be a $C^0$-isotopy of $\partial \mathcal{F}$ through $\Phi$-horizontal foliations on $\partial M$ which is smooth in the $t$ and leafwise directions. Then $h_t$ extends to a $C^0$ isotopy $\overline h_t$ of $\mathcal{F}$ through $\Phi$-horizontal foliations on $M$. Moreover, if $h_t$ is $\varepsilon$-small, then $\overline h_t$ is $O(\varepsilon)$-small, where the implicit constants may depend on $\Phi$ and $\mathcal{F}$ only.

Let n>=1 data (x_i,y_i) in R^d times {-1,+1} satisfy ||x_i||_2<=1. Assume a unit vector w_star and a fixed gamma>0 satisfy y_i <x_i,w_star> >= gamma for every i. Define ell(q)=log(1+exp(-q)), L(w)=(1/n)sum_i ell(y_i<x_i,w>), and full-batch GD w_{k+1}=w_k-eta grad L(w_k) with constant eta>0. Assume w_0=0. For every integer t>=1, (1/t)sum_{k=0}^{t-1}L(w_k)<=[1+log(gamma^2 eta t)^2+eta^2/4]/(gamma^2 eta t). Define F(w)=(1/n)sum_i exp(-y_i<x_i,w>). If L(w_s)<=1/eta at some nonnegative integer s, then risk is non-increasing from s onward, and every integer t>s satisfies L(w_t)<=[2F(w_s)+log(gamma^2 eta(t-s))^2]/[gamma^2 eta(t-s)]. There is such an s<=tau with F(w_s)<=1, where tau=(60/gamma^2)max{eta,n,exp(1),((eta+n)/eta)log((eta+n)/eta)}. The step eta can be any fixed positive real number. The all-time first estimate concerns the average loss; the second is a last-iterate estimate after the displayed stable-phase condition.
Finite nonempty binary-labeled data with Euclidean feature norms <=1
Unit separating vector w_star and margin gamma>0
Averaged logistic risk and full-batch constant-step gradient descent
Zero initialization
Integer time indices; stable last-iterate denominator uses t>s

Let P be a probability measure on a measurable space X, and W:X x X->[0,cmax] a measurable symmetric kernel, where 0<cmin<=d_P(x)=integral W(x,y)dP(y) and cmax>=cmin. Define L_P g(x)=integral W(x,y)g(y)/sqrt(d_P(x)d_P(y)) dP(y). For vector functions g=(g_i), write ||g||_2=(sum_i ||g_i||_(L2(P))^2)^(1/2) and ||g||_infty=(sum_i ||g_i||_sup^2)^(1/2), where sup is over X. Let f^(0)=f have finite indicated norm. For layers s=0,...,M-1 define f_j^(s+1)=sigma(sum_i h_ij^(s)(L_P) f_i^(s)+b_j^(s)), where b^(s) is a constant finite-dimensional vector, h_ij^(s)(z)=sum_{k>=0} beta_ijk^(s) z^k and |sigma(u)|<=|u|, |sigma(u)-sigma(v)|<=|u-v|. Set B_k^(s)=(beta_ijk^(s))_(j,i), H_2^(s)=sum_k ||B_k^(s)|| and H_infty^(s)=sum_k ||(|beta_ijk^(s)|)_(j,i)|| (2cmax/cmin)^k. Assume the H_* sums used are finite; polynomial filters are allowed. Then for every ell<=M and either *=2 or *=infty, ||f^(ell)||_* <= ||f||_* product_{s=0}^{ell-1} H_*^(s) + sum_{s=0}^{ell-1} ||b^(s)||_2 product_{p=s+1}^{ell-1} H_*^(p), with empty product equal to one. In the infinity norm the order of channel summation and supremum is part of the definition; it is not replaced by sup_x ||g(x)||_2. No Lipschitz partition assumption on W is needed for this norm estimate.

finite layer widths; constant finite biases; finite H_* coefficient sums
activation is 1-Lipschitz and obeys |sigma(u)|<=|u|, hence sigma(0)=0

Put N=w(tau+b-b psi w), K=gamma b(1-psi w)-N, L=b(1-w)(1-psi w)-tau w, D=bw(1-psi w), U=(KL)prime D-KL Dprime, V=Nprime K-N Kprime. [Lemma 38 of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] Fix $I\subseteq[d]$ and $A\subseteq I$.
Let $t$ be a stopping time such that $X_t[A]\sim \pi_{|A|}$ and $X_t[A]$ is independent of
\(
(S_t,U_t,S_{t+1},U_{t+1},\dots).
\)
On the event $E_t(A)$, set $i=N_t(A)$ and $A'=A\cup\{i\}$.
Then $X_{t+1}[A']\sim \pi_{|A'|}$ and $X_{t+1}[A']$ is independent of $(S_{t+1},U_{t+1},S_{t+2},U_{t+2},\dots)$.

Let L be a finite lattice with Moebius function mu. If a > 0, then for every b in L, sum over x with x v a = b of mu(0, x) = 0. Dually, if a < 1, then for every b, sum over x with x ^ a = b of mu(x, 1) = 0. In the Boolean lattice this is the vanishing of the alternating sum over the subsets X of B with X union A = B (A nonempty).

[Lemma lem:Idot_well_def_and_rep of arXiv:2605.15401, 'Noise Tradeoffs, Stationary Information Flow, and Structural Balance in Unit-Birth Network'] Fix $i \in \{1,\dots, N\}$.
For the unit-birth model with generator (equation eq:generator of the paper), suppose
Assumption~(ass:standing of the paper) holds. Then the series defining
$(\dot I)_{X_i}$ in (equation eq:Idot_clean_def of the paper) is absolutely convergent.

More precisely, writing
\[
(\dot I)_{X_i}
=
\sum_{n\ge0}\sum_v
\left(
\pi(n,v)f_i(v)-\pi(n+1,v)\frac{n+1}{\tau_i}
\right)
\big(h_i(n,v)-h_i(n+1,v)\big),
\]
each of the four nonnegative sums
\begin{align}

\sum_{n,v}\pi(n,v)f_i(v)\,h_i(n+1,v),
\qquad
\sum_{n,v}\pi(n,v)f_i(v)\,h_i(n,v),\\
\notag
\sum_{n,v}\pi(n+1,v)\frac{n+1}{\tau_i}\,h_i(n+1,v),
\qquad
\sum_{n,v}\pi(n+1,v)\frac{n+1}{\tau_i}\,h_i(n,v)
\end{align}
is finite. Consequently, $L_i h_i\in L^1(\pi)$ and
\begin{equation}
(\dot I)_{X_i}
=
-\mathbb{E}_\pi\big[(L_i h_i)(X)\big].
\end{equation}

body: Let X be a Banach space. X is reflexive if and only if every continuous linear functional f in X* attains its supremum on the closed unit ball of X, that is, there exists x in X with ||x|| <= 1 and f(x) = ||f||. If X is reflexive, attainment follows from weak compactness of the closed unit ball together with weak continuity of f; the converse, that attainment for every functional forces reflexivity, is the deep part of the theorem. [James (1964, 1972); see Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis]
title: James's Theorem (Reflexivity via Attainment of the Norm)

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2506.15159, 'Conditional central limit theorems for exponential random graphs'] (\cite[Theorem~3.7]{rollin2015})
    Let $(X, X^{\prime}, X^{\prime\prime})$ be three consecutive steps of a reversible Markov chain in equilibrium. Let $M: = M(X)$, $M^{\prime} := M(X^{\prime})$, and $M^{\prime\prime} := M(X^{\prime\prime})$ take
values on the integers $\mathbb{Z}$. Define
\begin{align*}
    &Q_{1}(x)=\mathbb{P}\left(M^{\prime}=M+1 \left.\right| X=x\right),\quad q_{1}=\IE Q_{1}(X)=\mathbb{P}(M^{\prime}=M+1),\\
    &Q_{1, 1}(x)=\mathbb{P}\left(M^{\prime}=M+1, M^{\prime \prime}=M^{\prime}+1\left.\right| X=x\right).
\end{align*}
Define $Q_{-1}(x)$ and $Q_{-1,-1}(x)$ similarly by changing all the $+1$ to $-1$.
Then, we have 
    \begin{align*}
       D(X) \leq &\frac{1}{q_{1}^{2}} \Big[2 \operatorname{Var} Q_{1}(X)+\IE\left|Q_{1, 1}(X)-Q_{1}(X)^{2}\right|\\
        &+2 \operatorname{Var} Q_{-1}(X)+\IE\left|Q_{-1,-1}(X)-Q_{-1}(X)^{2}\right|\Big].
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2506.15159

body:
[Theorem 1.2 (McDiarmid’s inequality [18]) of arXiv:2110.05374, 'When Janson meets McDiarmid: Bounded difference inequalities under graph-dependence'] Let f : Ω → R be c-Lipschitz and let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) be a vector of independent random variables taking values in Ω. Then for every t > 0, P(f(X) − E[f(X)] ≥ t) ≤ exp(−2t²/‖c‖₂²). This is McDiarmid's bounded differences inequality (C. McDiarmid, On the method of bounded differences, Surveys in Combinatorics 1989, pp. 148-188; reference [18] of the paper), which arXiv:2110.05374 restates as its starting point; it is not a result of that paper.
c-Lipschitz (Definition 1.1 of the paper): Ω = Ω_1 × ... × Ω_n is a product of Polish spaces, c = (c_1, ..., c_n) ∈ R_+^n, and f : Ω → R is c-Lipschitz when |f(x) − f(x')| ≤ Σ_{i=1}^n c_i 1{x_i ≠ x'_i} for all x, x' ∈ Ω (Lipschitz for the c-weighted Hamming distance).

Let mu be a probability measure on R^n satisfying a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant C, that is Ent_mu(f^2) <= 2 C E_mu[|grad f|^2] for all locally Lipschitz f. Then for every 1-Lipschitz F with E_mu[F] finite and every real lambda, E_mu[ exp( lambda (F - E F) ) ] <= exp( C lambda^2 / 2 ), and consequently mu( F - E F >= t ) <= exp( - t^2 / (2C) ) for every t > 0, with the same bound for the lower tail. For the standard Gaussian, C = 1 by the Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality, giving the sharp Gaussian concentration bound exp(-t^2/2) for 1-Lipschitz functions. The argument converts a functional inequality into an exponential moment bound and is the reason log-Sobolev, rather than Poincare, is the inequality one wants: Poincare alone yields only exponential, not Gaussian, tails. The hypothesis is a Lipschitz bound on F with respect to the EUCLIDEAN metric; changing the metric changes the effective constant. [Herbst, unpublished; see Ledoux, The Concentration of Measure Phenomenon, Chapter 5]
mu satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant C
F is 1-Lipschitz with respect to the Euclidean metric
E_mu[F] finite

For every \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\sfT>0\), there exist

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Reduce to the scaling limit of the IIC itself (C0077) plus a homogenisation of the walk on the limit tree. Result: If the IIC converges (as a measure-valued process indexed by intrinsic distance) to incipient infinite super-Brownian motion, then the walk on the IIC should converge to the Brownian motion on the associated continuum random tree embedded in R^d, time-changed by the IIC volume measure, i.e. to the 'Brownian motion on the ISE-type tree' with spatial displacement given by the embedding (the Ben Arous-Cabezas-Fribergh limit). The walk on the discrete tree structure of the IIC is a random walk on a graph that is tree-like at all scales in d > 6 (the number of cycles at scale r is bounded), so the spatial position is a Brownian motion time-changed by the intrinsic clock; the intrinsic clock converges by the tree scaling limit; the embedding of the tree in R^d is a branching random walk-type embedding whose limit is the ISE embedding. Each step is known for the branching random walk trace (BCF 2016) and the difficulty for the IIC is the dependence between the tree structure and the embedding (loops, self-intersections). The rigorous reduction: the walk's scaling limit follows from (i) the IIC tree scaling limit with its embedding, (ii) a resistance estimate showing the effective resistance across the IIC at intrinsic distance r is of order r (tree-like), which is known up to constants from Kozma-Nachmias-type estimates. So the problem is subsumed by C0077 plus a resistance-form convergence theorem (Croydon's framework), which needs the convergence of the IIC as a resistance metric space, a stronger statement than the measure-valued convergence in the source. Obstruction: Resistance-metric convergence of the IIC in d > 6 is not established.

Let $\bm{\mathcal{Y}} = \{\bm{Y}_\alpha\}_{\alpha \in \mathcal{I}}$ be a family of random variables indexed by finite ordered tuples of positive integers. For each $\alpha = (i_1, \dots, i_k)$, let $\operatorname{supp}(\alpha) = \{i_1, \dots, i_k\} \subset \mathbb{N}$ denote the set of indices involved. The family $\bm{\mathcal{Y}}$ is called dissociated (or jointly dissociated) if for any two disjoint index sets $I, J \subset \mathbb{N}$ (with $I \cap J = \emptyset$), the sub-collection $\bm{\mathcal{Y}}_I := \{\bm{Y}_\alpha : \operatorname{supp}(\alpha) \subseteq I\}$ is independent of $\bm{\mathcal{Y}}_J := \{\bm{Y}_\alpha : \operatorname{supp}(\alpha) \subseteq J\}$.
\mathcal{I} is a family of finite integer tuples
I \cap J = \emptyset
title: Dissociated Family of Random Variables

body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): With m batches, choosing one pivot p_s per witness pair and replacing Q_{p_s} by the sign-valued witness Y_s, the pivot matrix is triangular modulo B with nonzero diagonal, so (W, Y_1,...,Y_m, Q_j for j not a pivot) (tag 18) is an admissible sign basis. For each fixed boundary value it is an invertible change of private coordinates, hence preserves H(Q|W) and L. From sum c_s <= L and c_s >= beta, m <= L/beta (19). Keeping old selectors and adding the exchange discrepancies e_s = Q_{p_s} - Y_s (20) gives exchanged-basis quotient residual rank <= (2kappa+1)L + m <= (2kappa+1+beta^{-1})L (21). Notes: beta^{-1} = 1/log_2(4/3) = 2.40942 - the same constant as the NAE three-circuit floor, appearing here as the price of the exchange. The invariance of L under the exchange is what makes the charge additive rather than multiplicative.

body: [campaign status: partial_result - author-checked, unrefereed] Bradley, Basic properties of strong mixing conditions: a survey and some open questions (arXiv:math/0511078), Question 7 (Section 4.2, p. 19) asks: given an arbitrary nonincreasing sequence (b_1, b_2, ...) in [0,1], is there a strictly stationary sequence X with phi(n) = b_n for all n >= 1? Our result (id D0035, 2026-09-08): NO, refuted in one line from a result Bradley himself quotes - if phi(n) < 1/2 for some n >= 1 then X is phi-mixing, i.e. phi(n) tends to 0. The constant sequence b_n = 1/4 is nonincreasing and lies in [0,1] and gives phi(1) = 1/4 < 1/2, which forces phi(n) to tend to 0 and contradicts phi(n) = 1/4 for every n; the same argument rules out every sequence that dips below 1/2 without tending to zero. Verification as the source words it: this one came from the intake agent rather than from the author, and was verified by pulling the archived source, reading Question 7 at the stated locator word for word, and locating the quoted dichotomy in the survey. Honest scope, in the memo's own words: the literal general form is refuted from the survey's own material, not that a question its author believed open has been settled. Status: proof (unaudited), owner campaign claim T410-w739-C001 version 2; independent review pending. Assume a deterministic polynomial-time one-way function family secure against every polynomial-size nonuniform randomized circuit family. There is a uniformly polynomial-time weighted binary law P_L for every L, even with efficiently computable normalized probabilities and an efficient sampler, such that for every polynomial-size AR family with polynomial-bit parameters and polynomial-time absolute-precision next-bit evaluation, and every a>0, KL(P_L||Q_L)>a log L eventually. In particular the inverse-polynomial gap in Target 1 holds under this explicit circuit-secure OWF formulation. The law uses the fixed token order padded function output, uniform preimage, zero padding. The information-theoretic reduction gives ideal inversion success at least exp(-KL); rounding the n suffix kernels at precision t loses at most n*2^(1-t). This is not a proof that worst-case NP hardness alone is insufficient, and no novelty priority is asserted.
Nonuniform-secure OWF; ordinary uniform-only OWF security is not silently upgraded
Fixed output-before-preimage left-to-right binary token order
Polynomial-time next-bit probability computation to absolute precision 2^-t in poly(L,t) time
Polynomial circuit size and polynomial bit-length parameters; eventual threshold may depend on the model family

DRAFT scoped boundary result; written proof independently checked by w476, served-model diversity gate pending. For each 0<gamma<3, take a stationary unit-variance Gaussian field G on Z^3 with covariance R_gamma(z)=(1+|z|^2)^(-gamma/2), and set sigma_x=sign(G_x). The bounded spin field is stationary, spin-flip symmetric, positively associated, has two-point covariance (2/pi)arcsin R_gamma(z) asymptotic to (2/pi)|z|^(-gamma), and has on-site fourth cumulant -2. Yet for each finite list of compactly supported smooth tests f, the normalized sums N^(-3+gamma/2) sum_x f(x/N)sigma_x converge jointly to a centered Gaussian vector with covariance (2/pi) double_integral f(u)h(v)|u-v|^(-gamma) du dv. This refutes only a proposed implication from association, anomalous two-point decay and a local fourth cumulant to non-Gaussian smeared limits. The field is not shown to be a nearest-neighbor Ising Gibbs state or to satisfy random-current identities.

body:
[Proposition 21 (Partial proof of Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:red}) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] In the saturated regime of Definition~\ref{def:saturated}:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Single-cell correctness.) For an isolated parent--child pair the transmission probability equals \eqref{eq:wald} exactly. The error from treating the pair as isolated, when embedded in a tree, is $O(\varepsilon(\delta))$ per edge: the only neighbours that could perturb $v$'s drift before it crosses are siblings of $v$, which are absent on a tree (each $v$ has a unique parent), and the grandparent, whose influence is screened by the saturated parent.
\item (Back-reaction does not couple siblings.) The back-reaction $v\to u$ adds $+\gamma$ to the already-failed parent's drift; since $u\in B_{\mathrm{fail}}$ has $\sigma(s^{(u)}-\theta_{uw})\ge1-\varepsilon(\delta)$ for every child $w$, the extra forcing changes each child's forcing by at most $\gamma\,\sigma'(\cdot)\le\gamma\,\varepsilon(\delta)$. Hence $\Cov(\chi_{uv},\chi_{uw})=O(\varepsilon(\delta))$, vanishing as $\delta\to\infty$.
\item (Short cycles vanish.) On $G_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BS}}T$ the probability that a fixed vertex has two distinct failed neighbours through a cycle of length $\le L$ is $O(c_L(G_n))$, the density of length-$\le L$ cycles through a uniform root, which $\to0$ for every fixed $L$ by local weak convergence to a tree.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the per-edge marginal and the sibling-independence parts (Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:red}(i)--(ii) within a single generation, and (iii)) hold up to $O(\varepsilon(\delta)+\eta_n)$.

For f in L^2 of the circle, the partial sums of its Fourier series converge to f in the L^2 norm, and Parseval's identity holds: the sum of |c_k|^2 over all integers k equals the L^2 norm squared of f (with the standard normalization). The exponentials e^{ikx} form an orthonormal basis of L^2 of the circle.

Let N take values in {0, 1, ..., m} and F_r = E[binom(N, r)] for r = 0, ..., m (F_0 = 1). Then for k = 0, ..., m, P(N = k) = sum_{r=k}^m (-1)^(r - k) binom(r, k) F_r, and for k = 1, ..., m, P(N >= k) = sum_{r=k}^m (-1)^(r - k) binom(r - 1, k - 1) F_r. For the number of events that occur, F_r = S_r, the r-th intersection sum, so the probability that exactly k (or at least k) of the events occur is determined by S_k, ..., S_m.
N takes values in {0, ..., m}

open hemisphere.  Let $\kappa_1,\kappa_2\geq0$ be the principal curvatures of
$\partial U$ with respect to the outward unit conormal, let $\mathrm dA$
denote its area measure, and put $H_{\mathbb{S}^3}=\kappa_1+\kappa_2$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 |U|+\frac12\int_{\partial U}H_{\mathbb{S}^3}\,\mathrm dA\leq\frac{|\mathbb{S}^3|}{2}.
\end{equation}

 \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow Z_h.
\end{equation}
It intertwines the preceding central automorphisms with
\[
 \vartheta_h(H_j)=-H_{n+1-j},\qquad
 \delta_{c,h}(H_j)=H_j+c,
\]
and their values on $E_i,F_i$ from
\eqref{eq:vartheta-definition}--\eqref{eq:delta-definition}:
\begin{equation}
 \iota_h^{\cZ}\circ\vartheta
 =\vartheta_h\circ\iota_h^{\cZ},
 \qquad
 \iota_h^{\cZ}\circ\delta_c
 =\delta_{c,h}\circ\iota_h^{\cZ}.
\end{equation}
title: Faithful $h$-adic realization

Let n(lambda)>=1 be polynomially bounded and polynomial-time computable, h=32*n, T=ceil(h/p)+2, and let q>=2 be an efficiently samplable power of two of polynomial size. There is an efficient language model over q nonterminal symbols and END, with a uniform h-token prefix followed by a fixed legal deterministic suffix and total output length T, for which no sound, undetectable watermark can satisfy the literal full-text experiment of Golowich-Moitra Definition2.6 for all p-edit-bounded channels at threshold beta(ell)=8*n+6*alpha*ell (or its ceiling). Specifically, a word-only PPT channel deleting the first min(h,floor(p*|w|)) symbols is p-edit-bounded on every input. If eps_und bounds the support-test distinguishing advantage and eps_sound bounds soundness on the fixed surviving suffix, the probability of a high-entropy interval together with failed detection after this channel is at least1-eps_und-eps_sound. OWNER RESULT DRAFT: proof (unaudited), T336-w727-C013 v1; no novelty claim. Let d>=1,n>=0 be integers, ell,s,eps>0 and B>=0. A zero-mean GP on [0,1]^d has kernel k(x,z)=exp(-||x-z||^2/(2ell^2)), independent Gaussian observation noise variance s, and an exogenous design. Context length<=n and |y_i|<=B. Put b_mu=sqrt(s eps), b_v=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)), C_mu=nB/s+n^2 B/s^2, C_v=1+2n/s+n^2/s^2, tau=min(1/2,b_mu/(3(1+C_mu)),b_v/(3C_v)), a=d/ell^2, t=ceil(max(1,2e a,log(1/tau)/log(2))) and p=binomial(d+t-1,d), with e Euler's number. Use the known Gaussian Taylor feature projection onto degrees<t, which has dimension p, norm<=1 and PSD omitted diagonal-tail<=tau. Its coordinate Lipschitz constant with respect to L1 distance is K=1/ell. Set E_mu=nB(3/s+6n/s^2), E_v=3+12n/s, rho=min(1,b_mu/(3(1+E_mu)),b_v/(3E_v)), g=max(1,ceil(K d sqrt(p)/rho)) and J=(g+1)^d. The finite-grid cone encoder from accepted C004 computes approximating features from raw x, using the exact minimum of phi_j(u)+K||x-u||_1 over grid u in {0,1/g,...,1}^d; fixed grid feature samples are weights. Put eps0=min(eps/9,1/36), kappa=1+4max(1,n)/s, M=4nB/s, delta0=min(1/2,s/8,sqrt(s eps0)/(1+M),s sqrt(eps0)/4), T=ceil(sqrt(kappa)log(2/delta0)/2), D=7p+6+d+Jd+pJ, H=2Jd+pJ+4p+1 and L=T+5+ceil(log_2 J). Composing this encoder with accepted C002 gives a residual N-normalized ReLU-attention transformer with tokenwise residual ReLU MLPs, N=n+1 tokens, width D, MLP hidden width<=H, L layers, <=5 heads and <=L(15D^2+2DH)+2D dense parameters. It takes only raw coordinates, observed labels, two role flags and constants, and outputs N(muhat,vhat), vhat>=s, with KL(N(mu,v)||N(muhat,vhat))<=eps uniformly for the ORIGINAL RBF noisy-query posterior. All nonlinear feature approximation is included; fixed affine input placement is excluded as in C004. Each of truncation, encoding and solver gets one third of the scalar mean/variance budgets; the final KL argument allows signed variance error. This composition uses C002/C004 as independently accepted ground and the unaudited C011/C012 elementary tail/perturbation lemmas; it does NOT require C010's pending Newton construction. Arbitrary fixed real weights are allowed. No raw feature oracle, finite-bit, training, softmax, layernorm, causal-mask or adaptive-design guarantee is asserted.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:50ba0470b7ac1b2acd9eb45c23ea7f0fddd957d3970798fcdbd5430049d10d44","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/50/50ba0470b7ac1b2acd9eb45c23ea7f0fddd957d3970798fcdbd5430049d10d44.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b29fb87d98383eb3fea4b68e32b7cdd8a7f3a69b5c04aacefd6ba54f4ff7ea64","bundle_entry_key":"t336-w727-c013","bundle_id":"population.w727-t336-raw-rbf-encoder-chebyshev-008","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian processes; raw-input transformer approximation; kernel truncation","draft":"w727/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.transformers:draft-raw-input-gaussian-rbf-predictive-kl-grid-encoder-chebyshev","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C013 v1: fully counted raw-input RBF predictor on the cube

Kind: bound. Target: none (reviewer-authorized RBF continuation).
Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim. This extends the saved
supplied-feature result to raw coordinates. It uses the independently
accepted C002 v1 solver and C004 v1 encoder, not the pending Newton
construction C010. The Taylor kernel approximation is known prior art.

## 1. Theorem and all resource parameters

Fix integers d>=1,n>=0 and real ell,s,eps>0 and B>=0. On X=[0,1]^d take
the zero-mean Gaussian process with kernel

    k(x,z)=exp(-||x-z||_2^2/(2 ell^2)).

The observation noises are independent N(0,s). Designs are exogenous;
the statement is pointwise over every design of at most n context points,
every query in X, and context labels bounded by B in absolute value.
The predicted distribution is that of a NEW NOISY observation, not the
noiseless latent value. Define

    b_mu=sqrt(s eps), b_v=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)),
    C_mu=nB/s+n^2 B/s^2, C_v=1+2n/s+n^2/s^2,
    tau=min(1/2,b_mu/(3(1+C_mu)),b_v/(3 C_v)),
    a=d/ell^2,
    t=ceil(max(1,2 e a,log(1/tau)/log(2))),
    p=binomial(d+t-1,d).

Here e in the expression 2 e a denotes Euler's number. Below rho denotes
the encoder tolerance, so no constant is reused for two meanings.
For the feature encoder and its perturbation budget define

    K=1/ell, R=1, S=2,
    E_mu=nB(3/s+6n/s^2), E_v=3+12n/s,
    rho=min(1,b_mu/(3(1+E_mu)),b_v/(3 E_v)),
    g=max(1,ceil(K d sqrt(p)/rho)), J=(g+1)^d.

For the Chebyshev solver put

    eps0=min(eps/9,1/36),
    kappa=1+4 max(1,n)/s, M=4nB/s,
    delta0=min(1/2,s/8,sqrt(s eps0)/(1+M),s sqrt(eps0)/4),
    T=ceil(sqrt(kappa) log(2/delta0)/2).

There is a residual transformer with normalized ReLU attention and
tokenwise residual ReLU MLPs, taking ONLY raw coordinates, observed
labels, context/query flags and fixed constants, with

    N=n+1 tokens (n padded context slots and one query),
    D=7p+6+d+Jd+pJ token width,
    H=2Jd+pJ+4p+1 as an upper bound on MLP hidden width,
    L=T+5+ceil(log_2 J) total layers, at most five heads per layer,
    at most L(15D^2+2DH)+2D dense attention/MLP/readout parameters,

whose two outputs define N(muhat,vhat), vhat>=s, satisfying

    KL(N(mu,v) || N(muhat,vhat)) <= eps

uniformly for the ORIGINAL RBF noisy-query posterior and all contexts
above. Fixed affine input placement is excluded as in C004; ALL nonlinear
feature approximation is included in these layer and parameter counts.
Weights are arbitrary fixed reals depending on the prior and displayed
bounds, never on the current context. No finite-bit, training, softmax,
layernorm, causal-attention or adaptive-design guarantee is asserted.

## 2. Known Taylor projection supplies the uniform PSD tail

Use the p coordinates indexed by multi-indices alpha in N^d, |alpha|<t:

    phi_alpha(x)=exp(-||x||^2/(2ell^2))
                product_j(x_j/ell)^(alpha_j)/sqrt(product_j alpha_j!).

This is the collected-monomial version of Cotter, Keshet and Srebro,
Explicit Approximations of the Gaussian Kernel, arXiv:1109.4603v1,
Section 3, PDF pp.4-5, equations (6)-(11) and the following dimension
count. This known projection certificate is recorded in C012 Section 3;
only its feature-tail lemma is used, not C012's Newton corollary.

Write Phi for the full countable feature sequence and phi for its
degree<t coordinate projection. Its inner product is k and ||Phi(x)||=1.
Thus k_p=<phi,phi> is PSD, ||phi||<=1, and k-k_p is PSD on joint sets.
For ||x||^2/ell^2<=a its omitted diagonal is bounded by

    0<=k(x,x)-k_p(x,x)<=a^t/t!<=(e a/t)^t<=2^(-t)<=tau.

The factorial bound and feature count are the known Taylor argument,
not a new kernel-approximation theorem. In particular the conclusion is
a uniform PSD diagonal-tail certificate, not an integrated tail estimate.

## 3. The truncated feature map is Lipschitz independently of p

For any x,z in the cube, the full Hilbert feature map satisfies

    ||Phi(x)-Phi(z)||^2=2(1-k(x,z))
      =2(1-exp(-||x-z||^2/(2ell^2)))<=||x-z||^2/ell^2.

The last inequality is 1-exp(-u)<=u for u>=0. Orthogonal coordinate
projection cannot increase a Hilbert norm. Hence

    ||phi(x)-phi(z)||<=||x-z||_2/ell.

In particular every coordinate obeys
|phi_j(x)-phi_j(z)|<=K||x-z||_1 with K=1/ell, exactly the coordinate
Lipschitz hypothesis of the accepted C004 encoder. The constant does
not grow with the truncation degree or dimension p of the feature vector.

## 4. Apply the accepted grid encoder, counting its entire computation

Take G={0,1/g,...,1}^d and define the actual encoded feature coordinates

    psi_j(x)=min_{u in G}(phi_j(u)+K||x-u||_1).

C004 Sections 3-4 give both the exact residual-ReLU implementation of
this finite minimum and

    sup_x ||psi(x)-phi(x)||<=sqrt(p) Kd/g<=rho,
    ||psi(x)||<=1+rho<=2.

All phi_j(u) are finitely many constants in the network's weights.
They are not features supplied in the input and not a context-dependent
computation. C004 uses two absolute-value/cone layers, ceil(log_2 J)
minimum layers and one feature-gating layer: E=3+ceil(log_2 J).
Its context/query flags populate the solver's feature registers and set
padding contributions to zero. Its widths are precisely D and H in
Section 1. This instantiates the accepted encoder construction with
grid resolution g and tolerance rho; it does not re-audit its matrices.

Let (mu_p,v_p) be the exact noisy posterior for k_p and (mu_psi,v_psi)
the exact posterior for <psi,psi>. C004 Section 2 applies with
R=1,S=2,C_A=3n and feature error <=rho<=1. Its constants specialize to

    C_m=nB[(1+2)/s+2(3n)/s^2]=E_mu,
    C_v=1+2+2^2(3n)/s=E_v.

Therefore |mu_p-mu_psi|<=E_mu rho<=b_mu/3 and
|v_p-v_psi|<=E_v rho<=b_v/3. These are componentwise posterior bounds;
the encoded kernel need not be ordered below the RBF kernel.

## 5. Kernel truncation and solver error use the other two thirds

C011 Sections 1-2 give the absolute kernel-posterior perturbation bounds
for the PSD tail in Section 2:

    |mu-mu_p|<=C_mu tau<=b_mu/3,
    |v-v_p|<=C_v tau<=b_v/3.

For clarity, that lemma uses context covariance norm error <=n tau,
query cross-covariance vector error <=sqrt(n)tau, both context inverse
norms <=1/s, and the resolvent error <=n tau/s^2. It is independent of
C010 and uses no independence between the fixed label coordinates.
All exact noisy posterior variances here are >=s. The mean bounds also
cover n=0 and B=0, when their coefficients vanish.

Apply the independently accepted C002 Chebyshev solver to psi, whose
feature norm is <=S=2, with tolerance eps0. Its feature registers are
embedded in the larger width D as in C004; extra registers are preserved.
The kappa, M, delta0 and T in Section 1 are C002's constants for this
application. It costs T+2 attention layers, at most five heads, with
identity MLPs, and supplies

    vhat>=s,
    |mu_psi-muhat|<=sqrt(s eps0)<=b_mu/3,
    |v_psi-vhat|<=s sqrt(eps0)<=b_v/3.

The last inequality uses BOTH eps0<=eps/9 and eps0<=1/36:
s sqrt(eps0)<=min(s sqrt(eps)/3,s/6)=b_v/3.
Add the three scalar error budgets to obtain

    |mu-muhat|<=b_mu,
    |v-vhat|<=b_v<=s/2.

No triangle inequality for KL is invoked. Since vhat>=s, h=(v-vhat)/vhat
lies in [-1/2,1/2]. The accepted C002 Gaussian scalar inequality gives

    KL= (h-log(1+h))/2+(mu-muhat)^2/(2vhat)
      <=(v-vhat)^2/(2s^2)+(mu-muhat)^2/(2s)<=eps.

This allows either sign of the combined variance error, including the
possibility that the encoder or solver overestimates the exact variance.

## 6. Resource count and review boundary

The encoder costs 3+ceil(log_2 J) layers and the solver T+2, yielding L
in Section 1. The encoder attention is identity, and the solver MLPs
are identity; counting five full D-by-D Q/K/V triples and two D-by-H/H-by-D
MLP matrices at EVERY layer is therefore a valid dense upper bound.
The two-coordinate readout contributes 2D parameters. No p anchor tokens
from C010 are needed: N remains n+1 throughout.

This is a fully counted raw-input RBF theorem candidate on the cube,

body:
[Lem 43 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall the function $V_\gamma(\by)$ from \eqref{e:def-V-gamma-y}.
For any $\gamma \ge 0$, any local maximizer of $V_\gamma(\by)$ on the sphere $\{\|\by\|^2=N\}$ is of the form
    \beq
        
        \by =\dbA_\beta\Big(\gamma^{1/2}\dbg+\dbX\by\Big)\,,
    \eeq
    where we recall $\dbA_\beta \equiv (\beta \bI_N - \dbD)^{-1}$. Furthermore, for any such $\by$ we must have $\beta \ge \hw_1$.
\begin{proof}
We apply the method of Lagrange multipliers with the Lagrangian $\Lagr(\by;\beta)$ as defined in \eqref{e:fp-y-lagrangian}. Note that the Lagrangian Hessian (with respect to $\by$) is given by
    \[
        \nabla^2 \Lagr(\by;\beta)
        = -\frac{2}{N} \Big(
            \beta \bI_N - \dbD - \dbX
        \Big)\,.
    \]
At any local maximum, this Hessian must be negative semi-definite. Recall the definitions of $\dbD$ and $\dbX$ from \eqref{e:fp.dbD} and \eqref{e:fp.dbX} respectively. Since $|B_1|\ge\iota N$ by the assumption $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, we can find a non-zero vector $\bv$ that is zero outside the coordinates of $B_1$, and is additionally orthogonal to each of the vectors $\tbmeta^j$ ($1\le j\le r'$) in the definition \eqref{e:fp.dbX} of $\dbX$. It follows that
    \[
    0 \le \bv^\st \Big(\beta -\dbD-\dbX \Big)\bv
    =\bv^\st \Big(\beta -\dbD \Big)\bv
    =(\beta-\hw_1)\|\bv\|^2\,,
    \]
so we conclude $\beta\ge\hw_1$. 
For any local maximizer $\by$ satisfying $\|\by\|^2=N$, stationarity of $\Lagr$ at $\by$ yields the expression~\eqref{e:fp-g-prep2-stationarity}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 43 of arXiv:2608.29416

Let (X_k)_{k=1}^n be a matrix martingale difference sequence adapted to a filtration (F_k), where each X_k is a d x d Hermitian matrix such that E[X_k | F_{k-1}] = 0 and X_k^2 <= C_k^2 almost surely for fixed positive-semidefinite matrices C_k. Let sigma^2 = || sum_{k=1}^n C_k^2 ||. Then for all t >= 0, P( || sum_{k=1}^n X_k || >= t ) <= 2 * d * exp( - t^2 / (8 * sigma^2) ).
(X_k) is a matrix martingale difference sequence
X_k^2 <= C_k^2 almost surely

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited); independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2 and 1<=r<K be integers. There are N contexts with K candidates each, d disjoint pairs with exactly one arbitrary A context and one systematic S context per pair, and N-2d known S contexts. All K candidates are true in S; each A has an independent uniform random r-subset of truths. A world fixes pair orientations and subsets. Its factual law p chooses contexts uniformly then a true candidate uniformly. The orientation class has VC dimension d. Training supplies n iid uniform context indices and exact A/S tags, with no candidate identities. For a partition Pi, p_Pi is uniform within each cell with that cell total p mass, and Mis_Pi(g,p)=TV(p_Pi,g) with TV half the l1 distance. Output bins depend on g alone. Competing generators g are arbitrary laws on the NK candidates. Feasibility means Mis<=c for every world compatible with the observed information; the objective is worst-world false-output mass. After training a perfect verifier discloses the orientation and all r true candidates in the A member of each of k predetermined pairs, 0<=k<=d, selected independently of tags and worlds. It covers fraction k/d of arbitrary truths by both count and factual mass. U counts the other d-k pairs untouched by training. Set kappa=1-r/K, beta=r/K, a1=(d-k)/N and m=U/N. For exact probability-level calibration Mis_infinity, the exact conditional frontier is V_k=kappa*max(a1-c,(a1+m-c)/2,0), c in [0,1]. The known-unverified-partition oracle, with the same verifier facts, is kappa*(a1-c)_+. Exact expected minimax excess is kappa/(2N)*E[(U-|d-k-Nc|)_+], where E[z^U]=sum_{j=0}^{d-k} binom(d-k,j)*(z-1)^j*(1-2j/N)^n. At c=a1 it equals kappa*(d-k)/(2N)*(1-2/N)^n. At c=d/N it equals kappa/(2N)*E[(U-k)_+]. A polynomial-representation version-space generator attains this worldwise. The same conditional value holds with the stated uniform posterior averages. The lower bound covers arbitrary coarsenings of score levels, but the matching upper bound is claimed only for infinity. No ordinary factual-training or weaker/noisy/adaptive verifier is covered.
