[Question of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] \begin{enumerate}
\item A $d-$dimensional domino is a $ d$-dimensional box whose one side has length $2$ and all other sides have length 1 with its vertices in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. Does there exist a strongly irreducible subshift contained in the space of domino tilings of $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d\geq 3$?
    \item In general, is there a natural characterization of the set of boxes $\mathcal{R}$ for which the space of tilings of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by the boxes in $\mathcal{R}$ contains a strongly irreducible subshift?
    
    We know that if the collection $ \mathcal{R}$ satisfies the condition of (thm:eventuallyuniversaltiles of the paper), then there exists a shift-invariant finitely dependent process on the tiling space $X(\mathcal{R})$. However, if $ p_1, p_2, \cdots, p_d$ are prime numbers and $ \mathcal{R} = \{ R_1, R_2, \cdots, R_d\}$ is a collection of bars where $ R_i$ is a bar whose sidelength in $ e_i$ direction is $ p_i$, then does $ X(\mathcal{R})$ contain a strongly irreducible subshift?
    \end{enumerate} (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Unnumbered question of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'

[Thm DRC of arXiv:2602.06011, 'Excursion decomposition of the XOR-Ising model'] Let $D$ be a Jordan domain and $D_\delta$ be as above. For the (critical) coupling $\mathbb P_\delta$, 
    \begin{equation}
        (h_\delta, \hat\mathbf{n}_\delta, \hat\mathbf{n}_\delta^\dagger, c_\delta, c_\delta^\dagger, \xi_\delta, \xi^\dagger_\delta) \overset{(d)}{\longrightarrow} (\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}\lambda}\ h, \hat\mathbf{n}, \hat\mathbf{n}^\dagger, c, c^\dagger, \xi, \xi^\dagger),
    \end{equation}
    where
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item h is a GFF with zero boundary conditions in $D$, 
        \item The inner boundaries of the boundary cluster of $\hat\mathbf{n}_\delta$ converge to $\mathcal L_{-\sqrt{2}\lambda, \sqrt{2}\lambda}$. The label $c(\ell)$ of an inner boundary $\ell$ is such that the boundary values of $h$ in $\mathcal O(\ell)$ are $c(\ell)\sqrt{2}\lambda$.
        \item The outer boundaries of the outermost clusters of $\hat\mathbf{n}^\dagger_\delta$ converge to $\mathcal L_{-2\lambda, 2\lambda}$. The sign $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)$ of an outer boundary $\gamma$ is such that the boundary values of $h$ in $\mathcal O(\gamma)$ are $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)2\lambda$. Moreover, the inner boundaries of the cluster corresponding to $\gamma$ converge to
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item [(iii.a)] $\mathcal L_{-2\lambda, (2\sqrt{2}-2)\lambda}$ if $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)=+1$,
            \item [(iii.b)] $\mathcal L_{-(2\sqrt{2}-2)\lambda, 2\lambda}$ if $\xi^\dagger(\gamma)=-1$,
            \item [(iii.c)] where the label $c^\dagger(\ell)$ of an inner boundary $\ell$ is such that the boundary values of $h$ in $\mathcal O(\ell)$ are $\xi(\gamma)(c(\ell)+1)\sqrt{2}\lambda$. 
        \end{enumerate}
        \item The structure repeats iteratively by applying the Markov property (MP-free of the paper) of Theorem (thm:master of the paper), which gives the nesting of two-valued sets described in Section (sec:decomp of the paper).
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm DRC of arXiv:2602.06011

[Theorem 6 (the inverse problem) of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] Let $0<p<1$. 
For every $\omega\in \S^{n-1}$, let $\chi\in C_0^\infty(\Omega)$ satisfy $\supp\chi\cap\overline{B(0,R)}=\emptyset$. Let $T>0$ be such that every point of $\overline{B(0,R)}$ lies on a ray $z+t\omega$, with $z\in\{\chi\ne0\}$ and $0<t<T$, and every such ray has exited $\overline{B(0,R)}$ by time $T$. Assume that $\Omega$ contains all the relevant incoming and outgoing ray segments up to time $T$. Then the family of corresponding solutions $u$ of \r{1b}, \r{IC1}, restricted to $[0,T]\times(\Omega\setminus B(0,R))$, for a fixed $\lambda$ in \r{lambda} and all $0<h\ll1$, uniquely determines $\sigma_{\mathfrak{m}}$ and the full jet $\{m_k(x)\}_{k\ge0}$ of $m(s,x)$ at $s=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: the inverse problem

body: Publication record. Open Problem 7.27 of D. Aldous and J. A. Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, is answered by Y. Shmalo, Arc-transitive graphs that mimic the cycle (September 2026): over arc-transitive graphs other than the cycles, the maximal mean commute time need not be O(n log n), the relaxation time need not be O(n), and the ratio of the maximal mean commute time to twice the average hitting time need not tend to one. The paper gives the hitting times, the average hitting time and the relaxation time of the blow-up H[K_r-bar] of any regular graph H (each vertex replaced by r independent copies) in terms of those of H, and shows that every arc-transitive graph is such a blow-up of a twin-free arc-transitive graph, so the question reduces to twin-free graphs. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/arc-transitive-graphs-that-mimic-the-cycle (commit 9e30e48c8cf7); ResearchGate record 414324957. Not refereed.
title: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 7.27 answered negatively: arc-transitive graphs need not behave like the cycle in commute, relaxation and hitting times (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/arc-transitive-graphs-that-mimic-the-cycle)

[Proposition prop:variance_explicit of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Consider the empirical density $\overline{\rho}_t(V)$ (Definition~(def:empirical_density of the paper))
and empirical current $\overline J_t(U)$ (Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper))
and let Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper) hold.
Then for all $t>0$,
\begin{align}
  \mathrm{Var}_\mu(\overline\rho_t)
    &\leq \frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(V)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}t},
  \\
  \mathrm{Var}_\mu(\overline J_t)
    &\leq \frac{1}{t}\left(2\E^\mu[Q]
      +\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}\right)
      \leq \frac{1}{t}\left(2\|Q\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}
      +\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}\right),
  
\end{align}
where $\lambda_\mathrm{gap}$ denotes the spectral gap~(equation eq:gap_variational of the paper) of $\mathcal{L}_S$
and $W=v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U$ and $Q=U\cdot DU$ as before.
The corresponding asymptotic variances, 
defined by $\sigma_{A,\infty}^2\equiv\lim_{t\to\infty}t\mathrm{Var}_\mu(\overline A_t)$,
are bounded by the same constants, i.e., 
\begin{align}
  \sigma_{\rho,\infty}^2\leq\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(V)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}},
	\quad\quad
  \sigma_{J,\infty}^2\leq 2\E^\mu[Q]+\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}
  \leq 2\|Q\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}+\frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}.
  
\end{align}
title: Finite-time variance upper bounds

[Proposition prop:conformal_rectangles_tight of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] We have the following convergences:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item The number $N^\kappa$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^\kappa_A$ converges in law to the number $N^4$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^4_A$ as $\kappa \uparrow 4$. More precisely, for all $\kappa_n \uparrow 4$ there exists an ordering of the crossings $\eta_1^n, \ldots, \eta^n_{N^{\kappa_n}}$ of $\Gamma^{\kappa_n}_A$ for which the random vectors $(N^{\kappa_n}, \eta^n_1, \ldots, \eta^n_{N^{\kappa_n}})$ converge in law to $(N^4, \eta_1, \ldots, \eta_{N^4})$, where $\eta_1, \ldots, \eta_{N^4}$ are the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^4_A$, for the topology of Hausdorff convergence.
		\item Jointly with the above convergence, the compact sets $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{out}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{in}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$ converge in distribution for the Hausdorff distance to $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{out}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{in}}_A} \mathrm{int}(\SCL)}$.
		\item In particular, the conformal rectangles whose left and right sides are given by the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^{\kappa_n}_A$ and whose top and bottom sides are respectively included in $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{out}}_A} \SCL}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{\kappa_n, \mathrm{in}}_A} \SCL}$ converge in distribution as $n \to \infty$ in the Carath\'eodory sense (jointly with their corners) to the conformal rectangles whose left and right sides are given by the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^{4}_A$ and whose top and bottom sides are respectively included in $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{out}}_A} \SCL}$ and $\overline{\bigcup_{\SCL \in \Gamma^{4, \mathrm{in}}_A} \SCL}$, and their moduli are tight in $(0,\infty)$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:conformal_rectangles_tight of arXiv:2609.04138

[Lemma Local model convergence of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Assume
\(\partial M\) uniformly of class \(C^{1,1}\), and let
\(x_{\varepsilon} \in M\) satisfy
\(\operatorname{dist}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\partial M \right)/\varepsilon \rightarrow a \in \lbrack 0,\infty\rbrack\).
For fixed \(R > 1\) let \(D_{\varepsilon}(R)\) be the
Dirichlet energy of the capacitary potential of
\(B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right)\) in
\(B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},R\varepsilon \right)\backslash\overline{B_{M}\left( x_{\varepsilon},\varepsilon \right)}\)
with the Neumann condition on \(\partial M\), and
\(E_{a}(\varepsilon;R)\) the energy of the corresponding model
condenser at radii \((\varepsilon,R\varepsilon)\) --- the free
Euclidean condenser when \(a = \infty\), the reflected half-space
condenser at height \(a\) when \(a < \infty\). Then
\(D_{\varepsilon}(R) = E_{a}(\varepsilon;R)\left( 1 + o(1) \right)\)
as \(\varepsilon \rightarrow 0\) with \(R\) fixed,
uniformly along the sequence.

[Corollary 28 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] Let $d$ be even and let $a\geq b\geq 0$ be integers such that $a+b=d$.  Define $t_{(a,b)}$	by
 	$$	t_{(a,b)} = 
 \begin{cases}
 	\left\lfloor\ds\frac{(a-b)}{4} \right\rfloor + 1 -\delta_{a,b}-\delta_{b,0} & \text{ if } a\equiv b \equiv 0 \text{ mod 2} \\ 
 	& \\ 
 	\left\lfloor\ds\frac{(a-b)}{4} \right\rfloor  -\delta_{b,0} & \text{ if } a\equiv b \equiv 1 \text{ mod 2} \\
 	& \\ 
 	0 & \text{ else.}
 \end{cases}	
 $$	
Then
		$$ 
		H^\ast(\mathsf{T}_\Gamma(n)_d)= \bigoplus_{\substack{ a\geq b \\ a+b=d }} \Sigma^{d+1}t_{(a,b)}\Phi[n,(a,b)^\ast]
		$$

[Thm general.bound.Delta of arXiv:2609.02588, 'Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games'] Let $H$ be a graph with at least one edge.
Let $c:V(H)\rightarrow [\chi(H)]$ be a proper vertex colouring,
and let $\Delta_c(H) = \max\{d_H(v):~v\in V(H),~ c(v)=1\}$.
Then 
$$
s^b_{MB}(H) \leq 
\begin{cases}
2\Delta_c(H) - 1 & ~~ \text{if }b=1 \\
b\Delta_c(H) (\ln(\Delta_c(H)) + 2) & ~~ \text{if }b \geq 2 . \\
\end{cases}
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Method: Limit of the optimal online random spanning-tree cost structural calculation Result: The Poisson dynamic-programming recursion has exact small-state solutions. For two current components of sizes x,y, F=(xy/2)*F^2 and the positive solution is2/(xy). For three singleton vertices each merged state has cost1, giving F=(3/2)*(F-1)^2. The admissible root exceeding the child cost is(4+sqrt7)/3; the other root is below1 and violates strict monotonicity. Check: The first recursion follows by integrating the accepted-offer surplus over weights below the continuation-cost difference. For n2 the Poisson cost is2 while the combinatorial model must buy its sole Uniform(0,1) edge and has cost1/2, demonstrating why finite-n model identification is invalid. Obstruction: The recursion depends on the entire component-size partition and on n. Standard coagulation hydrodynamic limits assume a prescribed kernel, whereas these acceptance kernels are themselves defined by unknown value functions. A compactness and uniqueness argument for their joint limit is missing.

Under the hypotheses of the cross-cut theorem, let C have m elements. If R is uniform over the 2^m subsets of C, then mu(0, 1) = 2^m E[(-1)^|R| 1{R is spanning}]. If 0 < p < 1 and R_p contains each element of C independently with probability p, then mu(0, 1) = (1 - p)^(-m) E[(-(1 - p)/p)^|R_p| 1{R_p is spanning}]; p = 1/2 gives the uniform form. These are unbiased Monte Carlo estimators of the Moebius number.
L a finite lattice
C a cross-cut
0 < p < 1

[Definition D:productSpace of arXiv:2606.03079, 'Mean Field Limits for Stochastic, Underdamped Reactive Langevin Dynamics Models'] For reaction $\mathcal{R}_{\ell}$ with $\tilde{L}+1 \leq \ell \leq L$, i.e., having at least one product particle, define the product position and velocity product space analogously to $\mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V}'^{(\ell)}$,
$$
\mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V'}^{(\ell)}\in (\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d)^{|\beta^{(\ell)}|},
$$
where we write
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V}'^{(\ell)} & \supseteq (\bm{y},\bm{v'}) =\bigl((y_{1}^{(1)},{v'}_{1}^{(1)}), \cdots, (y_{\beta_{\ell 1}}^{(1)},{v'}_{\beta_{\ell 1}}^{(1)}), \cdots, (y_{1}^{(J)},{v'}_{1}^{(J)}), \cdots, (y_{\beta_{\ell J}}^{(J)},{v'}_{\beta_{\ell J}}^{(J)})\bigr).
\end{align*}

 For $(\bm{y},\bm{v'}) \in \mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V'}^{(\ell)}$ a sampled product position and velocity configuration for one individual $\mathcal{R}_{\ell}$ reaction, $y_{r}^{(j)}$ then labels the sampled position for the $r$th product particle of species $j$ involved in the reaction, and ${v'}_{r}^{(j)}$ labels the sampled velocity for the same product particle. Let $d \bm{y} d\bm{v'}=\bigl(\bigwedge_{j=1}^{J}(\bigwedge_{r=1}^{\beta_{\ell_{j}}} d y_{r}^{(j)}d {v'}_{r}^{(j)})\bigr)$ be the corresponding volume form on $\mathbb{Y}^{(\ell)} \otimes \mathbb{V}'^{(\ell)}$, which also naturally defines an associated Lebesgue measure.

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] Let $g\geq4$ be even, and let $G=(L\sqcup R,E)$ be a bipartite
graph of girth at least $g$, with $|L|=|R|=n\geq1$. Let $\mu$ be a

$\bs{p}$, $\bs{p}^{X_u}$, and $\on{gap}(u)$ as in
\cref{eq:p-defns,eq:p-defns-cond,eq:gap-def}. Then
\[
  \sum_{u\in L}\on{gap}(u)\geq0.
\]
In particular, there exists a good vertex $u\in L$.

Let G be a finite group and p a prime dividing the order |G|. Then G contains an element of order exactly p, hence a subgroup of order p. More precisely (McKay), the number of solutions to x^p = e in G is a multiple of p, and since x = e is one of them, there are at least p - 1 elements of order p; in fact the number of elements of order p is congruent to -1 modulo p. Cauchy's theorem is the p^1 case of Sylow's first theorem (a subgroup of order p^a exists whenever p^a divides |G|) and is the converse of Lagrange's theorem for prime orders; the converse of Lagrange fails in general (A_4 has order 12 and no subgroup of order 6).
G finite, p prime with p dividing |G|

body: [Lemma 16 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Let $\vertexset$ be a finite set and $w_n\colon \vertexset\times\vertexset \to [0,\infty)$ be a sequence of edge conductances such that each $(\vertexset,w_n)$ is connected. body: [Corollary 3.4 (Estimation of wavelet coefficients / $S$) in the first version of arXiv:2512.18592, 'Wavelet Latent Position Exponential Random Graphs'] Assume the conditions of Theorem 3.3. Let $f(x,y):=\log\!\Big(\frac{W(x,y)}{1-W(x,y)}\Big)$ denote the logit of $W$. Under Definition 3.1 we have $\|f\|_{\infty}\leq B$ for a fixed constant $B<\infty$, hence $W$ is uniformly bounded away from $0$ and $1$. Fix a clipping level $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and let $\widehat{W}_{n}^{\mathrm{clip}}$ be the clipped estimator from Theorem 3.3. Define $\widehat{f}_{n}(x,y):=\log\!\Big(\frac{\widehat{W}_{n}^{\mathrm{clip}}(x,y)}{1-\widehat{W}_{n}^{\mathrm{clip}}(x,y)}\Big).$ Let $\{\Psi_{\lambda}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be the tensor-product orthonormal wavelet basis used above and define the coefficient arrays $\beta:=\big(\langle f,\Psi_{\lambda}\rangle\big)_{\lambda\in\Lambda},\qquad\widehat{\beta}_{n}:=\big(\langle\widehat{f}_{n},\Psi_{\lambda}\rangle\big)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}.$ Equip coefficient arrays with the $\ell^{2}(\Lambda)$ (Hilbert–Schmidt) norm $\|T\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{2}:=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}T_{\lambda}^{2}$. Then there exists a constant $C_{1}^{\prime}>0$ (depending only on $s,p,q,M,B$ and $\varepsilon$) such that, with the same exponent $C_{2}$ as in Theorem 3.3, $\sup_{W\in\mathcal{F}^{s}_{p,q}(M)}\mathbb{E}\,\|\widehat{\beta}_{n}-\beta\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{2}\leq C_{1}^{\prime}\,N_{n}^{-\frac{2s}{2s+2}}(\log N_{n})^{C_{2}}.$

[Corollary 11 (Consistency of FP selection) of arXiv:2608.20998, 'Free-Probability Kernels for Zero-Rollout Hyperparameter Selection in Reservoir Computing'] Assume that the deterministic kernel and the finite reservoir use the
same feature map. Fix finite candidate and ridge grids, with all ridge
parameters strictly positive. For any fixed maximum retained lag $L$,
if the deterministic validation score has a unique minimizer, then
finite-width reservoir selection returns the same minimizer with
probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$.

In the stable regime, a unique complete-history optimum is preserved
by all sufficiently large finite contexts, and selection based on the
complete finite-reservoir trajectory converges to this optimum as

body:
[Lemma lem:singleton-renewal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For a Kac plane $i$, let
\[
 W_i^\circ=\Pi_{\mathcal W}(\mathsf P_i-N^{-1}I_W)
\]
be its pure-Weyl coefficient.  On the common star space, with an arbitrary
passive ancillary Hilbert space $E$, put
\[
 (\mathsf M h)(i,\theta)=(W_i^\circ\otimes I_E)h(i,\theta),
 \qquad \mathsf J=\mathscr E^*\mathscr E,
 \qquad \mathsf Q=I-\mathsf J.
\]
Relative to $\operatorname{ran}\mathsf J\oplus
\operatorname{ran}\mathsf Q$, write
\[
 \mathsf M=
 \begin{pmatrix}0&\mathsf S^-\\ \mathsf S^+&\mathsf V\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{3.2.10n}
\]
We call $0,\mathsf S^-,\mathsf S^+,\mathsf V$ the four
\emph{star statuses} of a passive singleton; a status record chooses one
of these four blocks for every singleton after equal-time fusion.  These
statuses are distinct from the derivative-placement coefficients
$(\alpha,\beta)$ used in the Ricci root calculus.
Then
\[
 \|\mathsf S^-\|=\|\mathsf S^+\|
 \le\sqrt{\frac{n-3}{N(n-1)}}\le N^{-1/2},
 \qquad \|\mathsf V\|\le2,
\tag{3.2.10o}
\]
and the one-sided utilized-step maps factor through the innovation:
\[
 \mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr T=\mathscr E\mathsf M\mathscr G,
 \qquad
 \mathscr T^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*
 =\mathscr G^*\mathsf M\mathscr E^*.
\tag{3.2.10p}
\]
Consequently a passive singleton isolated between invariant separators is
zero.  A run of $s\ge2$ passive singletons with $s-1$ prescribed finite
Green gates has norm at most
\[
 \frac{2^{2s-3}}N.
\tag{3.2.10q}
\]
Thus its two endpoints create one $N^{-1}$ resource and every interior
singleton transports that same resource; no additional token is created.
The same conclusion holds when an endpoint is a $\mathscr D$- or
$\mathscr L$-incidence, with the corresponding mixed bound of
(lem:riesz of the paper) and with the already existing root or packet token
transported.

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2609.02779, '2609.02779'] Let $\omega:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be nondecreasing, with $\omega(0)=0$ and
$\omega(r)\to0$ as $r\downarrow0$.  There exists $V\in C^\infty(\T)$ such that
\[
  V\le0,\qquad V^{-1}(0)=\{0\},\qquad
  V^{(m)}(0)=0\quad\text{for every }m\ge1,
\]
and, for $H(x,p)=\frac12p^2+V(x)$, the corresponding discounted solutions satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \|u_\lambda-u_0\|_\infty\ge\omega(\lambda)
\end{equation}
for every sufficiently small $\lambda>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 43 (Finite-order Cauchy--Dirichlet estimate for scalar-principal systems) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(m\geq2\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).  Let
\(Q_i^+=\Omega_i\times[a,a+\theta]\), where
\(\Omega_1\Subset\Omega_2\) are smooth Euclidean domains.  Suppose that a
smooth finite-dimensional vector-valued function \(Z\) satisfies on
\(Q_2^+\)
\[
 \partial_tZ-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_jZ
 =\mathsf B^i\partial_iZ+\mathsf CZ+G,
\]
where \(a^{ij}=a^{ji}\) is uniformly parabolic and
\(\partial_t-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j\) acts componentwise with the same
coefficient matrix on every component; only \(\mathsf B^i\) and
\(\mathsf C\) may couple components.  The coefficients
\(a^{ij},\mathsf B^i,\mathsf C\) have uniformly bounded
\(C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}\)-norms.  Assume that \(Z=0\) on the initial
face, and that \(Z\) and \(G\) vanish in a fixed spatial collar of
\(\partial\Omega_2\times[a,a+\theta]\).  Then
\[
 \|Z\|_{C^{m+\sigma,(m+\sigma)/2}(Q_1^+)}
 \leq C\left(
   \|G\|_{C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}(Q_2^+)}
   +\|Z\|_{C^0(Q_2^+)}\right),
\]
where \(C\) depends only on the displayed coefficient and parabolicity bounds,
\(m,\sigma,\theta\), the rank, and the fixed domains \(\Omega_1\Subset
\Omega_2\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-order Cauchy--Dirichlet estimate for scalar-principal systems

[Theorem 10 (the linear estimate) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $\breg\in(\frac12,1)$, $\varepsilon:=1-\breg$,
$\sreg\ge0$, $\preg\in\Real$ and $0<T\le1$. For every
$f_0\in Y^{\sreg,\preg}$,
$f_1\in Y^{\sreg,\preg-1}$ and
$G\in L^{2}_tY^{\sreg,\preg-1}(\Rst)$ there is
$u$ on $\Rst$ with
\[
 \Box u=G\quad\text{on }[0,T],\qquad
 (u,\partial_tu)|_{t=0}=(f_0,f_1),
\]
satisfying
\begin{equation}
\big\|u\big\|_{H^{\sreg,\preg}_{\breg}}
 \le C_{\rm lin}\Big(
 \big\|f_0\big\|_{Y^{\sreg,\preg}}
 +\big\|f_1\big\|_{Y^{\sreg,\preg-1}}
 +T^{\varepsilon}\big\|G\big\|_{L^{2}_tY^{\sreg,\preg-1}}\Big),
\end{equation}
where $C_{\rm lin}=C(\chi,\breg)$ is independent of $T\le1$, of the
field, of the data and of the indices $\sreg,\preg$. Moreover,
\[
 u\in C([0,T],Y^{\sreg,\preg})
 \cap C^1([0,T],Y^{\sreg,\preg-1}).
\]

body: [Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM. A map $\mu$ is said to be an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-additive function if $\im\mu\subset \mf A$ and $\mu(A) = \sum \mu\circ\mb A$ for every $A\in D_\mu$ and every countable partition $\mb A$ of $A$ into elements of $D_\mu$. A map $\mu$ is called an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-content (premeasure)  if $\mu$ is an $\mf A$-valued $\sigma$-additive function and $D_\mu$ is a ring (resp., a $\delta$-ring).

body:
[Corollary 43 of arXiv:2607.21374, 'Local structure at the maximum and sharp persistence asymptotics of rough fractional Brown'] Let
\begin{equation*}
  h_n=2^{-r_n}\downarrow0,
  \qquad
  u_n,L_n\in h_n\mathbb Z_{\geq0},
  \qquad
  u_n\to0,
  \qquad
  L_n\to\infty.
\end{equation*}
Put
\begin{equation*}
  P_{h,u,L}:=(\mathscr M_{u,L})_*Q_{h,u,L},
  \qquad
  P_u:=(\mathscr A_u)_*Q^u\quad(u>0),
\end{equation*}
and let \(P_0\) be the law on \(\mathcal Y\) with zero lifetime, height, and
left arm, and right arm \((G_s)_{s\geq0}\) under \(Q^0\).  Thus
\(K_0=P_0\).  Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
  \mathcal L_{Q_{h_n,u_n,L_n}}
    \bigl(W|_{[0,\infty)}\bigr)
  \Longrightarrow Q^0
  \quad\text{in }C_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty)),\\
  P_{h_n,u_n,L_n}\Longrightarrow P_0,
  \qquad
  K_{h_n,u_n,L_n}\Longrightarrow K_0
  \quad\text{in }\mathcal Y.
\end{gathered}
  
\end{equation}
Consequently, the arm-valued map \(u\mapsto P_u\) and the endpoint-tilted map
\(u\mapsto K_u\) are weakly continuous on \([0,\infty)\).

[Proposition 6 (All-partition normalization) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] Let $K$ be an oriented zero-framed knot.  For every $N\ge2$ and every
partition $\lambda$ with at most $N$ parts,
\begin{equation}
 \HH_\lambda(K;q^N,q)=J_K(V(\lambda);q^2).
\end{equation}
Here the right side is computed with the Hopf and ribbon convention
\eqref{eq:Hopf}--\eqref{eq:HL-R-convention}.  Thus the scalar family used
below in the algebraic dual interpolation formula is the standard reduced
colored HOMFLY--PT family.

[Lem 16 of arXiv:2605.15501, 'Well-posedness of the obstacle problem for generalized Dean--Kawasaki equation\thanks{ The'] (A priori estimates
for the kinetic measure) Let Assumption \ref{assu:assu for existence} and Assumption \ref{assu:assum for F} hold.

For any $n\in\mathbb{N}$
and $\alpha,\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, let $u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}$
be a solution to \eqref{eq:appro penalized eq}, then for all $N_{1},N_{2}\in(0,\infty)$
such that $N_{1}<N_{2}$, there exists a constant $C$ independent
of $n$, $\alpha$, $\varepsilon$, $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ such that
\begin{align}
 & \mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(N_{1},N_{2})\}}\Phi^{\prime}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})|\nabla_{x}u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^2+\alpha\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(N_{1},N_{2})\}}|\nabla_{x}u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^2\\
 & +\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\int_\theta|(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}-\psi)^+|^2 \mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(\theta^{-1}(N_{1}-\psi)+\psi,\theta^{-1}(N_{2}-\psi)+\psi)\}}\nonumber\\
 & \leq C(N_2-N_1)\mathbb{E}\int_x (u_{\mathrm{init}}-N_1)^{+}
+C\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\geq N_{1}\}}|\sigma_{n}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\land N_{2})|^{2}.\nonumber
\end{align}
In particular, we have
\begin{align}
 & \lim_{N\rightarrow \infty}\Big[\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(N,N+1)\}}\Phi^{\prime}(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon})|\nabla_{x}u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^2 +\alpha\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(N,N+1)\}}|\nabla_{x}u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}|^2\nonumber\\
 & +\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\mathbb{E}\int_{x,t}\int_\theta|(u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}-\psi)^+|^2 \mathbf{1}_{\{u_{\alpha,n,\varepsilon}\in(\theta^{-1}(N-\psi)+\psi,\theta^{-1}(N+1-\psi)+\psi)\}}\Big]=0.
 \end{align}

body: [Definition Cone-points of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] The $\delta$-forward cone from ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is the set $\ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleleft_\delta({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}) := {\ensuremath{\mathsf u}} + \{(x, y) \in \mathbb Z^2: |y| \leq \delta x\}$. Similarly, the backward cone from ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is the set $\ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleright_\delta({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}) = {\ensuremath{\mathsf u}} - \{(x, y) \in \mathbb Z^2: |y| \leq \delta x\}$. When $\delta$ is omitted from the notation, we assume $\delta = 1$. When ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is omitted from the notation, we assume ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}} = (0, 0)$. For a disagreement polymer $\gamma$, ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is a cone-point of $\gamma$ if $\gamma \subset \ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleright({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}) \cap \ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleleft({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}})$. Similarly, for an animal $\Gamma = [\gamma, \underline{\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}]$, ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}$ is a cone-point for $\Gamma$ if $\Gamma \subset \ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleright({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}) \cap \ensuremath{\mathcal Y}^\blacktriangleleft({\ensuremath{\mathsf u}})$.
title: Cone-points

body:
Let T be a bounded subset of R^n, let eps_1, ..., eps_n be independent Rademacher signs, and let phi_i : R -> R be 1-Lipschitz with phi_i(0) = 0 for every i. Then E sup_{t in T} sum_{i=1}^n eps_i phi_i(t_i) <= E sup_{t in T} sum_{i=1}^n eps_i t_i. With ABSOLUTE VALUES inside the supremum the same statement holds with a factor 2: E sup_{t in T} | sum_i eps_i phi_i(t_i) | <= 2 E sup_{t in T} | sum_i eps_i t_i |. The distinction between the constants 1 and 2 is a standard source of misquotation; the constant 1 belongs to the version WITHOUT absolute values. The hypothesis phi_i(0) = 0 is needed for the version without absolute values and can be arranged by subtracting a constant, which is harmless for a symmetric process. In statistical learning the principle is what lets one strip a Lipschitz loss off a function class without changing the Rademacher complexity by more than a constant. [Ledoux and Talagrand, Probability in Banach Spaces, Theorem 4.12]
phi_i 1-Lipschitz with phi_i(0) = 0
eps_i independent Rademacher signs
T bounded so the suprema are finite; constant 1 WITHOUT absolute values, 2 WITH them

D_{\theta,u}(t)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\dd}{\dd t}\,\Ebb_{1,t,u}^G[\lambda(\omega)], & \theta=1,\\[1.2ex]
\dfrac{\theta}{\theta-1}\dfrac{\dd}{\dd t}\log Z_G(\theta,t,u), & \theta\neq 1.
\end{cases}
\]

[Corollary prop:conditioned_Bernoulli1 of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph, $x_e\in (0,1)$ for each $e\in E$. Let $\Omega = \{0,1\}^E$, $\Sigma \subset \Omega$ , $f:\Omega\to 2^{\Sigma}$ be defined by $f(\omega)= \Sigma^{\downarrow}(\omega):=\{\eta \in \Sigma: \eta \subset \omega\}$ as well as
	$$\rho[\omega] \propto \mathbb{P}_{x}[\omega], ~\forall \omega\in \Omega, ~\gamma[\eta]\propto 1, ~\forall \eta\in \Sigma. $$
    	Then, under the coupling measure $\mathscr{P}$ defined in Theorem (thm:generalcoupling of the paper), 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$ is $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta]=\mathbb{P}_{\frac{x}{1+x}}[\eta \mid \Sigma] \propto \prod_{e\in \eta} x_e$. 
        For each $\omega\in\Omega$ with $\mathscr{P}_\Omega[\omega] \neq 0$, the  conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \omega]
        = \mathtt{UG}[\;\cdot \mid \Sigma^{\downarrow}(\omega)]$- the uniform subgraph of $\omega$ which belongs to $\Sigma$.
        \item[(b)]The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$ is $\mathscr{P}_\Omega= \mathscr{P}_{\Sigma} \cup \mathbb{P}_x$.
        For each $\eta\in\Sigma$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta]\neq 0$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \eta] = \mathbb{P}_x \cup \delta_{\eta}$. 
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary prop:conditioned_Bernoulli1 of arXiv:2506.10765

body: [Definition Nash equilibrium and coarse correlated equilibrium of arXiv:2608.24731, 'Optimal Alternating Regret for Online Learning and Games\thanks{Authors are alphabetically'] A joint strategy profile $(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y})$ is an \emph{$\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium ($\epsilon$-NE)} if $u_1(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y}) \le \min_{\boldsymbol{x}' \in \+X} u_1(\boldsymbol{x}', \boldsymbol{y}) + \epsilon$ and $u_2(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y}) \le \min_{\boldsymbol{y}' \in \+X} u_2(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbol{y}') + \epsilon$. A distribution $\sigma$ over joint strategy profiles $\+X \times \+Y$ is an \emph{$\epsilon$-coarse correlated equilibrium ($\epsilon$-CCE)} if $\-E_{(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})\sim \sigma}[u_1(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})] \le \min_{\boldsymbol{x}' \in \+X}\-E_{(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})\sim \sigma}[u_1(\boldsymbol{x}',\boldsymbol{y})] + \epsilon$ and $\-E_{(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})\sim \sigma}[u_2(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})] \le \min_{\boldsymbol{y}' \in \+Y}\-E_{(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})\sim \sigma}[u_2(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y}')] + \epsilon$.
title: Nash equilibrium and coarse correlated equilibrium

body:
Load-bearing hypotheses: (1) the growth bound $|F(z)|\le Ce^{A|z|}$ must hold for all complex $z$, not merely on $\mathbb R$; (2) $F$ must be square integrable on $\mathbb R$ (for the $L^2$ version) or have controlled polynomial growth (for the distributional version). Failure of (1): $F(z)=e^{-z^2}$ is entire and its restriction to $\mathbb R$ is in $L^2$, yet $|F(iy)|=e^{y^2}$, so $F$ is of order 2, not of exponential type; its Fourier transform is a Gaussian, supported everywhere - no band limitation. Failure of (2): $F(z)=\cos(Az)$ is entire of exponential type exactly $A$ and bounded on $\mathbb R$, but not in $L^2(\mathbb R)$; it is not $\int_{-A}^A\varphi(t)e^{itz}dt$ for any $\varphi\in L^2$, only for the measure $\frac12(\delta_A+\delta_{-A})$ - the correct statement in that regime is the Paley-Wiener-Schwartz theorem for compactly supported distributions, with a polynomial factor $(1+|\zeta|)^N$ allowed. Similarly $F(z)=e^{Az}$ has type $A$ but grows on the real axis. Two further traps: the exponential factor in Paley-Wiener-Schwartz measures the support of the transform only through the supporting function of its convex hull, so the theorem detects $\operatorname{ch}(\operatorname{supp}u)$, not the support itself; and no such function can have both itself and its transform compactly supported, since a nonzero entire function cannot vanish on an open set (see Benedicks' theorem for the measure-theoretic strengthening).
F entire on C (or C^d)
claims of band limitation require the growth bound off the real axis
L^2 version needs square integrability on R; distributions need the polynomial-growth version
title: Pitfall: Paley-Wiener Needs Exponential Type in Every Direction Plus Integrability on the Line

Conjectured bond analogue (do not treat as an established theorem without reviewing a current proof): Let G be an infinite connected locally finite graph with finitely many vertex orbits under its automorphism group. In independent Bernoulli bond percolation with p_c(G)<1, the configuration at p_c(G) almost surely has no infinite open edge cluster. Benjamini and Schramm expressly said their nonplanar questions extend to bond percolation; Hutchcroft's 2016 theorem proves the exponential-growth subcase. A September/October 2026 release claims the full bond statement, but that claim is not certified by this draft.

Assuming NP is not contained in P/poly, there exists an efficiently computable normalizable weighted language p_tilde for which no ELNCP weighted language q_tilde has support(q_tilde)=support(p_tilde). The p_tilde constructed in the companion Theorem1 card has this property, so its support is even a polynomial-time decidable language. This is exact support separation for locally normalized models with compact nonuniform parameters, not a distribution-approximation or finite-precision lower bound.
Complexity assumption NP is not a subset of P/poly; the assumption is stronger than merely P!=NP.
Finite binary alphabet and finite strings of unbounded length; exact rational output for the constructed weights.
ELNCP is efficient local normalization with compact parameters: a fixed polynomial-time scheme with polynomial-size nonuniform advice for each prefix-length bound returns the actual next-symbol and termination conditional probabilities at positive-mass prefixes up to that bound.
Exact representability and conditional evaluation are the subject; no assertion about approximation in TV or KL follows from this theorem alone.

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT: proof (unaudited); C011 v2 has no independent PASS. For fixed n>=2, x0*y0!=0, zero-sum fixed b_i of variance s>0, common-Hessian f_i=x^2/2+kappa*y^2/2+b_i*x and kappa log(T)/T -> c in (0,infinity) excluding 4/3: if c<4/3 then T eta_opt/log T ->3/2 and min P~(27 n(n+1)s/384)log^3(T)/T^3; if c>4/3 then min P~(x0^2/2)exp(-4T/kappa), T(eta_opt-2/kappa)->0, and kappa eta_opt->2, for every global minimizer over eta>=0. Here T=nK with K epochs, each using a fresh independent uniform permutation of the n components; s=(sum_i b_i^2)/n>0. The initial point (x0,y0) and component linear terms remain fixed as T grows. P_T(eta) is the expected excess of the average objective F(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa_T*y^2/2 at the final iterate after T component-gradient steps, using constant eta throughout. Curvature is normalized to mu=1 and kappa_T>=1. No assertion is made at c=4/3, for growing n, or for general noncommuting finite sums.
T=nK, fresh independent uniform permutation each epoch
Fixed n, b_i, nonzero initial x0,y0; s>0; no stiff-coordinate linear terms
kappa>=1 and kappa log(T)/T ->c>0, c!=4/3

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ab4ff9ca0abf3dfb7e5ca7cd659cdf5ae4a3c592a8a1c14e52748fc874240805","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ab/ab4ff9ca0abf3dfb7e5ca7cd659cdf5ae4a3c592a8a1c14e52748fc874240805.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:1b00f1371bd432e017c7bd448bee9064fecfc797b4d9f0ea5d49a490c21579cb","bundle_entry_key":"zero-stiff-noise-critical-ratio","bundle_id":"population.t362-zero-stiff-noise-010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Finite-sum strongly convex quadratic optimization; common diagonal Hessian; fixed n","draft":"w732/bundle_010.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.randomreshuffling:common-hessian-random-reshuffling-zero-stiff-noise-critical-threshold","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C011 v2: zero stiff noise in the critical condition-number regime

Status: proof (unaudited). Independent review required. No priority claim.
Target 1 only; this uses the approved C001 recursion and C003 flat-variance expansion, not different component Hessians.

Fix n>=2, T=nK tending to infinity, fixed x0!=0, y0!=0, and fixed zero-sum b_i with s=mean b_i^2>0. Set
f_i(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa_T*y^2/2+b_i*x, kappa_T>=1.
Each epoch uses a fresh independent uniform permutation. Let P_T(eta) be expected final objective error and minimize over every eta>=0. Assume kappa_T log(T)/T -> c in (0,infinity), excluding c=4/3. Define A=x0^2/2, Y=y0^2/2 and D=n(n+1)s/48, all strictly positive. Then every global minimizer satisfies:

(a) If 0<c<4/3:
    T eta_T/log(T) -> 3/2,
    min P_T ~ (27D/8) log(T)^3/T^3.
(b) If c>4/3:
    min P_T ~ A exp(-4T/kappa_T),
    T(eta_T-2/kappa_T) -> 0, and kappa_T eta_T -> 2.

The actual kappa_T, not merely its first-order equivalent, is retained in (b).

## 1. Exact decomposition and facts already proved
By C001 write, with a=1-eta,
P_T(eta)=A a^(2T)+R_T(eta)+kappa Y(1-kappa eta)^(2T).
R_T is the flat-coordinate noise contribution; it is nonnegative for every eta. For eta->0 and T eta->infinity, the C003 fixed-n flat-variance sandwich gives
    R_T(eta)=D eta^3(1+o(1)).
For eta->0 without this divergence it still gives R_T(eta)=O(eta^3) on eta>0, because the finite-horizon factor is at most one. The last epoch and pair (0,1) give, for every eta>=0,
    R_T(eta)>=s eta^4/[2(n-1)].
These are invoked as settled dependencies, not new results. The exact P_T is a continuous coercive polynomial; for example its stiff deterministic term has positive leading coefficient kappa^(2T+1)Y. Thus global minimizers exist.

## 2. Subcritical candidate, 0<c<4/3
Let ell=log(T) and eta_c=3ell/(2T). Then q_c=kappa eta_c ->3c/2 in (0,2), so eventually |1-q_c|<=rho for a fixed rho<1. The stiff initial term is O(kappa rho^(2T))=o(ell^3/T^3). Here kappa=O(T/ell), and exponential decay dominates any fixed polynomial. The slow initial term equals A T^-3(1+o(1)), because T eta_c^2=O(ell^2/T)->0. The flat variance is asymptotic to D eta_c^3. Hence
    min P_T <= (27D/8+o(1))ell^3/T^3.                 (2)

## 3. All subcritical global optimizers
The quartic bound and (2) imply eta_T->0. If t_T=T eta_T were bounded on a subsequence, A(1-eta_T)^(2T) would remain bounded away from zero, contradicting (2). Thus t_T->infinity, and R_T(eta_T)=D eta_T^3(1+o(1)). This and (2) imply t_T=O(ell), hence T eta_T^2->0. Comparing the slow initial term with (2) gives
    2t_T >=3ell-3log(ell)-O(1).
Therefore liminf t_T/ell>=3/2. Comparing the variance with (2) gives limsup t_T/ell<=3/2. Consequently t_T/ell->3/2 and the variance lower bound matches (2), proving (a). This applies to every choice of a global minimizer; a failure of uniform localization would produce a contrary sequence.

## 4. Supercritical candidate, c>4/3
Put r=T/kappa, ell=log(T), delta=3ell/T, q_c=2-delta and eta_c=q_c/kappa. Eventually 0<delta<1 and 0<eta_c<1. Since r~ell/c and T/kappa^2=O(ell^2/T),
    A(1-eta_c)^(2T)=A exp(-4r)(1+o(1)).
Indeed 2T eta_c=4r-2r delta and r delta=O(ell^2/T)->0; the quadratic logarithmic remainder is also O(ell^2/T). The stiff term obeys
    kappa Y(1-delta)^(2T)<=kappa Y exp(-2T delta)
                                   =kappa Y T^-6=O(T^-5/ell).
The flat variance is O(eta_c^3)=O(ell^3/T^3).
Since exp(-4r)=T^(-4/c+o(1)) and 4/c<3, both error terms are o(exp(-4r)). For a formal comparison, choose epsilon>0 with 4/c+epsilon<3; eventually exp(4r)<=T^(4/c+epsilon). Thus
    min P_T <= A exp(-4r)(1+o(1)) ->0.              (4)

## 5. Supercritical global lower bound and steps
If q_T=kappa eta_T>=2, then |1-q_T|>=1 and P_T(eta_T)>=kappa Y, contradicting (4). Thus eventually 0<=eta_T<2/kappa<1. On this interval the slow deterministic contribution gives
    P_T(eta_T)>=A(1-eta_T)^(2T)
              >=A(1-2/kappa)^(2T)
               =A exp(-4r)(1+o(1)).
The final expansion is valid because T/kappa^2->0. Combine with (4) to prove the error equivalent. Uniformly over eta in [0,2/kappa], the logarithmic remainder O(T eta^2) is o(1), so
    A(1-eta_T)^(2T)/(A exp(-4r))
      =exp(2T(2/kappa-eta_T)+o(1)) <=1+o(1).
The difference 2/kappa-eta_T is nonnegative. Taking logarithms forces T(2/kappa-eta_T)->0. Multiplication by kappa/T~c/ell->0 gives q_T->2. This proves (b).

## Scope and failure cases
The critical value c=4/3 is unpaid; subleading deviations of kappa can affect the relative slow bias and flat variance there. No conclusion is made for growing n or changing b_i/initialization. y0!=0 is essential to step 5: if y0=0, the stiff coordinate stays exactly zero and the objective and its optimized value are independent of kappa. x0!=0 and s>0 are essential to the balancing argument. The results concern this common-Hessian finite sum only and do not solve general last-iterate RR.

Prior work: C001/C003 and the 18 Oct common-Hessian work credited in PRIOR_WORK_ATTRIBUTION.md. The 2303.07160/2609.04578 primary-source context is already recorded in SOURCES.jsonl. New OpenAlex search is metadata-only; no priority or literature-exhaustiveness conclusion follows. Least-trusted review steps: all-optimizer localization in step 3 and uniform logarithmic comparison in step 5.

## Verification record and practical limitation

The saved script scripts/check_zero_stiff.py performed 20 exact rational checks of the stiff-instability boundary and 48 Decimal diagnostic optimizations (65-digit arithmetic, two fixed n values, six c values, four horizons). These do not certify global numerical minima or asymptotic limits. At n=3, c=1.4, T=3,000,000,000 the diagnostic value is approximately 596.73 times the supercritical leading term: crossover near 4/3 is extremely slow. No finite-horizon accuracy claim is made. The Lean attempt for q>=2 implying (1-q)^2>=1 timed out after 60 seconds without a certificate; the formal target remains UNVERIFIED. body: Witness: endpoints (0,0) and (L,0) on Z^2; one n x W block carrying weight a on every edge, weight b outside. The straight horizontal path is the geodesic, uses exactly n edges of the block, and resampling the block to all-b moves the passage time by exactly (b-a)n. Hence any pointwise a.s. bound B on (X^Lambda - X)^+ over configurations satisfies B >= (b-a)n = Theta(n); for non-atomic laws the same holds up to o(1) by a positive-probability Lipschitz perturbation. Consequence: pointwise-increment routes to fourth-moment control in the resampling engine are pinned at B ~ n on the lattice; only truncation-plus-tail (moment) formulations can charge the increment at a smaller scale. Refereed 2026-08-09 (referee's own witness, D1). Provenance: campaign CRUX section 6d.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2605.12475, 'Central limit theorem for the homozygosity of the hierarchical Pitman-Yor process'] For all $m \geq 1$ and $k \geq 1$, 
\bal
\E[W_k^m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta) \mid \bm{V}, \gamma_{1/\beta}] &= \sum_{j=1}^m \Cs(m,j,\beta) \gamma_{1/\beta}^j V_k^j, \\
\E[W_k^m(\alpha, \theta_0, \beta, \theta) \mid \bm{V}] &= \sum_{j=1}^m \frac{\Cs(m,j,\beta) \prod_{s=0}^{j-1} (\theta + s\beta)}{\beta^j} V_k^j,
\eal
where $\Cs(m,j,\beta)$ is the generalized factorial coefficient.

Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables and let Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) be a nonnegative random variable with E[Z log Z] finite. Write Ent(Z) = E[Z log Z] - E[Z] log E[Z] and let Ent^{(i)}(Z) denote the same functional computed with respect to X_i alone, with the other coordinates held fixed. Then Ent(Z) <= sum_{i=1}^n E[ Ent^{(i)}(Z) ]. The same statement with variance in place of entropy is the Efron-Stein inequality, and the two are the p = 2 and p = 1 members of a family of phi-entropies that all tensorize. Tensorization is what converts a ONE-DIMENSIONAL functional inequality into an n-dimensional one with no loss of constant: if each coordinate's law satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant C, then the product law satisfies it with the SAME constant C, independent of n. That dimension-free feature is the whole reason the entropy method produces concentration bounds that do not degrade as n grows. Independence of the coordinates is essential. [standard; e.g. Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Theorem 4.10 and Section 4.1]
X_1, ..., X_n independent
Z = f(X) nonnegative with E[Z log Z] finite

Fix any U with E[e^U] <= 1 and let E_i denote conditional expectation given X_1, ..., X_i, with E_0 = E and E_n e^U = e^U. Telescope the exponential rather than U itself: e^U = E[e^U] * prod_{i=1}^n ( E_i e^U / E_{i-1} e^U ), so with U_i = log E_i e^U - log E_{i-1} e^U one has U = log E[e^U] + sum_i U_i <= sum_i U_i, because log E[e^U] <= 0. Hence E[Z U] <= sum_i E[Z U_i]. Now condition on X^{(i)} = (X_j)_{j != i}. By independence, E_{i-1} e^U is a function of X_1, ..., X_{i-1} alone, hence fixed given X^{(i)}, and averaging E_i e^U over X_i with the other coordinates fixed returns E_{i-1} e^U, so E[ e^{U_i} | X^{(i)} ] = 1. The one-variable duality formula, applied in the variable X_i with the others held fixed, then gives E[ Z U_i | X^{(i)} ] <= Ent^{(i)}(Z). Taking expectations and summing over i, E[Z U] <= sum_i E[ Ent^{(i)}(Z) ]; the supremum over admissible U is Ent(Z), which proves the inequality. [Theorem 99 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Let $p \in \amsmathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. Consider a variational datum satisfying Assumptions~\ref{Assumption_A}, \ref{Assumption_B} and \ref{Assumption_C}, with segment filling fractions $\hat{\boldsymbol{n}}^0$, and such that for each $h \in [H]$ the segment $[\hat{a}^{\prime\, 0}_h,\hat{b}^{\prime\,0}_h]$ contains a single band of the equilibrium measure. There exists a constant $\delta > 0$ depending only on the constants in the assumptions, with the following properties.

Consider any family of variational data parameterized by $\boldsymbol{t} = (\hat{\boldsymbol{a}}',\hat{\boldsymbol{b}}',\hat{\boldsymbol{n}},u)$ varying in the $\delta$-neighborhood of $\boldsymbol{t}^0 = (\hat{\boldsymbol{a}}^{\prime\,0},\hat{\boldsymbol{b}}^{\prime\,0},\hat{\boldsymbol{n}}^{0},0)$ in $\amsmathbb{R}^{3H + 1}$, such that the first three entries of $\boldsymbol{t}$ represent the segment endpoints and filling fractions and the variational datum for $\boldsymbol{t} = \boldsymbol{t}^0$ coincides with the original one. Suppose that these variational data satisfy Assumption~\ref{Assumption_B} for a $\boldsymbol{t}$-independent tuple of integers $\boldsymbol{\iota}^{\pm}$ and $\boldsymbol{t}$-independent complex domains $(\amsmathbb{M}_h)_{h = 1}^{H}$, and that for any $h \in [H]$ the regular part of the potential $U_h^{\boldsymbol{t}}(z)$ is a $p$-times continuously differentiable function of $\boldsymbol{t}$ --- with any partial derivative up to order $p$ being a holomorphic function of $z \in \amsmathbb{M}_h$.

Then, denoting $\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\boldsymbol{t}}$ the equilibrium measure corresponding to the $\boldsymbol{t}$-dependent variational datum, for any $h \in [H]$ the function
\[
\boldsymbol{t} \longmapsto \Gm_{\mu^{\boldsymbol{t}}_h}(z)
\]
is $p$ times continuously differentiable, with any partial derivative up to order $p$ being a holomorphic function of $z \in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus [\hat{a}_h^{\prime\,\boldsymbol{t}},\hat{b}_h^{\prime\,\boldsymbol{t}}]$. Simultaneously, for any $\boldsymbol{t}$ as above there remains exactly one band per segment and the endpoints of the bands are $p$ times continuously differentiable functions of $\boldsymbol{t}$. All the derivatives depend on the matrix of interactions $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ in a continuous way.

[Definition 49 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Assume the same parameters as in Definition \ref{Def.ParametersEdge} and fix $\kappa \in [0, \bar{\kappa})$. Suppose $x \in [\zc(\kappa), c]$, $\theta \in (0, \pi)$, $R > q^{-1}$ and $r \in [0, q^{-1} - c]$. With this data we define the contour $C(x, \theta, R,r)$ as follows. Let $z^{\pm}$ be the points where the rays $\{x + te^{\pm \im \theta}: t \geq 0\}$ intersect the $x$-centered circle of radius $r$, and let $\zeta^{\pm}$ be the points where they intersect the $0$-centered circle of radius $R$. The contour $C(x, \theta, R,r)$ consists of three oriented segments that connect $\zeta^-$ to $z^-$, $z^-$ to $z^+$, and $z^+$ to $\zeta^+$, as well as the counterclockwise oriented circular arc of the $0$-centered circle that connects $\zeta^+$ to $\zeta^-$. See the left side of Figure \ref{Fig.ContoursEdge}. We also recall that $C_r$ is the positively oriented zero-centered circle of radius $r > 0$. 

For a fixed $a \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\varphi \in (0, \pi)$, we recall from Definition \ref{Def.S1Contours} that $\mathcal{C}_{a}^{\varphi}=\{a+|s|e^{\mathrm{sgn}(s)\im\varphi}, s\in \mathbb{R}\}$ is the infinite contour oriented from $a+\infty e^{-\im\varphi}$ to $a+\infty e^{\im\varphi}$.  For $r > 0$ we define the contour $\mathcal{C}_{a}^{\varphi}[r]$, so that outside of the disc $\{z: |z-a| \leq r\}$ it agrees with $\mathcal{C}_{a}^{\varphi}$ and inside the disc it is a vertical segment that connects $a + re^{-\im \varphi}$ and $a + re^{\im \varphi}$. See the right side of Figure \ref{Fig.ContoursEdge}.

body:
Every real α has a regular continued fraction expansion α = a_0 + 1/(a_1 + 1/(a_2 + ...)) = [a_0; a_1, a_2, ...], produced by the Gauss algorithm: a_0 = floor(α), α_1 = 1/(α − a_0), a_k = floor(α_k), α_{k+1} = 1/(α_k − a_k). Here a_0 is an integer, every a_k (k ≥ 1) is an integer ≥ 1 (the partial quotients), and the α_k are the complete quotients, so a_k < α_k < a_k + 1 whenever the expansion continues. The expansion is finite iff α is rational (then it is unique once the last partial quotient is required to be ≥ 2); for irrational α it is infinite and unique.

The convergents p_n/q_n = [a_0; a_1, ..., a_n] are computed by p_{-1} = 1, q_{-1} = 0, p_0 = a_0, q_0 = 1 and p_{n+1} = a_{n+1} p_n + p_{n-1}, q_{n+1} = a_{n+1} q_n + q_{n-1} for n ≥ 0.

Basic identities: p_n q_{n-1} − p_{n-1} q_n = (−1)^{n-1} for n ≥ 0, so gcd(p_n, q_n) = 1; α = (p_n α_{n+1} + p_{n-1})/(q_n α_{n+1} + q_{n-1}); the even convergents increase strictly to α and the odd convergents decrease strictly to α (for irrational α); |α − p_n/q_n| < 1/(q_n q_{n+1}) < 1/q_n^2. The denominators satisfy 1 = q_0 ≤ q_1 < q_2 < q_3 < ..., with q_0 = q_1 exactly when a_1 = 1. The Gauss map x ↦ {1/x} on (0,1) preserves the Gauss measure dx/((1 + x) log 2), the ergodic-theoretic setting for the statistics of partial quotients.
α real; for the infinite-expansion statements α irrational
title: Regular continued fraction, complete quotients and convergents

[Lemma 36 (No thin visited regions) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] We invoke Theorem~\ref{thm:ulmb}; we also use the one-arm bound
(Proposition~\ref{prop:KN}).
Fix $K<\infty$, $\kappa\in(0,K)$ and
$\delta\in(0,\kappa/(5\sqrt d)]$. Then for every
$\eta\in(0,1]$,
\begin{multline*}
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\;
n^2\,\bP\Bigl(\exists\,x\in \mathcal C:\ \kappa n\le|x|\le Kn,\
\bigl|\mathcal C\cap \overline B(x,3\sqrt d\,\delta n)\bigr|\le\eta(\delta n)^4\Bigr)
\\
\le\;C(d)\,C_3\,K_2\Bigl(\frac{K}{\delta}\Bigr)^{d}\kappa^{-2}\,\eta^{1/4},
\end{multline*}
where $C_3=C_3(\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda:=(K+\delta)/\delta$ is the
constant of Theorem~\ref{thm:ulmb} and $K_2$ is the constant of the one-arm
bound (Proposition~\ref{prop:KN}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:Lipschitzquotient of arXiv:2609.01557, '$L^\infty$ Variational Approximation of the Aubry Set'] Let \(v_1,v_2\) be two critical subsolutions and set
\[
    z:=v_1-v_2.
\]
Then for all \(x,y\in\mathbb T^n\),
\begin{equation}
    |z(y)-z(x)|
    \leq \delta_M(x,y).
\end{equation}
Consequently, \(z|_\mathcal A\) descends to a \(1\)-Lipschitz function
\[
    \overline z:(\mathcal A_M,\delta_M)\to\mathbb R.
\]
If
\[
    \mathcal H^1(\mathcal A_M,\delta_M)=0,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal H^1(z(\mathcal A))=0.
\end{equation}
In particular, \(z(\mathcal A)\) contains no nontrivial interval.

body: Ding-Lee-Peres Question 5.2 (arXiv:1004.4371, Section 5: when t_hit = o(t_cov), are the cover-time fluctuations of order t_hit?) is answered in the negative. On the clique-star G_k (a k-clique with one pendant leaf at each clique vertex; t_hit = 2k^2 + k + 1) the cover time satisfies Var(tau_cov) ~ t_hit t_cov and (tau_cov - E tau_cov)/sqrt(Var tau_cov) converges to a standard Gaussian; on the double star D_k (two adjacent centres, each with k pendant leaves; t_hit = 6k + 3) the cover time centred at 4k log k and divided by 2 sqrt(2) k sqrt(log k) converges to |Z|, a half-normal law, with t_cov = 4k log k + (4/sqrt(pi)) k sqrt(log k) + o(k sqrt(log k)) and Var(tau_cov) = 8(1 - 2/pi) k^2 log k (1 + o(1)). Centred at its mean instead, (tau_cov - t_cov)/sqrt(t_hit t_cov) converges to (|Z| - sqrt(2/pi))/sqrt(3), and the standardized cover time (tau_cov - E tau_cov)/SD(tau_cov) converges to (|Z| - sqrt(2/pi))/sqrt(1 - 2/pi), not to a half-normal law; SD(tau_cov)/t_hit ~ (sqrt(2)/3) sqrt(1 - 2/pi) sqrt(log k) -> infinity. The proofs use exact first-step hitting systems, an excursion transform f_k with mu = k^2 - k + 2 and sigma^2 = k^4 - 4k^2 + 5k - 2, stage and coupon-clock closed forms, a residual lemma (the trap is last with probability 1/(r+1)), second-order expansions with explicit error 3k log k + 5k, moderate deviations by Gartner-Ellis at speed a_k^2, an operational-time construction exact in law (tau = 2P + J - 1), and an occupation CLT with covariance (2/q) L^+.

[Theorem thm:whole-plane-persistence of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Fix $\kappa,M,R>0$.  Then there exists $C=C(\kappa,M,R)>0$ such that the following
holds.  For $\varepsilon>0$, let
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}\geq0,\qquad
  \int_{\mathbb R^2}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=\kappa,
  \qquad
  \|\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty\leq M\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R\varepsilon}(\mathbf0).
\end{equation}
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of the two-dimensional Euler equation in $\mathbb R^2$.  Then
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})^2
  \leq C\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0}).
\end{equation}
If, in addition,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\leq\frac{\kappa^2}{C},
\end{equation}
then, with
\[
  \mathbf X_\varepsilon
  :=\frac1\kappa\int_{\mathbb R^2}\mathbf x
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}(\mathbf x)\,\mathrm d\mathbf x,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf X_\varepsilon|
  \leq (1+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b|
  \leq(2+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
In particular, for any family of initial data satisfying
(equation eq:whole-plane-initial-data of the paper) with the same $\kappa,M,R$, if
$\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, then
\[
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})\longrightarrow0,
  \qquad
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in
  \mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}|\mathbf b|\longrightarrow0.
\]

If a_1 >= a_2 >= ... >= a_n and b_1 >= b_2 >= ... >= b_n (both sequences sorted the same way), then (1/n) sum a_i b_i >= ((1/n) sum a_i) ((1/n) sum b_i); if one sequence is increasing and the other decreasing, the inequality reverses. The integral form: for f and g both monotone in the same direction on [0,1], the integral of f g is at least the product of the integrals. This is the one-dimensional case of the Harris-FKG inequality (a product of two increasing functions of one uniform variable has nonnegative covariance), and its proof is the identity 2(n sum a_i b_i - sum a_i sum b_j) = sum_{i,j} (a_i - a_j)(b_i - b_j) >= 0.
both sequences (or functions) monotone in the same direction; opposite directions reverse the inequality
no independence or product structure needed beyond the single variable; the n-variable generalization is Harris-FKG

body: For the biased Bernoulli convolution at ratio 2/3 - the law of sum_k B_k (2/3)^k with B_k i.i.d., P(B_k = 1) = p - the measure is singular for every p < p* = 0.140277, where p* solves H(p) = log(3/2) in natural logarithms (H(p)/log(3/2) = 0.4896, 0.8018, 1.2341, 1.7095 at p = 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1/2). Proof: the dimension of the measure is at most the entropy-over-Lyapunov ratio H(p)/log(3/2), and a measure on the line of dimension below one is not absolutely continuous; Hochman's theorem is needed only for the matching lower bound dim = min(1, H(p)/log(3/2)), which this does not use. Two further thresholds govern the Fourier criterion at this ratio. The biased factor |(1-p) + p e^{i phi}|^2 = 1 - 2p(1-p)(1 - cos phi) has arithmetic mean 1 - 2p(1-p) over the phase, which gives the annealed (main-term) exponent alpha(p) = 1 + log(1 - 2p(1-p))/log(3/2), zero at p(1-p) = 1/6, i.e. p = (1 - 3^{-1/2})/2 = 0.211325; and log-mean 2 log(1-p), which gives the quenched (typical) threshold (3/2)(1-p)^2 = 1 at p = 0.183503. As a calibration control for statistics on the unbiased Bernoulli convolution at 2/3 (the same ratio, frequencies and arithmetic, only the weights changed): below p* the measure is singular and a detection is expected; above 0.2113 the main term decays and a pass is expected; between 0.1403 and 0.2113 the measure has dimension one while the main term already diverges, so a reading there means nothing - controls belong at p <= 0.12 and p >= 0.35. Unlike the Pisot control lambda = 1/phi, where one localised cell forces the reading a priori, the absence of such a cell at ratio 3/2 is Mahler's open problem on ||(3/2)^m xi||, so the control's genuineness rests on an empirical extensiveness test: a flat per-step rate means one cell forces the reading, a wobbling rate means a real measurement (flat to 0.0005 at 1/phi from K = 8; wobbling by 0.028 at the unbiased 2/3).

Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be a probability space (a finite or even $\sigma$-finite measure suffices here), $T: X \to X$ measure-preserving, $f \in L^1(\mu)$ real-valued. Write $S_n f = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f \circ T^k$ and $F_N = \max_{1 \le n \le N} S_n f$. Then
$$\int_{\{F_N > 0\}} f\,d\mu \ \ge\ 0 \quad \text{for every } N \ge 1,$$
and consequently $\int_{\{\sup_n S_n f > 0\}} f\,d\mu \ge 0$. The maximal inequality follows: for $\alpha > 0$, $\mu\big(\{ \sup_{n} \tfrac{1}{n} S_n f > \alpha \}\big) \le \tfrac{1}{\alpha} \int_{\{\sup_n S_n f / n > \alpha\}} f\,d\mu \le \tfrac{1}{\alpha}\|f\|_1$ (apply the first statement to $f - \alpha$; for the last step in infinite measure one needs $f \ge 0$ or $\mu$ finite, since $\int (f - \alpha)$ over the set is where $\mu$ finite is used). This is the only analytic input needed for the pointwise ergodic theorem. It fails if $T$ does not preserve $\mu$.
T is measure-preserving
f is integrable
the sets are defined through the partial sums S_n f, n >= 1

body: Measured on a frame spread in three dimensions (the 8 sign vectors divided by sqrt 8, leverages 3/8, two irrational rotations), comb laws with N teeth of width 1/N at the integers, Gaussian cells, lattice part exact: the two-dimensional frame integral J_2(kappa) = int int |E e^{i(yL + tV + kappa LP)}| dy dt that the Theorem H route needs grows with N at every fixed kappa (kappa = 1: 15.4, 18.6, 23.4, 28.2, 32.5 at N = 4..12; untwisted value about 32/N). The hub-conditioned integral with twist proportional to the partner frequency grows too. The mixed norms int dt ||T(., t)||_{L^p(dy)} with p >= 3/2 stay flat on one rotation but grow for every p <= 2 on the other. For fine combs of bounded range (teeth of width 1/N at spacing 2/N in [0, 2]) all of these stay flat, so the growth is driven by the spread of the laws. The density of the single hub 2 X_h (L + beta) + V^2 + 2 eps L P falls with N and does not feel eps, and its characteristic function is integrable uniformly in eps (fine combs: |eta|^{3/2}|phi_Q| in [1.0, 1.4], integral 3.0 at eps = 0, 0.03, 0.003). Lesson: every bound that takes moduli of the twisted light transform at a fixed hub value and a fixed Fresnel frequency loses; a proof must pair the hub with the light transform before any modulus, or be real-variable.

C009 v1. Target 2. Kind: bound. Status: proof (unaudited).
This is a necessary compatibility condition for a proposed oracle architecture,
not a proof of either target. No novelty priority is claimed.

## Setup and statement

Use the C006 v2 protected blocks, h_n=2^floor(n/2), M_n=2^(n^2).
At every unprotected input y put exactly one accepted n^2-bit witness u_y.
These locations may be arbitrary, but are fixed independently of the protected
bits and locations, including after other independent background data is fixed.
The auxiliary oracle obeys the same conditional full-reference condition:
after fixing other blocks and independent background it has at most 2^a(n)
references independent of this block's protected variables, with a polynomial.
Selection among references may depend arbitrarily on protected variables.

Fix a deterministic uniform polynomial-time oracle procedure R(y) returning
an n^2-bit candidate or failure. Define Z_R(n) as the number of unprotected
inputs y at length n for which R(y) fails to return an accepted witness.
R may query both the witness table and the selected auxiliary oracle. Fix
any positive integer-valued polynomial upper bound p(n)>=1.

There is one uniform efficiently weighted family W_R such that, for every
fixed uniform polynomial-time sampler S, almost surely the following two
events hold simultaneously at only finitely many n:

  (i) S approximates W_R at L(n)=1+n+n^2 within
      TV tau_n=1/[100(p(n)+1)L(n)];
 (ii) Z_R(n)<=p(n) h_n.

The probability-one set can be chosen simultaneously for all R, all such
polynomial bounds p, and all S, by countability. Hence on this set, IF C003 A
holds, every such R has Z_R(n)/h_n eventually greater than every polynomial.
This is a conditional necessity, not an existence claim for such an oracle.

## Efficient residual filter

Let G_R(y)=1 when R(y) does not return an accepted witness; verify every
candidate with the actual witness table, treating malformed outputs as failure.
At distinguished length L(n), give dummy 0^L weight 1 and word 1 y w
weight 4 iff G_R(y)=1 and (y,w) is accepted. Give all other words weight zero.
At other lengths give just the dummy weight 1. R is fixed code, so this is a
single uniform polynomial-time oracle weight family. It does not recognize H_n
and it does not contain S or a description/compiler for every weight family.

Write d=p(n)+1 and h=h_n. On event (ii), at most p(n)h unprotected accepted
words remain, and at most h protected accepted words remain. Therefore the
number N of accepted nondummy words in W_R is at most d h. Each has exact
target mass v=4/(1+4N). No assumption about their distribution over inputs or
their dependence on the selected auxiliary oracle has been made.

## A learner combines R with samples of the residual law

For analysis, evaluate R on every input in the fixed protected set H_n and
verify its output. Set the corresponding guessed bit to one on a successful
verification, otherwise zero. This has no false positive protected bits.
It may use H_n as fixed information: C006 allows unrestricted computation and
fixed descriptions independent of the sampled bits and locations. The weight
family and S do not get H_n. Any protected yes bit not found by this step has
its unique witness in the support of W_R, by the definition of G_R.

If N=0 there are no such missed yes bits, so this learner already recovers the
whole bit vector. Otherwise suppose (i) and (ii) hold for this fixed oracle.
Call a supported word bad if S emits it with probability less than v/2.
The positive-part characterization of total variation gives

    number of bad words < 2 tau_n/v
       = tau_n (1+4N)/2 <= (1+4dh)/(200dL) < h/8.

Every other supported word has S-probability at least

    v/2 >= 2/(1+4dh) >= 1/(3dh).

Run S independently t=6dh(n+2) times. Verify each output's residual filter
and witness predicate and set its protected bit to one if it is accepted.
Background outputs can simply be ignored when restricting to the fixed
protected coordinates. At most h good protected witnesses need be observed.
The probability that any is missed is at most

    h (1-1/(3dh))^t <= h exp(-2(n+2))
       <= h 2^(-2(n+2)) <= 1/16.

Thus on each oracle satisfying (i) and (ii), the learner guesses the protected
vector within floor(h/8) errors with probability at least 15/16 over the
independent S tapes. This remains valid even if R found some protected yes
witnesses: those were recorded before sampling. No assumption that R fails
on every protected input is needed.

## Unconditional direct-product bound and quantifiers

Let r(n) bound witness queries for R plus verifying its output, and let s(n)
bound witness queries per S call at this inverse-polynomial accuracy. These
are polynomials for fixed R,S,p. The learner uses at most

    Q <= h r(n) + 6dh(n+2)[s(n)+r(n)+1]

direct witness queries. Fix its random tapes, other blocks, and all independent
background information. C006 v2 followed by the C007 Hamming-ball union bound
gives unconditional success probability at most

    2^(a(n)-h/4) (1+1/M_n)^Q <= 2^(a(n)-h/4) exp(Q/M_n).

Average over the tapes and independent data. In particular, do NOT condition
the protected posterior on the residual-count event or the accuracy event.
Since success is at least 15/16 on their intersection, its probability is at
most (16/15) times this displayed upper bound. It is summable in n: Q is h
times a polynomial, Q/M_n tends to zero, and a(n)<=h/8 eventually. Tail union
bounds imply that intersection occurs only finitely often almost surely.

There are countably many fixed uniform R and S and integer-coefficient
polynomial upper bounds p. Taking the intersection of these probability-one
statements is legitimate, even when their codes are selected after O.
Now suppose A holds for an oracle in this intersection. For each fixed R,p,
A supplies a uniform sampler for W_R at the inverse-polynomial schedule
tau_n above (use any polynomial in L dominating 100(p(n)+1)L; n<=L).
An arbitrarily smaller error also suffices. This sampler is eventually accurate.
The intersection bound forces Z_R(n)>p(n)h_n eventually. Taking all p proves
the conditional superpolynomial ratio claim. A does not imply a uniform
compiler over R, and none has been used.

## Consequence and precise remaining gap

A sparse-background inversion interface cannot simply return a valid witness
at every unprotected input while ignoring the protected inputs. Its verified
failure predicate would be a residual filter with Z_R=0, contradicting the
necessary condition together with A almost surely. Even polynomially many
background failures per protected input are insufficient. A compatible
construction needs a much larger background failure set for every fixed
efficient deterministic search routine, despite requiring accurate law sampling.

This does not refute C003 B: B gives randomized average-case distributional
inversion, not a deterministic routine with the residual guarantee assumed
here. A residual set much larger than h_n can still have negligible fraction
among all 2^n inputs. Whether a hierarchy of such residual sets supports all
oracle-dependent weight families and inversion maps remains OPEN. No common
oracle, independent audit, formal proof certificate, or scored movement is claimed.

Sources: local C006 v2 and C007 v1. The new step is combining verified search

For n in [0, 2] and x = 1/sqrt(2 + sqrt(2 - n)) the honeycomb O(n) loop-model interface converges to SLE(kappa) with kappa = 4 pi/(2 pi - arccos(-n/2)); for x above that value it converges to SLE(kappa) with kappa = 4 pi/arccos(-n/2). Known only for n = 1 at the critical point (site percolation, Smirnov) and for the n = 0 boundary in the trivial sense. Source: Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012, Conjecture 3.7, p. 25. Status notes: The n = 0 critical case is the SLE(8/3) conjecture for SAW (the source's Conjecture 1.5), which the Codex campaign already records as P0003 (hexagonal SAW scaling limit); this record covers n in (0,2] and the dense phase, and the n = 0 dense case (x above critical, kappa = 8).
Posed in Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

For every prime power q = p^k there is a field with exactly q elements, unique up to isomorphism, denoted F_q; it is the splitting field of x^q - x over F_p. Every finite field has prime-power order, and the multiplicative group F_q* is cyclic of order q - 1.

body: [Theorem T:half-space-log-gamma-horizon of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $\theta > 0$ and $\alpha \in (-\theta, \infty)$. Then there exists a random function $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}$, such that $-\log \mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}\in \mathcal{D}((-\theta, \alpha \wedge 0], \mathbb{Z}, \alpha \wedge 0)$, and for any finite set $I = (\gamma_1 < \cdots < \gamma_k) \subset (-\theta, \alpha \wedge 0]$, the restriction $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}|_I$ is equal in law to the half-space log-gamma joint stationary measure given in Proposition (P:stationary-existence of the paper). In particular, $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}$ gives a coupling of all the log-gamma joint stationary measures identified above. We call $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}$ the \textbf{(extended) half-space log-gamma horizon}.
title: Theorem T:half-space-log-gamma-horizon of arXiv:2604.10020

Note that  $\incr([0,1];[0,1])$ coincides with the class $\sP$ from Section~\ref{s:intro}.
title: Definition 94 of arXiv:2608.29416

Let U ⊂ C be open, let A ⊂ U have no accumulation point in U (so A is discrete and closed in U, hence at most countable), and for each a in A let P_a(z) = Σ_{j=1}^{m_a} c_{a,j} (z - a)^{-j} be a given nonzero polynomial in 1/(z - a) with no constant term and finite m_a ≥ 1. Then there exists a function f meromorphic on U, holomorphic on U minus A, whose set of poles is exactly A and whose principal part at each a in A is P_a, i.e. f - P_a extends holomorphically across a. Any two such functions differ by a function holomorphic on all of U, so the general solution is f + h with h holomorphic on U. A standard instance is the pole structure of the Gamma function: U = C, A = {0, -1, -2, ...}, with prescribed principal part (-1)^n / (n! (z + n)) at the point z = -n for n = 0, 1, 2, ....
U ⊂ C is open
A ⊂ U has no accumulation point in U
each prescribed principal part is a finite polynomial in 1/(z-a) without constant term

Owner-own-work draft, T419-C032 v1, proof (unaudited), novelty unresolved. Let r>=2, N>=1024r(r+1), p=N+r and G=[Q Z] be r-by-p iid standard Gaussian with r-by-r signal block Q. Put M=GG^T, S0=M^(-1/2)Q, w0=sigma_min(S0)^2 and delta=||M/p-I||_op. For any 0<mu<=1, the event 0<delta<1/2 and delta>(mu^2/2)sqrt(w0) has probability at least (3/64)(1/(256r))^(r^2), uniformly in N. For the reduced flow Ydot=M^(-1)Y H(I-Y^T Y), H=diag(lambda_i^2,0), lambda_i in [mu,1], a worst-case sufficient condition preserving minimum signal-overlap square above w0/4 is gamma<(mu^2/2)sqrt(w0), gamma=delta/(1-delta). The event violates that condition even as input dimension grows. Thus Gram concentration alone cannot justify arbitrary-confidence convergence through this sufficient criterion. This is a certificate failure, not optimization failure or a target solution. The proof uses independent signal/null Gaussian blocks, exact second/fourth moments, Paley-Zygmund and a Frobenius variance bound; no simulation or asymptotic approximation.
Gaussian G, integers r>=2,N>=1024r(r+1),p=N+r; 0<mu<=1
Weighted-Stiefel reduced equation with fixed row Gram M and normalized positive target spectrum in [mu,1]
Only the stated worst-case overlap criterion is rejected; no convergence counterexample or target-progress claim

Kind: route-failure. Target1. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty or target-progress claim. This tests one sufficient criterion, not LoRA convergence, and builds on rather than reproves C030's rank-crossing obstruction.

## Proposed criterion

Write p=N+r, G=[Q Z] with r-by-r signal block Q and r-by-N null block Z. Let M=GG^T, Y0=M^(-1/2)G, S0 its first r columns and w0=sigma_min(S0)^2. Let

    delta=||M/p-I||_op<1, gamma=delta/(1-delta).

For the reduced Stiefel flow Y'=M^(-1)Y H(I-Y^T Y), H=diag(lambda_i^2,0) with lambda_i in [mu,1], set S=Y[:,1:r], W=S^T S, w=lambda_min(W), t=lambda_max(W)<=1. Its exact signal equation is

    S'=M^(-1) S D(I-S^T S), D=diag(lambda_i^2).

Write p M^(-1)=I+K with ||K||<=gamma. For every unit minimum eigenvector v of W, direct differentiation gives

    v^T W'v >= (2(1-w)/p) [mu^2 w-gamma sqrt(w t)].

Indeed S^T M^(-1)S=(W+S^T K S)/p. The main term is w v^T Dv, while the error is bounded by gamma ||S Dv|| ||Sv|| <=gamma sqrt(t w). This works for repeated minimum eigenvalues by taking the minimum over their unit eigenvectors.

In particular gamma<(mu^2/2)sqrt(w0) is a sufficient barrier for w>=w0/4: the lower derivative is strictly positive at a potential first crossing, unless w0=0. The non-strict version follows by continuity or a slightly smaller barrier. This route would need a high-probability guarantee of this criterion; a claim merely that delta->0 is insufficient because w0 also tends to zero.

## Uniform positive-probability failure of the sufficient criterion

For every r>=2, N>=1024r(r+1), and every 0<mu<=1, iid Gaussian G has

    P[0<delta<1/2 and delta>(mu^2/2)sqrt(w0)]
      >= (3/64) (1/(256r))^(r^2) >0.

Consequently, without further ideas, this criterion cannot deliver arbitrary confidence 1-rho merely by taking p large. The lower bound is extremely small and is an obstruction to the certificate, not a lower bound on optimization failure. No Gaussian asymptotic approximation is used.

Put epsilon=1/(128r). Restrict all r^2 entries of Q to [-epsilon,epsilon], an event A of probability at least (epsilon/2)^(r^2). To justify the bound, the standard Gaussian density exceeds1/4 on [-epsilon,epsilon] (use sqrt(2pi)<3 and exp(-epsilon^2/2)>3/4). Except on a null subset Q is nonsingular. Also ||Q||_F<=r epsilon and |(QQ^T)12|<=r epsilon^2.

Independently, let U=(ZZ^T)12=sum_(j=1)^N Z_1j Z_2j. Gaussian integration by parts gives E Z^2=1 and E Z^4=3, so

    E U^2=N, E U^4=3N^2+6N.

The elementary Paley-Zygmund inequality (obtained by Cauchy-Schwarz on the event X>theta EX) applied to X=U^2 yields

    P[|U|>=sqrt(N)/2] >= (9/16)/(3+6/N) >=1/16.

Entrywise moment calculation also gives

    E||ZZ^T-NI||_F^2=N r(r+1).

Markov's inequality therefore bounds P[||ZZ^T-NI||_op>N/4] by 16r(r+1)/N<=1/64. The intersection B of the two good events has probability at least3/64, with no independence assumption between them. A and B are independent, because Q and Z are independent column blocks.

On A intersect B,

    lambda_min(M)>=3N/4,
    delta >= |M12|/p >= (sqrt(N)/2-r epsilon^2)/p >=sqrt(N)/(4p),
    sqrt(w0) <=||M^(-1/2)Q||_F <=2r epsilon/sqrt(3N).

N>=r and the displayed assumptions imply

    delta/sqrt(w0) >=sqrt(3) N/(8p r epsilon)
                       >=sqrt(3)/(16r epsilon)=8sqrt(3)>mu^2/2.

The ratio is well defined off the null singular-Q set. Finally

    delta <= [N/4+r^2 epsilon^2+r]/p <1/2.

These inequalities prove the probability claim. Since gamma>=delta, the proposed inverse-Gram criterion fails on this event too. Its failure persists for arbitrarily large p, despite the usual unconditioned relative Gram concentration.

## Interpretation and provenance

This does not say that no other perturbation argument works. It rejects the specific worst-case minimum-overlap barrier with arbitrary-confidence Gaussian initialization, even at large aspect ratio. A successful quantitative argument could exploit correlations, avoid minimum-overlap barriers entirely, or control passage through their zero sets as allowed by C030. Both whole targets remain open.

Primary-source discovery for the route: papers/openalex_gram_perturbation.json lists a generalized-Stiefel preconditioning paper (arXiv:1902.01635). Metadata alone was not used as a theorem or as evidence that this target is solved. The argument above is direct elementary Gaussian moment algebra and the C029 reduced equation. scripts/check_C032_constants.py checks rational moment and probability constants, not a stochastic simulation or the whole proof. [Lemma 22 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $f:\Rsf^m\to\Rsf$ be a smooth, compactly supported function and let $\varepsilon, \tilde{\varepsilon}, \delta, \zeta\in [0,\infty)$ and $a,b, \tilde{a},\tilde{b}\in\Rsf^m$ be such that 
	\[
		|b-a|\leq \varepsilon, 
			\quad 
		|\tilde{b}-\tilde{a}|\leq \tilde{\varepsilon}, 
			\quad 
		|\tilde{a}-a|\leq \delta, 
			\quad\mbox{and}\quad 
		|\tilde{b}-\tilde{a} - (b-a)| \leq \zeta.
	\]
Let also $T_0,T_1: \Rsf^m\times\Rsf^m\to\Rsf$ be defined by 
	\begin{align*}
		& T_0(x,y):= f(y)-f(x),\\
		& T_1(x,y):= f(y)-f(x)- \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^j}(x)(y^j-x^j)
	\end{align*}
for $x,y\in\Rsf^m$. Then
	\[
		\left|T_0(a,b)\right|  \lesssim \varepsilon 
		\quad\mbox{and}\quad
		|T_0(\tilde{a},\tilde{b})-T_0(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon(\delta + \zeta) + \zeta,
	\]
and
	\[
		 |T_1(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon^2
		 \quad \mbox{and}\quad 
		 |T_1(\tilde{a},\tilde{b})-T_1(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon^2(\delta + \zeta) + (\varepsilon + \tilde{\varepsilon})\zeta
	\]
where the constants are non-decreasing functions of $C^1$, $C^2$, $C^2$, and $C^3$ norm of $f$, respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
