{"artifact_digest":"sha256:43dfff679777bde2aec8b50d70caba065aa1734605bc7baf904adc3af97ec957","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/43/43dfff679777bde2aec8b50d70caba065aa1734605bc7baf904adc3af97ec957.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ca1a9b2beabce8a013f230ad19d33675ba3eca93d0d4f7b8d360d4389fe3f8cf","bundle_entry_key":"small-beta-draft","bundle_id":"population.t323-symmetric-attention-frontier-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"spherical self-attention dynamics","draft":"w696/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:analysis.dynamical_systems:t323-aligned-indefinite-attention-small-beta-consensus-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Signature-(2,1) aligned attention: almost-everywhere consensus at small beta

T323-SMALLBETA-001 v2. Proof (unaudited). Kind narrowed; target 2.
This version includes repeated positive eigenvalues. Version 1 remains saved.

## Theorem and exact scope
Let n>=1 be finite and let V be a real symmetric 3x3 matrix with signature
(2,1). Write its eigenvalues lambda_1>=lambda_2>0>lambda_3, and let E_top
be its largest-eigenvalue eigenspace. Consider the full, self-inclusive,
normalized projected attention flow on M=(S^2)^n, with Q^T K=V:

 dot x_i = P_i sum_j exp(beta x_i^T V x_j) Vx_j / Z_i,
 Z_i = sum_j exp(beta x_i^T V x_j),  P_i=I-x_i x_i^T.

There exists epsilon(V,n)>0 such that, for every 0<beta<epsilon(V,n),
for product-volume-almost every initial configuration, every token
converges to the same unit vector u in E_top. In particular, if the top
eigenvalue is simple, the only possible generic limits are consensus at
+e_1 or -e_1. For a repeated top eigenvalue the limit is a single point
of the top-plane unit circle, not necessarily a predetermined orientation.
The same assertion holds for the unnormalized flow, omitting Z_i.

This is not a result for arbitrary Q,K, every beta, or uniformity in n.
The exceptional null set may depend on beta. No numerical lower bound on
epsilon is asserted. The source paper already gives local consensus
stability; the candidate increment is the complete almost-everywhere
small-beta classification for the indefinite family.

## 1. Energy and its regular zero-beta limit
For X=(x_i), S=sum_i x_i, set

 F_beta(X) = (1/(2 beta)) sum_ij [exp(beta x_i^T V x_j)-1],
 F_0(X) = (1/2) S^T V S.

Expanding the exponential shows joint real analyticity in beta and X near
beta=0, and uniform C^r convergence on compact M for each finite r.
Symmetry of V, including the diagonal terms i=j, gives

 grad_i F_beta=P_i sum_j exp(beta x_i^T Vx_j) Vx_j.

The normalized dynamics is its gradient ascent for the positive analytic
metric g_beta(U,W)=sum_i Z_i <u_i,w_i>; the unnormalized dynamics uses
the product metric. This is the known aligned gradient construction in
2312.10794 section 3.4. At beta=0, g_0 is n times the product metric.

## 2. Complete critical landscape at beta=0
For tangent U=(u_i), W=sum_i u_i, differentiating along product geodesics
produces the background-product-metric Hessian identity

 Hess F_0[U,U] = W^T V W - sum_i (x_i^T V S)||u_i||^2.       (H)

Criticality is P_i VS=0 for all i. The positive spectral space E_+ has
dimension two, so E_+ intersect x_i^perp always has a nonzero vector with
strictly positive V-quadratic form.

If S=0, take only one nonzero u_i in this intersection. Formula (H) is
u_i^T V u_i>0. Thus EVERY zero-mean critical point is a strict saddle.

If S!=0, invertibility gives h=VS!=0. Criticality implies
x_i=s_i u, s_i in {+1,-1}, u=h/||h||. If signs are mixed, choose i with
s_i=-1 and only u_i nonzero, again in E_+ intersect u^perp. Then (H) is
u_i^T V u_i + ||h|| ||u_i||^2>0. Every such point is a strict saddle.

If all tokens coincide at x, criticality says Vx=lambda x. When
lambda<lambda_1, a unit v in E_top is orthogonal to x. Taking every
u_i=v makes (H)=n^2(lambda_1-lambda)>0. Thus the only critical points
without a positive Hessian direction belong to

 C={ (u,...,u): u in E_top, ||u||=1 }.

C is two points when lambda_1>lambda_2 and a circle when they coincide.
At any point of C, diagonalize V in a basis starting with u. For each
transverse eigenvector with eigenvalue mu, the n-coordinate Hessian block
is mu 11^T - n lambda_1 I_n. Its eigenvalues are n(mu-lambda_1)
on the common mode and -n lambda_1 on the n-1 disagreement modes.
The only zero modes are common modes with mu=lambda_1, precisely T C.
Every normal mode is strictly negative. Thus C is a compact Morse-Bott
maximum manifold (in the simple case, two nondegenerate maxima).

## 3. No additional critical points can enter a neighborhood of C
C remains an exact critical manifold for every beta, since the weighted
sum at consensus is proportional to Vu=lambda_1 u. At C, the first
variation of every score x_i^T Vx_j vanishes on T M. Therefore

 Hess F_beta|_C = exp(beta lambda_1) Hess F_0|_C.

In particular its kernel is T C and its normal Hessian is strictly negative.
For clarity, the local isolation conclusion follows without asserting a
general persistence theorem: take tubular bundle coordinates (a,z) near C,
where a parametrizes C and z is normal. Since C is critical,
partial_z F_beta(a,0)=0 for all a and beta. The derivative in z of this
normal-gradient equation at beta=0,z=0 is the invertible negative normal
Hessian. The implicit function theorem gives z=0 as its unique nearby
solution, jointly for a and small beta. Compactness of C supplies a finite
collection of such charts and fixed U containing C, and eta>0, in which
all critical points of F_beta lie on C whenever |beta|<eta. The sphere's
normal bundle need not be trivial; this is a finite local-chart argument.

## 4. All critical points outside C stay strict saddles for small beta
K=M minus U is compact. If the conclusion failed arbitrarily near zero,
there would exist beta_j down to zero and critical X_j in K with no
positive Hessian direction. Pass to X_j->X_* in K. Uniform C^2 convergence
implies grad F_0(X_*)=0 and Hess F_0(X_*) negative semidefinite, measured
in a fixed background metric. Step 2 forces X_* in C, contrary to K
being disjoint from U. Thus some epsilon>0 works simultaneously for all
critical points: for 0<beta<epsilon the only critical points without a
positive Hessian direction are exactly C.

This compactness step gives a genuine interval, not a beta depending on
the starting point. It does not give a numerical threshold. At critical
points Hessian inertia is independent of the positive Riemannian metric.

## 5. Trajectory convergence and the null exceptional set
For each fixed beta in that interval, compactness and the real analytic
Lojasiewicz gradient inequality give convergence of every gradient
trajectory to one critical point. The metric g_beta is positive analytic;
there is no issue from normalization. A local inequality near a critical
accumulation point bounds remaining arc length by an energy gap to a
positive power; taking a sufficiently late entry traps the trajectory
there and makes it Cauchy. This also applies to a critical manifold: a
single limiting point is obtained, rather than convergence merely in
distance to C.

Geshkovski et al., 2312.10794 Appendix A Lemma A.1, states that on a
compact Riemannian manifold the initial points whose gradient-ascent
trajectory converges to a strict saddle form a volume-zero set. It does
not require isolated saddles. Apply it to F_beta with g_beta. Its volume
and product volume have positive smooth density ratios bounded above
and below on M, so their null sets agree. All remaining limits lie in C
by Step 4. This proves the statement. For USA, repeat with the product
metric throughout.

## Provenance and limits
The aligned metric and the convergence/avoidance architecture are known.
The Hessian block at simple consensus reproduces the known Kuehn-Yoon
2604.26085 Proposition 5.1; it is not claimed as new. Their Theorem 6.1
requires a common-sign initial cone and dominant absolute eigenvalue;
Theorem 6.4 requires negative definiteness and n=2. Neither supplies the
claimed almost-everywhere signature-(2,1) small-beta conclusion.

Candidate new step: classify EVERY beta=0 critical point using the
2-dimensional positive spectral space, and transport this landscape by
compactness plus normal isolation of C. No claim of independent audit
or exhaustive literature priority is made. Relevant current searches
and primary sources are recorded in logs/lit1.json through lit6.json
and SOURCES.jsonl. Full arbitrary-beta classification remains open here.

Verification: scripts/check_small_beta.py checks (H) exactly on rational
sphere jets, all collinear sign patterns for n<=7, and the full symbolic
n=2 normalized-flow Jacobian with self-indices. These are algebra checks,
not replacements for the analytic proof or an independent audit.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:eb3a4a4ce32416e4908cfb07f2258aeeecc15869d8813d03e2492f8805949d7b","revision_digest":"sha256:603878cb10d54ef884ffb295698f9ab2938694ea9441e66a020ae9a007d38883","source_id":"owner-own-work:w696:T323-SMALLBETA-001:v2","source_revision":"v2-as-read-2026-10-20","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Def 18 of arXiv:2604.24189, 'Malliavin calculus and densities for chaos-driven stochastic differential equations'] The one-dimensional Hermite process $Z^{H,q}=\left(Z_t^{H,q}\right)_{t \in \R_+}$ of order $q\geq 1$ and self-similarity parameter $H \in\left(\frac{1}{2}, 1\right)$ is defined by
\begin{align}
	Z^{H,q}_t=I_q(L_t^{H, q}) \qquad \text{where} \qquad L_t^{H, q}(\xi)=c(H, q) \int_0^t \prod_{j=1}^q\left(s-\xi_j\right)_{+}^{H_0-\frac{3}{2}} ds,
\end{align}
$$
H_0=1+\frac{H-1}{q} \in\left(1-\frac{1}{2 q}, 1\right), \quad\text{and}\quad c(H, q)=\sqrt{\frac{H(2 H-1)}{q!\,\beta^q\left(H_0-\frac{1}{2}, 2-2 H_0\right)}}.
$$
Here $\beta$ stands for the Beta function and we use the convention, for each $(\theta, \alpha) \in \R^2$,
		\[\theta^{\alpha}_+:=\left\{ \begin{array}{rl}\theta^{\alpha}, & \text{if }\theta>0,\\ 0, &  \text{otherwise}. \end{array}\right. \]
title: Definition 18 of arXiv:2604.24189

[Theorem thm: main result of arXiv:2609.02073, 'Existence of closed non-planar $p$-elasticae'] Let $p\in (1,\infty)$. Then there exists a countable family of closed non-planar $p$-elasticae in $\R^3$.

Let X, Y and Z be random variables with finitely many values on one probability space, with Z = f(Y) almost surely for some function f. Then H(X | Z) - H(X | Y) = H(Y | Z) - H(Y | X, Z), and both sides equal the conditional mutual information I(X; Y | Z). Entropies use natural logarithms with 0 ln 0 = 0, and a conditional entropy averages only over conditioning values of positive probability; dividing every term by ln 2 gives the same statement in bits.

[Lemma 40 (Equivalence of intrinsic and fixed-chart norms) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(n\), \(m\geq2\), \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), \(\Lambda\geq1\), and \(L>0\).
Suppose that
\(\PBG_m(s;\Lambda;[a,b])\) holds and \(b-a\leq L\).  Let
\(\|\cdot\|_{X_{s,{\mathrm{fc}}}^m[a,b]}\) and
\(\|\cdot\|_{Y_{s,{\mathrm{fc}}}^m[a,b]}\) denote the suprema of the Euclidean
component norms in the fixed lifted atlas supplied by
Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-parabolic-atlas}.  Then there is
\(C=C(n,m,\sigma,\Lambda,L)\) such that every deck-invariant tensor \(U\)
satisfies
\begin{align}
 C^{-1}\|U\|_{X_s^m[a,b]}
 &\leq \|U\|_{X_{s,{\mathrm{fc}}}^m[a,b]}
 \leq C\|U\|_{X_s^m[a,b]},                                      \\
 C^{-1}\|U\|_{Y_s^m[a,b]}
 &\leq \|U\|_{Y_{s,{\mathrm{fc}}}^m[a,b]}
 \leq C\|U\|_{Y_s^m[a,b]}.                                      
\end{align}
The analogous comparison holds for every spatial
\(C^{k,\sigma}\)-norm with \(0\leq k\leq m\).  For tensors on the universal
cover that are not deck-invariant, the same local comparison holds with the

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, The layer distribution of the random recursive tree and the minimum of the Poisson-weighted infinite tree (2026). The layer of a vertex of a tree is the number of rounds of leaf removal after which it is a leaf. Stepanyants, Krapivsky, Hartle and Krioukov (arXiv:2608.04303) showed that the limiting proportion of vertices at layer at least k in a random recursive tree is lbar_k = int_0^inf s_k(y) e^(-y) dy with s_0 = 1 and s_i(y) = 1 - exp(-int_0^y s_(i-1)), and conjectured that the proportion l_k at layer exactly k is exp[-k/e - (3/(2e)) log k - O(1)]. The paper proves lbar_k e^(k/e) k^(3/(2e)) -> C_* in (0, inf) and l_k e^(k/e) k^(3/(2e)) -> (1 - e^(-1/e)) C_*. The recursion is the distribution function of the minimal position M_k in generation k of the Poisson-weighted infinite tree, so lbar_k = E exp(-M_k), and the asymptotics follow from Addario-Berry and Ford (Ann. Appl. Probab. 2013) and Aidekon (Ann. Probab. 2013). It also proves the layer half of their Conjecture 2: in every finite tree the largest layer is floor(diameter/2), and for the random recursive tree on n vertices it is e log n - (3/2) log log n + O_P(1); the largest rank is not treated. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/rrt-layer-tail (commit 0f20604c8b2b). Not refereed.
title: Layer distribution of the random recursive tree: lbar_k e^(k/e) k^(3/(2e)) converges, proving Conjecture 1 of Stepanyants-Krapivsky-Hartle-Krioukov (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/rrt-layer-tail)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Identify what the log n scaling comes from and whether it survives without (POS1). Result: The log n factor at delta = 1 comes from the total progeny of the critical branching process with migration delta = 1 having a tail n^{-1/2} with a logarithmic correction, so that the time to make n right excursions is of order n^2 log n, equivalently the maximum after time t is of order sqrt(t)/log t... the source's scaling sqrt n log n for X_{[nt]} reflects the backtracking being negligible at that scale. Under (6.2) the migration has finite mean and the critical tail should persist (same mechanism as C0134). Removing (POS1) allows left-pushing cookies; the walk then has non-negligible backtracking below its maximum, and the limit of X itself (not only its maximum) may differ from the running maximum; the maximum process S should still converge to the running maximum of Brownian motion since the backtracking affects only the difference S - X, whose scale is the length of a typical left excursion, of order sqrt(n) (diffusive) which is o(sqrt n log n). So the expected answer is: the theorem persists under (6.2), and without (POS1) the maximum still converges but X - S is O(sqrt n), negligible at the sqrt n log n scale, so the conclusion for X persists too. The proof would need the branching-process comparison for two-sided cookies (the branching process with migration then has both immigration and emigration), which is the source's [KM11]-type framework; not carried out. Key identity: Backtracking scale sqrt(n) is negligible against the sqrt(n) log n scale of the maximum at delta = 1. Obstruction: Two-sided branching-with-migration comparison not verified under (6.2) without (POS1).

\eea

Consider synchronous nearest-neighbor particle-hole parking on Z^d, d>=3, with iid P(eta=1)=P(eta=-1)=p, P(eta=0)=1-2p, 0<p<1/2, and stationary capacity-one holes. Let U_t be the source time-t departure odometer, H_t unfilled-hole indicators, m_t=E U_t(0), and K a finite nonempty set. In an auxiliary process empty K initially and make it permanently absorbing; let U_t^K be its odometer, J_t^K its killed-arrival count and Lambda_t^K=(1/(2d))sum_{s in K}sum_{y adjacent s}U_t^K(y). With full-space SRW capacity cap(K)=sum_{s in K}P_s(T_K^+=infinity), P(H_t(s)=1 for every s in K)=p^|K| P(J_t^K=0) and m_t cap(K)<=E Lambda_t^K=E J_t^K<=m_t |K|. {"artifact_digest":"sha256:c64667de6eb6a75f773ad2bfad23ff918b0607bbec7806df5de5579d3eada5b5","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/c6/c64667de6eb6a75f773ad2bfad23ff918b0607bbec7806df5de5579d3eada5b5.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:65d11978ec33d8be369af5a745954f6f209062ceba8da95bb586b599673e43ca","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c13","bundle_id":"population.i0005-sink-capacity-and-gradient-obstruction-005","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"parking and killed random walks","draft":"w661/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:particle-hole-finite-sink-capacity-flux-and-void-identity-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C13 v1: finite-sink void identity and capacity flux bound

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN singleton result, Bou-Rabee--
Panagiotis arXiv:2609.02820v1 (50)-(51); UNCHECKED prior appearance of
this finite-set extension. This is an actual parking-process statement.

Consider the source's synchronous nearest-neighbor particle-hole process
on Z^d, d>=3, with iid P(eta=1)=P(eta=-1)=p, P(eta=0)=1-2p,
0<p<1/2. Holes have capacity one and never move. Let H_t(x) indicate an
unfilled hole, U_t(x) count departures through the source's time-t
odometer convention, and m_t=E U_t(0). Let K be any nonempty finite set.

Define a sink process by setting eta(x)=0 on K and making K permanent
absorbing sinks: any arrival there is removed; no particle departs there.
Off K use the original iid law, fresh walks/instruction stacks and the
same coupling conventions as the source. Let U_t^K be its odometer,
J_t^K the number of arrivals killed on K in the rounds corresponding to
U_t^K, and

    Lambda_t^K=(1/(2d)) sum_{s in K} sum_{y adjacent s} U_t^K(y).

Terms with y in K vanish. Let cap(K)=sum_{s in K}P_s(T_K^+=infinity),
the full-space discrete-time SRW escape-probability capacity. Then

    P(H_t(s)=1 for all s in K)=p^|K| P(J_t^K=0),
    m_t cap(K) <= E Lambda_t^K = E J_t^K <= m_t |K|.

The expectation identity and sandwich do not provide a bound on the
zero-arrival probability. In particular they do not establish C9's Palm
clustering hypothesis.

## 1. Exact void identity

All sites in K must initially be holes for the joint-hole event. This
has probability p^|K| and is independent of the signs off K and the
walk instructions. Conditional on those initial holes, the original and
sink evolutions agree until the first arrival to K, because neither
system has an initial particle or a departure there. At that first
arrival an original hole is filled, so the joint-hole event has already
failed. Hence the joint survival event is precisely the no-arrival event
in the sink process, proving the formula. No independence between the
arrivals or between individual hole-survival events is asserted.

## 2. Monotone sink comparison and the expected odometer

Through a fixed finite time t, represent each permanent sink by sufficiently
many initial holes that its capacity cannot be exhausted by that time.
There are finitely many potentially relevant initial particles in the
t-neighborhood of K and at most one at each initial site; a deterministic
capacity greater than that finite number suffices. This modified initial
configuration is coordinatewise below the original one. The source's
Lemma 2.3 comparison gives, off K,

    U_t^K<=U_t,   A_t^K<=A_t,   H_t^K>=H_t

in its coupled construction. Therefore f(y):=E U_t^K(y) is bounded by
m_t, is zero on K, and equals m_t whenever dist(y,K)>t. The last assertion
uses finite propagation: initial changes on K cannot affect such a site
before the time horizon. Expectations are finite by the source's finite-time
odometer estimates.

At y outside K, mean particle-hole conservation, or the source's (19)
with mean-zero instruction noise, yields

    (P-I)f(y)=E[A_t^K(y)-H_t^K(y)]-E eta(y)<=0.

Here P is one SRW step, E eta(y)=0 off K, and the inequality uses the
monotone comparison and E A_t(y)=E H_t(y) in the original critical law.
Thus f is superharmonic outside K.

## 3. Escape lower bound and boundary flux

Stop a free walk from y outside K when it hits K or leaves a large finite
ball containing the t-neighborhood of K and y. Superharmonicity makes
f of the stopped walk a supermartingale; optional stopping is justified
by boundedness and the almost-sure finite exit time. On K its value is
zero, while on the outer boundary it is m_t. Consequently

    f(y)>=m_t P_y(exit before hitting K)
         >=m_t P_y(T_K=infinity).

Together with f<=m_t this gives

    E Lambda_t^K >= (m_t/(2d)) sum_{s in K}
                              sum_{y adjacent s}P_y(T_K=infinity)
                  =m_t sum_{s in K}P_s(T_K^+=infinity)
                  =m_t cap(K).

For neighbors inside K the escape probability is zero, so including them
in the sum causes no error. The upper bound follows from f<=m_t and
at most 2d neighbor terms per s: E Lambda_t^K<=m_t |K|.

## 4. Compensator identity

Reveal departure instructions chronologically, revealing each only after
the preceding history determines that it is used, exactly as in the
source's Lemma 4.3 and proof of (50)-(51). Every departure from y has
conditional probability deg_K(y)/(2d) of entering K. Its killed-arrival
indicator minus that probability is a martingale difference. Only finitely
many departures can reach K through time t; finite propagation and the
bounded initial number of particles provide a deterministic finite bound
on the number of such instructions. Summing expectations gives

    E J_t^K = (1/(2d))sum_y deg_K(y) E U_t^K(y)
            = E Lambda_t^K.

## Missing estimate

The singleton case is the source's (50)-(51). For two sites the full-space
capacity is 2/(g+G(x-y)), but the identity here involves a stopping-dependent
sink process, not an independent Poisson cloud. A capacity-sized expected
arrival count does not determine P(J_t^K=0). A lower-tail/no-arrival
comparison uniform in t and separation would be needed to turn this
extension into a two-hole survival bound. The d4 logarithmic influence
convolution remains an obstacle to such a concentration estimate.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:fb8fccc578ac5b2adf0f53a9de6f6cd4ac7f55cbcca4e34b8b2f482f45071155","revision_digest":"sha256:6096b4022996cb8ce77c7b68df1a708123697db85dc0015eb22f41b41b1f5be8","source_id":"owner-own-work:w661:I0005-C13:v1","source_revision":"v1; 2026-10-14T06:02:25.9473414+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Let $\xi_m$ be centered real entry laws (a single fixed law is allowed) satisfying, uniformly in $m$, $\operatorname{Var}(\xi_m)=1$, $\|f_{\xi_m}\|_\infty \le K$ for a density $f_{\xi_m}$, and $\mathbb{E}|\xi_m|^4 \le B < \infty$. Let $A_m \in \mathbb{R}^{N_m \times m}$ have iid entries with law $\xi_m$ and $N_m/m \to \gamma > 1$. For a surplus $r_m \ge 0$ put $M_{m,r_m}(A_m) = \min_{T \subset [N_m],\,|T| = m + r_m} \sigma_m((A_m)_T)$ and $k_m = r_m + 1$. If $k_m \log m = o(m)$, then $\frac{k_m}{m}\log M_{m,r_m}(A_m) \to -h(\gamma)$ in probability, where $h(\gamma) = \gamma\log\gamma - (\gamma-1)\log(\gamma-1)$. For fixed $r$ this reads $\frac{1}{m}\log M_{m,r} \to -h(\gamma)/(r+1)$. STATUS, recorded as the source states it and deliberately not upgraded: this is a CANDIDATE COMPLETE PROOF and still requires two independent audits before closure. It weakens the subgaussian hypothesis of the published version (arXiv:2608.07410, Yang-Wen-Shmalo) to a uniform fourth moment, but does NOT retain that paper's explicit $Ce^{-c\sqrt{m}}$ deviation rate or its compact-aspect-ratio uniform almost-sure formulation. The complex analogue, and its factor $1/2$, remain OPEN.

[Lem 244 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Assume that $L\ge1$ and that condition \eqref{e:deriv.p.bound} holds. Let $\vX\equiv \vX^N$ be the process defined by \eqref{e:X.decomp} and \eqref{e:Delta.X.Ising}. We then have
	\begin{align*}
	\max_{\sigma\in\{\RomII,\RomIII\}}
	\max_{a\in[M]}
	\E\bigg[ \max_{0\le d\le\dmax}
	X^\sigma(q_d,a)^8\bigg] 
	&\le L^{O(1)}\,,\\
	\max_{i\in[N]}
	\E\bigg[ \max_{0\le d\le\dmax}
	X^\Ising(q_d,i)^8\bigg] 
	&\le L^{O(1)}\,,
	\end{align*}
with the estimates holding uniformly in $N$.

\begin{proof} First consider $X^{\RomII}(q_d,a)$ for fixed $a\in[M]$, as a process indexed by time $q_d$ with $0\le d\le \dmax$. For the purposes of the proof let us abbreviate
		\[
	\frac{\Delta X^{\RomII}(q_d,a)}{[\delta_d p(q_d)]^{1/2}}
	\equiv 
	\mathfrak{y}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)
	\equiv \frac{(\bar{\bg}^a(q_d), \by(q_{d+1}))}{N^{1/2}}
	\,.
	\]
 Note that for fixed $a\in[M]$, $X^{\RomII}(q_d,a)$ (indexed by time $q_d$) is a martingale with respect to the filtration $\cG(q_d)$. Define a modified version similarly to the argument of  Lemma~\ref{l:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound}: let
	\begin{align}\nonumber
	\tilde{\bg}^a(q_d)
	&\equiv
	\bar{\bg}^a(q_d)
	\min\bigg\{1,\frac{2N^{1/2}}{\|\bar{\bg}^a(q_d)\|}\bigg\}\,,\\ \nonumber
	\tilde{\by}(q_{d+1})
	&\equiv
	\by(q_{d+1})
	\min\bigg\{1,\frac{2N^{1/2}}{\| \by(q_{d+1})\|}\bigg\}\,, \\
	\frac{\Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)}{[\delta_d p(q_d)]^{1/2}}
	&\equiv 
	\tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)
	\equiv \frac{(\tilde{\bg}^a(q_d), \tilde{\by}(q_{d+1}))}{N^{1/2}}
	\,.
	\end{align}
We note that we have
$\tilde{\bg}^a(q_d)=\bar{\bg}^a(q_d)$ and 
$\tilde{\by}(q_{d+1})=\by(q_{d+1})$ on the event
	\[\cE\equiv
	\cE(q_d,a) 
	\equiv \bigg\{ 
	\frac{\|\bar{\bg}^a(q_d)\|}{2N^{1/2}} \le1 ,
	\frac{\| \by(q_{d+1})\|}{2N^{1/2}} \le1
	\bigg\} \,.
	\]
It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:y.subgaus} and standard estimates that the event $\cE(q_d,a)$ fails with probability $e^{-cN}$. We then argue similarly as in the proof of \eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l4.step2}: the random variables $\mathfrak{y}^{\RomII}$ and $\tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomII}$ always have the same sign, with $|\tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomII}| \le |\mathfrak{y}^{\RomII}|$, and they agree on the event $\cE\equiv\cE(q_d,a)$: therefore,
	\begin{align}\nonumber
	&\bigg|\E\bigg[
	\Big(\mathfrak{y}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)
	- \tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)
	\Big)^8
	\bigg]\bigg|
	\le \E[\mathfrak{y}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)^8;\cE^c]
	\le \E[\mathfrak{y}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)^{16}]^{1/2}
	\P(\cE^c)^{1/2}\\
	&\qquad\le
	\frac{\E[ \|\bar{\bg}^a(q_d)\|^{32}]^{1/4}
		\E[ \|\by(q_{d+1})\|^{32} ]^{1/4}}{N^4}
	\P(\cE^c)^{1/2}
	\le e^{-cN}\,.
	
	\end{align}
Essentially the same argument as for \eqref{e:RomII.tilde.discrepancy.second.mmt.bound} also gives
	\beq
	\E\bigg[ \Big\| \by(q_{d+1})-\tilde{\by}(q_{d+1})\Big\|^8\bigg]
	\le \E\Big[ \| \by(q_{d+1})\|^8 ; \cE^c \Big]
	\le e^{-cN}
	\eeq
Now let $\tilde{X}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)$ be the process started from zero with increments $\Delta\tilde{X}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)$. (Again, we consider this for fixed $a\in[M]$, as a process indexed by time $q_d$.) It follows from  \eqref{e:RomII.tilde.discrepancy.second.mmt.bound} above that
	\beq
	\E\bigg[ \max_{0\le d\le \dmax}
	\Big(X^{\RomII}(q_d,a)
		-\tilde{X}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)\Big)^8\bigg]
	\le o_N(1)\,.
	\eeq
Note also that $\Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)$ is a Lipschitz function of the gaussian input, with Lipschitz constant $L^{O(1)}(\delta_d)^{1/2}$.
Next define the re-centered increments
	\begin{align*}
	\frac{\Delta \bar{X}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)}{[\delta_d p(q_d)]^{1/2}}
	&\equiv
	\frac{\Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)}{[\delta_d p(q_d)]^{1/2}}
	-\E\bigg[
	\frac{\Delta \tilde{X}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)}{[\delta_d p(q_d)]^{1/2}}
		\,\bigg|\, \cG(q_d)
		\bigg]\\
	&= \tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)
	-\E\Big[\tilde{\mathfrak{y}}^{\RomII}(q_d,a)
		\,\Big|\,\cG(q_d)\Big]\,.
	\end{align*}

Let Q_n = [-1/2,1/2]^n and 1 <= k <= n. For every k-dimensional linear subspace H of R^n: vol_k(Q_n \cap H) <= min{ (n/k)^{k/2}, 2^{(n-k)/2} }. The first bound is attained when k divides n (H spanned by the sums of the coordinate vectors over k disjoint blocks of size n/k); the second is the smaller one and is attained when k >= n/2. Equivalently, a central section of codimension m has volume <= min{ (n/(n-m))^{(n-m)/2}, 2^{m/2} }, with 2^{m/2} attained when m <= n/2. Probabilistic form: if U is uniform on Q_n and P is the orthogonal projection onto an m-dimensional subspace E, the density of PU is largest at 0, where it equals vol_{n-m}(Q_n \cap E^perp); hence it is at most min{ (n/(n-m))^{(n-m)/2}, 2^{m/2} } <= 2^{m/2}.

Assumes: central sections (linear subspaces); Q_n = [-1/2,1/2]^n; the density statement is for the uniform distribution on the cube only

[Proposition prop:vector-valued-contraction-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Let \(q\in(1,2)\), let \(r\ge2\), let \(G\) be a finite set, and let
\(J\) be a finite index set. Let \((Z_j)_{j\in J}\) be independent mean-zero
random vectors in \(\mathbb C^G\) such that
\[
\mathbb{E}\lVert Z_j \rVert_{\ell^r(G)}^q<\infty
\qquad(j\in J).
\]
Let \(\mathcal A\) be a \(\sigma\)-field independent of \(\sigma(Z_j:j\in J)\),
and let \((a_j)_{j\in J}\) be complex-valued \(\mathcal A\)-measurable random
variables. Then, with both sides understood in the extended sense,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\left[
\left\|
\sum_{j\in J}a_jZ_j
\right\|_{\ell^r(G)}^q
\middle|\mathcal A
\right]
\le
C_q r^{q/2}
\sum_{j\in J}\lvert a_j\rvert^q
\mathbb{E}\lVert Z_j \rVert_{\ell^r(G)}^q
\end{equation}
almost surely.

body: [Theorem 20 of arXiv:2604.13454, 'Invariant and periodic measures in classical spin systems on infinite lattices with highly'] For $x \in \ell_\rho^{2\theta}(\mathbb{Z}^+)$, let $\tilde{X}^{(m), x}, \tilde{X}^{(n),x}$ be two different sequences of approximating processes on $\Omega_{Spin}$. Then there exists a probability measure $\mathbf{P}^x$ on $\Omega_{Spin}$ such that $$\lim_{m \rightarrow \infty} \mathbb{P} \circ (\tilde{X}^{(m), x})^{-1} = \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \mathbb{P} \circ (\tilde{X}^{(n), x})^{-1} = \mathbf{P}^x.$$

body: [Theorem 1.5 of arXiv:2302.05605, 'The "Power of Few" Phenomenon: The Sparse Case'] On a G(n, p) random graph where p ≥(1 + λ)n−1 log n for a constant λ > 0, majority dynamics with a random (pr, pb) initial coloring with pr = 1/2 + ω((pn)−1) terminates with a Red unanimity with probability 1 −o(1). By the Central Limit Theorem or Chernoff bound, it is easy to see that with probability 1 −o(1), |R| > |B| and the initial gap ∆= (|R| −|B|)/2 is ω(1/p).
title: Theorem 1.5 of arXiv:2302.05605: The "Power of Few" Phenomenon: The Sparse Case

body: In extremal graph theory, Szemerédi's regularity lemma states that a graph can be partitioned into a bounded number of parts so that the edges between parts are regular. The lemma shows that certain properties of random graphs can be applied to dense graphs like counting the copies of a given subgraph within graphs. Endre Szemerédi proved the lemma over bipartite graphs for his theorem on arithmetic progressions in 1975 and for general graphs in 1978. Variants of the lemma use different notions of regularity and apply to other mathematical objects like hypergraphs.
title: Szemerédi regularity lemma

body:
[Pro FourierHilbert of arXiv:2609.02882, 'A new proof that more than $2/3$ of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and '] Let $\lambda>0$ be a real number and $\eta\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ be a real valued even function with $\textup{supp} (\eta) \subset (-\lambda, \lambda) $, such that $\widehat{\eta^2}(0)=1$. Let $\mathcal{Z}$ be a non-empty finite multiset of complex numbers which is invariant under complex
conjugation. For $z\in \mathcal{Z}$ we let $m_z$ be its multiplicity in $\mathcal{Z}$.  Then we have 
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\substack{z\in \mathcal{Z}\cap \mathbb{R}\\ m_z=1}}1\geqslant 2\sum_{z\in \mathcal{Z}} 1 -
 \sum_{z,s\in\mathcal Z}K(z-s)^2,  
\end{equation}
where $K$ is the kernel $K(\xi):= \widehat{\eta^2}(\xi).$ Moreover, the number of distinct elements of $\mathcal{Z}$ is 
\begin{equation}
 \geqslant \frac{3}{2}\sum_{z\in \mathcal{Z}} 1 -
 \frac12\sum_{z,s\in\mathcal Z}K(z-s)^2.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pro FourierHilbert of arXiv:2609.02882

\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \Pbb(X^{(n)} \notin K_M)

\]

[Lemma lem:first-exit of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $V\subset\mathbb R^m$ be bounded and open, and suppose that
$w\in C(\overline V)$ has a unique minimum point
$\mathbf p_*\in V$ on $\overline V$.  Let
$d:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous, and let $S$ be a set-valued
map from $\mathbb R$ to $\mathbb R^m$ with nonempty compact values.  Fix
$\delta>0$.  Then there exist $\eta_*,r_*>0$, depending only on $V,w,\delta$,
with the following property.

Assume that $S$ is upper semicontinuous\footnote{As in
(lem:centers of the paper)(vi), this means that, for every $t_0\in\mathbb R$ and every open
set $O\subset\mathbb R^m$ with $S(t_0)\subset O$, there exists $\sigma>0$ such that
$S(t)\subset O$ whenever $|t-t_0|<\sigma$.} and that
\[
  \operatorname{diam}S(t)\leq r_*
  \quad\text{whenever }d(t)\leq\delta,
\]
and that
\begin{equation}
  d(t)+\sup_{\mathbf b\in S(t)}[w(\mathbf b)-w(\mathbf p_*)]
  \leq\eta_*
\end{equation}
whenever $S(t)\subset\overline V$ and $d(t)\leq\delta$.
Then $S(0)\subset V$ and $d(0)<\delta$ imply that
$S(t)\subset V$ and $d(t)<\delta$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.

[Proposition prop:rate of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] Under the hypotheses of Proposition~(prop:opmatch of the paper), and assuming in addition that
$b,f$ are bounded with bounded derivatives, there is $C=C(T,b,f)$ such that for every
$t\in[0,T]$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb{E}\big[W_{2}(L_{N}(t),\mu_{t})\big]\le C\,N^{-1/2},
\end{equation}
where $L_{N}(t)$ is the empirical spectral distribution of (equation eq:opmatrix of the paper).
Consequently, if the reverse-time dynamics of \S(sec:tweedie of the paper) are simulated at
dimension $N$ by an Euler--Maruyama scheme with $n$ steps on the eigenvalue system
(equation eq:opeigen of the paper), using a score $\widehat\xi$ satisfying
$\sup_{t}\mathbb{E}[\mathcal S_{t}(\theta)]\le\epsilon^{2}$ (Corollary~(cor:stein of the paper)), the
generated law $\widehat L_{N,n}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb{E}\big[W_{2}(\widehat L_{N,n},\mu_{0})\big]
  \le C_{1}N^{-1/2}+C_{2}n^{-1/2}+C_{3}\,\epsilon,
\end{equation}
with $C_{1},C_{2},C_{3}$ depending on $T,\beta,b,f$ but not on $N,n,\epsilon$.

[Lem 56 of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Let $d\ge 2$.
Suppose that $F:\mathbb [0,\infty)\to [0,\infty)$ 
    is a decreasing function of exponential decay at infinity. 
    Let $K > 0$. Then there exists some $\epsilon>0$ and a constant $C = C(K, F) >0$ such that uniformly over $|\varsigma|<\epsilon$, $   a_1,   a_2\in I$, and all $0 = r_0 < r_1 \leq \cdots \leq r_m$, we have  \begin{align*}
    \mathbf E^{(\varsigma,2)}_{(   a_1,   a_2)} \bigg[ \prod_{j=1}^{m} F(|   R^1_{r_j}-   R^2_{r_j}|)\bigg] \leq C \left( 1+ r_1^{-1/2} |   a_1 -    a_2|\right)^{-K} \prod_{j=1}^{m} 1 \wedge (r_j - r_{j-1})^{-d/2}. 
\end{align*}
In particular, for fixed $r\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ we have that \begin{equation}\sum_{1\le s_1\le ...\le s_{m-1} \le r}\mathbf E^{(\varsigma,2)}_{(   a_1,   a_2)} \bigg[ F(|R^1_r -R^2_r|) \prod_{j=1}^{m} F(|   R^1_{r_j}-   R^2_{r_j}|)\bigg] \leq \frac{C^m}{\omega_r(d)^{m-1} } r^{-d/2} (1+r^{-1/2} |   a_1-   a_2| \big)^{-K} .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:immerse of arXiv:2412.04589, 'Inverting the Markovian projection for pure jump processes'] Let $\mathbb{F}$, $\mathbb{G}$ and $(\mathbb{F}^i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be filtrations on some space.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), nosep]
		\item If $\mathbb{G}$ is the right-continuous regularization of $\mathbb{F}$, then $\mathbb{F} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{G}$.
		
		\item If $\mathbb{F}^{i-1} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{F}^i$ for all $i \in \mathbb{N^*}$, then $\mathbb{F}^k \hookrightarrow \newbigtriangledown_{i=0}^\infty \mathbb{F}^i$ for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
		
		\item If $Z$ is a random variable independent of $\mathbb{F}$, then $\mathbb{F} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{F} \newtriangledown \sigma(Z)$.
	\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:immerse of arXiv:2412.04589

[Lem convergence of coding functions and pointset for ER of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{[Berry_Broutin_Goldschmidt_12_The_continuum]}] 
  Assume that a sequence $(m_{n})_{n \geq 1}$ satisfies $n^{-2/3} m_{n} \to \sigma \in (0,\infty)$.
  Let $\mathcal{Q}^{p_{n}}$ be a binomial pointset of intensity $p_{n}$, independent of $\tilde{T}_{m_{n}}^{p_{n}}$,
  and define $\mathcal{P}_{n} \coloneqq  \{ ( (\sigma/m_{n}) i, (\sigma/m_{n})^{1/2} j ) \mid (i,j) \in \mathcal{Q}^{p_{n}} \}$.
  Then, it holds that
  \begin{align}
     & \left(
    \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{m_{n}}} H_{\tilde{T}_{m_{n}}^{p_{n}}} \left( \left\lfloor \frac{m_{n}}{\sigma} \cdot \right\rfloor \right),
    \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{m_{n}}} X_{\tilde{T}_{m_{n}}^{p_{n}}} \left( \left\lfloor \frac{m_{n}}{\sigma} \cdot \right\rfloor \right),
    \mathcal{P}_{n} \cap \left( \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{m_{n}}} X_{\tilde{T}_{m_{n}}^{p_{n}}} \left( \left\lfloor \frac{m_{n}}{\sigma} \cdot \right\rfloor \right) \right)
    \right) \notag                            \\
     & \xrightarrow[n \to \infty]{\mathrm{d}}
    (2 \tilde{e}^{(\sigma)}, \tilde{e}^{(\sigma)}, \mathcal{P} \cap \tilde{e}^{(\sigma)}),
    
  \end{align}
  where the convergence of the first and second coordinate takes place in $D([0,\sigma], \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})$
  equipped with the usual $J_{1}$-Skorohod topology
  and the convergence of the third coordinate takes place with respect to the Hausdorff metric. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let h be a (discrete or continuum) Gaussian free field on a domain D with Dirichlet boundary conditions, and let U be a deterministic subdomain of D. The Gibbs-Markov (domain Markov) property states that h decomposes as h = h_U + phi_U, where h_U is a zero-boundary Gaussian free field on U, phi_U is the harmonic extension into U of the values of h on the boundary of U, h_U and phi_U are independent of each other, and phi_U is measurable with respect to the sigma-field generated by h restricted to the complement of U. This is the discrete and continuum analogue of the strong Markov property for Brownian motion and harmonic functions, and it is the fundamental tool enabling induction-on-scale arguments, the theory of local sets, and the construction of conformally invariant objects such as Liouville quantum gravity from the field. It does not hold for general non-Gibbsian or non-Gaussian log-correlated fields without separate verification, and it requires exact specification of the domain and boundary conditions, since the decomposition depends on the harmonic extension operator for the particular pair (D,U) being used. Typical failure: Applying the plain Gibbs-Markov decomposition with U chosen depending on the field h itself, such as a random subdomain determined by a level set or an exploration process, without checking that U is a valid stopping domain for the field's filtration; naively random domains destroy the independence between h_U and phi_U, and the correct fix requires the more delicate theory of local sets developed by Schramm and Sheffield, not the plain domain Markov property. Canonical reference: Sheffield, 2007, Probability Theory and Related Fields; Schramm and Sheffield, 2013, Probability Theory and Related Fields.
h is a Gaussian free field with Dirichlet (or otherwise precisely specified) boundary conditions on domain D
U is a deterministic, or at least suitably measurable stopping-domain, subdomain of D
the Green's function and harmonic measure for D and U are well defined, requiring sufficient domain regularity
correct identification of phi_U as harmonic in U with boundary values equal to h on the boundary of U
title: Technique: Gibbs-Markov Property of the Gaussian Free Field

An absence theorem restricted to bigeodesic tails in deterministic thin horizontal or vertical tubes requires a further confinement theorem, or an obstruction for wider and adaptive wandering, before it can establish unrestricted absence. Countable intersections over fixed finite widths do not cover a path whose transverse displacement is unbounded. A directional limit permits unbounded sublinear transverse displacement. The separate compactness route, taking limits of geodesics between opposite distant endpoints, likewise needs anchoring near a bounded region; endpoints on opposite sides alone allow the connecting paths to escape every fixed ball. These are missing bridge premises, not refutations of absence for nonatomic iid planar FPP.
Ambient nearest-neighbor Z^2 FPP
The available absence theorem covers only specified deterministic tubes
No additional bigeodesic confinement or tightness premise is assumed

Let (X, Y, Z) be jointly Gaussian in R^a x R^b x R^c with covariance blocks A = Cov(X), C = Cov(Y), G = Cov(Z), B = Cov(X, Y), E = Cov(X, Z), F = Cov(Y, Z), possibly singular, and put A_c = A - E G^+ E^T, C_c = C - F G^+ F^T, B_c = B - E G^+ F^T and K = [[A_c, B_c], [B_c^T, C_c]]. Let rho_1, rho_2, ... be the singular values of R_c = A_c^(+1/2) B_c C_c^(+1/2), where A_c^(+1/2) is the Moore-Penrose inverse of the positive semidefinite square root (the partial canonical correlations). Then every rho_j <= 1; I(X; Y | Z) is finite exactly when every rho_j < 1; and then I(X; Y | Z) = -(1/2) sum_j log(1 - rho_j^2).
(X, Y, Z) is jointly Gaussian

[Lem lemma:left-convergence-locally-tree-like of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] Let $G_N=(\text{\boldmath $A$}_N,\text{\boldmath $h$}_N)$ be a sequence of weighted $k$-regular graphs
which converge locally to the $k$-regular tree. Let the edge weights
$(A_{ij}:\{i,j\}\in E(G_N))$ be i.i.d. random variables with common
distribution $Q_A$, and independent of the vertex weights $(h_{i}:i\in
[N])$ which are i.i.d. random variables with common distribution
$Q_h$. Assume that $Q_A,Q_h$ are independent of $N$ and have bounded
support. For a constant $c\in\text{\boldmath $R$}$, define
$G_N(c)=(\text{\boldmath $A$}_N(c),\text{\boldmath $h$}_N(c))$, where
$\text{\boldmath $A$}(c)=\text{\boldmath $A$}_N-c{\boldsymbol 1}{\boldsymbol 1}^{{\sf T}}/N$, $\text{\boldmath $h$}_N(c)=\text{\boldmath $h$}_N$.

Then, the sequence $(G_N(c): N\ge 1)$ is almost surely
left-convergent.

For separately bias-corrected scalar Adam beta1=.9,beta2=.999 with epsilon outside sqrt, standard m0=v0=0 and eta*lambda/epsilon=38, every initialization with 0<|x0|<=10^(-57)*eta has nonzero sign-alternating positions, converges to its origin, and has x_(t+1)/x_t tending to -1 rather than -.9. The invariant normalized raw-momentum cone is 0<=-m_t/(lambda*x_t)<=2/37. In particular this is an open standard-start interval at epsilon=eta,lambda=38 for every eta>0. The sufficient radius is extremely small; no generic root selection outside it is asserted.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:48110d63f4369adc569872e734b1f2e5c46ea9828cfc9b78931bddbdd42b6b3d","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/48/48110d63f4369adc569872e734b1f2e5c46ea9828cfc9b78931bddbdd42b6b3d.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:62666cafca9e533e0c9a1a55b5cec2544505ebbb84a1c6f2c724567b205ee868","bundle_entry_key":"critical-small-start-minus-one-cone","bundle_id":"population.adam-critical-cap38-small-start-minus-one-cone-022","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"adaptive optimization and difference equations","draft":"w706/bundle_022.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.adam:adam-critical-cap38-small-standard-start-minus-one-root-momentum-cone","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# An open standard-start interval selects the minus-one critical mode
Kind:special; target2. Status: proof (unaudited). No literature priority
or new frontier score claimed. This answers the reviewer's open-set
root-selection subquestion on an explicitly tiny interval.

STATEMENT. Let eta,epsilon,lambda>0 satisfy eta*lambda/epsilon=38.
Run separately bias-corrected scalar Adam with b=9/10,d=999/1000,
epsilon outside sqrt, and m_0=v_0=0. If
             0<|x_0|<=10^(-57)*eta,
then every position is nonzero, signs alternate from time0, x_t->0,
and x_(t+1)/x_t ->-1. The alternative limit -b=-.9 does not occur on
this interval. In particular this holds for epsilon=eta,lambda=38,
for every eta>0. This is not a generic-root or global-basin theorem.
The constant is a sufficient tiny radius, not a practical-scale basin.

NORMALIZATION AND EXACT IDENTITIES. Set X=x/eta,M=m/(eta*lambda),
V=v/(eta*lambda)^2,rho=epsilon/(eta*lambda)=1/38, ell=1-b=1/10.
With U_(t+1)=sqrt(V_(t+1)/(1-d^(t+1))), define
 a_t=38/[(1-b^(t+1))*(1+U_(t+1)/rho)].
Then V_(t+1)=d*V_t+(1-d)*X_t^2, M_(t+1)=b*M_t+ell*X_t,
X_(t+1)=X_t-a_t*M_(t+1). By odd symmetry assume X_0>0.
Whenever X_t!=0 put z_t=-M_t/X_t and N(z)=ell-b*z. Then
 H_t=a_t*N(z_t)-1,
 X_(t+1)=-H_t*X_t, z_(t+1)=N(z_t)/H_t.              (1)
Put Z_t=X_t+18*M_t and W_t=(-1)^t*Z_t. Direct substitution gives
 Z_(t+1)+Z_t=(38-a_t)*M_(t+1).                       (2)
These are exact actual corrected updates, not frozen-preconditioner steps.

1. A FORWARD-INVARIANT MOMENTUM CONE WHEN VARIANCE IS SMALL
Set Q=2/37, a_min=1443/38, h=1/54834. Exact arithmetic gives
 N(Q)=19/370, a_min=1/Q+1/N(Q),
 a_min*N(Q)-1=19/20, 1-18*Q=1/37.
For0<=z<=Q and a>=a_min, H=a*N(z)-1>=19/20>0.
The map f(z)=N(z)/(a*N(z)-1) has derivative b/(a*N(z)-1)^2>0
and decreases in a. Its maximum is f(Q) at a=a_min, equal to Q.
Thus0<f(z)<=Q: signs flip, the next position is nonzero, and the
cone0<=z<=Q is preserved whenever a>=a_min.

Inside this cone Z_t/X_t=1-18*z_t is between1/37 and1, so W_t>0
when signs have alternated and X_0>0. Also
 R(z)=N(z)/(1-18*z), R'(z)=(18*ell-b)/(1-18*z)^2>0,
             ell<=R(z)<=19/10.                    (3)
Equation(2) now reads
 W_(t+1)=W_t*[1-(38-a_t)*R(z_t)].                    (4)
The bracket is positive by cone preservation; no sign of38-a_t is assumed.

2. FINITE BIAS-CLOCK AMPLIFICATION, WITH A CERTIFIED INFINITE TAIL
For actual Adam, a_t<=38/(1-b^(t+1)). Equations(3),(4) therefore give
 W_(t+1)<=W_t*[1+c*b^(t+1)/(1-b^(t+1))], c=361/5.
Define P_T=product_(n=1)^T[1+c*b^n/(1-b^n)]. The exact certificate
scripts/check_critical_momentum_cone.py verifies P_100<10^50 and
 S=c*b^101/[(1-b)*(1-b^101)]<1.
For n>=101,1-b^n>=1-b^101, so the sum of the remaining nonnegative
clock terms is at most S. The elementary inequality log(1+u)<=u for
u>=0 bounds their infinite product by exp(S)<e<3. The last bound also
follows directly from the exponential series using n!>=2^(n-1),
strictly for n>=3. Hence
                P_infinity<3*10^50.               (5)
The100-factor product is computed exactly with rational arithmetic;
there is no floating logarithm, unbounded truncation, or numerical orbit.

3. CLOSE THE SMALL-VARIANCE BOOTSTRAP
Set K=111*10^50=37*(3*10^50), delta=h/K.
The same exact certificate verifies10^(-57)<=delta. We may prove the
slightly stronger assertion for0<X_0<=delta.
At time0,z_0=0,W_0=X_0. Inductively, suppose the preceding positions
have alternated,0<=z_j<=Q, and |X_j|<=37*P_j*X_0 for j<=t.
By(5), every such position is at most K*X_0<=h in absolute value.
Since V_0=0, the corrected variance V_(t+1)/(1-d^(t+1)) is a convex
combination of X_0^2,...,X_t^2. Thus U_(t+1)<=h and
 a_t>=38/(1+h/rho)=1443/38=a_min.
Section1 preserves the cone and gives a nonzero next position of the
opposite sign. Section2 gives W_(t+1)<=P_(t+1)*X_0, whence
|X_(t+1)|=W_(t+1)/(1-18*z_(t+1))<=37*P_(t+1)*X_0.
This closes induction for every finite time. The global product bound
is fixed in advance, so no future orbit bound is assumed in the bootstrap.

4. ORIGIN CONVERGENCE WITHIN THE CONE
By the preceding one-step bound, W_t/P_t is positive and nonincreasing.
Since P_t has a finite positive limit, W_t has a nonnegative finite limit.
If that limit were positive, then |X_t|>=W_t would be bounded below at
late times. The raw variance convolution, with d<1, would make U_(t+1)
bounded below by a positive constant. Since b^(t+1)->0, the exact a_t
would eventually satisfy a_t<=38-kappa for some kappa>0 (take kappa<1).
Then(3),(4) give W_(t+1)<=(1-kappa*ell)*W_t, contradicting a positive
limit. Therefore W_t->0. The cone bounds imply X_t->0,M_t->0 and the
stable variance recursion gives V_t->0, hence a_t->38.
This convergence argument does not need the global low-cap theorem012v2.

5. SELECT THE ROOT
Eliminate raw momentum as in independently PASSED028v1 Section1:
 X_(t+1)=[1+b*a_t/a_(t-1)-ell*a_t]*X_t
                          -b*a_t/a_(t-1)*X_(t-1), t>=1.
Its coefficients converge to the critical ones and its characteristic
polynomial is (r+1)*(r+b), with distinct root moduli1 and.9. The last
coefficient is nonzero at every finite time, and the solution never
vanishes, so Poincare's ratio theorem gives a limit of-1 or-b.
This uses exactly the classical ratio implication, not Perron's
root-attainment addition and not a convergence-rate assertion.
If the limit were-b, X_(t+1)=X_t-a_t*M_(t+1) would imply
 z_(t+1)=-(1-X_(t+1)/X_t)/(a_t*(X_(t+1)/X_t))
                      ->(1+b)/(38*b)=1/18.
But z_t<=2/37<1/18 at every time. This is a contradiction. Hence the
ratio tends to-1. The same identity then gives z_t->1/19 and Z_t/X_t->1/19,
so the exponentially small center direction in081 is excluded here.

SCOPE AND VALIDATION. This is an open punctured interval (and its closed
outer endpoints) of standard starts at every critical scaling. It does
not cover starts of order eta, nor rule out exceptional fast starts
outside the interval, nor establish a null supercritical origin basin.
The scalar critical curvature tends to38 here; this alone does not
settle the full two-eigenvalue problem. No frontier score is asserted.

The exact script checks rational cone endpoints, derivative numerators,
variance ceiling,100 clock factors, and an explicit bound on the entire
infinite clock tail. It certifies those arithmetic steps, not the
written induction and infinite-time argument. Independent audit pending.

# Unit-norm nonlinear ReLU teacher with paired initialization

T267 / Target 1 / C010 / proof draft (unaudited); novelty unestablished.

This removes the diverging teacher norm in C009, at the price of paired
initialization and noise that shrinks with the signal. It is a restricted
four-point, stratified-design, noise-averaged theorem. It does not establish
the generic iid Gaussian-input target or a fixed-positive-noise result.
The hardest remaining target step is sign-level population-risk control
for a genuinely sampled nonlinear model beyond this finite-support
infinite-width construction.

## Statement

Fix nu in (0,1]. For 0<e<1/4 let D=1+e^2+e^4 and use the same four inputs
x_(s,t)=(1,e s,e^2 t)/sqrt(D), s,t in {-1,1}. Training contains each once;
the test law is uniform on these four points. Let

u_e=(0,e,1)/sqrt(1+e^2),
c_e=e^2/[sqrt(D)*sqrt(1+e^2)], alpha_e=c_e/2,
g_e(x)=ReLU(u_e.x)-E_X ReLU(u_e.X).

The vector u_e has norm one. On this support u_e.x=c_e(s+t), so

g_e(x_(s,t))=alpha_e(s+t+st).

Thus the teacher is genuinely nonlinear even when restricted to the
support: no affine function of x has a nonzero st Walsh coefficient.
The centering constant is the population mean c_e/2. Labels are g_e(x_i)
plus independent equiprobable noise +/-c_e, so the noise standard deviation
is c_e, not a fixed positive constant as e decreases.

Take even width m=2N and initialize each independent pair by
w_(2j-1)=w_(2j)=W_j iid N(0,I_3),
a_(2j-1)=nu, a_(2j)=-nu.
Pairs are independent; the individual neurons are NOT iid. Initially f=0
exactly. Train both layers of every neuron by simultaneous GD at step 1/2,
loss ||f(X)-y||^2/(2n), n=4, with f=m^(-1/2) sum a ReLU(w.x) and gate
convention 1_{z>0}. No symmetry is imposed after initialization.

Let Q_(m,e)(k) be clean population squared risk, averaged over the sixteen
training-label-noise patterns, conditional on initialization. Let b_h be
C009's rates for the full initial tangent kernel h_nu=k+nu^2 g1, with mode
indices 0,1,2,12. Set

k0=ceil(e^(-1/2)), k1=floor(log(2)/b1),
k2=ceil(e^(-3/2)), k3=floor(log(2)/b2),
B=log[b1/(b2+b12)].

In the iterated limit m=2N->infinity first, then e->0, the probability of
failure of the strict witnesses

Q(k0)>Q(k1)<Q(k2)>Q(k3)

tends to zero. More precisely the four risks divided by alpha_e^2 converge
in probability, in that iterated sense, to 4,7/2,4,3.
For every fixed delta>0, every maximizer k_peak on the integer interval
I_e=[floor((B-1)/b1),ceil((B+1)/b1)] is interior and satisfies
|b1 k_peak-B|<delta with probability tending to one in the same iterated
sense. Consequently

k_peak ~ (4*pi/nu^2) e^(-1) log(1/e).

This localizes a central local peak, not a global maximum or all extrema.

## 1. Teacher identity and exact initialization

ReLU(s+t) takes values 2,0,0,0, whose mean is 1/2. Its centered version is
(s+t+st)/2. The unit norm and displayed teacher identity follow directly.
The nonzero interaction coefficient rules out an affine teacher on the
four inputs, even though two projections lie exactly at the teacher's
ReLU kink. No differentiability of the teacher is used in training.

Each pair has exactly cancelling outputs. Its two readout-Jacobian Gram
summands are identical. Its two hidden-Jacobian Gram summands are also
identical because their readout factors are squared. Dividing by m=2N
therefore gives the same expected full kernel as in C009:

C_(nu,e)(i,l)=[k(x_i.x_l)+nu^2 g1(x_i.x_l)]/4.

Strong laws apply to the N independent pairs. No independent-neuron
concentration or centered independent readout-sign argument is needed.

## 2. Transfer from the actual nonlinear GD

Here we specify why C009 Section 3 applies despite correlated pairs.
For e<1/4, c_e<e^2<1/16. The largest absolute teacher value is 3c_e/2;
the largest label magnitude is at most 5c_e/2<5/32. Thus ||y||<5/16<2.
The actual initial output is identically zero; use M=0 and R_0=2 in the
deterministic finite-horizon recurrences of C009 Section 3. Those bounds
are neuronwise and use no independence. They hold separately for both
members of every pair, even after their hidden weights separate.

The empirical mean of initial squared hidden norms converges almost surely
to 3 by the pairwise strong law. The weighted initial gate-band mass is
now exactly the mean over N independent W_j of
(1+||W_j||)^2 1{min_i|W_j.x_i| <= D_* (1+||W_j||)/sqrt(2N)}.
It tends to zero by the same rational-band strong-law and dominated-
convergence argument as C009. The initial kernel converges entrywise to
C by the pairwise strong law. These are the only probabilistic inputs to
the instantaneous-kernel and exact discrete-step remainder bounds in C009.
Their finite-horizon telescoping proof therefore gives

max_(k<=T) ||f_actual(k)-f_frozen(k)|| -> 0 in probability

for every fixed e,nu,T, uniformly over all sixteen noise patterns. The
frozen iteration starts at zero exactly. Here and below T may depend on e;
width tends to infinity separately for each fixed e. This does not claim a
uniform feature-scale rate or a feasible numerical width.

## 3. Risk margins

All three nonconstant teacher Walsh coefficients are alpha=alpha_e.
Independent +/-c_e label noise has Walsh variances c_e^2/4=alpha^2.
Parseval and the zero initial prediction give the exact frozen risk

Q_e^0(k)/alpha^2 = (1-q0^k)^2
                 + sum_(h=1,2,12) [q_h^(2k)+(1-q_h^k)^2],
q_h=exp(-b_h).

C009 Section 2 supplies b1~nu^2 e/(4pi), b2~nu^2 e^2/(8pi),
b12/b2->1, and b0 bounded away from zero. At k0 all nonconstant modes
remain unlearned, giving 1+1+1+1=4. At k1 the fast component has q1->1/2
and the two slow components remain at one, giving 1+1/2+1+1=7/2.
At k2 the fast component has q1->0 while slow components remain at one,
giving 4. At k3 both slow components have q->1/2, giving 1+1+1/2+1/2=3.
The three strict limiting margins are 1/2,1/2,1. For fixed e, alpha>0 and
the finite-horizon transfer changes risk by o_P(1), hence by o_P(alpha^2)
as width grows; division by a fixed positive alpha^2 is legitimate.
Then let e decrease. This proves the four strict actual-risk witnesses.

## 4. Central peak

Interpolate the frozen curve continuously and put z=(B+s)/b1 with
B=log[b1/(b2+b12)]. Uniformly for s in compact intervals,

(Q_e^0)'(z)/[2 alpha^2 (b2+b12)] -> exp(-s)-1,
(Q_e^0)''(z)/[2 alpha^2 b1 (b2+b12)] -> -exp(-s).

Indeed each nonconstant mode contributes 2 alpha^2 b_h q_h(1-2q_h).
The fast term contributes exp(-s); its quadratic correction is
O((b2+b12)/b1). The two slow terms contribute -b2/(b2+b12) and
-b12/(b2+b12), up to errors O(((b2+b12)/b1) B). The constant-mode
term and its derivatives vanish faster than any polynomial of e.
The same estimates after one further differentiation give the stated
second derivative. Thus the frozen central peak has scaled coordinate
s_e->0 and a strict value gap away from any fixed delta neighborhood,
of order alpha^2 (b2+b12)/b1, by integrating the derivative on [-1,1].
The grid spacing b1 tends to zero, so discrete maximizers obey the same
localization. When delta>=1, the conclusion follows from any smaller
positive delta, and interval endpoints are excluded as well.

For each fixed e the interval is finite and its positive peak gap is a
fixed positive number. Section 2 therefore transfers the maximizer
localization to the actual risk with probability tending to one as width
grows. No random initial-output perturbation occurs. Finally
b1/(b2+b12)~1/e and b1~nu^2 e/(4pi) give the peak asymptotic.

## Scope and dependencies

This proof depends on the unaudited deterministic bounds and Gaussian
kernel asymptotics in C009, not on an independent audit or a floating-point
fit. Pair cancellation is only an initial condition, not frozen weights.
The centering offset is part of the single-index link ReLU(z)-c_e/2.
The teacher has uniformly unit norm and is nonlinear on the support;
its variation and the label-noise standard deviation both vanish as e^2.
The design remains stratified, finite support, with every test input in
training, and risk averages over labels. No fixed-noise, iid-design,
macroscopic feature-learning, full-target or novelty claim is made.
Primary kernel source: Heckel--Yilmaz arXiv:2007.10099v2 Section 3 K1/K2.
The existence of two noise thresholds in Stephenson--Lee 2108.12006 is not
used to infer that this model has the same noise window.
All explicit definitions in proofs/BOUNDED_RELU_PAIRED.md
Even width; independent Gaussian hidden-weight pairs with equal hidden weights and opposite heads +/-nu, nu fixed in (0,1]; neurons are not iid
Unit-norm centered ReLU teacher with a nonzero interaction Walsh coefficient on the support
Noise standard deviation c_e=e^2/sqrt((1+e^2+e^4)(1+e^2)) tends to zero; n=4 stratified training and uniform test support
Risk averaged over sixteen independent label-noise sign patterns; GD step 1/2; width limit precedes feature-scale limit

Method: Variation of nearest-unvisited walk length under a random start structural calculation Result: Let m and M be the minimum and maximum start-dependent lengths, R=M/m. The elementary bound Var(X)<=(M-E X)*(E X-m) implies sd(X)/E X<=(R-1)/(2*sqrt(R)) for any X in[m,M]. Classical nearest-neighbor-tour comparison gives R=O(log n), since every walk length is at least MST length and its length is at most O(log n) times a TSP tour, at most twice MST length. Hence a rigorous O(sqrt(log n)) coefficient-of-variation bound follows, short of an absolute constant. Check: The variance inequality follows by averaging(X-m)*(M-X)>=0. Maximizing(M-u)*(u-m)/u^2 over u in[m,M] gives u=2Mm/(M+m) and the displayed exact ratio. This is sharper than simply bounding standard deviation by the range. Obstruction: The deterministic logarithmic approximation examples do not automatically give a large random-start coefficient of variation. ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Energy plus entropy conductance bound Result: Let G have odd n and edge expansion |boundary S|>=h|S| for all |S|<=n/2. Use H(sigma)=-J sum_edges sigma_u sigma_v-B sum_v sigma_v with J>0,B>=0,Jh>B, and Gibbs law pi proportional to exp(-beta H). Consider any reversible single-spin continuous-time chain with each individual spin-flip rate at most1. Put A={number of plus spins< n/2}. Global spin reversal maps A bijectively onto its complement and does not decrease Gibbs weight, so pi(A)<=1/2. An A-to-complement jump must start with(n-1)/2 plus spins, whose energy exceeds the all-minus energy by at least(Jh-B)(n-1). There are at most2^n such states and total exit rate at most n per state. Since pi(A) is at least the all-minus weight, the conductance Phi=Q(A,A-complement)/pi(A) is at most n*2^n*exp[-beta(Jh-B)(n-1)]. Starting with pi conditioned on A, the time-s law is bounded above by pi/pi(A), by Markov-kernel positivity and stationarity. Consequently the expected number of A-to-complement jumps by time t is at most t*Phi. The probability of still being in A at time t is at least1-t*Phi, giving total variation distance at least1/2-t*Phi. Convexity of total variation implies the same lower bound for the worst starting state. Therefore t_mix(1/4)>=1/(4*Phi), at least exp[beta(Jh-B)(n-1)]/(4*n*2^n). This is exponential in n when beta(Jh-B)>log2. The calculation accounts explicitly for entropy. It is a deterministic expansion-based mixing lower bound; it does not prove a metastable exit-time distribution, or expansion for every configuration-model degree law. Check: Boundary-layer counting and stationary domination give separate energy and time estimates. Obstruction: No general random-graph expansion theorem or metastable exit-time distribution is proved.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03946, 'The groups $\SL_2(\F_{13})$ and $\SL_2(\F_{19})$ are Galois over $\Q$'] Let $L/\Q$ be a finite Galois extension whose group $G$ acts faithfully and
transitively on a finite set $\Omega$, let $B$ be a point stabilizer, and put
$K=L^B$.  Fix a prime of $L$ above $q$ and let $I\trianglelefteq D\leq G$ be
its inertia and decomposition groups.  Then the primes of $K$ above $q$
correspond to the $D$-orbits on $\Omega$. An orbit $\mathcal O\ni\omega$ corresponds to a prime with
\begin{equation}
 e(\mathcal O)=|I\omega|,
 \qquad
 f(\mathcal O)=\frac{|D\omega|}{|I\omega|} .
\end{equation}

body: For every set A, there is no surjection from A onto its power set P(A) (the set of all subsets of A). Since a -> {a} is an injection from A into P(A), it follows that |A| < |P(A)| for every set A: every set is strictly smaller than its power set. In particular there is no largest cardinality, and iterating the power set on an infinite set produces an unbounded increasing hierarchy of infinite cardinalities.

body: A normed vector space (X, ||.||) is uniformly convex if for every epsilon in (0, 2] there exists delta > 0 such that, for all x, y in X with ||x|| <= 1, ||y|| <= 1, and ||x - y|| >= epsilon, we have ||(x+y)/2|| <= 1 - delta. Uniform convexity is a quantitative strengthening of strict convexity (which only requires ||(x+y)/2|| < 1 whenever x not equal to y, ||x||=||y||=1) and holds for every Hilbert space, via the parallelogram law, and for every L^p space with 1 < p < infinity. [standard, e.g. Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and PDEs]
title: Uniformly Convex Banach Space

body:
[Lem 250 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Suppose the random vector $\bX$ in $\R^N$ is \emph{subgaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$}, meaning that $(\theta,\bX)$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$ for all $\theta$ in the unit ball $B_N\subset\R^N$. Then
    \[
    \P\bigg(\frac{\|\bX\|}{N^{1/2}} \ge t\bigg)
    \le \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{Nt^2}{16\sigma^2} \bigg\}
    \]
provided $t\ge 6\sigma$. It follows that
$\E(\|\bX\|^p) \le  C_p \sigma^p N^{p/2}$
where $C_p$ is a constant depending only on $p$.

\begin{proof}
To bound the norm of a random vector $\bX$ in $\R^N$, the standard argument is to let $N_{1/2}$ be a $1/2$-net of the unit ball $B\subset \R^N$, and note that
    \begin{align*}
    \|\bX\|
    &= \sup \Big\{
    (\theta,\bX) : \theta\in B\Big\}
    \le 
    \sup\bigg\{
    (\theta_1+\theta_2,\bX):
    \theta_1\in N_{1/2},
    \theta_2\in \frac12 B\bigg\} \\
    &\le
    \sup\Big\{(\theta,\bX) :\theta\in N_{1/2}\Big\}
    + \frac{\|\bX\|}{2}
    \equiv S + \frac{\|\bX\|}{2} \,.
    \end{align*}
Rearranging the above gives
    \[\|\bX\|
    \le 2\sup\Big\{(\theta,\bX) :\theta\in N_{1/2}\Big\}
    = 2S\,.
    \]
We can arrange for $|N_{1/2}| \le 6^N$. If $(\theta,\bX)$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $\sigma^2$ for all $\theta\in B_N$, then a union bound over the net $N_{1/2}$ gives
    \beq
    \P\bigg(\frac{\|\bX\|}{N^{1/2}} \ge 2t\bigg)
    \le \P(S \ge N^{1/2} t)
    \le 6^N 
    \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{Nt^2}{2\sigma^2}\bigg\}
    \le \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{Nt^2}{4\sigma^2}\bigg\}\,,
    \eeq
where the last bound holds provided
$t\ge 3\sigma$. Integrating (similarly to \eqref{e:subgaus.mmt}) gives the moment bound
    \beq
    \frac{\E[ \|\bX\|^p]}{N^{p/2}}
    \le
    \frac{2^p \E(S^p)}{N^{p/2}}
    \le (6\sigma)^p
    +2^p \int_{3\sigma}^\infty
    pt^{p-1}
    \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{Nt^2}{4\sigma^2}\bigg\}\, dt
    \le C_p \sigma^p
    \eeq
for a constant $C_p$ depending only on $p$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: The Euler-Maclaurin formula relates the sum of a sufficiently smooth function f over consecutive integers a, a+1, ..., b to the integral of f over [a,b]. It states this sum equals the integral of f from a to b, plus (f(a)+f(b))/2, plus a finite sum for k=1 to m of B_{2k}/(2k)! times [f^{(2k-1)}(b) - f^{(2k-1)}(a)], where B_{2k} are Bernoulli numbers and f^{(2k-1)} denotes the (2k-1)-th derivative, plus an explicit, boundable remainder term. It is used to approximate sums by integrals, accelerate numerical summation of slowly convergent series, and derive Stirling's approximation. Found independently by Euler and Maclaurin in the 1730s.
title: Euler-Maclaurin formula

Fix positive input/output dimensions n_in,q, a nonzero deterministic input x in R^n_in, and positive constants alpha,lambda. Let n be the hidden width and d the number of residual blocks. All entries of W_0 (n by n_in), W_l (n by n), and W_out (q by n) are mutually independent N(0,1). Independently draw iid uniform signs s_lj in {-1,+1}, one per block and coordinate, and freeze them at initialization. Define z_0=W_0 x/sqrt(n_in), z_l=alpha z_(l-1)+lambda sqrt(2/n) W_l ReLU(s_l multiplied coordinatewise by z_(l-1)), and z_out=W_out z_d/sqrt(n). Write kappa=(5lambda^4+4alpha^2 lambda^2)/(alpha^2+lambda^2)^2 and beta_n=2/n+kappa d/n. There is an exact distributional representation z_out=(||x||_2/sqrt(n_in))(alpha^2+lambda^2)^(d/2) exp(G_n/2) Z, where Z is standard Gaussian in R^q independent of G_n. Its radial variable can be chosen as G_n=log(n_in ||z_d||_2^2/[n ||x||_2^2 (alpha^2+lambda^2)^d]). If n,d tend to infinity with d/n tending to a positive finite r, Theorem4 gives E[G_n]=-beta_n/2+O(d/n^2), Var(G_n)=beta_n+O(d/n^2), and G_n converges in distribution to H~N(-kappa r/2,kappa r). Thus the output normalized by its deterministic prefactor converges to exp(H/2)Z with H and Z independent. Constants in the error terms may depend on alpha,lambda and fixed lower/upper positive bounds on d/n. This is the marginal law for one fixed input, not a joint multiple-input process. The balanced result does not assume the vanilla model’s Conjecture5. The positivity restriction alpha>0 retains a nonzero skip connection and avoids finite-width extinction in the logarithm.

Let f_m:R^d->R be convex differentiable functions with beta-Lipschitz gradients, beta>0, sharing a minimizer w_star. For each t=1,...,J and m, let g_(t,m):R^d->R be a deterministic convex differentiable surrogate. Suppose nu_t>=0 and, for every w,m,t, 0<=g_(t,m)(w)-g_(t,m)(w_star)<=f_m(w)-f_m(w_star)<=(1+nu_t*beta)*[g_(t,m)(w)-g_(t,m)(w_star)]. Take independent uniform task indices tau_1,...,tau_J in {1,...,M}, deterministic w_1, and deterministic finite steps eta_t>=nu_t. Let w_(t+1)=w_t-eta_t*grad g_(t,tau_t)(w_t), gbar_t=M^(-1)*sum_m g_(t,m), and choose deterministic weights 0<v_0<=v_1<=...<=v_J. Assume the expectations of the displayed gaps, gradient squares and iterate squared distances are finite. Define cplus_t=eta_t*v_t^2-(1+eta_t*beta)*(v_t-v_(t-1))*sum_(s=t)^J eta_s*v_s. Then sum_(t=1)^J cplus_t*E[gbar_t(w_t)-gbar_t(w_star)] <=v_0^2*||w_1-w_star||^2/2 +(1/2)*sum_(t=1)^J eta_t^2*v_t^2*E||grad g_(t,tau_t)(w_t)||^2. The plus sign is essential under these unrestricted-step hypotheses; the printed minus-sign version is false.

Let U_n be a U-statistic with symmetric kernel h of degree m and \mathbb{E}[h(X_1, \dots, X_m)^2] < \infty. Let \theta = \mathbb{E}[h(X_1, \dots, X_m)] and define the projection h_1(x) = \mathbb{E}[h(x, X_2, \dots, X_m)] - \theta. Then U_n decomposes as U_n - \theta = \frac{m}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n h_1(X_i) + R_n, where \mathbb{E}[R_n] = 0 and \text{Var}(R_n) = O(n^{-2}).
U_n is a U-statistic with symmetric kernel h

body: [Definition 10 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $n\in\Nsf$ and let $M$ be a manifold. A \emph{rough velocity field} is a smooth section of $R_n^2M$, i.e.\ a smooth function $f:M\to R_n^2M$ such that $(\pi\circ f)(p) = p$ holds for every $p\in M$.

body: In linear algebra, the singular value decomposition (SVD) is a factorization of a real or complex matrix into a rotation, followed by a scaling, followed by another rotation. It generalizes the eigendecomposition of a square normal matrix with an orthonormal eigenbasis to any $m\times n$ matrix. It is related to the polar decomposition, and is a common means for implementing low-rank approximation for matrices.

\[
q_n=x\sqrt n+O(1),
\qquad
q_n\equiv n-1\pmod2.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n\to\infty}\log F_n(q_n)
=
\log(1+x)-\frac12.
\end{equation}

[Theorem 1 (Szeg\H{o} limit) of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\) and \(I_a=[1,a]\). For every \(\theta\in\mathbb{R}\), the limit
\[
\Lambda_a(\theta):=\lim_{L\to\infty}\Lambda_{a,L}(\theta)
\]
exists, and the convergence is locally uniform in \(\theta\in\mathbb{R}\). Moreover,
\[
\Lambda_a(\theta)
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}
\int_0^{\infty}
\log\left(
1+(e^{\theta}-1)(e^{-2\xi}-e^{-2a\xi})
\right)
\,\mathrm{d}\xi.
\]
The function \(\Lambda_a\) is real analytic on \(\mathbb{R}\) and extends holomorphically to \(S_{\pi}\), where the logarithm is the branch obtained by analytic continuation from \(\theta=0\). Furthermore,
\begin{equation}

\Lambda_a'(0)
=
\frac{1}{4\pi}\left(1-\frac{1}{a}\right),
\qquad 
\Lambda_a''(0)
=
\frac{(a-1)(a+3)}{8\pi a(a+1)}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Szeg\H{o} limit

PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. Under (IID)+(UE) transience in direction l gives the Sznitman-Zerner regeneration structure with tau_1 < infinity a.s.; ballisticity is E[tau_1 | D = infinity] < infinity (Drewitz-Ramirez Open Question 2.20). Under (UE) a trap of diameter r holds the walk at most exponentially long in r, so sub-ballistic behaviour needs polynomially rare traps of logarithmic size along the path, which i.i.d. environments do allow; the question is whether the tail P(tau_1 > n) can be as heavy as n^{-1+eps}. Open Question 3.20 (does positive velocity imply (P)_M for M > 15d + 5) asks at least as much as whether a finite first moment of tau_1 self-improves to higher moments: (P)_M for M >= 15d + 5 implies (T') and with it finite moments of tau_1 of every order, so a yes to 3.20 gives the self-improvement. The converse, (P)_M from a moment of tau_1 of order about M/d, is not established, so reading 3.20 as equivalent to moment self-improvement is a conjecture, not a reduction. The Guerra-Ramirez theorem (T) <=> (T') (2018) settles Open Question 3.28 but neither of these. Recorded as a one-directional moment-self-improvement reformulation.

Let U ⊂ C be open and connected, let f_n be holomorphic on U, and assume the family {f_n} is uniformly bounded on every compact subset of U. Assume also that the limit of f_n(z) exists in C for every z in a set E ⊂ U that has at least one accumulation point inside U. Then f_n converges uniformly on every compact subset of U, and the limit is holomorphic on U. (This is the complex-analytic Vitali convergence theorem; it is unrelated to the measure-theoretic theorem of the same family of names.)

Let nu be a real signed Borel measure on R such that every polynomial is absolutely integrable with respect to its total variation. Suppose q_0,...,q_(N+1), for an integer N>=0, are monic orthogonal polynomials for nu with deg(q_j)=j. Fix 0<=i<=N and r in R such that q_i(r)!=0. Assume that (t-r)dnu(t) has a unique monic polynomial of degree i orthogonal to all polynomials of degree<i. Then that polynomial is [q_(i+1)(t)+alpha_i q_i(t)]/(t-r), where alpha_i=-q_(i+1)(r)/q_i(r). The numerator vanishes at r, so the quotient is a polynomial. The existence and uniqueness assumption for the modified signed measure is essential; positivity of nu is not assumed. This is Cohn-Kumar Lemma3.3.

monic orthogonal family through degree N+1
0<=i<=N; r real; q_i(r)!=0

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2607.13273, 'Asymptotics of transition densities for L\'evy processes with stochastic resetting'] Let $\beta\in(0,1)$ and $Y_t$ be a $\beta$ -- stable subordinator, i.e., real-valued L\'evy process with non-decreasing sample paths, such that 
	\[
          \mE e^{-s Y_t} = 
          e^{-t s^\beta},\quad s,t>0, 
	\]
        and $\mP(Y_t<0)=0$ for all $t>0.$ Then, for all $\lambda>0, t>0,$ and $x\in\R,$ the density $p_\lambda(t,x,\cdot)$ of
        the corresponding process with resetting exists and satisfies
        \begin{equation}
		   p_\lambda(t,x,u)\sim_{t,u}\,\, \frac{\beta}{\lambda\Gamma(1-\beta)}u^{-1-\beta}.
	\end{equation}

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Consider the setup described just above. There exists a unique (up to a deterministic factor) collection of measurable functions $\Gamma^D \mapsto \rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}$ for each simply connected domain $D \subseteq \C$ where each $\rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D} = ((\rformres{k}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}, \rfdomainres{\Upsilon_k}{\Gamma^D}))_{k \in \N}$ is a collection of resistance forms with the following properties. There is a further collection of resistance forms $((\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}, \rfdomainres{V}{\Gamma^D}))_{V \in \metregions}$ such that the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[I.]
 \item For each $k \in \N$ we have that $(\rformres{k}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}, \rfdomainres{\Upsilon_k}{\Gamma^D})$ is a local, regular resistance form on $\Upsilon_k$. Its associated resistance metric $\rmetres{k}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D}$ is topologically equivalent to $\dpathY[\Upsilon_k]$.
 \item Let $V_1,\ldots,V_n \in \metregions[k]$, $n \in \N$, such that $V_i \cap V_j = \emptyset$ for $i \neq j$ and $\bigcup_i \ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_k = \Upsilon_k$. Then
 \begin{align*}
  \rfdomainres{\Upsilon_k}{\Gamma^D} &= \{ f : f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_k} \in \rfdomainres{V_i}{\Gamma^D} \text{ for each } i \} ,\\
  \text{and}\quad
  \rformres{k}{f}{f}{\Gamma^D} &= \sum_i \rformres{V_i}{f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_k}}{f|_{\ol{V_i} \cap \Upsilon_k}}{\Gamma^D} .
 \end{align*}
\item If $V,V' \in \metregions[k]$, $V \subseteq V'$, and $f\colon \ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_k \to \R$ is a continuous function that is constant on each $\dpathY$-connected component of $\ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_k \setminus \ol{V}$, then
\begin{align*}
 & f \in \rfdomainres{V'}{\Gamma^D} \text{ if and only if } f|_{\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_k} \in \rfdomainres{V}{\Gamma^D} \\
 \text{and}\quad & \rformres{V'}{f}{f}{\Gamma^D} = \rformres{V}{f}{f}{\Gamma^D} .
\end{align*}
 \item For each open set $U \subseteq \C$, the collection of forms $(\rformres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D})_{V \in \metregions[U]}$ is a.s.\ a measurable function of $\Gamma^D|_U$ that does not depend on the choice of $D$.
\item For each simply connected domain $D \subseteq \C$ and $z \in \C$, we have
\[ \rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D} = \rform{T_{z}\cdot}{T_{z}\cdot}{\Gamma^D+z} \quad\text{a.s.,} \]
where $T_{z} f = f(\cdot -z)$ denotes translation by $z$.
\item There exists a constant $\resexp > 0$ so that the following holds. For each simply connected domain $D \subseteq \C$ and $\lambda > 0$, we have
\[ \rform{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma^D} = \lambda^{\resexp}\rform{S_{\lambda}\cdot}{S_{\lambda}\cdot}{\lambda\Gamma^D} \quad\text{a.s.,} \]
where $S_{\lambda} f = f(\lambda^{-1}\cdot)$.
\end{enumerate}
The analogous statement holds for the \clekp{} Brownian motion. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let (X,Sigma,mu) be a probability space (more generally a finite measure space) and T: X -> X a measurable, measure-preserving transformation (mu(T^{-1}A)=mu(A) for all A in Sigma). Then for every measurable A with mu(A)>0, mu-almost every x in A returns to A infinitely often: for a.e. x in A there are infinitely many n>=1 with T^n(x) in A.
(X,Sigma,mu) is a finite (e.g. probability) measure space
T is measurable and measure-preserving

Let N take values in {0, 1, ..., m} on a probability space, mu = E[N] > 0 and beta = E[binom(N, 2)] = E[N(N-1)/2]; put x = 2 beta / mu and r = 1 + floor(x). Then 1 <= r <= m and P(N > 0) >= D := 2 mu/(r+1) - 2 beta/(r(r+1)); writing theta = x - (r - 1) in [0, 1), D = mu[(1 - theta)/r + theta/(r+1)]. This r maximizes the bound of the linear family over integers r >= 1: when x is a positive integer, r = x and r = x + 1 tie and r is the latter; when x = 0, r = 1 is the unique maximizer. Integer values are needed: for X = 3/2 surely, with beta read as E[X(X-1)/2], mu = 3/2, beta = 3/8, r = 1 and the formula gives 9/8 > 1 = P(X > 0).
N is integer valued with 0 <= N <= m
mu = E[N] > 0

[Thm A. thm: convergence in hatC of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Convergence in $\widehat{C}_{c}(M, \Xi)$}]  
  Let $f, f_{1}, f_{2}, \ldots$ be elements of $\widehat{C}_{c}(M, \Xi)$.
  The following conditions are equivalent.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item  
      The functions $f_{n}$ converge to $f$ in the compact-convergence topology with variable domains.
    \item 
        The sets $\dom(f_{n})$ converge to $\dom(f)$ in the Hausdorff topology in $M$,
        and there exist functions $g_{n}, g \in C(M, \Xi)$ such that $g_{n}|_{\dom(f_{n})} = f_{n}$, $g|_{\dom(f)} = f$
        and $g_{n} \to g$ in the compact-convergence topology.
    \item 
      The sets $\dom(f_{n})$ converge to $\dom(f)$ in the Hausdorff topology in $M$,
      and, for any $x_{n} \in \dom(f_{n})$ and $x \in \dom(f)$ with $x_{n} \to x$,
      it holds that $f_{n}(x_{n}) \to f(x)$.
  \end{enumerate}
