[Lemma 14 (Residual identity) of arXiv:2609.02389, 'The Class Edge-Reconstruction Number of a\\ Maximal Planar Graph Is One or Two'] Suppose the same card has completions \(G=C+e\) and \(H=C+e'\), and set
\[
                  Q=A_G(e)-A_H(e').
\]
If \(G-g\cong H-h\), then
\[
                  A_G(g)-A_H(h)=Q.                 \tag{C.1}
\]
Write \(Q=P-N\), where \(P,N\) have disjoint supports and nonnegative
integer entries.  Their common total mass \(r\) is zero, one, or two.  If
every edge card of \(G\) has a degree-sequence match among the edge cards of
\(H\), then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em]
\item if \(r=2\), every edge of \(G\) has the same unordered endpoint-degree
pair;
\item if \(r=1\), the vertices of one fixed degree form a vertex cover of
\(G\);
\item if \(r=0\), then \(Q=0\).
\end{enumerate}

Let V be an affine algebraic set and p in V with local dimension dim_p(V) >= 1. For a general affine hyperplane H passing through p, the local dimension drops by exactly 1: dim_p(V intersect H) = dim_p(V) - 1.

body:
[Lem LM41 of arXiv:2608.16170, '\bf On hitting time distributions of Markov processes with sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds'] Let $X$ be a Borel right process on $(E,d)$ satisfying (AC), (H1a) and (H1b).

Let $B\subset E$ be a nearly Borel set of finite $1$-order capacity. Then for any $\lambda>0$, there exists a unique finite, positive measure $\nu^{(\lambda)}_B$ on $E$ with $\mathrm{supp}[\nu_B^{(\lambda)}]\subset \overline{B}$ such that
\begin{equation}
     p_B^{(\lambda)}(x):=\mathbb{E}^x[\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda \sigma_B}]=\int_E u_\lambda(x,y)\nu_B^{(\lambda)}(\mathrm{d} y),\quad \forall x\in E.
 \end{equation}
In particular, for any $\lambda>0$, 
\[
{\mathbb{P}}^x\left[\sigma_B\le t\right] \ge \emph{Cap}_{(\lambda)}(B)  \inf_{y\in \overline B} \int_0^t \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda s} p(s, x, y)\mathrm{d} s,\quad \forall t>0,x\in E.
\]
title: Lem LM41 of arXiv:2608.16170

[Definition 44 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Fix $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$. We define the contours 
$$\gamma^+_N(a,0) = \{1 + aN^{-1/3} + |s|N^{-1/3} e^{\mathrm{sgn}(s)\im(\pi/3)}: s \in [-N^{1/4}, N^{1/4}] \}, \mbox{and }$$
$$\gamma^-_N(a,0) = \{1 + aN^{-1/3} + |s|N^{-1/3} e^{\mathrm{sgn}(s) \im(2\pi/3)}: s \in [-N^{1/4}, N^{1/4}] \},$$
both oriented in the direction of increasing imaginary part. We further let $\gamma^+_N(a,1)$ be the arc of the $0$-centered circle that connects the points $1 + aN^{-1/3} + N^{-1/12} e^{\im(\pi/3)}$ to $1 + aN^{-1/3} + N^{-1/12} e^{-\im(\pi/3)}$, and $\gamma^-_N(a,1)$ be the arc of the $0$-centered circle that connects the points $1 + aN^{-1/3} + N^{-1/12} e^{\im(2\pi/3)}$ to $1 + aN^{-1/3} + N^{-1/12} e^{-2\im(\pi/3)}$. Both $\gamma^+_N(a,1)$ and $\gamma^-_N(a,1)$ are oriented counter-clockwise. Finally, we set $\gamma_N^+(a) = \gamma_N^+(a,0) \cup \gamma_N^+(a,1)$ and $\gamma_N^-(a) = \gamma_N^-(a,0) \cup \gamma_N^-(a,1)$. See Figure \ref{S21} for an illustration of these contours. We also recall from Section \ref{Section4.2} that $C_r$ is the positively oriented zero-centered circle of radius $r > 0$.

[Theorem thm:int-0 of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $\bm{X}$ be 
a genuinely $d$-dimensional L\'evy process and $\bm{Z}$ a  standard Gaussian random vector in $\mathbb{R}^d$. 

Let $\mathscr{A}$ be either $\mathscr{K}$ or $\mathscr{C}$ defined above. Then the following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=2.5em, nosep]
\item[{\nf(a)}] 
 $\mathds{E}[|\bm{X}_1|^2]<\infty$.
\item[{\nf(b)}] There exist measurable $\bm{A}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\bm{B}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, such that $\bm{B}(t)$ is invertible for all sufficiently large $t$, the limits $\bm{e}_j^\intercal \bm{B}(t)^\intercal \bm{B}(t)\bm{e}_j \to \infty$ and $\bm{B}(t)^{-1}\bm{B}(f(t))\to \bm{I}_d$ hold for all $j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and non-decreasing functions $f$ with $f(t)/t\to 1$ as $t \to \infty$, respectively, and 
\[
t \mapsto t^{-1}d_\mathscr{A}(\bm{X}_t-\bm{A}(t),\bm{B}(t) \bm{Z} )\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(+\infty).
\]
\end{itemize}
Moreover,  for any function $\bm{B}$ satisfying condition~{\normalfont{(b)}}, we have $\lim_{t\to\infty}d_\mathscr{C}(\bm{X}_t-t\mathds{E}\bm{X}_1,\bm{B}(t) \bm{Z} )=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\ell_{\mathrm{LL}}\bigl(\pi,\phi\bigr)=\ell_{\mathrm{LL}}\bigl(v^{-1}\pi,v^{-1}\phi\bigr).
    $$ 
    \end{enumerate}

Use the network and empirical FIM in assumptions. Suppose explicitly that, for each of the finitely many t,k,l, ||h_(l-1)(x_t)||^2/M_(l-1)->qhat_(l-1) and ||delta_(k,l)(x_t)||^2->qtilde_l, with the same deterministic limits for each t,k. These limits may be assumed almost surely or in probability; the conclusion holds in the same mode. Let P=sum_(l=1)^L M_l*(M_(l-1)+1), alpha=sum_(l=1)^(L-1) alpha_l*alpha_(l-1)>0, m_lambda=Tr(F)/P, and kappa_1=(1/alpha)*sum_(l=1)^L alpha_(l-1)*qtilde_l*qhat_(l-1). Then M*m_lambda->C*kappa_1. Taking qhat,qtilde from the companion mean-field closure gives the leading formula in source Theorem1, m_lambda~C*kappa_1/M when kappa_1>0. This card makes the norm-limit premise explicit; it does not prove that premise or the backward decoupling closure for the original tied-weight network. It concerns the mean, not the second moment or largest eigenvalue.
Fixed L>=2 and fixed positive integers C,T. Widths M_l/M->alpha_l>0 for l=0,...,L-1; M_L=C. Hidden layers h_l=phi(u_l), u_l=W_l*h_(l-1)+b_l; output f=u_L is linear.
Independent Gaussian initialization W_l[i,j]~N(0,sigma_w^2/M_(l-1)) and b_l[i]~N(0,sigma_b^2), sigma_w>0 and sigma_b>0. Inputs are iid standard Gaussian. Parameters theta include all weights and biases.
phi and phi_prime have finite squared Gaussian integrals at each recursively occurring preactivation variance. The empirical FIM normalization is F=(1/T)*sum_(t=1)^T sum_(k=1)^C grad_theta f_k(x_t)*grad_theta f_k(x_t)^T.
The explicitly stated forward/backward norm limits are assumptions. Fixed finite T,C,L; alpha_l>0; qhat,qtilde finite and common across samples and output coordinates.

$C\cap E_{\underline{r}}(\omega)\subset C_0^{\beta_0}$ and 
\[
C\cap E_{\underline{r}}(\omega)
           \begin{cases} 
                  =\emptyset&\text{ if } \, C_0^{\beta_0}=\emptyset,\\
                  \ne\emptyset&\text{ if }\,  C_0^{\beta_0}\ne\emptyset.
           \end{cases}       
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem construction_muf of arXiv:2604.23751, 'Large deviation principles for pattern-avoiding permutations, and limit shapes for constra'] Let $f\in\mathcal{F}$.
There exists a unique $231$-avoiding permuton $\mu_f$ such that
\begin{equation}
    \text{for all }(x,y)\in[0,1]^2,\quad
    \mu_f([x,1] \times [0,y])=P_f(x,y).
\end{equation}
Moreover, the RLM-curve of $\mu_f$ is $f$.

body: In mathematics, especially general topology and mathematical analysis, compactness is a property of a space that makes it behave in many ways like a finite set. For instance, on a finite set every infinite sequence must take some value infinitely often, by the pigeonhole principle. For subsets of Euclidean space, the analogous statement is sequential compactness: a set is compact if and only if every infinite sequence in the set has a subsequence that converges to a point of the set. Likewise, whereas every real-valued function on a finite set is bounded and attains its maximum and minimum, every continuous real-valued function on a compact space has these properties. For compact subsets of Euclidean space, this is the extreme value theorem.
title: Compact space

[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2512.05340, 'The rate of convergence of the critical mean-field $O(N)$ magnetization via multivariate n'] Let $V$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{assumption: assumptions on V} and let $\mu$ be the probability measure with Lebesgue density proportional
  to $e^{-V}$. Then:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
  \item  The equation~\eqref{eq: overdamped langevin} is well posed
  \item For each fixed $x,u,v,w\in\RR^d$, equations~\eqref{eq: overdamped langevin}, \eqref{eq: 1st
    variation}, \eqref{eq: 2nd variation} and~\eqref{eq: 3rd variation} have unique solutions
  \item The process $X_t^x$ is 3-times mean-square differentiable with respect to $x$, and for all
    $u,v,w\in\RR^d$ we have $D_u X_t^x=\sU_{u}^x(t)$, $D_v D_u X_t^x =\sU_{u,v}^x(t)$ and $D_w D_v D_u X_t^x =
    \sU_{u,v,w}^x(t)$  

  \item For each $h\in\smoothlip$, the unique classical solution to the corresponding parabolic problem
    \begin{equation}
      \begin{split}
        \frac{\partial u(t, x)}{\partial t} &= \mathrm{L}\, u(t, x),  \qquad t>0, \,x\in \RR^{d},\\
        u(0, x) &= h(x),  \quad \qquad x\in \RR^{d},
        \end{split}
    \end{equation}
    is given by $u(t,x) = P_t h(x)$.
  \item For each $h\in\smoothlip$, and each fixed $t\ge0$, if $u(t,x)=P_t h(x)$ then
    $u(t,\cdot)\in C^2(\RR^d)$
  \item For each $h\in\smoothlip$, and each fixed $x\in\RR^d$, if $u(t,x)=P_t h(x)$ then
    $u(\cdot,x)\in C^1(0,\infty)$
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 8 of arXiv:2512.05340

[Corollary cor: duality of arXiv:2504.04792, 'Uniqueness and Longtime Behavior of the Completely Positively Correlated Symbiotic Branchi'] Let $\dot{W}$ and $\dot{W_0}$ be two independent white noises on $\mathbb{R}_+ \times \mathbb{R}$. Let $\psi \in C_{\text{tem}}^+$ and $\phi \in C_{\text{rap}}^+$. Define $(V_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\Tilde{V}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ as the unique solutions with values in $C_{\text{tem}}^+$ and $C_{\text{rap}}^+$, respectively, of equation $((eq: dual of the paper))$, driven by $\dot{W}$ and $\dot{W_0}$, respectively, with initial conditions $V_0 = \psi$  and $\Tilde{V}_0 = \phi$. Then, for each $T > 0$, the following self-duality formula holds:
\begin{equation}

    \mathbb{E}\left[e^{-\langle \Tilde{V}_T, \psi \rangle}\right] = \mathbb{E}\left[e^{-\langle \phi, V_T \rangle }\right].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics, the uniform boundedness principle or Banach–Steinhaus theorem is one of the fundamental results in functional analysis. Together with the Hahn–Banach theorem and the open mapping theorem, it is considered one of the cornerstones of the field. In its basic form, it asserts that for a family of continuous linear operators whose domain is a Banach space, pointwise boundedness is equivalent to uniform boundedness in operator norm.
title: Uniform boundedness principle

[Lem 144 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall $s$ and $s_\delta$ from 
\eqref{e:s.sqrt.fn} and \eqref{e:s.sqrt.fn.delta}.
  There exists $C=C(L)$ such that for all $t\in [q_0,1]$,
  \[
     \Big|s(t)
      -s_{\delta}(t)\Big|
  \le C\delta.
  \]

\begin{proof}
Since $p(q_0)\geq 1/L$ and $p$ is increasing, we have
\[
  s(t) + s_\delta(t) \ge s(t) \ge L^{-1/2}\,.
\]
By adjusting $C$ appropriately it suffices to show
  \[
     \Big|s(t)^2
      -s_{\delta}(t)^2\Big|
  \le C\delta.
  \]
Note that
$s_\delta(t)^2$ is the average value of $s(t)^2$ on the interval $[t_\delta,t_{\delta+}]$:
  \[
  s_\delta(t)^2
  = \frac{t_{\delta+} p(t_{\delta+})
    -
    t_{\delta} p(t_{\delta})
    }{\delta}
    = \frac{1}{\delta}\int_{t_\delta}^{t_{\delta_+}}
    (tp)'(t)\,dt
    = \frac{1}{\delta}\int_{t_\delta}^{t_{\delta_+}} s(t)^2\,dt\,.
  \]
By the mean-value theorem, it suffices to show that $s(t)^2=(tp)'(t)$ is Lipschitz, which is clear since assumption (\ref{i:IAMP-main-p}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main} gives that  $\|p\|_{C^2([0,1])}\leq L$.
    \end{proof}

Let E be finite and f: 2^E -> R symmetric (f(S) = f(E \ S)) and submodular. With the posimodular slack P(A, B) = f(A) + f(B) - f(A \ B) - f(B \ A) and the submodular slack D(X, Y) = f(X) + f(Y) - f(X n Y) - f(X u Y), P(A, B) = D(A, E \ B) for all A, B, so f(A) + f(B) >= f(A \ B) + f(B \ A), with equality exactly when submodularity is tight at (A, E \ B). No normalization or monotonicity is needed. Symmetry cannot be dropped: on E = {1, 2}, f(empty) = f({1}) = f({2}) = 0 and f(E) = -1 is submodular, and A = E, B = {2} gives f(A) + f(B) = -1 < 0 = f(A \ B) + f(B \ A).
E is finite
f is real valued on all subsets of E
f(S) = f(E \ S) for every S
f is submodular

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2506.16259, 'Two-dimensional Rademacher walk'] Let $d_1,d_2,d_3\dots$ be a sequence of distinct positive integers, and let $T_k=d_1\eps_1+\dots+d_k\eps_k$ where  $\eps_i$ are i.i.d.\ Rademacher. Then for every integer $\displaystyle  m\ge \max_{1\le i\le k}d_i$ and every  $M\in\Z$ we have
$$
\P(T_k-M\equiv 0\pmod m)\le \frac{C \log k}{k}    
$$
for  some universal constant $C>0$.
title: Lemma 3 of arXiv:2506.16259

On {-1, 1}^n (n >= 1) with the uniform probability measure mu, chi_S(x) = prod over i in S of x_i for S inside [n], and f^(S) = E[f chi_S] is the Walsh-Fourier coefficient of a real function f, so f = sum over S of f^(S) chi_S. For real f put W_f(S) = sum over x of f(x) chi_S(x) = 2^n f^(S). Then sum over S of W_f(S)^2 = 2^n sum over x of f(x)^2, equivalently sum over S of f^(S)^2 = E f^2. For h = 1_A, A any subset: W_h(empty) = |A|, sum over S of W_h(S)^2 = 2^n |A| and sum over S of h^(S)^2 = mu(A); every W_h(S) is an integer congruent to |A| mod 2 with |W_h(S)| <= |A|. For f with values +-1 and n >= 1, sum over S of W_f(S)^2 = 4^n (so sum over S of f^(S)^2 = 1) and every W_f(S) is even; on the one-point cube n = 0 the single sum W = f(empty word) is odd. For sigma_A = 2 1_A - 1: W_sigma(empty) = 2|A| - 2^n and W_sigma(S) = 2 W_{1_A}(S) for nonempty S; equivalently sigma_A^(empty) = 2 mu(A) - 1 and sigma_A^(S) = 2 1_A^(S).
uniform measure
A any subset of {-1, 1}^n
n >= 1 for the evenness of +-1 sums

OWNER OWN WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited), no novelty established. For the equal-weight teacher q_a=(1/3)sum_j N(a E u_j,I_d), where d>=2, E^T E=I_2 and u_j are the unit equilateral vertices, unrestricted physical unit-step population DDPM mean GD admits a fast centroid/slow shape decomposition. Write M=a b 1^T+a sqrt(3/2) Z V^T, V=sqrt(2/3)U^T, P=EE^T, gamma=2a^2/3. On ||b||<=11, ||Z||<=5, b_+=(I/3+(2a^2/3)ZZ^T)b+O(a^4) and Z_+=Z+gamma[(P-ZZ^T)Z+2bb^T Z+O(a^2)]. For ||b_0||<=10 the centroid impulse in shape is O(a^2); the covariance-flow comparison error through rescaled time S is at most C a^2(1+||b_0||^2)exp(76(S+1)). Set sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)), S=10 log(100/(sigma_0 rho)), and choose a^2<=c rho exp(-76(S+1)) with c and rho sufficiently small absolute constants. At N=ceil(3S/(2a^2)), the unrestricted trajectory enters a fixed equilateral tube, with normalized centroid O(a^4). For iid mean initialization N(0,3a^2/(2d)), entry with surrogate angle away from the three unstable sectors has probability at least 553/1600. In that tube the full normal error contracts by 1-kappa a^2 per step and the tangent perturbation is quadratic in the normal error. This is a dynamic lemma; an empirical learning guarantee is not asserted here.

canonical mixture-score DDPM population objective at one fixed noise time
unrestricted mean parameters; physical Euclidean unit GD step
d>=2, sufficiently small fixed tube radius rho and absolute constant c
a at the stated inverse-polynomial scale; real arithmetic
C06 v1, C07 v2, C08 v2 dependencies remain unaudited

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6d39032b1739aca3943b901fde292ae0b0b1d25d12d0379c33b897387d9da88f","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/6d/6d39032b1739aca3943b901fde292ae0b0b1d25d12d0379c33b897387d9da88f.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:6e5f092d12a35c0cac86f29a54f7c5f9e8e47b935e0ecef558c294436a5c2b0d","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c10","bundle_id":"population.t309-free-centroid-ddpm-entry-normal-tracking-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and diffusion objectives","draft":"w721/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:equilateral-gaussian-mixture-ddpm-free-centroid-entry-normal-tracking","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"OWNER OWN WORK DRAFT; T309-w721-C10 v2, proof (unaudited), Target 2.

# Fast centroid relaxation releases the centering constraint in the equilateral DDPM route

This is a dynamic lemma toward the named random-initialization target. It builds on C06's free-centroid expansion and C07--C09's equilateral centered route, rather than rechecking those results. All these claims remain unaudited. The present lemma treats a centered true equilateral teacher but imposes no centroid constraint on the learned means or their initialization.

## 1. Coordinates and exact GD metric

Use the notation of C07: U is the 2-by-3 unit equilateral vertex matrix, E^T E=I_2, P=EE^T, V=sqrt(2/3)U^T and c=sqrt(3/2). Every unrestricted mean matrix has a unique decomposition

    M=a b 1^T+a c Z V^T,
    b=M1/(3a), Z=MV/(ac).

The squared Euclidean metric on means is

    ||dM||_F^2=3a^2||db||^2+c^2 a^2||dZ||_F^2.

For the exact population DDPM excess risk F_a(b,Z), physical unit-step mean GD is therefore exactly

    b_+=b-(1/(3a^2)) partial_b F_a,
    Z_+=Z-(2/(3a^2)) grad_Z F_a.                     (1)

Taking a unit step directly in b coordinates would describe a different algorithm and would miss the fast centroid rate.

## 2. Fast centroid and its impulse during covariance entry

C06 Section 5 gives, after substituting C_V=ZZ^T/2,

    F_a(b,Z)=a^2||b||^2
       +a^4[||ZZ^T-P||_F^2/4-b^T ZZ^T b]+a^6 H_a(b,Z). (2)

On ||b||<=11, ||Z||_F<=5, the remainder and any fixed finite number of parameter derivatives are bounded by absolute constants independent of d. The reason is the same finite-span Gaussian/softmax differentiation bound used in C05--C07; increasing the fixed b bound to 11 changes constants only. No analyticity assumption is needed, only the smooth Taylor remainder. We use (2) as settled input from C06, with its metric now included dynamically.

Set gamma=2a^2/3 and f(Z)=(P-ZZ^T)Z. Equation (1) becomes

    b_+=(I/3+(2a^2/3)ZZ^T)b-(a^4/3)partial_b H_a,
    Z_+=Z+gamma[f(Z)+2bb^T Z-a^2 grad_Z H_a].       (3)

For a sufficiently small absolute a and ||Z||<=5,

    ||b_+||<=||b||/2+C a^4,
    ||b_k||<=2^(-k)||b_0||+2C a^4.                 (4)

In particular initial ||b_0||<=10 keeps ||b||<11, conditional only on the shape ball. The dependence of H on b does not invalidate (4), since its b derivative is uniformly bounded throughout this ball.

Compare the Z iterates with the covariance flow of C07, on its stopped radius-5 ball. The extra forcing is bounded by C||b_k||^2+C a^2. Let e_k be the factor error and retain C07's L=76 for the leading flow. Its Euler defect is Cgamma^2. Then

    e_{k+1}<=(1+Lgamma)e_k
                    +Cgamma a^2+Cgamma||b_k||^2+Cgamma^2. (5)

The transient centroid term has total impulse

    gamma sum_{k>=0} 2*4^(-k)||b_0||^2
       =(8/3)gamma||b_0||^2=O(a^2||b_0||^2).       (6)

The constant floor in ||b_k||^2 is O(a^8). Its contribution to the geometric-series bound in (5) is O(a^8 exp(Lk gamma)), not a factor exponential in a^(-2). Thus

    e_k<=C a^2(1+||b_0||^2)exp(Lk gamma).           (7)

The usual constant-forcing geometric series also absorbs the O(a^2) remainder and Euler defect. Choosing the absolute constant in C07's bound a^2<=c rho exp(-76(S+1)) smaller accommodates ||b_0||<=10 and makes (7)<=rho/4 through N=ceil(3S/(2a^2)). The stopped bound closes induction: the exact flow has norm at most 4 and the error is less than 1, so no Z exit occurs. Together with (4), neither coordinate leaves its assumed ball.

At N, b_N=O(a^4); indeed 10*2^(-N)<=C a^4 for the specified small a and S>=1. Consequently the unrestricted means enter the same equilateral tube as C07, with an additional normalized centroid error O(a^4). The fast centroid transient changes the entry estimate by an absolute constant, not a dimension-dependent exponent or a long-time instability factor.

## 3. Gaussian initialization and its entry angle

Initialize all 3d mean entries independently as N(0,3a^2/(2d)). Orthogonal right projection onto span(1) and its complement gives Z_0 with iid N(0,1/d) entries and b_0~N(0,I_d/(2d)). In particular E||b_0||^2=1/2, so

    P(||b_0||>10)<=1/200.

Combining with C07's good centered-factor event G, of probability at least 2/5, by a union bound gives

    P(G and ||b_0||<=10)>=79/200.                  (8)

Independence follows as well from orthogonal Gaussian projections, but is not needed for this probability bound. The joint event is invariant under rotations in the teacher plane, acting simultaneously on b_0 and Z_0. The surrogate factor flow is rotation-equivariant and its planar polar factor exists on G. Thus the argument of C08 gives a uniform surrogate entry angle conditional on this joint event, in either determinant branch. Excluding delta=pi/24 neighborhoods of its three unstable angles removes exactly fraction 1/8. Hence the simultaneous entry-and-angle event has probability at least

    (79/200)*(7/8)=553/1600.                       (9)

Actual unrestricted GD inherits the small angular error via (7); its own objective has no assumed continuous rotational symmetry. The extra b_N term is normal to the equilateral subspace and does not change the projected angle.

## 4. Normal contraction for unrestricted mean parameters

Use normalized Euclidean coordinates J=M/a and the same two-dimensional equilateral linear subspace L as C08, now inside all d-by-3 mean matrices. Exact population GD preserves L. The simultaneous teacher rotation, cyclic label permutation and perpendicular reflection used in C02 still have L as their fixed space even when free means are allowed. In particular the family has zero centroid without requiring the optimization to enforce one.

Write J=v+w, v in L, w perpendicular to L. In a small fixed tube, v has radius r in [0.9,1.1] and ||w||<=rho_0. Decompose w into its centroid and centered-shape parts, using orthonormal coordinates u=sqrt(3)b and Y=cZ for the whole normalized mean space. The physical mean Hessian restricted to normal directions has blocks

    H_cc=(2/3)I+O(a^2),
    H_ss=a^2 A+O(a^2||w||+a^2||b||^2+a^4),
    H_cs=O(a^2||b||+a^4),                           (10)

where A has a dimension-independent positive lower bound and finite upper bound by C05's centered normal Hessian estimate. The centroid block follows from a^2||b||^2 in (2) and the factor 3 of the metric. The b-dependent quartic term contributes O(a^2||b||^2) to the physical shape block and O(a^2||b||) to the cross block. The sixth-order remainder contributes O(a^4). These estimates hold along normal segments within the tube.

Choose rho_0 small and then a small. Completing the square in the centroid block, whose inverse is uniformly bounded, shows that the cross-block Schur correction is O(a^4||b||^2+a^8), smaller than the positive order-a^2 shape block. Consequently, for absolute kappa>0,

    kappa a^2 I <= H_normal <= (9/10)I.             (11)

For the upper bound, the leading centroid eigenvalue is 2/3, all shape eigenvalues are O(a^2), and all remaining blocks vanish as a decreases. Bounds are in physical Euclidean mean coordinates; a single crude global Lipschitz-square estimate is not used to select the step.

Since normal gradient vanishes on L, its value at v+w equals the integral of the normal Hessian applied to w along v+t w. In physical coordinates the unrestricted unit-step normal update is therefore (I-Hbar_normal)w, with the integral block Hbar satisfying (11). Rescaling to J preserves the inequality. Hence

    ||w_+||<=(1-kappa a^2)||w||                     (12)

as long as the radial annulus and tube are retained. The unit physical step is admissible because the largest normal eigenvalue is below 1, despite the unequal centroid and shape time scales.

## 5. Tangent forcing remains quadratic

In J coordinates, use rescaled step a^2 and vector field g_a=-a^(-4)grad_J F_a. It contains a large linear centroid term of order a^(-2), so its full derivative is not uniformly bounded as a->0. However that term is entirely normal: its tangent projection onto L is identically zero. The tangent part and its first two derivatives are uniformly bounded. This follows from (2): after projection and division by a^4, the divergent centroid quadratic disappears, the quartic polynomial has bounded derivatives, and the remainder is O(a^2) with its derivatives.

Invariance of L and self-adjointness of the gradient Hessian imply Pi_L Dg_a(v)w=0 for normal w, just as in C08. Taylor's theorem applied to the tangent projection therefore gives

    ||Pi_L g_a(v+w)-g_a(v)||<=C||w||^2.             (13)

Equations (12),(13) are precisely the normal-decay and summable-tangent-forcing inputs to C08, after replacing its fixed coordinate constants by the J metric constants. They close radial confinement by the same inward leading field (1-r^2)r. Their accumulated angular impulse is O(||w_0||^2), since a^2 sum_k (1-kappa a^2)^(2k) is bounded. An a^(-2) loss from the fast centroid is not present in (13).

## Scope and audit priorities

This lemma establishes entry, entry-angle probability and full normal tracking for unrestricted means in the equilateral population case. A learning corollary is recorded separately to keep this dynamic statement distinct from its empirical concentration extension. The centered teacher, known radius, equal weights, identity covariance and equilateral geometry remain assumptions. No extension to the anisotropic trap C06 or general triangles is implied.

The least trusted steps are uniform remainder derivatives for bounded free centroid, the metric and accumulated transient in (3)--(7), and the physical-coordinate Hessian bounds (10)--(13). body: In computational complexity, problems that are in the complexity class NP but are neither in the class P nor NP-complete are called NP-intermediate, and the class of such problems is called NPI. Ladner's theorem, shown in 1975 by Richard E. Ladner, is a result asserting that, if P ≠ NP, then NPI is not empty; that is, NP contains problems that are neither in P nor NP-complete. Since it is also true that if NPI problems exist, then P ≠ NP, it follows that P = NP if and only if NPI is empty.
title: NP-intermediate

body: Record of outside readings, 14 October 2026, of Y. Shmalo, A nonergodic flow rule with Galton-Watson stationary measure (repository yspennstate/nonergodic-galton-watson-flow-rule, commit 837dd0c8da7d), which answers Lyons-Peres Question 17.18 negatively. Two readers working from fresh clones without seeing each other, one a Claude model and one a Codex model, both found the argument correct, with no fatal or major finding. They agree on the question's wording and location (Probability on Trees and Networks, 2016 hardback p. 572; Question 3 of Section 10 of Lyons, Pemantle and Peres 1995), that a flow rule may send zero flow to a child (strict positivity is the extra hypothesis of Proposition 17.17), on d_1 = 5/16 and d_2 = 1849/8192, and that GW(.|C = 0) and GW(.|C = 1) are the two ergodic components; one reader also checked stationarity on all Borel sets, the other simulated 333,300 finite trees to depth 15 with no bias after the flow step (a biased control was detected). Minor findings: 'stationary' should allow sigma-finite measures; the step from Borel coordinates to a Borel flow needs one sentence; the repository's check script reports failures but exits with status 0. The n-ray example of Exercise 17.22 gives only absolute continuity, so it does not already answer the question, and a web and arXiv search found no earlier answer (Rousselin 2017/2018 assumes strictly positive child masses). Not refereed.
title: Outside readings of the nonergodic Galton-Watson flow rule (Lyons-Peres Question 17.18), 14 October 2026: two independent readings find it correct

Let X be a real random variable with characteristic function f(t) = E exp(itX) and Q(X; l) = sup_x P(x <= X <= x + l). For all l > 0 and a > 0: Q(X; l) <= (96/95)^2 max(l, 1/a) int_{|t|<a} |f(t)| dt. With a = 1/l: Q(X; l) <= (96/95)^2 l int_{|t|<1/l} |f(t)| dt. Consequently, if int |f| < infinity, X has a density bounded by (96/95)^2 int |f| (Fourier inversion gives the better constant 1/(2 pi)).

Assumes: any real random variable; l > 0, a > 0

[Lemma a16 of arXiv:2411.19926, 'Sparse Pseudospectral Shattering'] Suppose $A$ has distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\cdots,\lambda_n$ ordered such that $\kappa(\lambda_1)=\max_j\kappa(\lambda_j)$.
    Then

[Proposition 102 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be a monoid, $K$ be a finite set, $f(k)\in \mf A$ for all $k\in K$, and $x = \finsum_{k\in K}f(k)$.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] Let $\tau\colon J\to K$ be a bijection. Then $x = \finsum_{j\in J}f(\tau(j))$.
  \item[(ii)] Let $g(k)\in \mf A$ for all $k\in K$. Then $\finsum_{k\in K}(f(k) + g(k)) = x + \finsum_{k\in K}g(k)$.
  \item[(iii)] Let $\mf B$ be a monoid and $\varphi\colon\mf A\to\mf B$ be a monoid homomorphism. Then $\finsum_{k\in K} \varphi(f(k)) = \varphi(x)$.  
  \item[(iv)] Let $K = I\cup J$, where $I\cap J = \varnothing$. Then $x = \finsum_{k\in I}f(k) + \finsum_{k\in J}f(k)$.
  \item[(v)] Let $f(k) = 0$ for all $k\in K$. Then $x = 0$.
  \end{enumerate}

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a195ea190c4f4c90821eeb752d856ee0283beb1d7574178d86fc9042d1e1bc52","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a1/a195ea190c4f4c90821eeb752d856ee0283beb1d7574178d86fc9042d1e1bc52.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:00f2f50b0458da289a7211d057d656d5e10720aa60861f9d0d5f0f8ddb63463b","bundle_entry_key":"stationary-variance-strict-monotonicity-common-hessian","bundle_id":"population.t362-jn-monotonicity-009","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"optimization; random reshuffling; geometric sums; stationary variance monotonicity","draft":"w732/bundle_011.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.randomreshuffling:common-hessian-random-reshuffling-jn-strict-monotonicity","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C010 v1: strict monotonicity of J_n and the explicit C004 limit

Kind: lemma. Target: 1, requested by the reviewer after PASS of C004.
Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty or general-RR claim.

For every fixed integer n>=2 and q in (0,2), define a=1-q and

    W_n(q)=sum_{0<=i<j<n}(a^i-a^j)^2,
    J_n(q)=q^2*W_n(q)/(2*(n-1)*(1-a^(2n))).

Then J_n is differentiable and strictly increasing on (0,2), with

    J_n(q) = [n*q/(2-q)-(1-a^n)/(1+a^n)]/[2*(n-1)],       (1)

    J_n'(q) = n*(1-a^(n-1))*(1-a^(n+1))
                /[(n-1)*(1+a)^2*(1+a^n)^2] > 0.          (2)

Consequently, in the exact hypotheses of independently checked C004 v1
(fixed n, common diagonal Hessian, x0!=0, s2>0, and
kappa_T*log(T)/T->c in (0,4)),

    kappa_T*min_eta P_T(eta) -> s2*J_n(c/2),
    kappa_T*eta_T -> c/2

for every global minimizing sequence. No claim is made about approaching
c/2 from a particular side at finite T.

## Proof

1. Since -1<a<1, both a!=1 and a!=-1, and 1-a^n and 1+a^n
are strictly positive. Every denominator below is nonzero. The finite
pairwise-square identity gives W_n=n*S2-S1^2, where

    S1=sum_{i=0}^{n-1}a^i=(1-a^n)/(1-a),
    S2=sum_{i=0}^{n-1}a^(2i)=(1-a^(2n))/(1-a^2).

These sums have n terms. Multiplying by q^2=(1-a)^2 and dividing
by 1-a^(2n) yields

    q^2*W_n/(1-a^(2n))
      = n*(1-a)/(1+a) - (1-a^n)/(1+a^n).

Here the last cancellation uses 1-a^(2n)=(1-a^n)*(1+a^n)
and 1-a^n>0. Division by 2*(n-1)>0 proves (1).

2. Differentiate (1) with respect to q, remembering da/dq=-1:

    d[q/(2-q)]/dq=2/(2-q)^2=2/(1+a)^2,
    d[(1-a^n)/(1+a^n)]/dq=2*n*a^(n-1)/(1+a^n)^2.

Thus

    J_n'=n/(n-1)*[1/(1+a)^2-a^(n-1)/(1+a^n)^2].

The numerator on a common positive denominator is

    (1+a^n)^2-a^(n-1)*(1+a)^2
      = 1-a^(n-1)-a^(n+1)+a^(2n)
      = (1-a^(n-1))*(1-a^(n+1)).

All exponents n-1 and n+1 are positive integers. Since |a|<1,
|a^k|<1 for either exponent; hence both factors are strictly positive.
This covers odd and even n, negative a, and a=0 without a parity split.
Equation (2) and the mean value theorem give strict increase on (0,2).

3. C004 v1 already proves convergence to the minimum of J_n over
[c/2,2) and convergence in distance to its argmin. By (2), that minimum
is uniquely attained at c/2. Substitution in the two independently
checked conclusions of C004 gives the displayed explicit limit and
optimizer convergence. Its boundary recovery, not an assumed finite-T
constraint q>=c/2, makes this use legitimate.

## Scope and checks

The n>=2 condition makes n-1 positive and n-1 a positive exponent.
The open q interval is needed for the geometric cancellations and positive
denominators. Endpoints q=0 and q=2 are not included in (1)-(2) as written.
The C004 corollary retains its positive stiff-noise and slow-initialization
hypotheses; this lemma does not remove them. Growing n remains out of scope
for the asymptotic corollary, even though the finite algebra holds for each n.

Finite exact checks, if completed, certify only their listed rational inputs.
Any formal check of the numerator identity concerns that algebraic identity,
not the derivative, positivity, mean-value argument or asymptotic corollary.
The exact factorization and the C004 substitution await independent audit.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:e8169642cf544470d8e437ba5ab4344377483951617d36d5008c19da19731a49","revision_digest":"sha256:6d1664a1ec55993d9eaff8bc449838dcf1f338184ec16d555666d2fa5de69914","source_id":"owner-own-work:w732:T362:C010:v1","source_revision":"C010-v1-proof-unaudited; depends on approved C004 v1 for optimizer corollary","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Owner-own-work research draft; status proof (unaudited), independent review pending. Fix a feedforward ReLU architecture with L>=1 affine layers and affine output in R^D. Each affine coefficient is fixed or one of W>=1 scalar parameter slots, possibly shared. All coefficients have magnitude <=R>0. F is the maximum number of incoming weighted edges per neuron, counting repeated uses of a shared slot. The latent law is fixed and supported on [-1,1]^d; graph and fixed coefficients are target-independent. Set K=max(1,R(F+1)) and Cnet=sqrt(D)*L*(F+1)*K^(L-1). The output laws have a W1 t-cover with at most [1+ceil(2R*Cnet/t)]^W elements for every t>0, by rounding the parameters within t/Cnet in maximum norm. For a target class whose error against every <=2^S output family is at least c(S+1)^(-alpha), the bounded-real-weight minimax error E_R is at least c[W*log2(1+ceil(2R*Cnet/t))+1]^(-alpha)-t. In particular E_R<=epsilon requires W*log2(1+ceil(2R*Cnet/epsilon))+1 >=[c/(2epsilon)]^(1/alpha). The saved density-slack manifold packing uses alpha=1/k; the fixed-volume uniform-manifold packing uses alpha=2/k, each under its own stated compatibility conditions. No novelty or unrestricted-real-weight lower rate is asserted; unbounded magnitude, changing latent law or uncounted architecture choices are excluded.
Fixed architecture and latent law; bounded cube latent support; all coefficients bounded by R; F counts edges, W counts variable slots; hidden coordinate ReLU and affine output.
title: Draft: deep ReLU bounded-real-weight Wasserstein cover with shared parameters

Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a finite measure space and let F be a subset of L^1(mu). Then F is uniformly integrable if and only if there exists a nondecreasing convex function Phi on [0, infinity) with Phi(0) = 0 and Phi(t)/t tending to infinity as t tends to infinity, such that sup over f in F of integral Phi(|f|) dmu is finite. The 'if' direction is the one used in practice: a uniform bound on a superlinear moment forces uniform integrability.
mu finite.
Phi must be convex, nondecreasing and superlinear (Phi(t)/t to infinity);
mere growth of Phi is not enough.

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.23383, 'Near-Lipschitz stability of the Kim--Milman flow map'] Let $X_0 \sim \mu$ and $Z \sim \gamma$ be independent, and write $X_t = e^{-t}\,X_0 + \sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}\,Z$.
    Then, for all $t > 0$,
    \begin{align}
        \nabla \log \frac{q_t^\mu}{\gamma}(x_t)
        &= -\frac{e^{-t}}{1-e^{-2t}}\, \E[e^{-t} X_t - X_0 \mid X_t = x_t]\,, \\[0.25em]
        \nabla^2 \log \frac{q_t^{\mu}}{\gamma}(x_t)
        &= -\frac{e^{-2t}}{1-e^{-2t}}\,I + \frac{e^{-2t}}{(1-e^{-2t})^2} \Cov(X_0 \mid X_t=x_t)\,.

body:
Consider the Hamilton-Jacobi initial value problem u_t + H(Du) = 0 in R^n times (0, infinity) with u = g at time 0, where H is convex and superlinear (H(p)/|p| tends to infinity) and g is Lipschitz. Then the function u(x,t) = min over y in R^n of ( t L( (x - y)/t ) + g(y) ), with L the Legendre transform of H, is Lipschitz, solves the equation almost everywhere, attains the initial data continuously, and is the unique viscosity solution. In particular, for H(p) = |p| the formula gives the distance-like representation u(x,t) = min over |x - y| <= t of g(y), and for g the indicator-style data of a set the solution is the signed distance function, which is why the Hopf-Lax representation is the control-theoretic tool for distance functions.
H convex AND superlinear, g Lipschitz (or merely continuous with growth conditions, with care).
Without convexity of H the formula is not the viscosity solution;
uniqueness holds in the viscosity class, not among almost-everywhere solutions, of which there are many.

[Definition of arXiv:2608.30848, '\huge \bf Limit Laws of the Iterated Logarithm Under Sub-linear Expectations'] \begin{itemize}
\item[(i)](Identical distribution) Let $\bm{X}_1$ and $\bm{X}_2$ be two $n$-dimensional random vectors defined on sub-linear expectation spaces $(\Omega_1,\mathscr{H}_1,\widehat{\mathbb E}_1)$ and $(\Omega_2,\mathscr{H}_2,\widehat{\mathbb E}_2)$, respectively. If for any $\varphi\in C_{b,Lip}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ we have
$$ \widehat{\mathbb E}_1[\varphi(\bm{X}_1)]=\widehat{\mathbb E}_2[\varphi(\bm{X}_2)], $$
then they are said to be identically distributed, denoted by $\bm{X}_1\overset{d}{=}\bm{X}_2$. If $X_i\overset{d}{=}X_1$ for each $i\geq 1$, then the sequence of random variables $\{X_n;n\geq 1\}$ is said to be identically distributed.
 \item[(ii)](Independence) In a sub-linear expectation space $(\Omega,\mathscr{H},\widehat{\mathbb E})$, a random vector $\bm{Y}=(Y_1,\cdots,Y_n)$, $Y_i\in\mathscr{H}$ is said to be independent of another random vector $\bm{X}=(X_1,\cdots,X_m)$, $X_i\in\mathscr{H}$ under $\widehat{\mathbb E}$, if for every test function $\varphi\in C_{b,Lip}(\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n)$ we have
     $$\widehat{\mathbb E} [\varphi(\bm{X},\bm{Y})]=\widehat{\mathbb E} [\widehat{\mathbb E} [\varphi(\bm{x},\bm{Y})]\vert_{\bm{x}=\bm{X}}].$$

  If for each $i\geq 1$, $X_{i+1}$ is independent of $(X_1,\cdots,X_i)$, then the sequence of random variables $\{X_n;n\geq 1\}$ is said to be independent.
\end{itemize}

For every real parameter n>=3 (in particular every integer n>=3) let p_n=n^(-1/6), a_n=n^(1/3), s_n=sqrt(n/log n), and b_n=s_n log n=sqrt(n log n). Let R_n have masses (1-p_n)/2 at each of +/-a_n and p_n/2 at each of +/-b_n. Set X_n=n+R_n. Each X_n is positive, has mean n and finite moments of every order, and |X_n/n-1|<=sqrt(log n/n)->0 for every realization.

    Var(X_n) = (1-p_n)n^(2/3) + n^(5/6) log n,
    log Var(X_n)/(2 log n) -> 5/12,
    Var(X_n)/n^(2/3) -> infinity.

It even has the known-form concentration bound at the larger subdiffusive scale:

    P(|X_n-E X_n| >= lambda sqrt(n/log n))
        <= exp(1/3) exp(-lambda/6)   for all lambda>=0 and n>=3.

For 0<=lambda<=r, the left side is at most 1 and the stated right side is at least 1. For r<lambda<=t, the left side is p_n=exp(-t/6), bounded by exp(-lambda/6). For lambda>t it vanishes. Endpoint atoms satisfy the displayed weak inequality. The variance formula follows directly from the four masses; its leading term has log exponent 5/6. Also

    E R_n^4 / Var(R_n)^2 ~ n^(1/6) -> infinity.

[Dfn 97 (occupation measures) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In the setting described above,
let $\rho_{\vY}$ be the occupation measure of the $\vY$ process, so that
	\[\int_{t,y} 
	f(t,y)\,\rho_{\vY}(dt\,dy)
	= \bE
	\int_0^1 f(t,\vY(t))\,dt\,.
	\]
Let $\rho_{D^i}$ and $\rho_{Q^{ij}}$
be the occupation measures of the drift and quadratic variation processes, so that
	\begin{align*}
	\int_{t,y}
	f(t,y) \rho_{D^i}(dt\,dy) 
	&= \bE
	\int_0^1 f(t,\vY(t))\,dD^i(t)\,,\\
	\int_{t,y} f(t,y) 
	\rho_{Q^{ij}}(dt\,dy) 
	&= \bE
	\int_0^1 f(t,\vY(t))\,dQ^{ij}(t)\,.
	\end{align*}
for any continuous bounded function $f$.

[Lem 181 (annealed second moment bounds for $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$ and $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$ as in \eqref{e:drift.error.Ising}, we have
	\[\E\Big[\Delta\bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)^2\Big]
	\le\frac{ L^{O(1)}\BUCKETS\delta}
		{N}
	 \]
for all $0\le d\le \dmax-1$, with $\BUCKETS$ as in 
\eqref{e:buckets.scB}. The same bound holds with $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$ in place of $\bar{D}^\Ising$.
	
\begin{proof} Recalling the notation from \eqref{e:normalized.vectors.y}, we can rewrite \eqref{e:drift.error.Ising} as
	\[
	\frac{\Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)}{(\delta_d)^{1/2}}
	=\frac{1}{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg(\sum_{i\in B}
	\frac{\be_i}{|B|^{1/2}},
	\by(q_{d+1})\bigg)
	\equiv \frac{(\be_B,\by(q_{d+1}))}{|B|^{1/2}}\,,
	\]
where we abbreviate $B\equiv B^\Ising$.
The vector $\be_B$ is measurable with respect to $\cG(q_d)$. It follows by applying 
Lemma~\ref{l:y.subgaus} that
	\[
	\frac{\E[\Delta \bar{D}^{\Ising}(q_d)^2]}{\delta_d}
	= \frac{1}{N}\E\bigg[
	\sum_{B\in\mathcal{B}^{\Ising}(q_d)}
	(\be_B,\by)^2\bigg]
	\le \frac{L^{O(1)}\BUCKETS}{N}\,.
	\]
This proves the claim for $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$, and the claim for
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$ follows by using \eqref{e:barD.vs.plus}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: annealed second moment bounds for $\bar{D}^{\Ising}$ and $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\Ising}$

Let X_n, X be random variables or vectors with X_n -> X in distribution as n -> infinity, and let Y_n -> c in probability for a constant c. Then X_n + Y_n -> X + c in distribution, X_n Y_n -> c X in distribution, and, provided c is not 0, X_n / Y_n -> X / c in distribution. More generally, if g(x,y) is continuous at every point (x,c), then g(X_n,Y_n) -> g(X,c) in distribution. Slutsky's theorem lets one combine a distributional limit with a probability limit as though the latter were a genuine constant. Due to Eugen Slutsky.
For the scalar arithmetic conclusions, X_n, X, and Y_n are real-valued random variables and c is a deterministic real constant.
X_n converges in distribution to X.
Y_n converges in probability to c.
For division, c is nonzero.
For a vector or general mapping formulation, explicitly choose separable metric state spaces S, T, and U; take X_n and X to be measurable S-valued random elements, Y_n to be measurable T-valued random elements, and c in T deterministic.
For the general mapping conclusion, g:S x T -> U is measurable and continuous at every point (x,c) with x in S; a weaker almost-sure continuity formulation would require a separately revised statement.
Any named vector addition, multiplication, or division operation must be explicitly defined and continuous on the selected state spaces; scalar multiplication cX is distinct from an unspecified vector product.

body:
[Proposition prop:pseudo-bloch of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Let $N=2M$ and let $\{\Sigma_a\}_{a=1}^{d}$, with $d=\tfrac{N(N+1)}2-1$, be a
trace-orthonormal basis of the traceless complex-symmetric matrices, so that
$\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma_a\Sigma_b)=\delta_{ab}$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Sigma_a=0$, and
$\Sigma_a^{T}=\Sigma_a$. Orthonormality here is meant for the bilinear trace form
$\operatorname{Tr}(\Sigma_a\Sigma_b)$, with no complex conjugation, and such a basis exists
because that form is nondegenerate on the complex-symmetric matrices, for instance
the symmetrised units $(E_{ij}+E_{ji})/\sqrt2$ for $i<j$ together with an
orthonormal set of $N-1$ real traceless diagonal matrices work. The
$\Sigma_a$ are complex symmetric, not Hermitian, so they are the bilinear analogue
of the Gell-Mann matrices rather than the matrices themselves. Write

\[
\rho_z=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}\rho_z}{N}\,\mathrm{I}+\sum_{a=1}^{d}r_a(z)\,\Sigma_a,\qquad
r_a(z)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_z\Sigma_a).
\]

Then the coordinate vector obeys the linear flow

\[
\dot r_a(z)=\sum_{b}\Omega_{ab}\,r_b(z),\qquad
\Omega_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\Sigma_a[K,\Sigma_b]\bigr),\qquad \Omega^{T}=-\Omega.
\]

Hence the flow lies in $\OO(d,\mathbb{C})$ and preserves the bilinear quantity
$\sum_a r_a^{2}$.

[Theorem thm:geounicont of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Fix $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$.
	\begin{enumerate}[nosep, label=\arabic*.]
		\item Almost surely, for all $(p; q) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, there exists at least one geodesic in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ from $p$ to $q$.
		\item Almost surely, all geodesics in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ are H\"older-$(2/3-\epsilon)$ continuous for all $\epsilon > 0$.
		\item For any fixed $(p; q) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, almost surely there is a unique geodesic in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ from $p$ to $q$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Fix training data D of size n>=1, a prior probability pi, model likelihood p(D|theta), and a test-observation distribution nu on pairs s=(y,x). For lambda in a positive open interval containing1, assume Z(lambda)=integral p(D|theta)^lambda pi(dtheta) is finite and positive, and define q_lambda(dtheta)=p(D|theta)^lambda pi(dtheta)/Z(lambda). This is likelihood-only tempering; the prior is not raised to lambda. Temperature T=1/lambda is cold when lambda>1. For a posterior rho let m_rho(y|x)=E_rho p(y|x,theta), B(rho)=E_nu[-log m_rho(y|x)], J(rho)=E_rho[-log p(D|theta)], and Ghat(rho,D)=J(rho)/n. Assume the losses used are finite and lambda->B(q_lambda) is differentiable at1. Definition1 calls the local CPE present exactly when Bprime(1)<0. This definition concerns infinitesimal cooling at1; Bprime(1)=0 alone does not imply a minimum or rule out improvement at another temperature. The authors call q_1 underfitting if some posterior rho has simultaneously B(rho)<B(q_1) and Ghat(rho,D)<Ghat(q_1,D).

[Definition DefSGP of arXiv:2410.23899, 'Tightness for interlacing geometric random walk bridges'] Fix a set $\Sigma = \llbracket 1, N \rrbracket$ with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ or $N = \infty$ and $T_0, T_1\in \mathbb{Z}$ with $T_0 \leq T_1$. A $\Sigma$-indexed geometric line ensemble $\mathfrak{L} : \Sigma \times \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ is said to satisfy the {\em interlacing Gibbs property} if it is interlacing, meaning that 
$$ L_i(j-1) \geq L_{i+1}(j) \mbox{ for all $i \in \llbracket 1, N - 1 \rrbracket$ and $j \in \llbracket T_0 + 1, T_1 \rrbracket$},$$
and for any finite $K = \llbracket k_1, k_2 \rrbracket \subseteq \llbracket 1, N - 1 \rrbracket$ and $a,b \in \llbracket T_0, T_1 \rrbracket$ with $a < b$ the following holds.  Suppose that $f, g$ are two increasing paths drawn in $\{ (r,z) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : a \leq r \leq b\}$ and $\vec{x}, \vec{y} \in \mathfrak{W}_k$ with $k=k_2-k_1+1$ altogether satisfy that $\mathbb{P}(A) > 0$ where $A$ denotes the event $$A =\{ \vec{x} = ({L}_{k_1}(a), \dots, {L}_{k_2}(a)), \vec{y} = ({L}_{k_1}(b), \dots, {L}_{k_2}(b)), L_{k_1-1} \llbracket a,b \rrbracket = f, L_{k_2+1} \llbracket a,b \rrbracket = g \},$$
where if $k_1 = 1$ we adopt the convention $f = \infty = L_0$. Then, we have for any $\{ B_i \in \Omega(a, b, x_i , y_i) \}_{i = 1}^k$ that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}\left( L_{i + k_1-1}\llbracket a,b \rrbracket = B_{i} \mbox{ for $i \in \llbracket 1, k \rrbracket$} \, \vert  A \, \right) = \mathbb{P}_{\mathsf{Inter}, \operatorname{Geom}}^{a,b, \vec{x}, \vec{y}, f, g} \left( \cap_{i = 1}^k\{ Q_i = B_i \} \right).
\end{equation}
title: Definition DefSGP of arXiv:2410.23899

Fix 0<alpha<log(2)/2 and rho in [0,1/2) with 2alpha<I(1-2rho), where I(t)=((1+t)log(1+t)+(1-t)log(1-t))/2 and I(1)=log(2). For integers N with rho N integral, let M=floor(exp(alpha N))+1 and let xi^1,...,xi^M be iid uniform patterns in {-1,+1}^N (all bits mutually independent). Conditional on the stored patterns, draw one input sigma^nu independently and uniformly on the Hamming sphere of radius rho N about xi^nu, for every nu. Set T_i(sigma)=sign(sum_mu [exp(xi_i^mu+sum_{j!=i}xi_j^mu sigma_j)-exp(-xi_i^mu+sum_{j!=i}xi_j^mu sigma_j)]). Equivalently T_i(sigma)=sign(sum_mu xi_i^mu exp(sum_{j!=i}xi_j^mu sigma_j)), since the omitted common factor is 2sinh(1)>0. Then P(exists nu exists i: T_i(sigma^nu)!=xi_i^nu) tends to zero as N tends to infinity. The sign at zero may be arbitrary. In particular rho=0 gives simultaneous fixed-point stability of every stored pattern whenever alpha<log(2)/2. This is one random corrupted input per pattern and coordinate evaluation on that initial input, not uniform correction of all Hamming-ball inputs and not a claim about an adaptively changing asynchronous trajectory. Source: Demircigil--Heusel--Lowe--Upgang--Vermet, Theorem 1.3 and Remark 1.4, arXiv:1702.01929v2, PDF p4; model equation (1), PDF p2. Integer rounding of the paper's M=exp(alpha N)+1 is immaterial.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Integrable supremum of routes to a bounded region structural attempt Result: Let L(x)=len R(0,x). Suppose on a containing square E|L(x)-L(y)|^p<=C*|x-y|^p for a p>2, with a jointly measurable version and finite mean at one anchor. On the dyadic grid of mesh2^-k there are order2^(2k) parent-child or neighbor pairs. The expected maximum increment is at most Cprime*2^(-k*(1-2/p)). This is summable, so telescoping along grid ancestors constructs a continuous modification with finite expected supremum. Check: Use max_j |Z_j|<=(sum_j |Z_j|^p)^(1/p) and Jensen, then sum the resulting geometric series. The increment bound implies stochastic continuity, identifying the modification at each deterministic point; Fubini identifies it at each independent uniform sample point, and countability handles the entire sampled sequence. Obstruction: The source only gives first moments of individual route lengths, not p-moment increments of L. Its compatibility condition does not make Euclidean route length an automatic metric with a triangle inequality, so a metric-chaining shortcut is unjustified.

body: [Proposition prop:big_loops_are_fat_simple_cle of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] Let $(\kappa_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be a sequence in $(8/3,4)$ with $\kappa_n \uparrow 4$. For all $\varepsilon>0$ such that a.s.\ no loop of $\Gamma^4$ has diameter exactly $\varepsilon$ (all but countably many $\varepsilon$, since $\varepsilon \mapsto \BE[\#\{\SCL \in \Gamma^4 \colon \diam(\SCL) \ge \varepsilon\}]$ is finite and non-increasing, hence has countably many discontinuities), the number of loops of $\Gamma^{\kappa_{n}}$ with diameter at least $\varepsilon$ converges in law as $n \to \infty$ to the number of loops of $\Gamma^4$ with diameter at least $\varepsilon$. Moreover, for all $\varepsilon, \varepsilon'>0$, there exists $\delta>0$ (depending on $\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon'$, and on the sequence $(\kappa_n)_{n \ge 1}$) such that for all $n\ge 1$, with probability at least $1-\varepsilon'$, all the loops of $\Gamma^{\kappa_n}$ with diameter at least $\varepsilon$ encircle a Euclidean ball of radius $\delta$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:haar-passive-zero of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $V_-$ and $V_+$ be orthogonal $\mathrm{SO}(n)$-modules.  On their
star dilations write $\mathscr T_\pm,\mathscr E_\pm,\mathsf Q_\pm$ and
$\mathscr G_\pm=\mathsf Q_\pm\mathscr T_\pm$ for the maps in (eq:3.2.2 of the paper).
Let $\mathsf M:(V_-)_\star\to(V_+)_\star$ be a typed passive singleton,
so that
\[
 (\mathsf Mh)(i,\theta)=M_i h(i,\theta),\qquad
 \rho_+(R_i(\theta))^*M_i\rho_-(R_i(\theta))=M_i,
 \qquad \sum_iM_i=0.
\tag{3.2.10s$_1$}
\]
Put $\mathsf S^+_{+,-}=\mathsf Q_+\mathsf M\mathscr E_-^*$.
If $\Pi_-$ is the projection onto $V_-^{\mathrm{SO}(n)}$, then
\[
 \boxed{\mathscr G_+^*\mathsf S^+_{+,-}\Pi_-=0.}
\tag{3.2.10s$_2$}
\]
Writing
$\mathsf S^-_{-,+}=\mathscr E_-\mathsf M^*\mathsf Q_+$, applying the
same statement to $\mathsf M^*$ gives the oppositely oriented identity
$\Pi_-\mathsf S^-_{-,+}\mathscr G_+=0$.
Consequently every maximal residual temporal component made only of
passive singleton supernodes is identically zero, term by term in its
weak order and finite residual gaps.  This includes either end component
under the common auxiliary Haar projection of
(lem:haar-residual of the paper).

body: Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space and let p, q in [1, infinity] be conjugate exponents, meaning 1/p + 1/q = 1 (with 1/infinity read as 0). If f is in L^p(mu) and g is in L^q(mu), then fg is in L^1(mu) and integral of |fg| dmu <= ||f||_p ||g||_q, where ||f||_p = (integral |f|^p dmu)^(1/p) for p < infinity and the essential supremum of |f| for p = infinity. The discrete form is sum |x_i y_i| <= (sum |x_i|^p)^(1/p) (sum |y_i|^q)^(1/q). For 1 < p < infinity, equality holds iff |f|^p and |g|^q are proportional a.e.
title: Holder's inequality

[Lemma 27 (Matsuda, Lemma 3.4 and Remark 3.5) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186']

Let $t>0$ be fixed.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item If $0\leq a<b\leq t$, then
as $\eps\to0$, one has
\[\mbf E\big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(B^{0,0}_t)\big]
=\frac{b-a}{2\pi}\big(\log(1/\eps)+\log t\big)+\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{b-a}\log r-\log(t-r)\d r+o(1)\]
and
\[\mbf E\big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_{\leq}}(B^0)\big]
=\tfrac{b-a}{2\pi}\big(\log(1/\eps)+\log(b-a)-1\big)+o(1).\]
\item If $0\leq a<b\leq c<d\leq t$, then as $\eps\to0$, one has
\[\mbf E\big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(B^{0,0}_t)\big]=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{c-a}^{d-a}\log r-\log(t-r)\d r
-\frac1{2\pi}\int_{c-b}^{d-b}\log r-\log(t-r)\d r+o(1).\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For Macdonald polynomials P_lambda(x; q, t) and the weights b^el_lambda(q, t) = prod over the boxes s of lambda with even leg length l(s) of b_lambda(s; q, t) = (1 - q^{a(s)} t^{l(s)+1}) / (1 - q^{a(s)+1} t^{l(s)}), where a(s) and l(s) are the arm and leg lengths of s, the summation over all partitions lambda evaluates to the explicit product: sum_lambda b^el_lambda(q, t) * P_lambda(x; q, t) = prod_{i >= 1} (t*x_i; q)_infinity / (x_i; q)_infinity * prod_{i < j} (t*x_i*x_j; q)_infinity / (x_i*x_j; q)_infinity, with (a; q)_infinity = prod_{r >= 0} (1 - a*q^r). This is Macdonald's identity (Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., p. 349, Example 4(ii)), quoted as Lemma 3.2, (3.3), of arXiv:2505.17825; its skew form, Lemma 3.3, (3.12) there, is sum_lambda b^el_lambda P_{lambda/eta}(x; q, t) = Theta_el(x) * sum_mu b^el_mu Q_{eta/mu}(x; q, t), with Theta_el(x) the product above.
Absolute convergence of the series (|x_i| < 1)
Parameters |q|, |t| < 1

[Lem deterministic_discrete_coupling_lemma of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] Let
  $Y^L$ and $\tilde Y^L$ be as in definition
  (def:discrete_discrete_coupling of the paper) and assume that
  $\sigma^1_0 = \tilde \sigma^1_0$ and
  $\sigma^2_0 = \tilde \sigma^2_0$. For any fixed realization, one has
$$
\left| S^L(T) \right| \ge L - 1 \implies \inf \{ t \ge 0 : y^L(t) = \tilde y^L(t) \} \le T,
$$
\green{where $S^L(t)$ is defined as in lemma~(lem:toy_problem of the paper).}

[Cor 3 of arXiv:2512.03884, '2512.03884'] Under assumption \eqref{psicondition}, for any $1 \le p\le \infty$, we have the limit laws
\[ \sqrt{N} W_{I,p}(\mu_N,\lambda) \overset{d}{\to} \| Y \|_{L^p ([0,1])} \quad \textrm{and} \quad \sqrt{N} W_{\mathbb{T},p}(\mu_N,\lambda) \overset{d}{\to} \inf_{c \in \mathbb{R}} \| Y -c \|_{L^p ([0,1])}, \]
and the laws of the iterated logarithm
\[ \begin{split} \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sqrt{N}W_{I,p} (\mu_N, \lambda)}{\sqrt{2 \log \log N}} &= \sup_{f \in B(\Gamma)} \| f \|_{L^p ([0,1])} \quad \textrm{a.s.}, \\ \limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sqrt{N}W_{\mathbb{T},p} (\mu_N, \lambda)}{\sqrt{2 \log \log N}} &= \sup_{f \in B(\Gamma)} \inf_{c \in \mathbb{R}} \| f -c \|_{L^p ([0,1])} \quad \textrm{a.s.} \end{split} \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition AC homeo extension on Cantor of arXiv:2608.30346, '\textbf{Classification complexity of homeomorphism group actions}'] Let \(A\) and \(B\) be closed, non-empty and nowhere dense subsets of \(2^\mathbb{N}\). Suppose there is a homeomorphism \(h: A \to B\) such that for every Borel \(E \subset A\) we have \(\lambda^0(E) = 0 \iff \lambda^0(h(E)) = 0 \). Then there is a homeomorphism \(\hat{h} \in \AC(2^\mathbb{N})\) extending \(h\).

Owner-own-work draft, claim w733-T363-023 v1; proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. On x1=(1,1/4),x2=(-1,1/4), labels+1, train both layers of f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j.x), with no biases, by gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss, ReLU derivative zero at zero. Initially require exactly one positive-output both-active neuron C, at least one positive-output x1-only neuron A, no x2-only neuron, and all remaining neurons strictly dead with arbitrary output. There is no initial restriction on C tilt, output-to-hidden norm ratio, initialization scale, or prediction imbalance. A global absolutely continuous flow exists; every such flow creates a positive x2-only B seed at finite time and then attains global normalized margin sqrt17/16, with normalization by total parameter squared norm. Reflection exchanges the two points. This is an entire activation-pattern family, extending the prior tilted balanced subcone. A C-to-A exit is impossible because the incoming C normal velocity at that boundary is positive. Under hypothetical absence of B, y and v diverge, homogeneity gives v>=3y/4 eventually, and a late E=f1-f2 barrier becomes invariant. The weighted variable s=v+(w.x1)/a then obeys s<=s(base)exp(aI1-bI2), a=sqrt17/4,b=15/(8sqrt17)-1/3>0, I_i=integral[-ell_prime(fi)]dt; the clock contradiction forces B creation. For iid Gaussian hidden/output coordinates N(0,sigma^2), sigma>0, p=atan(1/4)/pi, the exact probability of this family and its disjoint reflection is J_m=m*p[(1/4+p/2)^(m-1)-p^(m-1)]. It adds70 proposed global signed permutation orbits at widths2..6:2,6,12,20,30. With the prior two-initial-seed family this gives196 proposed global orbits and2643 unclassified. These are sufficient-family masses and unaudited labels, not total basin probabilities or a solution of the general max-margin question. Do not add the full prior subcone mass P_m to H_m+J_m: its single-C contribution is already contained in J_m. Only k>=2 subcone terms are disjoint extras. Multiple C neurons and negative-output live neurons remain outside this theorem.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:86c95ee5c518a4ff7c79edfa250fa9c9df7efed33ab77cee6fa0382902b47bb1","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/86/86c95ee5c518a4ff7c79edfa250fa9c9df7efed33ab77cee6fa0382902b47bb1.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:04ff8d68dd6430e39cf0ae8fcb14e0ecd4256acc9907d72f99f8f9e2628d2864","bundle_entry_key":"exactly-one-shared-positive-neuron-global-margin","bundle_id":"population.relu-exactly-one-shared-positive-neuron-global-margin","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"neural-network implicit bias","draft":"w733/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.implicit_bias:relu-two-point-one-shared-positive-neuron-one-point-seed-global-margin","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# A permanent one-point sector and exactly one positive shared neuron reach global margin
Claim w733-T363-023 v1; kind moved; target2; proof (unaudited). No novelty claim.

## Statement
Consider x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), both labels+1, f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j.x), no biases, both layers trained by continuous gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss, ReLU derivative zero at zero. Initially there is exactly one positive-output both-active neuron C, at least one positive-output x1-only neuron A, and all remaining neurons are strictly dead with arbitrary output. There is no x2-only neuron initially. There are NO restrictions on the tilt, output-to-hidden norm ratio, scale, or initial prediction imbalance. A global absolutely continuous flow exists; every such flow creates a positive x2-only seed at finite time and then attains the global normalized margin sqrt17/16. Reflection exchanges the two inputs. This is a whole activation-pattern family.

The margin is min(f(x1),f(x2))/N, N=sum_j(v_j^2+||w_j||^2). This theorem does not classify initializations with two or more C neurons or with a negative-output live neuron. No independent review or literature novelty is claimed.

## 1. Setup and the only possible strict exit
Use claims015/017 section1 for positive-live continuation: A stays strictly A, dead neurons stay dead, C output v increases and stays positive. Global absolutely continuous continuation exists; Ndot<=2a(a1+a2)N, where a=||x_i||=sqrt17/4 and ai=-ell_prime(fi)>0. Since fi>=0, ai<=1 and no finite-time blowup occurs. C boundary contacts have measure zero under the prescribed zero-derivative convention: the surviving input gives a strictly negative normal derivative at the missing-input boundary, whereas an absolutely continuous function has derivative zero almost everywhere on a level set. Thus C-mask equations hold almost everywhere before a strict exit. Uniqueness at grazing contacts is not assumed.

Write C hidden weights as w=(u,y), its output as v>0, and H_A=sum_A v_j(w_j.x1)>0. A prospective exit into A would reach z2=w.x2=0,z1>0. At that boundary f2=0 and f1>0, hence a1<a2. The incoming C-mask normal velocity would be
 z2dot=v[(-15/16)a1+(17/16)a2]>0.
This excludes a first such hit from the strict C side: continuity makes z2dot positive in a preceding neighborhood, incompatible with positive z2 approaching zero. Near that boundary the other preactivation is positive, so there is no other mask change in that neighborhood. The same argument applies after any earlier grazing contacts at the other boundary. Therefore C cannot exit into A. Since y increases, C cannot hit both preactivations zero. Its only possible strict exit is into B (x2-only), after which B persists by claim015.

It remains to prove that a strict B exit occurs in finite time. Assume for contradiction that no strict B exit ever occurs. Then C remains in the closed C cone y>=4|u| for all time, with its equations holding almost everywhere. In the rest of the proof all clocks may be reset at a finite base time; constant prefactors depend on that base time.

## 2. Eventual output-to-height control without an initial hypothesis
Put Ii=integral ai dt and T=I1+I2. Bounded T would bound N and both predictions by the norm inequality, keeping a1+a2 bounded below on the infinite physical-time trajectory; contradiction. Thus T->infinity.

Almost everywhere ydot=v(a1+a2)/4 and v>=v(0)>0, so y>=y(0)+v(0)T/4->infinity. Homogeneity preserves delta=v^2-u^2-y^2. Hence v^2>=y^2+delta, and at all sufficiently late times
 v>=3y/4.
No sign assumption on delta or initial v/y was used. Fix L after this inequality holds permanently.

## 3. A permanent positive prediction imbalance eventually appears
Let E=f1-f2=H_A+2vu. At E=0, u<0, a1=a2=b0>0, and the C equations give udot=0, vdot=b0*y/2. Thus
 Edot=b0[||grad H_A||^2+u*y].
At E=0, uv=-H_A/2; since y/v<=4/3 and uv<0, u*y>=(4/3)u*v=-2H_A/3. The one-point gradient bound is ||grad H_A||^2>=2aH_A. Therefore, for times after L,
 Edot>=b0(2a-2/3)H_A>0.
An E=0 contact cannot occur on a C boundary: on the A-side boundary f2=0<f1, while on the B-side boundary E=0 would give a1=a2 and incoming z1dot=v(a^2-15/16)b0=v*b0/8>0, excluding an incoming hit from C. The preceding inequality is therefore a genuine local inward derivative at every possible late E=0 contact. Once E>0 after L, it remains positive under the no-B assumption.

Such a positive E must occur after L. Otherwise E<=0 for all sufficiently late times, so a1>=a2 and, after resetting clocks there, I1>=T/2. The exact A hyperbolic formula gives H_A>=H_A(base) exp(2aI1). Claim016's C-cone estimate, which needs no output balance assumption, gives
 N_C<=N_C(base) exp(kappa T), kappa=4/sqrt17<a,
 and f2<=N_C/sqrt17.
Consequently E>=H_A-f2>=H_A(base)exp(aT)-N_C(base)exp(kappa T)/sqrt17->infinity, contradicting E<=0. Hence choose L1>=L with E>0 forever afterward.

## 4. The shared neuron eventually leans toward the missing point
For t>=L1, a1<a2 and udot=v(a1-a2)<0 almost everywhere. If u is already nonpositive, it stays so. Otherwise suppose u remains positive forever. Then E=H_A+2vu>=H_A(L1)=h0>0. For exponential loss a1/a2<=exp(-h0)<1. For logistic loss, f2>=0 and E>=h0 imply
 a1/a2=(1+exp(f2))/(1+exp(f2+E))<=2/(1+exp(h0))<1.
Thus a1<=r*a2 for a constant r<1. Since T->infinity and eventually a1<=a2, I2->infinity. Integrating udot<=-(1-r)v(0)a2 forces u->-infinity, a contradiction. Hence at some finite L2>=L1 we have u<=0 permanently, while E>0 and v>=3y/4.

## 5. A dissipative clock variable forces the missing B seed
Reset clocks at L2. Let q1=(w.x1)/a>=0 and s=v+q1. In C with u<=0 and y<=4v/3,
 v<=s<=v+y/sqrt17<=v(1+4/(3sqrt17))<2v,
 z2=-u+y/4<=y/2<=2v/3.
The exact C equations give
 sdot=a*a1*s+a2[z2-(15/(4sqrt17))*v]
      <=(a*a1-b*a2)*s,
 b=15/(8sqrt17)-1/3>0.
The sign of b follows from45>8sqrt17, or2025>1088. Thus
 s<=s(L2)exp(aI1-bI2).
Also ||w||^2<=17y^2/16<=17v^2/9, so N_C=v^2+||w||^2<=26v^2/9<=26s^2/9. Therefore
 N_C<=C exp(2aI1-2bI2),
 H_A>=H_A(L2)exp(2aI1),
 N_C/H_A<=C' exp(-2bI2)->0.
If I1 were bounded, N_C->0 would contradict v>=v(0)>0. Thus I1->infinity, H_A->infinity, and E>=H_A-N_C/sqrt17->infinity. For exponential or logistic loss, a1/a2->0. Integrating the eventual inequality a1<=epsilon*a2, for each epsilon>0, gives I1/I2->0. Hence aI1-bI2->-infinity, forcing s->0 and contradicting s>=v(0)>0. The no-B assumption is impossible.

After a finite strict B entry, the network has positive A and B neurons and only dead neurons otherwise. Claim009 supplies global normalized margin sqrt17/16 for this no-C family. No mixed-C asymptotic theorem is needed for this final implication.

## 6. Exact Gaussian probability and new whole-pattern labels
For iid hidden/output N(0,sigma^2) coordinates, sigma>0, let p=atan(1/4)/pi and q=1/4-p/2. C+ has probability p/2, A+ and B+ each have probability q, and a dead neuron with arbitrary output has probability p. A family with exactly one C+, at least one A+, and all other neurons dead has probability m(p/2)[(q+p)^(m-1)-p^(m-1)]. The reflected family is disjoint, so their combined exact mass is
 J_m=m*p[(1/4+p/2)^(m-1)-p^(m-1)].
This holds at any positive scale, including1e-6. It is a sufficient-family probability, not a total basin probability.

Resolving dead output signs produces m(m-1)/2 permutation orbits per orientation, or m(m-1) combined:2,6,12,20,30 at widths2..6, totaling70. These are disjoint from claim017's two-initial-seed family, whose whole-orbit count was126. The resulting proposed global labels total196; the prior2994-orbit inventory then contains196 global,20 source-bad,135 nonfitting, and2643 unclassified. These labels all inherit their proofs' unaudited status.

The whole-family mass H_m+J_m is disjoint. Do NOT add the full P_m of claim020 to that sum: its k=1 contribution is now contained in J_m. Only the k>=2 terms of that subcone formula are disjoint additional contributions. This prevents double counting while preserving the older sufficient bounds.

## Review limits
The hardest new points are the eventual imbalance barrier in section3 and excluding a C-to-A exit at a boundary. Sections2?5 contain the new seed-creation argument; existing claims009/015/016 and017 section1 are used at their stated scope and remain independently unaudited dependencies. No floating-point result or formal certificate is needed or asserted for this analytic proof. Prior subcone simulations concern only a subset of this larger family. Full unconstrained Gaussian basin classification remains open, especially multiple C and negative-output live neurons.

[Lemma lemlocal of arXiv:2606.29036, 'The limit law of the largest interpoint distance in a $d$-dimensional ellipsoid'] There exist constants $C>0$ and $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that the following
holds. Let $x=x(e,\delta,w)$, $y=x(e',\delta',w')$, and suppose that
$2-\|x-y\|\le\varepsilon$ for some $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$. Then
\[
\delta+\delta'\le C\varepsilon,
\]
and
\[
\|w\|^2+\|w'\|^2\le C\varepsilon.
\]
Moreover, $\langle e,e'\rangle+1\le C\varepsilon$.

Equivalently, if $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ is defined by
$\langle e,-e'\rangle=\cos\theta$,
then $\theta^2\le C\varepsilon$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem hittingprobforregularmeasure of arXiv:2506.10448, 'Hitting probabilities and the Ekstr\"om--Persson conjecture'] Let $X:=[0,1]^d$ and denote by $\Leb$ the restriction of the $d$-di\-men\-sion\-al Lebesgue 
measure to $X$. Let $\underline{r}$ be a sequence of radii such that 
$s_2(\underline{r})\leq d$. Then, for  analytic sets $C\subseteq X$, 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[i)] if 
          $\dimp C<d- s_2(\underline{r})$, then $C\cap E_{\underline r}(\omega)=\emptyset$
          almost surely,
 \item[ii)] if 
           $\dimh C>d- s_2(\underline{r})$, then 
           $C\cap E_{\underline{r}}(\omega)\neq\emptyset$ almost surely,        
\item[iii)] if  $C$ is compact and
           $\dimMBl C>d- s_2(\underline{r})$, then 
           $C\cap E_{\underline{r}}(\omega)\neq\emptyset$ almost surely,
\item[iv)]  if 
             $\underline r=\underline r{(\alpha)}$  for some  
            $\alpha>0$ and $\dimp C>d-\frac 1\alpha$, then 
            $C\cap E_{ \alpha}(\omega)\neq \emptyset$ almost surely.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:pi-moments of arXiv:2603.20078, '\bf \Large Gated Infinite Server Queues in Light Traffic'] In the framework of this section, assume that the service time
distribution has finite moments of all orders:
$\mathbb{E} \sigma_1^n = \int_0^\infty y^ng(y)dy < \infty$ for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$.
Then the Markov chain $\boldsymbol{Y}:=\{Y_n\}$ of the stage length process 
has a unique stationary probability measure $\pi$ with
density with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^+$, $f$, 

which satisfies the integral equation 
\begin{equation} 
f(y)=\int_0^\infty f(x) q(x,y)dx \hspace{0.2in} \mbox{ for all $y \in \mathbb{R}^+$.}
\end{equation}
The stationary measure $\pi$ has finite moments of all orders: 
$\int_0^\infty y^n \pi(dy) <\infty$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

PROOF (UNAUDITED). For 0<q<=1, -1<=c<1, n>=64, take n independent standard Gaussian pairs of correlation c, apply tanh(sqrt(q)*x), and let Dhat be one minus the uncentered empirical Gram correlation. Writing delta=1-E[tanh(sqrt(q)X)tanh(sqrt(q)Y)]/E[tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2], there is an explicit universal rational K (given in the proof) such that |E Dhat-delta|<=K*delta/n, E(Dhat/delta-1)^2<=K/n, and Var Dhat<=K*delta^2/n. At c=1 both gaps are exactly zero. Bounds hold conditionally on any past with equal CURRENT variances and fresh independent paired Gaussian rows. Equal initial variances alone do not justify iteration: with |c0|<1 their next empirical variances differ almost surely.
Equal current Gaussian marginal variances q in (0,1]; n>=64; independent rows; empirical means not subtracted.
